title: "With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to sacrifice"
description: The primal rite closes as the first ordinances (dharmas), by which the mighty reach the heaven of the ancient Sādhyas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Acchodā generated as mind-born daughter of the Pitṛs
description: The Agniṣvātta ancestors produce the maiden Acchodā, at once celestial girl, Himalayan river, and the clear-water lake Acchoda
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Acchodā's lapse and fall
description: After a thousand years of tapas Acchodā desires the descending Pitṛ Amāvasu, who refuses; the misplaced longing strips her celestial standing and she falls from the sky
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aghamarṣaṇa cosmogony (creation from tapas)
description: From kindled tapas (cosmic heat/austerity) are born ṛta (cosmic order) and satya (truth), then night, the cosmic ocean, the year, and the Dhātṛ-ordained sun and moon, heaven and earth, mid-air and light — a terse austerity-driven creation sequence
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras born as mind-born Prajāpati of Brahmā
description: Aṅgiras is emitted as one of Brahmā's mānasaputra Prajāpatis and primordial ṛṣis at the dawn of creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Atharvaveda elevated as Brahmaveda
description: The Pūrvabhāga opens by proclaiming the Atharvaveda the Brahmaveda, source and crown of the other three Vedas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Atri emitted as mind-born Prajāpati
description: Brahmā emits Atri as one of his mānasaputra Prajāpatis and primordial Saptarṣi at the dawn of creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Being wills to become many (Chāndogya cosmogony)
description: In the beginning Being alone (Sat) exists; it wills 'May I be many' and emits heat, water and food, from which all forms recombine
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Bhṛgu emitted as mind-born Prajāpati
description: Brahmā emits Bhṛgu as a mānasaputra and Prajāpati, apical patriarch of the Bhārgavas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Manu Smṛti 1.35; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1

title: Bhṛgu's vision of the eaters and the eaten in the other world
description: Varuṇa sends his proud son Bhṛgu to the next world, where he sees men devoured by the men, animals, and plants they had consumed in this life, then teaches him the Agnihotra as release
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa I.42–44; cf. Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 11.6.1

title: Bila-svarga named as the heaven of caverns
description: Sukadeva designates the seven subterranean realms collectively as bila-svarga and declares their sense-enjoyment superior to the upper heavens
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Agastya from the Pot
description: Mitra and Varuna, aroused at the sight of the apsara Urvashi, spill their seed into a clay pot, from which Agastya (and in some tellings Vasishtha) is born
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Aruṇa from the Broken Egg
description: Impatient Vinatā cracks one egg early, releasing the half-formed Aruṇa, who curses her to 500 years of slavery and flies up to become Sūrya's charioteer and the red dawn
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Brahmā from the navel-lotus
description: Brahmā emerges seated on the lotus growing from Viṣṇu's navel as Viṣṇu reclines on Śeṣa in the cosmic ocean at the start of each Kalpa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Gaṇeśa and the elephant head
description: Pārvatī forms a guardian boy from her body-paste; Śiva beheads him for barring the door, then revives him with an elephant's head as Gajānana with first-worship precedence
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Kāma from Brahmā's mind
description: as Brahmā emanates his mind-born sons, the love-god Kāma springs from his mind alongside Sandhyā, the first woman, and is given his flower-bow and the office of driving procreation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Kaśyapa from Marīci
description: Kaśyapa is born to the mind-born seer Marīci (and Kalā), making him a second-generation Prajāpati and grandson of Brahmā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Madhu and Kaiṭabha
description: Two asuras embodying tamas arise from the sleeping Viṣṇu's body (ear-wax) and threaten the newborn Brahmā on the lotus
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Narmadā from Śiva's Sweat
description: While Shiva performs tapas on Mount Riksha/Mekala, a drop of his perspiration falls to earth and becomes the maiden Narmada, whom he commands to flow as a sin-destroying river
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Āptya trio from Agni-in-the-waters
description: the fourth Agni hides in the waters in fear, and from his spittle spring the water-born deities Trita, Dvita, and Ekata, the "watery ones"
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Rākṣasas from Brahmā
description: As Brahmā recited the Vedas at the dawn of creation he grew hungry, and beings born of his hunger cried 'rakṣāma!' becoming rākṣasas (and those of thirst, yakṣas)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Yama and Yami
description: Yama and his twin sister Yami are born to Vivasvat/Surya and Saranyu/Sanjna as the primordial mortal pair
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma emits the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)
description: At the dawn of the kalpa Brahma produces his first conscious offspring from mind without union, the Prajapatis and first Saptarshis
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's curse on Kāma (the first curse)
description: enraged at the incestuous flush, Brahmā curses that Śiva will one day burn Kāma to ash, softening it with the promise of rebirth when Śiva marries
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's seed-pot floated on the pralaya
description: at the close of the last kalpa Brahmā seals the bīja of all future beings with amṛta in a kumbha and floats it on the deluge, whence it drifts south and grounds at Kuḍandhai
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma–Vishnu Supremacy Quarrel and Lingodbhava
description: Brahma and Vishnu dispute who is supreme, and Shiva manifests as a boundless flaming pillar of light (jyotirlinga) piercing the three worlds to settle the contest
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā Creates Mānasarovara from His Mind
description: Brahmā forms the lake Mānasa-sarovara out of his consciousness as the abode of his haṃsa mount, manifesting it on earth for the gods' austerities at Kailāsa's foot
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā creates the worlds (Brahma Purāṇa sarga)
description: Brahmā emerges from the cosmic egg / Viṣṇu's navel-lotus and brings forth the Prajāpatis, the Manus, and the worlds
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā emits the mind-born seers
description: At the dawn of the present kalpa Brahmā emits Marīci, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu (with the other mānasaputras) from his mind without union, making them the first sāttvic beings, Prajāpatis and original Saptarṣi
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā First Sacrifices in Ānandavana (Founding of Kāśī)
description: In its origin-myth Kashi is the first light-pillar of creation, the ground where Brahmā first performed sacrifice and the liṅga of light manifested in the grove of bliss
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā reveals Āyurveda at creation
description: Brahmā recalls/recites the beginningless science of life (as an upāṅga of the Atharvaveda) in 100,000 verses at the dawn of creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Suśruta Saṃhitā Sū. 1; Caraka Saṃhitā Sū. 1

title: Brahmā Slays the Demon Vajranābha with the Lotus
description: Brahma strikes down the asura Vajranabha with the lotus he holds; petals fall to earth at three places and well up as the three Pushkar lakes
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's lotus-creation
description: The Purāṇas narrate the primary creation (sarga), including Brahmā's emergence and the lotus-creation unfolding the universe at the start of his day
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's Prakṛṣṭa Yajña at Prayāga
description: At the start of creation Brahma performs the supreme prakrsta yajna at the confluence, giving Prayaga its name and making it the cosmic sacrificial altar
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Cosmos emitted from Death/Hunger (Bṛhadāraṇyaka cosmogony)
description: In the horse-sacrifice opening, Death (Mṛtyu / Prajāpati / Hunger) appears as the primal reality from which the worlds are emitted
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation by Vishnu/Vasudeva (sarga)
description: Vishnu as material and efficient cause unfolds prakriti and the tattvas, the cosmic egg, and Brahma's emergence in the model Puranic cosmogony
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation of Svayambhuva Manu & Shatarupa
description: Brahma divides his body into male and female halves, producing the first human couple and progenitors of mankind
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation, the cosmic egg, and Brahma's day (Vamana)
description: The Vamana Purana supplies a sarga account of the cosmic egg (anda) and the unfolding of the elements and the gods at the start of the kalpa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Dakṣiṇā wed to Yajña-puruṣa
description: the barren personified Sacrifice receives the fee-goddess Dakṣiṇā in marriage and their son Phala is born, so no rite bears fruit without the priestly fee
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Definition of the Āraṇyaka stratum (the 'forest book')
description: The Āraṇyaka is the third śruti layer, a forest-studied bridge from ritual karma-kāṇḍa toward the gnosis of jñāna-kāṇḍa
actors: Vedic ṛṣis; forest-dwelling students (vānaprastha); Vyāsa as divider
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Diggajas Created by Brahmā
description: The eight directional world-elephants, headed by Airāvata, are born at creation and ordained by Brahmā to uphold the earth at the quarters and serve as the Dikpālas' mounts
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Emanation of the four Kumāras
description: Brahmā emits Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra from his mind as his first, seniormost mind-born sons at the dawn of the kalpa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Emūṣa the boar raises the Earth (Brāhmaṇa antecedent)
description: The boar Emūṣa, identified with Prajāpati, lifts the hand-span Earth out of the primeval waters in the Vedic cosmogony
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 14.1.2.11; Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.1.5; Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10.1.8

title: Etymology of the name Rāma (rā + ma)
description: The Pūrva-tāpanī analyses the name Rāma as the resting-place of yogins and as a Brahman-disclosing mantra split into liberating seed-syllables
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gaṇeśa identified as Brahman (tvam eva pratyakṣaṃ tat tvam asi)
description: The Atharvaśīrṣa addresses Gaṇeśa directly as the perceptible Brahman, maker-sustainer-destroyer, and eternal Self, folding 'tat tvam asi' into worship of Gaṇapati
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gavam-ayana year-long sattra
description: The year-long soma session modelled on the solar year, with its Vishuvant turning-point and Mahavrata crowning day, identified with Prajapati's body reassembled in time
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hayagrīva recovers the stolen Vedas
description: Viṣṇu in his horse-headed Hayagrīva form recovers the Vedas stolen from Brahmā by the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha (or slays the asura Hayagrīva who stole them)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Hayagrīva Upaniṣad; Devī Bhāgavata

title: Indra Shears the Wings of the Mountains
description: In primeval ages winged mountains flew about crushing settlements until Indra cut off their wings with his vajra to fix them in place
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kāma's first arrows
description: testing his power, Kāma looses the five effect-arrows (Harṣaṇa, Rocana, Mohana, Śoṣaṇa, Māraṇa) on Brahmā and the prajāpatis, striking them with lust for Sandhyā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Mahāviṣṇu gives the Guruvāyūr icon to Brahmā
description: at the beginning of creation Viṣṇu hands his own worship-image to Brahmā, first custodian in the icon's lineage
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Manu's cosmogony (Manusmṛti ch. 1)
description: the Self-existent deposits his seed as a golden cosmic egg from which Brahmā and the ordered world arise, prefacing the law-code with a Sāṃkhya-tinged creation account
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Mūla-Prakṛti's aṁśa-catalogue
description: Prakṛti manifests as five full goddesses and then a train of part- and digit-portions, issuing Sanskritic pedigrees to Ṣaṣṭhī, Maṅgalā Caṇḍī, Svadhā and Dakṣiṇā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nikumbha's piśācas make Kashmir a half-year land
description: Under the piśāca king Nikumbha, whose hordes occupy the valley each winter, humans may dwell in Kashmir only in summer, evacuating before the snows
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nīla-nāga declares his ordinances to Candradeva
description: The serpent-king Nīla teaches the wintering brahmin Candradeva the festivals and rites whose observance ends the piśāca terror and lets humans dwell in Kashmir year-round — the nīla-mata that names the text
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Padma-sṛṣṭi, the lotus creation
description: from Viṣṇu on the causal waters rises the lotus bearing Brahmā, who creates the worlds — the padma that names the Purāṇa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prajāpati desires his daughter
description: the Creator conceives a passion for his own daughter, the Dawn (Uṣas) or the Sky (Dyaus), and pursues her as a stag while she flees as a red doe
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Puruṣa and Virāj beget each other
description: From the Puruṣa is born Virāj, and from Virāj the Puruṣa again — the circular double birth at the head of creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa's pañcarātra sattra
description: Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa performs the five-day sacrificial session and thereby becomes all this, welding the hymn's Puruṣa to Nārāyaṇa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rādhā emanates in Goloka
description: before creation, Rādhā emerges from the left half of Kṛṣṇa's body in the eternal cow-realm Goloka as his co-eternal śakti and presides as Rāseśvarī over the rāsa-maṇḍala
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rati created and wed to Kāma
description: from Dakṣa's perspiration arises Rati, and Brahmā gives her to the newly-cursed Kāma as his consort
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ṛbhu born a son of Brahmā, innately realized
description: The sage Ṛbhu comes into being as a son of the supreme Brahmā, endowed from birth with knowledge of truth and needing no instruction
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rebirth as Arundhatī and marriage to Vasiṣṭha
description: reborn fire-bright from Medhātithi's sacrifice and named Arundhatī, Sandhyā is wed by the Trimūrti to Vasiṣṭha, becoming the chastity-exemplar and mother of his hundred sons
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rudra's boon of Paśupati
description: before shooting, the avenger bargains for the over-lordship of animals, the charter of the name Paśupati, as his fee for punishing the Creator
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sandhyā's vow against lust-at-birth
description: shamed that desire arose in her father, brothers and herself, Sandhyā vows to legislate that no creature feel lust at the moment of its birth and departs for penance at Mount Candrabhāga
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ṣaṣṭhī emanates as the sixth portion of Prakṛti
description: in the Prakṛti-catalogue, Mūla-Prakṛti's aṁśa-rūpā goddesses include Ṣaṣṭhī-Devasenā, whence her name "the Sixth"
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva assumes the Śarabha form to subdue Narasiṃha
description: Śiva takes the eight-legged lion-bird Śarabha form to pacify or overpower Viṣṇu's raging man-lion Narasiṃha after the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śarabha Upaniṣad; Liṅga Purāṇa 2.48; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Kṛṣṇa divides into male and female (Brahmavaivarta cosmogony)
description: The universe issues from Kṛṣṇa as Para-Brahman, who first divides into male (Kṛṣṇa) and female (Rādhā/Prakṛti); Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva are produced as functionaries
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kaśyapa's progeny seed the beings of the cosmos
description: Kaśyapa's unions produce the opposed classes of beings: Ādityas (devas) by Aditi, Daityas by Diti, Dānavas by Danu, Nāgas by Kadrū, and Garuḍa and Aruṇa by Vinatā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Liṅgodbhava
description: An infinite pillar of fire erupts in the Brahmā-Viṣṇu supremacy quarrel; neither finds its end, establishing Śiva as the unbounded Absolute and origin of the liṅga
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Kūrma Purāṇa, Vāyu Purāṇa

title: Liṅgodbhava — the pillar of fire
description: When Brahmā and Viṣṇu quarrel over supremacy, an infinite fiery liṅga erupts; both fail to find its end, Viṣṇu concedes and Brahmā lies and is cursed, establishing Śiva as the unbounded Absolute
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śiva Purāṇa Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā; Liṅga Purāṇa; Kūrma Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa

title: Lingodbhava
description: Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over supremacy; Shiva manifests as an infinite pillar of fire (jyotirlinga) and challenges them to find its ends, establishing the origin of linga-worship
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara-samhita); cf. Linga, Kurma, Vamana, Skanda, Brahmanda, Vayu Puranas

title: Lingodbhava — rising of the cosmic pillar of light
description: Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over supremacy; Shiva manifests as an infinite blazing jyotirlinga and neither finds its end — Vishnu (as Varaha) admits failure while Brahma lies and is cursed to receive no worship, establishing the linga as supreme
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lotus cosmogony (padma-srishti)
description: From Vishnu's navel on the cosmic ocean rises a lotus bearing Brahma, who creates the worlds — the myth giving the Padma Purana its name
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Manu catches the fish (Śatapatha layer)
description: Manu finds a tiny fish in his cupped hands that begs protection in exchange for warning him of a coming flood
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Muktikā enumeration of the 108 Upaniṣads
description: The Muktikā Upaniṣad lists 108 Upaniṣads, from which editors group a sectarian block by deity
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Music derived from the Sāmaveda / divine origin
description: Classical song (gīta) is traced to Sāmavedic chant and to divine musicians — Sarasvatī's vīṇā, Nārada, the Gandharvas — and classed under the Gāndharvaveda
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Sāmaveda tradition; Nāṭya Śāstra 28; Purāṇic tradition

title: Nadīstuti — the praise of the rivers
description: The ṛṣi Sindhukṣit sings RV 10.75, exalting the Sindhu as the mightiest, roaring bull-flood among streams and rolling off the river-catalogue of the Sapta-Sindhu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Namakam: pacification of the wrathful Rudra
description: The Namakam (TS 4.5) salutes and pacifies the fierce-and-gracious Rudra, begging him to lay down his bow and arrow and turn his benign (śiva) face to the worshipper
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nasadiya Sukta — Hymn of Creation
description: Before existence/non-existence, 'That One' (Tad Ekam) breathes windless and arises through tapas, with kama as the first seed of mind — the agnostic origin hymn
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nasadiya Sukta — the first impulse from That One
description: Before existence or non-existence, 'That One' breathes windless by its own impulse; through tapas it arises and kama (desire) becomes the first seed of mind, the agnostic Vedic origin account
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nārada born as Brahmā's mind-born son
description: Nārada springs from Brahmā's mind as a mānasa-putra prajāpati and refuses the command to procreate, choosing celibacy and ceaseless wandering
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nārada mind-born from Brahmā
description: Nārada is emitted as a manasaputra/Prajāpati from Brahmā's mind among the foundational sages
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nārada teaches Prācīnabarhi via parable
description: Nārada arrives to redirect the sacrifice-obsessed King Prācīnabarhi from karma-kāṇḍa to self-knowledge by telling the veiled story of Purañjana
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Parvati's Penance and the Sand-Linga at Kanchipuram
description: Parvati, having covered Shiva's eyes and plunged the cosmos into darkness, does penance at Kanchi and moulds a sand-linga under a mango tree to worship as Ekambareswarar
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Pitṛs Beget the Devas, Asuras and Humans
description: As primordial demiurges the sevenfold Pitṛ orders precede and beget the three great classes — devas via Agniṣvātta, asuras via Barhiṣad, and humankind/varṇas via the four corporeal orders
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prajāpati emits and is dismembered in creation
description: Prajāpati emits the cosmos out of himself and falls apart, exhausted and scattered, requiring ritual reintegration
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prajāpati emits creation from the waters
description: Prajāpati, the Lord of Creatures, arises from the primal flood and through tapas emits the gods, worlds, the year, and the metres
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prior birth — Sudāmā cursed to become Śaṅkhacūḍa
description: Kṛṣṇa's gopa-attendant Sudāmā is cursed by Rādhā in Goloka and reborn as the daitya Śaṅkhacūḍa, son of Dambha
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Priyavrata Furrows the Earth-Disc into Oceans
description: Priyavrata, grandson of Manu Svayambhuva, furrows the lotus-disc Bhu-mandala with his chariot-wheels to make the seven ring-oceans, his seven sons ruling the seven dvipas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Puruṣa Sacrifice (Puruṣa Sūkta)
description: The cosmic person (Puruṣa) is sacrificed, and from his dismembered body the worlds and the four varṇas originate
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva brings down the Vitastā
description: At Kaśyapa's entreaty Śiva causes Pārvatī to flow forth as the river Vitastā through a trident-dug channel one vitasti deep, purifying the piśāca-defiled valley
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva shames Brahmā, the Pitṛs sweat-born
description: Śiva rebukes Brahmā for desiring his own daughter; the ashamed creator perspires, and from his sweat the Pitṛ classes (Agniṣvāttas, Barhiṣads) are born
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva the kirāta breaks the kumbha
description: to begin the new creation Śiva takes the form of a hunter and shatters the grounded pot with an arrow, its amṛta pooling as the Mahāmaham tank
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva's three boons to Sandhyā
description: after four yugas of penance Śiva grants that creatures feel no lust at birth, that Sandhyā attain matchless chastity, and that any lustful gazer be struck impotent
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śrī Sūkta as a Ṛgveda khila
description: The Śrī Sūkta is composed/transmitted as a khila (appendix) hymn attached to Ṛgveda maṇḍala 5, outside the received saṃhitā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Saptarishi emitted as mind-born sons of Brahma
description: The original Saptarishi are emitted as manasaputras (mind-born sons) from Brahma to begin procreation, simultaneously titled Prajapatis and seeders of all beings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Manu Smriti 1.34-35; Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12

title: Sarasvati as Vac utters creation
description: Sarasvati, who is Vac, the primordial sound/speech, is the means through which Brahma utters creation; she is co-emergent with the spoken cosmos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sati's birth as Daksha's daughter
description: The Great Goddess incarnates as Sati, daughter of the Prajāpati Daksha, specifically to win Shiva as her husband
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda, Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII

title: Sri emerges from Prajapati
description: In an early distribution-of-fortune myth, Sri emerges radiant from Prajapati and the gods seize her many powers (food, sovereignty, beauty)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Svadhā given to the Pitṛs
description: Brahmā manifests the personified ancestral oblation-call Svadhā and weds her to the Fathers, making every śrāddha offering efficacious
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Svayambhū Raṅga-vimāna worshipped by Brahmā
description: The self-manifest reclining Raṅganātha vimāna arises in the Ocean of Milk and is first worshipped by Brahmā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Tapas ignites creation
description: before gods or being, "That One" arises through the power of tapas-heat, and ṛta and satya are born of blazing tapas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Ādi Kumbheśvara liṅga hand-made by Śiva
description: Śiva gathers the nectar-soaked sand of the broken pot and forms the liṅga with his own hands, giving Kumbakonam its name-charter deity
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The contest of the faculties (prana-vidya)
description: In the recurring Upanishadic parable the senses each leave the body to prove their primacy and the body survives, but it collapses when Prana prepares to depart, proving breath the chief and support of all faculties
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The cosmogonic world-bearing tortoise
description: The pan-Indic image of a great tortoise supporting the earth/cosmos on its back, the 'Atlas' substrate Kurma inherits
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The curse of Śrīdāman
description: Rādhā curses Kṛṣṇa's attendant Śrīdāman to fall as the demon Śaṅkhacūḍa, and he counter-curses her to a human birth in Vraja with a hundred years' separation from Kṛṣṇa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The four varṇas from the Primeval body
description: Brāhmaṇa is brought forth from the mouth, Kṣatriya from the arms, Vaiśya from the thighs and Śūdra from the feet of the Self-existent, echoing the Puruṣa-sūkta
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The four varṇas issue from the Puruṣa's body
description: Brāhmaṇa from the mouth, Rājanya from the arms, Vaiśya from the thighs, Śūdra from the feet — the sole Ṛgvedic four-varṇa passage [late text] [disputed]
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The gods compound Bhūtavat/Rudra
description: finding no punisher among themselves, the gods pool their most dreadful forms into one avenging god, Bhūtavat (Rudra), named for being made of the terrors
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Gods Question the Goddess
description: All the gods approach the Great Goddess and ask 'Who are you and whence have you arisen?'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The heavens figured as the Śiśumāra (cosmic dolphin)
description: The Bhāgavata directs contemplation of the entire stellar sphere (jyotiś-cakra) as the coiled body of a porpoise/dolphin, head bent down, identified as the body of Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva-Kāla
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kumāras' question on mind and sense-objects
description: Brahmā's four mind-born sons (Sanaka, Sananda, Sanātana, Sanat-kumāra) ask how the mind can be separated from its sense-objects, which seem inextricably bound
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The naming of amāvāsyā
description: Because the steadfast Pitṛ of the episode is Amāvasu, the new-moon day is called amāvāsyā after him and śrāddha offered then is declared inexhaustible
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The piercing of the Creator
description: Rudra takes aim and pierces Prajāpati mid-act; the wounded Creator flies upward into the sky
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Pitṛs decree Acchodā's rebirth as Satyavatī
description: Consoling the fallen maiden, the ancestors script her mortal sentence: birth in the 28th Dvāpara from King Vasu's seed via the fish Adrikā, life as Kālī/Satyavatī, motherhood of Vyāsa, queenship under Śāntanu, then restoration to heaven
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Prātiśākhyas as a text-class
description: Veda-specific phonetic-grammatical manuals fix the precise oral text of each śākhā, deriving the saṃhitā recitation from the padapāṭha
actors: Vedic ṛṣis and śākhā schools; phoneticians of the Śikṣā vedānga
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ātman creates the worlds (Aitareya cosmogony)
description: In the Aitareya Upaniṣad's opening, Ātman alone exists and brings forth the worlds, the cosmic guardians, and the human person
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The primal sacrifice of the Puruṣa
description: The gods, Sādhyas, and ṛṣis offer the thousand-headed Cosmic Man as the first sacrifice, with spring as ghee, summer as fuel, autumn as oblation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The seed becomes a lake
description: Prajāpati's spilled seed runs on the ground; the gods make it a lake ringed with Agni so it is not lost, and creatures arise from it
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Vārāha war (third saṅgrāma)
description: Viṣṇu as the Boar raises the sunken Earth on his tusks and slays Hiraṇyākṣa in the underwater duel
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Vedas, animals, and worlds arise from the sacrifice
description: From the dismembered offering come the ṛcs, sāmans, metres and yajus, the beasts of air and village, and the worlds — moon from mind, sun from eye, sky from head, earth from feet
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Varaha lifts the Earth and instructs Bhu-devi
description: The Boar avatara Vishnu raises the submerged Earth-goddess Bhu-devi from the cosmic ocean and instructs her, the kalpa-opening frame of the whole Varaha Purana
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Varaha Purana; cf. Vishnu P., Bhagavata 3, Linga P.

title: Varaha lifts the submerged Earth
description: At the dawn of the Shveta-Varaha Kalpa the Varaha (boar) avatara lifts the submerged Earth, opening the Svayambhuva manvantara and naming the whole Kalpa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vasiṣṭha instructs Sandhyā
description: Brahmā sends Vasiṣṭha, disguised as a brahmin boy, to teach the untrained Sandhyā the mantra Oṃ Namaḥ Śaṃkarāya Oṃ and the method of tapas by Lake Bṛhallohita
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vishnu Reclines on the Ocean of Milk (Tiruparkadal)
description: In the celestial Vyuha state, Vishnu reclines as Kshirabdhinatha on Adishesha upon the Ocean of Milk attended by Lakshmi, the cosmic source from which the Dashavatara descents issue
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viśvakarmā's twin-bow contest (Pināka and Śārṅga)
description: Viśvakarmā forges two bows — Pināka for Śiva and Śārṅga for Viṣṇu — to settle the dispute over which deity is supreme; Viṣṇu prevails and Śiva's Pināka passes to the kings of Mithilā while Śārṅga remains Viṣṇu's own
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: mysutradhar (All About Divine Bows); Rāmāyaṇa (variant tradition)

title: Adyar sectarian groupings established
description: Adyar Library editions with Upaniṣad-brahmayogin's commentary fix the Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, and Śākta groups and their membership
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras marries Smṛti / daughters of Dakṣa
description: Aṅgiras weds Smṛti (or Dakṣa's daughters Śraddhā/Svadhā), founding his ṛṣi-progeny line
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ardhanārīśvara manifestation
description: Śiva fuses with Pārvatī into a single half-male, half-female body, expressing the inseparability of consciousness and energy and enabling sexual generation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Skanda Purāṇa

title: Ardhanārīśvara — the half-male/half-female form
description: Śiva fuses with Pārvatī into one body split down the centre, expressing the inseparability of Śiva (consciousness) and Śakti (energy); in one variant it enables sexual generation when Brahmā's mind-born creation cannot multiply
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa

title: Birth of Garuḍa
description: After five hundred years the second egg bursts and Garuḍa emerges fully formed and blazing like cosmic fire, mistaken for Agni until he diminishes his heat
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahman knows itself as 'I am Brahman'
description: In the beginning Brahman knows only itself, declaring 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi,' and thereby becomes the All
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma's lie and curse over the lingam
description: Brahma falsely claims to have found the pillar's top, producing the ketaki flower as false witness; Shiva curses Brahma to receive no worship and rewards the honest Vishnu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma's mind-born daughter and the growth of his heads
description: Brahma brings forth Sarasvati from his own mind as a being of dazzling beauty; captivated, he sprouts a face on each side and one upward to never lose sight of her, the origin of his four or five heads
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā meditates and the Lord appears as the swan
description: Unable to resolve the doubt, Brahmā meditates on the supreme Lord, who manifests before the Kumāras as a haṃsa (swan); they ask 'Who are you?'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's Yajña and Marriage to Gāyatrī at Pushkar
description: To complete his Pushkar fire-sacrifice on time without the delayed Savitri, Brahma marries the local girl Gayatri to sit beside him as ritual wife
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Cosmogony grounding Atharvan primacy
description: Brahman and the cosmic waters generate the worlds and the Vedas, weaving the Atharvan corpus into the origin of knowledge
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation from Vāc, the waters, and tapas
description: Subsidiary ŚB cosmogonies derive creation from Speech (Vāc), from cosmic waters bearing a golden egg, and from Prajāpati's heat/austerity
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation of the Prajāpatis and Manus
description: Brahmā emanates his mind-born sons (the Kumāras, Saptarṣi, Marīci, Atri, etc.) and the Manus who govern each Manvantara
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Descent of the Sarayu from Vishnu's Foot
description: The Sarayu river issues divinely, created from Vishnu's left foot-thumb as the Ganga issued from his right, making it a pada-tirtha of Vishnu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Dhruva fixed at the tail-tip as the cosmic pivot
description: Dhruva the pole star sits at the tip of the dolphin's upraised tail as the immovable point about which the whole heaven revolves, untouched even by pralaya
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Earth sunk in the cosmic ocean at the kalpa's dawn
description: At the start of the Śveta-Varāha-Kalpa the Earth lies submerged in the lower waters, blocking Brahmā's recreation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gangā's Descent on Brahmapurī
description: The celestial Gangā falls onto Brahmā's city atop Meru and divides into four cosmic rivers flowing to the four quarters off Meru's flanks
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: God Bears and Watches the Seer Kapila at the Beginning
description: The Lord brings forth and observes the seer Kapila, born at the beginning, an early scriptural reference tying the founding of Samkhya to the cosmic dawn
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hamsa Avatara Instructs the Four Kumaras
description: Vishnu's swan-avatara Hamsa reveals the doctrine to the four Kumaras, the origin myth of the Kumara/Sanakadi Sampradaya transmitted through Narada to Nimbarka
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Heti and Praheti, the first rākṣasas
description: The two first-born rākṣasa brothers spring at creation; Praheti turns ascetic while Heti founds the dynasty by marrying
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hiranyagarbha arises as sole lord
description: A golden germ arises in the beginning as the sole lord of all, floating on the primordial waters and becoming the cosmic egg / source of the world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hiranyagarbha — the Golden Womb arises
description: A golden germ (Hiranyagarbha) arises in the beginning as sole lord, floating on the primeval waters and becoming the cosmic egg / source of the world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Internalization of the sacrifice
description: The outward yajña is reinterpreted as inner meditation, with breath (prāṇa) as the inner fire and body/cosmos mapped onto the altar
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Invocation of golden, lotus-borne Śrī
description: The hymn invokes Agni/Jātavedas to bring Śrī, described as golden-hued (hiraṇya-varṇā), lotus-seated, and elephant-attended
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva Vows Never to Leave Kāśī (Avimukta)
description: Śiva installs the liberation-giving liṅga at Kashi and binds himself never to abandon the city, making it Avimukta, the never-forsaken zone outside ordinary time and karma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kala draws forth the worlds (Kala-sukta)
description: In the oldest hymn personifying Time, Kala as a seven-reined horse draws forth the worlds, the waters and even Prajapati, creating heaven and the earths
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kaśyapa among the Saptarṣi
description: Kaśyapa is counted among the Seven Sages presiding over the current Vaivasvata Manvantara
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ṛk-Prātiśākhya composed
description: Śaunaka's verse Prātiśākhya for the Śākala branch of the Ṛgveda, stating rules deriving the saṃhitā from Śākalya's padapāṭha
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Madhu and Kaiṭabha slain through the Goddess
description: At the dawn of creation the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha menace Brahmā on the lotus; Brahmā hymns the Goddess as Yoganidrā, who withdraws from Viṣṇu and wakes him, enabling the demons' slaying
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Madhu and Kaitabha arise from Vishnu's ear
description: While Vishnu lies in Yoganidra on Shesha at the end of a cosmic cycle, the asuras Madhu and Kaitabha arise from his ears and move to kill Brahma on the navel-lotus
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Marīci begets Kaśyapa
description: Marīci by Kalā (daughter of Kardama) fathers Kaśyapa, becoming the genealogical apex and grandfather of devas, asuras and nearly all beings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Marriages to Khyāti and Pulomā
description: Bhṛgu weds Khyāti (mother of Śrī and Dhātṛ/Vidhātṛ) and Pulomā (mother of Cyavana)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Mind-Born Daughters of the Pitṛs
description: Each Pitṛ-class generates a mind-born daughter — Menā (mother of Pārvatī and Gaṅgā), Acchodā, Narmadā — seeding the river- and mountain-genealogies of the cosmos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Narada praises Patala over Svarga
description: Returning from the nether regions, the sage Narada tells the gods that Patala is far more delightful than Indra's heaven, the canonical statement of the inversion doctrine
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nāsadīya creation-mystery hymn
description: The Ṛgvedic creation hymn contemplates the primordial state before being and non-being, framing the cosmos's emergence from neither existence nor non-existence
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Origin of Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya within the Namakam
description: The Namakam line 'namaḥ śivāya ca śivatarāya ca' supplies the Vedic seed of the five-syllabled Pañcākṣara mantra Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Parvati's Flood-Embrace of the Earth-Linga
description: Shiva looses a flood to wash away Parvati's sand-linga; she embraces it with her whole body to shield it, leaving the imprint of her bangles, and a pleased Shiva marries her at Kanchi
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Per-Varsha Avatara Worship Established in Jambudvipa
description: Each of the nine varshas of Jambudvipa becomes the eternal heaven where a specific avatara (Hayagriva, Matsya, Kurma, Nrsimha, Varaha, Rama, Nara-Narayana) is worshipped by a chief devotee
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prajapati equated with the sacrifice and the year
description: The PB identifies Prajapati with the sacrifice and the year; the year-sattra restores his dismembered body through chant
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prakriti unfolds the 23 evolutes (Samkhya emanation)
description: Disturbed from equilibrium by Purusha's mere proximity, Prakriti evolves in fixed sequence into Mahat, ahamkara, manas, the eleven indriyas, the five tanmatras and the five gross elements — the cosmogonic emanation of the manifest world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Proto-karma reciprocity (the dead weighed and requited)
description: JB passages on requital between this world and the next furnish one of the earliest pre-Upaniṣadic intimations of retributive reciprocity, a conceptual seed of karma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Purañjana finds the City of Nine Gates
description: The wandering king Purañjana (the embodied soul), accompanied by an unknown friend (Paramātman) he never recognizes, discovers a splendid nine-gated city (the body) in the Himālayan foothills
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Revelation of the tāraka (Rāma) mantra
description: The two-syllable name Rāma is declared the tāraka that ferries souls across saṃsāra, grounding the Vārāṇasī death-bed tāraka tradition
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Rāma-tāpanī Up., Pūrva; Kāśī tāraka tradition

title: Samjna Flees the Sun and Leaves Chhaya
description: Samjna/Saranyu, unable to bear the Sun's heat, flees and leaves her shadow-double Chhaya in her place; Chhaya becomes mother of the future 8th Manu Savarni by Surya
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sati weds Shiva against Daksha's will
description: Sati performs tapas to win the ascetic Shiva and marries him, deepening Daksha's resentment of the cremation-ground bridegroom
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Surabhi Born from Dakṣa's Belch
description: After Dakṣa drinks the churned amṛta, Surabhi is born from his belch, and from her spring the golden Kapilā cows, mothers of the world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Surabhi emanates from Kṛṣṇa in Goloka
description: The wish-cow Surabhi/Kāmadhenu emanates from Kṛṣṇa in Goloka, grounding cow-worship and the cowherd cosmology
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The agnicayana tortoise identified with Prajapati
description: In the Vedic fire-altar rite a living tortoise is laid in the altar and identified with Prajapati the creator, the pre-Vishnu layer of the kurma motif
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Atharvaveda deifies Prana
description: Atharvaveda 11.4 glorifies Prana as a cosmic deity, lord of all that breathes, present in wind, rain, trees and foetus — the earliest extended deification of breath as cosmic power
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The exhausted Prajāpati restored by sacrifice
description: Having emitted creation Prajāpati collapses, disjointed, and is re-membered and restored through the fire-altar sacrifice, which thereby sustains the cosmos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The failed first creation: the four Kumaras refuse to procreate
description: Brahma's first mind-sons, the four Kumaras, choose eternal childhood and celibacy, forcing Brahma to emit the procreating Prajapatis
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Theft of the Vedas
description: At the dawn of the cycle the demons seize/scatter the Vedas, leaving Brahmā unable to begin creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Goddess Declares 'I Am Brahman'
description: The Goddess answers in the first person 'ahaṃ brahma-svarūpiṇī' — I am of the nature of Brahman, from me proceed prakṛti and puruṣa, void and plenum
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kumāras refuse to procreate
description: As naiṣṭhika-brahmacārins fixed on mokṣa, the four decline Brahmā's command to beget offspring, the 'failed' first creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The pantheon and praṇava collapsed into Gaṇeśa
description: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Indra, Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, the Moon, the three worlds and Oṃ are all predicated of Gaṇeśa as the one reality
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The prodigious growth of the fish
description: The fish outgrows jar, pit, ground, and sea, revealing its supernatural nature
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Mahābhārata Vana Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24

title: The triple-mother river triad
description: RV 10.64.9 invokes Sarasvatī, Sarayū and Sindhu together as 'great mothers' summoned to the sacrifice
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vaiṣṇava counter — Narasiṃha as Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa
description: Vaiṣṇava traditions reverse the outcome, with Narasiṃha taking the two-headed eagle Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa form to prevail over Śiva's Śarabha — a sectarian flashpoint
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Varaha and Hamsa Seek the Pillar's Ends
description: Vishnu descends as the boar Varaha to find the pillar's base and Brahma ascends on his swan to find its top, but neither reaches an end of the infinite linga
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vishnu Stations the Dvādaśa Mādhava to Guard the Sangam
description: At Brahma's yajna, Vishnu stations himself in twelve Madhava forms around the Prayaga kshetra to perpetually guard the confluence
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Matsya Purana; Padma Purana; Agni Purana

title: Vāyu Hides Maināka in the Ocean
description: Vāyu spirits away his friend Maināka and hides him in the ocean, so Maināka alone among mountains keeps his wings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Yama, the First Mortal to Die
description: Yama becomes the first human to die, treading the path to the afterlife and so becoming lord and guide of the dead, welcoming souls to a sunlit Svarga
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras seated among the Saptarṣi
description: Aṅgiras takes his place among the Seven Sages, an office that recurs across manvantaras
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Agrarian fertility imagery and the children of Śrī
description: Śrī is praised as moist and dung-rich (ārdrā, karīṣiṇī) and her sons Kardama, Ciklīta, and Ānanda are invited into the household
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Bhairava severs Brahma's fifth head
description: Shiva as Mahakala emanates Bhairava, who severs Brahma's arrogant fifth head with a thumbnail and is condemned to wander as Kapalika bearing the skull until released at Kashi
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Shiva Purana; Skanda Purana Kashi Khanda

title: Brahma hymns Yoganidra to wake Vishnu
description: Unable to wake Vishnu, Brahma praises the goddess Yoganidra/Mahamaya (the Brahma-stuti), begging her to withdraw so Vishnu can rouse
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā and the Śatarūpā incest, cursed by Śiva
description: Smitten by the goddess Śatarūpā he created, Brahmā grows extra heads to keep gazing at her, for which Śiva curses him to lack worship, explaining his absence of temples
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Matsya Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Brahmā Purāṇa

title: Brahma's Lie and Shiva's Curse on Brahma and the Ketaki
description: Brahma falsely claims to have reached the summit using a ketaki flower as witness, and an enraged Shiva curses Brahma to have no worship and bars the ketaki flower from his worship while blessing the honest Vishnu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's anger and the cascade of creation
description: Frustrated by the refusal, Brahmā's wrath births Rudra from his brow and he emits the procreating Prajāpatis who carry creation forward
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Construction of the gaṇa-bīja mūla-mantra 'gaṃ'
description: The text builds the Gaṇapati root-mantra by phonetic exegesis (ga + anusvāra + bindu, crowned with Oṃ), enshrining 'gaṃ' / 'oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ' as Gaṇeśa's sound-body
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Dakṣiṇāmūrti teaches the Kumāras in silence
description: Śiva as the south-facing supreme guru expounds jñāna, yoga, and śāstra wordlessly through the cinmudrā to the four aged Kumāras, teaching ultimate truth through silence
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Deity-as-Brahman identification (the shared thesis)
description: Each sectarian Upaniṣad identifies its chosen deity (Viṣṇu, Śiva, or Devī) with the impersonal Brahman of the mukhya Upaniṣads
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Divine contest-myths and the seizing of soma
description: Indra's exploits, the gods' quarrels with the Asuras, races and wagers, and the purchase/seizing of soma are told as etiologies attached to particular sāmans
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Exposition of the Rāma ṣaḍakṣara
description: The six-syllabled Rāma mantra built on the bīja rāṃ is given as the mūla-mantra of Rāma worship with its ṛṣi, chandas, devatā and ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gayatri's flight for Soma
description: The metre Gayatri takes bird-form and flies to heaven to seize Soma for the gods, bringing the soma-draught to earth
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Goddess Pratyaṅgirā/Śūlinī aids in quelling Narasiṃha
description: The lion-faced goddess Pratyaṅgirā (Śūlinī Durgā) emerges from or fights alongside Śarabha to subdue Narasiṃha and is invoked in counter-sorcery
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hiranyagarbha golden egg splits into heaven and earth
description: The golden womb-egg floats on the primordial waters for a cosmic year before splitting into heaven and earth, the Vedic antecedent of the Puranic Brahmanda
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Indra releases the seven rivers
description: Indra slays the serpent Vṛtra and frees the pent waters, setting loose the cosmic sapta sindhavaḥ — the seven rivers that double as the Punjab streams
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lakṣmī Becomes the Badrī Tree to Shelter Vishnu
description: While Vishnu does austere tapas exposed to Himalayan cold, Lakshmi transforms into a badri (jujube) tree to shade him, giving Badrinath its name Badri-ka-ashrama
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Manu finds the fish (Matsya)
description: Manu Vaivasvata finds a tiny fish in his washing water; the fish begs protection and promises to save him from a coming flood
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Marriage of Heti and Bhayā
description: Heti weds Bhayā, sister of Kāla (Time/Death), begetting Vidyutkeśa and continuing the rākṣasa line
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Marriage to Dakṣa's thirteen daughters
description: Dakṣa gives thirteen daughters (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru, Vinatā and others) to Kaśyapa, whose wombs become the matrix of every species
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Marriage to Queen Purañjanī
description: At the seventh gate Purañjana meets and weds Purañjanī (buddhi/intelligence), guarded by a five-hooded serpent (prāṇa) and served by eleven attendants (ten senses plus the mind)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Matsya preaches the Matsya Purāṇa to Manu
description: At the start of the kalpa the fish-avatāra Matsya preaches the Matsya Purāṇa to Manu, making the deluge a frame for revelation itself
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Naciketas given to Yama (Death)
description: The father Vājaśravasa, in anger during an all-goods sacrifice, consigns his son Naciketas to Yama; the boy goes to the house of Death
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nārāyaṇa-anuvāka proclaims Nārāyaṇa as supreme Brahman
description: The Nārāyaṇa Sūkta hails the thousand-headed Nārāyaṇa as the cosmic Self (viśvātman) and supreme refuge, the Vedic root of Vaiṣṇava-supremacy theology
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prakṛti divides into the five primary goddesses
description: On Kṛṣṇa's will Prakṛti divides into Rādhā, Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Sāvitrī, each assigned a cosmic office, with all other goddesses their portions
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Pulastya begets Viśravas
description: Pulastya fathers Viśravas, the hinge from which the Yakṣa (Kubera) and Rākṣasa (Rāvaṇa) dynasties branch
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Purusha Sukta — creation by cosmic sacrifice
description: The gods dismember the cosmic Man Purusha in a primal yajna, and from his parts arise the moon, sun, Indra, Agni, Vayu, the worlds, and the four varnas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rudra saluted as immanent in all beings and trades
description: The middle anuvākas of the Namakam hail Rudra as present in every place, person, and profession — forests, paths, thieves, householders, artisans, hunters
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Saraswati's manifestation on Vasant Panchami
description: Brahma brings forth Saraswati to give voice, melody, and order to a silent creation, honored on Magha Shukla Panchami as her birthday/appearance
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sati's self-immolation at the Daksha-yajna
description: Publicly humiliated by Daksha, who reviles Shiva at his great sacrifice, Sati renounces her body in yogic fire
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Serpent-gems illuminate the sunless caverns
description: Though sun and moon do not reach below the earth, the gem-crests on the hoods of the great Nagas (Vasuki and kin) dispel all darkness, giving constant light without day or night
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Shiva descends into matter (36-tattva emanation)
description: In Kashmir Shaiva cosmogony a single divine consciousness Shiva, through Shakti, Sadashiva, Ishvara, Shuddhavidya, then Maya and the five kanchukas, contracts and descends into the individuated soul and the 24 tattvas of matter — the self-display of one consciousness as the universe
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Shiva severs Brahma's fifth head
description: Condemning Brahma's pursuit of his own daughter, Shiva severs Brahma's fifth head
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Soma's abduction of Tara and the Tarakamaya war
description: Soma, swollen with pride after his Rajasuya, carries off Tara wife of Brihaspati, sparking the Tarakamaya war until Brahma forces her return; Tara then bears Budha, founder of the Lunar dynasty
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Supremacy of the Brahman priest
description: Argues the four chief priests culminate in the Brahman, who oversees and corrects the rite; a sacrifice without a true Brahman fails as 'one-winged.'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Surabhi Granted Goloka by Brahmā
description: After ten thousand years of austerities to Brahmā at Kailāsa, Surabhi is made a goddess, decreed worthy of universal worship, and granted the cow-heaven Goloka
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sāvitrī's Curse on Brahmā
description: Finding another woman in her ritual seat, the enraged Savitri curses Brahma to be worshipped nowhere in the universe (and curses the attendant gods), explaining Brahma's near-total absence from temples
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Taittirīya-Prātiśākhya composed
description: Phonetic manual in 24 chapters governing recitation of the Black Yajurveda's Taittirīya Saṃhitā
actors: Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The anatomy of the figure — planets and asterisms as limbs
description: Sun, Moon, the five planets, Rāhu, the Aśvins, the nakṣatras and Nārāyaṇa (as the heart) are mapped onto specific limbs of the dolphin, with variant assignments in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Goddess as Source and Substrate of the Pantheon
description: The Goddess enumerates herself as the all-gods — moving with the Rudras, Vasus, Ādityas and All-gods, bringing forth Heaven, bending Rudra's bow
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kumaras' curse on Jaya and Vijaya
description: Barred from Vaikuntha by the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, the Kumaras curse them to three demonic births, engine of three Vishnu avatars
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Mahāvrata rite expounded
description: The great one-day Soma rite of the year-long Gavāmayana sattra is given esoteric exposition in the Rigvedic Āraṇyakas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The swan's reply on the one Self
description: The swan answers that the question 'who are you?' is empty since the Self is one in all beings; any posited difference is unreal, all being made of the same elements
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Varāha emerges from Brahmā's nostril
description: A thumb-sized boar issues from Brahmā's nostril and swells into a colossal cosmic form, hailed by the ṛṣis with Vedic hymns
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viṣṇu assumes the Hayagrīva form
description: Viṣṇu takes the horse-headed Hayagrīva/Hayaśiras descent to recover the Vedas and destroy the Madhu-class demons
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viṣṇu speaks the Catuh-sloki to Brahma
description: Viṣṇu speaks the four-verse seed of the Bhagavata to Brahma, the cosmogonic teaching treated as the text in miniature
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Wager of Kadrū and Vinatā; Vinatā Enslaved
description: The sisters bet on the color of Uccaiḥśravas's tail; Kadrū's nāga sons blacken it by deceit, Vinatā loses the wager and becomes Kadrū's slave, rooting Garuḍa's hatred of serpents
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Warning of the pralaya and order to build a boat
description: The grown fish foretells the world-ending deluge and bids Manu build a ship and embark
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Mahābhārata Vana Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24

title: Yama-Yami Dialogue and Rejected Union
description: Yami proposes incestuous union with her twin Yama to propagate humankind, but Yama refuses on grounds of dharma, staging moral restraint winning over desire at humanity's origin
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: A hundred years of sense-enjoyment
description: Purañjana lives ruled by his queen's moods, hunting and indulging the senses for a hundred years, forgetful of his eternal friend and his own nature
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Atharvan and Angiras Hear the Atharvaveda at the Cosmic Dawn
description: By the scripture clock, the rishis Atharvan, Angiras (and Bhrigu) 'hear' the eternal Atharvaveda — the twin streams of healing and aggressive magic — at the dawn of the cosmic order
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Ādityas (devas) from Aditi
description: From Aditi are born the twelve Ādityas including Indra and Vivasvat, the deva pole of the cosmos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma's creation from Garbhodakasayi Viṣṇu
description: Brahma emerges and undertakes secondary creation as the tattvas unfold from prakṛti, the cosmogonic core of skandha 3
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā's Creative Sacrifice at Brahma Sarovar
description: Tradition holds Brahmā performed the cosmic sṛṣṭi-yajña at Brahma Sarovar in Kurukṣetra, the universe created from this very ground
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation from Vishnu and Lakshmi
description: The Garuda Purana's cosmogony makes the manifest world the fruit of the union of Lakshmi-Narayana, anchoring the cosmic time-spine
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation of Night to Heal Yami's Grief
description: After Yama's death, the perpetually grieving Yami cannot feel time pass, so the gods create Night to separate the days, healing her sorrow with the coming of tomorrow
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Dahara-vidyā: Paramātman in the heart-lotus
description: A meditation locates the Supreme Self as a subtle flame within the heart-lotus, identified with Brahmā, Śiva, Hari and Indra, recasting the Chāndogya dahara-ākāśa in Vaiṣṇava terms
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Daksha's daughters wed to Kashyapa breed all classes of beings
description: Daksha gives 13+ daughters (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru, Vinata, etc.) to Kashyapa, who become the mothers of devas, asuras, nagas, birds and beasts
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Vishnu Purana 1.21; Bhagavata Purana 6.6; Mahabharata Adi Parva

title: Descent of Kubera and the royal Rākṣasas from Pulastya
description: Through Viśravas's wives Iḍaviḍā and Kaikasī are born Kubera and the rākṣasas Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa and Śūrpaṇakhā, rooting the Rākṣasa line in Pulastya's house
actors: Pulastya; Viśravas; Iḍaviḍā; Kaikasī; Kubera; Rāvaṇa; Kumbhakarṇa; Vibhīṣaṇa; Śūrpaṇakhā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Eggs emanate from Maha-Vishnu's pores (Causal Ocean)
description: On the exhalation of Maha-Vishnu reclining on the Causal Ocean, millions of brahmandas issue from his pores as bubbles, withdrawn again on his inhalation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Existence born from non-existence (Brahmanaspati)
description: The gods are born, existence arises from non-existence, and Brahmanaspati forges the worlds like a smith, with Daksha and Aditi mutually generated
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Expulsion of Alakṣmī
description: The hymn asks Śrī to drive out her dark sister Alakṣmī (Nirṛti), establishing the auspicious-vs-inauspicious polarity of the cult
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Garuḍa's Amṛta-Quest and Battle with the Devas
description: To ransom his mother, Garuḍa fights through the devas, a fire-ring, a razor-wheel and serpent-guardians to seize the amṛta from the gods
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gāyatrī's Boon and Sāvitrī's Mitigation at Pushkar
description: Placated, Savitri softens her curse so Brahma may be worshipped only at Pushkar, and Gayatri blesses the spot to be the king of pilgrimages granting liberation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Identification with Mahālakṣmī, Durgā and the Brahmavidyās
description: The gods recognize and hymn the one Goddess as Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī, Mahāsarasvatī, Durgā/Bhadrakālī, Gāyatrī and mother of the Vedas
actors: the Devī in her multiple forms
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Inhabitants live ageless and outside felt time
description: Denizens of bila-svarga remain youthful, free of disease, fear of death, and wrinkles, and do not perceive the passage of time amid continuous luxury
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kena (Talavakāra) Upaniṣad embedded in the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa
description: The school's esoteric Talavakāra Āraṇyaka houses the Kena Upaniṣad on Brahman as the unknowable power behind mind and senses, with the Umā-Haimavatī parable
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa / Talavakāra Āraṇyaka; Kena Upaniṣad

title: Kushmanda creates the cosmos with a smile
description: The Navadurga form Kushmanda is said to have created the cosmic egg (Anda) with a smile and to dwell in the sun's core
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Loading the saptarṣi and seeds of all life
description: Manu boards with the seven sages, herbs, seeds, and living creatures to preserve life through the flood (Purāṇic/epic addition)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Manu rears the fish and builds a ship
description: Manu rears the growing fish from jar to ditch to sea; the fish instructs him to build a ship for the deluge
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nara–Nārāyaṇa Penance at Badarikāśrama
description: Vishnu incarnate as the twin sages Nara and Narayana performs eternal penance in the open at Badarikashrama, the eponymous ascetics of the peaks flanking the shrine
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Om / praṇava speculation
description: Sustained analysis of the syllable Om as Brahman and the totality of the Vedas, prefiguring the Atharvan Upaniṣads
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Paṇis steal the cosmic cows into the Vala cave
description: The demon Paṇis steal and hide the cosmic cows (dawns/light/waters) in the Vala cave, prompting Indra to send a tracker
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rāma exalted as para-Brahman via the tāraka name
description: Rāma-tāpanīya and Rāma-rahasya declare Rāma the supreme Brahman, teaching the Rāma-mantra and the tāraka name said at Kāśī
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sacrifice of the Cosmic Purusha
description: The thousand-headed Purusha is dismembered by the gods in a primal yajna; from his body arise the cosmos and the four varnas (Brahmana from mouth, Kshatriya from arms, Vaishya from thighs, Shudra from feet), plus moon, sun, Indra, Agni, and Vayu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Samkhya-Shaiva creation from the unmanifest linga
description: Creation proceeds from the unmanifest linga (avyakta/pradhana) through mahat and the tattvas to the manifest world, with Shiva-Shakti as the ultimate ground
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sat born from Asat (Brahmanaspati account)
description: The devas are born and existence arises from non-existence; Brahmanaspati forges the worlds, with Daksha and Aditi mutually generating each other
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Shuka's Dharana and the Avatara Catalogue
description: Shuka teaches the cosmic-body (Virat-purusha) meditation and recites the locus-classicus list of Vishnu's twenty-two avataras
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha; Vedas restored
description: The demons are killed and the Vedas returned to Brahmā so creation may proceed; Viṣṇu earns the epithet Madhusūdana
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Devī Māhātmya 1 (Goddess as agent, variant)

title: Sun, Moon, planets and Saptarṣi tethered to Dhruva by wind-cords
description: All celestial bodies are bound to Dhruva by cords of wind (pravaha) and wheel about him like oxen at a central post; the Saptarṣi circumambulate him, generating the kāla-cakra (wheel of time)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Aṅgirasas split the rock Vala
description: With Indra and Bṛhaspati the Aṅgirasa singer-priests break open Vala by the bṛhat chant and release the stolen cows/dawns, establishing sacrifice and song as cosmic forces
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The cosmic dive and lifting of the Earth on the tusks
description: Varāha plunges into the waters, scents out the Earth, and bears her up on his tusks; the Earth-goddess sings the Bhū-stuti
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Gaṇeśa Gāyatrī and ekadanta mantra
description: Supplies the Gaṇapati Gāyatrī 'eka-dantāya vidmahe, vakra-tuṇḍāya dhīmahi, tan no dantī/buddhiḥ pracodayāt' and the ekadanta dhyāna of the four-armed deity
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kumāras fixed as eternal five-year-olds
description: By their tapas and chastity the four remain forever in the form of naked, ageless five-year-old boys
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Pravargya (Gharma) hot-milk esoterica
description: The red-hot Mahāvīra pot offered milk is identified with the sun and cosmic Puruṣa as forest-secret ritual
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Rāma-gāyatrī
description: A Rāma-Sāvitrī/gāyatrī form is supplied, placing Rāma-meditation in the prestige register of the Vedic Gāyatrī
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The teaching on mind, objects, and the witnessing Self
description: The swan teaches that mind and sense-objects are alike modifications of the three guṇas and non-Self; the Self is the detached witness (sākṣin), and discriminating it from the guṇa-apparatus is the sought-for separation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Tryambaka / Mṛtyuñjaya strand in the Namakam
description: The Namakam carries the Tryambaka (three-eyed) mantra associated with healing and release from death, the Vedic root of the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya prayer
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Tvaṣṭṛ forges Indra's vajra
description: Tvaṣṭṛ, the first smith of the gods, forges Indra's thunderbolt vajra, his signature creation and the weapon that slays Vṛtra
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vidyutkeśa weds Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā; abandonment of Sukeśa
description: Vidyutkeśa marries Sālakaṭaṅkaṭā, daughter of Twilight, who bears a son and abandons the infant on a mountain
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vishnu beheads Madhu and Kaitabha
description: Mahamaya withdraws and Vishnu wakes, battles the demons for 5000 years, tricks them via their own boon, and beheads them on his thighs with his discus
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viśvāmitra and the swelling Vipāśā–Śutudrī
description: Viśvāmitra leads the Bharatas to the flooded Beas–Sutlej confluence and, praising the two river-goddesses, persuades them to lower their waters so the host can ford
actors: Viśvāmitra (ṛṣi); the Bharatas; the rivers Vipāśā and Śutudrī
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vājasaneyi-Prātiśākhya composed
description: Kātyāyana's systematic, grammar-like Prātiśākhya for the White Yajurveda, closest in method to Pāṇini
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Yama's three nights and the Nāciketa fire boon
description: Naciketas waits three unfed nights in Yama's house; Yama grants boons, the central one being knowledge of the Nāciketa fire that conquers re-death
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Adbhuta Brahmana of portents
description: The final chapter of the Shadvimsha Brahmana, a systematic treatise on omens, prodigies (eclipses, earthquakes, unnatural births) and the shanti expiations that avert their evil
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras as co-revealer of the Atharvaveda
description: The fourth Veda is named the Atharvāṅgirasa after the Atharvan and Aṅgiras priest-lines, with Aṅgiras eponym of its fierce abhicāra formulae
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aitareya Āraṇyaka composed
description: Five-book Rigvedic forest text of the Aitareya school covering the Mahāvrata, prāṇa speculation, and recitation theory
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Assault of Caṇḍavega and the Gandharvas (Time)
description: The swift Gandharva king Caṇḍavega with 360 male and 360 female soldiers (the days and nights of the year) and the serpent Prajāra repeatedly plunder the city, eroding its lifespan
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Atharva-Prātiśākhya / Śaunakīya Caturādhyāyikā composed
description: Śaunaka's four-chapter phonetic charter for the Śaunaka branch of the Atharvaveda
actors: Śaunaka (ascribed); Śaunaka school of the Atharvaveda
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Daityas from Diti
description: From Diti are born the senior asura Daityas including Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the primordial Pitrs from Brahma
description: The classical classes of divine ancestors (Agnishvattas, Barhishads, Somapas, Ajyapas, Sukalins) arise as mind-born sons of Brahma, becoming the primal ancestor-races worshipped above ordinary dead
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Chamakam: the 'ca me' enumeration of boons
description: After pacifying Rudra, the Chamakam (TS 4.7) petitions for a comprehensive list of boons — food, prosperity, progeny, health, vigour, truth, and cosmic powers — each ending 'ca me yajñena kalpantām'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Daksha's 27 daughters wed to Candra become the nakshatras
description: Daksha gives 27 daughters to the Moon as the lunar mansions; the Moon's neglect of all but Rohini brings Daksha's curse causing the lunar phases
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ādi Jāmbava set as primordial ancestor in Mādiga counter-purāṇa
description: In the Mādiga (Dalit) oral Jāmbapurāṇa, the primordial ancestor Jāmbava / Ādi Jāmbava is asserted as supreme at creation, ranked above the Brahmanical gods who are made his juniors, a non-Brahmanical cosmogony recited by Cindu/Dakkali bards and bound to the Mātaṅgi/Yellammā cults; this Jāmbava is distinct from the Rāmāyaṇa/Kṛṣṇa bear-king Jāmbavān
actors: Jāmbava / Ādi Jāmbava; Cindu/Dakkali bards; (cult-linked Mātaṅgi
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Jāmbapurāṇa / Jāmbava Purāṇa (Jāmbavanta-purāṇamu); Jambava Purana — Wikipedia

title: Emanation of innumerable universes from Maha-Vishnu's breath
description: Universes (brahmandas) issue like bubbles from the pores of Maha-Vishnu with each exhalation, each sealed in seven concentric layers and birthing its own Brahma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Embedded pañca-sūkta liturgy (Bhū, Durgā, Puruṣa)
description: The text anthologises the Bhū Sūkta (Earth-goddess Bhūdevī), Durgā Sūkta and a Yajurvedic Puruṣa-sūkta into the standard pañca-sūkta abhiṣeka recitation
actors: Bhūdevī; Durgā; cosmic Puruṣa; Vaiṣṇava-Smārta reciters
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gāyatrī and vyāhṛti doctrine
description: Expounds the Gāyatrī and the vyāhṛtis (bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ), correlating them with worlds, Vedas, and breaths as the verbal skeleton of the cosmos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva and Pārvatī bless Sukeśa
description: The abandoned infant Sukeśa is found and blessed by Śiva and Pārvatī, granted immortality, eternal youth and a flying city, becoming the patriarch of the Laṅkā kings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kumāras head the Bhāgavata avatāra list as prathama-avatāra
description: The four Sanas are enumerated as the very first of Viṣṇu's twenty-two descents, the jñāna-avatāra
