period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Liṅgodbhava — the Infinite Pillar of Fire
description: When Brahma and Vishnu dispute supremacy, Shiva appears as an infinite column of fire whose ends neither god can find; Vishnu as Varaha digs down and Brahma as a swan flies up, and the column cools into the Arunachala hill
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Liturgical use in pañca-sūkta abhiṣeka and Lakṣmī pūjā
description: The Śrī Sūkta becomes a core pañca-sūkta abhiṣeka text and the spine of Lakṣmī pūjā, homa, and japa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Pañca-sūkta abhiṣeka and Lakṣmī pūjā vidhi; Śrī Sūkta homa

title: Maya Danava builds the subterranean cities
description: The asura master-architect Maya constructs the jewelled palaces, gardens, and illusory mansions that furnish the seven patalas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Narasiṃha identified with Brahman
description: Nṛsiṃha-tāpanīya expounds Narasiṃha as Brahman through the Nṛsiṃha-anuṣṭubh mantra and Sudarśana-cakra, resolving into praṇava Advaita
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prajapati creates by tapas and self-multiplication
description: Prajapati, alone and desiring to be many, performs tapas and emits the worlds, creatures and Vedas, becoming exhausted and reconstituted by sacrifice
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Prajapati creates by tapas / self-multiplication
description: Prajapati, alone and afraid, desires to be many, performs tapas and emits the worlds, creatures, and Vedas, becoming exhausted and reconstituted by sacrifice
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Pulastya transmits the Purāṇa to Parāśara
description: Pulastya grants Parāśara the boon of being a complete narrator of Purāṇa-lore, establishing the Pulastya → Parāśara chain of transmission of the Viṣṇu Purāṇa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Revelation of the Devī Gāyatrī and Navārṇa Mantra
description: The text supplies the Devī Gāyatrī (mahā-devyai ca vidmahe...) and the nine-syllable navārṇa mantra (oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ cāmuṇḍāyai vicce) as the means of approaching the Goddess
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Devī Upaniṣad (mantra verses); Devī Māhātmya navārṇa liturgy

title: Saramā crosses the Rasā and tracks the cows
description: Indra's divine bitch Saramā crosses the impassable boundary-river Rasā and tracks the lowing stolen cattle to the Paṇis' stronghold
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: That One Arises Through Tapas and Kama (Nasadiya creation)
description: Before being and non-being, 'That One' breathes windless by its own impulse; through tapas it arises and kama (desire) becomes the first seed of mind — the agnostic Vedic cosmogony
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Ṛbhus split Tvaṣṭṛ's cup into four
description: The artisan-elf Ṛbhus split Tvaṣṭṛ's single soma-cup (camasa) into four, a feat earning them divine status and provoking Tvaṣṭṛ's jealousy
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The boat tethered to the fish's horn
description: Manu fastens the ship to the horned fish, tying it with a rope (in the Bhāgavata the serpent Vāsuki), and is towed across the deluge
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Mahābhārata Vana Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24

title: The Dāśarājña — Battle of the Ten Kings
description: King Sudās of the Tṛtsu-Bharatas, with Vasiṣṭha as purohita and Indra's aid, defeats a confederacy of ten kings on the Paruṣṇī (Ravi), the river drowning the enemy crossing
actors: Sudās; Vasiṣṭha; Indra; the ten allied kings/tribes
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The flood and the towing to the northern mountain
description: The deluge carries off all creatures; the fish tows Manu's ship by a rope on its horn to the northern mountain
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Hamsa-avatara teaches the Four Kumaras
description: In the namesake passage, Vishnu as a swan instructs the Four Kumaras on the three gunas and the discrimination of Self from matter, wisdom Krishna re-transmits
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Śiśumāra-dhāraṇā and closing mantra
description: Bhāgavata 5.23 prescribes a daily meditation visualising the dolphin-form as Vāsudeva-Kāla, with a thrice-daily namaskāra mantra said to dissolve the day's sins
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The nakṣatra deity-lists and constellation offerings
description: The TB establishes the lunar mansions with their presiding deities (Kṛttikā–Agni, Rohiṇī–Prajāpati, etc.) and prescribes the Nakṣatra-iṣṭi offerings to each
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The phala-śruti and liturgical prescription
description: Closing section promises Brahman-attainment, obstacle-removal and sinlessness through recitation, prescribing times, modaka offerings, an initiatory caveat, and the abhiṣeka/Aṅgārakī Caturthī liturgical use
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Rāma-yantra and bīja-meditation
description: A lotus/cakra yantra inscribed with the bīja rāṃ enthrones Rāma with Sītā, the brothers and Hanumān as āvaraṇa-devatās for syllabic meditation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The three states and the witness Self
description: The swan analyses waking, dream, and deep sleep as states of the intellect/guṇas, locating the Self as the unchanging consciousness that witnesses all three and is bound by none
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viṣṇu beheaded by the snapped bowstring (Devī Bhāgavata)
description: Resting his chin on his bow, Viṣṇu is decapitated when ants gnaw the bowstring and it snaps, his head lost
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viṣṇu Digs the Cakra-Puṣkariṇī; Śiva Drops His Earring
description: Viṣṇu digs the Maṇikarṇikā kuṇḍa with his discus in primal devotion and Śiva, trembling with delight, drops his jewelled earring (maṇi-karṇikā) into it, naming the great cremation-ground
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viṣṇu's Boon and Garuḍa Becomes His Mount
description: Impressed in the amṛta-flight, Viṣṇu grants Garuḍa immortality without drinking the nectar and a perch above him, setting him on his banner and making him his vāhana
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Yajña-Varāha allegory of the boar's body as sacrifice
description: Every limb of the boar is equated with a component of the Vedic yajña, making the lift a cosmic sacrifice sustaining the world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Yami Becomes the River Yamuna
description: In Puranic tradition Yami's grief at Yama's death transforms her into the sacred river Yamuna
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aitareya Upaniṣad embedded
description: AĀ 2.4–2.6 forms the Aitareya Upaniṣad, opening 'ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīt' and stating 'prajñānaṃ brahma'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Alignment of Dhruva, Meru and the lokas
description: The Śiśumāra-cakra occupies the starry region above the planetary spheres and Mount Meru, with Dhruva as the celestial pole directly above the Meru world-axis, all contained within the one Brahmāṇḍa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Atman splits into male and female
description: In the beginning the Self alone, lonely, desires a second and splits into husband and wife, from whose union all beings arise through name and form
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Atman splits into male and female (Upanishadic monism)
description: The lonely Self (Atman) desires a second, splits into husband and wife, and from their union all beings arise through name and form
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Bhrigu's journey to the other world
description: The proud Bhrigu, sent by his father Varuna to the next world, witnesses men devoured by the men, animals and plants they had consumed in life; returns chastened to be taught the Agnihotra's inner meaning
actors: the eaten and the eaters in the afterworld
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Bṛhaspati, guru of the gods
description: Aṅgiras fathers Bṛhaspati, lord of sacred speech and Devaguru, structural counterpart to Śukra guru of the asuras
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the daitya twins Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu
description: Diti bears twin daitya sons by Kaśyapa at a feared twilight conception; they are the first demonic birth of Jaya and Vijaya
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Dānavas from Danu
description: From Danu descend the Dānavas including Vṛtra and the Vipracitti line
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the eight diggajas from Brahmā's chanting
description: Per the Mātaṅgalīlā, Airāvata and the seven other world-elephants spring from Brahmā chanting hymns over Garuḍa's eggshell, forming the aṣṭa-diggaja that uphold the quarters of space
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Daksha's sons renounce; Narada is cursed
description: Narada dissuades Daksha's Haryashva and Shabalashva sons from procreating; the enraged Daksha curses Narada to wander eternally
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Genesis of the Shakti Pithas
description: Vishnu's Sudarshana Chakra dismembers Sati's corpse as the grief-stricken Shiva dances; each landing-spot of a body-part becomes a Shakti Pitha
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Devi-Bhagavata VII, Kalika Purana, Mahabhagavata Purana, Pithanirnaya

title: Horse-head affixed; demon Hayagrīva slain
description: By the Goddess's decree a horse's head is joined to Viṣṇu's body, forming Hayagrīva, who then slays the demon Hayagrīva killable only by a horse-headed being
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Instruction to abide as the unattached witness
description: The swan instructs the realized soul to abandon false identification with body and mind, remain unattached amid sense-experience, and rest in the Self — the paramahaṃsa ideal
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Journey to Vaikuṇṭha and barring at the seventh gate
description: The boy-sages travel to Vaikuṇṭha to behold Viṣṇu but are blocked at the seventh gate by doorkeepers Jaya and Vijaya
actors: The four Kumāras; Jaya and Vijaya
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kṛṣṇa-Gopāla identified with Brahman
description: Gopāla-tāpanī and Kṛṣṇa Upaniṣad declare the Vṛndāvana Kṛṣṇa the supreme Brahman via the eighteen-syllable mantra, a Gauḍīya foundation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kardama Weds Devahuti
description: The prajapati Kardama performs tapas, marries Svayambhuva Manu's daughter Devahuti, builds an aerial palace, and fathers nine daughters and a son who is Vishnu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kālakanyā, Yavana-rāja and the siege
description: Kālakanyā (old age), rejected by all, is allied with Yavana-rāja (Death) and Prajvāra (fever) to overrun and sack the nine-gated city
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Mahānārāyaṇa hymns to Nārāyaṇa and the Puruṣa-sūkta
description: Taittirīya Āraṇyaka prapāṭhaka 10 (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad) hymns Nārāyaṇa as supreme Brahman and houses an expanded Yajurvedic Puruṣa-sūkta recension
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Manu re-progenerates humanity through Iḍā
description: Sole survivor Manu offers an oblation into the waters from which the woman Iḍā arises, and through her he regenerates the human race
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Mooring at Naubandhana on the northern peak
description: The fish tows the boat to the highest Himālaya peak (Naubandhana, 'ship-binding'), where the sages secure it
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Origin of Chitragupta from Brahma's Body
description: Chitragupta springs from the body (kaya) of Brahma to keep the master-ledger of every being's deeds when Yama could not track them all
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Garuda Purana; Padma Purana; Kayastha tradition

title: Prātiśākhyas as predecessors of Pāṇini
description: The oldest extant Indian linguistic science supplies the vocabulary and pada-analysis that Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī inherits and generalizes into universal grammar
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Pulaha fathers creature-classes
description: Pulaha by his wife Kṣamā/Gati fathers various beasts, demi-races and sons (Karmaśreṣṭha, Varīyāṃs, Sahiṣṇu)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rāma's iconographic dhyāna
description: Meditation visualizes dark-hued two-armed Rāma bearing bow and arrow with Sītā in his transcendent Sāketa/Ayodhyā abode
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sindhu in the Bhāratavarṣa river-rosters
description: The Purāṇic geographies catalogue the Sindhu among the holy northern rivers of the karma-bhūmi as sacred attention shifts east to the Gaṅgā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.3; Vāyu Purāṇa; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa

title: Sukeśa weds Devavatī; birth of Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī
description: Sukeśa marries Devavatī and fathers the celebrated triad Mālyavān, Sumālī and Mālī, the great rākṣasa kings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Golden Womb (Hiranyagarbha) Arises
description: A golden germ/egg arises as the sole lord of creation, sustaining heaven and earth, named in the final verse as Prajapati — the seed of the later cosmic egg and Brahma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kuśa-Grass Trick and the Serpents' Forked Tongues
description: Garuḍa delivers the amṛta to the nāgas to free Vinatā but sets it on kuśa grass; while they bathe Indra snatches it back, and the nāgas licking the grass split their tongues — the aetiology of the forked tongue
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The number-litany of the Chamakam
description: A Chamakam anuvāka enumerates the odd (1–33) and even (4–48) numbers as 'ca me' requests, asking that all numerical orders of reality including the 33 Vedic gods be made favourable through sacrifice
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Phala-śruti of Recitation
description: Closing benediction prescribing recitation at the sandhyās, on aṣṭamī and during Navarātri, promising destruction of sin and attainment of the Goddess's world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Saramā–Paṇi dialogue and refusal
description: In the saṃvāda hymn the Paṇis try to bribe Saramā to defect; she refuses as Indra's envoy, foretelling that Indra and the Aṅgirases will break Vala
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The seven patalas roster and their rulers
description: Atala (Bala), Vitala (Siva as Hatakeshvara), Sutala (Bali), Talatala (Maya), Mahatala (Kadru's Nagas), Rasatala (the Pani Daityas/Danavas), and Patala (Vasuki) are named in descending order
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Unfolding of the cosmic egg (Adi-Sāṅkhya cosmogony)
description: From the unmanifest Pradhāna arise mahat, ahaṃkāra, the tanmātras and gross elements, condensing into the golden cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) within which Brahmā fashions the worlds
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Uttarabhāga digest of Soma ritual
description: The latter part treats Soma ritual mechanics (dīkṣā, pravargya, savanas, grahas) largely by excerpting older Brāhmaṇas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vishnu Appears as an Old Man to Sage Nārada at Vridha Badri
description: Vishnu appears in the form of an old man to sage Narada during his penance at Animath, where the current Badrinath idol carved by Vishvakarma was first worshipped
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vāyu breaks the peak of Meru to form Laṅkā
description: Incited by Nārada and after Garuḍa abandons his shielding post, Vāyu shears off the summit of Mount Meru and hurls it into the southern ocean, where it becomes the three-peaked Trikūṭa island of Laṅkā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras's wider progeny — Utathya, Saṃvarta and the gotra lines
description: Aṅgiras fathers sons including Utathya (ancestor of Bharadvāja) and Saṃvarta, seeding the Āṅgirasa house
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Antaryāmin: Nārāyaṇa as inner controller
description: The Supreme is named the Antaryāmin, the inner ruler dwelling in and governing all beings, an explicitly Vaiṣṇava reading later central to Rāmānuja's body-soul theology
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Bali installed in Sutala by Vamana
description: After surrendering the three worlds to Vamana/Trivikrama, the virtuous Daitya emperor Bali is granted kingship of Sutala, with Vishnu standing guard at his gate
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Nāgas from Kadru
description: From Kadru are born the thousand serpents Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and the rest
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Borrowing from older Brāhmaṇas
description: The Uttarabhāga excerpts and paraphrases the Aitareya, Kauṣītaki, and Śatapatha Brāhmaṇas, marking the GB as a late compilation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā composes the Daṇḍanīti and the first king is instituted
description: In primeval anarchy men appeal to Brahmā, who composes a vast treatise on polity; Śiva abridges it and the first king is installed to wield the rod of punishment
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Divine contest myths and saman origins
description: The Jaiminiya Brahmana preserves numerous myths of Indra's exploits, the gods' rivalries, and the seizing of soma, many tied to the origin of particular saman-melodies
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hiraṇyākṣa drags the Earth into the deep
description: The boon-emboldened Hiraṇyākṣa challenges Varuṇa, then seizes the Earth and drags her down into Rasātala/the lower waters
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Identification of Rāma as para-Brahman and Ātman
description: The Uttara-tāpanī declares Rāma the supreme sat-cit-ānanda Brahman identical with the innermost Self, appearing as Daśaratha's son through his own māyā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Indra and the Aṅgirases split Vala and release the cows
description: Acting on Saramā's report, Indra with the Aṅgirases breaks open the Vala cave and frees the cows/dawns
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kapila's Teaching to Devahuti
description: Vishnu incarnate as the sage Kapila instructs his mother Devahuti in Sankhya, bhakti-yoga, and liberation, and she attains moksha
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kauṣītaki / Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka composed
description: Fifteen-adhyāya Rigvedic forest text of the rival Kauṣītaki school treating the Mahāvrata, Puruṣa-vidyā, and the inner Agnihotra
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kratu fathers the Vālakhilyas
description: Kratu by his wife Kriyā fathers the sixty thousand thumb-sized Vālakhilya ascetics who escort the Sun's chariot; in the Mahābhārata their austerity generates Garuḍa
actors: Kratu; Kriyā; the Vālakhilyas; Garuḍa; Indra
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.10; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva

title: Lotus-born Brahma from Vishnu's navel
description: During pralaya Vishnu reclines on Shesha on the causal ocean; at creation's dawn a lotus springs from his navel bearing Brahma, the delegated creator
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nārāyaṇa declared the All
description: Nārāyaṇa, Tārasāra, Vāsudeva, and Tripādvibhūti texts proclaim Nārāyaṇa/Vāsudeva the source of all, teaching the aṣṭākṣara and dvādaśākṣara mantras
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Parvati's rebirth and tapas to win Shiva
description: Sati reincarnates as Parvati, daughter of Himavan, and undertakes ferocious austerities (Aparna) to win the meditating Shiva, passing his Brahmin-disguise test
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Shiva Purana Parvati Khanda, Kumarasambhava 1-5, Devi-Bhagavata

title: Pravargya and the severed head of the sacrifice
description: The Pravargya hot-milk rite identifies the red-hot Mahāvīra pot with the sun and the severed head of the sacrifice (Makha/Viṣṇu), whose decapitation myth anchors the rite
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Purañjana's anxious death and rebirth as a woman
description: Dying with his mind fixed on his queen rather than his eternal friend, Purañjana is reborn as Vaidarbhī, daughter of King Vidarbha, illustrating that the last thought at death determines the next body
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rudrābhiṣeka and graded Rudra-japa
description: The Śrī Rudram becomes the supreme abhiṣeka-chant for bathing the Śiva-liṅga, recited in graded tiers (Rudra, Ekādaśa-rudri, Laghu-rudra, Mahā-rudra, Ati-rudra) framed by laghu-nyāsa and Śānti
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Rudra-yajña paddhati; laghu-nyāsa; living temple liturgy

title: The Kumāras' liberation and the swan's disappearance
description: Having grasped the teaching, the Four Kumāras worship the swan, who then vanishes — the entire span of the avatāra
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Matsya in-flood teaching (brahma-jñāna)
description: During the night of dissolution Matsya expounds knowledge of the Self and Absolute to Satyavrata and the sages (the 'Matsya Purāṇa')
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vishnu reclines on Shesha and projects Brahma
description: During the cosmic night Vishnu reclines on the serpent Shesha upon the causal ocean; at creation's dawn a lotus springs from his navel bearing Brahma the delegated creator
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Bhagavata Purana 3.8; Vishnu Purana; Matsya Purana

title: Viśvakarmā builds Laṅkā
description: At the brothers' request the divine architect Viśvakarmā raises the golden city of Laṅkā on Mount Trikūṭa for the first rākṣasa masters
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Agnicayana rebuilds Prajāpati as the bird-altar
description: The fire-altar of 10,800 bricks in five layers shaped as a falcon reassembles the dismembered Prajāpati and Agni, encoding the year in its bricks
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ananta-Shesha reclines below Patala
description: Beneath the lowest tier Patala, the cosmic serpent Ananta-Shesha bears all the worlds on a single hood
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Garuḍa and Aruṇa from Vinatā
description: From Vinatā are born Aruṇa and Garuḍa, and the Kadru–Vinatā wager seeds the eternal serpent–bird enmity
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma born from the navel-lotus of Vishnu
description: Within each cosmic egg, Vishnu reclines on the Garbhodaka womb-ocean and from his navel-lotus is born Brahma, who then builds the dvipas and lokas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Creation of the worlds by the Self (Aitareya Upanishad)
description: The Self/Atman, alone in the beginning, creates the worlds, the cosmic Person and the deities, then enters his creation through the crown of the head
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Devi slays Madhu and Kaitabha (Prathama-carita)
description: The Goddess as Yoganidra/Mahamaya rouses Vishnu from cosmic sleep to slay the demons Madhu and Kaitabha who threatened Brahma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Formation of the eight Āṅgirasa gaṇas
description: The Āṅgirasa pravara-cluster, largest of the brahmin gotra groupings, organizes into eight gaṇas including the Bharadvāja and Gautama lines
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Baudhāyana Śrautasūtra pravara lists; gotra–pravara tradition

title: Garuḍa wins the amṛta to free his mother Vinatā
description: Garuḍa, son of Kaśyapa and Vinatā, wins the amṛta from Indra to ransom his enslaved mother, whereupon Viṣṇu grants him immortality and makes him his mount and banner
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad embedded
description: Adhyāyas 3–6 form the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad, teaching Prāṇa = Brahman, the Indra–Pratardana dialogue, and the Devayāna soul-journey
actors: Indra; Pratardana; the soul on the Devayāna
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lingodbhava — the pillar of fire
description: Shiva manifests as the infinite pillar of fire between Brahma and Vishnu, establishing the linga as supreme; carried by the Kurma Purana
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Matrix of the Atharvan Upaniṣads
description: Its Om, Gāyatrī, and Brahman speculation becomes the prose matrix behind the Muṇḍaka, Praśna, and Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣads
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rāma as turīya and inner controller
description: Rāma-Brahman is read as the Oṃkāra turīya and antaryāmin, source and dissolution of all worlds, whom even Śiva meditates upon
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha
description: Two demons born from Vishnu's ear-wax threaten the newborn Brahma and steal the Vedas; Vishnu slays them, ordering creation against primordial chaos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The brāhmaṇa-friend's revelation and liberation
description: As the widowed Vaidarbhī grieves, the forgotten Unknown Friend appears as a brāhmaṇa, reveals their identity as jīva and Paramātman, and the soul is freed through self-knowledge
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kali-crossing mahā-mantra given
description: Kalisantaraṇa Upaniṣad gives the sixteen-name Hare-Rāma–Hare-Kṛṣṇa mantra as the means of crossing the Kali age
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Sārameyas guard Yama's path of the dead
description: Saramā's two four-eyed brindled hounds, Śyāma and Śabala/Śarvara, watch the road the dead must travel to reach Yama's realm and serve as his messengers
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The thousand-year underwater duel
description: Varāha and Hiraṇyākṣa fight a colossal mace-and-grapple battle for a thousand years; Brahmā warns Viṣṇu to finish before dusk
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vac Ambhrini Proclaims Herself the Supreme Power
description: The seeress Vac Ambhrini, daughter of Ambhrina, speaks in the first person proclaiming the goddess Speech as the supreme power pervading all gods — the Vedic seed of Shakta theology
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Veda-theft by the demon and recovery
description: A demon (Hayagrīva/Śaṅkhāsura) steals the Vedas from a sleeping Brahmā; Matsya slays him and restores the scriptures (Purāṇic strand)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viṣṇu accepts the curse and offers terms
description: Viṣṇu honours the Kumāras, accepts the curse, and offers Jaya and Vijaya seven devotee-births or three enemy-births; the curse seeds the three demonic incarnation-triads
actors: Viṣṇu; the four Kumāras; Jaya and Vijaya
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Wedding of Shiva and Parvati
description: After Parvati's penance, the Saptarishi arrange the divine wedding of Shiva and Parvati, drawing all the gods to Himavan's city
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras takes up the function of fire
description: When Agni withdraws, Aṅgiras blazes as the sacrificial fire and is honoured as Agni's first kindler/father
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of birds, beasts and remaining classes
description: From Tāmrā, Surabhi, Surasā, Ariṣṭā, Krodhavaśā, Irā, Khasā and Muni descend birds, cattle, Gandharvas, beasts, plants, Yakṣas/Rākṣasas and Apsarases
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Doctrine of the three births and Prajnanam Brahma
description: The Aitareya Upanishad teaches a man's three births (seed, womb, rebirth), cites Vamadeva's prenatal knowledge, and proclaims the mahavakya prajnanam brahma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Hiraṇyākṣa-vadha and re-establishment of the Earth
description: Varāha sets the Earth on the waters and slays Hiraṇyākṣa with a blow at the root of the ear, discharging the first Jaya–Vijaya birth
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kadrū–Vinatā wager over Uccaiḥśravas' tail
description: The wager between Kadrū and Vinatā over the colour of the churning-born horse Uccaiḥśravas' tail triggers Vinatā's enslavement, the origin of Garuḍa's nectar-quest and the Nāga–bird enmity
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Madhu-Kaitabha slain by Vishnu
description: Two demons born from Vishnu's ear-wax threaten the newborn Brahma and steal the Vedas; Vishnu slays them, asserting order against primordial chaos
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Narakas placed as a distinct tier below the patalas
description: The 28 punitive narakas are located below all seven patalas in Yama's southern quarter, kept textually and geographically separate from the paradisal bila-svarga
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Non-difference of name and named
description: The Uttara teaches that the name Rāma and Rāma-Brahman are non-different, making utterance of the tāraka-nāma itself realization of the absolute
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Nārada's explicit decoding of the allegory
description: Nārada itemizes the parable's key — Purañjana as jīva, the friend as Supersoul, the city as body, the woman as intelligence, the senses, Time, old age and death — and applies the lesson to Prācīnabarhi
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Parvati becomes Gauri and Annapurna
description: Parvati performs tapas to shed her dark complexion as Gauri (the cast sheath becoming Kali), and manifests as Annapurna at Kashi to feed even Shiva
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rudra/Śiva declared the sole reality
description: Atharvaśiras and Atharvaśikhā assert Rudra as the one reality and identify Oṃ and its mātrās with Śiva's faces
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sanatkumāra instructs King Pṛthu
description: The four descend to Pṛthu's sacrifice and Sanatkumāra delivers a discourse on ātma-jñāna, detachment and bhakti
actors: Sanatkumāra and the Kumāras; King Pṛthu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Satyavrata reborn as Vaivasvata Manu
description: When the waters recede Satyavrata is installed as Vaivasvata, the seventh Manu and progenitor of the present Manvantara
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Taittirīya Āraṇyaka composed
description: Ten-prapāṭhaka Krishna-Yajurveda forest text spanning the Āruṇa solar section, Pravargya, Pitṛmedha, and embedded Upaniṣads
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Cosmic Egg (Brahmanda) splits open
description: The creator's golden seed becomes an egg incubating on the waters; it splits — upper shell to heaven, lower to earth, the space between to sky
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Yājñavalkya's Upaniṣadic dialogues (Bṛhadāraṇyaka)
description: The closing kāṇḍa records Yājñavalkya's dialogues with Maitreyī, Gārgī, and King Janaka, articulating neti neti and Ātman = Brahman
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, closing kāṇḍa (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad; Mādhyandina kāṇḍa 14 / Kāṇva book 17)

title: Aṅgiras teaches Śaunaka the two knowledges
description: In the Atharvanic transmission Aṅgiras instructs the householder Śaunaka in the parā/aparā (higher/lower) knowledge distinction
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Forging of Sudarśana, Triśūla, and Puṣpaka from Sūrya's radiance
description: When Saṃjñā could not bear Sūrya's heat, Viśvakarmā grinds the sun on his lathe and forges Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra, Śiva's Triśūla, and the Puṣpaka Vimāna from the shavings of solar radiance
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kaivalya through Śiva-as-ātman
description: Kaivalya Upaniṣad teaches liberation through meditation on Maheśvara as the Self — 'I am Śiva, the Brahman.'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Phala-śruti of liberation
description: Knowing the name, tāraka, yantra and Rāma-Brahman grants crossing of saṃsāra, freedom from fear and sin, and attainment of Rāma's supreme abode
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sanatkumāra teaches Nārada the bhūmā-vidyā
description: Nārada approaches Sanatkumāra knowing the texts but not the Self; Sanatkumāra leads him up the ascending series to the doctrine of bhūmā, the Infinite Self
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Taittirīya Upaniṣad embedded
description: Praśnas 7–9 form the Taittirīya Upaniṣad with its three vallīs (Śikṣā, Brahmānanda, Bhṛgu)
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Varaha lifts the Earth at the Kalpa's dawn
description: At the dawn of the current Shveta-Varaha Kalpa, Vishnu as the boar Varaha lifts the Earth from the cosmic waters, the act that names this Day of Brahma
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Varaha lifts the earth at the Shveta-Varaha Kalpa's dawn
description: The current kalpa is named Shveta-Varaha for Vishnu's boar avatara who lifted the earth at its dawn on the first day of Brahma's 51st year
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aṅgiras's manvantara recurrences
description: On the scriptural clock Aṅgiras re-manifests across world-ages as Saptarṣi/Prajāpati, his name an office recurring each cycle and distinguished from his later namesake descendants
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Ash and rudrākṣa lore codified
description: Kālāgnirudra, Bhasmajābāla, Bṛhajjābāla, and Rudrākṣajābāla codify the tripuṇḍra ash-marks and the rudrākṣa beads born of Śiva's tears
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma seeks the root of the lotus-stalk
description: Brahma, born on the lotus and ignorant of his origin, descends the stalk seeking its root, fails, performs tapas, and is granted vision of Vishnu, establishing Vishnu's supremacy
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Devi creates the Trimurti (Shakta account)
description: The Supreme Goddess (Adi Parashakti) brings forth Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, assigns their cosmic functions, and grants each a consort-shakti from her own portions
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kaśyapa drains lake Satīsaras and founds Kashmir
description: Kaśyapa, with Viṣṇu and the gods, breaches the mountain at Varāhamūla to drain lake Satīsaras; Viṣṇu slays Jalodbhava and the valley Kaśmīra is named for and settled by Kaśyapa
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad as TĀ prapāṭhaka 10
description: Prapāṭhaka 10 of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka is the Mahānārāyaṇa (Yājñikī) Upaniṣad, hymning Nārāyaṇa as Brahman and supplying sandhyā and sannyāsa mantras
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Martanda cast away and reclaimed as Surya
description: In the Rigvedic account Aditi casts away her eighth son Martanda, who is reclaimed as Surya the Sun
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Agastya Mediates Indra and the Maruts
description: As Rigvedic seer Agastya composes hymns mediating a quarrel between Indra and the storm-gods, reconciling the Indra-Maruts dispute
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma forms within the cosmic egg and splits it
description: The creator's seed becomes a golden egg incubating a divine year; Brahma develops within and splits it into heavens, earth, and the sky between, with fluids becoming mountains and oceans
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Embedded suktas and famous mantras housed in the TĀ
description: The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka houses Yajurvedic Puruṣa-, Nārāyaṇa-, Bhū-, Durgā-, and Medhā-sūktas plus the Mṛtyuñjaya/Tryambaka mantra
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Gaṇeśa declared Brahman
description: Gaṇapati-Atharvaśīrṣa proclaims Gaṇeśa as Brahman with the bīja 'gaṃ' — the principal Gāṇapatya Śruti text
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Kaśyapa father of Vāmana
description: On Kaśyapa's instruction Aditi performs the Payovrata and Viṣṇu is born to the couple as the dwarf Vāmana to reclaim the worlds from Bali
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Primary unfolding of prakriti (Prakrita sarga)
description: From Vishnu's will, unmanifest prakriti is disturbed and the gunas lose equilibrium, emitting mahat, ahamkara, the tanmatras, senses, and gross elements into the cosmic egg
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Viśvakarmā forges the twin bows Pināka and Śārṅga
description: To settle the Śiva–Viṣṇu superiority contest, Viśvakarmā crafts the twin bows Pināka (Śiva) and Śārṅga (Viṣṇu); Viṣṇu 'wins' and Śiva's bow passes to the kings of Mithilā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Bhairava severs Brahmā's fifth head
description: From his fury at the arrogant fifth head of Brahmā, Śiva manifests Kāla Bhairava, who shears off the offending head, incurring brahmahatyā that clings as a skull until expiated at Kāśī
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation
source: Śiva Purāṇa Śatarudra-saṃhitā; Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa

title: Brahma creates the universe and begins time (Ugadi charter)
description: The Gudi Padwa/Ugadi charter marks the day Brahma created the universe and began kala (time) — Yuga-adi, the 'beginning of the age'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lingodbhava — the infinite pillar of light
description: Brahma and Vishnu dispute supremacy when an endless fiery jyotirlinga appears; neither finds its end and Shiva emerges from the linga as the true source of both
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Āraṇyaka–Upaniṣad embedding map
description: Each surviving Āraṇyaka embeds a principal Upaniṣad; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka is simultaneously Āraṇyaka and Upaniṣad of the Śukla Yajurveda
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Sadāśiva's five faces and the Hari-Hara harmony
description: Pañcabrahma sets out Śiva's five faces (Sadyojāta to Īśāna), while Rudrahṛdaya affirms the non-difference of Śiva and Viṣṇu
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The nine creations (sargas) of Brahma
description: Creation proceeds through nine graded sargas — three elemental (Prakrita) and five derived (Vaikrita) plus the Kaumara — from Mahat down to the Kumaras
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)
description: Brahma produces from his mind the Brahmarshis/Prajapatis — Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, Vasishtha — progenitors of all beings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śiva as Śarabha subdues Narasiṃha
description: Śarabha Upaniṣad asserts Śaiva supremacy: Śiva as the Śarabha overpowers Viṣṇu's Man-Lion avatāra — a sectarian polemic
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Yoganidra withdraws so Vishnu slays Madhu-Kaitabha
description: At a cycle's start the Goddess as Yoganidra withdraws from the sleeping Vishnu so he can wake and slay Madhu and Kaitabha, showing the Goddess drives even Vishnu's creative role
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Devi brings forth the Trimurti
description: The Supreme Goddess brings forth Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, assigns their cosmic functions, and grants each a consort-shakti who is her own portion
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Goddess answers 'I am Brahman'
description: Devī-Atharvaśīrṣa and Bahvṛca have the Goddess declare herself the sole Brahman and primordial existent, with the Devī mantra and Gāyatrī
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kumaras refuse to procreate
description: Brahma's first sons, the four eternal celibate Sanaka-kumaras, reject creation and remain renunciant, frustrating Brahma's plan to populate the world
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lalita Tripurasundari manifests from the sacrificial fire
description: Lalita Tripurasundari manifests from the cosmic fire of the gods' sacrifice and creates and orders the worlds
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lingodbhava establishes Shiva's supremacy
description: Shiva manifests as an infinite column of fire whose top (Brahma as swan) and bottom (Vishnu as boar) neither can find, establishing his supremacy and grounding the 12 Jyotirlingas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Śrīvidyā / Tripurā mantra and Śrīcakra expounded
description: Tripurā, Tripurātāpinī, and Bhāvanā expound Tripurasundarī, the pañcadaśī mantra, and the Śrīcakra interiorised on the body
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma splits into Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa
description: Brahma divides his body into male and female halves becoming Svayambhuva Manu (the first Manu) and Shatarupa, whose union begins the human dynastic line
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Sītā, Annapūrṇā as the supreme Śakti
description: Saubhāgyalakṣmī, Sarasvatī-rahasya, Sītā, and Annapūrṇā identify these goddesses with Mūla-Prakṛti / non-dual Brahman and give their vidyās
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Primary unfolding of prakriti into the tattvas
description: From Vishnu's will unmanifest prakriti is disturbed, the gunas lose equilibrium, and mahat, ahamkara, the tanmatras, senses and gross elements emerge in sequence, forming the cosmic egg
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahma emanates the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)
description: Brahma produces his Brahmarshi/Prajapati sons from his mind, the progenitors of all beings
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Daksha populates the worlds (maithuni srishti)
description: Daksha Prajapati fathers numerous daughters who, married to gods and sages, become mothers of devas, asuras, animals, and all living kinds, beginning sexual generation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Rudra from Brahma's anger
description: Enraged at the Kumaras' refusal, Brahma emits Rudra (half male, half female) from his brow; bidden to divide, the male becomes eleven Rudras and the female the shaktis
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Vishnu's cosmic sleep induced by Mahamaya
description: Vishnu's cosmic sleep is induced by Yoganidra/Mahamaya, the deluding power of the Goddess, in the Devi Mahatmya opening
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Innumerable universes from Maha-Vishnu's breath
description: Universes (brahmandas) emanate like bubbles with each exhalation of Maha-Vishnu, each sealed in seven concentric layers, a Brahma born in each
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of Narmada from Shiva
description: The river Narmada is born from a drop of Shiva's sweat during the tandava and granted to be imperishable, alone flowing through pralayas
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The cosmic lotus and Brahmā spring from reclining Viṣṇu
description: From the navel of Viṣṇu reclining on Ananta-Śeṣa springs the cosmic lotus bearing Brahmā, who begins the next creation
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Maruts from Rudra and Pṛśni
description: In the Vedic account the storm-troop Maruts are born together as sons of Rudra and the dappled cow-goddess Pṛśni, self-arising from the storm
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā emits the mind-born sons
description: At the dawn of the kalpa Brahmā emits his first conscious beings, the mānasaputra Prajāpatis and seers, from his mind/body without sexual union
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The four Kumāras refuse procreation
description: Brahmā's first mind-sons, the four Kumāras, are born fully realized and choose eternal childhood and celibacy, the 'failed first creation' that forces Brahmā to emit the procreating Prajāpatis
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Brahmā emits Manu Svāyambhuva and Śatarūpā
description: To get creation moving Brahmā emits from his body the first man Manu Svāyambhuva and the first woman Śatarūpā
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: The Kumāras curse Jaya and Vijaya
description: Barred from Vaikuṇṭha by the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, the wrathful Kumāras curse the pair to three demonic births, the engine of three of Viṣṇu's avatāra-descents
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aditi casts away and recovers Mārtāṇḍa
description: In the original Āditya account, the mother Aditi flings away the 'dead egg' eighth son Mārtāṇḍa (Sūrya) and then recovers him
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Rudras born from Brahmā's weeping brow
description: The eleven Rudras are born from Brahmā's brow when he wept, hence their name from rud, 'to cry'
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Birth of the Vālakhilyas to Kratu
description: The Saptarṣi-Prajāpati Kratu and his wife Sannati beget sixty-thousand thumb-sized celibate ascetic sons, the Vālakhilyas, who escort the Sun's chariot
period: Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation

title: Aged Śaibyā bears Vidarbha
description: In time the old queen conceives and bears Vidarbha, the miracle son whose birth makes the king's blurted promise true
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.38; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12; Matsya Purāṇa 44

title: Anasūyā's Trimūrti humbled
description: Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva come to break Anasūyā's chastity-vow and are turned to infants, the tri-unity that the Sucīndram māhātmya reads as the origin of its one-liṅga-three-gods form

title: Aṅga Abandons the Throne over Vena
description: King Aṅga weds Sunīthā, daughter of Death, whose evil grandson Vena is born; despairing of his wicked son, Aṅga abandons the throne for the forest

title: Ajāmila's fall and life of sin
description: The virtuous brāhmaṇa Ajāmila is ruined by lust for a dāsī, abandons his wife and dharma, and lives by theft and deceit, naming his youngest son Nārāyaṇa

title: Atri and Anasūyā's austerity for a divine son
description: The sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā perform severe tapas seeking a son equal to the Supreme, and the Trimūrti grant that portions of all three will be born to them

title: Avatar Satyasena destroys the evil spirits
description: Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and Dharma, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas and lying bhutas, fighting beside Indra Satyajit

title: Avatar Vaikuntha creates the realm of Vaikuntha
description: Vishnu's avatar Vaikuntha, born of his own accord, creates his eternal abode Vaikuntha at the request of his consort Rama (Lakshmi)

title: Bahulā recovered from the Nāga world; birth of Manu Auttama
description: the mute Nāga princess Nandā, her speech restored by a Sarasvatī rite, blesses Uttama with a son who becomes the 3rd Manu, Auttama

title: Betrothal of Ruru and Pramadvarā
description: The Bhārgava youth Ruru is betrothed to Pramadvarā, foundling daughter of the apsarā Menakā reared by sage Sthūlakeśa, and a wedding-day is fixed

title: Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest, origin of the Śrīvatsa mark
description: The sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu on the chest to test which of the three gods is greatest (the trimūrti-test). Far from angered, Viṣṇu honours and embraces the foot-mark; the auspicious whorl left on his breast becomes the Śrīvatsa, and Lakṣmī (Śrī), born of the milk-ocean, takes her seat there

title: Birth of Andhaka from Parvati's covering of Shiva's eyes
description: Parvati playfully covers Shiva's three eyes, plunging the cosmos into darkness; a drop of her sweat becomes the blind, deformed boy Andhaka
source: Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana

title: Birth of Cyavana
description: The Rākṣasa Puloman abducts the pregnant Pulomā, and the unborn Bhārgava child slips prematurely from the womb (hence 'Cyavana'), his radiance burning the Rākṣasa to ashes

title: Birth of Jalandhara from Shiva's brow-fire
description: The fire from Shiva's opened third eye is cast into the ocean and gestated into the asura Jalandhara

title: Birth of Kakshivat from the substituted nurse
description: Queen Sudeshna sends her shudra nurse to the blind sage in her place, and on her Dirghatamas begets eleven brahmin sons headed by the future rishi Kakshivat (Aushija)

title: Birth of Kapila to Kardama and Devahuti
description: Viṣṇu descends as the son of the patriarch Kardama and Devahūti in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara to teach Sāṃkhya-yoga

title: Birth of Rishabhadeva from Merudevi
description: King Nabhi and Merudevi perform a sacrifice longing for a son, and Vishnu descends, born as Rishabha (the bull), counted an avatara of Narayana

title: Birth of the avatar Vaikuntha
description: In the Raivata Manvantara Vishnu manifests of his own accord as Lord Vaikuntha, born together with the deva-class called Vaikunthas

title: Birth of Vaivasvata Manu
description: Vaivasvata, the 7th and current Manu, is born of Surya (Vivasvat) and Saranyu/Chhaya, becoming the present progenitor of humankind

title: Birth of Viśravas from Pulastya
description: The rākṣasa line descends from Brahmā's mind-born son Pulastya, whose circumstance at Tṛṇabindu's hermitage produces the sage Viśravas

title: Birth of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā to Ākūti and Ruci
description: Viṣṇu descends as the twin Yajña (a portion of Viṣṇu) alongside his sister-consort Dakṣiṇā, born to Ākūti (daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu) and the Prajāpati Ruci

title: Brahma to Vaivasvata Manu Descent
description: The cosmological spine runs Brahma to Marichi to Kashyapa to Vivasvan (Surya) to Vaivasvata Manu, whose children fork into the two royal dynasties
source: Vishnu Purana IV; Bhagavata Purana IX

title: Chakshusha Manu's previous-birth as Ananda
description: Before becoming the sixth Manu, the future Chakshusha lives as Ananda, switched at birth by a cat into a royal household, and on learning the truth withdraws to the forest for tapas, whereupon Brahma blesses him to be reborn as Manu

title: Daṇḍa violates Arajā
description: Ikṣvāku's son Daṇḍa, king at Madhumanta, ravishes Arajā the daughter of Śukrācārya in the forest near the sage's hermitage

title: Dadhīci teaches the Madhu-vidyā through a horse's head
description: To evade Indra's curse, the Aśvins fit Dadhyañc with a horse's head so he can teach them the honey-doctrine, then restore his own head

title: Daksha's Yajna and Snub of Shiva
description: Daksha Prajapati holds a great sacrifice and deliberately omits to invite Shiva and Sati out of contempt for his ascetic son-in-law
source: Devi Bhagavata Purana VII; Kalika Purana; Mahabhagavata Purana

title: Descent of the Gomatī from Vasiṣṭha's tapas
description: The river-goddess Gomatī is born as the daughter of the brahmarṣi Vasiṣṭha, flowing forth from his tapas to purify the earth; she wells up at the spring-tank Gomat Tāl (Fulhar Jheel) and becomes the river of Naimiṣāraṇya

title: Dhruva is slighted by his stepmother and vows penance
description: The boy-prince Dhruva, pushed from his father's lap by queen Suruci's scorn, resolves to win the highest station and leaves for the forest

title: Dirghatamas cast into the Ganga and rescued by King Bali
description: Expelled by his wife Pradveshi and sons over the go-dharma scandal, the blind sage is set adrift on a raft, survives the dasa Traitana's attack, and is found and honoured by the eastern king Bali

title: Dirghatamas consecrates Bharata Daushyanti
description: The blind seer Dirghatamas Mamateya performs the mahabhisheka royal consecration of Bharata son of Dushyanta, the emperor after whom Bharata-varsha is named

title: Founding of Ayodhya by Manu Vaivasvata
description: Vaivasvata Manu lays out Ayodhya on the south bank of the Sarayu as the capital of Kosala, founding the Suryavamsha/Ikshvaku city
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala-kanda 1.5; Skanda Purana Ayodhya-mahatmya

title: Founding of Ayodhyā by Manu Vaivasvata
description: Ayodhya, the unconquerable city and Suryavamsha capital, is founded by Manu Vaivasvata himself as one of the oldest cities

title: Founding of Videha-Mithilā
description: The bodiless king Nimi's churned-out son Mithi founds Mithilā, establishing the Videha/Janaka line that will rule from Janakpur

title: Gajendra-moksha
description: The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile and dragged toward death over a thousand celestial years, surrenders to the Supreme and is rescued by Vishnu, who arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his Sudarshana chakra

title: Gajendra-moksha (liberation of Gajendra)
description: The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile, surrenders to the Supreme; Vishnu arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his chakra

title: Gaṇeśa counter-curses Tulasī: an asura husband, then a plant
description: Gaṇeśa dooms Tulasī to marry a demon and thereafter become a plant, fixing the destiny fulfilled in the Śaṅkhacūḍa cycle

title: Gaṇeśa refuses the proposal on ascetic grounds
description: Gaṇeśa declines, declaring marriage inimical to tapasyā and rebuking Tulasī as a breaker of meditation

title: Gaṇeśa tempers the curse with blessing but bars tulasī from his worship
description: Propitiated, Gaṇeśa prophesies Tulasī will become the most sacred of plants, dearest to Nārāyaṇa, yet forever unacceptable in Gaṇeśa-pūjā

title: Ghosha continues the seer-line
description: Kakshivat's daughter Ghosha, granddaughter of Dirghatamas, becomes a brahmavadini and seer of the twin Ashvin-hymns RV 10.39-40

title: Jaḍa Bharata relates the parable to the Sauvīra king
description: The brāhmaṇa Jaḍa Bharata, pressed into palanquin service, tells the Ṛbhu–Nidāgha story to the king of Sauvīra, who abandons his notion of difference and turns toward liberating knowledge

title: Jahnu listed among the sons of Kuru
description: Purāṇic rosters place Jahnu as a son of Kuru in the Pauravā throne-line, though son-lists vary by recension
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22

title: Jaratkāru beholds his Pitṛs over the pit
description: The celibate ascetic Jaratkāru finds his forefathers hanging head-down over an abyss, their lineage-rope gnawed by the rat of Time because he refuses to beget a son

title: Jyāmagha's daughter-in-law and the founding of Vidarbha
description: The henpecked exile Jyāmagha declares a captive maiden his daughter-in-law before he has a son; the later-born Vidarbha marries her and founds the Vidarbha cousin-kingdom

title: Jyāmagha's exile to the Narmadā country
description: Displaced when his brother Rukmeṣu takes the throne, Jyāmagha departs south, settles on Mount Ṛkṣavat at Mṛttikāvatī, and later takes Śuktimatī

title: Kacha steals the Mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā
description: Bṛhaspati's son Kacha serves Śukra to learn the dead-reviving mantra; killed thrice by the asuras and revived from Śukra's own belly, he masters it

title: Kāmodā rises at the churning of the milk-ocean
description: Third of four divine maidens (Ramā, Vāruṇī, Kāmodā, Varā) born of the Samudra Manthana, Kāmodā becomes the beloved of Hari, wedded to Viṣṇu in perpetual meditation

title: Kapila descends and teaches Samkhya to Devahuti
description: The sage Kapila, an avatara of Vishnu, descends and expounds the Samkhya tattva-system (the Kapila-gita) to his mother Devahuti, the foundational teaching of the school

title: King Uttama banishes Queen Bahulā
description: Uttama, son of Uttānapāda, casts his cold queen Bahulā into the forest after she spurns him at court, forfeiting (a rishi warns) all his righteousness

title: Krishna teaches the imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, Manu, and Ikshvaku
description: Krishna recounts that at the dawn of the current Manvantara he first taught this imperishable yoga to the sun-god Vivasvan, who told Manu, who told Ikshvaku, a royal-sage lineage later lost and now restored

title: Kubera's penance and Brahma's boons
description: Kubera performs severe tapas standing on one leg and Brahma grants him immortality, lordship of all wealth and the nine nidhis, the office of Lokapala of the North, and the Pushpaka vimana

title: Manu delegates the śāstra to Bhṛgu
description: having composed the law, Manu teaches it to his mind-born son Bhṛgu, who recites chapters 2–12 to the assembled sages, fixing the code's nested narration

title: Mṛkaṇḍu's Boon and Choice
description: The childless sage Mṛkaṇḍu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son destined to live only sixteen years over a dull long-lived one
source: Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana

title: Nārada liberates the Pracetas
description: After ruling as their father wished, the Pracetas hear Nārada's discourse on bhakti as the essence of all duty and attain the Lord's abode

title: Nidāgha attains liberation
description: Recognizing his master and receiving the teaching of the one undivided Self, Nidāgha thereafter beholds all beings as non-different from himself and attains final mokṣa

title: Niyoga fathering of Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Pundra and Suhma
description: At childless King Bali's request Dirghatamas begets upon Queen Sudeshna the five sons who become eponyms of the eastern kingdoms

title: Penance of Tāraka's sons
description: Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, and Kamalākṣa undertake fierce penance to avenge their slain father Tāraka

title: Pippalāda's revenge pacified
description: Dadhīci's tree-reared orphan vows to destroy the gods who cost him his parents, but the mare-demon from Śiva's third eye turns on him and Śiva pacifies him, the fire merging into the Gautamī

title: Pravara rejects Varuthini
description: The pious brahmana Pravara, stranded in the Himalayas after a flying-paste wears off, is propositioned by the lovesick apsaras Varuthini but refuses her, bound by his vow of one wife

title: Ṛbhu instructs Nidāgha, who clings to duality
description: Ṛbhu imparts the whole of divine knowledge to Nidāgha, son of the Prajāpati Pulastya, yet perceives his disciple remains inwardly attached to duality

title: Ṛbhu's first visit — the meal at Vīranagara
description: After a thousand divine years Ṛbhu arrives unrecognized as a guest at Nidāgha's house on the Devikā river and turns each courtesy question about food and dwelling into a lesson that hunger, satisfaction, coming and going do not belong to the omnipresent Self

title: Ṛtavāc pulls the Revatī star from the sky
description: cursing his wicked son's birth-nakṣatra, the rishi Ṛtavāc makes the constellation Revatī fall onto Mount Kumuda, which is thereby renamed Raivataka

title: Saraṇyū flees Vivasvat and the substitute is made
description: After bearing Vivasvat twin children, Saraṇyū vanishes; the gods fashion a likeness (savarṇā) in her place, on whom the Aśvins are later begotten

title: Ṣaṣṭhī revives Priyavrata's stillborn son
description: the goddess reveals herself to the grieving king (son of Svāyambhuva Manu, 1st Manvantara), revives the child Suvrata, and her sixth-day worship is instituted

title: Sati born as Daksha's daughter
description: The Great Goddess consents to be born as a daughter of the Prajapati Daksha, named Sati, specifically to win Shiva as her husband
source: Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda; Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII

title: Satīsaras, the lake of Satī, fills the Kashmir valley
description: From the beginning of the kalpa the valley is the mountain-lake Satīsaras, remaining water through the first six manvantaras until the Vaivasvata age

title: Satīsaras, the six-manvantara lake
description: the Kashmir basin is the mountain-lake Satīsaras, "the lake of Satī (Umā)," remaining water through the first six manvantaras

title: Satyasena destroys the Yakshas and evil spirits
description: Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and accompanied by the Satyavratas, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas, and lying evil spirits, fighting alongside Indra Satyajit in the Uttama manvantara

title: Saudāsa's clash with Śakti and the curse of cannibalism
description: Ikṣvāku king Saudāsa meets Vasiṣṭha's son Śakti on a narrow path, insults/strikes him, and is cursed to become a man-eating rākṣasa

title: Śiva rises from the lake to bless the Pracetas
description: Rudra emerges from the water with his attendants and, declaring Viṣṇu's devotees most worshipful, offers the young ascetics a hymn to accomplish their purpose

title: Soma abducts Tara
description: The moon-god Soma, proud after his Rajasuya, carries off Tara, the chaste wife of Brihaspati, and refuses to return her

title: Soma abducts Tārā, igniting the Tārakāmaya War
description: The moon-god Soma carries off Tārā, wife of Bṛhaspati, and refuses to return her, sparking the fifth Devāsura war

title: Soma pacifies the Pracetas and gives Māriṣā
description: The moon-god and lord of plants halts the burning and, to seal peace, presents the tree-nursed maiden Māriṣā as the brothers' shared bride

title: Sukanyā pierces the anthill-sage Cyavana's eyes
description: Princess Sukanyā blinds the anthill-buried sage Cyavana with a thorn; his tapas afflicts her father Śaryāti's army
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 122–123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5

title: Suruci humiliates the child Dhruva
description: When five-year-old Dhruva climbs onto his father Uttānapāda's lap, the proud queen Suruci taunts that the royal lap is not for a rival's son unless he is reborn from her or wins it by propitiating Viṣṇu

title: Surya weds Saranyu and she flees as a mare
description: Surya weds Saranyu, daughter of Vishvakarma, but unable to bear his blaze she leaves behind her shadow-double Chhaya and flees as a mare

title: Sutapas and Pṛśni receive the icon
description: Brahmā bestows the image on the austere couple, whose tapas wins Viṣṇu's boon to be born as their son in three successive lives

title: Svarāṣṭra dethroned by Vimarda
description: the righteous king Svarāṣṭra, stripped of wives and kingdom by his rival Vimarda, withdraws to the forest as an ascetic

title: Ten thousand years of tapas and Viṣṇu's boon
description: Chanting the Rudra-Gītā underwater for ten millennia, the Pracetas win Viṣṇu's darśana and boons of good progeny, enjoyment, and final release

title: The Amṛta-manthana war (fourth saṅgrāma)
description: The churning of the milk-ocean breaks into open battle over the nectar; Mohinī diverts the amṛta and Rāhu is beheaded

title: The Andhakāra war (eighth saṅgrāma)
description: Śiva impales the blind asura Andhaka on the triśūla while the Mātṛkās drink his multiplying blood

title: The blurt: 'wife of your son yet unborn'
description: Cornered, Jyāmagha declares the girl his daughter-in-law, bride of the son barren Śaibyā will yet bear, and the Viśvedevas and Pitṛs ratify the impossible word
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.36–38; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12

title: The burning of the tree-overgrown earth
description: Emerging to find the earth choked with forest, the wrathful Pracetas breathe fire and wind from their mouths to reduce the trees to ash

title: The captive girl on the queen's chariot-seat
description: Old and sonless, Jyāmagha returns from campaign with a captive maiden seated in the queen's place, and Śaibyā confronts him as a cheat
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.35–36; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12

title: The demon rebirths of the six
description: the cursed sons are born as offspring of Hiraṇyakaśipu (Devī-Bhāgavata: first of Kālanemi, then Hiraṇyakaśipu), fated to be slain by their own former father

title: The doe-queen and the birth of Manu Tāmasa
description: in a great flood Svarāṣṭra meets his cursed dead queen Utpalāvatī as a doe; her flood-born son becomes the 4th Manu, Tāmasa, and she is freed from Sutapas's curse

title: The king fashioned from the gods (rājadharma)
description: the Lord creates the king from eternal particles of Indra, Vāyu, Yama, Sūrya, Agni, Varuṇa, Candra and Kubera so the strong do not devour the weak like fish

title: The king-and-elephant exchange
description: Returning after another thousand years, Ṛbhu asks which is the king and which the elephant, and when Nidāgha leaps on his shoulders crying "I am above, you below," counters "which of us is you, and which is I?", collapsing his disciple's dualism

title: The mocking of Brahmā (origin of the Ṣaḍgarbha)
description: in the first (Svāyambhuva) Manvantara the six godling sons of Marīci and Ūrṇā laugh at Brahmā's passion for his own daughter and are cursed to fall into asura birth

title: The Pracetas set out to beget progeny
description: Prācīnabarhi's ten sons, of one accord, journey west to a great lake to perform austerity as their father charged them to increase the world's population

title: The Rākṣasa who ate a shrew's temper
description: a brahman's abducted wife is found in the Utpalāvataka forest, her ill-nature already consumed by the Rākṣasa Valāka, and her disposition is remade by rite

title: The rebirth of Dakṣa from Māriṣā
description: The Prajāpati beheaded for reviling Śiva returns as the son of the ten Pracetas and Māriṣā — the "second Dakṣa" who re-seeds all progeny

title: The Rudra-Gītā — Śiva sings to Viṣṇu
description: Śiva teaches the Pracetas a stotra glorifying Vāsudeva/Saṅkarṣaṇa, the Bhāgavata's Śaiva–Vaiṣṇava bridge in which the God of the Śaivas extols the God of the Vaiṣṇavas

title: The sages slay the tyrant Vena
description: King Vena forbids all sacrifice and proclaims himself the sole god; the enraged brāhmaṇas kill him with charged mantras

title: The star-maiden Revatī and the birth of Manu Raivata
description: Pramuca fosters the girl born of the fallen star, Agni names King Durgama her husband, the star is restored for the wedding, and their son becomes the 5th Manu, Raivata

title: The Tārakāmaya war (fifth saṅgrāma)
description: Soma's abduction of Tārā splits gods and asuras into two armies; Viṣṇu slays Kālanemi before Brahmā halts the war

title: The Traipura war (seventh saṅgrāma)
description: Śiva as Tripurāntaka burns the three flying fortresses of Tāraka's sons with a single arrow at their alignment

title: The twelve-year drought and Varuṇa's boon
description: During a long Deccan drought, sage Gautama propitiates Varuṇa and gains unfailing grain/water at Brahmagiri, feeding the starving sages

title: The twelve-year sattra of Shaunaka at Naimisha
description: 88,000 sages assemble in Naimisharanya for a perpetual long-session Soma-sacrifice led by Kulapati Shaunaka, the setting for hearing the Puranas

title: Tāraka's tapas and boon
description: The daitya Tāraka performs fierce penance and wins from Brahmā the boon that he can die only by a (seven-day-old) son of Śiva
source: Śiva Purāṇa (Kumāra-khaṇḍa); Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa

title: Trimūrti test Anasūyā and are reborn as her sons
description: Sent to break Anasūyā's chastity, Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva are turned into infants by her power and reborn as Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā

title: Tulasī curses Gaṇeśa to be married
description: Humiliated by the rejection, Tulasī curses the celibate Gaṇeśa that he will certainly wed, vow or no vow

title: Tulasī departs for tapas toward her cursed destiny
description: Tulasī leaves for austerities, her course bent toward the demon-marriage to Śaṅkhacūḍa and ultimate union with Nārāyaṇa

title: Tulasī interrupts Gaṇeśa's meditation with a proposal
description: The ascetic maiden Tulasī, smitten by the young Gaṇeśa absorbed in meditation on Kṛṣṇa, breaks his tapas and proposes marriage

title: Vidarbha weds the waiting bride
description: Grown, Vidarbha marries the very captive girl long accepted as the household's daughter-in-law, and gives his name to the southern Vidarbha kingdom
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.38–39; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12

title: Vidarbha's sons head the Kratha-Kaiśika and Cedi lines
description: Vidarbha's sons (Kratha, Kaiśika, Romapāda; the Bhāgavata reads Kuśa for Kaiśika) head the Vidarbha king-line and, downstream, the Caidya kings
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.24

title: Viṣṇu gifts Ambarīṣa the Sudarśana and the Ekādaśī vow
description: Pleased by Ambarīṣa's total devotion, Viṣṇu awards him the Sudarśana-cakra as guardian; the king undertakes a year-long Ekādaśī vow

title: Yadu refuses his father's old age and is cursed
description: Yayāti curses his eldest son Yadu that his descendants shall never hold imperial sovereignty, barring the senior Yādava branch from the Lunar throne
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~84-85; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.10; Bhāgavata IX.18-19

title: Yama becomes the first mortal to die and king of the dead
description: Yama, son of Vivasvat and twin of Yami, is the first mortal to die and thereby becomes king of the dead, lord of Naraka in the southern quarter

title: Yuvanāśva drinks the consecrated fertility-water
description: The childless Ikṣvāku king Yuvanāśva, parched at night, accidentally drinks the mantra-charged conception-water the sages had prepared for his queen

title: Ajāmila cries 'Nārāyaṇa' and is saved by the Viṣṇudūtas
description: Dying, Ajāmila calls his son's name 'Nārāyaṇa'; four Viṣṇudūtas stop the Yamadūtas and debate the saving power of the holy name

title: Anasūyā turns the Trimūrti into infants
description: When the disguised Trimūrti demand to be served food naked to break her vow, Anasūyā by the power of her chastity transforms them into crying babies and serves them without sin

title: Andhaka adopted by Hiranyaksha and granted a boon
description: Shiva gives the dark boy to the childless daitya Hiranyaksha, who rears him; Andhaka wins from Brahma a boon making him slayable only if he lusts after his own mother
source: Shiva Purana; Matsya Purana; Vamana Purana

title: Atri serves as Saptarṣi of the Vaivasvata Manvantara
description: Atri is installed among the Seven Sages presiding over the present Vaivasvata Manvantara

title: Bharata gives the dynasty its name
description: From Dushyanta and Shakuntala is born Bharata, after whom Bharata-varsha and the Mahabharata are named

title: Birth of Māndhātṛ from his father's side
description: The child gestates within Yuvanāśva and is delivered by splitting open the king's flank, the father surviving by the sages'/Aśvins' grace

title: Birth of Mārkaṇḍeya
description: The radiant son is born and named Mārkaṇḍeya, mastering the Vedas precociously while his parents conceal his death-date

title: Birth of Nandi
description: The bull-faced Nandi is born to sage Shilada by Shiva's grace and is made chief of Shiva's hosts and eternal gatekeeper and mount

title: Birth of Nara and Narayana
description: The twin sage-incarnations of Vishnu, Nara and Narayana, are born as sons of Dharma and Murti/Ahimsa, becoming the perpetual ascetics of Badarikashrama (later reincarnated as Arjuna and Krishna)
source: Puranic Encyclopaedia / Devi-Bhagavata; (variant: Bhagavata Purana 4.1 places in Svayambhuva)

title: Birth of the avatar Hari
description: Vishnu manifests in the Tamasa Manvantara as the avatar Hari, son of sage Harimedha and his wife Harini, born expressly to liberate the devotee Gajendra

title: Brahma's prophecy and naming
description: The infant grips Brahma's beard; Brahma names him Jalandhara and decrees he can be slain only by Shiva

title: Brahmā restores Tārā; birth and naming of Budha
description: Brahmā halts the war and recovers the pregnant Tārā; she confesses the child is Soma's, and Soma names the boy Budha, founder of the Lunar line

title: Brahmā's boon of the three cities
description: Brahmā grants three impregnable flying cities destructible only by a single arrow at a once-in-a-millennium alignment

title: Creation of Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa
description: Brahma divides his own body into male and female halves, the male becoming Svayambhuva Manu and the female Shatarupa, the first human couple and progenitors of mankind

title: Creation of Vaikuntha realm
description: At the request of his consort the goddess Rama (Lakshmi), the avatar Vaikuntha creates the supreme eternal abode known as Vaikuntha to please her

title: Dadhīci gives his bones for Indra's vajra
description: To slay Vṛtra, Dadhīci yields his life so his thunder-charged spine can be forged by Viśvakarman into the vajra

title: Dakṣa-prajāpati's daughters wed the gods
description: Dakṣa's daughters marry Kaśyapa, Soma and others, seeding the gods, demons, and creatures in the standard Prajāpati genealogy

title: Dattātreya teaches the 24 gurus of nature
description: As the avadhūta sage, Dattātreya tells King Yadu how he learned liberation from twenty-four teachers drawn from the natural world

title: Devahuti's plea for liberation
description: The aged, lonely Devahūti approaches her divine son Kapila and asks him to dispel the darkness of saṃsāra, opening the discourse

title: Devi-Mahatmya frame: Suratha and Samadhi worship the Goddess
description: In the Svarochisha manvantara King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi worship the Goddess, and Suratha is reborn as the future Savarni Manu

title: Dhruva's great penance and Viṣṇu's darśana
description: Instructed by Nārada in the Vāsudeva mantra, Dhruva's escalating austerity in Madhuvana chokes the worlds and wins Viṣṇu's appearance

title: Dhruva's tapas and exaltation as the Pole Star
description: The child prince Dhruva, slighted by his stepmother, performs extreme austerity, receives Vishnu's darshana, and is exalted as the immovable Dhruva-loka (Pole Star)

title: Dhruva's vow and departure to the forest
description: Consoled by his mother Sunīti to seek refuge in Viṣṇu, the boy Dhruva resolves to win a station higher than any being ever attained and leaves the palace alone for the forest

title: Durvāsā's wrath and the Sudarśana's pursuit
description: Enraged over the Dvādaśī water-sip, Durvāsā hurls a fire-demon at Ambarīṣa; the Sudarśana burns it and chases the sage across the three worlds

title: Gaṅgā's descent floods Jahnu's sacrifice
description: As Bhagīratha leads the descending Gaṅgā across the plains, her torrent drowns sage-king Jahnu's sacrificial enclosure

title: Gajendra's hymn of surrender and rescue by Viṣṇu
description: Helpless Gajendra offers the Gajendra-stuti to the unnamed Absolute; Viṣṇu flies on Garuḍa and severs the crocodile with the Sudarśana

title: Gods Elect Nahuṣa as Indra
description: The gods and sages install the earthly emperor Nahuṣa on heaven's throne for his unmatched tapas, augmenting his merit to hold the office

title: Ila/Sudyumna and the Founding of the Lunar Line
description: Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna unites with Budha (son of Candra), and their son Pururavas founds the Candravamsha

title: Śiva's axe severs Gaṇeśa's tusk (Ekadanta origin)
description: When the boy Gaṇeśa barred Śiva's door, Śiva's axe (the paraśu later given to Paraśurāma) struck off one of Gaṇeśa's tusks, which he refused to dodge out of respect for his father's weapon — the origin of his epithet Ekadanta ('one-tusked')

title: Jaratkāru vows to marry on strict conditions
description: Recognizing himself as the sonless descendant, Jaratkāru pledges to wed only a same-named bride given freely whom he need not support, reserving the right to leave at the first displeasure

title: Kakudmi and Revati visit Brahmaloka (time dilation)
description: King Kakudmi takes his daughter Revati to Brahmaloka to seek a husband; Brahma reveals 27 chaturyugas have passed on Earth during the brief wait

title: King Janaka attains perfection through action
description: Krishna cites King Janaka and others who reached liberation through action itself, the standing proof that ruling and self-realization can coexist

title: King Kuru Ploughs the Field of Dharma
description: King Kuru ploughs the Kurukṣetra plain with a golden plough, sowing eight dharmic virtues to make it a Dharma-kṣetra

title: Kubera made world-guardian and lord of Laṅkā
description: Kubera, son of Viśravas, wins by austerity the lordship of the north, the yakṣas, and wealth, gaining the Puṣpaka chariot and the golden city of Laṅkā

title: Marriage of Śaṅkhacūḍa and Tulasī; the double armor
description: Śaṅkhacūḍa weds Tulasī, becoming invincible through her pativratya plus the Viṣṇu-Kavaca, and conquers the three worlds

title: Marriage of Kardama and Devahuti at Bindu-sarovara
description: Svayambhuva Manu brings his daughter Devahuti to wed Kardama, who creates an aerial vimana for their ascetic married life

title: Marriage of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā and birth of the twelve Yāmas
description: Yajña weds his twin Dakṣiṇā and they father the twelve Yāma gods, who become the deva-class of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara

title: Pauloma and the birth of Cyavana
description: A Rakshasa abducts the pregnant Puloma, causing the premature birth of Cyavana whose radiance burns the Rakshasa to ash, founding the Bhrigu line

title: Pramadvarā killed by snakebite
description: On the eve of the wedding Pramadvarā treads on a hidden snake and dies instantly, struck down by fate

title: Pṛthu churned from Vena's corpse and crowned first king
description: The sages churn Niṣāda then the Viṣṇu-marked Pṛthu from Vena's body; Pṛthu is consecrated the first anointed king

title: Pulastya fathers Vaishravana (Kubera)
description: The Prajapati Pulastya fathers Vaishravana/Kubera, who is granted lordship of wealth and the city of Lanka, angering his father's line

title: Rebirth of Vasishtha's seven sons as the Saptarishis of the Uttama manvantara
description: The seven sons Vasishtha had by his wife Urja in the Svayambhuva manvantara are reborn as the Saptarishis of the third (Uttama) period, a clear sage-reincarnation statement

title: Rishabha rains on his realm and fathers a hundred sons
