description: When envious Indra withholds rain, Rishabha rains by yoga-power on Ajanabha; he marries Jayanti and fathers a hundred sons, eldest Bharata, after whom the land becomes Bharata-varsha

title: Sañjñā creates the shadow-wife Chhāyā and flees
description: Scorched by Sūrya's blaze, Sañjñā creates an identical shadow-double Chhāyā to act as his wife, then flees to the northern forests in the form of a mare
source: Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa

title: Sati's Self-Immolation
description: Sati attends Daksha's sacrifice uninvited, is insulted, and gives up her body in the sacrificial fire (or by yogic agni), the act that names sati

title: Sati's tapas and marriage to Shiva
description: Sati performs the Nanda-vrata austerities to obtain the ascetic Shiva, who grants the boon and weds her against Daksha's will
source: Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita; Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4

title: Sukanyā pierces Cyavana's eyes
description: King Śaryāti's daughter Sukanyā pierces the glowing eyes of the anthill-buried sage Cyavana with a thorn, blinding him, whereupon his tapas afflicts the king's army with retention of urine and stool
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 122–123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5

title: Sukanyā wed to Cyavana; the Aśvins restore his youth
description: Sukanyā is given in atonement to the aged Cyavana; refusing the Aśvins' advances, she correctly picks her husband from three identical youths after they rejuvenate him
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 123–124; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5

title: Suta Ugrashravas recites the Puranas to the assembly
description: The bard Suta Ugrashravas (son of Romaharshana), in the transmission chain Vyasa to Romaharshana to Ugrashravas, narrates the eighteen Puranas to the Naimisha sages
source: Bhagavata Purana 1.1-1.4; Vayu Purana 1.16; Vishnu Purana 1.1

title: The Atri-Anasuya triad: birth of Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas
description: From the chaste Anasuya the Trimurti take partial birth: Brahma as Soma, Vishnu as Dattatreya, Shiva as Durvasas

title: The gandharva's deception and birth of Svarocis
description: A spurned gandharva takes Pravara's form to seduce Varuthini; meditating on the true Pravara's radiance she bears the self-luminous Svarocis

title: The gandharva's deception and conception of Svarocis
description: A spurned gandharva takes Pravara's exact form and unites with Varuthini; because she conceived meditating on the true Pravara's radiance, her son Svarocis is born self-luminous, giving the manvantara its name

title: The sages' jealousy and conspiracy
description: When rains return, the other sages grow envious of Gautama's merit and honour and plot to drive him from his hermitage

title: The thousand-year struggle and Gajendra's surrender
description: After a thousand-year contest in which his herd abandons him and his strength fails, Gajendra at last lets go of pride and turns his whole mind to the Supreme, raising a lotus and pouring out the Gajendra-stuti of total surrender

title: Tāraka's oppression of the devas
description: Tāraka conquers the three worlds, seizes Indra's heaven and the divine treasures, and inverts cosmic order
source: Matsya Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa

title: Śukra's curse creates the wilderness
description: Enraged Śukra curses Daṇḍa so Indra rains a seven-day dust-storm burying the kingdom for a hundred yojanas, making the desolate Daṇḍaka forest (Arajā's grove alone spared)

title: Vasishtha-Vishvamitra cow rivalry and Vishvamitra's penance
description: King Vishvamitra covets Vasishtha's wish-cow Kamadhenu, who conjures an army that routs his forces; humiliated, he renounces his throne and undertakes millennia of penance to rise from Rajarshi to Brahmarshi
source: Valmiki Ramayana Bala Kanda 51-65; Mahabharata Adi Parva

title: Vena's Misrule and Execution
description: Crowned Vena forbids all sacrifice, proclaiming himself the sole object of worship; when he refuses the sages' appeal, the brāhmaṇas slay him with mantra-charged kuśa-grass

title: Vimāna passed to Ikṣvāku and the Sūryavaṃśa
description: Brahmā grants the Raṅga-vimāna to Ikṣvāku, and it is worshipped down the Solar dynasty to Ayodhyā

title: Viśvāmitra sends a rākṣasa to possess the king
description: Viśvāmitra, exploiting his feud with Vasiṣṭha, dispatches a rākṣasa to possess the cursed Saudāsa so the curse falls on Vasiṣṭha's sons

title: Viśvāmitra waives the fee; Gālava insists
description: Viśvāmitra dismisses his devoted pupil Gālava owing no guru-dakṣiṇā, but Gālava proudly insists on paying

title: Ajāmila's repentance and liberation at Haridvāra
description: Restored to life and transformed, Ajāmila renounces all, practices bhakti-yoga at Haridvāra, and is borne to Vaikuṇṭha

title: Andhaka conquers the three worlds and lusts after Parvati
description: The mighty blind asura overruns the devas and seizes the three worlds, then beholds Parvati on Kailasa and resolves to take her, not knowing she is his mother
source: Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana

title: Śarmiṣṭhā casts Devayānī into the well
description: After a quarrel of precedence, Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into a dry well; King Yayāti rescues her by the hand, which she treats as betrothal

title: Atri-Anasuya triad birth (Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas)
description: From the chaste Anasuya, wife of sage Atri, the Trimurti take partial birth — Brahma as Soma/Candra, Vishnu as Dattatreya, and Shiva as Durvasas — anchoring the great guru-avatar Dattatreya's origin here

title: Bharata-varsha Named After King Bharata
description: The southern karma-bhumi varsha is named after King Bharata, son of Rishabha (Bhagavata) or son of Dushyanta and Shakuntala (epic tradition)

title: Birth of Dattātreya, Soma, and Durvāsā
description: Pleased by Anasūyā and restored by her, the Trimūrti are born as her sons — Soma (Brahmā-portion), Dattātreya (Viṣṇu-portion), and Durvāsā (Śiva-portion), the triple-deity avatar fused in three heads and six arms

title: Birth of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Śūrpaṇakhā
description: From the rākṣasī Kaikasī and Viśravas are born Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, the gentle Vibhīṣaṇa, and the sister Śūrpaṇakhā

title: Birth of the nine daughters and of Kapila; Kardama's renunciation
description: Devahuti bears nine daughters wed to the rishis and a son Kapila, Vishnu incarnate; Kardama then takes sannyasa

title: Birth of Vasiṣṭha and Agastya from Mitra-Varuṇa
description: The sages Vasiṣṭha and Agastya are miraculously born from the seed of Mitra-Varuṇa at the sight of the apsaras Urvaśī, Agastya being pitcher-born

title: Birth of Vishravas from Pulastya's anger
description: Slighted when Kubera attends Brahma over him, Pulastya produces the sage Vishravas from half his own being, into whom his wrath passes

title: Brahma's infatuation with Shatarupa and Shiva striking off his head
description: In a variant, Brahma is infatuated with his daughter Shatarupa, sprouts extra heads to keep her in view, and Shiva later strikes one off

title: Chhāyā curses Yama and the deception is exposed
description: Chhāyā curses Yama in anger, revealing she cannot be the true mother; Yama complains to Sūrya, who interrogates Chhāyā and uncovers the substitution

title: Churning of the Ocean of Milk (Ajita as Kurma)
description: Vishnu's avatar Ajita bears Mount Mandara as the tortoise Kurma and distributes the amrita at the devas' churning of the milk-ocean

title: Churning of Vena's Body — Birth of Niṣāda
description: From Vena's churned thigh emerges the dark hunter Niṣāda, ancestor of the forest peoples, carrying away all of Vena's accumulated sin

title: Cyavana creates Mada and wins the Aśvins their soma-share
description: Cyavana paralyzes Indra's arm and creates the giant Asura Mada to force the Aśvins' admission to the soma-cult, then distributes Mada into the four kingly vices
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5

title: Death of Vasishtha's hundred sons
description: In the feud, Vishvamitra causes king Kalmashapada, possessed by a rakshasa, to devour all of Vasishtha's hundred sons; the grieving Vasishtha attempts suicide but is preserved

title: Devouring of Śakti and Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons
description: The possessed Kalmāṣapāda eats Śakti first and then all of Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons, extinguishing the sage's line of sons

title: Dhruva granted the immovable polar seat
description: Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the Dhruva-pada, the fixed pole-star station enduring a full Kalpa, plus a long earthly reign

title: Founding of the royal lineages by Vaivasvata's sons
description: Vaivasvata Manu's sons found the great dynasties, Ikshvaku seeding the Solar line and Ila/Sudyumna seeding the Lunar line through Pururavas

title: Gods dispossessed appeal to Śiva
description: Driven from heaven, the devas petition Brahmā and Śiva, who agrees to destroy Śaṅkhacūḍa
source: Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Book IX

title: Gods petition Brahmā for a remedy
description: The dispossessed devas approach Brahmā, who reveals that only a son of Śiva, born as war-general, can slay Tāraka
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava II; Skanda Purāṇa

title: Indra names the child 'mām dhāsyati'
description: Asked who will suckle the motherless infant, Indra answers 'he shall suckle me' and feeds him nectar from his finger, giving the name Māndhātṛ

title: Jahnu drinks the entire Gaṅgā
description: Enraged at the ruined rite, Jahnu swallows the whole river in one draught by his ascetic power, undoing Bhagīratha's effort

title: King Suratha Worships the Goddess and Is Reborn as Savarni
description: King Suratha, having lost his kingdom, worships the Goddess Mahamaya/Durga in a forest hermitage alongside the merchant Samadhi and by Her boon is destined to be reborn as Savarni, son of Surya, the future 8th Manu
source: Markandeya Purana 81-93 (Devi Mahatmya / Durga Saptashati); Devi Bhagavata

title: Marriage of Atri and Anasūyā
description: Anasūyā, daughter of Kardama and Devahūti and sister of Kapila, becomes Atri's wife and the archetypal pativratā

title: Marriage of Cyavana and Sukanyā
description: To appease the wronged sage, Śaryāti bestows his young daughter Sukanyā in marriage on the aged blind ascetic Cyavana, and she devotedly serves him
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.7

title: Marriage of Jaratkāru and Manasā (Vāsuki's sister)
description: Vāsuki offers his sister—herself named Jaratkāru (later Manasā)—freely and undertakes her maintenance, fulfilling every condition, so the sage weds her to fulfil Brahmā's promise of a serpent-deliverer

title: Marriage to Vrinda
description: Jalandhara, crowned king of the asuras, weds the supremely chaste Vrinda whose pativratya makes him invincible

title: Maya builds Tripura
description: The asura-architect Maya constructs the three fortresses of gold, silver, and iron in heaven, air, and earth
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva

title: Mārkaṇḍeya Initiated into the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya Mantra
description: Foreseeing his death, Mārkaṇḍeya is initiated into (or composes) the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya mantra and devotes himself to ceaseless Shiva worship

title: Nahuṣa Covets Śacī
description: Corrupted by power, Nahuṣa lusts after Indra's queen Śacī and demands her; she takes refuge with Bṛhaspati and sets a trap-condition

title: Nārada initiates Dhruva with the Vāsudeva mantra
description: The sage Nārada tests and then instructs Dhruva, directing him to Madhuvana and bestowing the twelve-syllable mantra 'Oṃ Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya' — a canonical first-giving of the dvādaśākṣara mantra

title: Pṛthu inherits the bow Ājagava
description: In the Pṛthu-narrative, Śiva's celestial bow Ājagava descends as the royal bow inherited by Pṛthu, the first consecrated king, who uses it to compel the Earth to yield her bounty

title: Pṛthu milks the Earth-cow; origin of agriculture
description: Pṛthu chases the fugitive Earth as a cow, levels the land, and milks her of grains and herbs, whence Earth is named Pṛthvī

title: Puru and the founding of the Paurava line
description: Yayati's son Puru accepts his father's old age, founding the Paurava line from which the Kurus descend

title: Ruru gives half his lifespan to revive her
description: A messenger of the gods offers that Pramadvarā will live if Ruru surrenders half his remaining lifespan; he consents and she rises, and they wed

title: Ruru Revives Pramadvarā
description: The Bhārgava youth Ruru gives half his own lifespan to revive his betrothed killed by snakebite, then vows to slay snakes until a serpent preaches ahiṃsā

title: Shiva's Cosmic Grief-Dance
description: Maddened with sorrow, Shiva takes up Sati's charred corpse and roams the worlds in a tandava of grief that threatens to unbalance creation
source: Devi Bhagavata Purana VII.30; Kalika Purana 18

title: Svarocis rescues and marries Manorama
description: Grown Svarocis saves the maiden Manorama from a demon with mantric arrows and weds her, later marrying her two companions who teach him secret vidyas

title: Svarocis rescues Manorama and marries her
description: Grown and trained, Svarocis saves the maiden Manorama and her companions from a demon using mantric arrows, then marries her

title: The curse-backstories of Indradyumna and Hūhū revealed
description: The slain crocodile and freed elephant are revealed as the cursed king Indradyumna and gandharva Hūhū, both liberated by Viṣṇu

title: The Daksha-yajna and the insult to Shiva
description: Daksha organizes a colossal yajna deliberately omitting Shiva and Sati and, when Sati attends, reviles Shiva before the assembly as a skull-bearing cremation-ground madman
source: Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4; Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana

title: The impossible price of 800 horses
description: Irritated, Viśvāmitra demands 800 moon-white horses each with a single black ear (śyāmakarṇa) as fee

title: The Kapila-gita — theistic Sankhya taught to Devahuti
description: Kapila delivers a nine-chapter discourse on bhakti-yoga, the tattvas subordinated to Īśvara, aṣṭāṅga-yoga meditating on Viṣṇu's form, grades of devotion, Kāla, and the wheel of rebirth

title: The Māṇḍavya curse on Yama
description: Wrongly impaled and surviving, the sage Māṇḍavya curses Yama to be born a man, a Śūdra woman's son, for unjustly punishing a child's act — fulfilled as Vidura

title: The phantom-cow ruse (māyā-dhenu)
description: An illusory dying cow enters Gautama's field and collapses dead when he shoos it, framing him for go-hatyā (cow-slaughter)
actors: the māyā-cow (variant: Gaṇeśa as the cow)

title: The Prachetasas and Daksha's re-creation
description: The ten Prachetasa sons emerge from austerity in the waters and, with Daksha, repopulate the world in the secondary creation

title: The Rishabha-gita teaching to his sons
description: Before renouncing, Rishabha delivers a celebrated discourse that the body is meant for tapas and self-realization, not sense gratification, and that sadhu-sanga liberates

title: Ugrashravas re-tells the Mahabharata at Naimisha (outermost frame)
description: Arriving from Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, Ugrashravas recites the entire Mahabharata to Shaunaka's sages, forming the epic's outermost narrative layer

title: Vena slain and Prithu churned forth
description: The tyrant Vena is slain by the rishis, who churn from his body the first righteous king Prithu, a Vishnu amshavatara who milks the Earth (Prithvi) of grain and becomes the model cakravartin

title: Vishnu's boon and the fixing of the Pole Star
description: Vishnu grants Dhruva the immovable celestial Dhruva-loka, making the North Star the model bhakta

title: Vishnu slays Kalanemi and Indra slays Virochana
description: In the Tarakamaya fighting Vishnu kills the asura Kalanemi and Indra kills Virochana, son of Prahlada

title: Viṣṇu declares 'I am subject to My devotees'
description: Viṣṇu refuses to recall the discus, uttering the bhakta-vātsalya verse and sending Durvāsā back to beg Ambarīṣa's pardon

title: Viṣṇu rescues Gajendra and slays the crocodile
description: Hearing the unsectarian cry, Viṣṇu flies on Garuḍa to the lake, lifts the elephant, and severs the crocodile's head with his Sudarśana Cakra, liberating Gajendra

title: Viṣṇu Tests Kuru and Grants the Liberation-Boon
description: Viṣṇu tests Kuru by severing his limbs and head; satisfied, he grants that the land be named Kurukṣetra forever and that bathing, dying, or being dusted by it confers mokṣa

title: Yajña assumes the office of Indra of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara
description: The Viṣṇu-aṃśa Yajña takes the rotating throne of Indra/king of the devas for the first Manvantara — a rare case of the deva-kingship being held by an incarnation of Viṣṇu

title: Agastya curses King Indradyumna to be an elephant
description: The backstory revealed: the Pāṇḍya king Indradyumna, absorbed in a silent vow, failed to honor the sage Agastya, who cursed him to be reborn as a dull elephant — the prior birth of Gajendra

title: Agastya Curses Nahuṣa to Become a Python
description: Yoking the Saptarṣis to his palanquin and kicking Agastya while crying 'sarpa, sarpa,' Nahuṣa is cursed to fall from heaven as a python
source: Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 17; Vana Parva 178; Bhagavata 6.13

title: Ajita as Kurma at the churning
description: In the Bhagavata frame the avatar Ajita of this manvantara bears Mount Mandara as the tortoise Kurma and distributes the amrita at the devas' churning of the ocean

title: Ambarīṣa prays the Sudarśana to spare Durvāsā
description: The wronged king prays to the discus to spare his persecutor; the Sudarśana relents and the two reconcile over a feast

title: Anasūyā halts the river by her vow
description: By the power of her chastity-vow Anasūyā stops a river's flow (or ends a drought), proving satya-saṃkalpa overrides nature

title: Asura misrule
description: After a thousand years the empowered asuras abandon dharma and oppress the worlds, provoking the gods

title: Aśvins restore Cyavana's youth
description: The Aśvins, after Sukanyā refuses their seduction, enter a magical lake with Cyavana so all three emerge as identical youths; Sukanyā chooses rightly and Cyavana is restored to youth, beauty, and sight
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 124; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.8–13; Ṛgveda 1.116–117

title: Birth of Pṛthu from Vena's Arms
description: From Vena's purified arms the sages draw forth the radiant Pṛthu (with his queen Arci), bearing the cakra and lotus marks of a Viṣṇu aṃśa-avatāra

title: Birth of Yajna and Dakshina to Akuti
description: Manu's daughter Akuti marries rishi Ruci and bears twins Yajna (the era's Indra and a Vishnu amsa) and Dakshina, who becomes Yajna's wife; their sons are the twelve Yama gods

title: Brahma halts the war and restores Tara
description: Facing cosmic ruin, Brahma intervenes and compels Soma to surrender Tara, who is returned to Brihaspati already pregnant

title: Budha weds Ilā and founds the Lunar Dynasty
description: Budha weds Ilā and fathers Pururavas, first king of the Candravaṃśa, so the adulterous Tārā union seeds an entire royal lineage

title: Daksha's curse on Chandra and the Moon's waxing and waning
description: Chandra marries the 27 Nakshatras but favors Rohini, so Daksha curses him to waste away; the relented cyclic curse becomes the waxing and waning of the Moon

title: Dattātreya teaches the 24 gurus to King Yadu
description: The avadhūta Dattātreya answers King Yadu by recounting how he took 24 gurus from the natural world — earth, wind, python, courtesan Piṅgalā, spider, wasp and more — each yielding one lesson, freeing Yadu of attachment

title: Devahuti's liberation and Kapila's departure
description: Devahūti takes up bhakti-yoga, attains realization at the Sarasvatī (Siddhapada), and Kapila departs north-east to abide in samādhi by the sea

title: Dhruva's great penance suffocates the worlds
description: Through six months of ever-intensifying fasting and breath-suspension on one leg, Dhruva's concentrated heat chokes the three worlds, prompting the alarmed gods to appeal to Viṣṇu

title: Dhruva's war on the Yakṣas and final ascent
description: Avenging his slain brother, Dhruva wars on Alakā until Manu stays his wrath; in old age he ascends to Dhruva-loka with his mother Sunīti

title: Dhruva's war with the Yakshas
description: After his brother Uttama is slain, Dhruva wars on the Yakshas until Svayambhuva Manu halts him, then ascends a celestial vehicle

title: Embassy to Shiva and outbreak of war
description: Andhaka sends an emissary (in some texts Prahlada, who counsels against it) demanding the goddess; refused, he marches on Kailasa and the deva-asura war begins

title: Gajendra-moksha (Hari rescues the elephant-king)
description: In the Tamasa manvantara the avatar Hari rescues the elephant-king Gajendra from the crocodile, a variant placement of the Gajendra-moksha

title: Garuḍa carries Gālava in search of horses
description: After Gālava despairs, Garuḍa appears and flies him across the directions, advising him to seek the generous emperor Yayāti

title: Gender-shift of Ila/Sudyumna
description: Vaivasvata's offspring Ila/Sudyumna, born female, becomes male and alternates gender, a major lineage variant seeding the Chandravamsha

title: Grievance over the Churning and war on the devas
description: Jalandhara demands return of the ocean's stolen treasures and routs Indra and the gods, seizing the three worlds

title: Kaca Steals the Sañjīvanī Vidyā
description: The deva youth Kaca infiltrates Śukrācārya, is killed thrice and revived, learns the resurrection science from within Śukra's belly, then is cursed by the rejected Devayānī

title: Killing of the brāhmaṇa couple and the wife's counter-curse
description: The rākṣasa-king devours a forest brāhmaṇa (or serves human flesh as alms); the bereaved wife curses him to die instantly if he ever unites with a woman, blocking procreation
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.9; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa

title: Kāma sent and burned (Kāma-dahana)
description: Indra sends Kāmadeva to rouse the ascetic Śiva's desire; Śiva opens his third eye and incinerates Kāma to ash

title: Kubera's three rakshasis bear the demon clan
description: To placate the angry Vishravas, Kubera sends three rakshasa women as wives, from whom spring Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Khara, Shurpanakha, and Vibhishana

title: Matsya rescues Vaivasvata Manu at the manvantara junction
description: At the Chakshusha-Vaivasvata sandhya, Vishnu's fish-avatar rescues Vaivasvata Manu from the great flood, ushering in the current age

title: Māndhātṛ's universal conquest and dharmic reign
description: Māndhātṛ becomes cakravartin of the seven continents, earns the epithet Trasaddasyu, and his just digvijaya rule becomes the proverbial benchmark of kingship
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.39–41; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.2; Mahābhārata Droṇa Parva

title: Pṛthu's aśvamedhas and Indra's theft of the horse
description: Pṛthu's hundred horse-sacrifices threaten Indra, who repeatedly steals the horse until Brahmā and Viṣṇu intervene and Pṛthu forgives him

title: Rishabha's renunciation and avadhuta wandering
description: Rishabha crowns Bharata, abandons his kingdom, and wanders as a naked avadhuta behaving like a madman to escape social entanglement

title: Ruru's vow to slay all serpents
description: Grief turned to hatred, Ruru vows to kill every snake he meets and roams the forests slaughtering venomous and harmless serpents alike

title: Rāvaṇa wins Brahmā's boon of invulnerability
description: After extreme penance offering his ten heads, Rāvaṇa gains Brahmā's boon of invulnerability to all divine and demonic beings, disdaining protection from men and monkeys — the loophole that dooms him

title: Shantanu weds Ganga; the drowning of the Vasus
description: King Shantanu weds Ganga, who drowns her first seven sons (the cursed Vasus) and surrenders the eighth, Devavrata, when he breaks his vow

title: Svarocis weds his three wives and receives the secret vidyas
description: Svarocis weds Manorama's two companions Vibhavari and Kalavati, who impart esoteric knowledge including the secret Padmini Vidya

title: The abrupt departure and the 'asti' prophecy
description: When Manasā wakes the sleeping Jaratkāru to save his sunset prayers, he construes it as displeasure and leaves, but first declares a blazing son already lives in her womb—naming him Āstīka

title: The Bhagavata's opening question at the dawn of Kali
description: Troubled by the onset of Kali Yuga, the Naimisha sages ask Suta for the essence of scripture and receive the Bhagavata he heard from Shuka

title: The false expiation demanded
description: The conspiring sages tell Gautama his sin can be cleared only by bringing the Gaṅgā down to Brahmagiri — an impossible task meant to expel him

title: The gods propitiate Jahnu
description: Devas, ṛṣis and Bhagīratha entreat the angry sage to release the river, asking him to accept her as his daughter

title: The Kapilopadesha (Devahuti-putra Gita) at Bindu-sarovara
description: Kapila expounds theistic Samkhya and bhakti-yoga to his mother Devahuti at the lake, and she attains moksha

title: The Pushkara yajna and Savitri's curse on Brahma
description: At Brahma's yajna at Pushkara, the late Savitri arrives to find Brahma has wed the milkmaid Gayatri in her seat and curses Brahma to be worshipped almost nowhere, explaining the near-absence of Brahma temples

title: Trishanku's heaven
description: When Vasishtha refuses to send king Trishanku bodily to heaven, Vishvamitra does so by tapas; Indra hurls him back and Vishvamitra freezes him mid-fall and begins building a counter-heaven and a second set of stars

title: Vishnu's Sudarshana Dismembers Sati
description: To free Shiva and restore order, Vishnu severs Sati's corpse piece by piece with his discus; each falling part sanctifies a spot and becomes a Shakti Pitha
source: Devi Bhagavata Purana; Pithanirnaya / Tantra Cudamani

title: Viṣṇu begs away the Viṣṇu-Kavaca
description: Viṣṇu, disguised as an old brāhmaṇa mendicant, begs Śaṅkhacūḍa to give the Viṣṇu-Kavaca as alms, stripping his first protection

title: Viśvakarmā trims the Sun on the cosmic lathe
description: To win Sañjñā back, Sūrya submits to his father-in-law Viśvakarmā/Tvaṣṭṛ, who grinds away one-eighth of his unbearable radiance on a cosmic lathe to make him gentler
source: Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.2

title: Yajña leads the Yāmas to slay the Rākṣasas assailing Manu's sacrifice
description: When hunger-maddened Rākṣasas attack to devour Svāyambhuva Manu and despoil his cosmic yajña, Viṣṇu-as-Yajña takes up arms with his sons the Yāmas and drives them off, defending the sacrifice he embodies

title: Yama Comes for Mārkaṇḍeya
description: On the appointed day Yama arrives to claim the boy, who clings to a Shiva-liṅga in unbroken worship

title: Austerity and the Trimūrti boon
description: Atri and Anasūyā perform tapas for a son equal to the Supreme; the Lord grants that portions of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva will be born to them

title: Aṣṭāvakra Defeats Bandin at Janaka's Court
description: Born crooked from a womb-curse, the boy Aṣṭāvakra defeats the philosopher Bandin in debate, frees those he drowned and recovers his father, later being straightened in a sacred river

title: Avatar Vibhu instructs the ascetics
description: Vishnu's avatar Vibhu, born to Vedashiras and Tushita, lives a lifelong celibate and instructs 88,000 ascetics in self-control

title: Birth and rearing of Āstīka
description: Āstīka is born half-brāhmaṇa, half-nāga, reared among the serpents and schooled in the Vedas by Cyavana, uniquely fit to mediate between brahminical rite and the nāgas

title: Birth of Garuda and theft of the Amrita
description: Garuda is born of Vinata, raids heaven to steal the amrita to ransom his enslaved mother, and pacts with Vishnu (as mount) and Indra (Nagas as food)

title: Birth of Kapila and the Devahuti-putra Gita
description: Devahuti marries Prajapati Kardama and bears Kapila, the Samkhya teacher and Vishnu avatara, who delivers the Devahuti-putra Gita to his mother

title: Birth of the five sons of Yayāti
description: Devayānī bears Yadu and Turvaśu while Śarmiṣṭhā, secretly fathered by Yayāti, bears Druhyu, Anu and Pūru, the sons whose lines split the Lunar dynasty

title: Birth of Virabhadra and Bhadrakali
description: Learning of Sati's death, Shiva dashes a lock of his matted hair to the ground, from which spring the wrathful warrior Virabhadra and the fierce goddess Bhadrakali to avenge her
source: Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana; Linga Purana

title: Brahma's wheel founds the Naimisha-kshetra (nemi origin)
description: Seeking a sin-free sacrifice ground, the rishis follow Brahma's mind-made wheel whose rim (nemi) sinks at this spot, naming the forest Naimisha and opening the Chakra-tirtha

title: Chandra's abduction of Tara and the Tarakamaya war
description: Chandra abducts Brihaspati's wife Tara, sparking the Tarakamaya war between devas and asuras settled by Brahma; Tara bears Budha, founding the Chandravamsha

title: Coronation of Pṛthu — First Consecrated King
description: The sages and gods crown Pṛthu the first anointed king and cakravartin, the bardic Sūta and Māgadha appear, and the devas endow him with divine emblems
source: Bhagavata Purana 4.15; Vishnu Purana 1.13; Shatapatha Brahmana 3.5.4

title: Cyavana paralyzes Indra's arm
description: At Śaryāti's soma-sacrifice Cyavana offers the Aśvins a soma-cup against Indra's objection, and when Indra raises his vajra the sage withers and freezes Indra's arm in mid-air

title: Dattātreya grants boons to Kārtavīrya Arjuna
description: As divine teacher Dattātreya imparts brahmavidyā and grants boons to the thousand-armed Haihaya king Kārtavīrya Arjuna, and instructs Alarka and Prahlāda

title: Devala curses the gandharva Hūhū to be a crocodile
description: The gandharva Hūhū pulled the bathing sage Devala's leg in sport and was cursed to become a crocodile, with the boon that Viṣṇu himself would one day slay and release him — the prior birth of the crocodile

title: Embassy to Shiva and lust for Parvati
description: Jalandhara (via Rahu) demands Parvati from Shiva; Shiva's fury births a devouring being and war becomes inevitable

title: Establishment of the Shakti Pithas
description: At each site where a body part or ornament of Sati fell, a triad is fixed of the fallen anga, a presiding Devi, and her guardian Bhairava, founding the Shakta pilgrimage network

title: Gaṅgā released and named Jāhnavī
description: Jahnu releases the river from his ear (or thigh, in variants), so she is thereafter called Jāhnavī, 'daughter of Jahnu'

title: Gautama's tapas and Śiva's boon
description: Gautama undertakes fierce penance to Śiva at Tryambak/Brahmagiri; Śiva appears with Pārvatī and offers a boon

title: Impalement on the trishula and the multiplying blood
description: Shiva transfixes Andhaka on his trident, but every drop of blood that falls spawns a full-grown Andhaka-clone, filling the field with duplicates
source: Matsya Purana; Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Kurma Purana

title: Indra Restored to the Throne
description: With the usurper fallen, Indra is purified of brahmahatyā and returns to his throne

title: Installation of Vaivasvata Manu (manvantara transition)
description: At the close of the Chakshusha age's twilight, a partial dissolution installs Vaivasvata Manu (son of Vivasvan-Surya) as the seventh and current Manu, beginning our manvantara

title: Kimpuruṣa Granted the Kimpuruṣa-varṣa
description: Kimpuruṣa, son of Agnīdhra by the apsarā Pūrvacitti, becomes the eponymous king-ancestor of the kimpuruṣas and is granted the Kimpuruṣa-varṣa as his hereditary portion

title: Kumbhakarṇa's boon twisted to sleep
description: Asking for destruction of the gods, Kumbhakarṇa is made by Sarasvatī to say 'sleep' instead, gaining his curse of months-long sleep

title: Māndhātṛ's marriage and progeny
description: Māndhātṛ weds Bindumatī and fathers Purukutsa, Mucukunda, Ambarīṣa, and fifty daughters

title: Priyavrata's chariot-furrows form the seven oceans and continents
description: Priyavrata circles the Earth seven times in his chariot; the wheel-ruts carve the seven oceans and seven dvipas

title: Pārvatī's tapas and the divine wedding
description: Pārvatī (Satī reborn) wins Śiva by her own austerity and his disguised test, and the two are wed at Himavān's palace

title: Ravana's boon of invulnerability with the man-and-monkey loophole
description: Ravana wins from Brahma immunity from gods, gandharvas, yakshas, and rakshasas but proudly omits men and monkeys, the loophole that necessitates Vishnu's human incarnation

title: Rediscovery and re-establishment of worship (Pururavā)
description: King Pururavā of the lunar line rediscovers the buried composite icon, re-establishes worship, and is commanded to keep it coated in sandalwood

title: Rishabha's death by forest fire
description: Wandering the Kutakachala region, Rishabha's austerity-emaciated body is consumed by a bamboo-friction wildfire as he quits the body absorbed in the Self

title: Sagara's Asvamedha and the stolen horse
description: King Sagara of Ayodhyā performs the horse-sacrifice; Indra steals the horse and tethers it beside the meditating Kapila in the netherworld

title: Shiva Slays Yama as Kālāntaka
description: When Yama's noose falls around the liṅga, Shiva bursts forth and strikes down Death, earning the epithets Kālāntaka and Mṛtyuñjaya

title: Tara's confession of Budha's paternity
description: With both Soma and Brihaspati claiming the luminous child, Brahma questions Tara, who admits the son is Soma's

title: The curse-water and the 'spotted-foot' naming
description: Stayed by Queen Madayantī from cursing the brāhmaṇa, Mitrasaha pours the curse-charged water on his own feet, scorching them black and earning the name Kalmāṣapāda

title: The doe and the birth of Svarochisha Manu
description: A doe appeals to Svarocis for mercy and asks him to embrace her; when he does she conceives and instantly delivers Svarochisha Manu amid celestial rejoicing and a rain of flowers

title: The dundubha's sermon on ahiṃsā
description: A non-venomous dundubha snake stops Ruru's sword and teaches that non-injury (ahiṃsā) is the brāhmaṇa's highest dharma

title: The solar off-cuts forged into divine weapons
description: The shorn solar brilliance is forged by Viśvakarmā into the great weapons of the gods, including Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra, Śiva's Triśūla, and Kārttikeya's spear

title: Vaikuntha manifests the realm Vaikuntha
description: In the Raivata manvantara the avatar Vaikuntha, born of Vikuntha, manifests Vishnu's abode Vaikuntha for the pleasure of the goddess Ramaa

title: Viṣṇu as Māyāmoha corrupts the asuras
description: Viṣṇu emanates a heretic preacher who seduces the Tripura asuras from Vedic dharma, stripping their protection
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa

title: Viṣṇu impersonates Śaṅkhacūḍa to break Tulasī's vow
description: Viṣṇu assumes Śaṅkhacūḍa's exact form and approaches Tulasī as her husband, breaking her chastity-vow and dissolving the invincibility lock
source: Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Book IX

title: Viṣṇu's darśana and the Dhruva-stuti
description: Viṣṇu manifests to the unwavering child and, touching Dhruva's cheek with his conch, floods him with Vedic eloquence so he pours forth the celebrated Dhruva-stuti hymn

title: Vrinda becomes Tulsi, ever-wed to Vishnu
description: Vishnu breaks the chastity of Vrinda (wife of the asura Jalandhara) by taking her husband's form, breaking Jalandhara's invincibility; the transformed Vrinda becomes the Tulsi plant eternally married to Vishnu, re-enacted as Tulsi Vivah

title: Yayāti gives his daughter Mādhavī
description: Lacking the horses, Yayāti gives Gālava his daughter Mādhavī, who regains her virginity after each childbirth, as renewable bride-wealth

title: Ṛṣabhanātha Attains Nirvāṇa on Aṣṭāpada (Kailāsa)
description: In Jain tradition the first Tīrthaṅkara Ṛṣabhanātha (Ādinātha) attains nirvāṇa/mokṣa on Kailāsa (Aṣṭāpada), the foundational liberation-site of Jainism

title: Assembly of Śiva's cosmic chariot
description: The pantheon becomes Śiva's weapon-system: Earth the chariot, Sun/Moon wheels, Vedas horses, Brahmā charioteer, Meru bow, Viṣṇu arrow
source: Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva (8.24); Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa

title: Birth and naming of Budha
description: Soma names the boy Budha (Mercury) and takes him to his realm; Budha is the founder of the Lunar dynasty

title: Birth of Durvasa as Shiva's portion
description: Durvasa is born of Atri and Anasuya as the Rudra-portion, the short-tempered sage whose curses drive major plots

title: Birth of Vaivasvata Manu and the Surya cycle
description: Vivasvat marries Samjna/Chaya, the Sun's excess radiance is trimmed by Vishvakarman, and the Solar dynasty descends through Vaivasvata Manu, opening the present age

title: Boon of Eternal Deathlessness to Mārkaṇḍeya
description: Shiva blesses Mārkaṇḍeya to remain eternally sixteen and never die, granting him chiranjīvi status to outlive kalpas

title: Both Gajendra and Hūhū liberated
description: The single stroke of the Sudarśana liberates both beings: Hūhū regains his gandharva form, and Gajendra/Indradyumna is granted a divine form (sārūpya) and taken to Vaikuṇṭha

title: Burning of Sagara's 60,000 sons
description: Sagara's sixty thousand sons dig up the earth, wrongly accuse the meditating Kapila of theft, and are reduced to ash on the spot
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8.11–13; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 40; Mahābhārata Vana Parva

title: Conception and birth of Skanda-Kārttikeya
description: Śiva's unbearable seed is borne by Agni and Gaṅgā to a reed-bed, where the Kṛttikās nurse the six-faced infant Skanda
source: Mahābhārata (Śalya-parvan); Skanda Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava

title: Creation of the Asura Mada
description: Cyavana generates from his ascetic energy a colossal Asura, Mada ('Intoxication'), with vast jaws and fangs, who advances to devour Indra and the worlds

title: Destruction of the Daksha-yajna and beheading of Daksha
description: Virabhadra, Bhadrakali and Shiva's hordes storm the yajna, maim the assembled gods and priests, and Virabhadra decapitates Daksha, his head thrown into the fire
source: Bhagavata Purana IV.5; Vayu Purana; Linga Purana

title: Durga armed by the devas for the Mahishasura war (Ayudha Puja charter)
description: The devas each yield their weapon to arm Durga for her battle with Mahishasura, the charter for worshipping weapons and tools as forms of the Goddess on Maha Navami

title: Śiva slays Śaṅkhacūḍa with the triśūla
description: With both protections gone, Śiva strikes down Śaṅkhacūḍa with his trident, reducing him to ash; his bones become the world's conches

title: Jalandhara's impersonation of Shiva to seize Parvati
description: Jalandhara takes Shiva's form to deceive Parvati, who detects the fraud and incites Vishnu to repay it on Vrinda

title: Kuśika line threaded through Jahnu
description: The Bhāgavata routes the Kuśika/Gādhi line through Jahnu's descendants, making him the junction linking the Kuru and Kuśika branches

title: Loan to Haryaśva of Ayodhyā
description: King Haryaśva begets Vasumanas on Mādhavī, pays 200 śyāmakarṇa horses, and returns her virgin

title: Matsya flood at the Chakshusha-Vaivasvata junction
description: Vishnu's fish-avatar rescues Vaivasvata Manu in the deluge that closes the Chakshusha age and ushers in our manvantara (text-dependent boundary placement)

title: Menaka breaks Vishvamitra's penance and bears Shakuntala
description: The apsara Menaka breaks Vishvamitra's penance, and he fathers Shakuntala by her

title: Mithilā as Śakti Pīṭha (Satī's left shoulder)
description: During Śiva's grief-wandering with Satī's corpse, her left shoulder falls at Mithilā, fixing the Śakti Umā and Bhairava Mahodara
source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Tantra Cūḍāmaṇi / Pīṭhanirṇaya

title: Nārada provokes the goddesses
description: Nārada praises Anasūyā as the most chaste woman alive, stinging Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, and Pārvatī into sending their husbands to test her

title: Prasuti's daughters become mothers of cosmos and dharma
description: Prasuti marries the first Daksha and bears daughters including Sati, Aditi, Diti, Danu and the personified virtues, who become mothers of the cosmos and dharma

title: Pṛthu Pursues and Milks the Earth-Cow
description: When the famine-stricken Earth withholds all seed, Pṛthu pursues her as a fleeing cow, levels the mountains, and milks her of all grains, originating agriculture; she is named Pṛthvī

title: Rebirth of Sati as Parvati
description: Sati is reborn as Parvati, daughter of the mountain-king Himavan, and rewins Shiva, closing the loop of the destroyed first marriage

title: Rishabha as first Tirthankara (Jain account)
description: In Jain tradition Rishabhanatha/Adinatha, born to Nabhi and Marudevi at Ayodhya, founds civilization, teaches the six livelihoods, fathers a hundred sons including Bharata and Bahubali

title: Rāvaṇa seizes Laṅkā from Kubera
description: On Sumālī's urging Rāvaṇa demands and takes Laṅkā and the Puṣpaka chariot by force; Kubera withdraws to Mount Kailāsa

title: Sahasrapāt revealed and released from his curse
description: The dundubha discloses he is the sage Sahasrapāt, cursed into snake-form by Khagama for a jest, and is freed on meeting Ruru, resuming his ṛṣi body

title: Sarasvati cursed to flow with blood (Sthanu-tirtha)
description: Caught between the feuding sages, Sarasvati warns Vasishtha instead of bringing him to be killed and is cursed by Vishvamitra to flow with blood; demons drink and bathe in her waters until sages purify her as Aruna and free the demons to heaven

title: Satī's throat falls at Amarnāth
description: In the Dakṣa-yajña dismemberment cycle, Satī's throat falls here, fixing the Śakti Pīṭha of Mahāmāyā with Bhairava Trisandhyeśvara
source: Tantra Cūḍāmaṇi / Pīṭhanirṇaya (51 Śakti Pīṭha list)

title: Sūrya and Sañjñā reunite as stallion and mare, begetting the Aśvins
description: Gentled, Sūrya finds Sañjñā in mare-form and unites with her as a stallion, producing the horse-faced Aśvins (and Revanta), after which she returns as his full wife

title: Āstīka halts Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice
description: At the sarpa-satra Āstīka wins a boon from Janamejaya and asks that the rite cease, saving Takṣaka in mid-air and the surviving serpents—the same sattra at which the Mahābhārata is first recited
actors: Āstīka; Janamejaya; Takṣaka; Vāsuki and the nāgas; Vaiśampāyana

title: Summoning of the Matrikas/Bhairavas to drink the blood
description: Shiva (or the Devi) emanates the Saptamatrika and Bhairava blood-drinkers to lap every drop before it touches the ground, halting the multiplication
source: Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana; Vamana Purana; Linga Purana

title: The descent of the Gautamī Gaṅgā (Godāvarī)
description: Śiva looses a strand of Gaṅgā from his locks at Brahmagiri; she flows out as the Gautamī Gaṅgā / Godāvarī, washing away the cow-sin and remaining as the Dakṣiṇa Gaṅgā

title: The Nimisha demons slain in a wink (alternate name-legend)
description: A horde of demons is destroyed 'in an instant' (nimisha) at the site, yielding the alternate etymology of Naimisha

title: The Saubhari parable — sage weds the fifty daughters
description: The aged sage Saubhari, desire awoken, makes himself youthful and weds all fifty of Māndhātṛ's daughters, builds palaces of pleasure, then renounces it all in disillusion

title: The slaying of the tyrant Vena
description: Vena bans all sacrifice and claims to be Hari himself; the sages kill him with kusha-grass blades and hum-mantras

title: Śukra curses Yayāti with old age
description: Learning the broken oath, Śukra curses Yayāti to instant decrepit old age, granting only the loophole that he may exchange it for a willing person's youth

title: Uttaṅka and Madayantī's earrings
description: In his man-eating state Saudāsa grants the sage Uttaṅka leave to fetch Queen Madayantī's celestial earrings before being eaten

title: Vibhu instructs 88,000 ascetics
description: The avatara Vibhu, born to the sage Vedashiras and Tushita, lives as a lifelong brahmacarin and instructs 88,000 ascetics in self-control and austerity

title: Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the polar seat
description: Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the immovable celestial station Dhruva-loka above the saptarṣi, enduring a full Kalpa untouched by pralaya, and decrees he will first rule the earth for 36,000 years

title: Yavakrī's Pride and Death
description: Yavakrī wins Vedic knowledge from Indra by extreme tapas, grows arrogant, molests Raibhya's daughter-in-law, and is slain by a rākṣasa conjured from Raibhya's matted lock

title: All Beings Milk the Earth-Cow
description: After Pṛthu, every class of being in turn milks the Earth-cow with its own calf and vessel, each drawing the boon proper to its nature

title: Amsuman recovers the horse and learns of Ganga
description: Sagara's grandson Aṃśumān reverently approaches Kapila, recovers the horse, and is told only the heavenly Gaṅgā can liberate the ashes

title: Anasuya turns the Trimurti into infants
description: To test her chastity the Trimurti come disguised as mendicants demanding to be fed while she is nude; Anasuya turns them into three infants, and they are reborn as her sons Dattatreya, Soma, and Durvasa

title: Aśvins admitted to the soma-cult
description: Faced with annihilation by Mada, Indra relents and concedes the Aśvins their rightful share of soma, ending their exclusion forever — the etiological climax of the tale
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.18

title: Bahubali's duel with Bharata and renunciation (Jain)
description: Rishabha's eldest son Bharata becomes the first cakravartin while his second son Bahubali renounces after a duel with Bharata and attains kevala-jnana

title: Budha fathers Pururavas
description: Budha marries Ila, the gender-changing offspring of Vaivasvata Manu, and fathers Pururavas, the first king of the Chandravamsha

title: Budha weds Ila
description: Budha marries Ila, the gender-shifting child of Vaivasvata Manu, the dynastic hinge of the Lunar line

title: Daksa's sacrifice and Sati's self-immolation
description: Sati immolates herself at Daksa's sacrifice over the insult to Siva, rupturing the relationship between Daksa and Siva

title: Daksha revived with a goat's head
description: Pacified by the supplicating gods, Shiva restores the maimed deities and brings Daksha back to life fitted with the head of the sacrificial goat, who becomes his devotee
source: Bhagavata Purana IV.6-7; Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana

title: Death of Māndhātṛ at the hands of Lavaṇāsura
description: In the Rāma-cycle backstory tradition, the world-conqueror Māndhātṛ is slain by the asura Lavaṇa wielding Śiva's invincible trident
source: Uttara-rāmāyaṇa / Padma Purāṇa traditions; Mahābhārata allusions

title: Death of Uttama and Suruci by Yakṣas
description: During Dhruva's reign his half-brother Uttama is slain by a Yakṣa while hunting in the Himālaya, and the grieving Suruci who goes searching is also killed

title: Grihapati wins lordship over death
description: Born to the brahmin Vishvanara, threatened by death-by-lightning at twelve, Grihapati's worship of Shiva wins him lordship of all directions and the fire-god's domain

title: Kaca steals the Mritasanjivani mantra
description: Brihaspati's son Kaca infiltrates Shukracharya's school to steal the death-reviving mantra, and mutual curses doom Devayani to a kshatriya marriage

title: Loan to Divodāsa of Kāśi
description: King Divodāsa of Kāśi begets Pratardana on Mādhavī and pays 200 horses

title: Priyavrata takes up kingship
description: The reluctant ascetic Priyavrata is persuaded by Brahma to take up kingship, marries Kamya, and fathers ten sons and two daughters, founding dynasties

title: Prolonged impalement and Andhaka's penitent redemption
description: Held aloft on the trident for a vast span until drained, the humbled Andhaka perceives Shiva's majesty, praises him with a hymn, and begs forgiveness
source: Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana

title: Pūru gives his youth; elder sons cursed
description: The four elder sons refuse and are cursed to lesser fates, while the youngest Pūru gladly takes his father's old age and lends his youth

title: Ruru renounces his vow
description: Chastened, Ruru abandons his slaughter of serpents and embraces the gentleness proper to a brāhmaṇa

title: Rāvaṇa pinned under Kailāsa and named by Śiva
description: Lifting Mount Kailāsa in pride, Rāvaṇa is pinned by Śiva's toe and howls for a thousand years until Śiva releases him, names him Rāvaṇa, and gives him the sword Candrahāsa

title: Sati's body-part falls — the Naimisha Shakti Pitha
description: In the Daksha-yajna dismemberment a part of Sati (upper lip / heart-portion) falls here, fixing Devi Lingadharini (Lalita) and Bhairava as the resident Shakti Pitha
source: Devi Bhagavata Purana VII; Tantra Chudamani (Pithanirnaya); Shiva Purana

title: Skanda consecrated senāpati
description: The gods anoint the days-old Skanda as commander of the divine army, fulfilling the boon's slayer-clause

title: The binding of the reluctant river
description: The released Gaṅgā tries to flee or vanish underground; Gautama/Śiva binds her with darbha grass to flow on, explaining her interrupted spring-fed emergence (Kuśāvarta as ritual source)

title: The single arrow burns Tripura
description: At the rare alignment Śiva looses one Viṣṇu-arrow incinerating all three cities and their asuras at once
source: Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva; Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa

title: Trimūrti's chastity-test and the infants miracle
description: Disguised mendicants demand Anasūyā serve them naked; she turns the three gods into infants and serves them sinlessly

title: Vasiṣṭha releases the king from possession
description: Refusing vengeance for his slain sons, Vasiṣṭha sprinkles consecrated water on the king, expelling the rākṣasa after twelve years and restoring his mind and kingship
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4

title: Vishnu impersonates Jalandhara and breaks Vrinda's vow
description: Vishnu conjures a vision of Jalandhara's death, then takes his form so the embrace breaks Vrinda's pativratya

title: Yamī proposes union to Yama
description: In the Ṛgvedic dialogue-hymn Yamī proposes incestuous union to her twin Yama, who refuses on grounds of dharma

title: Andhaka transformed into the gana Bhringi
description: Moved by his devotion, Shiva grants Andhaka liberation through service, making him a leader of his ganas, identified in Shaiva tradition with the emaciated devotee Bhringi

title: Bhārgava lineage transmitted to Śaunaka
description: Through Pramadvarā, Ruru fathers Śunaka, ancestor of Śaunaka, the sattra-patron at whose recitation the Mahābhārata is told

title: Bhrigu kicks Vishnu
description: Tasked with judging which of the Trimurti is supreme, Bhrigu kicks the sleeping Vishnu in the chest, who responds by gently massaging his foot, winning the test as most forbearing and originating Vishnu's Shrivatsa mark

title: Birth of Pururavas
description: From Budha and Ila is born Pururavas, first sovereign of the Chandravamsha (Lunar dynasty)

title: Dadhichi gives his bones at the kshetra (Misrikh)
description: At the twin site Misrikh within the Naimisha-kshetra, the sage Dadhichi surrenders his bones to forge the Vajra that slays Vritra

title: Daksha's Sacrifice and Sati's Self-immolation
description: Daksha insults Shiva, Sati self-immolates, Virabhadra wrecks the yajna, and Daksha is restored with a goat's head

title: Dhruva's war on the Yakṣa city Alakā
description: Enraged at Uttama's death, Dhruva marches on the Yakṣa city Alakāpurī and slaughters them with celestial weapons until his grandfather Svāyambhuva Manu stays his hand against killing innocents

title: Dhruva wins the pole-star station
description: The child-prince Dhruva performs austerity, wins Viṣṇu's vision, and is granted the immovable pole-star station (Dhruva-loka)

title: Distribution of Mada into the four vices
description: Having won his point, Cyavana dissolves Mada and parcels 'Intoxication' out among drink, women, dice, and hunting — the origin of the four kingly vices

title: Goddesses' plea and the boon to be born as sons
description: The three goddesses beg back their husbands; Anasūyā restores them and the pleased Trimūrti grant they will be born as her sons

title: Indra Steals Pṛthu's Sacrificial Horse
description: To prevent Pṛthu's hundredth aśvamedha from unseating him, Indra repeatedly steals the sacrificial horse in heretic disguise until Brahmā and Viṣṇu intervene and Pṛthu forgives him

title: Śiva remains as Tryambakeśvar Jyotirliṅga
description: Śiva stays at the Godāvarī's source as the three-faced (Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva) Tryambakeśvar Jyotirliṅga, 'Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautamī.'

title: Loan to Uśīnara of the Bhojas
description: King Uśīnara begets Śibi on Mādhavī and pays 200 horses; only 600 horses are gathered, with 200 un-findable

title: Niyoga birth of Aśmaka
description: Because the death-on-intercourse curse stands, Vasiṣṭha begets a son on Queen Madayantī by niyoga; after a long gestation the stone-delivered child Aśmaka continues the Ayodhyā Solar line
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.9

title: Priyavrata's chariot-furrows carve the seven oceans and continents
description: Driving his chariot around the Earth seven times to make a second sun's daylight, Priyavrata's wheel-ruts carve out the seven oceans and demarcate the seven dvipas

title: Pṛthu levels the earth and milks Pṛthivī
description: The first consecrated king Pṛthu flattens the ground and, threatening the earth-as-cow, milks her of all crops and treasures, giving the earth her name Pṛthivī

title: Pṛthu milks and names the earth (origin-of-kingship variant)
description: In the kingship-origin accounts, the first consecrated king is variously Manu Vaivasvata or Pṛthu son of Vena, from whom the earth (Pṛthivī) is milked and named

title: Rishabha attains omniscience and nirvana (Jain)
description: Witnessing the dancer Nilanjana's sudden death, Rishabha renounces, fasts a year broken by Shreyamsa's sugarcane juice, attains kevala-jnana at Purimatala, and reaches nirvana on Mount Ashtapada (Kailasa)

title: Rāvaṇa's world-conquest (digvijaya)
description: Rāvaṇa defeats kings, yakṣas, and nāgas, subjugates Yama himself, overruns the three worlds, and abducts women

title: Seed of the Ganga-descent (Bhagiratha)
description: After Aṃśumān and Dilīpa fail, Bhagīratha's austerities bring Gaṅgā to earth (Śiva catching her fall) to redeem the 60,000 — the Gaṅgāvataraṇa

title: Shakuntala, Dushyanta, and the birth of Bharata
description: The hermitage romance and lost signet-ring lead to the birth of Bharata, eponym of Bharata-varsha and founder of the Kuru love-story

title: Shiva's Tandava of grief and Vishnu's dismemberment of Sati
description: Inconsolable Shiva carries Sati's corpse in a frenzied Tandava that threatens pralaya, so Vishnu cuts the corpse to pieces with his Sudarshana Chakra, the fragments falling across the subcontinent
source: Devi-Bhagavata VII; Kalika Purana; Mahabhagavata Purana

title: Slaying of Jalandhara by Shiva
description: As Vrinda's chastity lapses, Jalandhara's protection fails and Shiva beheads him with a cakra struck from his toe

title: Sparing of Maya and devotees
description: Śiva spares the architect Maya and remnant true devotees who had not abandoned his worship

title: Tapatī weds Saṃvaraṇa and mothers Kuru
description: The solar daughter Tapatī marries the Kuru king Saṃvaraṇa and becomes mother of Kuru, making the Mahābhārata clan partly solar-descended; the river Tāpī is named for her

title: The milking of the Earth by Prithu
description: Prithu pursues the Earth-cow with his bow and milks her of grain (using Manu as calf), naming her Prithvi and leveling the land for cultivation

title: The Māndhātā / Omkāreśvar tīrtha named for the king
description: The sacred Narmadā island at Omkāreśvar is traditionally called Māndhātā, said to be named for the king who won the jyotirliṅga's manifestation there through tapas

title: Tāraka-māya war and slaying of Tāraka
description: Skanda leads the devas in the Tāraka-māya war and slays Tāraka with his śakti/spear, restoring the worlds
source: Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Tulasī curses Viṣṇu and is reborn as river and basil-plant
description: Discovering the fraud, Tulasī curses Viṣṇu to become the śālagrāma stone; her body becomes the Gaṇḍakī river and her hair the sacred Tulasī plant

title: Vipula Guards Ruci by Yoga
description: Charged to protect his guru's wife from Indra, the disciple Vipula enters her body by yoga to bar the seducer's reach

title: Yayāti's renunciation and crowning of Pūru
description: After a thousand years of indulgence Yayāti realizes desire only flares like fire fed with ghee, returns Pūru's youth, crowns him sovereign over the elders, and retires to the forest, attaining heaven

title: Aftermath: the three sons' vengeance
description: Tāraka's three surviving sons later perform penance and raise the flying cities, setting up the separate Tripura-dāhana

title: Agastya drinks the ocean dry
description: When the Kalakeya asuras hide in the sea, Agastya drinks the entire ocean dry in one sip so the gods can destroy them, after which the ocean must be refilled

title: Birth of Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā
description: The three deity-portions are born to Atri and Anasūyā: Soma (Brahmā-portion), Dattātreya (Viṣṇu-portion), Durvāsā (Śiva-portion)

title: Cyavana tests King Kuśika and foretells Viśvāmitra
description: Cyavana tests King Kuśika and his queen with extravagant demands, rewards their forbearance, and foretells the eventual birth of Viśvāmitra in their line

title: Dhruva's penance
description: The boy Dhruva, pushed off his father's lap by the proud queen Suruci, is counseled by Narada and performs extreme tapas in Madhuvana until the worlds tremble

title: Dhruva Wins the Pole-Star
description: The slighted boy-prince Dhruva performs tapas and is fixed as the immovable pole-star

title: Emperor Bharata's reign and renunciation at Pulaha-ashrama
description: Bharata rules Bharata-varsha righteously, marries Panchajani, then divides the empire among his sons and retires to Pulaha's hermitage on the Gandaki, absorbed in worship

title: Kubera grants Dhruva a boon
description: Kubera, lord of the Yakṣas, appears, praises Dhruva's restraint, and grants him a boon; Dhruva asks only for unbroken remembrance of Viṣṇu

title: Mandavya curses Dharma; birth of Vidura
description: The ascetic Mandavya, wrongly impaled, curses Dharma to be reborn as the wise shudra-born Vidura

title: Naimisha named a supreme ford in the Tirtha-yatra Parva
description: Pulastya/Narada extol Naimisha on the Gomati among the highest tirthas, a month's bathing there yielding horse-sacrifice merit and purifying the lineage

title: Origin of the Shakti Pithas
description: Wherever a body-part or ornament of Sati fell, the spot became a Shakti Pitha where the Goddess is enshrined in a regional form, each guarded by a paired form of Shiva as Bhairava

title: Pṛthu milks the Earth
description: Pṛthu, the first consecrated king and a Viṣṇu avatara, milks the Earth (Pṛthvi) to restore abundance after the tyrant Vena

title: The Four Kumāras Teach Pṛthu Bhakti
description: The eternal boy-sages appear and instruct Pṛthu in bhakti and self-knowledge, one of the Bhāgavata's notable devotional discourses

title: Tripurāntaka-mūrti and cultic afterlife
description: The deed crystallizes into the Tripurāntaka icon, the Tripurāri epithets, Kālidāsa allusion, and the Kārttikai Dīpam festival association
source: Kāraṇāgama / Śilpa tradition; Kālidāsa; Tamil Śaiva tradition

title: Viśvakarmā carves the unfinished Jagannātha image
description: Disguised and demanding to work unobserved, Viśvakarmā carves the wooden image of Jagannātha at Puri, leaving it armless when interrupted

title: Viśvāmitra takes Mādhavī and 600 horses; Aṣṭaka born
description: Viśvāmitra accepts the 600 horses plus Mādhavī herself for the missing 200, begetting Aṣṭaka on her

title: Vrinda's curse upon Vishnu
description: Discovering the fraud, Vrinda curses Vishnu to become the shalagrama stone and to be separated from his wife (Rama's loss of Sita)

title: Yayāti's fall from heaven and rescue
description: Boasting of his merit, Yayāti is cast from svarga but saved mid-fall by four royal-sage grandsons through his daughter Mādhavī, who share their merit to restore him

title: Agastya humbles the Vindhyas
description: The Vindhya range grows skyward to block the sun; Agastya asks the mountains to bow until he returns and never returns, permanently flattening them and carrying Vedic culture south

title: Anaraṇya's curse on Rāvaṇa
description: The defeated Ikṣvāku king Anaraṇya, dying, curses Rāvaṇa that a future descendant of his line (Rāma) will kill him

title: Bharata rescues the orphaned fawn
description: At the Gandaki a pregnant doe startled by a lion's roar miscarries and dies; Bharata rescues the newborn fawn and rears it at his ashrama

title: Churning of Vena into Prthu and the Milking of the Earth
description: The wicked king Vena is churned into Prthu, the first consecrated king, who milks the Earth (Prithvi) for crops

title: Dhruva's ascent to Dhruva-loka
description: In old age Dhruva is borne by Viṣṇu's attendants Nanda and Sunanda on a celestial vimāna; refusing to go without his mother Sunīti, he sets his foot on the head of personified Death and enters the imperishable polar seat

title: Kaca sent to steal the Mṛtasañjīvanī
description: To end the asuras' monopoly on resurrection, the devas send Kaca, son of Bṛhaspati, to enroll as Śukra's pupil and obtain the Mṛtasañjīvanī mantra by service and by courting Devayānī

title: Mādhavī returned to Yayāti
description: With the dakṣiṇā discharged, Gālava restores the still-virgin Mādhavī to her father Yayāti

title: Mādhavī's vow of the forest life
description: Repeatedly lent by sage Gālava to kings for dowry-horses and each time regaining virginity, Mādhavī finally chooses the ascetic forest life over remarriage

title: Priyavrata carves the seven dvipas
description: Svayambhuva Manu's son Priyavrata drives his chariot around the earth, his wheel-tracks carving the seven continents

title: Priyavrata restores a stillborn child (Chhath charter)
description: In one Chhath charter King Priyavrata, son of Svayambhuva Manu, has his stillborn child restored to life by Chhathi Maiya (Surya's sister Usha), instituting sun-worship

title: Pṛthu Milks the Earth-Cow
description: In the Pṛthu myth the gods, sages, ancestors, nāgas and men each milk the Earth figured as a cow for their respective sustenance (grain, soma, etc.)

title: Pṛthu's Renunciation and Death
description: In old age Pṛthu retires to the forest, enters samādhi and yields up his body, and his queen Arci follows him onto the pyre in an early sati narrative

title: Rebirth of the Goddess as Parvati
description: Sati incarnates again as Parvati, daughter of Himavan and queen Mena, so that a son of Shiva may be born to slay the asura Taraka
source: Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Parvati Khanda; Kumarasambhava 1

title: Soma founds the Chandravaṃśa
description: Through son Soma/Candra, Atri becomes genealogical root of the Lunar dynasty leading to Budha, Purūravas, and the Yādava/Kuru houses

title: Tapas of the ten Prachetas and the Rudra-Gita
description: The ten Prachetas perform 10,000 years of underwater tapas; Shiva appears and teaches them the Rudra-Gita, and Vishnu grants the boon of progenitorship

title: Uccaiḥśravas made king of horses under Pṛthu
description: When Pṛthu is installed as earth's first king, Uccaiḥśravas is made the king of horses in the parallel installation of category-kings

title: Vishnu's boon and the fixing of Dhruva as the Pole Star
description: Vishnu appears, touches Dhruva's cheek with His conch, and grants him Dhruva-loka, the immovable celestial point around which all stars wheel for a full Kalpa

title: Viśvakarmā fashions Tilottamā
description: On Brahmā's order Viśvakarmā fashions the supremely beautiful apsarā Tilottamā from measures of every excellence to undo the asura brothers Sunda and Upasunda

title: Vrinda's self-immolation and rebirth as Tulsi
description: Grief-stricken Vrinda enters fire; from her springs the Tulsi plant, declared dearest to Vishnu and united with the shalagrama

title: Agastya digests Vatapi and drinks the ocean dry
description: The sage swallows the demon Vatapi, weds Lopamudra, and drinks the ocean dry to expose the Kalakeya demons

title: Bharata dies thinking of the deer and is reborn a deer
description: Bharata's heart fastens on the deer, slackening his devotion; dying with the deer in mind he is reborn as a deer, illustrating that one's last thought determines the next birth

title: Bharata reborn as a deer then Jada Bharata
description: King Bharata, through attachment to a deer, is reborn as a deer and then as the enlightened ascetic Jada Bharata

title: Birth of Shani to Surya and Chhaya
description: Shani is born to Chhaya, Surya's shadow-wife, his dark complexion attributed to her fierce tapas under the sun while pregnant; Surya's rejection makes Sun and Saturn natural enemies

title: Dhruva's war with the Yakshas and final ascent
description: After his brother Uttama is slain, Dhruva wars with the Yakshas until halted by Manu Svayambhuva, then ascends on a celestial vehicle alongside his mother Suniti

title: Kashyapa fathers all classes of beings
description: By his thirteen wives, daughters of Daksha, the Prajapati Kashyapa fathers the Adityas, Daityas, Danavas, Nagas, birds and most living classes, the universal patriarch of the Vaivasvata creation

title: Kubera's weapons forged from Surya's radiance
description: The shavings trimmed from Surya's excess radiance on Vishvakarma's lathe are forged into divine weapons, including Kubera's

title: Marriage of the Prachetas to Marisha and the rebirth of Daksha
description: Soma mediates the Prachetas' quarrel with the trees and gives them the tree-born Marisha, from whom the second Daksha is born

title: Mādhavī's svayaṃvara and choice of the forest
description: At her svayaṃvara Mādhavī rejects all royal suitors and chooses the forest, living as an ascetic — her single act of agency

title: Nalakūbara's curse on Rāvaṇa
description: For violating the apsarā Rambhā, Nalakūbara curses Rāvaṇa that his head will split if he ever forces an unwilling woman — explaining why he cannot touch Sītā

title: Narada prophesies Parvati's marriage to Shiva
description: Narada foretells that Parvati will wed Shiva, and she dedicates herself to that destiny from childhood

title: Narada's Purañjana Allegory
description: Narada teaches King Pracinabarhi the allegory of Puranjana, the soul in the body's city of nine gates, entangled in samsara and reborn as a woman

title: The three killings of Kaca
description: Suspecting Kaca's purpose, the asuras kill him three times — fed to beasts, pounded to paste in the sea, and burnt to ash mixed in Śukra's wine — Devayānī twice pleading him back to life

title: Indrajit conquers Indra
description: Rāvaṇa's son Meghanāda defeats and binds Indra himself; Brahmā ransoms Indra and renames the son Indrajit, granting the secret Nikumbhilā sacrifice

title: Kamadeva burned to ash
description: Indra sends Kamadeva to kindle desire in the meditating Shiva; the arrow stirs Shiva, who opens his third eye and incinerates Kama, who becomes Ananga, the bodiless

title: Mādhavī's merit redeems Yayāti
description: The ascetic merit of Mādhavī and her four sons arrests Yayāti's fall from heaven and restores him

title: Slaying of the tyrant Vena
description: The tyrant Vena bans all yajna and worship claiming to be Hari himself; dharma collapses and the sages kill him with sanctified kusha-grass blades and hum-mantras

title: Sudarśana and Oghavatī Conquer Death by Hospitality
description: When Dharma in disguise demands the wife's body, Sudarśana's and Oghavatī's unwavering atithi-dharma conquer Death itself

title: The belly-revival and the wine-curse
description: With Kaca inside his belly, Śukra teaches him the Mṛtasañjīvanī so Kaca can revive him after bursting forth; sobered by having drunk his pupil, Śukra decrees that any brahmin who drinks wine incurs sin equal to brahminicide

title: The conscious deer-Bharata quits its body detached
description: Born remembering his past life, the deer-Bharata abandons the herd, returns to Pulaha-ashrama, lives austerely, and quits the deer-body wholly detached

title: The Pracetas and the Rudra-gita
description: The ten Pracetas meet Shiva who teaches them the Rudra-gita, then perform a 10,000-year underwater austerity and father Daksha reborn

title: Birth of Hanumān and the vajra-strike
description: Hanumān, son of Vāyu and Añjanā, leaps at the sun as an infant and is struck on the jaw by Indra's vajra (hence Hanumān), then heaped with boons by the gods

title: Churning of Vena's corpse and birth of Prithu
description: From the churned thigh of dead Vena emerges the dwarf Nishada, then from his churned arms arise Prithu (a Vishnu amsa-avatara) and his consort Arcis; Prithu is the first consecrated king

title: Parvati's tapas and the Brahmin-test
description: Parvati undertakes ferocious austerities to win Shiva by merit, earning the name Aparna; Shiva, disguised as a young Brahmin, disparages himself to test her, and on her fierce defense reveals himself and accepts her

title: Priyavrata Carves the Oceans and Continents
description: Priyavrata drives his chariot seven times round Meru and the wheel-ruts become the seven oceans and continents

title: Rebirth as Jada Bharata, the silent sage
description: The soul is reborn in an Angirasa brahmana family and deliberately acts deaf, dumb, and dull to avoid entanglement, earning the mocking name Jada Bharata

title: Sagara's sons burnt by Kapila
description: Sagara's sons digging the ocean-bed for the lost sacrificial horse are incinerated by Kapila's glance

title: The mutual curses of Kaca and Devayānī
description: When Kaca refuses to marry Devayānī on grounds of kinship, she curses that the Sañjīvanī will fail when he wields it, and he counter-curses that no brahmin will ever marry her — fating her to wed the kṣatriya Yayāti

title: Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into the well
description: After Indra swaps their garments and a quarrel over rank erupts, the asura princess Śarmiṣṭhā strips, strikes, and casts Devayānī into a dry well, leaving her for dead

title: Bhadra Kali saves Jada Bharata from human sacrifice
description: Seized by a dasyu-chief's robbers to be offered to Bhadra Kali, Jada Bharata is saved when the goddess springs from her image, slays the would-be sacrificers, and frees him

title: Prithu milks the Earth
description: When the famished Earth-cow hides her herbs, Prithu pursues her with drawn bow until she yields and is milked, using Svayambhuva Manu as calf, giving grain to beings and naming the Earth Prithvi

title: Sagara's 60,000 sons burnt by Kapila
description: King Sagara's sixty thousand sons, digging for the sacrificial horse, wrongly accuse the meditating sage Kapila and are burnt to ash by his glance

title: Sages curse Hanumān to forget his powers
description: For childhood mischief the ṛṣis curse Hanumān to forget his immense powers until reminded — the back-story for Jāmbavān's reminding before the ocean leap

title: Shibi offers his flesh to ransom a dove
description: King Shibi, tested by Indra as a hawk and Agni as a dove, offers his own flesh to ransom the dove

title: Sunatanartaka wins Parvati's hand
description: Shiva takes the graceful dancer form to appear before Himavan as a wandering performer and win the hand of Parvati

title: The Three Lives of Bharata (Jada Bharata)
description: King Bharata, son of Rishabha, lives through three births (king, deer, then the realized dull brahmana) and instructs King Rahugana

title: The wedding of Shiva and Parvati
description: Himavan consents and Shiva sends the Saptarishi and Arundhati to ask for Parvati; the divine wedding draws all the gods

title: Birth of Skanda and the slaying of Taraka
description: From the union of Shiva and Parvati comes Kumara/Skanda/Kartikeya, the war-god, who slays Taraka, the purpose of the whole rebirth-cycle

title: Cyavana restored to youth by the Ashvins
description: The aged Bhargava is restored to youth by the Ashvins, who in return gain a share of the soma

title: Descent of the Gaṅgā (Gaṅgāvataraṇa)
description: Bhagīratha's austerities bring Gaṅgā from heaven to redeem Sagara's sons' ashes; Śiva breaks her fall in his hair as Gaṅgādhara

title: Jada Bharata teaches King Rahugana (Bharata-gita and forest allegory)
description: Conscripted to carry Rahugana's palanquin and rebuked for his erratic gait, Jada Bharata breaks his silence with the Bharata-gita and the bhavatavi forest-of-samsara allegory, humbling the king

title: Prithu's 100 horse-sacrifices and clash with Indra
description: Indra repeatedly steals Prithu's sacrificial horse in disguises until Brahma brokers peace, after which the four Kumaras and Vishnu instruct Prithu, who delivers a discourse and retires to the forest

title: Yayāti rescues Devayānī from the well
description: King Yayāti, hunting and thirsty, finds Devayānī in the well and lifts her out by her right hand, which she construes as a betrothal

title: Śarmiṣṭhā enslaved to Devayānī
description: Threatened with abandonment by his indispensable preceptor, Vṛṣaparvan gives his daughter Śarmiṣṭhā with a thousand maidens as a servant to the woman she wronged

title: Aruna hatched prematurely as Surya's charioteer
description: The legless dawn-deity Aruna, hatched prematurely from Vinata's egg, becomes the charioteer of Surya

title: Birth of Ganesha and his beheading
description: Parvati creates Ganesha from the paste of her own body; his beheading and elephant-head restoration follows as a parallel myth

title: Narada Curses Daksha's Sons to Renunciation
description: Narada turns Daksha's sons the Haryashvas and Savalashvas to renunciation, earning Daksha's counter-curse that Narada wander forever

title: The ten Prachetas perform underwater tapas
description: The ten Prachetas brothers undertake 10,000 years of underwater tapas, receiving from Vishnu the boon to be progenitors of mankind

title: Dadhichi gives his bones for the Vajra
description: The sage gives his bones to forge Indra's Vajra weapon

title: Marriage of Yayāti and Devayānī
description: Śukra weds Devayānī to Yayāti on the binding condition that he never summon Śarmiṣṭhā, who enters the palace as part of the dowry-train

title: Parvati becomes Gauri
description: Taunted as dark, Parvati performs tapas to shed her dark complexion and emerges radiant as Gauri, the sloughed dark sheath becoming the goddess Kaushiki/Kali

title: Shiva teaches the Prachetas the Rudra-Gita
description: Shiva (Rudra) appears to the Prachetas as they begin their austerity and teaches them the hymn of self-realization, the Rudra-Gita

title: The Prachetas' quarrel with the trees and birth of the second Daksha
description: Emerging to find the Earth overgrown, the Prachetas nearly burn the forests until Soma mediates and gives them the tree-born maiden Marisha, from whom the reborn Daksha is born

title: The two queens bear five sons
description: Yayāti secretly fathers children on Śarmiṣṭhā despite the oath; Devayānī bears Yadu and Turvaśu, Śarmiṣṭhā bears Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru — the breach that later provokes the curse of old age and splits the Lunar dynasty

title: Viśvāmitra wars with Vasiṣṭha over the wish-cow
description: The kṣatriya king Viśvāmitra covets Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā, wars with him and loses, then begins millennia of tapas to become a brahmarṣi

title: Vīrabhadra destroys Dakṣa's sacrifice
description: After Satī self-immolates at her father Dakṣa's yajña, the grief-maddened Śiva creates Vīrabhadra, who storms the sacrifice and beheads Dakṣa; Satī's scattered limbs become the Śakti Pīṭhas
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Kālikā Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa

title: Triśaṅku raised to heaven and the counter-heaven
description: Viśvāmitra raises the outcast king Triśaṅku bodily to heaven and, when the gods cast him down, creates a counter-heaven holding him mid-sky

title: Birth of Budha and the Tara Scandal
description: Candra abducts Tara, wife of Brihaspati, triggering the Tarakamaya war; Tara bears Budha of disputed paternity, and the Moon's waning is linked to a resulting curse

title: Śunaḥśepa saved from sacrifice
description: The human-sacrifice victim Śunaḥśepa is saved by mantras Viśvāmitra gives him at Ambarīṣa's rite

title: Dhruva's Penance at Madhuvana
description: The boy Dhruva performs tapas at Dhruva-ṭīlā in Madhuvana, one of the twelve forests of Braj

title: Menakā breaks Viśvāmitra's penance; birth of Śakuntalā
description: The apsarā Menakā seduces Viśvāmitra, begetting Śakuntalā; he later conquers desire and anger to win the title Brahmarṣi

title: Savitri wins back Satyavan from Yama
description: The devoted wife out-argues Yama to win back her husband's life

title: Daksha populates the worlds through his daughters
description: Daksha Prajapati's daughters, married to the sages and to Kashyapa, become mothers of the Adityas (gods), Daityas, Danavas, animals, nagas and all living kinds; he later resorts to sexual generation

title: Indra seduces Ahalyā and is cursed
description: Indra, disguised as the sage Gautama, seduces his wife Ahalyā; Gautama curses Indra and condemns Ahalyā to penance to be released only by Rāma

title: Galava and Madhavi
description: Sage Galava lends out the princess Madhavi, who bears a king to each of four lords while regaining her virginity each time, to gather the guru-dakshina horses

title: Yayati's Exchange of Old Age
description: Cursed with premature old age by Shukra for wronging Devayani, Yayati borrows youth from his son Puru, later returns it and crowns Puru over the elder Yadu
source: Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana IV.10; Bhagavata IX.18-19

title: Pururavas and Urvasi
description: The Lunar-line tale of Pururavas and the apsara Urvasi, a morality story on lust and renunciation

title: Sudyumna/Ila's Monthly Sex-Change
description: Vaivasvata Manu's child enters Shiva's forbidden grove and alternates monthly between man (Sudyumna) and woman (Ila), branching the solar and lunar lines

title: Nahusa kicked from heaven into serpenthood
description: The over-proud Nahusa, made temporary Indra, is kicked from heaven by Agastya into serpenthood

title: Reign of Svayambhuva, the first Manu
description: Svayambhuva, the self-born spiritual son of Brahma, rules the first manvantara and is the reputed promulgator of the Manu Smriti

title: Vaivasvata's sons found the royal lineages
description: Vaivasvata Manu's sons found the great dynasties — Ikshvaku begins the Solar line and Ila/Sudyumna seeds the Lunar line through Pururavas

title: Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest (the Trimūrti test)
