description: The sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest in the Bhṛgu-pada test to decide the supreme god, cursing and blessing the Trimūrti accordingly and earning the Śrīvatsa mark

title: Soma Abducts Tara and the Birth of Budha
description: Soma abducts Brihaspati's wife Tara, Budha is born of the union, and the lunar dynasty begins

title: Vamana subdues Bali in the Vaivasvata manvantara
description: The dwarf-brahmin Vamana, manvantara-avatara of the present age, reclaims the three worlds from the demon-king Bali in three steps and restores them to Indra Purandara

title: Birth of the submarine fire from Aurva's wrath
description: The seer Aurva's world-burning wrath against the kṣatriyas produces the submarine fire (Vāḍava), which is restrained into the ocean-mare's-mouth

title: Rantideva's Fourfold Charity
description: After a 48-day fast, King Rantideva gives away his last food and water to a brahmana, a shudra, a man with dogs, and a chandala, and the testing Trimurti grant him liberation

title: The caru-swap of Ṛcīka and Satyavatī
description: The brahmin and kṣatriya rice-cakes are exchanged in the marriage of Ṛcīka and Satyavatī, producing a martial brahmin line and a priestly king

title: Birth of Soma, Dattātreya and Durvāsas to Atri
description: By the Trimūrti's boon, the sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā father three deities as sons: Soma (Candra), Dattātreya and Durvāsas

title: Birth of Chandra from Atri
description: Chandra is born to the sage Atri and his chaste wife Anasuya, welling from Atri's penetrating gaze/tears of austerity (in some versions as an amsa of Brahma), and is placed in the sky by Brahma

title: Budha weds Ila and Pururavas is born
description: Budha marries Ila (originally Sudyumna, Vaivasvata Manu's son cursed to alternate sexes), and their son Pururavas begins the human lunar dynasty (Aila line)

title: Indra grants the Puṣpaka and Uparicara Vasu's vimāna
description: Indra grants King Uparicara Vasu a crystalline aerial car letting him move godlike through the sky

title: Dakṣa-yajña: Satī's self-immolation and Dakṣa's beheading
description: Satī self-immolates at her father Dakṣa's sacrifice; in the catastrophe Dakṣa is beheaded by Vīrabhadra and later restored with a goat's head

title: Nārada cursed by Dakṣa to wander ceaselessly
description: For persuading Dakṣa's sons to renounce procreation, Nārada is cursed by Dakṣa to wander the worlds eternally

title: Nārada converts the Haryaśvas to renunciation
description: Dakṣa's first thousand sons, the Haryaśvas, sent to procreate, are dissuaded by Nārada's riddle and renounce and disperse forever

title: Nārada converts the Śabalāśvas
description: Dakṣa's next thousand sons, the Śabalāśvas, are likewise converted by Nārada, enraging Dakṣa into cursing him, after which Dakṣa begets daughters instead

title: Dakṣa's daughters wed Kaśyapa and breed all beings
description: Dakṣa's daughters married to Kaśyapa (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā and others) produce every class of being — devas, daityas, dānavas, nāgas, birds, beasts and more
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.21; Bhāgavata 6.6

title: Dakṣa gives 27 nakṣatra-daughters to Candra; the Moon's curse
description: Dakṣa marries 27 daughters (the lunar mansions) to Candra, whose neglect of all but Rohiṇī provokes Dakṣa's curse that the Moon waxes and wanes, partly relieved at Prabhāsa
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.14; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa

title: Birth of Nara-Nārāyaṇa to Mūrti and Dharma
description: Dakṣa's daughter Mūrti, married to Dharma, mothers the twin sage-avatāra Nara-Nārāyaṇa of Viṣṇu

title: Satī reborn as Pārvatī
description: After self-immolating at the Dakṣa-yajña, Dakṣa's daughter Satī, wife of Śiva, is reborn as Pārvatī

title: Agastya's curse of Indradyumna
description: King Indradyumna, a Pandya/Dravida devotee, is cursed by sage Agastya to be reborn as an elephant for a lapse of courtesy, becoming Gajendra

title: Devala's curse of the gandharva Huhu
description: The gandharva Huhu is cursed by sage Devala to become a crocodile for seizing his leg in the water, becoming the graha that attacks Gajendra

title: Anasūyā restores the sun and revives Kauśika
description: honouring the pativratā, Anasūyā releases the dawn with the arghya at the tenth midnight, so Kauśika dies by the curse and is at once raised up young, whole, and free of leprosy

title: Anasūyā's boon: the Trimūrti as her sons
description: grateful for the restored world-clock, the gods grant Anasūyā's request that Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva be born as her sons and that she and Atri attain liberation

title: Anasūyā's clay liṅga outweighs Atri's trance
description: while Atri sits fifty-four years in prāṇāyāma-samādhi, Anasūyā fashions an earthen liṅga by mantra and worships without pause, her service adjudged by the gods greater than the sage's penance

title: Apsarās arise from the Samudra Manthana
description: The celestial nymphs arise from the churned waters between devas and asuras; claimed by neither side, they become common (sādhāraṇa) to all
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 45; Mahābhārata

title: Aurva arms Sagara with the Āgneyāstra
description: The Bhārgava sage performs the exiled prince's rites, teaches him Veda and arms, and bestows the fire-weapon of his reconquest

title: Avatara of Mahotkata Vinayaka
description: Ganesha descends in Satya Yuga as the ten-armed lion-mounted Mahotkata Vinayaka and slays the demon-brothers Narantaka and Devantaka (and Dhumraksha)

title: Avīkṣit abducts Vaiśāliṇī
description: Karandhama's son seizes the princess of Vaiśālī at her svayaṃvara and carries her off, defeating the assembled suitor-kings

title: Avīkṣit captured and rescued
description: the humiliated suitor-kings combine, defeat Avīkṣit and take him prisoner, until his father Karandhama comes to the field and frees him

title: Bhagīratha renounces before bringing the Gaṅgā
description: In the Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha telling Bhagīratha gives his kingdom away, begs unrecognized in his own capital, attains knowledge under Tritala, and only then performs the tapas that brings Gaṅgā to earth

title: Bhṛgu's boon and the gourd-birth of the 60,000
description: After a hundred years' tapas Bhṛgu grants Keśinī one dynastic son (Asamañja) and Sumati sixty thousand sons, born from a gourd and reared in jars of ghee

title: Bhū-Varāha lifts the Earth at Śrīmuṣṇam
description: Viṣṇu as the Boar slays the demon Hiraṇyākṣa and lifts Bhū-devī from the cosmic ocean on his tusk, the deed the kṣetra localizes

title: Birth of Ekādaśī-devī and the slaying of Mura (Utpannā)
description: a radiant śakti springs from the sleeping Viṣṇu at Badarikāśrama, slays the daitya Mura of Candrāvatī, and is granted the eleventh tithi as her own, founding the Ekādaśī fast

title: Birth of Ekavīra the mare-born
description: Śiva's boon lets Viṣṇu approach the mare-Lakṣmī as a horse; their son Ekavīra (Haihaya) is left on earth and raised by the childless king Śatajit

title: Birth of Nara–Nārāyaṇa to Dharma and Mūrti
description: The twin sage-avatāra of Viṣṇu are born to the prajāpati Dharma and his wife Mūrti (var. Ahiṃsā), among the ascetic offspring of Dharma's line

title: Birth of Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsas
description: three sons are born to Anasūyā as guṇa-portions: Soma (Brahmā), Dattātreya the sattva-brahman (Viṣṇu), and Durvāsas the tamas-ascetic (Śiva)

title: Cīnācāra from Viṣṇu-as-Buddha
description: in Mahācīna Vasiṣṭha finds the Buddha (Viṣṇu's Buddha-form) amid the pañca-makāra and, past his brāhmaṇa revulsion, is initiated into Cīnācāra / Vāmācāra and at last attains Tārā's darśana and siddhi

title: Dama wins Sumanā of Daśārṇa
description: Nariṣyanta's son Dama is chosen at the svayaṃvara of the Daśārṇa princess Sumanā and defeats the rival suitor-kings who unlawfully oppose the match

title: Dama's blood-libation śrāddha
description: fulfilling his vow, Dama slays Vapuṣmat and performs his father's funeral rites with the murderer's own flesh and blood, feasting rākṣasa-descended brāhmaṇas — the Purāṇa's grim close

title: Danda's curse and the origin of Dandakaranya
description: Ikshvaku's son Danda violates Araja, daughter of guru Shukracharya, who buries his kingdom under seven days of dust, creating the wilderness named Dandaka-aranya
source: Valmiki Ramayana Uttara-kanda 79-81; Brahmanda Purana; Vishnu Purana 4

title: Dattātreya's Triloki-tilaka mantra
description: the sage Dattātreya initiates Ekavīra into the Yogeśvarī-mahāmantra granting unobstructed travel through the three worlds

title: Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana
description: When devas and asuras churn the Ocean of Milk with Mount Mandara and Vasuki, Dhanvantari rises bearing the pot of amrita, precipitating the deva-asura war over the nectar
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Ramayana Bala-kanda 45

title: Durvāsā's curse launches the ocean-churning
description: the spurned garland-curse drains the devas' strength, forcing the Samudra Manthana for amṛta

title: Ekavīra slays Kālaketu
description: descending to Pātāla by the mantra's power, Haihaya breaks Kālaketu's army and strikes the daitya dead with his mace, freeing Ekāvalī

title: Exile of Asamañja
description: Sagara banishes his own heir for drowning the townsmen's children in the Sarayū, keeping the virtuous grandson Aṃśumān as successor
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 38; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4

title: First jalabhisheka on Nilakantha
description: After Shiva drinks the Halahala of the churning, the devas pour Ganga water over him to cool the poison's burning — the charter-act the Kanwar Yatra re-enacts [folk]

title: Haihaya–Tālajaṅgha overthrow of Bāhu
description: King Bāhu of Ayodhyā is dethroned by the Haihaya–Tālajaṅgha clans with their Śaka, Yavana, Kāmboja, Pārada and Pahlava confederates, and dies in forest exile

title: Hiraṇyakaśipu's boon and persecution of Prahlāda
description: The daitya king Hiraṇyakaśipu wins a near-invincibility boon from Brahmā and persecutes his Vishnu-devoted son Prahlāda

title: Hiraṇyakaśipu's lattice boon
description: anthill-buried tapas compels Brahmā to grant death by no man, beast, weapon, time or place, the loophole answered by Narasiṃha

title: Ikṣvāku taught by Manu
description: Rāma's ancestor, first Solar king, asks what lies beyond decay and receives from Manu the vision of one consciousness and the seven bhūmikās of knowledge

title: Ilā born of a flawed rite
description: Vaivasvata Manu's sacrifice to Mitra-Varuṇa for a son miscarries and yields a daughter, Ilā, whom Vasiṣṭha's prayer then converts into the boy Sudyumna
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.1

title: Ila of Bāhlī and the kiṃpuruṣa origin
description: in the Rāmāyaṇa's version Ila, son of Kardama, is feminised in Śiva's grove, and Budha turns Ila's transformed retinue into the kiṃpuruṣa people before an Aśvamedha to Rudra restores Ila to permanent maleness

title: Jalodbhava slain, Kashmir drained
description: Kaśyapa's austerities bring the gods, the barrier at Varāhamūla (Baramulla) is breached, and Viṣṇu slays the water-demon Jalodbhava on drained ground, naming the land Kaśmīra

title: Jaya–Vijaya born as Hiraṇyakaśipu (birth #1)
description: Viṣṇu's cursed Vaikuṇṭha gatekeepers incarnate as the daitya brothers Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu, the first of three demonic births

title: Kālaketu abducts Ekāvalī
description: the daitya Kālaketu seizes the Devī-devotee princess Ekāvalī, daughter of King Raibhya, and carries her to Pātāla

title: Karandhama's sigh-born army
description: attacked with no host to defend him, King Balāsva exhales a whole phantom army out of his own body and routs his enemies, winning the name Karandhama by this "fanciful victory"

title: Kavaṣa Ailūṣa followed by the Sarasvatī
description: cast into the desert by ṛṣis as a slave-woman's son, Kavaṣa praises the Waters and the river Sarasvatī flows out after him, proving him a true seer

title: Keśin Dārbhya and the ghost Kaupayeya
description: the Pañcāla sage-king is taught hidden chant-knowledge and the fate of the dead by the preta of Kaupayeya, a spirit instructing the living

title: Khanitra and the recoiling kṛtyā
description: the minister Viśvavedin sets four rebel brothers' purohitas to raise a four-fold sorcery-deity against the beneficent king Khanitra, but his store of merit alone repels it and it falls back to destroy its own senders

title: Khanitra's grieving renunciation
description: victorious without lifting a hand yet stricken that his kinsmen and their priests died on his account, Khanitra resigns the kingdom to his son and withdraws to the forest with his queen

title: Kilāta and Ākuli trick Manu
description: two Asura priests con Manu into sacrificing first his demon-slaying bull, then his wife Manāvī, but the slaying-voice escapes into the sacrifice itself

title: King Camatkāra founds Camatkārapura
description: the Ānarta king Camatkāra builds and endows a town, gifting it to Brāhmaṇas, which is named Camatkārapura (later Vaḍnagar) after its royal donor

title: Kubera's Rākṣasas rout the king's army
description: Vaiśravaṇa looses a host of Rākṣasas that overwhelms and slaughters Mucukunda's forces, humbling the earth-conqueror against powers no weapon can touch

title: Lakṣmī cursed to a mare's body
description: distracted by Revanta on Uccaiḥśravas, Lakṣmī ignores Viṣṇu and is cursed to be born on earth as a mare

title: Madhu & Kaiṭabha Slain
description: Two primordial Dānava brothers born from Viṣṇu's ear menace Brahmā and steal the Vedas, slain by Viṣṇu after the Goddess Yoganidrā withdraws her sleep-spell; their fat forms the earth

title: Māṇḍavya's sunrise-curse on Kauśika
description: the impaled sage Māṇḍavya, spurned by the leprous brahmin Kauśika of Pratiṣṭhāna on the night-road, curses him to die the instant the sun rises

title: Marriage and the seed of the Haihayas
description: King Raibhya weds Ekāvalī to Ekavīra; she bears Kṛtavīrya, founding the Haihaya line that culminates in Kārtavīrya Arjuna

title: Marutta the universal monarch
description: Avīkṣit's son is consecrated where his father refused, becoming a cakravartin, a great sacrificer and lavish patron of brāhmaṇas

title: Marutta's golden sacrifice
description: Marutta Āvīkṣita performs the enormous yajña (priest Saṃvarta) whose buried Himālayan gold the Pāṇḍavas later recover to fund Yudhiṣṭhira's horse-sacrifice
source: Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa CXXXI; Mahābhārata, Aśvamedhika Parva

title: Marutta's Nāga war averted
description: Marutta marches on the troublesome Nāgas, but his father Avīkṣit interposes on their behalf and the ṛṣis avert the battle, the Nāgas making reparation

title: Matsya avatara and the great deluge
description: Vishnu as a fish warns Vaivasvata Manu of the world-ending flood, tows his boat (Saptarshi, seeds, creatures) to safety via Vasuki tied to his horn, and slays Hayagriva to recover the stolen Vedas
source: Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24; Shatapatha Brahmana

title: Matsya saves Manu from the deluge flood
description: A tiny fish begging Manu's protection grows monstrous and reveals itself as Vishnu, warns of the deluge, and tows Manu's ark — loaded with the seeds of beings, the seven rishis and the Vedas — to safety, then narrates the Purana

title: Mithi churned from Nimi's body; Mithilā founded
description: Fearing anarchy, the ṛṣis churn Nimi's preserved corpse and a son emerges — Janaka by birth, Vaideha as son of the bodiless, Mithila from the churning — who builds the city Mithilā
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.13.13; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5

title: Mithi churned from the bodiless king
description: fearing anarchy, the ṛṣis churn Nimi's preserved body to produce a son named Janaka (from birth), Vaideha (from the bodiless father), and Mithi (from churning), who founds Mithilā

title: Mucukunda challenges Vaiśravaṇa
description: not content with the mortal world, Mucukunda sends a challenge to Kubera, lord of Alakā and guardian of the north, imagining kṣatra can measure itself against a lokapāla

title: Mucukunda conquers the earth by his own arms
description: the Ikṣvāku emperor Mucukunda subjugates the whole earth through personal prowess, priding himself on the might of his two arms

title: Mucukunda refuses the earth as a gift
description: Vaiśravaṇa offers to bestow dominion, but Mucukunda declines sovereignty as charity, holding a Kṣatriya must enjoy rule won by his own valour

title: Mucukunda reproaches Vasiṣṭha
description: stung by defeat, the king turns on his purohita Vasiṣṭha, asking what use is a Brahmaṇa priest if the king is still crushed in war

title: Mudāvatī renamed Sunandā
description: after the kill the serpent-king Śeṣa takes the club Sunanda and gives the rescued princess Mudāvatī the new name Sunandā after it, whom Vatsaprī then weds

title: Nābhāga's accepted caste-fall
description: the kṣatriya prince Nābhāga abducts an unnamed vaiśya maiden by the Rākṣasa rite against the ṛṣis' counsel, and when a wandering muni rules he has thereby fallen to vaiśya-hood, he keeps the wife and wears the demotion without repenting

title: Nābhānediṣṭha and Rudra's leavings
description: Manu's disinherited son wins cattle for teaching the Aṅgirases to reach heaven, then truthfully cedes them to a dark Rudra who, pleased, returns them

title: Namuci's loophole-boon and Indra's twilight betrayal
description: The Dānava Namuci wins a boon making him slayable by neither wet nor dry, neither day nor night, by no weapon, on neither land nor water; Indra swears a truce/friendship with him, then betrays it by decapitating him at twilight on the shore using sea-foam (apām phena) wrapped on the vajra as the boon-evading instrument
source: Ṛgveda 5.30, 8.14; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 12.7.3; Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa

title: Narasiṃha bursts from the pillar at Ahobilam
description: Challenged to show Vishnu in the pillar, Hiraṇyakaśipu strikes it and Narasiṃha erupts on the Ahobilam hill to void the boon
source: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Ahobila-māhātmya); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7; Vishnu Purāṇa 1

title: Nimi and Vasiṣṭha's mutual curse
description: Supplanted at Nimi's sacrifice, Vasiṣṭha curses the king's body to fall and Nimi curses him back, leaving both bodiless
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.13; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5

title: Nimi refuses re-embodiment
description: his corpse kept in unguents through the sattra, Nimi declines the gods' offer to restore his body, calling embodiment bondage, and asks instead to dwell among living beings

title: Nimi refuses re-embodiment and dwells in the blink
description: Offered his body back by the gods, Nimi declines embodiment as bondage and is granted residence in the eyes of all creatures — the blink (nimeṣa) etymology

title: Nimi's thousand-year sattra and Vasiṣṭha's prior retainer
description: Ikṣvāku's son Nimi engages the family priest Vasiṣṭha, who is already retained by Indra and bids him wait; Nimi, holding life fleeting, begins the rite with Gautama instead

title: Poison-birth of Sagara at Aurva's āśrama
description: Aurva stops Bāhu's poisoned widow from ascending the pyre; her son is born together with the poison and named Sa-gara, "with the gara"
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.8

title: Prahlāda charges the armed ascetics with hypocrisy
description: finding two matted-haired sages in antelope skins beside the divine bows Śārṅga and Ājagava, Prahlāda condemns their mixing of tapas and weapons as dambha; Nara replies that for the truly capable the two are one authority
source: Vāmana Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9

title: Prahlāda's pilgrimage to Naimiṣa
description: counseled by Cyavana that inner purity outranks any tīrtha, the Daitya sovereign Prahlāda leads the Daityas and Dānavas from Rasātala to Naimiṣāraṇya to bathe in the Sarasvatī
source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.8; Vāmana Purāṇa

title: Prahlāda's self-awakening (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha version)
description: Prahlāda attains realization by his own inquiry and sinks into nirvikalpa absorption so deep the asura realm falls into disorder, until Viṣṇu wakes him and bids him rule as a jīvanmukta

title: Prahlāda's submission at Badarikāśrama
description: the humbled asura renounces his kingdom to Andhaka, journeys to Badarī, hymns Nārāyaṇa as Acyuta, Varāha and Narasiṃha, and is granted freedom from karmic bondage

title: Prahlāda's yajña at Manchāle (Mantrālayam)
description: Mādhva tradition holds the Tuṅgabhadrā site of Rāghavendra's future bṛndāvana to be the ground where Prahlāda performed a sacrifice in Kṛta Yuga [traditional]

title: Rājyavardhana's ten-thousand-year youth
description: after a grey hair at seven thousand years his subjects win him a Sun-boon of ten millennia of enduring youth, but the king despairs at outliving everyone until a second penance extends the long life to all his people together

title: Sagara installs Aṃśumān and departs to heaven
description: After a reign of thirty thousand years, with his 60,000 sons still unredeemed ash, Sagara enthrones his grandson and ascends, leaving the Gaṅgā-labor to Bhagīratha's generation
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 42; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4

title: Sagara's Aśvamedha and Indra's theft of the horse
description: Emperor Sagara performs a horse-sacrifice; Indra, fearing his merit, steals the horse and hides it at Kapila's āśrama in Pātāla
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 38–40; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8

title: Sagara's reconquest of Ayodhyā
description: Sagara all but exterminates the Haihaya–Tālajaṅgha power and recovers the Ikṣvāku empire, fulfilling his vow of vengeance

title: Samudra Manthana and the Spilling of Amṛta
description: The churning of the ocean of milk produces the kumbha of amrita; in the ensuing fight, drops spill at four earthly sites that become the Kumbh Mela cities

title: Samudra Manthana — emergence of the fourteen ratnas
description: The Devas and Asuras churn the milk-ocean using Mt. Mandara and the serpent Vāsuki, drawing up the fourteen ratnas including Amṛta, Kāmadhenu, Kalpavṛkṣa, Kaustubha, Airāvata, Uccaiḥśravas and Lakṣmī

title: Śiva roots as Atrīśvara and Gaṅgā fills the kuṇḍa
description: Śiva manifests from the clay liṅga and stays permanently as Atrīśvara, while Gaṅgā, given a year of Anasūyā's worship-merit, abides in the sacred pit, ending the drought

title: Sudyumna's abdication and liberation
description: deemed unfit to reign as a half-time woman, Sudyumna cedes the throne to Purūravas and retires to the forest to attain liberation

title: Sudyumna's three regional sons
description: in his male months Sudyumna fathers Utkala, Gaya, and Vinatāśva (Bhāgavata: Vimala), eponyms of Utkala/Odisha, Gayā, and the western marches
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.1; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1.42

title: Surabhi Churned from the Ocean of Milk
description: Surabhi/Kāmadhenu rises among the fourteen ratnas churned from the Ocean of Milk, and Brahmā assigns her to yield the milk and ghee of Vedic sacrifice, giving her to the seven ṛṣis
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu and Bhāgavata Purāṇas

title: The Devī names the rescuer
description: Ekāvalī's companion Yaśovatī worships Caṇḍikā, who appears in a dream and directs her to the Goddess's devotee King Ekavīra/Haihaya

title: The Gaupāyanas recall Subandhu's soul
description: after Āsura sorcerers hired by king Asamāti kill Subandhu, his three brothers chant his departed life-breath back from Yama and the sky, and he revives

title: The gods beg Brahmā, who sends them to Anasūyā
description: with sacrifices and seasons collapsing, the gods appeal to Brahmā, who cannot overrule a faithful wife and directs them to propitiate Atri's wife Anasūyā

title: The hundred-year drought in the Kāmada forest
description: a century-long drought parches the forest of Kāmada by Citrakūṭa, driving the saptarṣi Atri and his wife Anasūyā to penance for relief

title: The imposed marks on the Śakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas
description: At Vasiṣṭha's intercession Sagara spares the foreign hosts but strips their dharma and brands them with shaven heads, half-shaven heads, loose hair and beards, making them mlecchas

title: The king who refused his crown
description: so shamed by having been captured, Avīkṣit refuses to be consecrated king; the impasse breaks only when his son Marutta is born to succeed him

title: The Matsya flood and Manu's survival
description: Vishnu as the Fish warns Vaivasvata Manu of a world-dissolving deluge, has him build a boat carrying the seven sages, seeds, and creatures, and tows it to a Himalayan peak by a horn on the fish's head, preserving the seeds of life into the new age
source: Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Mahabharata Vana Parva 3.186; Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana

title: The monthly alternation granted
description: Vasiṣṭha propitiates Śiva, who cannot revoke his decree but compromises: Sudyumna will be male one month and female the next for life
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1.38–40; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.1

title: The Nārasiṃha war (first saṅgrāma)
description: Viṣṇu as the Man-Lion slays the boon-armored Daitya emperor Hiraṇyakaśipu at twilight for his devotee-son Prahlāda

title: The Nava-Yogendras arrive at Nimi's sattra
description: Ṛṣabha's nine avadhūta sons appear at the Videha king's sacrifice and answer his nine questions on bhāgavata-dharma

title: The Nimi–Vasiṣṭha mutual curse
description: the slighted Vasiṣṭha curses the sleeping king to bodilessness, and the guiltless Nimi curses his guru back in kind, so both their bodies fall away
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 56; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5

title: The pativratā halts the dawn
description: to save her cursed husband, Kauśika's faithful wife decrees "the sun verily shall not arise," and by her fidelity the sun fails to rise, throwing the worlds into continual night

title: The Śiva-grove transformation
description: Sudyumna rides into a forbidden reed-grove (Śaravaṇa/Sukumāra) at Meru's foot where Śiva sports with Pārvatī, and is turned female — becoming Ilā again — along with his companions and horse

title: The soma-sacrifice performed in a pit
description: trapped in the well, Trita turns pebbles into soma-grains and the water into ghee and mentally performs an entire soma-rite, whose chants reach the gods led by Bṛhaspati, who lift him out

title: The thousand-year battle of Prahlāda and Nārāyaṇa
description: the boon-armored asura fights Nara-Nārāyaṇa for a thousand divine years, archery escalating without result until the Brahmāstra and Māheśvarāstra cancel each other
source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9; Vāmana Purāṇa

title: The Vārtraghna war (tenth saṅgrāma)
description: Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra with the vajra forged from Dadhīci's bones, releasing the pent-up waters

title: The Vitastā brought down
description: Śiva opens a trident-channel one vitasti (span) deep and Pārvatī flows forth as the river Vitastā (Jhelum) to purify the piśāca-defiled valley, taking her name from the span

title: Trita betrayed into the well
description: journeying with cattle earned by sacrifice, the brothers Ekata and Dvita covet the herd and abandon Trita when he falls into a deep dry well at Udapāna on the Sarasvatī

title: Trita's curse on his brothers
description: freed from the well, Trita curses the greedy Ekata and Dvita to become wolves and beasts of prey, so the wolf that scattered the herd becomes their own descendants' fate

title: Vamana measures the three worlds (Trivikrama)
description: Born as a dwarf brahmana to Aditi and Kashyapa, Vishnu begs three paces from the asura-king Bali, swells into cosmic Trivikrama, and presses Bali to the netherworld, restoring Indra's sovereignty

title: Vapuṣmat murders Nariṣyanta
description: Vapuṣmat, one of the suitors Dama had beaten, waylays and kills King Nariṣyanta in the forest

title: Vasiṣṭha Journeys to Mahācīna
description: directed that Tārā yields only to another ācāra, Vasiṣṭha travels to Mahācīna (the trans-Himalayan Buddhist north) seeking her secret mode of worship

title: Vasiṣṭha reborn from the kumbha
description: directed by Brahmā, the bodiless Vasiṣṭha lodges in the seed of Mitra and Varuṇa spilled at the sight of Urvaśī and is reborn womblessly from a pot, gaining his Maitrāvaruṇi and Kumbhayoni names

title: Vasiṣṭha's Failed Tārā Worship
description: the Brahmā-born ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha undertakes ages of Vedic/Dakṣiṇācāra austerity to Tārā at Tārāpīṭha and gains no vision of the goddess

title: Vasiṣṭha's tapas vanquishes the Rākṣasas
description: the ṛṣi brings his brahma-tejas to bear through severe penance, and the enemy that kṣatra could not touch is dissolved by brahman power

title: Vatsaprī slays Kujṛmbha in Pātāla
description: descending with scimitar and bow, Vatsaprī kills the Daitya Kujṛmbha — whose Prajāpati-forged club Sunanda gapes the earth open to Pātāla — with his fire-weapon after the captive princess secretly drains the club's power by touching it

title: Videgha Māthava carries Agni east to found Videha
description: Agni Vaiśvānara flashes from the mouth of king Videgha Māthava at his priest's ghee-verse and burns eastward over the rivers to the Sadānīrā, granting the king his abode east of it — the founding charter of Videha/Mithilā

title: Vishnu-as-Kurma bears Mount Mandara at the churning
description: Vishnu descends as the tortoise Kurma to support sinking Mount Mandara during the Samudra-manthana, and from within that episode discourses the whole Purana to King Indradyumna

title: Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī to recover the amṛta
description: Viṣṇu takes the form of the enchantress Mohinī after the asuras seize the nectar pot from Dhanvantari at the churning

title: Vāsuki the Churning-Rope at Samudra Manthana
description: The nāga-king Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope wound round Mount Mandara at the Samudra Manthana, vomiting the Hālāhala poison that Śiva drinks, and is worn by Śiva as a neck-ornament

title: Dhanvantari rises last bearing the Amṛta-kumbha
description: The divine physician Dhanvantari, patron of Āyurveda, rises last from the churning bearing the pot (kumbha) of amṛta, the nectar of immortality

title: Durvasa's curse and Lakshmi's withdrawal
description: Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra slights and Airavata tramples; the offended Lakshmi abandons the three worlds, which lose their lustre, prompting the churning to recover her

title: Durvasa's curse triggers the churning
description: Durvasa's garland is trampled by Indra's elephant Airavata; he curses the Devas to lose their shri, Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean, and the Asuras rout the weakened Devas

title: Eternal tapas at Badarīkāśrama
description: Nara and Nārāyaṇa retire to the Himālayan hermitage of Badarī (Badrīnāth) and perform unbroken, cyclically-renewed austerity for the welfare of the worlds

title: Hiraṇyakaśipu's vow of vengeance
description: After Hiraṇyākṣa is slain by Varāha, Hiraṇyakaśipu swears to destroy Viṣṇu and all his devotees

title: Hiraṇyākṣa Slain by Varāha
description: The daitya Hiraṇyākṣa drags the Earth down into the cosmic ocean and is slain by Viṣṇu as the Boar Varāha, who lifts Earth back on his tusks

title: Matsya saves Manu and recovers the Vedas from Hayagrīva
description: Viṣṇu's fish-avatāra grows enormous, warns Vaivasvata Manu of the deluge, tows his boat with the seven ṛṣis and the seeds/Vedas to safety, and recovers the Vedas from the demon Hayagrīva

title: Matsya slays Hayagriva and recovers the Vedas
description: In the Puranic version the Matsya avatar slays the demon Hayagriva and recovers the Vedas he had stolen

title: Mohinī distributes the amṛta to the devas
description: After the ocean-churning Viṣṇu takes his only female form, Mohinī, beguiling the asuras and distributing the nectar of immortality to the devas alone

title: Mohini Tricks the Asuras for the Amṛta
description: Viṣṇu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini to seize the pot of amrita and trick the asuras out of immortality

title: Mohinī's unfair distribution of the nectar
description: Mohinī seats devas and asuras separately and serves the amṛta only to the devas, beguiling the asuras with delay

title: Namuci steals Indra's strength and Soma
description: In the Brāhmaṇa version Namuci drinks away Indra's strength together with the Soma/Surā, carrying off Indra's vigour in the intoxicant; the weakened Indra makes a truce to recover it, the Aśvins and Sarasvatī supply the foam as the loophole-weapon, and the strength is restored upon Namuci's slaying

title: Origin of Mahalakshmi at the churning
description: Lakshmi (Sri) rises among the treasures churned from the milk-ocean and chooses Vishnu, exalted as the supreme Shakti

title: Prahlada counsels Andhaka and undertakes a tirtha-circuit
description: The Vishnu-devotee Prahlada counsels his kinsman Andhaka against lust for Gauri and later makes an extended pilgrimage circuit, serving as a vehicle for the text's pilgrimage doctrine

title: Prahlāda cast from the Lion-Hill and rescued
description: Prahlāda is hurled into the sea from the mountain on his father's order, rescued by Vishnu, and builds the first shrine on the hill

title: Raivata Kakudmin and Revatī's domain
description: Folk etymology of the hill ties it to the Ānarta king Raivata Kakudmin, whose daughter Revatī wed Balarāma

title: Samudra Manthana — churning of the ocean
description: Gods and asuras churn the milk-ocean with Mandara and Vasuki over Kurma, producing the fourteen ratnas (Lakshmi, Dhanvantari with amrita, the poison Shiva swallows, etc.), and Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar

title: Slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu at the Jvālā / Rakta-kuṇḍa spot
description: Narasiṃha in flaming form tears Hiraṇyakaśipu apart, his blood reddening the Rakta-kuṇḍa pool below

title: The 60,000 sons dig to the sea (Sāgara etymology)
description: Sumati's 60,000 sons excavate the earth seeking the horse, hollowing the ocean-bed — whence the sea is called sāgara, 'of Sagara'

title: The Matsya flood and rescue of Vaivasvata Manu
description: Vishnu as Matsya the fish warns Vaivasvata of a coming deluge; the Manu builds a boat tied to the fish's horn and carries the seven sages, seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, founding current humanity
source: Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24; Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Mahabharata Vana Parva

title: Varāha remains permanently manifest at Śrīmuṣṇam
description: After the Earth-rescue the Boar does not vanish but stays eternally visible at the spot, sometimes at Bhū-devī's petition, founding the perpetual-presence claim

title: Vishnu takes Mohini form to recover the amrita
description: After the asuras seize the amrita-pot, Vishnu takes the enchantress Mohini form to recover and redistribute the nectar to the devas

title: Vāruṇī Emerges at the Churning
description: Vāruṇī, goddess of wine and consort of Varuṇa, emerges among the treasures churned from the ocean at the Samudra Manthana

title: Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope at the Samudra Manthana
description: The Nāga-king Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope wound round Mt. Mandara at the Samudra Manthana

title: Viṣṇu reveals the twins' invincibility
description: Viṣṇu discloses that Nara and Nārāyaṇa are his own aṃśas doing tapas for the worlds and tells Prahlāda he can conquer the Lord by devotion but never by battle
source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9; Vāmana Purāṇa

title: Vṛśa Jāna revives the boy under the chariot
description: after king Tryaruṇa's chariot kills a brāhmaṇa boy and the blood-guilt is apportioned, the purohita Vṛśa restores the dead child to life with an Agni-hymn

title: Yogeśvarī Emitted Against Andhaka's Blood
description: When Śiva spears Andhaka and each blood-drop becomes a new demon, Śiva emits Yogeśvarī from his mouth-flame and the gods send their śaktis to follow and drink the blood, checking the flood

title: Beheading of Svarbhānu and the birth of Rāhu and Ketu
description: Svarbhānu infiltrates the deva row to drink the nectar; Sūrya and Candra expose him and Mohinī beheads him with the Sudarśana Cakra, creating the immortal shadow-grahas Rāhu and Ketu

title: Consecration of Yoga-Narasiṃha on the summit
description: The summit Yoga-Narasiṃha shrine, Narasiṃha in seated meditative posture, is held the original guardian deity, consecrated in legend by Prahlāda

title: Cursed devas churn the Milk Ocean
description: The weakened devas lose to the asuras and are told to churn the Milk Ocean in alliance with them to recover amṛta and lost treasures, from which Airāvata and Uccaiḥśravas re-emerge

title: Dhanvantari emerges at the Samudra Manthana
description: The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the churned ocean bearing the pot of amṛta, hailed as deva of medicine and aṃśa-avatāra of Viṣṇu

title: Emergence of Lakshmi from the Samudra Manthana
description: When devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean, Lakshmi rises seated on a lotus among the ratnas, is bathed by the celestial elephants, and garlands Vishnu as her eternal consort

title: Hiraṇyakaśipu Slain by Narasiṃha
description: Granted a loophole-bound boon of invulnerability, Hiraṇyakaśipu tortures his devotee-son Prahlāda and is slain by Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha at twilight on a threshold

title: Ikshvaku Founds Ayodhya
description: Ikshvaku, eldest son of Manu, establishes the Solar dynasty and the kingdom of Kosala at Ayodhya after the deluge

title: Kapila's glance burns the 60,000 sons to ash
description: The sons find the horse by the meditating Kapila and abuse him; Kapila's opened eyes incinerate all 60,000, leaving their un-rited ashes restless
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 40–41; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8 (Kapila as Viṣṇu-avatāra); Mahābhārata Vana Parva (Agastya narration)

title: Kurma avatara supports Mount Mandara
description: As Mandara (churning rod) wound with Vasuki sinks into the ocean of milk, Vishnu incarnates as the tortoise Kurma to bear the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana

title: Manu and the Flood (Matsya rescue)
description: Viṣṇu as the fish (Matsya) warns Manu of the pralaya-flood and saves him and the seeds of life across the deluge — the earliest extant Hindu flood account

title: Marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī
description: The Śiva Purāṇa narrates the marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī among the central cosmic Śaiva events

title: Maya builds Tripura's three cities
description: Maya constructs the gold, silver and iron flying fortresses for Tāraka's three sons, later burned by Śiva Tripurāntaka
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Matsya Purāṇa 129–140; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva 8.24

title: Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu at the threshold
description: Vishnu bursts from the pillar as the Man-Lion at twilight on the threshold and kills Hiraṇyakaśipu, voiding the boon; the kṣetra claims the deed for Siṃhācalam

title: Nārāyaṇa produces Urvaśī from his thigh to humble Indra's apsarās
description: When Indra sends Kāmadeva and apsarās to break their penance, the unmoved Nārāyaṇa creates the nymph Urvaśī from his thigh, shaming Indra's nymphs, then gifts her to the gods

title: Samudra Manthana (Churning of the Ocean of Milk)
description: Devas and asuras use Mandara as the churning-rod and Vasuki as the rope to churn the ocean; Vishnu as Kurma bears the sinking mountain, and the fourteen ratnas including amrita and Lakshmi rise
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.6-8; Mahabharata Adi-parva; Vishnu Purana 1.9

title: The boon of near-invulnerability
description: Through extreme tapas Hiraṇyakaśipu wins from Brahmā a death hedged by impossibilities — no created being, no weapon, not day or night, not inside or outside, not earth or sky, not man or beast

title: The devas name the hill (Ahō-balam / Ahō-bilam)
description: Watching the deed, the gods cry 'Ahō balam!' (what strength) or 'Ahō bilam!' (what a cave), naming the kṣetra

title: The Mātṛkās' Rampage and Pacification
description: Drunk on power after drinking the demon-blood, the Mātṛkās begin devouring gods, demons and creatures indiscriminately until Viṣṇu/Śiva must pacify them

title: The white-boar (Śveta-Varāha) self-manifestation at the tank
description: The svayam-vyakta icon reveals itself via a white boar appearing at the Nitya-puṣkariṇī tank, sometimes drawn by a sage's tapas; the lost-and-refound motif also attaches

title: Vaivasvata Manu begets the ten progenitor children
description: Through a son-yielding sacrifice, Manu and his wife Shraddha beget ten children who found the two great royal lines, including Ikshvaku and Ila/Sudyumna

title: Airāvata emerges from the churning
description: The white elephant-king Airāvata rises from the Samudra-manthana as one of the ratnas and is seized by Indra as his vāhana and East-guardian

title: Amṛta Falls at Brahmakund (Haridwar)
description: A drop of amṛta from the celestial kumbha spills at Brahmakund within Har-ki-Pauri during the flight after the Samudra Manthana, making it Haridwar's holiest bathing point and a Kumbh site
source: Wikipedia, Haridwar Kumbh Mela; Puranic Kumbh sources

title: Births of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya
description: The Śiva Purāṇa records the births of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya (Skanda)

title: Conquest of the three worlds
description: Armoured by the boon, Hiraṇyakaśipu usurps the realms of the devas and rules heaven, earth, and underworld as universal tyrant

title: Dhanvantari rises from the ocean with the amṛta
description: The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the churned ocean bearing the pot of amṛta, founding and patronizing Āyurveda

title: Drops of amṛta fall at the four Kumbh Mela sites
description: During the deva-asura scramble for the kumbha, drops of nectar fall at Prayāg, Haridvāra, Ujjain and Nāsik — the etiology of the Kumbh Mela

title: Halahala poison and Shiva Nilakantha
description: The world-destroying Halahala poison rises first from the churn; Shiva drinks it and Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Shiva Purana; Vishnu Purana

title: Śiva beholds the Mohinī form and is overpowered by māyā
description: Śiva asks to see the enchantress form; Viṣṇu reappears as Mohinī and Śiva, maddened with desire, demonstrates that even he is not beyond Viṣṇu's māyā

title: Kūrma supports the churning of the ocean
description: The tortoise-avatāra Kūrma serves as the support beneath Mount Mandara during the churning of the ocean

title: Narasiṃha teaches yoga to Prahlāda (Yōgānanda form)
description: His fury cooled after the slaying, Narasiṃha instructs Prahlāda in yoga, fixed as the Yōgānanda Narasiṃha shrine

title: Nityakalyāṇa — the eternal auspiciousness/wedding
description: The Lord is invoked as Nityakalyāṇa, conferring perpetual marital weal; read also as Varāha eternally 'wedded' to the rescued Earth on his body

title: Prahlāda Survives His Father's Attempts
description: Prahlāda, a Viṣṇu-devotee from the womb, miraculously survives poison, fire and the pillar, becoming the paradigmatic bhakta and a righteous asura-king

title: Sharabha pacifies Narasimha
description: Shiva assumes the colossal part-lion part-bird Sharabha form to pacify Vishnu's Narasimha when his fury threatens the cosmos

title: The Churning of the Ocean (Amrita-manthana)
description: The churning of the milk-ocean to win amrita, told within the Astika frame to explain the gods' immortality

title: The condition for redemption revealed
description: Aṃśumān recovers the horse and learns that only the celestial Gaṅgā brought down over the ashes can liberate the burnt sons

title: Vikukshi Shashada Eats the Sacrificial Hare
description: Sent to fetch sacrificial meat, Vikukshi eats a hare himself, earning the nickname Shashada and a brief exile

title: Vishnu descends as Ajita and becomes Kurma
description: During the churning Vishnu descends as Ajita and, when Mandara sinks, becomes the tortoise to bear the mountain on his shell as the pivot
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.5-8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva

title: Vṛtra slain by Indra
description: Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra, who withheld the cosmic waters, with the Vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers

title: Birth and devotion of Prahlāda
description: Prahlāda, son of Hiraṇyakaśipu, is a perfected Viṣṇu-devotee from the womb (taught by Nārada), rejecting demon-schooling and preaching bhakti

title: Dakṣa's sacrifice
description: The Śiva Purāṇa narrates Dakṣa's sacrifice and its destruction, a key cosmic Śaiva event

title: Descent of the Ganga (Gangavataran) at Gangotri
description: The Ganga descends from heaven at Gangotri to liberate the ancestors of King Bhagiratha, the headstream named Bhagirathi after him

title: Emergence of Lakshmi from the ocean
description: The goddess of fortune re-emerges radiant from the churned ocean and of her own choice garlands and weds Vishnu, restoring shri to the cosmos

title: First demonic birth: Hiranyaksa and Hiranyakasipu slain
description: Jaya and Vijaya are reborn as the asura brothers Hiranyaksa (slain by Varaha) and Hiranyakasipu (torn open by Narasimha) in Satya-yuga

title: Ila/Sudyumna roots the Lunar Dynasty
description: Ila/Sudyumna, who shifts between female and male after entering a Shiva-sacred grove, becomes root of the Chandra Vamsha via the child Pururavas, descending to the Kurus, Pandavas, and Krishna's kin

title: Kakutstha Rides Indra-as-Bull
description: Puranjaya rides into battle against the Asuras seated on Indra's hump in bull form, earning the patronymic Kakutstha later applied to Rama

title: Kāmadhenu given to the Saptarṣi and Vasiṣṭha
description: The wish-cow Kāmadhenu emerges from the churning and is given to the seven sages, passing into the keeping of Vasiṣṭha

title: Kurma named in the Bhagavata avatara-list (1.3.16)
description: The kurma/kacchapa tortoise descent that supported Mandara is enumerated in the Bhagavata's master list of Vishnu's avataras

title: Marriage of Narasiṃha to Chenchu-Lakṣmī
description: Lingering on the hill, Narasiṃha falls in love with and weds the Chenchu tribal maiden Chenchu-Lakṣmī, making the Chenchus his in-laws

title: Namuci beheaded by Indra
description: Indra circumvents Namuci's boon by decapitating him at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra, neither wet nor dry, by day nor night

title: Nārada turns Dakṣa's sons to renunciation; cursed to wander
description: Nārada counsels Dakṣa's sons toward renunciation so they never beget subjects, and Dakṣa curses him to wander ceaselessly without rest, feeding the Dakṣa–Satī cycle

title: Sanaka-kumaras curse Jaya and Vijaya
description: Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya are cursed by the four child-sages to three demonic births each ending in death at the Lord's hand, of which Shishupala is the third

title: Shiva Drinks the Hālāhala Poison at Alangudi
description: During the Samudra Manthana the world-destroying halahala poison rises first and Shiva drinks it to save creation, his throat turning blue; Alangudi is held to be the spot, making Shiva Apatsahaya, savior in distress

title: Three generations of failed penance
description: Aṃśumān and his son Dilīpa perform austerities to draw Gaṅgā down but die without success, passing the task to Bhagīratha

title: Varaha avatara slays Hiranyaksa
description: The Boar avatara lifts the Earth from the cosmic waters and slays the demon Hiranyaksa, the first life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse

title: Varaha Stays on Venkata Hill After Slaying Hiranyaksha
description: In a variant, the Varaha avatar remains on the hill as guardian after lifting the earth and slaying Hiranyaksha, and Shrinivasa must obtain his permission to settle there

title: Agastya drinks the ocean to expose the Kālakeyas
description: To destroy the ocean-hiding Kālakeyas who devoured sages by night, the gods enlist Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry

title: Bhagīratha's penance and Brahmā's boon
description: Bhagīratha renounces his throne for vast tapas; Brahmā grants Gaṅgā's descent but warns only Śiva can bear her fall

title: Birth of Mandhatr from His Father's Side
description: Mandhatr is born from his father Yuvanashva's side after the king drinks consecrated water meant for his queen, and becomes a universal emperor

title: Daksha's yajna and Sati's self-immolation
description: Prajapati Daksha holds a grand sacrifice snubbing his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva; insulted when she attends uninvited, Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire
source: Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana

title: Dhanvantari rises with the amrita
description: The divine physician Dhanvantari, patron of Ayurveda and an aspect of Vishnu, rises last from the ocean bearing the kalasha of amrita, the goal of the entire churning

title: Garuḍa's vision of the nine Narasiṃhas
description: Garuḍa does tapas in the Nallamala and is shown all nine self-manifest Narasiṃha forms across the hill

title: Hālāhala / Nīlakaṇṭha — Śiva drinks the world-poison
description: During the churning of the milk-ocean Vāsuki disgorges the all-destroying Hālāhala poison; Śiva drinks it and Pārvatī halts it at his throat, making him the blue-throated saviour of creation
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Indra bears the Kalpavṛkṣa to Svarga
description: The wish-fulfilling tree Kalpavṛkṣa emerges at the churning and Indra carries it to his paradise, rooting it in the Nandana-vana

title: Jyeshtha/Alakshmi rises from the churning
description: Alakshmi as Jyeshtha, elder sister of Lakshmi, rises from the churning before the nectar and is later married off to the sage Duhsaha, dwelling wherever inauspiciousness is found

title: Kapila teaches Devahuti (Kapilopadesa)
description: The Kapila avatara, born to Kardama and Devahuti, teaches his mother devotional Sankhya and bhakti-yoga, a primary scriptural Sankhya source

title: King Indradyumna Seeks Nila-Madhava
description: Satya-Yuga Malava king Indradyumna sends brahmin Vidyapati (who weds the Shabara chief's daughter Lalita) to find the secret Nila-Madhava image; it vanishes, directing the king to worship a sacred floating log instead

title: Markandeya conquers death at the Shiva-linga
description: At his destined hour of death the boy Markandeya clasps the Shiva-linga chanting the Maha-mrityunjaya mantra; Shiva bursts forth, defeats Yama, and grants him eternal youth

title: Mohinī's Muktanṛtya dance-trap of Bhasmāsura
description: Viṣṇu as Mohinī lures the ash-demon Bhasmāsura into mirroring her dance and touching his own head, reducing him to ashes (regional/folk version of the Vṛkāsura kernel)
source: Regional / folk tradition; Kathakali Bhasmāsura Mohinī (cf. Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.88 Vṛkāsura)

title: Nārada initiates the child Dhruva
description: Nārada meets the boy Dhruva, tests his resolve, sends him to Madhuvana, and bestows the dvādaśākṣara mantra that ignites Dhruva's penance

title: Prahlāda expounds navadhā bhakti
description: Confronting his father, Prahlāda declares Hari is everywhere and teaches the ninefold path of devotion, sealing his father's murderous resolve

title: The Kurma Purana spoken from the tortoise
description: Vishnu in tortoise form narrates the Kurma Purana to sages and Devas/Asuras during the churning, the only Mahapurana named for its avatara-narrator

title: Gaṅgādhara — Śiva bears the descent of Gaṅgā
description: When Bhagīratha's penance brings the celestial Gaṅgā down to redeem Sagara's 60,000 sons, Śiva catches her world-shattering fall in his matted locks and releases her as a tamed stream, humbling her pride
source: Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Mahābhārata

title: Śiva catches Gaṅgā in his locks (Gaṅgādhara)
description: Śiva traps the plunging Gaṅgā in his matted hair to tame her, releasing her in a thinned stream — the Gaṅgādhara icon

title: Mohini distributes the nectar to the Devas
description: The Asuras seize the amrita; Vishnu takes the enchantress form Mohini, beguiles them, and serves the nectar only to the Devas

title: Nārada's prenatal instruction of Prahlāda
description: Kayādhu shelters in Nārada's hermitage during the deva-asura war and the unborn Prahlāda absorbs Nārada's teaching on Viṣṇu-bhakti, the root of his invincible devotion

title: The failed killings of Prahlāda
description: Hiraṇyakaśipu has Prahlāda trampled, bitten, hurled from cliffs, burned, poisoned, and cast into the sea; Viṣṇu shields him each time. Folk tradition adds the Holikā fire-ordeal (etiology of Holī)

title: The Unfinished Carving of Jagannatha
description: A divine carpenter carves the Puri triad on condition of being undisturbed; the door is opened early, so the images remain armless and legless, and Brahma is brought to consecrate the temple
source: Madala Panji; Skanda Purana; Brahma & Narada Puranas

title: Virabhadra destroys Daksha's sacrifice
description: Enraged at Sati's death, Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of his hair, who destroy the yajna and behead Daksha; Shiva later revives Daksha with a goat's head

title: Viṣṇu claims the Kaustubha jewel from the churning
description: The supreme jewel Kaustubha emerges from the Samudra Manthana and Viṣṇu claims it, wearing it on his chest alongside the Śrīvatsa and Vaijayantī

title: Beheading of Svarbhānu (Origin of Rāhu and Ketu)
description: During the Samudra Manthana the asura Svarbhanu disguises himself to sip the amrita; exposed by Sun and Moon, Vishnu as Mohini beheads him with the Sudarshana Chakra, and his immortal head becomes Rahu and body becomes Ketu, who cause eclipses

title: Founding of the Shakti Pithas
description: Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse; Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts it into pieces that fall across the land, founding the Shakti Pithas, and Sati reincarnates as Parvati
source: Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature

title: Harishchandra's Truth-Test
description: Harishchandra sells himself, wife, and son to honor a debt to Vishvamitra and is tested mercilessly but never lies, restored and ascending to heaven as the archetype of satya

title: Indra Slays Vṛtra with the Vajra
description: The drought-serpent Dānava Vṛtra withholds the cosmic waters and is slain by Indra with the vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers — the foundational Vedic combat

title: The descent reaches the sea and redeems the ashes at Gaṅgāsāgar
description: Gaṅgā follows Bhagīratha's chariot to the ocean and over the ashes of the 60,000 at Sāgara-dvīpa, granting them heaven — establishing the first ancestral water-rite tīrtha
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.9

title: The pillar challenge and Narasiṃha bursting forth
description: Hiraṇyakaśipu strikes a pillar to disprove Viṣṇu's omnipresence; Narasiṃha, the man-lion, erupts from it roaring
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.12–22; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.20; Narasiṃha Purāṇa

title: Varāha lifts the Earth
description: Viṣṇu as the boar (Varāha) raises the Earth from the cosmic waters — a Satya-Yuga / Manvantara-boundary avatāra event framing the Varāha Purāṇa

title: Indra Decapitates Namuci with Sea-Foam
description: Bound by a truce and a no-wet-no-dry boon, Indra beheads the asura Namuci at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra — the loophole-archetype and origin of his brahmahatyā guilt-stain

title: Nārada instructs Prahlāda in the womb
description: Nārada teaches the unborn Prahlāda (via Kayādhu), seeding the Vaiṣṇava devotion of the Narasiṃha cycle

title: Skanda slays Tārakāsura
description: The Skanda Purāṇa records Skanda/Kārttikeya's birth and his slaying of the demon Tārakāsura

title: The threshold disembowelment of Hiraṇyakaśipu
description: At twilight, on the doorway threshold, on his lap, with bare claws, Narasiṃha disembowels Hiraṇyakaśipu — voiding every loophole of the boon

title: Uccaiḥśravas emerges from the churning
description: The seven-headed snow-white horse-king Uccaiḥśravas arises at the Samudra-manthana, born of the amṛta, and is seized by Indra (or claimed by Bali)

title: War over the nectar and Indra restored
description: Strengthened by the amrita, the Devas with Vishnu defeat the Asuras in the post-churning war and Indra is reinstated to Svarga

title: Agastya Drinks the Ocean Dry, Kālakeyas Slain
description: The ocean-hiding Kālakeyas devour sages by night until the gods beg Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry, exposing and enabling the slaughter of the Kālakeya asuras

title: Bhagiratha Brings Down the Ganga
description: Through epic tapas Bhagiratha brings Ganga from heaven to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons, with Shiva catching her in his locks; the river is named Bhagirathi for him
source: Ramayana Balakanda; Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata IX.9

title: Curse of the Sanaka-kumaras on Jaya and Vijaya
description: Brahma's four child-sages curse Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya to three demonic births, setting off the Hiranyaksha/Hiranyakashipu and later demon incarnations

title: Kāmadahana — the burning of Kāma
description: Sent by the gods to kindle Śiva's desire for Pārvatī so a son can slay Tārakāsura, Kāmadeva fires his arrow and Śiva's third eye burns him to ash; Śiva later restores him bodiless (Ananga)
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Matsya Purāṇa; Kālidāsa's Kumārasaṃbhava

title: Prahlāda pacifies Narasiṃha's wrath
description: Narasiṃha's fury terrifies even the gods and Lakṣmī; the child Prahlāda alone calms him with the Nṛsiṃha-stuti and is offered any boon

title: Samudra Manthana - the curse that triggers it
description: Sage Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra's elephant Airavata tramples; Durvasa curses the devas to lose their fortune and strength, and Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean

title: Varaha rescues Bhudevi from the cosmic ocean
description: As Bhudevi, the Earth goddess is rescued by the boar Varaha from the cosmic ocean

title: Hiraṇyakaśipu liberated; Prahlāda enthroned
description: Slain by the Lord's own hand, Hiraṇyakaśipu attains liberation (dveṣa-bhakti), discharging curse-birth #1; Narasiṃha enthrones Prahlāda as righteous daitya king, whose line leads to Bali

title: Kurma supports Mount Mandara
description: As the churning rod Mount Mandara sinks, Vishnu becomes the giant tortoise Kurma and bears the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning the Ocean of Milk for amrita

title: The Kadrū–Vinatā wager over the horse's tail
description: Kadrū and Vinatā wager over the colour of Uccaiḥśravas's tail with the loser to become slave; Kadrū's nāga sons coil as black hairs to deceive, winning and enslaving Vinatā

title: Tārakāsura Slain by Skanda
description: The daitya Tāraka, boon-protected to die only by a son of Śiva, forces the gods to engineer Śiva's marriage to Pārvatī, whose son Kārttikeya/Skanda slays him in the Tārakāmaya war

title: Varaha avatara rescues the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha
description: The Asura Hiranyaksha drags Bhumi to the bottom of the cosmic ocean; Vishnu as the boar Varaha dives in, slays him in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth on his tusks

title: Emergence of the fourteen ratnas
description: During the churning fourteen treasures rise from the ocean — including Kamadhenu, Uccaihshravas, Airavata, Kaustubha, Parijata, the Apsaras, Lakshmi, Varuni, Candra, Shankha, and Dhanvantari with the amrita
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8.8; Vishnu Purana; Mahabharata Adi Parva

title: Śiva Burns the Three Cities (Tripurāntaka)
description: Three sons of Tāraka win three indestructible flying fortresses destroyable only by a single aligned arrow; Śiva as Tripurāntaka burns all three with one shaft from his earth-chariot

title: Kadrū curses the reluctant nāgas
description: The serpents who refuse to deceive the tail are cursed by their mother Kadrū to perish in King Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, driving the Mahābhārata's nāga frame-story

title: Matsya saves Manu from the pralaya-flood
description: Viṣṇu as the fish Matsya saves Manu and the seeds of life across the deluge — the Manvantara-transition framing the Matsya Purāṇa

title: Andhaka Impaled by Śiva
description: The blind asura Andhaka, born of Pārvatī covering Śiva's eyes, lusts after Pārvatī and is impaled on Śiva's triśūla until his clone-spawning blood dries, drunk by the Mātṛkās; redeemed, he becomes the gaṇa-chief Bhṛṅgi

title: Garuḍa ransoms Vinatā by stealing the amṛta
description: To redeem his enslaved mother Vinatā, Garuḍa is forced to fetch the amṛta from Indra's heaven, originating his nectar-theft, his enmity with the serpents and his recruitment as Viṣṇu's vāhana

title: Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu
description: Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha kills the demon Hiraṇyakaśipu to protect the devotee Prahlāda — a Satya-Yuga avatāra event

title: Prahlada's devotion survives every attempt to kill him
description: Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-bhakti by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives poison, elephants, weapons, and fire

title: Saptarishi carried across the flood by Vaivasvata Manu
description: In the Matsya flood, Vaivasvata Manu carries the seven sages, the seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, re-seeding knowledge for the current humanity

title: Shiva drinks the Halahala poison (Nilakantha)
description: To save the cosmos from the world-destroying Halahala poison that first rises, Shiva drinks it; Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha

title: Holika burns in the fire - origin of Holi
description: Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but perishes while he survives, the origin myth of the festival of Holi

title: Jalandhara Slain by Śiva
description: Jalandhara, born of Śiva's third-eye fire and shielded by his wife Vṛndā's chastity, is undone when Viṣṇu deceives Vṛndā in his form, and Śiva slays him with a toe-carved cakra; Vṛndā self-immolates and becomes the Tulsī plant
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa

title: Mohini distributes the amrita
description: Vishnu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini, beguiles the Asuras who had seized the nectar pot, and distributes the amrita only to the Devas

title: Beheading of Svarbhanu (origin of Rahu and Ketu)
description: The Asura Svarbhanu disguises himself among the Devas to drink amrita; exposed by Surya and Candra, he is beheaded by the Sudarshana chakra, his immortal head and body becoming Rahu and Ketu who cause eclipses out of grudge

title: Hiranyakasipu's boon of near-invincibility
description: Hiranyakasipu obtains a boon of near-invincibility (not by man or beast, day or night, indoors or out), the second life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse

title: Mahalakshmi born at the Samudra Manthana
description: The supreme Lakshmi, consort of Vishnu, is born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk

title: Narasimha avatara slays Hiranyakashipu
description: Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha and kills Hiranyakashipu at twilight on the threshold upon his lap with claws, voiding every clause of the boon

title: Sudarśana severs Rāhu at the churning
description: Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra severs the asura Rāhu's head at the Samudra Manthana after he steals a sip of amṛta

title: The Matsya and Manu flood narrative
description: Manu rears a tiny fish that grows into the giant Matsya, who tows his boat to safety through the deluge

title: Churning of the Ocean (Samudra Manthana)
description: Viśvāmitra tells the Bāla-Kāṇḍa version of devas and asuras churning the Milk-Ocean with Mandara and Vāsuki, yielding the Hālāhala poison, Dhanvantari, apsarases, and Amṛta

title: Narasimha disembowels Hiranyakasipu
description: The Man-Lion avatara bursts from a pillar at twilight to disembowel Hiranyakasipu, threading every clause of the boon, and saves Prahlada

title: Prahlada enthroned as righteous Asura king
description: Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers; Prahlada is enthroned as a virtuous Asura king and becomes ancestor of Bali

title: War over the nectar and Indra's reinstatement
description: Devas and Asuras battle over the nectar; with strength restored the Devas prevail and Indra is reinstated as king of the gods

title: Dhruva becomes the Pole Star
description: Rebuffed by his stepmother, the boy Dhruva performs intense tapas guided by Narada; Vishnu appears and fixes him as the immovable Dhruva Nakshatra around which the Saptarshi revolve
source: Vishnu Purana 1.11-1.12; Bhagavata Purana 4.8-4.12 (canonically Svayambhuva Manvantara)

title: Varaha lifts the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha
description: When the Asura Hiranyaksha drags Earth (Bhumi) to the bottom of the cosmic ocean, Vishnu becomes the colossal boar Varaha, slays Hiranyaksha in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth back on his tusks

title: Daksha Yajna and Sati's self-immolation
description: Prajapati Daksha snubs his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva at a grand yajna; the insulted Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire
source: Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Kalidasa Kumarasambhava

title: Hiranyakashipu's boon of near-invulnerability
description: Enraged at his brother's death, Hiranyakashipu performs extreme tapas and wins from Brahma a boon that he cannot be slain by man or beast, day or night, indoors or outdoors, on earth or sky, by any weapon, then tyrannizes the three worlds

title: Nimi and Vasishtha's Mutual Curse
description: Nimi and his purohita Vasishtha curse each other to bodilessness over a sacrifice dispute; from Nimi's churned body is born Janaka, founding the Videha/Mithila line

title: Samudra-manthana (churning of the milk-ocean)
description: Devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean with the Kurma avatara as pivot, producing amṛta, Dhanvantari, and Lakṣmi

title: Manu and the Flood (Matsya Avatara)
description: The fish-avatara (Matsya) saves Manu from the cosmic deluge in the earliest extant Hindu flood narrative recorded in the Shatapatha Brahmana

title: Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar
description: The Mohini avatara enchants the asuras and distributes the amṛta to the devas, denying the demons immortality

title: Prahlada's devotion and survival
description: Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-devotion by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives his father's repeated murder attempts by poison, elephants, weapons, and fire

title: Virabhadra's rampage and beheading of Daksha
description: Enraged Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of hair; they destroy the yajna and behead Daksha, who is later revived with a goat's head

title: Founding of the Shakti Pithas and Sati's rebirth as Parvati
description: Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse, which Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts into pieces that fall across the land founding the 51 Shakti Pithas; Sati reincarnates as Parvati
source: Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature

title: Holika burned (origin of Holi)
description: Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but herself perishes while he survives — the origin myth of Holi

title: Narasimha Bursts from the Pillar to Slay Hiranyakashipu
description: In defense of the boy-devotee Prahlada, the man-lion Narasimha bursts from a pillar at dusk and slays the demon-king Hiranyakashipu

title: Ikshvaku founds the Solar dynasty
description: Vaivasvata Manu's eldest son Ikshvaku, granted Aryavarta/Kosala, becomes progenitor of the Suryavamsha, the line of Mandhata, Sagara, Bhagiratha, Raghu, and Rama

title: Matsya saves Satyavrata and the Vedas from the flood
description: The Fish avatara saves Satyavrata (Manu), the seeds of life, and the Vedas from the dissolution-flood, the manvantara-transition par excellence

title: Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu
description: When challenged whether Vishnu is in a pillar, Hiranyakashipu smashes it and Vishnu bursts out as the man-lion Narasimha, seizing the Asura at twilight on the threshold upon his lap and disemboweling him with claws — voiding every clause of the boon

title: Pururavas and Urvashi
description: The first mortal king of the Lunar line loves the apsara Urvashi under conditions, loses her when they break, and is eventually reunited
source: Rigveda X.95; Shatapatha Brahmana XI; Vishnu Purana

title: Dhanvantari Emerges at the Churning Bearing Amrita
description: The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana carrying the pot of amrita, linking the churning of the ocean to the origin of Ayurveda

title: Ila/Sudyumna and the founding of the Lunar dynasty
description: From Vaivasvata Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna springs the Lunar dynasty (Chandravamsha) via Budha

title: Prahlada enthroned as Asura king
description: After Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers, Prahlada is enthroned as a righteous Asura king and ancestor of Bali

title: Kapila burns the 60,000 sons of Sagara
description: Sage Kapila incinerates King Sagara's 60,000 sons for accusing him of stealing the ashvamedha horse, the curse later driving Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga

title: Kapila burns the sons of Sagara
description: Sage Kapila incinerates the 60,000 sons of King Sagara for accusing him of stealing the sacrificial horse — the curse that later drives Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga

title: Markandeya granted a short brilliant life
description: The childless sage Mrkandu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son fated to die at sixteen; the radiant boy Markandeya is born and masters the Vedas
source: Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana

title: Matsya Rescues Manu and the Vedas
description: The fish-avatara Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge at the pralaya

title: Descent of Ganga (Gangavatarana)
description: Ganga is brought to earth by Bhagiratha's austerities, her fall broken by Shiva's matted hair, to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons

title: Shiva as Kalantaka conquers Death for Markandeya
description: When Yama casts his noose around the boy clinging to a Shiva-linga, Shiva bursts forth as Kalantaka/Mrtyunjaya, strikes down Death, and blesses Markandeya to remain eternally sixteen and deathless

title: Sudarshana Chakra beheads Rahu
description: Vishnu's time-disc the Sudarshana Chakra (Kala-chakra) beheads the demon Rahu who stole the amrita, the weapon-face of Time cutting off every form at its appointed moment

title: Rishabhadeva avatara born to Nabhi and Merudevi
description: Vishnu descends as Rishabha, son of King Nabhi and Merudevi of the Priyavrata line, an avatara of Narayana who fathers a hundred sons, the eldest being Bharata

title: Rishabha's renunciation and death by forest fire
description: After delivering the Rishabha-gita to his sons and crowning Bharata, Rishabha wanders as a naked avadhuta and quits his body, consumed by a wildfire, absorbed in the Self

title: Emperor Bharata's reign and renunciation
description: Bharata rules Bharata-varsha righteously while inwardly detached, then divides the empire among his sons and retires to Pulaha-ashrama on the Gandaki to meditate

title: Bharata's attachment to the deer and rebirth as a deer
description: The ascetic Bharata becomes attached to an orphaned fawn he rescues; dying with the deer in his mind, he is reborn as a conscious deer remembering his past life

title: Jada Bharata the silent sage and the Rahugana teachings
description: Reborn as a brahmana, the soul feigns idiocy as Jada Bharata, is nearly sacrificed to Bhadra Kali (who saves him), then teaches King Rahugana the forest-of-samsara allegory and attains liberation

title: Satya Yuga — the Age of Truth
description: Dharma stands on all four legs; humans live ~100,000 years in spontaneous righteousness, with meditation as the path to liberation

title: Soma emerges from the churning of the ocean
description: In the Samudra Manthana the Moon (Soma/Chandra) emerges among the fourteen ratnas and is taken by Shiva onto his head, fusing the soma-as-nectar and soma-as-moon ideas

title: Kapila born to Kardama and Devahuti
description: Kapila, an avatara of Viṣṇu and founder-sage of Sankhya, is born to the Prajapati Kardama and Devahuti to impart self-knowledge to his mother

title: Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge
description: Vishnu as the fish Matsya warns Manu of the coming pralaya, has him build a boat loaded with the seeds of life and the seven sages, tows it through the flood, and (in variants) slays the demon Hayagriva to restore the stolen Vedas — marking the start of our Manvantara
source: Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24

title: Kurma supports Mount Mandara at the churning
description: As devas and asuras churn the ocean of milk for amrita using Mount Mandara and the serpent Vasuki, the sinking mountain is supported on the back of Vishnu as the giant tortoise Kurma
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva

title: Dhanvantari and Mohini emerge at the churning
description: During the Samudra Manthana the physician-god Dhanvantari emerges bearing the nectar pot, and Vishnu takes the Mohini form to trick the asuras out of the amrita

title: Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu and saves Prahlada
description: To evade the demon-king Hiranyakashipu's boon, Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha at twilight on a threshold, and disembowels him with his claws while saving his devotee-son Prahlada

title: Rahu beheaded at the churning
description: At the Samudra Manthana the asura Rahu steals the amrita and is beheaded by Vishnu as Mohini, becoming the eclipse-node

title: Exile of the Daityas and Danavas
description: In Krita/Satya Yuga the Daityas and Danavas are exiled from heaven by the devas and take refuge in the Vindhya mountains and the sea (Patala)

title: "I desire not the eight siddhis"
description: giving away the last water, Rantideva renounces even liberation, asking only to enter into and bear the suffering of all embodied beings so they be freed from misery

title: A Brāhmaṇa Is Adaṇḍya
description: Rāma's councillors Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha and Kaśyapa rule that a brāhmaṇa cannot be corporally punished, forcing Rāma to let the plaintiff dog name the sentence

title: Agastya finds the corpse-eater at the empty lake
description: wandering the deserted future-Daṇḍaka, Agastya sees a radiant heaven-dweller descend from a swan-chariot to devour a human corpse floating in a pristine lake

title: Ahalyā's śāpa-mokṣa
description: Gautama's curse on Ahalyā is capped with an end-condition and released by Rāma's presence, the classic curse-liberation

title: Aṅgada crowned king of Kiṣkindhā
description: at Rāma's final departure Sugrīva follows him into retirement, first enthroning his nephew Aṅgada so the once-disinherited prince inherits his father Vālī's throne in full

title: Aṅgada leads the fast unto death on the southern shore
description: deadline broken and Sītā unfound, the despairing prince, recalling his father's killing and dreading Sugrīva's wrath, resolves with his party on prāyopaveśa rather than return in disgrace

title: Aṅgada leads the southern search-party
description: Sugrīva entrusts the decisive southern quarter to Aṅgada, commanding Hanumān, Jāmbavān, Nīla and others to seek Sītā across the Vindhyas and the southern ocean within one month

title: Aṅgada made crown prince of Kiṣkindhā
description: at Sugrīva's consecration by Lakṣmaṇa, Vālī's orphaned son Aṅgada is installed as yuvarāja (heir-apparent), fulfilling his father's dying wish and securing the succession without civil war

title: Aṅgada plants his immovable foot (Aṅgada-Rāyabāram)
description: in vernacular retelling Aṅgada roots his foot in the assembly and challenges the whole court to lift it; every rākṣasa champion and Rāvaṇa himself fail, and he taunts the emperor to bow at Rāma's feet instead

title: Aṅgada slays the rākṣasa Vajradaṃṣṭra
description: in the successive sorties before Laṅkā's gates the crown prince kills the commander Vajradaṃṣṭra, fighting as the foremost vānara duellist after Hanumān

title: Aṅgada's defiant embassy to Rāvaṇa's court
description: sent as Rāma's envoy demanding Sītā's release on pain of death and Vibhīṣaṇa's enthronement, Aṅgada is ordered seized, but leaps to the palace roof wrecking a turret and returns unharmed

title: Aśokasundarī curses Huṇḍa
description: inviolate and enraged, she dooms the demon to die at the hands of the very Nahuṣa she is destined to marry, converting prophecy into fate

title: Bharata looses the Saṃvarta weapon
description: unable to break the Gandharvas by ordinary arms, Bharata discharges the pralaya-scaled Saṃvarta astra and annihilates the host in a single stroke — three hundred thousand slain
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 101; the three-crore host under Śailūṣa is the Agni Purāṇa's, ch. 11

title: Birth of Kuśanābha's hundred daughters
description: King Kuśanābha of Mahodaya begets one hundred daughters of unmatched beauty on the apsarā Ghṛtācī

title: Birth of Mandodarī to Maya and Hemā
description: the asura-architect Maya and the apsarā Hemā have a daughter, Mandodarī, left in Maya's care when Hemā is recalled to the celestial sphere

title: Birth of Śala, Dala and Vala
description: Suśobhanā bears Parikṣit three sons under her father's curse, the eldest Śala succeeding to the Ikṣvāku throne

title: Birth of Śūrpaṇakhā
description: Śūrpaṇakhā is born to the sage Viśravas and the rākṣasī Kaikasī, youngest sibling of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa and Vibhīṣaṇa

title: Brahmā commands the creation of the vānara host
description: the devas beget shape-shifting monkey-sons (and Jāmbavān springs from Brahmā's yawn) as an army for the coming Rāma-avatāra

title: Brahmā parts them and ends the feud
description: the Grandfather descends, dissolves their brute-nature, restores the sages to human form, declares Viśvāmitra's ordeal had won Hariścandra heaven, and reconciles the rivals in an embrace

title: Brahmā's oracle names Raji the pivot of the devāsura war
description: Deadlocked devas and asuras both ask Brahmā who will win, and he answers: whichever side the mortal king Raji joins

title: Brahmā's rebuke: tapas without dāna
description: reaching Brahmaloka yet stricken by impossible hunger, Śveta is told by Brahmā that he gave no gifts, and is sentenced to eat his own endlessly-regenerating flesh daily

title: Brahmadatta's marriage heals the hundred hunchbacked daughters
description: Kuśanābha gives all hundred daughters to King Brahmadatta of Kāmpilya, and at the touch of his hand in the wedding rite each maiden's crookedness vanishes and her beauty returns

title: Breaking of Śiva's bow and wedding of Sītā
description: escorted by Viśvāmitra to Mithilā, Rāma snaps the bow of Śiva and wins Sītā's hand in the quadruple wedding of Daśaratha's sons

title: Bṛhaspati's heterodox-delusion rites corrupt the Rājeyas
description: The destitute Indra begs Bṛhaspati, who performs strengthening rites and promulgates a deluding anti-Vedic teaching that makes Raji's sons fall from dharma
source: Vishnu Purana IV.9; Matsya Purana 24; Bhagavata Purana 9.17

title: Cirakārī deliberates too slowly to kill his mother
description: ordered by the enraged Gautama to slay the adulterous Ahalyā, the habitually slow-acting son Cirakārī deliberates until his father repents, and slowness redeems them both

title: Cūlī grants Somadā a mind-born son, Brahmadatta
