description: The gandharvī Somadā, daughter of Ūrmilā, serves the ascetic Cūlī and, being husbandless, asks as her boon a son by his tapas; the sage brings forth the mānasa son Brahmadatta, who rules Kāmpilya

title: Dala's poisoned arrow kills prince Senajit
description: the defiant heir Dala aims a poisoned shaft at Vāmadeva, but by the sage's word it turns and slays his own ten-year-old son Senajit, and a second arrow freezes in his hand

title: Daśaratha rides into the sky
description: by kingly merit and tapas Daśaratha mounts his war-chariot and ascends past the winds into the region of the nakṣatras to confront Saturn where he approaches Rohiṇī

title: Death of Dhruvasandhi and the Kosala usurpation
description: the Solar-line king is killed by a lion while hunting, and Yudhājit of Ujjayinī slays Vīrasena of Kaliṅga to crown the younger prince Śatrujit at Ayodhyā

title: Devarāta receives Śiva's bow in trust
description: The gods deposit Śiva's colossal bow (Pināka) as a nyāsa with king Devarāta of Videha, the heirloom on which the Rāmāyaṇa marriage-plot turns

title: Durgā worship instituted at Vārāṇasī and Ayodhyā
description: Subāhu wins the boon that the Goddess remain forever as Kāśī's guardian Durgā, and the restored King Sudarśana establishes her worship throughout Kosala — the text's charter of royal Devī cult

title: Fall of Rāvaṇa and the agni-parīkṣā
description: Rāma slays Rāvaṇa at Laṅkā, then publicly repudiates Sītā, who is returned unscathed from the fire by Agni before Rāma accepts her

title: Founding of Puṣkalāvatī for Puṣkala
description: in the adjacent Gandharva country Bharata founds Puṣkalāvatī (Charsadda) and installs his younger son Puṣkala, then dwells in the two cities five years before returning to Ayodhyā

title: Founding of Takṣaśilā for Takṣa
description: on the conquered Gāndhāra land Bharata raises the city of Takṣaśilā (Taxila) and consecrates his elder son Takṣa as its king

title: Gaṇeśa grounds the Raṅganātha vimāna
description: bearing the vimāna south after the Laṅkā war, Vibhīṣaṇa entrusts it at Tiruvaraṅgam to a cowherd boy (Gaṇeśa in disguise) who sets it on the earth, rooting Raṅganātha at Śrīraṅgam forever

title: Gaṇeśa installs Mahābala at Gokarṇa
description: after Rāvaṇa wins Śiva's liṅga by penance and is tricked into setting it down, Gaṇanāyaka roots it at Gokarṇa as Mahābala, its power reaching to the seven nether worlds

title: Gaṅgā is named at Devprayag
description: the Bhāgīrathī of Bhagīratha's descent meets the Alaknandā, and from this confluence the united river is first called Gaṅgā

title: Haihaya–Kāśī wars and Pratardana's vengeance
description: After the Vītahavyas/Haihayas crush Haryaśva, Sudeva and Divodāsa of Kāśī, Bharadvāja's putrakāmeṣṭi yields Pratardana, who exterminates the Vītahavyas; Vītahavya is made a brāhmaṇa by Bhṛgu

title: Hanumān mistakes Mandodarī for Sītā
description: searching Rāvaṇa's sleeping palace, Hanumān momentarily takes the radiant queen Mandodarī for Sītā, then reasons the captive could never sleep amid luxury

title: Hariścandra restored by the Ajā Ekādaśī
description: the truth-king, enslaved at the cremation ground, keeps the Ajā fast on Gautama's counsel and regains son, wife, and kingdom

title: Huṇḍa abducts Aśokasundarī
description: the daitya lord of Mahodaya carries her off and tries to win her by conjured illusion, an āśrama and false ascetic she sees through

title: Huṇḍa kidnaps the infant Nahuṣa
description: learning his destined slayer is born to King Āyu, Huṇḍa steals the newborn and orders him killed and cooked, but the cook's compassion spares the child

title: Indra declares himself Raji's son to keep the throne
description: Owing Raji the rank of Indra, Indra bows at his feet claiming 'you are my father,' and the gratified Raji leaves him functioning as king of heaven

title: Indra purified at Suchindram
description: sin-stained from seducing Ahalyā and cursed by Gautama, Indra travels to the far-southern liṅga and is washed pure (*śuci*), giving the town its name *Śuci-Indram*

title: Indra slays the apostate sons of Raji and regains heaven
description: Once the deluded Rājeyas abandon the Veda and dharma, Indra kills all five hundred with the thunderbolt and recovers his station and sacrificial shares
source: Vishnu Purana IV.9; Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Matsya Purana 24

title: Indra surrenders heaven to Raji for his lifetime
description: In the Bhāgavata's variant, Indra, terrified of Prahlāda, hands the celestial kingdom back to Raji and clasps his feet, and Raji holds heaven until his death

title: Indra's endless night-watch
description: because his cleansing is held to continue, the temple's late-night *ardhajāma* pūjā is understood as Indra's own worship, kept invisibly each night

title: Initiation into the inverted mantra "marā marā"
description: too sin-laden for the Name itself, the penitent robber is set to repeating Rāma's name in reverse, which becomes Rāma on the tongue

title: Instigation of Khara and the battle of Janasthāna
description: the mutilated Śūrpaṇakhā rouses Khara, whose fourteen champions and then full host of 14,000 with Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras are annihilated by Rāma single-handed

title: Jāmbavān awakens Hanumān's forgotten powers
description: the aged bear-king, who once circumambulated Trivikrama, rouses Hanumān to leap the ocean to Laṅkā

title: Janaka gives Yājñavalkya the Videhas and himself
description: Taught the Self as one's own light through waking, dream and deep sleep, and told 'you have attained the fearless, Janaka,' the king answers: 'I give you the Videhas, and myself with them, into servitude'

title: Janaka passes the agnihotra test to Yājñavalkya
description: Janaka of Videha quizzes three brāhmaṇas on the agnihotra and drives off; Yājñavalkya pursues him, and the king wins the boon of unlimited questions — 'thenceforth Janaka was a brahman'

title: Kārtavīrya Arjuna's thousand-armed empire and fall
description: The Haihaya-Yādava emperor of Māhiṣmatī, boon-armed by Dattātreya, seizes Jamadagni's wish-cow and is slain by Paraśurāma, triggering the twenty-one Kṣatriya exterminations
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.11; Bhāgavata IX.15-16, IX.23; Mahābhārata

title: Kaśyapa and Aditi worship the icon
description: reborn as Kaśyapa and Aditi, the couple keep the image and Viṣṇu is born to them as Upendra/Vāmana, the second of the three births

title: Khaṭvāṅga wins the devas' war
description: the unconquerable Ikṣvāku king Khaṭvāṅga, son of Viśvasaha and ancestor of Rāma, is summoned by the demigods to fight the asuras, secures their victory, and is offered any boon he wishes

title: King Śveta of Vidarbha renounces for tapas
description: Sudeva's son Śveta, after a thousand-year righteous reign, sets his brother Suratha on the throne and withdraws to austerities by the forest lake

title: Kuśa's four sons found their cities
description: The Brahmā-born king Kuśa's sons Kuśāmba, Kuśanābha, Ādhūrtarajasa, and Vasu build Kauśāmbī, Mahodaya, Dharmāraṇya, and Girivraja respectively

title: Kuśanābha's putrakāmeṣṭi and the birth of Gādhi
description: The sonless Kuśanābha performs a son-yielding sacrifice at which his father Kuśa promises a supremely righteous son, and Gādhi — Viśvāmitra's father — is born

title: Kuśanābha's teaching of kṣamā
description: Rather than avenging the god's assault, Kuśanābha praises his daughters' forbearance, declaring that on kṣamā the universe is established, and takes counsel on their marriage

title: Liberation in a single muhūrta
description: returning at once to earth, Khaṭvāṅga declares nothing dearer to him than Nārāyaṇa, casts off queens, kingdom and the guṇa-swayed senses, and merges in Vāsudeva/Brahman before the 48-minute hour is out

title: Makarākṣa slain by the Āgneyāstra
description: Rāma fits the fire-weapon of Agni to his bow and pierces Makarākṣa through the chest, felling Khara's son as his father had fallen

title: Makarākṣa's vow of vengeance
description: the son of Khara joyfully accepts the charge, vowing to avenge his father slain by Rāma at Janasthāna

title: Māṇḍakarṇi yields and weds all five
description: unlike the wrathful Viśvāmitra, the sage succumbs to desire and takes the five apsaras as his wives rather than cursing them

title: Māṇḍakarṇi's ten-thousand-year immersion
description: the sage stands submerged in the lake living on air alone for ten thousand years, heaping up ascetic power that alarms the gods

title: Mandodarī bears Meghanāda (Indrajit)
description: Laṅkā's crown prince is born to Rāvaṇa and Mandodarī, named for his thundercloud birth-cry

title: Mandodarī counsels Rāvaṇa to return Sītā
description: with Vibhīṣaṇa and Mālyavān, Mandodarī urges restoring Sītā and peace with Rāma, declaring him no mere man; Rāvaṇa refuses

title: Mandodarī remarries Vibhīṣaṇa (later tradition)
description: at Rāma's counsel the widowed queen weds the newly crowned Vibhīṣaṇa, securing Laṅkā's throne; absent from the Vālmīki critical edition [late text] [disputed]

title: Mandodarī's lament over the slain Rāvaṇa
description: widowed on the battlefield, Mandodarī names lust for Sītā as the cause of Laṅkā's ruin and recognises Rāma as the eternal Viṣṇu

title: Manoramā's flight to Bharadvāja's hermitage
description: the widowed queen escapes Ayodhyā with the child-heir Sudarśana and the minister Vidalla, taking refuge under the sage's protection against Yudhājit's pursuit

title: Nahuṣa fostered by Vasiṣṭha
description: the rescued infant is laid in Vasiṣṭha's hermitage, where the sage and Arundhatī raise him and school him in the Vedas and arms

title: Nahuṣa weds Aśokasundarī
description: blessed by Śiva and Pārvatī, the Candravaṃśa king marries the Kalpavṛkṣa-born maiden, who in this Padma frame (not Virajā of the epics) becomes mother of Yayāti

title: Nala bridges the sea to Laṅkā
description: Viśvakarman's vānara son directs the building of the Setu in five days for Rāma's army

title: Nārada boasts against Śiva's warning
description: ignoring Śiva's counsel to tell no one, Nārada brags of his victory over lust to Brahmā and then to Viṣṇu, who resolves to humble him by māyā

title: Nārada curses the mocking Rudra-gaṇas
description: the two attendants of Śiva who laughed at his monkey face are cursed to be born as demons from a rākṣasa womb, with the mitigation that they will return to Śiva's side

title: Nārada recites the saṃkṣipta-Rāmāyaṇa to Vālmīki
description: asked who is the perfectly virtuous man, Nārada answers "Rāma" and plants the seed of the epic

title: Nārada's penance and the false conquest of Kāma
description: Kāmadeva, sent by Indra, fails to break Nārada's Himalayan tapas at Śiva's hallowed spot, and the sage swells with pride

title: Nārada's three-fold curse on Viṣṇu
description: the enraged sage curses Viṣṇu to a mortal birth, to grief in separation from his wife, and to monkey companions — the Śaiva seed of the Rāma avatāra, which Viṣṇu gladly accepts

title: Nikumbha's curse empties Vārāṇasī
description: Dishonored by King Divodāsa, the gaṇa Nikumbha curses Vārāṇasī to stand deserted a thousand years, and Śiva and Pārvatī dwell in the emptied city while the king removes to the Gomatī

title: Parashurama founds the Pura Mahadev yatra
description: Parashurama carries Ganga water on foot from Garhmukteshwar to worship Shiva at Pura Mahadev, an alternative founding of the kanwar vow [folk] [regional]

title: Paraśurāma reclaims Gomāntaka
description: the axe-bearing avatar shoots an arrow into the sea, forces the waters back, and settles Brahmin gotras on the uncovered Konkan strip that becomes Goa

title: Paraśurāma seeks out Dattātreya
description: sick at heart after exterminating the kṣatriyas twenty-one times, the axe-wielder comes to his guru Dattātreya asking what world, bondage, and release truly are, and receives the Tripurā Rahasya

title: Paraśurāma's axe releases the Lauhitya
description: bathing in the Brahmakuṇḍa frees Paraśurāma's axe and matricide-sin, and he cleaves the mountain wall to loose the river into the world

title: Puruṣottama appears in the guise of an ascetic
description: after Ratnagrīva's five-day fast at the Gaṅgā-ocean confluence the Lord comes disguised, promising darśana at noon and naming five who will reach the highest place

title: Raji destroys the asura host for the devas
description: Fighting for the gods under the Indra-ship bargain, the Aila king Raji slays the asura armies and wins the war the devas could not
source: Vishnu Purana IV.9; Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Matsya Purana 24

title: Rājñā Devī carried from Laṅkā
description: displeased with Rāvaṇa who first installed her, the goddess Rājñā (Ragnya) asks Hanumān to bear her seat north from Laṅkā to Tulmul, where she settles as Kṣīr Bhavānī

title: Rāma accepts fourteen years' exile
description: honouring Daśaratha's boons to Kaikeyī, Rāma renounces the throne without protest and departs for the forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa

title: Rāma appoints Bharata over the Gandharva war
description: Rāma assents to the conquest and dispatches Bharata with his two sons Takṣa and Puṣkala, the campaign framed from the outset as a city-founding for the next generation

title: Rāma breaks the bow; the quadruple wedding at Mithilā
description: Rāma snaps Śiva's bow and the Videha and Ikṣvāku houses are knit fourfold: Rāma–Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa–Ūrmilā, Bharata–Māṇḍavī, Śatrughna–Śrutakīrti

title: Rama carries water from Sultanganj to Baidyanath
description: Eastern tradition holds Rama himself bore Ganga water from the uttaravahini Ganga at Sultanganj to the Vaidyanath Jyotirlinga at Deoghar, chartering the Shravani Mela route [folk] [regional]

title: Rāma keeps the Vijayā Ekādaśī at the ocean
description: counselled before the crossing to Laṅkā, Rāma keeps the Vijayā fast by whose merit the ocean is crossed and Rāvaṇa defeated

title: Rāma recognizes Satī and dispels her doubt
description: Undeceived, Rāma salutes Satī by name as Dakṣa's daughter and asks why she wanders alone in Sītā's guise; her doubt collapses in shame

title: Rāma's akāl-bodhan founds the autumn Durgā Pūjā calendar
description: Rāma awakens Durgā out of season in autumn and worships her from Ṣaṣṭhī to Daśamī before the Laṅkā war, the charter of Bengal's Śāradīyā festival days

title: Rāma's Aśvamedha and the capture of the horse by Lava and Kuśa
description: after the return to Ayodhyā the sacrificial horse wanders under Śatrughna's guard until Sītā's twin sons seize it at Vālmīki's āśrama, forcing recognition and reunion

title: Rāma's aśvamedha horse nears the Nīla mountain
description: Śatrughna's army reaches the Puruṣottama region and the minister Sumati recounts the old tale of Ratnagrīva of Kāñcī

title: Rāma's enlightenment and the charter of jīvanmukti
description: Rāma attains repose in the Self, is roused from absorption, and chooses to rule and act while inwardly free, recasting the coming Rāmāyaṇa as a jīvanmukta's career
source: Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, Nirvāṇa Uttarārdha VI.2, final sargas

title: Rāma's expiation at Devprayag
description: Rāma performs penance at the Bhāgīrathī–Alaknandā confluence to cleanse the brahma-hatyā of killing Rāvaṇa; the Raghunāthjī temple marks the site [regional]

title: Rāma's Navarātri before the war on Rāvaṇa
description: after Sītā's abduction, Nārada prescribes the autumn Navarātra-vrata; Rāma performs it and the Devī grants victory, the recovery of Sītā, and long rule

title: Rāma's offered eye (akāl-bodhan)
description: the Śākta twin of the tale: worshipping Durgā before Laṅkā with 108 blue lotuses, Rāma finds one hidden and prepares to give his own lotus-eye until the Goddess stays his hand

title: Rāma's retort and the arrow-duel
description: Rāma recalls slaying Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras and fourteen thousand rākṣasas alone at Janasthāna, then breaks Makarākṣa's chariot and horses in a shaft-storm

title: Rāma-paṭṭābhiṣeka and Rāma-rājya
description: Rāma is crowned at Ayodhyā and his reign becomes the proverbial ideal polity of dharma, without untimely death or want

title: Rāmavaradāyinī — the boon to Rāma
description: southbound in search of Sītā, Rāma is blessed by the goddess at Tuljapur, folding the kṣetra into Rāmāyaṇa geography

title: Rantideva keeps nothing for the morrow
description: the Bhārata-line king, son of Saṅkṛti, gives away all that comes to him and lives in voluntary poverty, he and his household bearing want with perfect equanimity

title: Ratnagrīva proclaims the pilgrimage to Puruṣottama
description: minister Uttama announces the yātrā through Kāñcī and all four varṇas and occupational groups march east singing of Kṛṣṇa and Viṣṇu

title: Ravana carries the first kanwar
description: Ravana fetches Ganga water in a shoulder-pole kanwar and pours it on the Shiva-linga at Pura Mahadev (Baghpat), releasing Shiva from the poison's heat — the most-cited first-kanwariya charter [folk]

title: Rāvaṇa dispatches Makarākṣa
description: grieving his lost champions, Rāvaṇa sends Makarākṣa, son of the slain demon-lord Khara, out from Laṅkā to destroy the Rāghavas

title: Rāvaṇa weds Mandodarī; Maya gifts the śakti
description: meeting Maya in the forest, Rāvaṇa receives Mandodarī in marriage along with an unfailing śakti-javelin later hurled at Lakṣmaṇa

title: Rāvaṇa's contempt-clause boon
description: ten-thousand-year head-offering tapas wins invulnerability from all beings except the humans and monkeys he omits

title: Rāvaṇa's funeral; Mandodarī's water-offering
description: at Rāma's direction Vibhīṣaṇa performs full funeral rites and Mandodarī with the harem women makes the water-offering before Vibhīṣaṇa's coronation

title: Ṛkṣarajas' pool-transformation begets Vālī and Sugrīva
description: the first vānara, turned woman in an enchanted pool, bears Indra's son Vālī and Sūrya's son Sugrīva

title: Śabarī awaits Rāma at Pampā Sarovar
description: Directed by Kabandha, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa reach the lake-side āśrama where the ascetic Śabarī, having long awaited Rāma's darśana, offers him fruit (famously pre-tasted berries) before attaining liberation
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 70–74; folk amplification of the tasted berries

title: Agastya directs Rāma to Pañcavaṭī
description: Agastya gifts Rāma Viṣṇu's bow and divine weapons and names Pañcavaṭī on the Godāvarī as the exiles' dwelling-site

title: Śala borrows Vāmadeva's Vāmī mares
description: to run down an uncatchable deer King Śala borrows the wind-swift Vāmī mares of the ṛṣi Vāmadeva, on pledge to return them

title: Śala slain by four Rākṣasas
description: Śala breaks his word and keeps the mares as unfit for a brāhmaṇa, rebuffing Atreya and the sage, until Vāmadeva's tapas conjures four spear-armed Rākṣasas who kill him

title: Sampāti sets Aṅgada's party on the path to Laṅkā
description: the wingless vulture, roused by the lament for his brother Jaṭāyu, tells the fasting vānaras that Rāvaṇa holds Sītā in Laṅkā a hundred yojanas across the sea, giving the search its target

title: Saṃvarta the avadhūta unsettles Paraśurāma
description: the naked, serene wanderer Saṃvarta, brother of Bṛhaspati, whose unaccountable bliss punctures the warrior's pride, points Paraśurāma toward the secret of the Goddess Tripurā

title: Sarvārtha-siddha's Blow
description: the brāhmaṇa mendicant Sarvārtha-siddha admits he struck the dog on the head while hungry on his alms-round because it blocked the road and would not move

title: Śaśikalā's svayaṃvara and night wedding at Kāśī
description: the Devī commands the Kāśī princess in a dream to wed Sudarśana; defying the assembled kings' threats, King Subāhu marries her to the exile privately in his palace

title: Satī tests Rāma in Sītā's form
description: Doubting that the weeping prince is Viṣṇu incarnate, Satī assumes Sītā's exact form and places herself in Rāma's path

title: Satī's vision of multiplied Rāmas
description: Withdrawing abashed, Satī sees countless Rāmas, Sītās and Lakṣmaṇas on every side, attended by all the gods — the one Lord reflected through creation

title: Śatrughna Slays Lavaṇāsura and Founds Mathurā
description: Mathurā is said to be founded where Śatrughna, Rāma's brother, slays the asura Lavaṇa, son of Madhu, bridging the Rāmāyaṇa and Kṛṣṇa eras

title: Bali's Conquest of the Three Worlds
description: Revived and empowered by Śukra and the Bhṛgus, the Asura king Bali storms Svarga and dispossesses Indra, becoming sovereign of all three worlds

title: Bharadvāja receives Rāma on the exile journey
description: On the vana-yātrā, Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa cross the Yamunā and reach the sage Bharadvāja's āśrama at the Prayāga confluence; he honours them and directs them onward to Chitrakūṭa as the place of exile-dwelling

title: Birth and naming of Raghu
description: Raghu is born to Dilipa and Sudakshina after Dilipa's service to the wish-cow Nandini, named 'the swift' for his future conquests

title: Birth in the Bhargava line
description: Paraśurāma, aṃśa of Viṣṇu, is born to the Bhṛgu sage Jamadagni and Reṇukā as the youngest of five sons

title: Birth of Hanuman to Anjana and Vayu
description: Hanuman is born to the apsara-turned-vanari Anjana and the vanara chief Kesari, conceived through the agency of Vayu, making him Vayuputra
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 66; Uttara Kanda 35-36

title: Birth of Lakṣmaṇa and the pāyasa division
description: From Daśaratha's putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice a divine being yields sacred pāyasa; Sumitrā's two half-portions produce the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, Lakṣmaṇa attaching to Rāma

title: Birth of Māndhātā from His Father's Body
description: The Ikṣvāku cakravartin Māndhātā is born from his father's body after the king drank consecrated fertility-water, and is suckled by Indra
source: Mahabharata Vana & Drona Parvas; Bhagavata 9; Vishnu Purana

title: Birth of Rāvaṇa and his siblings
description: Approaching Viśravas at an inauspicious twilight, Kaikasī bears the ten-headed Rāvaṇa (marked by ill omens), Kumbhakarṇa, the righteous Vibhīṣaṇa, and Śūrpaṇakhā

title: Birth of Sītā from the furrow
description: Ploughing a sacrificial field, King Janaka turns up an infant girl in the furrow and adopts her as Sītā, an ayonijā born of the Earth-goddess

title: Birth of Subāhu to Tāṭakā and Sunda
description: Subāhu is born of the yakṣiṇī Tāṭakā by the yakṣa Sunda, brother of Mārīca, in the line cursed by Agastya

title: Birth of Tāṭakā from Suketu
description: The childless yakṣa Suketu wins from Brahmā a daughter, Tāṭakā, endowed with the strength of a thousand elephants

title: Birth of the Shloka Meter (Valmiki's Curse)
description: Grieving a hunter's killing of a mating krauncha bird, Valmiki utters a curse that spontaneously takes metrical form, birthing the shloka (shoka to shloka) — the meter of Sanskrit epic

title: Birth of Vālī and Sugrīva from Ṛkṣaraja
description: The vānara lord Ṛkṣaraja is transformed into a woman; Indra's seed on his hair begets Vālī and Sūrya's on his nape begets Sugrīva

title: Birth of Ṛśyaśṛṅga from a doe
description: Vibhāṇḍaka's seed is swallowed by a doe, who bears a single-horned boy raised in total isolation, ignorant of women, his chastity amassing great tapas

title: Choice of Citrakūṭa on Bharadvāja's counsel
description: After crossing the Gaṅgā with Guha and reaching Bharadvāja's Prayāga āśrama, Rāma is directed to settle at Citrakūṭa as the ideal tapovana

title: Ṛcīka's swapped oblations and the birth of Jamadagni
description: Two caru-porridges meant for brahmin and warrior sons are exchanged between Satyavatī and her mother, deferring the kṣatriya temper a generation so Jamadagni is born serene but Paraśurāma becomes the axe-bearer

title: Counsel at the putrakāmeṣṭi — relaying the Sanatkumāra prophecy
description: Sumantra privately advises childless Daśaratha, recalling Sanatkumāra's forecast about Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, prompting the son-seeking sacrifice sealed by Vasiṣṭha

title: Daśaratha resolves to crown Rāma yuvarāja
description: The aged Daśaratha resolves to install Rāma as crown prince while he lives; the assembly acclaims the choice and the rite is rushed under Puṣya nakṣatra

title: Daśaratha's righteous reign as last pre-Rāma Ikṣvāku king
description: Daśaratha, son of Aja and grandson of Raghu, reigns at Ayodhyā as the last Sūryavaṃśa king before Rāma, prosperous but childless, served by Vasiṣṭha and his ministers
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 5–8; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.10; Kālidāsa Raghuvaṃśa 8–9

title: Descent of the Gaṅgā at Gaṅgā-dvāra
description: The Gaṅgā debouches from the Himalaya onto the plain at Haridwar, the gateway by which the goddess first enters the world of men, linked to Bhagīratha's bringing-down of the river

title: Descent of the Sarayū from Brahmā's Mānasa lake
description: The Sarayū flows forth from Brahmā's Mānasa(rovara) lake, whence its name (sarat, 'flows out'), and runs to meet the Gaṅgā
actors: Sarayū (river); pointed out by Viśvāmitra to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 23–24; (variant) Skanda Purāṇa Ayodhyā-māhātmya — Viṣṇu's foot-thumb

title: Devas petition Brahmā for the Nāṭyaveda
description: At the Tretā-yuga's dawn the gods ask Brahmā for an accessible 'fifth Veda' diversion open to all four varṇas

title: Dilīpa's childlessness and the journey to Vasiṣṭha
description: The ideal Sūryavaṃśa king Dilīpa, childless despite a flawless reign, drives with queen Sudakṣiṇā to Vasiṣṭha's hermitage to seek the cause and cure

title: Ganga springs from Vishnu's foot (Vamana)
description: When Vamana's raised step pierces the cosmic shell, the Causal Ocean pours in and washes his foot, becoming the Ganga, hence Vishnupadi

title: Gādhi's place in the Kuśika line
description: Gādhi, Lunar-dynasty king of Kānyakubja in the Kuśika branch, stands as the genealogical hinge-node father of Viśvāmitra and Satyavatī
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.15; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 32–34; Mahābhārata Ādi & Vana Parva

title: Guha welcomes Rama at Shringaverapura
description: The Nishada chief Guha rushes out, embraces his friend Rama, and offers his whole kingdom; Rama accepts only water and fodder

title: Hanumān meets Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa
description: Sent by the anxious Sugrīva, Hanumān approaches the brothers disguised as a mendicant, is reassured of their good faith, and carries them on his shoulders to Sugrīva

title: Hanumān's leap across the ocean
description: From Mount Mahendra Hanumān launches a hundred-yojana leap across the southern ocean toward Laṅkā

title: Hanumān's leap and search of Laṅkā
description: Hanumān crosses the ocean, searches Rāvaṇa's city by night, and comes upon the Aśoka-vāṭikā

title: Hariścandra's vow to Varuṇa and Rohita's birth
description: Childless Hariścandra vows to sacrifice his firstborn to Varuṇa; a son Rohita is born, but the king endlessly postpones the offering

title: Harishchandra's vow to Varuna for a son
description: Childless King Harishchandra prays to Varuna and vows to sacrifice his promised son; Varuna grants the boon and Rohita is born

title: Satyavatī becomes the river Kauśikī
description: Viśvāmitra tells how his elder sister Satyavatī, wife of Ṛcīka, followed her husband to heaven in her very body and became the Himalayan river Kauśikī (Kosi), by whose banks he dwells

title: Shravan Kumar bears his parents in a kavad
description: The devoted son carries his blind parents in slung baskets on a shoulder-yoke and is accidentally shot by Dasharatha; pilgrimage lore makes his yoke the prototype of the kanwar

title: Śibi and the dove — the flesh-offering
description: Indra (hawk) and Agni (dove) test King Śibi, who protects the refugee dove by offering his own flesh equal to its weight, finally his whole body

title: Indumatī's svayaṃvara at Vidarbha
description: At her bride-choice, Indumatī passes the gallery of suitor-kings and garlands Aja, choosing him before all the assembled royalty

title: Jabali counsels Rama (materialist argument)
description: The brahmin Jabali urges Rama with proto-Carvaka materialist arguments (no afterlife, ritual for the dead is futile); Rama rebukes him

title: Janaka's debate-assembly convened
description: King Janaka of Videha assembles the learned Brahmins at a sacrifice, offering a thousand gold-horned cattle to the greatest knower of Brahman; Yājñavalkya claims the prize, provoking eight challengers

title: Kabandha's double curse and disfigurement
description: The celestial being (Viśvāvasu/Danu) is struck by Indra's vajra into a headless trunk and cursed by sage Sthūlaśiras to remain a monster until Rāma severs his arms and burns him

title: Kaikasī's washed-away earthen liṅga
description: Rāvaṇa's mother Kaikasī loses her daily sand liṅga to the tide and Rāvaṇa vows to fetch Śiva's true Ātma-liṅga

title: Kaikeyī's marriage-condition
description: Aśvapati gives Kaikeyī to Daśaratha on the condition that her son inherit Ayodhyā's throne

title: Kauśika's hospitality at Vasiṣṭha's hermitage
description: King Kauśika, resting with his army, is feasted entirely by Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā/Kāmadhenu, igniting his covetousness for it

title: Kāmadhenu conflict — the spark
description: King Kauśika tries to seize Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā/Nandinī by force after the sage refuses to sell her

title: Lakṣmaṇa's request for liberating knowledge
description: After Rāma's coronation at Ayodhyā, Lakṣmaṇa asks his brother to teach him the bhakti and jñāna by which one crosses saṃsāra, supplying the Gītā's seeker-frame

title: Mantharā sees Ayodhyā festive
description: Mantharā climbs the palace terrace and learns Rāma is to be consecrated yuvarāja the next dawn

title: Mataṅga's disciples promise Śabarī that Rāma will come
description: The aged tribal ascetic Śabarī, having humbly served Mataṅga's hermitage, is blessed by the departing sages and told to wait at Pampā for Rāma

title: Mārīca and Subāhu defile Viśvāmitra's sacrifice
description: Mārīca and his brother Subāhu rain flesh and blood on Viśvāmitra's forest yajña, which the boy-princes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are sent to guard

title: Nahuṣa installed as Indra
description: After Indra flees the sin of slaying Vṛtra, the gods elect the virtuous mortal emperor Nahuṣa to the vacant throne of heaven, augmenting his tapas

title: Śāntā fostered from Ayodhyā to Aṅga
description: Daśaratha of Ayodhyā gives his daughter Śāntā (born to Kausalyā), elder sister of Rāma, as a foster/adopted daughter to his childless friend King Lomapāda of Aṅga, where she is raised as the Aṅga princess
source: Mahābhārata Vana-parva ~113; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa ~9–11; Purāṇic genealogies

title: Paraśurāma Fills Five Lakes with Kṣatriya Blood
description: Between Tretā and Dvāpara, Paraśurāma in his twenty-one exterminations of the kṣatriyas fills five lakes at Samanta-pañcaka with their blood and offers tarpaṇa, naming the field

title: Paraśurāma receives the Paraśu from Śiva
description: After his austerities, Paraśurāma is gifted Śiva's battle-axe (paraśu), the name-giving weapon of the sixth Daśāvatāra ('Rāma-with-the-axe'), with which he later annihilated the kṣatriya warrior-class twenty-one times over

title: Paraśurāma retires to Mahendragiri
description: After exterminating the kṣatriyas twenty-one times and ceding the conquered earth (to Kaśyapa / to Rāma Dāśarathi), the immortal sixth avatāra Paraśurāma withdraws from worldly action and retires to Mahendragiri in the Eastern Ghāts to perform tapas until the end of the age, making the peak a living Paraśurāma-tīrtha

title: Puṣpaka halted over Kailāsa
description: Rāvaṇa's aerial car Puṣpaka is mysteriously halted as he crosses Mount Kailāsa returning from conquest

title: Purūravas born of Budha and Ilā
description: Purūravas is born to Budha (son of the Moon) and Ilā, Manu's gender-shifting child, grafting Manu's line onto the Moon's at the hinge of the Lunar dynasty
source: Bhagavata Purana IX.1, IX.14; Vishnu Purana IV.1, IV.6

title: Putrakāmeṣṭi and the divine pāyasa
description: Daśaratha's son-seeking sacrifice via Ṛṣyaśṛṅga yields divine pāyasa from the fire to be shared among the queens

title: Putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice and the divine pāyasa
description: Daśaratha performs the son-seeking sacrifice; a being from the fire brings golden pāyasa to beget heirs in whom Viṣṇu descends

title: Reṇukā's chastity and the magic pot
description: Reṇukā, chaste wife of Jamadagni, carries water in an unbaked sand pot held together by her faith alone

title: Reṇukā's unbaked-pot chastity feat
description: Reṇukā, by the power of her perfect chastity, daily moulds a fresh unbaked clay/sand pot at the riverbank and carries water in it back to Jamadagni's hermitage, sometimes balancing it on a live coiled cobra
source: Mahābhārata 3 (Vana-parvan); Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; South Indian folk Māhātmyas

title: Rāma despondent before the final duel
description: On the battlefield before Laṅkā, a war-weary and anxious Rāma faces Rāvaṇa advancing for the climactic duel

title: Rāma dissolves the Setu with his bow-tip at Dhanuṣkoḍi
description: After the war, at Vibhīṣaṇa's request so the causeway could not be reused for invasion, Rāma touches the tip of his bow (dhanuṣ-koḍi) to the Setu to dissolve it, naming the southernmost headland of Pamban Island

title: Rāma exhausted on the battlefield
description: After a punishing day of war, Rāma stands worn out and anxious before the undefeated Rāvaṇa for the final duel

title: Rāma reaches Śṛṅgaverapura; Guha welcomes him
description: On the first stage of exile Rāma arrives at the Niṣāda town on the Gaṅgā and Guha, chief of the Niṣādas and Rāma's friend, comes out with gifts and offers his kingdom

title: Rāma singles out the Māṇḍūkya for Hanumān
description: In the Muktikā dialogue Rāma instructs Hanumān on a graded path of Upaniṣadic study, declaring 'the Māṇḍūkya alone is enough for the liberation of the seeker.'

title: Rāma threatens the ocean and Setu is built
description: When the sea-lord refuses passage to Laṅkā, Rāma readies the brahmāstra; Varuṇa appears, submits, and advises building Rāma Setu with Nala's help

title: Rāvaṇa's digvijaya reaches Ayodhyā
description: In his world-conquest Rāvaṇa marches against the Solar kings and comes to Anaraṇya, reigning Ikṣvāku sovereign of Ayodhyā

title: Satyavrata commits the three sins
description: As a wild prince Satyavrata angers his father, abducts a bride, and kills and eats Vasishtha's sacred cow, for which Vasishtha curses and names him Trishanku

title: Sītā born to Mandodarī and exposed (Jain/Śākta variant)
description: in Guṇabhadra's Uttarapurāṇa, Saṅghadāsa's Vasudevahiṇḍī and the Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa, Sītā is Mandodarī's daughter, abandoned over a doom-prophecy and found by Janaka [regional] [late text]

title: Sītā found in the furrow
description: Ploughing the sacrificial ground, Sīradhvaja Janaka uncovers an infant girl in the furrow (sītā) and raises the ayonijā Earth-daughter as his own

title: Śiva bows to the grieving Rāma in the Daṇḍaka forest
description: Roaming with Satī, Śiva salutes the Sītā-bereft Rāma from afar without revealing himself, planting Satī's doubt about Rāma's divinity
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Satī-khaṇḍa 24; Rāmcaritmānas, Bāl-kāṇḍa

title: Śiva mentally renounces Satī as wife
description: Because Satī wore the form of Sītā, the consort of his chosen Lord, Śiva takes an inner vow of estrangement, acclaimed by a celestial voice that Satī overhears in grief

title: Slander of Sītā in Ayodhyā
description: A washerman's grumble about taking back a wife who lived in another man's house becomes public censure (loka-apavāda) that Rāma the king cannot ignore

title: Slaying of Virādha
description: The rākṣasa Virādha seizes Sītā; the brothers bury him alive, and dying he reverts to the gandharva Tumburu, released by Rāma's touch

title: Sītā's abduction and Rāma's grief (frame)
description: After Rāvaṇa carries off Sītā, Rāma wanders the Daṇḍaka forest in despair, the crisis that occasions the Gītā
source: Padma Purāṇa, Śiva-Gītā 1; cf. Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya Kāṇḍa

title: Sītā's earth-birth in the furrow of Mithilā
description: King Janaka, ploughing the sacrificial field, lifts an infant girl (Sītā) from the furrow and takes her as his daughter; she is ayonijā, born of Earth
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 66; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa (Lakṣmī variant); Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa & Jaina tellings (Rāvaṇa's-daughter variant)

title: Sudarśana receives the Kāmarāja bīja
description: the exiled boy, mishearing the word "klība," unknowingly repeats the seed-syllable "klīṁ," and the pleased Goddess appears, granting him divine bow, inexhaustible arrows, and armour

title: Sudeva of Vaidiśa dies sonless and becomes a preta
description: a pious vaiśya merchant, lacking any heir to perform the sixteen monthly śrāddhas, is fixed in ghosthood despite a life of merit

title: Śūrpaṇakhā goads Rāvaṇa in Laṅkā
description: she taunts Rāvaṇa with the fall of Janasthāna and dwells on Sītā's beauty, steering him toward the abduction that dooms Laṅkā

title: Suśobhanā vanishes into the tank
description: the thirsty queen, led to water when the vow is forgotten, plunges in and disappears, leaving only a single frog behind

title: Śveta freed by Agastya's acceptance of the ornament
description: Śveta presses a celestial ornament on Agastya as the price of deliverance, and the instant the sage accepts it his self-consuming body melts away and he ascends to Svarga

title: Years of war at Lake Mānasa
description: nesting on trees by Mānasarovara, the two ṛṣi-birds fight for many years with beaks, wings, and nails, bloodied red as Kiṃśuka trees

title: The 108 lotuses become the Sandhi Pūjā offering
description: Rāma's offering of 108 blue lotuses (and his readiness to give his own eye) is the prototype of the 108 lamps and lotuses offered at Sandhi Pūjā

title: The Āḍi and Baka grow titanic
description: Vasiṣṭha's mainā swells to two thousand yojanas and Viśvāmitra's heron to three thousand and ninety, two colossal birds joined in combat

title: The anthill rebirth — the robber emerges as Vālmīki
description: after ages of motionless japa an anthill (valmīka) covers him; the returning sages call him out and name him Vālmīki
source: Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 2.6; variant: Skanda Purāṇa, Vaiśākhamāsa-māhātmya 21

title: The ascetic at Ratnagrīva's court
description: an emaciated brāhmaṇa ascetic appears in Kāñcī's assembly and answers the king's question of which god and tīrtha grant liberation with Puruṣottama and the Nīla mountain

title: The asuras refuse Raji's price, the devas accept
description: Raji demands the rank of Indra after victory; Prahlāda's asuras refuse ('Prahlāda is our lord') while the gods consent to the bargain

title: The birth of Paraśurāma told at Hāṭakeśvara
description: the sixth avatāra's nativity is recounted among the kṣetra's glories, grafting the Bhārgava axe-wielder onto the Vaḍnagar ground

title: The boon that asks the hour of death
description: instead of wealth or heaven Khaṭvāṅga asks the gods only how long he has to live, and is told a single muhūrta remains

title: The Carmaṇvatī (Chambal) arises
description: from the hides and blood of the thousands of animals dressed daily at Rantideva's kitchens, a stream is said to flow, named Carmaṇvatī, "she furnished with hides" — the modern Chambal

title: The concealed mansion beneath the lake
description: by his ascetic power Māṇḍakarṇi builds a hidden palace within the water where he dwells unseen with his five wives, their revels heard as music from the surface

title: The consolation-grant of Daṇḍaka
description: to appease the widowed Śūrpaṇakhā, Rāvaṇa grants her free range of the Daṇḍaka forest with Khara and 14,000 rākṣasas installed at Janasthāna as her guardians

title: The converted hunter is reborn as Vālmīki
description: after a pious life of Rāma-japa the redeemed robber dies and is reborn as son of the anthill-covered sage Kṛṇu (Valmīka), destined to popularize Rāma's story in verse

title: The curse ripens as Rāma and the loss of Sītā
description: Bhṛgu's curse comes due when Viṣṇu is born as Rāma and endures years parted from his abducted consort, the frame running on to Durvāsa's prophecy of his reign

title: The Daṇḍa curse empties the Daṇḍaka
description: answering Rāma's question why the land is lifeless, Agastya tells how Ikṣvāku's son Daṇḍa violated Arajā and Śukra's seven-day dust-storm annihilated his kingdom into the deserted Daṇḍaka

title: The Daśaratha-kṛta Śani-stotra composed
description: the king praises Saturn under a cascade of names (Kṛṣṇa, Piṅgala, Babhru, Raudra, Antaka, Saurī, Śanaiścara, Manda), and Śani vows that whoever recites the hymn shall be spared his affliction

title: The Devī's battlefield theophany outside Vārāṇasī
description: ambushed by the usurpers, Sudarśana invokes the Goddess, who appears on her lion and slays Yudhājit and Śatrujit while the surviving kings hymn her

title: The Dog at Rāma's Gate
description: in the open court of Rāma-rājya a wounded dog comes to the palace gate demanding justice, and Rāma orders Lakṣmaṇa to admit the suppliant, refusing to turn away even a dog
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa, prakṣipta sargas after 59; Baroda CE App. I

title: The Dog Departs for Kāśī
description: its case won, the fallen abbot-dog seeks no reinstatement but sets out for Vārāṇasī to fast unto death (prāya) in the sacred city

title: The estranged silence on Kailāsa before the Dakṣa-yajña
description: Śiva passes into long samādhi and thereafter keeps aloof from Satī while conversing kindly, the stated backdrop to her uninvited visit to Dakṣa's sacrifice and self-immolation

title: The family refuses to share the robber's sins
description: sent home by the waylaid Seven Sages, the highwayman learns his wife and children will share his loot but not his guilt

title: The famine averted
description: Daśaratha asks not for wealth but that Śani never again pierce the cart of Rohiṇī, sparing the earth the twelve-year drought, and Saturn grants it

title: The five apsaras sent to break the penance
description: the gods (Agni foremost; popularly Indra) dispatch five foremost celestial nymphs to seduce Māṇḍakarṇi and disperse his merit

title: The five hundred Rājeyas seize Indra's throne
description: After Raji's death his sons demand Indra-ship as their inheritance and, refused, take heaven by force and appropriate Indra's sacrificial shares
source: Vishnu Purana IV.9; Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Matsya Purana 24

title: The forty-eight-day famine fast
description: a great famine strikes and Rantideva with his family takes neither food nor water for forty-eight days, until a little kheer, food, and water arrive at dawn to break the fast

title: The four-quarter muster of Kiṣkindhā
description: Sugrīva summons the world's vānaras, golāṅgūlas and ṛkṣas and dispatches search-parties for Sītā to the four directions

title: The fourfold charity
description: about to eat, Rantideva gives his last meal in succession to a brāhmaṇa, a śūdra, and an outcaste with a pack of dogs, then surrenders his final water to a caṇḍāla begging for it

title: The fourfold Mithilā wedding
description: All four princes of Ayodhyā wed on a single day at Mithilā: Sītā–Rāma, Ūrmilā–Lakṣmaṇa, Māṇḍavī–Bharata, and Śrutakīrti–Śatrughna, the latter two being Kuśadhvaja's daughters

title: The Gaṇḍakī māhātmya and the Śabara hunter's rescue
description: at the Gaṇḍakī the king learns the śālagrāma's glory, and a dying Śabara robber is freed from Yama's servants by a śālagrāma laid on his chest and Rāma's name

title: The Guha boon fulfilled
description: by Śiva's Śivarātri boon the hunter is reborn as Guha, Niṣāda chief of Śṛṅgaverapura, whom Rāma visits and befriends on the way to exile
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Koṭirudra-saṁhitā 40; Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa 50

title: The invisible music of Pañcāpsaras
description: journeying from Sutīkṣṇa's hermitage toward Agastya, Rāma hears song, instruments, and jingling ornaments rising from an empty-seeming lake and asks the marvel's cause

title: The Jāpaka and King Ikṣvāku
description: a lifelong Gāyatrī-reciter wins emancipation as Death and the gods dispute his merit, and he and the Solar king Ikṣvāku each try to give the other the fruit of his deeds

title: The king challenges Saturn
description: Daśaratha strings his bow and threatens the graha to drive him from the cart of Rohiṇī, and Śani, delighted by a mortal's fearlessness, offers a boon instead of striking him down

title: The kirāta child transfigured on Mount Nīla
description: a forest-tribe child eats a particle of rice offered to Viṣṇu in the hidden temple and gains a four-armed divine body, followed by his whole tribe

title: The krauñca bird and the first śloka
description: grief at a hunter's killing of a krauñca bird at the Tamasā bursts from Vālmīki as the first metrical verse

title: The Kulapati's Doom Revealed
description: the dog discloses that it was itself the former, conscientious kulapati of Kālañjara yet fell to a dog-birth, so making an angry man abbot over sacred wealth is a punishment disguised as a boon

title: The lost hunt of King Babhruvāhana
description: the king of Mahodaya wounds a deer, loses his army in the deep forest, and rests at a lotus lake beneath a fig tree

title: The massacre of frogs and Āyu's curse
description: the enraged king orders frogs slaughtered realm-wide, until the frog-king Āyu reveals his deceitful daughter and curses her sons to scorn brāhmaṇas before restoring her

title: The māyā withdrawn and Śiva-bhakti prescribed
description: Viṣṇu dissolves the illusion, reveals it as Śiva's māyā curing Nārada's pride, and directs the repentant sage to Śiva-worship, launching the Brahmā–Nārada frame of the Rudra-saṃhitā

title: The monkey-face humiliation at Śrīmatī's svayaṃvara
description: in the phantom city of King Śīlanidhi, Nārada begs Viṣṇu for "Hari's form," receives a monkey's face by the hari-pun, and is spurned by princess Śrīmatī, who garlands Viṣṇu himself

title: The mutilation at Pañcavaṭī
description: Śūrpaṇakhā woos Rāma, is deflected in jest, lunges at Sītā, and has her nose and ears cut off by Lakṣmaṇa — the spark of the whole war

title: The mutual curse into birds
description: Vasiṣṭha curses Viśvāmitra into a baka (crane) and Viśvāmitra retorts by cursing Vasiṣṭha into an Āḍi bird, hurling both brahmarṣis out of their human forms

title: The naming of Pañcāpsaras tīrtha
description: the pool is named 'Five-Apsaras lake' after the nymphs won and hidden there, the Araṇya Kāṇḍa's one embedded sacred-lake etiology

title: The Nīla mountain unveiled and five ascend to Vaikuṇṭha
description: the blazing mountain and its golden temple where Brahmā worships Viṣṇu appear, and the king with his wife, minister, brāhmaṇa and the weaver receive four-armed bodies and ride a vimāna to Vaikuṇṭha

title: The omen of Rohiṇī's cart
description: Ayodhyā's astrologers warn King Daśaratha that Śani is about to enter the Rohiṇī-śakaṭa-bheda, a transit portending a twelve-year drought and famine on earth

title: The preta teaches the king its own liturgy of release
description: the deformed ghost prescribes the Nārāyaṇa rite, vṛṣotsarga (bull-release) and the golden ghee-pot gift, then pays the king with a great jewel and vanishes

title: The queen's boon ends the feud
description: Dala's queen worships the ṛṣi and asks as her boon only that he forgive her husband, whereupon Dala returns the Vāmī mares and the curse-driven quarrel is closed

title: The rākṣasa rout
description: with their commander dead, the surviving demons break and flee back into Laṅkā as the war moves on to Indrajit's Māyā-Sītā sorcery

title: The robber waylays the brāhmaṇa Śaṅkha
description: a hunter-robber strips the sage of his goods, then, pitying his scorched feet in the Vaiśākha heat, returns his sandals and converts

title: The Śambūka episode
description: to revive a brahmin's dead son, Rāma beheads the śūdra ascetic Śambūka for yuga-forbidden tapas, the sharpest ethics flashpoint of the epic [late text][disputed]

title: The Sentence of Abbacy
description: the dog asks that its assailant be made kulapati of the Kālañjara maṭha, and Rāma, taking it for a reward, consecrates Sarvārtha-siddha to the office

title: The seven-night battle on the Sindhu
description: Bharata's army fights the illusion-wielding Gandharva host for seven days and nights without decision
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 101; the host's king Śailūṣa and its three-crore count are the Agni Purāṇa's, ch. 11

title: The shattered trident
description: dismounted, Makarākṣa hurls a blazing śūla (pike) at Rāma, who cuts it to pieces in mid-air with his arrows

title: The storming of Mahodaya and Huṇḍa slain
description: grown and armed, Nahuṣa breaks Huṇḍa's fortress-host and kills the demon, fulfilling Pārvatī's prophecy and Aśokasundarī's curse in one stroke

title: The stranger-king's śrāddha releases the preta
description: Babhruvāhana performs the rites at Mahodaya and Sudeva, freed from the preta-state, attains heaven — proof-case that even a stranger's śrāddha saves the dead

title: The suitors' siege of Mithilā
description: Kings who fail the vīrya-śulka bow-test besiege Mithilā for a year until Janaka, granted an army through tapas, routs them

title: The thousand-headed Rāvaṇa of Vilaṅkā is defeated
description: after Laṅkā's war Rāma faces a mightier thousand-headed Rāvaṇa, with Sītā's śakti given the decisive role in cognate tellings [regional] [disputed]

title: The Trimūrti revealed and the liberation
description: the four guests prove to be Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva in disguise; Rantideva, desiring no boon and fixed in Vāsudeva, sheds all grief and, with his followers, attains the yoga of Nārāyaṇa

title: The Vālī-vadha
description: Rāma shoots Vālī from concealment during the duel with Sugrīva and answers the dying king's indictment with his rājadharma defense, the epic's classic ethics debate

title: The Vāmana war (second saṅgrāma)
description: Viṣṇu as the Dwarf begs three paces from Bali, strides the worlds as Trivikrama and binds the asura-emperor

title: The vengeance-challenge to Rāma
description: Makarākṣa confronts Rāma on the field and taunts him for killing Khara in the Daṇḍaka forest, demanding single combat

title: The wager over Hariścandra's truthfulness
description: Vasiṣṭha praises Hariścandra as the most truthful king; Viśvāmitra disputes it and undertakes to break him, with the king as the stake

title: The water-covenant of Parikṣit
description: the Ikṣvāku king Parikṣit weds a singing maiden he meets by a forest lake on her one condition — that he never show her water

title: The worlds shaken by wing-blows
description: the birds' battering topples mountains, tilts the earth, and surges the oceans, killing multitudes and threatening the ruin of the worlds

title: Trijaṭā among the Aśoka-vana guard
description: Trijaṭā is set among the rākṣasīs guarding the captive Sītā in Rāvaṇa's Aśoka grove in Laṅkā

title: Triśaṅku hung between earth and heaven, localized at Vaḍnagar
description: the Ikṣvāku king's bodily ascent and mid-sky suspension by Viśvāmitra is re-homed to the Hāṭakeśvara tīrtha-cycle

title: Trishanku's three sins and curse-naming
description: Prince Satyavrata angers his father, abducts a bride, and kills Vasiṣṭha's cow, earning the curse-name Triśaṅku from the sage

title: Ucchi Piḷḷaiyār — struck on the crown
description: the enraged Vibhīṣaṇa chases the fleeing boy up the Tiruchirāppaḷḷi rock and strikes him on the crown of the head (ucci) at the summit, whereupon Gaṇeśa reveals himself and stays enshrined at the apex

title: Urvaśī weds Purūravas under three conditions
description: The apsarā Urvaśī marries the first Lunar king Purūravas on conditions including that she never see him naked
source: Ṛgveda X.95; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa XI.5.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.6

title: Vālī commends Aṅgada with his dying breath
description: struck by Rāma's arrow, the reconciled king of Kiṣkindhā entrusts his son Aṅgada and queen Tārā to the protection of Rāma and Sugrīva, begging the boy be treated as a son

title: Vālmīki shelters Sītā and swears to her purity
description: the sage raises Lava and Kuśa, teaches them the poem for Rāma's Aśvamedha, and stakes his sinless tapas on Sītā's innocence

title: Vamana avatara & subduing of Bali
description: Vishnu as a dwarf brahmana begs three paces from asura-king Bali, grows cosmic (Trivikrama), and pushes Bali to Patala
source: Bhagavata Purana, Vishnu Purana, Vamana Purana

title: Vamana Subdues Bali (Boon of Future Indra-hood)
description: Vishnu as Vamana reclaims the three worlds from the daitya king Bali in three strides, pushing him to Patala/Sutala but granting that Bali will become Indra in the future Savarni manvantara as recompense for his truthfulness

title: Vamana subdues Bali (Trivikrama)
description: Vishnu, born as the dwarf brahmana Vamana, begs three paces of land from the asura-king Bali, then grows cosmic (Trivikrama), covers earth and heaven in two strides, and sets his third foot on Bali's head pushing him to rule Patala
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23; Vishnu Purana; Vamana Purana

title: Varuṇa grants Hariścandra a son to be sacrificed
description: Counselled by Nārada, the sonless Hariścandra prays to Varuṇa, who grants him a son, Rohita, on condition the boy be sacrificed back to Varuṇa

title: Vasiṣṭha narrates the Cūḍālā-ākhyāna to Rāma
description: At Daśaratha's court, Vasiṣṭha tells young Rāma the tale of Cūḍālā and Śikhidhvaja as the model of liberation-in-action: live and rule as they did

title: Vasiṣṭha teaches Rāma the world is mind
description: the sage Vasiṣṭha narrates the Līlā-upākhyāna to young Rāma at Daśaratha's court as the corpus's proof that creation is a projection in consciousness

title: Vasiṣṭha's discourse to the despondent Rāma
description: At Daśaratha's court, as Viśvāmitra arrives, Vasiṣṭha teaches the world-weary sixteen-year-old Rāma through nested parables over successive days

title: Vasiṣṭha's discourse to the world-weary Rāma (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha frame)
description: At Daśaratha's court, as Viśvāmitra arrives, sage Vasiṣṭha answers young Rāma's vairāgya with the six-prakaraṇa teaching of ajāta-vāda across hundreds of nested parables

title: Vasiṣṭha's wrath at the Hariścandra ordeal
description: returning after twelve years by the Gaṅgā, Vasiṣṭha learns Viśvāmitra has ruined his royal protégé and burns with anger fiercer than at his own sons' deaths

title: Vāyu's wrath twists the hundred maidens
description: Refused by Kuśanābha's daughters, who insist their father alone may give them in marriage, the wind-god Vāyu enters their limbs and bends them into hunchbacks (kubjā) — the traditional etymology of Kanyākubja/Kanauj

title: Vibhīṣaṇa defects to Rāma
description: Spurned by Rāvaṇa for urging Sītā's return, Vibhīṣaṇa surrenders to Rāma, who rules that a refuge-seeker must never be turned away and pre-crowns him king of Laṅkā

title: Vibhīṣaṇa's tapas and boon of righteousness
description: In joint austerities at Gokarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa alone asks that his mind never stray from dharma; pleased, Brahmā additionally grants him immortality

title: Vibhandaka sheds his seed and the doe conceives Rishyashringa
description: The ascetic Vibhandaka, overcome at a lake, involuntarily sheds his seed; a doe (a cursed apsaras) drinks it and conceives, bearing a boy and being freed of her curse

title: Vidyujjihva slain by Rāvaṇa
description: Śūrpaṇakhā's husband, the Kālakeya lord Vidyujjihva, is killed by Rāvaṇa in his world-conquest campaign, widowing his own sister
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa, Kālakeya episode

title: Vihuṇḍa's revenge and the Kamodā coda
description: Huṇḍa's kinsman Vihuṇḍa takes up the vendetta and is slain by Nahuṣa, and the cycle closes with the loosely-transmitted episode of the celestial maiden Kamodā

title: Virādha seizes Sītā in Daṇḍaka
description: On entering the Daṇḍaka forest, the man-eating rākṣasa Virādha takes up Sītā in his arms — the first abduction-attempt of the epic

title: Vālmīki composes the first śloka
description: Grief at seeing a hunter kill a krauñca bird bursts from Vālmīki as the first anuṣṭubh verse (śoka becoming śloka), birthing Sanskrit poetry

title: Vālmīki witnesses the krauñca bird's death and utters the first śloka
description: Grieving a hunter's killing of a mating curlew, Vālmīki's sorrow bursts out as metrical verse, birthing the anuṣṭubh meter and poetry itself

title: Vānara host reaches the Setu-kshetra bridgehead
description: Rāma marches the vānara army to the Pamban/Dhanuṣkoṭi shore opposite Laṅkā and petitions the ocean-god Sāgara for passage

title: Vāyu fathers Hanumān upon Añjanā
description: Vāyu fathers Hanumān upon the apsarā-turned-vānarī Añjanā by his wind-agency, making Hanumān Vāyuputra/Pavanaputra

title: Aditi's Payovrata
description: Grieving for her dispossessed sons, Aditi performs the twelve-day Payovrata milk-vow on Kaśyapa's instruction; Viṣṇu promises to be born as her son

title: Agastya approaches and offers the secret
description: The sage Agastya, watching the war among the devas, steps forward and offers Rāma an eternal secret for victory

title: Agastya approaches Rāma
description: The sage Agastya, present among the watching gods, draws near and offers Rāma an eternal secret

title: Agastya prescribes the Pāśupata vow
description: Sage Agastya comes to the grieving Rāma and prescribes the Pāśupata vrata and worship of Śiva as the means to recover Sītā

title: A lifetime of waiting at Pampā
description: Śabarī keeps the empty āśram ready and gathers fruit day after day for years, watching the road for the promised prince

title: Anaraṇya gives battle
description: Unlike kings who submitted, Anaraṇya accepts battle to defend Ayodhyā and the honor of the Ikṣvāku line

title: Śarabhaṅga's self-immolation
description: Having gained Rāma's darśana, the sage Śarabhaṅga enters the fire and ascends in a radiant body to Brahmaloka

title: Arrival of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa at Mithilā under Viśvāmitra
description: Viśvāmitra escorts Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Janaka's court, where they are received by Janaka and his priest Śatānanda, and Viśvāmitra asks that the boys be shown Śiva's bow

title: Avatara of Mayureshvara
description: Ganesha descends in Treta Yuga as the peacock-mounted Mayureshvara and slays the demon Sindhu(rasura); his Morgaon form heads the Ashtavinayaka shrines

title: Bharadvāja's miraculous feast for Bharata's army
description: Bharata, marching with his army to bring Rāma back, halts at Bharadvāja's āśrama; the sage by ascetic power conjures a vast miraculous feast — divine food, palaces, music and apsaras — entertaining the whole host before Bharata proceeds to Chitrakūṭa

title: Birth of Bharata
description: Kaikeyī bears Bharata from her share of the sacrificial pāyasa

title: Birth of Kauśika (Viśvāmitra), Gādhi's son
description: Gādhi's son Kauśika, born a kṣatriya prince, renounces kingship and rises by tapas to brahmarṣi status as Viśvāmitra
source: Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Mahābhārata Ādi & Vana Parva

title: Birth of Rāma at Ayodhyā
description: Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, is born at Ayodhya on the Sarayu in the Treta Yuga

title: Birth of the horned Rishyashringa
description: Because of his doe-mother the child is born with a single horn on his forehead, hence Rishyashringa, and is raised in total forest isolation ignorant of women

title: Brahma Commissions the Ramayana
description: Brahma appears to Valmiki and commissions him to compose the story of Rama, establishing the adi-kavya (first poem)

title: Brahmā commissions Vālmīki to compose the Rāmāyaṇa
description: Brahmā commands Vālmīki to compose Rāma's life in the new meter, granting divine insight into every event

title: Brahmā creates the Fifth Veda from the four Vedas
description: Brahmā draws recitation from Ṛg, song from Sāma, abhinaya from Yajus, and rasa from Atharva to form the Nāṭyaveda

title: Brahmā gives Ahalyā to Gautama in marriage
description: Brahmā fashions Ahalyā as the most beautiful woman and awards her to Gautama (in a variant, via a contest to circle the worlds that Gautama wins over Indra), seeding Indra's resentment
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 48; Brahma Purāṇa

title: Building of the Setu (Rāma-Setu)
description: After Rāma's penance compels the ocean-god Sāgara, the vānara Nala directs the building of a hundred-yojana floating causeway in five days, and the army crosses to Laṅkā

title: Courtesans lure Ṛśyaśṛṅga to end Aṅga's drought
description: King Lomapāda sends courtesans disguised as ascetics to lure the chaste sage to Aṅga; his arrival breaks the years-long drought with rain

title: Descent of Vishnu as Rama
description: In the standard avatar-to-yuga mapping of this Mahayuga, Vishnu descends as Rama in the Treta Yuga

title: Forester's vow and Lakṣmaṇa's night-watch
description: Rāma declines cooked food and beds, taking only water and fodder; Lakṣmaṇa keeps vigil with Guha through the first night by the sleeping Rāma and Sītā

title: Gālava's Horses and Mādhavī's Loaning
description: Pressed for 800 special horses as guru-dakṣiṇā, Gālava loans Yayāti's daughter Mādhavī to three kings and Viśvāmitra to earn sons and horses, the debt finally closed by Garuḍa

title: Gārgī's first questioning — the warp-and-woof chain
description: Gārgī Vācaknavī asks on what each cosmic level is woven 'warp and woof', driving Yājñavalkya up a regress from water through air, sun, moon, stars, the gods, Indra and Prajāpati to the worlds of Brahman

title: Hanumān passes Maināka and outwits Surasā
description: On the crossing Hanumān courteously refuses the rest offered by the golden mountain Maināka and outwits the nāga-mother Surasā's mouth-test of strength and wit

title: Hanumān's leap from Mahendragiri to Laṅkā
description: From the summit of Mahendra(giri) Hanumān makes his great ocean-leap to Laṅkā, treading the peak down under the force of his spring at the opening of the Sundara-kāṇḍa

title: Hariścandra surrenders his kingdom
description: To appease Viśvāmitra, Hariścandra gives away Ayodhyā and all its wealth, keeping only his wife, son, and bark-cloth, then owes a further gold dakṣiṇā

title: Hariscandra's vow to Varuna for a son
description: Childless Ikshvaku king Hariscandra, counselled by Narada, prays to Varuna for a son and vows to sacrifice the boy back; Rohita is born

title: Harishchandra defers the sacrifice and Varuna curses him with dropsy
description: Harishchandra repeatedly postpones offering Rohita; for the broken vow Varuna seizes him with dropsy, and the grown Rohita flees to the forest

title: Indra strikes the infant Hanuman's jaw
description: Mistaking the sun for a fruit, infant Hanuman leaps to swallow it; Indra strikes him with the vajra, breaking his jaw and giving him his name

title: Śiva presses the mountain down
description: Śiva pins Rāvaṇa beneath Kailāsa with the toe of His foot, crushing his arms

title: Jamadagni's marriage to Reṇukā
description: Jamadagni weds Reṇukā, daughter of King Prasenajit/Reṇu, a model pativratā whose yogic merit lets her carry water in unbaked clay

title: Kabandha seizes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa
description: Searching south after Jaṭāyu's death, the brothers are caught one in each of Kabandha's yojana-long arms and drawn toward his belly-mouth

title: Kaikeyī's boons and Bharata's absence
description: While Bharata and Śatrughna are away in Kekaya, Kaikeyī (prompted by Mantharā) extracts the boons exiling Rāma and crowning Bharata; the brothers return to find Daśaratha dead

title: Kapila's Wrath Burns Sagara's Sons
description: Sage Kapila's wrath burns Sagara's 60,000 sons to ash, the catastrophe that prompts the eventual descent of Gaṅgā to redeem them; his ashrama tradition is localized at Haridwar

title: Kausalyā receives the foremost half of the pāyasa
description: Daśaratha gives the senior queen Kausalyā a full half of the divine pāyasa, from which Rāma is conceived

title: Kāmadhenu at the hermitage
description: Jamadagni's āśrama holds the wish-cow Kāmadhenu (Suśīlā/Surabhi) who furnishes endless hospitality

title: Lakṣmaṇa weds Ūrmilā (fourfold wedding)
description: At Mithilā, alongside Rāma's wedding to Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa weds Ūrmilā in a fourfold marriage binding Ayodhyā and Mithilā

title: Lomapāda's brāhmaṇa-slight and the Aṅga drought
description: Lomapāda, distracted in conversation with Śāntā, slights a visiting brāhmaṇa, whose departure brings on the drought (Indra withholding rain) that will require the chaste ascetic Ṛśyaśṛṅga

title: Mantharā alarmed for Bharata
description: Seized with fury, she fears Kaikeyī and Bharata will be subordinated to Kausalyā under King Rāma

title: Mantharā poisons Kaikeyī's mind
description: The hunchback maid Mantharā convinces Kaikeyī that Rāma's coronation will ruin her and Bharata, coaching her to invoke the two old boons

title: Marriage to Sunda and birth of her sons
description: Tāṭakā weds the yakṣa Sunda and bears two sons, Mārīca and Subāhu

title: Maya fathers Mandodarī
description: Maya's daughter Mandodarī becomes the chief queen of Rāvaṇa, binding the architect to the Laṅkā rākṣasa world

title: Nahuṣa's pride and lust for Śacī
description: Corrupted by heaven's splendour, Nahuṣa covets Indra's queen Śacī, who stalls him by demanding he arrive in a palanquin borne by the Saptarṣis

title: Nandī's warning and curse
description: Nandī forbids passage as Śiva sports with Pārvatī; mocked by Rāvaṇa, he curses that monkey-like beings will destroy him

title: Night vigil and matting of hair
description: Rama sleeps on a grass-bed; Lakshmana and Guha keep watch through the night, and at dawn Guha supplies banyan sap to mat Rama's and Lakshmana's hair into ascetic jata

title: Parashurama avatara & Kartavirya Arjuna
description: Vishnu as the brahmana-warrior Parashurama slays the thousand-armed king Kartavirya Arjuna who seized the wish-cow Kamadhenu

title: Parashurama slays Kartavirya Arjuna
description: The thousand-armed Haihaya king Kartavirya Arjuna seizes the wish-cow Kamadhenu from Jamadagni's hermitage, and Parashurama slays him; in revenge Kartavirya's sons kill the unarmed Jamadagni

title: Paraśurāma's test of the Śārṅga bow on Rāma
description: After Rāma breaks Śiva's Pināka at Sītā's svayaṃvara, Paraśurāma confronts him and challenges him to string Viṣṇu's bow Śārṅga as a test of his divinity; Rāma bends the bow, confirming him as Viṣṇu's portion, and Paraśurāma yields
source: Rāmāyaṇa (Bāla Kāṇḍa); mysutradhar (All About Divine Bows)

title: Purūravas founds the Lunar dynasty at Pratiṣṭhāna
description: Purūravas performs penance to Brahmā, gains sovereignty, and becomes the first king of the Candravaṃśa, ruling from Pratiṣṭhāna (Prayāga)
source: Vishnu Purana IV.6; Bhagavata Purana IX.14

title: Raghu's duel with Indra over the sacrificial horse
description: When Indra steals Dilipa's hundredth Ashvamedha horse, the boy Raghu pursues and duels Indra, winning his admiration and a boon

title: Rama enters Dandakaranya
description: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana pass into the vast demon-haunted southern forest at the opening of the Aranya-kanda

title: Reṇukā's lapse on seeing Citraratha and loss of power
description: Reṇukā glimpses the gandharva Citraratha (variant: a king) sporting with celestial women and is moved for an instant; her broken chastity-power dissolves the unbaked pot and she returns empty-handed, and Jamadagni perceives her lapse and rages

title: Rāma breaks Śiva's bow and wins Sītā
description: At Mithilā's bow-test Rāma lifts and snaps the colossal divine bow of Śiva, winning Sītā's hand; the four princes wed in one ceremony

title: Rāma hurls Mārīca into the sea with the Mānavāstra
description: Rāma looses the Mānavāstra at Mārīca, which spares his life but flings him a hundred yojanas into the ocean, while Subāhu is slain by the Āgneyāstra

title: Rāma's lament at the lotus-lake Pampā
description: Arriving at the blossoming spring lake Pampā near Kiṣkindhā, Rāma's grief for the abducted Sītā is sharpened, opening the Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa

title: Rāma teaches bhakti as gateway, jñāna as cause
description: Rāma answers that devotion to him as supreme Lord is the gateway and that liberating knowledge is the direct cause of release

title: Rohita flees and Indra's 'caraiveti' refrain
description: Told he must die, Rohita flees to the forest for years while Indra, disguised, repeatedly urges him to keep wandering

title: Rohita flees and Varuṇa curses Hariścandra
description: Told he is to die, Rohita escapes to the forest and wanders six years urged on by Indra ('caraiveti'), while Varuṇa afflicts the king with dropsy for the broken vow

title: Rāvaṇa's Austerities at Rākṣas-tāl
description: The rākṣasa king Rāvaṇa performs severe austerities at Rākṣas-tāl, offering his ten heads to Śiva to win boons, naming the lake Rāvaṇa-hrada
source: folk / sthala tradition; Valmiki Ramayana Uttara-kanda

title: Rāvaṇa's tapas and Brahmā's boon
description: After fierce penance, Rāvaṇa offers his heads one by one into the fire; Brahmā stops him and grants invulnerability to all celestial and demonic beings — but, in contempt, Rāvaṇa omits men and animals

title: Rāvaṇa's tapas and the boon of the Ātma-liṅga
description: Rāvaṇa performs extreme austerities, offering his heads, until Śiva grants the Ātma-liṅga with the warning that it roots wherever it touches earth

title: Satyavrata's charity during the twelve-year famine
description: The exiled prince sustains Viśvāmitra's starving family by hunting, freeing the son Gālava from being sold; the sage repays with gratitude

title: Sītā discovered beneath the śiṃśapā
description: Hidden in an aśoka tree, Hanumān beholds the captive Sītā among rākṣasī wardresses and recognises her by Rāma's described ornaments

title: Sītā's earth-birth in the furrow
description: King Janaka ploughs the sacrificial field and uncovers the infant Sītā in the furrow — ayonijā, daughter of Earth
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa 66; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa

title: Sumitrā receives a doubled share of the pāyasa
description: Sumitrā is given two portions drawn from both co-queens' shares, and so conceives twins

title: Summons of Rāma before the abhiṣeka
description: Sumantra is sent by Daśaratha to fetch Rāma to the assembly for the heir-apparent consecration, and again into the king's chamber past Kaikeyī as the crisis breaks

title: The cow's army routs Kauśika
description: Śabalā/Nandinī snorts forth armies of foreign peoples who defeat Kauśika's forces, and the sage's brahmadaṇḍa swallows every weapon

title: The demonesses threaten Sītā
description: The other rākṣasīs cajole then threaten to devour Sītā, driving her to despair

title: The fire-witnessed friendship-pact of Rāma and Sugrīva
description: Rāma and Sugrīva swear mutual aid with Agni as witness — Rāma to slay Vāli and restore Sugrīva, Sugrīva to mobilize the vānaras to find Sītā

title: The gandharvas' trick breaks the condition; Urvaśī departs
description: Gandharvas steal Urvaśī's rams; Purūravas leaps up naked, a lightning-flash exposes him, and Urvaśī vanishes
source: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa XI.5.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.6

title: The gods' revelation and boon to Śibi
description: Indra and Agni reveal themselves, heal Śibi's wounds, declare his fame imperishable, and promise him a son Kapotaroma

title: The lapse — loss of chastity by thought
description: Reṇukā momentarily admires the gandharva Citraratha; her chastity-power breaks and the pot dissolves in her hands

title: The leaf-hut on the Mandākinī
description: Lakṣmaṇa builds a parṇa-śālā at Citrakūṭa where the three live in forest-domesticity beside the Mandākinī river

title: The Śravaṇa-kumāra accidental killing and death-by-grief curse
description: Young Daśaratha kills the ascetic boy Śravaṇa with a sound-aimed arrow and is cursed by the boy's blind parents to die of grief for his own son

title: The Setu-bandha (Nala-setu / Rāma-setu) is built
description: Sāgara names the boon-blessed vānara Nala, who directs construction of the 100×10 yojana causeway in five days; the army crosses to Laṅkā

title: The slighted kings ambush Aja
description: The rejected suitors waylay Aja's wedding party on the road to Ayodhyā; Aja defeats and (using the gāndharva/Saṃmohana weapon) stupefies them, then releases them

title: The weapon-proof boon and capture of the brothers
description: Virādha reveals Brahmā's boon making him invulnerable to weapons; the brothers' arrows fail and he seizes both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, one under each arm

title: The wish-cow's army routs Kauśika
description: Refused the cow and trying to seize her by force, Kauśika is routed when the cow snorts forth armies of foreign peoples and his hundred sons are burnt to ash

title: Trishanku's charity during the twelve-year famine
description: During a twelve-year famine the exiled Satyavrata hunts to feed Vishvamitra's destitute family and frees the son Galava from being sold, earning the sage's gratitude

title: Vamana grants Bali immortality and rule of Patala
description: Vishnu as Vamana presses Bali to Patala in three strides but, moved by his truthfulness, grants him rulership of Sutala, immortality, and guards his door

title: Vasiṣṭha's diagnosis — the slighted wish-cow
description: Vasiṣṭha reveals that Dilīpa once passed the celestial cow Surabhi (Kāmadhenu) without homage and was cursed childless, prescribing service to her daughter Nandinī as expiation

title: Vibhīṣaṇa's śaraṇāgati at the Kodaṇḍarāma site
description: Local sthala tradition ties the Dhanuṣkoḍi Kodaṇḍarāma shrine to the spot where Vibhīṣaṇa surrendered to and took refuge with the bow-bearing Rāma and was anointed king-to-be of Laṅkā

title: Vibhīṣaṇa spurned in Rāvaṇa's court
description: Counseling the return of Sītā and warning of ruin, Vibhīṣaṇa is enraged-spurned and insulted by Rāvaṇa in open court, driving the final break

title: Viśvāmitra names Mārīca and Subāhu and asks for Rāma
description: Viśvāmitra seeks the boy-princes from Daśaratha because Mārīca and Subāhu repeatedly wreck his sacrifices

title: Vālī kills Dundubhi and earns Mātaṅga's curse
description: Vālī slays the buffalo-demon Dundubhi and hurls the carcass onto Mātaṅga's hermitage, earning a curse that his head will burst if he sets foot on Ṛṣyamūka

title: Vāyu withdraws air at Hanumān's striking down
description: When the infant Hanumān is struck down by Indra's vajra, the grieving Vāyu withdraws all air from the worlds, suffocating creation until the gods revive Hanumān and grant him boons
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa 36; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Accession of Raghu to Kosala
description: Dilipa installs Raghu on the throne of Ayodhya and retires to the forest as a vanaprastha

title: Aṅgada's embassy to Rāvaṇa
description: Rāma sends Vāli's son Aṅgada as envoy demanding Sītā's release; Rāvaṇa orders him seized, but Aṅgada shakes off the guards and departs defiantly

title: Agastya's curse turns Nahuṣa into a python
description: Yoking the Saptarṣis and kicking Agastya while crying 'sarpa', Nahuṣa is cursed by the sage to fall from heaven as a python

title: Agastya teaches the Āditya-Hṛdayam
description: Agastya imparts the ~30-śloka Sūrya-hymn, declaring it will let Rāma conquer all enemies in battle

title: Ajīgarta sells and binds his son Sunaḥśepa
description: Rohita buys the middle son Sunaḥśepa for a hundred cows as a substitute victim; the father Ajīgarta agrees to bind and butcher his own child for more cattle

title: Śatrughna beats Mantharā
description: On returning, Śatrughna seizes and beats the hunchback Mantharā in fury until Bharata restrains him

title: Bharata's march to Citrakūṭa
description: Refusing the throne after Daśaratha's death, Bharata leads all of Ayodhyā to Citrakūṭa to beg Rāma to return and reign

title: Birth and naming of Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna
description: Sumitrā bears the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, named and horoscoped by Vasiṣṭha; each attaches to an elder brother

title: Birth of Rama at Ayodhya
description: After Dasharatha's putra-kameshti sacrifice, Rama and his brothers are born at Ayodhya on Rama Navami, the seventh avatara of Vishnu descending into Suryavamsha flesh

title: Birth of Rama via Putra-kameshti Sacrifice
description: Dasharatha performs the putra-kameshti (son-desiring) sacrifice, resulting in the birth of Rama and his brothers — the avatara-descent of Vishnu

title: Birth of Rāma
description: Kausalyā bears Rāma in Caitra under Punarvasu with planets exalted, marked with the signs of Viṣṇu (Rāma-Navamī)

title: Birth of Vāmana
description: Viṣṇu is born to Aditi and Kaśyapa as the dwarf-brahmin Vāmana, fifth of the Daśāvatāra, and undergoes upanayana receiving staff, deerskin and water-pot

title: Boons earned from Kaikeyī in the Devāsura (Śambara) war
description: Wounded fighting as Indra's ally against the asura Śambara, Daśaratha is saved by Kaikeyī and grants her two boons to be claimed at will

title: Breaking and burying Virādha alive
description: Unable to slay him by weapons, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa hack off his arms, dig a pit, and bury him alive — circumventing the boon by interment

title: Children of Gautama and Ahalyā
description: The union produces Śatānanda (Janaka's purohita) and, in some traditions, Cirakārī and the daughter Añjanā
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 51; Mahābhārata Śānti Parva

title: Crossing the Ganga
description: Guha provides a boat and personally has Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana ferried across the Ganga; Sita prays to the river for a safe return

title: Daśaratha performs the Putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice
description: The childless Ikṣvāku king Daśaratha, on Vasiṣṭha's counsel, has the sage Ṛśyaśṛṅga conduct the son-desiring oblation after an Aśvamedha

title: Death of Sunda and Agastya's curse
description: After Sunda is destroyed and Tāṭakā with Mārīca attacks his hermitage, Agastya curses her into a hideous man-eating rākṣasī and Mārīca into a rākṣasa

title: Defeat and mortal wounding of Anaraṇya
description: Rāvaṇa routs Anaraṇya's army and strikes the king down mortally wounded; Rāvaṇa taunts the famed might of the Ikṣvākus

title: Driving the exiles' chariot out of Ayodhyā
description: Sumantra yokes the royal chariot and drives Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa from the palace; caught between Daśaratha's plea to halt and Rāma's order to drive faster

title: Drought strikes Anga after Lomapada's offence
description: Indra withholds rain from Anga because King Lomapada sinned against a brahmana; the brahmins counsel that only the chaste ascetic Rishyashringa can break the drought

title: Entry into Daṇḍaka and the hermits' plea
description: Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa enter Daṇḍaka, are shown the bones of brahmins devoured by rākṣasas, and Rāma vows to clear the forest of demons

title: Goddess slays Mahishasura (charter)
description: The Devi Mahatmya charter in which the Goddess as primordial garbha-shakti/mula-prakriti slays the buffalo-demon Mahishasura, underwriting the womb-energy reading of the garbo

title: Hanuman and the mermaid Suvannamaccha
description: A pan-Southeast-Asian non-Valmiki episode in which the mermaid princess Suvannamaccha tries to sabotage the bridge to Lanka but is won over by Hanuman and bears him a fish-tailed son, Macchanu

title: Hanumān kills Siṃhikā
description: The shadow-seizing sea-monster Siṃhikā drags Hanumān down; he plunges into her, rends her organs from within, kills her, and flies on

title: Hariścandra sells his family and himself
description: To pay the fee, Hariścandra sells queen Śaivyā and son Rohitāśva into bondage and sells himself to a Cāṇḍāla running the Kāśī cremation ground
