title: Śibi gives away his eyes (Jātaka)
description: In the Buddhist Sibi Jātaka, Sakka disguised as a blind brāhmaṇa begs an eye; Sivi gives both, and his sight is restored by an Act of Truth

title: Indra's caraiveti refrain keeps Rohita wandering
description: Five times Indra appears as a brahmin urging the wandering Rohita onward with the verse 'keep wandering.'

title: Institution of Navarātri; Rāma's Navarātri-pūjā
description: The Devī Bhāgavata institutes Navarātri and recounts Rāma performing the Navarātri-pūjā to win the Goddess's aid

title: Śiva grants the axe
description: Paraśurāma worships Śiva and receives the celestial battle-axe (paraśu) from which he takes his name, with martial mastery

title: Śiva's theophany
description: Pleased by Rāma's austerities, Śiva appears with Pārvatī and the gaṇas to answer Rāma's questions on suffering and the self

title: Jamadagni's order to behead her
description: Enraged, Jamadagni commands each son to slay their mother; the four elders refuse and are cursed

title: Kabandha directs Rāma to Śabarī
description: The freed headless rākṣasa Kabandha sends Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Pampā and to Śabarī's hermitage

title: Kabandha revealed as the cursed gandharva Viśvāvasu
description: On cremation the headless rākṣasa Kabandha reveals he was the gandharva Viśvāvasu (var. Danu son of Śrī), cursed and now released, and directs Rāma toward Sugrīva

title: Kaikeyī demands Bharata's crowning and Rāma's exile
description: Binding Daśaratha to his oath, Kaikeyī claims her two boons: Bharata consecrated king and Rāma exiled to the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years

title: Kauśika abandons kingship for tapas
description: Humiliated by brahman-power, Kauśika renounces his kingdom to pursue ascetic ascent toward brahmarṣi status

title: Kubera rules golden Lanka
description: Kubera first rules the golden island-city of Lanka, built for him by Vishvakarma as the wealth-god's seat

title: Kumbhakarṇa's boon of endless sleep
description: Sarasvatī twists Kumbhakarṇa's tongue so he asks for sleep instead of a world without gods, dooming him to sleep six months and wake one day

title: Lakṣmaṇa builds the leaf-hut on the Godāvarī
description: Lakṣmaṇa raises the parṇa-śālā at Pañcavaṭī where the three settle into forest-domesticity through the seasons

title: Lakṣmaṇa insists on accompanying Rāma into exile
description: When Kaikeyī's boons force Rāma into exile, Lakṣmaṇa first urges seizing the throne, then vows to accompany Rāma as servant and guard

title: Mantharā wakes Kaikeyī and twists the news
description: She rouses the delighted Kaikeyī and reframes Rāma's coronation as a catastrophe for her son

title: Marriage of Śāntā to Ṛśyaśṛṅga
description: In gratitude for the rains brought by the horned ascetic, Lomapāda gives the foster-princess Śāntā in marriage to Ṛśyaśṛṅga, making the sage son-in-law of both Aṅga and (through her true parentage) Ayodhyā

title: Marriage of Satyavatī to Ṛcīka
description: Gādhi's daughter Satyavatī (distinct from the Cedi Satyavatī) is given to the Bhārgava sage Ṛcīka, the conduit of kṣatriya nature into the brahmin clan
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 115; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7; Bhāgavata IX.15

title: Marriage of Ṛśyaśṛṅga and Śāntā
description: The grateful Lomapāda weds his daughter Śāntā to Ṛśyaśṛṅga, turning the forest-celibate into a householder

title: Marriage, Raghu's retirement, birth of Daśaratha
description: Aja brings Indumatī home and marries her; Raghu consecrates Aja king and retires to asceticism; Indumatī bears Daśaratha

title: Matting the hair with banyan-sap (jaṭā-bandhana)
description: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa mat their hair into ascetic jaṭā using the milky sap of the vaṭa/banyan, formally assuming the forest-hermit form for the exile

title: Mārīca and Subāhu defile the Siddhāśrama sacrifice
description: During Viśvāmitra's six-day sacrificial session the two brothers pour flesh and blood upon the altar, defiling the rite

title: Mārīca's second defeat and retreat to asceticism
description: Routed a second time by a Rāma-arrow in the forest, the terrified Mārīca renounces demon-life and lives as an abstemious hermit haunted by Rāma's name

title: Parashurama's twenty-one-fold kshatriya annihilation
description: Enraged at his father's murder, Parashurama vows to rid the earth of the kshatriya class twenty-one times, filling five lakes at Samanta-panchaka with their blood

title: Paraśurāma's matricide and restoration boon
description: Jamadagni orders each son to behead Reṇukā; all refuse and are cursed except Paraśurāma, who obediently strikes off his mother's head, then uses the boon Jamadagni grants to restore her to life (without memory of her death) and revive his cursed brothers

title: Purchase of Śunaḥśepa as sacrificial substitute
description: Rohita buys the middle son Śunaḥśepa from the starving ṛṣi Ajīgarta for a hundred cows to be sacrificed in his place, and Ajīgarta agrees for further cows to bind and butcher his own son

title: Purūravas becomes a gandharva by the fire-ritual
description: Grieving Purūravas wins the gandharvas' fire-boon, establishes the three sacred fires via the śamī-aśvattha araṇi, and ascends to the gandharva-world; son Āyu continues the line

title: Rāma gifts the vimāna to Vibhīṣaṇa
description: After the Laṅkā war Rāma rewards Vibhīṣaṇa with the family deity to carry south to his island kingdom

title: Rāma incurs brahma-hatyā by killing Rāvaṇa
description: Slaying Rāvaṇa, a Brahmin descended from Brahmā via Pulastya, burdens Rāma with the gravest sin, requiring Śiva-worship at the Setu-kṣetra to expiate

title: Rāma pierces the seven sāla trees
description: To prove his prowess to a doubtful Sugrīva, Rāma kicks Dundubhi's skeleton ten yojanas and shoots a single arrow through seven sāla trees

title: Rāma's Jala-samādhi into the Sarayū
description: At the close of his reign Rama makes his final departure by walking into the Sarayu river, the anchoring event of Ayodhya's sanctity

title: Rāma slays Tāṭakā and guards Viśvāmitra's sacrifice
description: Sage Viśvāmitra takes the young Rāma to kill the demoness Tāṭakā and protect the sages' sacrifices

title: Rāma vows to clear Daṇḍaka of demons
description: Shown the bones of ascetics devoured by rākṣasas, Rāma vows to rid the Daṇḍaka forest of demons, the dharmic pledge driving the kāṇḍa

title: Rohita defers and flees the promised sacrifice
description: Hariscandra repeatedly postpones the offering; the grown Rohita refuses and flees to the forest as Varuna afflicts the king with dropsy

title: Rāvaṇa's roar and naming
description: Trapped in agony, Rāvaṇa roars so terribly that Śiva gives him the name 'Rāvaṇa' (maker of roars)

title: Rāvaṇa's wooing and Sītā's refusal
description: Rāvaṇa courts Sītā in the grove with threats and blandishments; she repels him with a blade of grass and he sets a death-deadline

title: Sagara's horse-sacrifice and Indra's theft
description: Emperor Sagara performs an Ashvamedha; Indra, fearing his power, steals the sacrificial horse and hides it at sage Kapila's hermitage in Patala

title: Sita and Rama bless Hanuman with deathlessness
description: Sita blesses Hanuman with deathlessness and eternal youth and Rama decrees he shall live as long as the Rama-katha is told on earth

title: Sita's Agni-pariksha and Return to the Earth
description: Sita, daughter of the earth and King Janaka, abducted by Ravana, undergoes the fire-ordeal and finally returns into the earth

title: Sita's curse on the Phalgu river
description: A Ramayana-linked legend holds Sita cursed the Phalgu river at Gaya to run underground, a story tied to the ancestral pinda-offering circuit

title: Slaying of Viradha
description: The rakshasa Viradha seizes Sita; the brothers bury him alive, releasing him from a gandharva curse

title: Sītā insists on accompanying Rāma into exile
description: When Kaikeyī's boon sends Rāma into forest exile, Sītā refuses palace comfort and insists a wife's place is at her husband's side

title: Sugrīva sights the brothers from Mount Ṛṣyamūka
description: From Ṛṣyamūka — the one hill Vāli cannot enter due to Mataṅga's curse — the exiled Sugrīva spots two armed strangers and, fearing Vāli, sends Hanumān to investigate

title: Teaching of the Āditya-hṛdaya
description: Agastya imparts the Sun-hymn as upadeśa, directing Rāma to worship Sūrya/Āditya and recite it thrice with a purified mind

title: The Śambara war and origin of the two boons
description: Kaikeyī rescues the wounded Daśaratha in the war against the asura Śambara and is granted two boons on demand
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā 9; Pauranic, Telugu Dvipada, Kṛttivāsī Rāmāyaṇ variants

title: The arms are severed
description: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa simultaneously hack off Kabandha's two arms at the shoulder, felling the monster

title: The brahmadaṇḍa swallows Kauśika's astras
description: Kauśika hurls Śiva-given astras including the brahmāstra at the hermitage, but Vasiṣṭha's brahmin staff swallows them all, teaching him brahman-strength is supreme

title: The cave, the sealing, and Vālī's usurpation
description: Pursuing Māyāvī into a cave, Vālī is sealed in by Sugrīva who believes him dead; returning enraged, Vālī banishes Sugrīva, seizes his kingdom, and takes his wife Rumā

title: The clinging skull falls at Kapālamocana
description: A skull-fragment of a rākṣasa, struck off by Rāma Dāśarathi's arrow and fastened to the thigh of the sage Mahodara, falls away when he bathes at Kapālamocana, freeing him and giving the ford power to absolve even brahminicide

title: The Dhanuṣa-yajña — Rāma breaks Śiva's bow (Pināka)
description: Rāma lifts and strings the colossal Śiva-dhanus (Pināka), snapping it with a thunderclap, and so wins Sītā's hand as the vīrya-śulka bride-price of valour
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 66–67; Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa (Varuṇa-bow variant); Tulsīdās Rāmcaritmānas, Bāla-kāṇḍa (svayaṃvara/Phulwārī expansion)

title: The Dhanuṣa-yajña vow
description: Janaka pledges Sītā as vīrya-śulka to any king who can string the colossal bow of Śiva (Pināka) held by his house

title: The 'do not over-question' warning
description: When Gārgī presses on what the worlds of Brahman are woven, Yājñavalkya warns her not to over-question (atipraśna) lest her head fall off; she falls silent for the moment

title: The gods appeal to Viṣṇu and Gaṇeśa
description: Alarmed at an invincible Rāvaṇa, the devas beg Viṣṇu and Gaṇeśa to stop the liṅga reaching Laṅkā

title: The gods revive Hanuman and grant boons
description: After Vayu withdraws all air in wrath, the devas revive Hanuman and each grants a boon of invulnerability, strength, and longevity, making him effectively immortal
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 36; Shiva Purana

title: The leaf-hut on the Godāvarī
description: Lakṣmaṇa builds the parṇa-śālā and the three settle into forest life at Pañcavaṭī

title: The qualified seeker (sādhana-catuṣṭaya)
description: Rāma describes the adhikārin endowed with discrimination, dispassion, the six virtues, and longing for release, fit for brahma-vidyā

title: The twenty-one-day service of Nandinī
description: Laying aside royal state, Dilīpa tends the wish-cow Nandinī as a herdsman for twenty-one days while Sudakṣiṇā worships her morning and evening

title: The wish-cow at the āśrama
description: Jamadagni's hermitage holds an all-yielding wish-cow (Kāmadhenu/Surabhi/Suśīlā/Nandinī) furnishing endless food and hospitality, the engine of the coming tragedy

title: Transmission of the Nāṭyaveda to Bharata Muni
description: Brahmā confers the Nāṭyaveda on Bharata Muni, who teaches it to his hundred sons with Apsarās and Gandharvas

title: Triśaṅku's wish and Vasiṣṭha's refusal
description: King Triśaṅku asks to ascend bodily to heaven; Vasiṣṭha refuses as adharma, and the sage's sons curse him to become a cāṇḍāla

title: Twenty-one-fold kshatriya annihilation
description: Enraged at his father's murder, Parashurama rids the earth of the kshatriya class twenty-one times, filling lakes at Kurukshetra

title: Uprooting of Mount Kailāsa
description: Enraged Rāvaṇa thrusts his twenty arms under Kailāsa and heaves it up, shaking the mountain so Pārvatī clings to Śiva in alarm

title: Urvaśī cursed to dwell among mortals
description: The apsarā Urvaśī is sent to earth by a curse (of Mitra or Mitra-Varuṇa), occasioning her marriage to Purūravas
source: Vishnu Purana IV.6; Bhagavata Purana IX.14

title: Vasishtha refuses the bodily-ascent wish
description: Trishanku desires to ascend to Indra's heaven in his living body, but his purohita Vasishtha refuses the rite as impossible and against dharma

title: Vibhīṣaṇa's śaraṇāgati and refuge with Rāma
description: Rejected by Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa surrenders to Rāma, who vows to never reject one who seeks refuge and at once consecrates him future king of Laṅkā

title: Viśvāmitra recites his Kuśika origin at the Śoṇa
description: Camped on the Śoṇa en route to Mithilā, Viśvāmitra tells Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa the history of his ancestors, closing with "I am Kauśika, born in the line of Kuśa"

title: Viśvāmitra rises from kṣatriya to brāhmaṇa by tapas
description: The kṣatriya sage Viśvāmitra attains brahminhood through austerity, adduced by Bhīṣma to show varṇa can be transcended by conduct

title: Vālmīki shelters Sītā
description: The sage Vālmīki, knowing Sītā by ascetic insight, takes the abandoned queen into his āśrama

title: Śabarī receives Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa
description: At last seeing Rāma, Śabarī rises in joy, touches their feet, and offers hospitality, her lifelong wait fulfilled

title: Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa — Rāma as Brahman with Māyā-Sītā
description: The embedded Advaita Rāmāyaṇa retells Rāma's life as supreme Brahman with Sītā as Yoga-Māyā; a shadow Māyā-Sītā is abducted by Rāvaṇa while the real Sītā is hidden in fire

title: Agastya bestows the bow of Viṣṇu on Rāma
description: The great sage Agastya gives Rāma the Viṣṇu-bow, inexhaustible quivers, a sword, and a divine arrow, and directs him to settle at Pañcavaṭī

title: Agastya digests the asura Vātāpi
description: Agastya eats the goat-disguised Vātāpi and commands 'Be digested', dissolving the cannibal demon, then reduces his brother Ilvala to ash

title: Ajigarta sells his middle son Sunahshepa
description: Rohita buys the starving rishi Ajigarta's middle son Sunahshepa for a hundred cows to die in his place as the sacrificial victim

title: Anaraṇya's dying curse foretelling Rāma
description: The dying king replies that his defeat is fate's doing, then curses Rāvaṇa that a future king of his own Ikṣvāku line (Rāma) will slay him; the gods affirm the decree

title: Anasūyā gifts Sītā celestial garments
description: Visiting sages' hermitages during the forest exile, Sītā receives celestial garments and unguents from Anasūyā at Atri's āśrama

title: Bali's Aśvamedha and the Boon of Three Paces
description: At Bali's horse-sacrifice on the Narmadā, Vāmana asks only for three paces of land measured by his own steps, declining all greater gifts

title: Ballal's Devotion and the Boon at Pali
description: In the Treta Yuga the boy Ballal, beaten and bound by his father for worshipping a stone as Ganesha, is freed and blessed by Ganesha, who grants that his devotee's name precede the Lord's as Ballaleshwar

title: Beheading and restoration of Reṇukā
description: At Jamadagni's command Paraśurāma beheads his mother Reṇukā for a momentary lapse of mind, then asks as a boon that she be restored to life and his brothers' wits returned
source: Mahābhārata 3.116; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.16; Brahmāṇḍa & Padma Purāṇas; Reṇukā-Yellammā folk variant

title: Bharata's appeal at Citrakūṭa
description: Bharata leads the court to Citrakūṭa to beg Rāma to return and rule; Rāma refuses, bound by his vow and his father's word

title: Coronation proclaimed and Kausalyā's joy
description: Rāma's consecration as yuvarāja is announced and Kausalyā prepares thanksgiving worship

title: Courtesans lure Rishyashringa to Anga and the rains fall
description: Courtesans on a floating hermitage-barge approach the innocent Rishyashringa as fellow ascetics and entice him to Anga; the moment he enters, Indra sends torrential rain

title: Devastation of the Malada–Karūṣa country
description: Enraged by her transformation, Tāṭakā lays waste the once-fertile Malada and Karūṣa lands near Agastya's grove into a shunned wasteland

title: Digvijaya — four-quarter world-conquest
description: Raghu conquers the kings of all four directions (east, south, west, north) following the freed Ashvamedha horse and returns to Ayodhya laden with tribute

title: Exposition of the mahāvākya 'tat tvam asi'
description: Rāma resolves jīva and Īśvara into the one undivided Brahman, teaching that bondage is avidyā and liberation is direct knowledge of identity

title: First drama staged at Indra's Banner Festival and disrupted by Asuras
description: The inaugural play on the gods' victory over the Asuras is staged at the Dhvaja-mahā; the Asuras disrupt it, prompting Brahmā to ordain the protected stage

title: Gārgī's two final arrows and the akṣara teaching
description: Gārgī returns with two whetted-arrow questions; Yājñavalkya answers that all is woven on ākāśa and ākāśa on the Imperishable (akṣara), describing the akṣara by negation as the unseen seer and unknown knower

title: Hanuman Leaps to Lanka
description: The vanara minister Hanuman, son of Vayu, leaps across the ocean to Lanka in the Sundara Kanda

title: Hanuman struck by Indra's vajra and granted boons as a child
description: As a child Hanuman is struck down by Indra's vajra for leaping at the sun, and the devas each grant boons making him invulnerable

title: Hanumān fells Laṅkinī at the gate
description: The city's guardian goddess Laṅkinī challenges Hanumān; he fells her with a single blow, and she recalls the prophecy that her defeat means the rākṣasas' doom

title: Hanumān's embassy and meeting with Rāma
description: Hanumān approaches disguised as a brāhmaṇa mendicant, wins Rāma's trust with eloquent speech, and carries both princes on his shoulders to Sugrīva — his entry into the epic's main action

title: Hanumān sent to Kailāsa for a liṅga
description: Rāma dispatches Hanumān to Kailāsa (or Vārāṇasī) to fetch a Śiva-liṅga, but he is delayed past the installation muhūrta

title: Indrajit binds Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with nāga-arrows
description: Fighting invisibly, Indrajit binds Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with serpent-arrows so that both fall as if slain, until Garuḍa descends and dissolves the bonds

title: Indra seduces Ahalyā in Gautama's form
description: Indra disguises himself as Gautama and approaches Ahalyā; in the Vālmīki critical reading she knowingly yields, while Purāṇic/devotional versions make her wholly deceived and innocent
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 48; Brahma Purāṇa; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; Rāmcaritmānas; Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa

title: Instruction to recite thrice facing the Sun
description: Agastya bids Rāma purify himself, face the rising Sun, and recite the hymn three times to gain victory

title: Śiva pins the mountain with a toe
description: Śiva presses Kailāsa back down with the great toe of one foot, crushing Rāvaṇa's arms beneath its weight

title: Jatayu's Cremation at Tirupullam Bhoothankudi
description: The Ramayana site where Valvil Raman (Rama) performs the cremation of the vulture Jatayu, slain by Ravana while defending Sita

title: Kabandha recognizes Rāma and tells his story
description: Learning he is held by Rāma, the maimed Kabandha rejoices, narrates his curse, and asks to be cremated so the curse may be discharged

title: Kaikeyi's Two Boons and Rama's Exile
description: At Ayodhya Kaikeyi invokes her two boons, sending Rama into 14-year exile while Bharata rules as regent from Nandigrama with Rama's sandals on the throne

title: Kapila burns Sagara's 60,000 sons to ash
description: Sagara's 60,000 sons accuse the meditating Kapila of the theft, and he incinerates all of them to ash with his ascetic fire

title: Kauśika renounces kingship for tapas
description: Humiliated, Kauśika abandons his kingdom to pursue tapas, the hinge that launches his multi-life quest for brahmarṣi status

title: Lakshmi incarnates as Sita with Rama
description: When Vishnu descends as Rama, Lakshmi incarnates as Sita, born of the earth-furrow, his consort

title: Marriage of Purūravas and Urvaśī under three conditions
description: Urvaśī weds Purūravas on conditions (protect her two rams, never be seen naked, fed only ghee), the kernel of the oldest narrated Indian romance
source: Rgveda X.95; Shatapatha Brahmana XI.5.1; Vishnu Purana IV.6

title: Mārīca hurled a hundred yojanas by the Mānavāstra
description: Rāma looses the Mānavāstra at Mārīca, flinging him a hundred yojanas into the ocean without killing him

title: Parashurama beheads and restores Renuka
description: At Jamadagni's command Parashurama beheads his own mother Renuka for a lapse of mind, then asks a boon to restore her to life

title: Paraśurāma beheads Reṇukā
description: In filial obedience Paraśurāma strikes off his mother's head with the axe at one stroke

title: Phra Ram orders Sida's death over a drawn portrait
description: In Rama I's Ramakien a rakshasa tricks Sida into drawing Tosakanth's portrait, triggering Phra Ram's suspicion and an order for her death, which he later repents

title: Rama Installs the Rameswaram Linga
description: Rama installs the Ramanatha linga at Rameswaram to expiate the sin of killing the brahmin Ravana, making it both a Char Dham point and a Jyotirlinga

title: Rama Protects Vishvamitra's Yajna
description: The boy-sages Rama and Lakshmana guard Vishvamitra's sacrifice, slaying the rakshasas who would defile it

title: Rama's Ashvamedha, Lava-Kusha, and Sita's earth-return
description: The Padma Purana's Pataala-khanda Rama narration frames Rama-Sita as Vishnu-Lakshmi and recounts Rama's Ashvamedha, the Lava-Kusha episode, and Sita's return to the earth

title: Ravana usurps Lanka from Kubera
description: After his own austerities and boons, Ravana drives his half-brother Kubera out and seizes Lanka, making it the rakshasa capital

title: Release of the gandharva Tumburu
description: Dying, Virādha reveals he is the gandharva Tumburu cursed by Kubera; freed by Rāma's act, he rises restored and ascends, directing Rāma onward to sage Śarabhaṅga

title: Renuka's beheading and restoration
description: At Jamadagni's command Parashurama beheads his own mother Renuka, then wins a boon to restore her to life

title: Reṇukā's lapse of purity
description: Sent to the river, Reṇukā's mind strays at the sight of the Gandharva Citraratha sporting with apsarases; her yogic purity breaks and Jamadagni perceives it
source: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; cf. Mahābhārata 3.116

title: Rāma accepts exile
description: Bound by his father's word as dharma, Rāma serenely accepts the fourteen-year exile without anger toward Kaikeyī or Daśaratha

title: Rāma breaks Śiva's bow
description: Brought by Viśvāmitra, Rāma lifts and bends the Pināka to string it; the bow snaps with a thunderclap and Sītā is won

title: Rāma slays Vāli
description: During Sugrīva's rematch with Vāli, Rāma shoots Vāli from concealment; the dying Vāli rebukes Rāma's stealth, hears his tenfold justification, and commends Aṅgada and Tārā to his care

title: Rāma's Mahā-prasthāna and procession to the Sarayū
description: Having installed Kuśa and Lava and lost Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma walks out of Ayodhyā in solemn procession with priests, women, ministers and citizens to the Sarayū bank as the gods watch

title: Rāma's question on suffering and the highest good
description: Rāma asks why the righteous suffer and what the highest good (śreyas) is — the Śaiva mirror of Arjuna's despondency

title: Rāma's threefold recitation of the hymn
description: Rāma sips water, gazes at the sun, and recites the Āditya-hṛdaya three times, becoming renewed and joyful

title: Rāma's Visit to the Prayāga Akṣayavaṭ
description: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana visit the imperishable banyan at Prayaga during their exile, near sage Bharadvaja's ashram

title: Śūrpaṇakhā's suit to Rāma
description: The rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, smitten with Rāma, demands him as husband and is deflected toward Lakṣmaṇa

title: Rāvaṇa coerces Mārīca and Mārīca counsels against the abduction
description: Rāvaṇa demands Mārīca become a golden deer; Mārīca twice warns him that Rāma is invincible and begs him to spare Sītā

title: Rāvaṇa seizes Laṅkā from Kubera and takes the Puṣpaka
description: Rāvaṇa defeats and expels his half-brother Kubera from golden Laṅkā and carries off the flying chariot Puṣpaka as his signature vehicle

title: Sages curse Hanuman to forget his powers
description: For tormenting sages as a child, Hanuman is cursed to forget his own immense powers until reminded at the destined moment

title: Sage Sharabhanga's self-immolation
description: Sharabhanga, having awaited Rama's darshan, immolates himself in his sacrificial fire and ascends to Brahmaloka

title: Shunahshepa bought as substitute victim
description: Rohita buys the rishi Ajigarta's middle son Shunahshepa for a hundred cows to serve as substitute victim in the rajasuya sacrifice

title: Soorasamharam (Skanda Shashti)
description: The climax of the six-day Aippasi Skanda Shashti fast: Murugan slays the asura Surapadma with the Vel, splitting him in two so that one half becomes his peacock mount and the other his cock-banner; re-enacted on the Tiruchendur seashore, followed the next day by Murugan's wedding to Deivanai (Tirukalyanam)
source: Wikipedia (Skanda Sashti, Soorasamharam); Tiruchendur Murugan Temple [traditional]

title: Sumitrā's farewell counsel to Lakṣmaṇa
description: As Lakṣmaṇa departs for the forest exile, Sumitrā blesses him, bidding him treat Rāma as father, Sītā as mother, and the forest as Ayodhyā, and to serve without faltering
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa; Tulsīdās, Rāmcaritmānas, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa

title: Sunaḥśepa freed by his hymns
description: Bound to the stake, Sunaḥśepa prays in Ṛgvedic verses to Varuṇa, Uṣas and others; his bonds fall away and Hariścandra is cured of dropsy

title: The agni-sākṣi pact of Rāma and Sugrīva
description: With fire as witness Rāma swears to kill Vālī and restore Sugrīva's throne, while Sugrīva vows to marshal the vānaras to find Sītā

title: The Bharata-milāp (reunion of the brothers)
description: Rāma and Bharata meet in grief and love and debate kingship and dharma before the assembled sages; Rāma refuses to cut short the exile

title: The boon of sleeplessness and Ūrmilā-nidrā
description: Lakṣmaṇa begs the goddess Nidrā to stay awake for the fourteen years; she consents on condition someone sleep his share, and Ūrmilā sleeps continuously throughout

title: The dead son and the cremation-fee test
description: Rohitāśva dies of snakebite; at the pyre Hariścandra, bound by duty, demands the cremation fee from his own grieving wife

title: The four-fold wedding at Mithilā (Vivāha Pañcamī)
description: Daśaratha arrives with Vasiṣṭha; the Ikṣvāku and Videha genealogies are recited and the four sons of Daśaratha wed Sītā, Ūrmilā, Māṇḍavī and Śrutakīrti in one ceremony on Mārgaśīrṣa Śukla Pañcamī
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 70–73; Maithilī Vivāha Pañcamī tradition

title: The Gaṅgā crossing and the Kevaṭ episode
description: Guha summons a boat and his kinsmen ferry Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa across the Gaṅgā; in Tulsīdās the boatman (Kevaṭ) first washes Rāma's feet before launching. Sītā prays to Gaṅgā and Sumantra is sent back
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa 52; Rāmcaritmānas, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa, Kevaṭ-prasaṅg

title: The Kevat foot-washing episode (Tulsidas)
description: In the Ramcharitmanas the boatman refuses to row Rama until allowed to wash his feet, then ferries them and asks only for devotion as payment

title: The lion-test and Dilīpa's offer of his own body
description: On the final day a lion (Śiva's servant) seizes Nandinī and freezes the king's arm; Dilīpa offers his own flesh in the cow's place, whereupon the illusion dissolves and Nandinī, satisfied, grants the boon of a son

title: The poisoning of Kaikeyī's mind
description: Mantharā plays on jealousy and maternal fear, arguing Bharata must be enthroned and Rāma removed

title: The Putrakāmeṣṭi and birth of Rāma and his brothers
description: Ṛśyaśṛṅga performs Daśaratha's son-desiring sacrifice; the divine pāyasa given to the queens produces Rāma, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna

title: The Putrakāmeṣṭi with Ṛṣyaśṛṅga and the divine pāyasa
description: Childless Daśaratha performs the Aśvamedha and son-seeking Putrakāmeṣṭi under Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, receiving divine pāyasa carrying Viṣṇu's descending portions

title: The swapped outcaste body — Reṇukā/Yellammā split etiology
description: In the Deccan version Paraśurāma mismatches the heads while restoring his mother, joining Reṇukā's head to an outcaste (Mātaṅgī/Cāṇḍāla) woman's body and vice versa, producing the two-natured goddess worshipped as brāhmaṇ-headed Reṇukā by upper castes and outcaste-bodied Yellammā/Māriyammaṉ by lower castes
source: South Indian folk variants; oral Yellamma/Mariyamman traditions

title: The thousand-horse bride-price
description: Ṛcīka wins Satyavatī by furnishing Gādhi a thousand white horses each with one black ear, obtained from Varuṇa
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 115; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7

title: The vīṇā strung from his own head
description: In the Tamil Śaiva variant, Rāvaṇa tears off a head and strings a vīṇā from it with his own sinews to accompany the hymn

title: Trijaṭā restrains the rākṣasīs
description: On the strength of the dream Trijaṭā forbids the demonesses to harm Sītā and urges them to seek her favour

title: Trijaṭā's omen-dream
description: The aged rākṣasī Trijaṭā restrains the others, recounting her dream of Rāma's victory and Laṅkā's doom

title: Trivikrama Measures the Worlds (Ulagaḷanta form)
description: Viṣṇu as Vāmana/Trivikrama strides the cosmos with raised foot, the deed enshrined in the Ulagaḷanta Perumāḷ temple of Kāñcī

title: Turned back at the Gaṅgā at Śṛṅgaverapura
description: At the riverbank Rāma dismisses the grieving Sumantra with the empty chariot while Guha ferries the exiles across the Gaṅgā into the forest

title: Śunaḥśepa's self-rescue by hymn
description: Bound to the stake, Śunaḥśepa prays in turn to the gods and his bonds fall away of themselves while Hariścandra is simultaneously cured of his illness

title: Vasishtha's sons curse Trishanku to chandala
description: Insulted that he spurned their father, Vasishtha's hundred sons curse Trishanku to become a chandala and his form is instantly disfigured

title: Vibhīṣaṇa reveals the secret of Rāvaṇa's death
description: When Rāma's arrows fail, Vibhīṣaṇa discloses that amṛta stored in Rāvaṇa's navel must be dried up, prompting Rāma to loose the brahmāstra there

title: Virādha revealed as the cursed gandharva Tumburu
description: The Daṇḍaka rākṣasa Virādha, slain and buried by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, reveals at death that he was the gandharva Tumburu cursed by Kubera, and his death releases him back to heaven

title: Virādha-vadha
description: The man-eating rākṣasa Virādha seizes Sītā; Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa maim and bury him alive, freeing the gandharva Tumburu from a curse

title: Viṣṇu agrees to incarnate as Daśaratha's sons
description: The gods, oppressed by the boon-protected Rāvaṇa, petition Viṣṇu, who agrees to be born as Daśaratha's sons to slay Rāvaṇa as a mortal

title: Viṣṇu hides the sun for a false dusk
description: Viṣṇu conceals the sun with Sudarśana to force the punctilious Rāvaṇa to halt for his evening sandhyā prayers

title: Viśvāmitra spends tapas on a counter-heaven
description: the sage sends Triśaṅku bodily skyward and creates a duplicate southern heaven when Indra hurls him down

title: Viśvāmitra's yajña and the curse of the boycotting sages
description: Viśvāmitra undertakes Triśaṅku's heaven-rite and curses Vasiṣṭha's sons and Mahodaya, who refuse to attend, to become outcastes

title: Agastya and Lopāmudrā
description: Agastya fashions and weds the princess Lopāmudrā; at her condition he gathers wealth, and they beget the Veda-chanting son Dṛḍhasyu

title: Ajigarta binds and offers to butcher his own son
description: After the four priests refuse to bind the boy, Ajigarta binds Sunahshepa for more cattle and offers to slaughter him for yet more, drunk on the promised cows

title: Ajigarta offers to bind and slay his own son
description: When no one will bind or slay the boy, the father Ajigarta offers to bind and then slay his own son for further hundreds of cows

title: Śatrughna Slays Lavaṇa and Founds Mathurā
description: Rama's brother Shatrughna kills the demon Lavana and founds Mathura on the site of the older Madhuvana

title: Bali Subdued by Vāmana (Trivikrama)
description: The dharma-keeping asura-emperor Bali, having conquered the three worlds, is begged three paces of land by Viṣṇu as the dwarf Vāmana, who grows to Trivikrama, strides over creation and pushes Bali to Pātāla while blessing him as a future Indra

title: Battle of Janasthāna (Khara–Dūṣaṇa)
description: Rāma alone destroys Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras and fourteen thousand rākṣasas of Janasthāna

title: Bhagiratha's penance brings Ganga down
description: After three generations fail, King Bhagiratha performs a thousand years of tapas; Brahma grants Ganga's descent but warns only Shiva can bear her fall

title: Bharata at Śṛṅgaverapura; Guha's suspicion and guidance
description: Bharata's army halts at Śṛṅgaverapura; Guha first suspects hostile intent then, reassured, shows Bharata the grass-bed where Rāma slept and helps ferry the host across the Gaṅgā

title: Breaking of Shiva's Bow
description: Rama breaks the bow of Shiva at Janaka's court, winning the contest that qualifies him to marry Sita

title: Ṛcīka prepares two charged charus
description: Ṛcīka cooks one brāhmaṇa-tejas caru for Satyavatī and one kṣatriya-tejas caru for her mother, to seed a brahmin heir and a warrior heir respectively

title: Cremation and celestial release
description: The brothers burn Kabandha's body in a pit, and a luminous gandharva rises from the pyre on a celestial chariot, the curse undone

title: Daśaratha's death and the queens' mourning
description: Daśaratha dies of grief after Rāma's exile; Sumitrā shares the widowed household's vigil, deferring to Kausalyā

title: Delivery of Rāma's signet-ring
description: Hanumān drops Rāma's name-engraved signet-ring before Sītā, who accepts him as Rāma's true envoy

title: Discrimination of Self from the sheaths
description: Rāma teaches dṛg-dṛśya-viveka and negation of the five kośas and three bodies, identifying the Self as the unchanging witness

title: Division of the pāyasa and birth of the four sons
description: Daśaratha apportions the pāyasa among his queens, and Rāma, Bharata, and the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna are born as Viṣṇu's aṃśas
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 16–18; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.10

title: Fall of the rākṣasa champions and Prahasta
description: In successive sorties Rāvaṇa's commanders Dhūmrākṣa, Akampana, Vajradaṃṣṭra, and the chief general Prahasta are slain by Hanumān, Aṅgada, and Nīla

title: Gaṇeśa as the brahmin boy tricks Rāvaṇa
description: Gaṇeśa, as a cowherd boy, agrees to hold the liṅga but sets it down after calling out three times when Rāvaṇa's prayers run long

title: Gandharvas steal the rams and break the condition
description: The Gandharvas steal Urvaśī's rams by night; Purūravas leaps up naked in pursuit and a lightning-flash reveals him, breaking the taboo, so Urvaśī vanishes
source: Shatapatha Brahmana XI.5.1; Vishnu Purana IV.6; Bhagavata Purana IX.14

title: Gautama curses Indra
description: Gautama curses Indra to lose his testicles (later replaced with a ram's), or in Purāṇic versions to bear a thousand marks softened into a thousand eyes (Sahasrākṣa)
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 48; Brahma Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa

title: Gautama curses the Moon
description: In a Purāṇic strand Candra, implicated as Indra's accomplice in the dawn-ruse, is cursed to wane or bear the lunar blemish

title: Gift of the pādukā (sandals) as regent-token
description: Rāma surrenders his gold sandals; Bharata enthrones them and rules Kosala as their servant from Nandigrāma for the remaining exile

title: Gārgī concedes Yājñavalkya's supremacy
description: Satisfied, Gārgī tells the assembled Brahmins that none of them will defeat Yājñavalkya in debate about Brahman, withdrawing her challenge with honor

title: Guha suspects and then receives Bharata
description: When Bharata's army halts at Shringaverapura, Guha first musters his Nishadas fearing harm to Rama, then, finding Bharata grief-worn, honours him as a guest

title: Hanuman brokers the Rama-Sugriva alliance
description: Serving Sugriva, Hanuman first meets Rama and Lakshmana and brokers their alliance, impressing Rama with his flawless speech

title: Hanumān finds Sītā in the Aśoka grove
description: After searching Laṅkā's mansions in vain, Hanumān spots the wasted, sorrowful Sītā guarded by rākṣasīs in the Aśoka-vana

title: Hariścandra vindicated and son revived
description: The gods reveal the ordeal as a test Hariścandra passed without a lie; Rohitāśva is revived, the family and kingdom restored, and heaven won and shared with his people

title: Indra seduces Ahalya and is cursed
description: Indra takes sage Gautama's form to lie with Ahalya; the returning sage curses Indra (losing his testicles or bearing a thousand marks that become eyes, hence Sahasraksha)

title: Śiva and Pārvatī complete the art with Tāṇḍava and Lāsya
description: Śiva contributes the vigorous Tāṇḍava (via Taṇḍu) and Pārvatī the graceful Lāsya, completing the dance dimension of drama

title: Jaṭāyu pledges to guard Sītā
description: On the way to Pañcavaṭī the family meets the aged vulture-king Jaṭāyu, friend of Daśaratha, who pledges to protect Sītā in the brothers' absence

title: Kaikeyī retreats to the krodhāgāra
description: Persuaded, Kaikeyī casts off her ornaments and lies in the anger-chamber to ambush the king

title: Kaikeyī's boons and Rāma's exile
description: On the eve of his coronation Kaikeyī invokes two boons sending Rāma into 14-year exile and Bharata to the throne; Rāma departs with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa

title: Kausalyā's lament at the exile
description: Learning of the fourteen-year exile, Kausalyā grieves and would at first forbid Rāma to go

title: Kārtavīrya Arjuna seizes Kāmadhenu
description: The thousand-armed Haihaya king Kārtavīrya Arjuna (Sahasrārjuna) of Māhiṣmatī seizes the wish-cow by force and wrecks the hermitage

title: Kubera founds Alaka
description: Dispossessed of Lanka, Kubera builds his magnificent new capital Alakapuri in the Himalayas near Kailasa, the archetypal city of inexhaustible riches

title: Mantharā recalls the two boons
description: She reminds Kaikeyī of Daśaratha's two boons and counsels demanding Bharata's coronation and Rāma's fourteen-year exile

title: Marriage of Rishyashringa to Shanta
description: The grateful Lomapada gives his daughter Shanta (originally Dasharatha's daughter) to Rishyashringa, turning the forest-celibate into a householder, and pacifies the wrathful Vibhandaka

title: Mārīca's fatalist consent
description: Threatened with death by Rāvaṇa, Mārīca chooses death-by-Rāma as the nobler end and consents to the deer-ruse, foreseeing and accepting his own doom

title: Mutilation of Śūrpaṇakhā
description: When the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā lunges at Sītā, Rāma orders Lakṣmaṇa to disfigure her; he cuts off her nose (and ears), the immediate spark of the war

title: Mutilation of Śūrpaṇakhā (nose & ears cut)
description: Lakṣmaṇa, at Rāma's word, cuts off Śūrpaṇakhā's nose and ears as she lunges at Sītā — the act that names Nāsik and ignites the war
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 18; Nāsik regional tradition

title: Paraśurāma slays Kārtavīrya and the kṣatriyas
description: The axe-bearing avatāra Paraśurāma, after the Kāmadhenu theft and his father Jamadagni's death, slays the thousand-armed Kārtavīrya Arjuna and vows to clear the earth of kṣatriyas twenty-one times

title: Rama crowns Vibhishana king of Lanka
description: After Ravana's fall Rama crowns the defector Vibhishana king of Lanka and grants him life lasting to the Kalpa's end

title: Rama's Darbha-Sayanam at Tirupullani
description: At the Sethu site of Tirupullani, Rama performs darbha-sayanam (lying on sacred grass) before the crossing to Lanka

title: Rama's Triumphant Return to Ayodhya
description: Rama returns to Ayodhya after exile and the war, the prototype celebration of Dipavali

title: Renewed advance and slaying of Rāvaṇa
description: Strengthened by the Sun's grace, Rāma takes up his bow, advances on Rāvaṇa, and goes on to slay him
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 105.31 and following sargas

title: Return to relay Rāma's parting words at Daśaratha's deathbed
description: Sumantra returns with the empty chariot and recites Rāma's messages and serenity to the dying Daśaratha, the king's last contact with his son before his death

title: Rāma's jala-samādhi at Gopratāra — return as Viṣṇu
description: At the Gopratāra (Guptār) ford Brahmā says 'Enter, O Viṣṇu'; Rāma casts off his human body, resumes his Vaiṣṇava form, and ascends to Vaikuṇṭha
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa; Skanda Purāṇa Ayodhyā-māhātmya; (variant) Svargadvāra ghāṭ

title: Rāma slays Subāhu with the Āgneyāstra
description: Rāma looses the fire-weapon Āgneyāstra at Subāhu, who is struck in the chest and falls dead — Rāma's second slaying

title: Rāma's twin proofs of strength
description: To convince the doubting Sugrīva, Rāma flicks Dundubhi's skeleton ten yojanas with his toe and splits seven sāla trees with a single arrow

title: Rāma worships Sūrya and slays Rāvaṇa
description: Rāma recites the hymn, gazes at the Sun thrice, is filled with resolve, and—urged on by Sūrya himself—takes up his bow and kills Rāvaṇa

title: Rāvaṇa Lifts Mount Kailāsa
description: The demon-king Ravana tries to uproot Kailasa; Shiva pins it with his toe crushing Ravana, who then composes the Shiva-tandava-stotra

title: Rāvaṇa's digvijaya and Indrajit's victory over Indra
description: Rāvaṇa subdues yakṣas, gandharvas, nāgas, and kings, even defeating Yama, while his son Meghanāda conquers Indra and earns the name Indrajit

title: Rāvaṇa sings the Śiva Tāṇḍava Stotra
description: Rāvaṇa composes and sings the hymn praising Śiva's cosmic dance to win release and favor

title: Sagara's Aśvamedha and the theft of the horse
description: Indra steals the horse of King Sagara's Aśvamedha, leading to the destruction of his 60,000 sons and ultimately framing the descent of the Gaṅgā

title: Shiva-Gita: Shiva instructs Rama and grants the Pashupata weapon
description: In a Shaiva counterpart to the Bhagavad Gita, Shiva instructs Rama in self-knowledge and grants him the pashupata weapon

title: Slaughter of Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons
description: In the Mahābhārata telling Viśvāmitra engineers the death of Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons via the cannibal rākṣasa Kalmāṣapāda

title: Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa insist on accompanying Rāma
description: Sītā refuses to be left behind, declaring a wife's place is at her husband's side, and Lakṣmaṇa is granted leave to follow as servant-protector

title: Sītā fashions the sand-liṅga (Rāmaliṅga)
description: With the muhūrta lapsing, Sītā makes a liṅga from seashore sand which Rāma installs and worships as the Rāmanātha-liṅga, the temple's sanctum deity

title: Sugrīva enthroned, Aṅgada made heir
description: Lakṣmaṇa enters Kiṣkindhā and consecrates Sugrīva king of the vānaras, with Vāli's son Aṅgada installed as crown prince

title: Sutikshna and Rama's vow to clear Dandaka
description: At Sutikshna's ashram the rishis beg protection and Rama vows to rid the forest of the rakshasas devouring them

title: Teaching on bhakti as precondition of knowledge
description: Śiva declares single-minded devotion to Śiva, not rite or lineage, opens liberating knowledge

title: The beheading of Reṇukā
description: Jamadagni orders his sons to slay their mother; the four elders refuse and are cursed to idiocy, while Paraśurāma alone obeys and beheads Reṇukā with the axe

title: The boon fulfilled — birth of Raghu
description: Curse lifted, Dilīpa and Sudakṣiṇā return to Ayodhyā and bear the son Raghu, whose glory renames the senior Solar line the Raghuvaṃśa

title: The fallen garland and Indumatī's sudden death
description: Nārada's celestial garland falls from the sky onto Indumatī in a pleasure-garden; the touch of a heavenly object fulfills the curse-term and she dies instantly, Hariṇī released to heaven

title: The fire-witnessed Rāma-Sugrīva alliance
description: Hanumān kindles fire; Rāma and Sugrīva circumambulate it and swear mutual aid with Agni as witness — Rāma to slay Vāli and restore Sugrīva's kingdom, Sugrīva to find Sītā

title: The four-fold wedding at Mithilā
description: Daśaratha arrives and all four sons wed together: Rāma-Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa-Ūrmilā, Bharata-Māṇḍavī, Śatrughna-Śrutakīrti, on Vivāha Pañcamī

title: The golden deer lures Rāma away
description: Mārīca takes the form of a dazzling golden deer at Rāvaṇa's order; the enchanted Sītā begs Rāma to capture it, drawing him from the hermitage

title: The half-tasted berries offered to Rāma
description: Śabarī offers forest fruit — in the devotional tradition, berries she has bitten first to test for sweetness — which Rāma eats with delight as the purest offering of love, over Lakṣmaṇa's dismay
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya-kāṇḍa 74; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; folk/bhakti retellings

title: The pādukā and the Nandigrāma regency
description: Bharata takes Rāma's golden sandals, enthrones them as sovereign, and rules as ascetic regent from Nandigrāma for fourteen years, vowing self-immolation if Rāma does not return on time

title: The pāyasa distributed to the queens
description: A divine being rises from the sacrificial fire bearing pāyasa for the queens; its distribution gives Sumitrā two sons

title: The reviving boon
description: Pleased, Jamadagni grants boons; Paraśurāma asks that his mother be revived without memory and his brothers restored

title: The roar and the naming of Rāvaṇa
description: Pinned, the demon screams so the three worlds shudder; from this cry Śiva gives him the name Rāvaṇa ('he who makes roar/cry')

title: The trials of Harishchandra
description: The truthful Ikshvaku king Harishchandra is stripped of kingdom, wife and son to honor a debt to Vishvamitra and becomes a cremation-ground slave, yet never lies and is finally restored to heaven

title: Triśaṅku's ascent and Indra's kick
description: By Viśvāmitra's tapas Triśaṅku rises bodily to heaven, but Indra and the devas kick him back down head-first

title: Trijaṭā consoles Sītā
description: Trijaṭā reassures the despairing Sītā that rescue is near, steadying her resolve

title: Śukra's Warning, Curse, and the Blinded Eye
description: Recognizing Viṣṇu, Śukra forbids the gift and curses Bali; lodging in the kamaṇḍalu spout to block the consecration-water, he is pierced in one eye by Vāmana's kuśa-grass, becoming one-eyed

title: Vamana's three strides reclaiming the worlds from Bali
description: The dwarf avatara takes three strides to reclaim the worlds from the asura king Bali, embedded in the Matsya Purana's deva-asura material

title: Vasiṣṭha's grief and Parāśara's restrained vengeance
description: Bereaved Vasiṣṭha survives repeated suicide attempts and dissuades grandson Parāśara from a world-destroying revenge sacrifice

title: Vibhīṣaṇa performs Rāvaṇa's last rites
description: At first refusing to perform funeral rites for the brother who wronged him, Vibhīṣaṇa is persuaded by Rāma that enmity ends at death and performs the obsequies

title: Vishvajit sacrifice — giving away all wealth
description: Raghu performs the Vishvajit rite, whose vow requires him to give away the entire accumulated wealth of his conquests, leaving himself only earthen vessels

title: Vishvamitra performs the ascent yajna and curses the boycotters
description: Vishvamitra agrees to send Trishanku bodily to heaven and curses Vasishtha's sons and Mahodaya to ash/chandala rebirth when they refuse to attend

title: Viśvāmitra adopts Sunaḥśepa as Devarāta
description: Hotṛ-priest Viśvāmitra adopts the rescued boy as eldest son Devarāta; fifty of his own sons refuse and are cursed to become border peoples

title: Viśvāmitra adopts Śunaḥśepa and curses his sons
description: Viśvāmitra adopts Śunaḥśepa as eldest son, renaming him Devarāta, and curses the fifty of his own sons who refuse the foundling to become outcastes — an aetiology of border tribes

title: Viśvāmitra brings the princes to her forest
description: Viśvāmitra leads Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa into the Tāṭakā-vana, recounts her story, and commands Rāma to slay her

title: Vālmīki composes the Rāmāyaṇa and teaches it to the twins
description: The ādi-kavi composes the 24,000-śloka Rāmāyaṇa (śoka turned to śloka) and trains the twins to chant it, making the hero's unrecognised sons its first reciters

title: Vāmana reclaims the three worlds
description: Viṣṇu as the dwarf Vāmana reclaims the three worlds from the asura king Bali in three strides

title: Śabalā's Army vs. Viśvāmitra
description: When King Viśvāmitra tries to seize Vasiṣṭha's cow Śabalā by force, she generates whole foreign armies from her body that rout his forces

title: Śabarī awaits Rāma at the Pampā-sarovara
description: The devotee Śabarī awaits Rāma at the Pampā lotus-lake and offers her tasted berries before he passes into Kiṣkindhā

title: Agastya equips Rāma in the South
description: At his Daṇḍaka hermitage Agastya gifts Rāma the bow of Viṣṇu and divine arms, and later teaches him the Āditya-Hṛdayam before slaying Rāvaṇa

title: Agastya gifts Rama divine weapons
description: Agastya gives Rama the bow of Vishnu, an inexhaustible quiver and the arrows of Indra and Brahma, and directs him to Panchavati

title: Agastya narrates the condensed Rāmāyaṇa
description: The sage Agastya recounts a compressed Rāma-carita — Rāma's birth, exile, Sītā's abduction by Rāvaṇa, the alliance with Sugrīva and Hanumān, the war at Laṅkā, and the return

title: A thousand years of praise (Śiva Tāṇḍava Stotra)
description: Trapped, Rāvaṇa propitiates Śiva with praise (traditionally the Śiva Tāṇḍava Stotra, in one telling on a vīṇā strung from his own severed head) for a thousand years
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttarakāṇḍa 16; Śiva Tāṇḍava Stotra; Tēvāram tradition

title: Atri and Anasūyā counsel Sītā
description: At the Mandākinī-side hermitage, Anasūyā instructs Sītā on pati-vrata-dharma and gifts her divine ornaments; her tapas is credited with bringing down the Mandākinī

title: Bali Grants the Gift Despite the Warning
description: Invoking Prahlāda and the supreme dharma of truth, Bali refuses to retract his word, accepts Śukra's curse, and pours the water to seal the three paces

title: Brahmā orders the gods to father the vānaras
description: Brahmā commands the gods to beget mighty vānaras (Vālin, Sugrīva, Hanumān, Nala) as Rāma's future army

title: Counsel to ally with Sugrīva
description: Out of gratitude the freed gandharva names Sugrīva at Ṛśyamūka, advises Rāma to swear fire-witnessed friendship with him, framing the reciprocal bargain that drives the Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa

title: Creation of the counter-heaven (Triśaṅku-svarga)
description: Enraged Viśvāmitra builds a parallel southern heaven with new stars and a second Indra; the gods relent, fixing Triśaṅku head-down as a constellation

title: Death of Kumbhakarṇa
description: Roused from his cursed long sleep, the colossal Kumbhakarṇa devours and scatters vānaras until Rāma severs his limbs and head with celestial arrows

title: Departure from Ayodhyā into exile
description: Donning bark garments, Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa leave on Sumantra's chariot as the grieving city follows

title: Exposing the illusory head of Rāma
description: When Rāvaṇa conjures a false severed head of Rāma to break Sītā, Trijaṭā reveals the deception and assures her Rāma lives
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa; later retellings

title: First slaying of Kārtavīrya
description: Paraśurāma pursues, severs Kārtavīrya's thousand arms and beheads him, recovering the cow

title: Gaṅgādhara — descent of Gaṅgā
description: Śiva catches the celestial Gaṅgā in his matted locks to break her world-shattering fall, brought down by Bhagīratha's penance to redeem Sagara's 60,000 sons
source: Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa, Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Skanda Purāṇa

title: Ganesha breaks his tusk against Parashurama
description: In a variant, Ganesha blocks Parashurama at Kailasa and takes Shiva's axe on his tusk out of reverence, breaking it

title: Gautama curses Ahalyā to stone/invisibility
description: Gautama curses Ahalyā — in Vālmīki to invisible ash-strewn penance, in Purāṇic/devotional tradition to become stone — until released by Rāma's advent
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 48; Brahma Purāṇa; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; Rāmcaritmānas; Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa

title: Guha shows Bharata Rama's grass-bed and guides him onward
description: Guha points out the bed of grass and ingudi tree where Rama slept, then arranges Bharata's host across the Ganga and directs him toward Bharadvaja's ashrama

title: Hanuman leaps the ocean to Lanka
description: Reminded of his powers by Jambavan, Hanuman expands to colossal size and bounds across the ocean to Lanka, defeating Surasa and slaying Simhika en route

title: Hanumān's Viśvaliṅga honored first by Śiva's decree
description: Hanumān returns with the Kailāsa Viśvaliṅga to find worship done; Rāma decrees it be worshipped before the Rāmaliṅga, honoring Hanumān's devotion

title: Hariscandra the truthful
description: Ikshvaku king Hariscandra surrenders kingdom, wife, and son to honor a debt to Vishvamitra, is tested to the extreme, and elevated to heaven
source: Markandeya Purana, Aitareya Brahmana, Devi Bhagavata

title: Śiva's grace (Rāvaṇānugraha) and the boon
description: Pleased, Śiva frees Rāvaṇa, restores his strength, and grants a boon (often the sword Candrahāsa)

title: Kautsa episode and the assault on Kubera
description: The brahmin Kautsa begs fourteen crore gold coins for his guru's fee; the now-penniless Raghu prepares to attack Kubera, who rains gold into his treasury

title: Lakṣmaṇa recalls Sugrīva to his vow
description: When Sugrīva lapses into pleasure and forgets his oath, an enraged Lakṣmaṇa is sent to Kiṣkindhā; Tārā's diplomacy rouses Sugrīva to mobilize the search

title: Lakṣmaṇa returns as Śeṣa
description: Lakṣmaṇa, who entered the Sarayū before Rāma, is taken up as Śeṣa/Ananta, the cosmic serpent on whom Viṣṇu reclines

title: Maināka Rises to Aid Hanumān
description: As Hanuman leaps the ocean to Lanka, Mainaka rises from the sea to offer him rest as a debt repaid to Vayu; Hanuman touches it courteously and flies on

title: Marriage of Rama and Sita
description: Having broken Shiva's bow, Rama marries Sita, princess of Mithila

title: Menakā breaks Viśvāmitra's tapas; birth of Śakuntalā
description: Indra sends apsarā Menakā to seduce Viśvāmitra; they live together ten years and beget Śakuntalā, future mother of Bharata
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 63; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva

title: Māyā and superimposition
description: Rāma explains the world as the play of māyā, an apparent superimposition on Brahman like silver on nacre or snake on rope

title: Rama's Jala-Samadhi into the Sarayu
description: At his reign's close Rama appoints Kusha and Lava, walks into the Sarayu at Gopratara, takes his Vaishnava form and ascends to Vaikuntha

title: Rambhā assaulted by Rāvaṇa and Nalakūbara's curse
description: Rāvaṇa assaults Rambhā despite her protests, prompting Nalakūbara to curse that Rāvaṇa's head would burst into seven pieces if he ever forced a woman — the curse that later protected Sītā

title: Ravana steals the Pushpaka
description: Ravana assaults Kubera again and carries off the self-willed flying palace-chariot Pushpaka

title: Reunion at Rāma's coronation
description: On Rāma's return and coronation the three queens are reunited with their sons; Sumitrā recovers her twins honoured in service and kingship

title: Reunion at the swan-lake and the annual-night boon
description: Wandering and lamenting, Purūravas finds Urvaśī among apsarās as aquatic birds at Anyataḥplakṣā; she grants him one night a year and the promise of a son

title: Rāma instructs Hanumān on the 108 Upaniṣads
description: In the Muktikā Upaniṣad, Rāma teaches Hanumān that liberation comes from studying the 108 Upaniṣads and enumerates them

title: Rāma reconciles his mother and receives her blessing
description: Rāma argues that obeying a father's word is supreme dharma; Kausalyā yields and gives a protective benediction for the forest journey

title: Rāma's Aśvamedha with the golden Sītā
description: Refusing to remarry, Rāma performs the imperial horse-sacrifice using a golden image of Sītā in the wife's ritual seat

title: Rāma's Śrāddha for Daśaratha at Gayā
description: Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa come to Gayā to perform śrāddha for Daśaratha; while the men bathe, the ancestor's hand appears demanding the piṇḍa

title: Rāma's return and coronation
description: Rāma flies home by the Puṣpaka vimāna; Hanumān reassures Bharata, who hands back the kingdom at the Rāma-rājya coronation

title: Rāma teaches Śabarī the navadhā bhakti
description: In the Rāmcaritmānas, Rāma tells the low-born Śabarī he reckons devotion alone above caste and expounds the nine forms of bhakti, declaring her dear to him

title: Śūrpaṇakhā and Akampana rouse Rāvaṇa
description: Survivors carry word of the slaughter to Laṅkā, steering Rāvaṇa toward abduction

title: Rāvaṇa lifts Mount Kailāsa and receives Candrahāsa
description: Affronted at Kailāsa, Rāvaṇa tries to uproot the mountain; Śiva pins him with a toe, and after Rāvaṇa sings his praises for a thousand years Śiva releases him and grants the sword Candrahāsa

title: Rāvaṇa threatens Sītā with two months
description: Rāvaṇa courts Sītā with promises of queenship; she rejects him utterly, and he gives her two months to relent or be killed

title: Sanatkumara's prophecy of Rishyashringa
description: The sage Sanatkumara foretold that Vibhandaka's son Rishyashringa would come to Anga, end its drought, marry Shanta, and later enable an Ikshvaku king to obtain sons

title: Second demonic birth: Ravana and Kumbhakarna slain
description: The cursed pair are reborn as the rakshasa brothers Ravana and Kumbhakarna of Lanka, both slain by the single avatara Rama in Treta-yuga

title: Shiva catches Ganga in his locks
description: Shiva traps the proud, plunging Ganga entirely in his matted hair, then releases her in streams to earth, becoming Gangadhara

title: Shunahshepa freed by praising the gods
description: Bound to the stake, Shunahshepa praises Prajapati, Agni, Savitr, Varuna and the Vishvedevas with rc; his bonds loosen verse by verse and the king is cured

title: Slaughter of Khara, Dūṣaṇa and 14,000 rākṣasas at Janasthāna
description: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa annihilate Khara, Dūṣaṇa, and 14,000 rākṣasas at Janasthāna, driving Rāvaṇa to plot Sītā's abduction

title: Slaughter of Khara, Dūṣaṇa and the host of Janasthāna
description: Rāma alone destroys the fourteen-thousand-strong rākṣasa army of Janasthāna, clearing the district and goading Rāvaṇa toward abduction

title: Sītā casts down her jewels as a trail
description: Borne off by Rāvaṇa, Sītā drops her jewels to leave a trail later recovered with the vānaras, pointing the search toward Laṅkā

title: Sītā's cūḍāmaṇi token
description: Sītā gives Hanumān her crest-jewel and the private kākāsura recollection as recognition-tokens to carry back to Rāma

title: Sītā's ornaments dropped over Ṛṣyamūka
description: Sugrīva produces jewels Sītā cast from Rāvaṇa's flying chariot as it passed over Ṛṣyamūka; Rāma recognizes only her foot-ornaments and weeps — the first trace of the abduction route

title: Sunahshepa's hymns free him and cure Harishchandra
description: Bound to the post, Sunahshepa praises the gods with Rigvedic hymns; his fetters fall verse by verse and with the hymn to Ushas the last bond falls and Harishchandra is cured

title: Sutīkṣṇa's hermitage
description: Rāma is received by the ascetic Sutīkṣṇa, who hosts the party and directs them deeper south toward Agastya

title: Teaching on the jīva and embodiment
description: Śiva expounds the constitution of the body, the sheaths, transmigration, and the wretchedness of repeated birth

title: The Ajavilāpa (Aja's lament)
description: Aja pours out the celebrated vilāpa lament over Indumatī's body — the flower-turned-thunderbolt, his loss of wife/counselor/pupil/companion at one stroke — and refuses all consolation, including Nārada's revelation

title: The Ambarīṣa variant of the Sunaḥśepa rescue
description: King Ambarīṣa procures Sunaḥśepa (son of Ṛcīka) as victim when Indra steals his sacrifice; Viśvāmitra teaches the boy mantras and Indra grants him long life

title: The boon and restoration of Reṇukā
description: Pleased by his obedience, Jamadagni grants boons; Paraśurāma asks that his mother be revived without memory, his brothers regain their wits, and for invincibility and long life

title: The caru-swap
description: The queen-mother, coveting a finer son, persuades Satyavatī to exchange charus (and trees), so the brāhmaṇa-caru goes to the mother and the kṣatriya-caru to Satyavatī
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 116; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7

title: The coronation plan and Mantharā's redemption of the boons
description: Daśaratha resolves to crown Rāma yuvarāja, but Mantharā goads Kaikeyī to invoke her two dormant boons demanding Bharata's crown and Rāma's fourteen-year exile

title: The death of Vālī
description: After a garland marks Sugrīva in the rematch, Rāma shoots Vālī from concealment; the dying Vālī rebukes Rāma, then accepts the justice of it and commends his son and queen

title: The dharma-debate over killing a woman
description: Rāma hesitates to kill a woman; Viśvāmitra resolves that protecting the world from a predator overrides the prohibition, citing precedents

title: The golden deer lures Sītā and Rāma
description: Mārīca takes the form of a jewel-like golden deer (Mārīca-mṛga) near Pañcavaṭī; Sītā longs for it and sends a reluctant Rāma to capture it

title: The kopa-bhavana scripted
description: On Mantharā's instruction Kaikeyī enters the chamber of wrath in soiled garments to confront Daśaratha

title: The rākṣasa host scattered and the sacrifice completed
description: Rāma disperses the remaining night-rangers with the Vāyavyāstra, letting Viśvāmitra complete the sacrifice unpolluted

title: The Ātma-liṅga roots as Mahābaleśvara
description: The liṅga roots immovably at Gokarṇa; Rāvaṇa's vain great force (mahā-bala) to lift it names it Mahābaleśvara

title: The two demands and Daśaratha's ruin
description: Kaikeyī binds Daśaratha to his oath and demands Bharata's coronation and Rāma's fourteen-year exile, breaking the king

title: Trishanku ascends and Indra kicks him down
description: By Vishvamitra's tapas Trishanku rises bodily to heaven's gates, but Indra and the devas kick the cursed chandala back down and he plummets head-downward

title: Vasiṣṭha's restraint and survival
description: Bereaved, Vasiṣṭha attempts suicide in fire, sea and rivers which refuse to kill him, then dissuades grandson Parāśara from a world-destroying revenge sacrifice

title: Vibhīṣaṇa crowned king of Laṅkā
description: After victory Rāma fulfils his pledge and has Vibhīṣaṇa formally crowned king of Laṅkā, establishing dharmic rule in place of Rāvaṇa's tyranny

title: Vishnu agrees to descend as Dasharatha's sons
description: Oppressed by Ravana, the gods petition Brahma/Vishnu, and Vishnu agrees to be born as the four sons of Dasharatha to destroy the demon

title: Viśvāmitra demands Hariścandra's kingdom
description: After Hariścandra disrupts his penance and promises him anything, Viśvāmitra claims the rājasūya dakṣiṇā and demands the entire kingdom, leaving the king only his body, wife, and son

title: Yājñavalkya's renunciation and division of his estate
description: Resolving to leave householder life for renunciation, Yājñavalkya proposes to divide his property between his two wives, the brahmavādinī Maitreyī and the worldly Kātyāyanī

title: Śabarī's self-immolation and ascent
description: Her purpose fulfilled, Śabarī enters fire by her own yogic power with Rāma's grace and ascends to the highest worlds to rejoin Mataṅga's disciples

title: Agastya Humbles the Vindhya Mountain
description: The Vindhya grows skyward in jealousy of Meru until sage Agastya asks it to bow until he returns from the south and never returns, fixing it low and marking Agastya's southward journey

title: Agastya's gift of Viṣṇu's bow
description: At Agastya's āśrama the sage gives Rāma the bow of Viṣṇu, an inexhaustible quiver, a sword, and arrows of Indra and Brahmā

title: Aja's renunciation and death
description: Wasting in grief, Aja rears Daśaratha to kingship, crowns him, then ends his own life by willed self-release to rejoin Indumatī, passing the Solar dynasty cleanly to Daśaratha

title: Atikāya and Rāvaṇa's sons slain
description: Narāntaka, Devāntaka, Triśiras, Mahodara, Mahāpārśva, and the Brahmā-armored giant Atikāya (slain by Lakṣmaṇa with the brahmāstra) fall in turn

title: Śatrughna slays Lavaṇāsura
description: Rāma sends Śatrughna against the asura Lavaṇa; Śatrughna ambushes him when Lavaṇa has left behind his invincible Śiva-given trident and kills him with Rāma's divine arrow

title: Ayodhya's Citizens Follow Rama into the River
description: The people and even animals of Ayodhya enter the Sarayu behind their king and attain the higher worlds, the city dissolving en masse into liberation

title: Birth of Aja and Raghu's retirement
description: Blessed by Kautsa, Raghu fathers his heir Aja, then in old age abdicates to Aja and dies as a yogin in contemplation; the senior Solar line is renamed Raghuvamsha after him
source: Raghuvamsha 5.36, 8.11-25; Vishnu Purana IV; Bhagavata Purana IX

title: Birth of Rama and his brothers (Ramopakhyana)
description: Vishnu is born as Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna to Dasharatha of Ayodhya, the childhood compressed without the putrakameshti elaboration

title: Birth of Rāma and his brothers
description: In Caitra the four princes are born — Rāma to Kausalyā, Bharata to Kaikeyī, and the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna to Sumitrā — embodying portions of Viṣṇu

title: Brahmā grants Viśvāmitra the title Rājarṣi
description: After long southern austerity Viśvāmitra wins only the rank of rājarṣi, stinging him to redouble his penance

title: Ṛcīka's deferral boon
description: Perceiving the swap by tapas, Ṛcīka relents at Satyavatī's plea and defers the misplaced kṣatriya ferocity from her son to her grandson
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 116; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7

title: Daśaratha bound by oath and the Raghu truth-vow forces the exile
description: Sworn by oath before naming the price, Daśaratha collapses but cannot break the Raghu vow of word-keeping, and lets Kaikeyī pronounce Rāma's exile

title: Daśaratha's Aśvamedha
description: King Daśaratha of Ayodhyā performs the great consecratory horse sacrifice that opens the Rāmāyaṇa, preceding the son-desiring rite

title: Dasharatha summons Rishyashringa for the putrakameshti
description: The childless Dasharatha, on Sumantra's and Vasishtha's counsel, invites his son-in-law Rishyashringa from Anga to Ayodhya to officiate an heir-producing sacrifice

title: Devastation of the Aśoka-vāṭikā
description: Hanumān uproots and lays waste the grove, slays the warriors sent against him, and is bound by Indrajit's brahmāstra

title: Ganga liberates the 60,000 sons
description: Ganga flows behind Bhagiratha's chariot to the ocean and netherworld, washing the ashes of the 60,000 sons and granting them heaven

title: Garuḍa Frees Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa from the Nāgapāśa
description: Garuḍa appears to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa and dispels Indrajit's nāgapāśa serpent-arrows by his mere presence

title: Grace and the boon of Candrahāsa
description: Pleased, Śiva frees Rāvaṇa, restores his strength, and grants him the invincible sword Candrahāsa — the Rāvaṇānugraha grace

title: Guha receives the exiles and they cross the Ganges
description: The Niṣāda chief Guha hosts the exiles at Śṛṅgaverapura; Rāma mats his hair into ascetic locks, crosses the Ganges, and sends Sumantra back

title: Hariścandra sells his queen and son in Kāśī
description: To raise the gold dakṣiṇā Viśvāmitra still demands, the destitute Hariścandra sells his queen Śaivyā and son Rohitāśva into bondage to an old brahmin in Kāśī

title: Identity of jīva and Brahman (Advaita core)
description: Śiva teaches that the individual self is not other than Brahman/Śiva and liberation is realising 'I am That'

title: Kaikeyī delivers the exile sentence and the bark garments
description: Kaikeyī announces the exile to Rāma's face, hurries his departure, and produces bark robes; Vasiṣṭha checks her attempt to make Sītā wear bark

title: Kausalyā blesses Sītā
description: The senior queen blesses Sītā as a daughter and instructs her in wifely dharma before the exile

title: Kārtavīrya Arjuna's theft of the wish-cow
description: The thousand-armed Haihaya king of Māhiṣmatī, feasted by the cow, covets and seizes her (or her calf) by force, wrecking Jamadagni's āśrama

title: Kubera's curse on the Pushpaka and Rama's homecoming
description: Kubera curses that whoever slays Ravana shall ride the Pushpaka; after Ravana's death Rama flies home to Ayodhya in it with Sita, the homecoming celebrated at Dipavali, later restoring the vimana to Kubera

title: Maitreyī's question on wealth and immortality
description: Maitreyī asks whether all the earth's wealth could make her immortal; Yājñavalkya replies there is no hope of immortality through wealth (amṛtatvasya tu nāśāsti vittena), and she asks instead for his knowledge

title: Mārīca's dying cry in Rāma's voice
description: Pierced by Rāma's arrow, the dying Mārīca mimics Rāma's voice crying for Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, driving Lakṣmaṇa away and leaving Sītā unguarded for Rāvaṇa's abduction

title: Mārīca's golden-deer ruse
description: Mārīca takes the form of a jewelled golden deer to lure Rāma away from the hut

title: Nishadraj Guha as model bhakta (devotional afterlife)
description: Tulsidas and Kamban expand Guha into a model devotee whose low birth is dissolved by Rama's embrace, paired with Shabari and the Kevat as emblems that bhakti levels caste

title: Nārada frames the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa
description: Questioned by Vālmīki on the ideal man, Nārada narrates the Saṃkṣepa-rāmāyaṇa, instigating the epic

title: Purūravas institutes the three sacred fires and becomes a Gandharva
description: By the gandharvas' boon Purūravas makes the śamī-aśvattha araṇi, kindles and establishes the three sacred fires, and ascends to gandharva-hood, rejoining Urvaśī
source: Shatapatha Brahmana XI.5.1; Bhagavata Purana IX.14; Vishnu Purana IV.6

title: Putra-kameshti yajna & birth of Rama and brothers
description: Childless Dasaratha performs a son-granting sacrifice; sacred payasa yields Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna

title: Recognition of Lava and Kuśa by recitation
description: The twins chant the Rāmāyaṇa at the sacrificial assembly and their song and faces reveal them as Rāma's sons in Vālmīki's gentle, non-martial climax

title: Rāma breaks the Setu at Dhanuṣkoṭi
description: At Vibhīṣaṇa's request Rāma breaks the bridge with his bow-tip (or arrow) so it cannot be reused, naming the spot Dhanuṣ-koṭi

title: Rāma redeems Ahalyā
description: Guided by Viśvāmitra, Rāma reaches the deserted hermitage and liberates Ahalyā — by his darśana in Vālmīki, by his foot-dust/touch in the dominant devotional tradition — the first overt sign of his redemptive divinity
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 48-49; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; Rāmcaritmānas; Kamban Irāmāvatāram

title: Rāma slays Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras and the 14,000
description: Facing Khara's army single-handed, Rāma kills Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras, Khara, and all fourteen thousand demons of Janasthāna; the gods rain flowers

title: Rāvaṇa captured by Kārtavīrya Arjuna
description: The thousand-armed Haihaya king Kārtavīrya Arjuna captures and binds Rāvaṇa until releasing him, showing a non-divine being could subdue him

title: Shurpanakha's mutilation and Khara-Dushana's destruction
description: At Panchavati Lakshmana cuts off Shurpanakha's nose and ears, and Rama single-handedly annihilates Khara, Dushana and their host, clearing Janasthana (pivotal node detailed in the Panchavati file)

title: Slaying of Tāṭakā — Rāma's first kill
description: After disfiguring her arms, ears, and nose, Rāma kills the charging Tāṭakā with an arrow to the chest — his maiden slaying — as the gods rejoice
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 26; Rāmcaritmānas, Bāla Kāṇḍa

title: Sītā captive and steadfast in the Aśoka grove
description: Confined in the Aśokavanikā and guarded by rākṣasīs, Sītā fasts in grief, rejects Rāvaṇa's wooing and threats, and never wavers in fidelity to Rāma

title: Sītā's Sand-Piṇḍa and Curse of the False Witnesses
description: Sītā offers a piṇḍa of sand with five witnesses; when four lie and only the Akṣayavaṭa tells truth, she curses the Phalgu to run underground and the others, blessing the banyan with imperishability

title: Sugrīva's coronation and Lakṣmaṇa's wrath
description: Sugrīva is enthroned and Aṅgada made crown prince, but Sugrīva forgets his vow in pleasure until the enraged Lakṣmaṇa, cooled by Tārā, spurs him to mobilize

title: Surveying the battlefield with Sītā
description: Trijaṭā takes Sītā to a high vantage to view the war, naming warriors and reporting Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa unharmed

title: The cow's-ear shape and place-name
description: Rāvaṇa twists the fixed liṅga into a cow's-ear (go-karṇa) form, giving the liṅga its shape and the kṣetra its name

title: The exile plot succeeds
description: Bound by his word, Daśaratha grants the boons; Rāma accepts exile, triggering the whole onward epic

title: The four-quarter search for Sītā launched
description: Sugrīva dispatches vānara armies to the four directions to find Sītā within one month; Rāma gives Hanumān his signet ring as a token for Sītā

title: The golden deer (māyā-mṛga)
description: Mārīca becomes a jewelled golden deer luring Rāma away from the hut while Lakṣmaṇa is posted to guard Sītā

title: The Jayanta-crow at Sphaṭik Śilā
description: Indra's son Jayanta in crow-form pecks Sītā's foot at the crystal rock and is punished by Rāma's brahmāstra-reed, losing one eye

title: The jīvanmukta described
description: Rāma describes the one liberated-in-life, free of egoism and doership, untouched while prārabdha karma plays out

title: The Lakṣmaṇa-rekhā and Lakṣmaṇa's departure
description: Provoked by Mārīca's false cry in Rāma's voice and Sītā's accusation, Lakṣmaṇa leaves to find Rāma after drawing a protective line Sītā must not cross

title: The people of Ayodhyā enter the Sarayū and attain heaven
description: The citizens of Ayodhyā — men, women, even animals — enter the Sarayū at Gopratāra behind their king and attain the higher worlds (the Santānaka heaven)
actors: The people and animals of Ayodhyā

title: The Śrīraṅgam Ranganātha legend
description: Carrying the Raṅga-vimāna icon of Viṣṇu gifted by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa sets it down at Śrīraṅgam, where it roots forever facing south toward Laṅkā

title: The slaying of Vāli
description: At the second challenge, ignoring Tārā's warning, Vāli fights Sugrīva and Rāma shoots him from concealment, triggering the epic's most-debated dharma-dilemma

title: Trijaṭā's prophetic dream
description: The aged rākṣasī Trijaṭā recounts an omen-dream foretelling Laṅkā's burning, Rāvaṇa's death, and Rāma's triumph, restraining the others from harming Sītā

title: Trivikrama Measures the Worlds
description: Vāmana swells into the cosmic Trivikrama and with two strides covers earth and the heavens; his toe pierces the universe's shell, releasing the celestial Gaṅgā, leaving no space for the third pace

title: Vishvamitra adopts Shunahshepa as Devarata
description: The officiating Hotr Vishvamitra adopts the rescued boy as eldest son, renaming him Devarata, and curses the fifty resisting sons to outcaste descent

title: Vishvamitra adopts Sunahshepa as Devarata
description: Vishvamitra adopts the rescued boy, renames him Devarata, and makes him eldest heir to his Vedic line; Sunahshepa rejects Ajigarta as no father

title: Vishvamitra builds the counter-heaven and suspends Trishanku
description: Vishvamitra halts the fall mid-air and creates a parallel southern heaven with new stars and a new Indra; Brahma brokers a truce leaving Trishanku fixed head-down among the new stars

title: Viśvāmitra Renounces His Throne for Tapas
description: Humiliated that brahma-tejas crushed his kṣatra-bala in the cow-quarrel, Viśvāmitra renounces his kingdom and undertakes the austerities that make him a Brahmarṣi

title: Wayfinding to Pampā and Śabarī, then ascent
description: Kabandha gives the route west then south to Pampā lake and Mataṅga's hermitage where Śabarī awaits, circles Rāma in reverence, and ascends to heaven

title: Śabarī directs Rāma to Sugrīva
description: Before departing, Śabarī shows Rāma the hermitage and directs him to Lake Pampā and Sugrīva on Ṛṣyamūka, handing the narrative on to the Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa

title: Abduction of Sītā and death of Jaṭāyu
description: Mārīca's golden-deer ruse lures Rāma away; Rāvaṇa abducts Sītā to Laṅkā and the vulture Jaṭāyu dies trying to stop him

title: Abduction of Sītā by Rāvaṇa
description: Disguised as a mendicant, Rāvaṇa seizes the undefended Sītā and carries her off in the puṣpaka

title: Śatrughna founds Madhurā/Mathurā
description: On the Madhuvana site of Lavaṇa's realm, Śatrughna raises the city of Madhurā (Mathurā) and rules it for twelve years

title: Bali's Surrender and Exaltation to Sutala
description: Bali offers his own head for the third stride; interceded for by Prahlāda and Vindhyāvali, he is sent to rule Sutala as an immortal and future Indra of the Sāvarṇi Manvantara, with Viṣṇu as his gatekeeper

title: Bharata's wrath at Mantharā
description: On learning the truth Bharata is enraged at Mantharā; in some versions she is seized and beaten before being spared
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa 78 (with regional amplifications)

title: Bhārgava line gains the warrior-seed
description: Satyavatī bears the serene sage Jamadagni, whose son Paraśurāma manifests the deferred kṣatriya ferocity and exterminates the kṣatriyas
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 115–117; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7, IV.11; Bhāgavata IX.15–16

title: Birth of Āyu and the six sons
description: Through the annual reunions Urvaśī bears Purūravas six sons, chief among them Āyu, the heir through whom the Lunar line continues to Nahuṣa and Yayāti
source: Vishnu Purana IV.6; Bhagavata Purana IX.14

title: Daśaratha's death
description: Daśaratha dies of grief over the exile, his death laid at Kaikeyī's feet

title: Daśaratha's death by grief and deathbed confession
description: On the sixth night after Rāma's departure Daśaratha dies of grief crying Rāma's name, having confessed the Śravaṇa curse to Kausalyā as it comes to term

title: Death of Dasharatha
description: Grief-stricken at Rama's departure into exile, King Dasharatha dies

title: Descent of Ganga and Sagara's sons
