description: Among the Solar dynasty legends, Sagara's 60,000 sons perish and the descent of Ganga is brought about to redeem them

title: Descent of the Gangā (Gangāvataraṇa)
description: After Kapila burns Sagara's 60,000 sons to ash, their descendant Bhagiratha performs millennia of tapas to bring Ganga from heaven; Shiva catches her crashing flow in his matted locks to spare the earth and liberate the ashes

title: Eleven-year residence and departure
description: After eleven-plus years — the longest single exile residence — rākṣasa disturbances drive Rāma's party from Citrakūṭa toward Atri's āśrama and Daṇḍaka/Pañcavaṭī

title: First Sañjīvanī flight: Hanumān carries the mountain
description: After Indrajit's brahmāstra fells the host, Hanumān flies to the Himālaya and, unable to tell the healing herbs apart, carries the whole Droṇagiri mountain back to revive the fallen

title: First slaying of Kārtavīrya Arjuna
description: Paraśurāma pursues to Māhiṣmatī, severs the king's thousand arms, beheads him, and recovers the cow — the opening blow of the kṣatriya war

title: Hanuman conceived as Rudravatara
description: The vayu-borne portion of Shiva is placed in Anjana's womb, conceiving the vanara hero Hanuman, the fullest womb-born Shiva-descent and supreme devotee of Rama

title: Hanuman reveals himself to Sita with Rama's ring
description: Hanuman presents Rama's signet ring as a token, offers to carry Sita back (she refuses), and receives her crest-jewel for Rama

title: Hanumān gives Sītā Rāma's signet ring
description: Hanumān reveals himself, recites Rāma's story, and presents Rāma's named signet ring as proof; Sītā weeps with joy and questions him about Rāma

title: Hanumān meets Sītā and exchanges tokens
description: Hanumān finds Sītā in the grove, gives Rāma's signet ring as proof, and receives her crest-jewel; she refuses rescue, insisting Rāma win her honorably

title: Hariścandra sells himself to a Cāṇḍāla
description: The remainder of the fee is exacted by selling Hariścandra himself to a Cāṇḍāla keeper of the cremation ground — revealed to be Yama/Dharma in disguise — who sets him to collect the death-tax from every corpse

title: Hosting Rama at the Prayaga ashram en route to Chitrakuta
description: At his hermitage at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence, Bharadvaja welcomes the exiled Rama, Sita and Lakshmana and counsels them to settle at Chitrakuta

title: Jahnu swallows and re-releases Ganga
description: When Ganga floods sage Jahnu's hermitage he drinks the whole river in one gulp, then releases her from his ear, fathering her anew as Jahnavi

title: Jñāna-yoga and the jīvanmukta
description: Śiva expounds knowledge-yoga, dispassion, sense-control, and the marks of the liberated-in-life

title: Kausalyā rebukes Daśaratha
description: In anguish after Rāma departs, Kausalyā reproaches Daśaratha for his weakness before Kaikeyī, yet does not abandon him

title: Kārtavīrya-Arjuna Seizes Jamadagni's Cow
description: The thousand-armed Haihaya emperor Kārtavīrya-Arjuna, feasted by Jamadagni's wish-cow, seizes her (or her calf) by force and wrecks the hermitage
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva; Bhāgavata, Padma, Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇas

title: Kusha Founds the Nageshvaranatha Temple
description: Rama's son Kusha founds the Shiva shrine Nageshvaranatha at Ayodhya after recovering an armlet from a naga-maiden of the Sarayu

title: Laṅkā-dahana (the burning of Laṅkā)
description: His tail set alight, Hanumān burns Laṅkā, quenches the fire in the sea, and recrosses to report to Rāma

title: Later tradition: daughter of Vibhīṣaṇa and bhakti reframing
description: Later tradition makes Trijaṭā the daughter of Vibhīṣaṇa and Saramā and recasts her as a devotee of Rāma in the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa and Rāmcaritmānas
source: Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; Rāmcaritmānas; later Rāmāyaṇa tradition

title: Meghanada captures Indra (Indrajit)
description: Ravana's son Meghanada captures Indra and earns the name Indrajit

title: Nalakubara curses Ravana
description: After Ravana violates Rambha, Kubera's son Nalakubara curses Ravana that he can never force an unwilling woman on pain of his head bursting, a curse later credited with sparing Sita in captivity

title: Nārada prompts Vālmīki's composition of the Rāmāyaṇa
description: Vālmīki questions Nārada about the perfectly virtuous man; Nārada recites the essence of Rāma's life, seeding the composition of the Rāmāyaṇa

title: Pampā-sarovar — Rāma meets Śabarī
description: In the Kiṣkindhā country Rāma meets the devotee Śabarī at Pampā-sarovara and is guided toward Sugrīva and Hanumān in his search for Sītā

title: Parashurama annihilates the Kshatriyas twenty-one times
description: Parashurama beheads and restores his mother at his father's word and destroys the Kshatriyas twenty-one times to avenge Jamadagni, filling the lakes of Samanta-panchaka

title: Phala-śruti and close of the Gītā
description: The Gītā closes with the fruit-declaration that whoever recites it crosses saṃsāra and attains Rāma's supreme abode

title: Puñjikasthalā cursed to become Añjanā, mother of Hanumān
description: The apsarā Puñjikasthalā is cursed to be born as the vānara princess Añjanā; Durvāsa softens the curse so she weds Kesari and bears Hanumān before being freed

title: Putrakāmeṣṭi and the birth of Rāma and his brothers
description: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga performs the son-desiring sacrifice for childless Daśaratha; Agni rises with pāyasa divided among the queens, begetting Rāma, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, and Śatrughna as portions of Viṣṇu

title: Rama's exile and Dasharatha's death (Ramopakhyana)
description: Kaikeyi's two boons force Rama's banishment, Dasharatha dies, and Bharata takes up the regency, told in telescoped form

title: Reunion of Ahalyā and Gautama
description: Gautama returns, his wrath spent and the appointed time fulfilled, accepts the purified Ahalyā, and the couple resume married ascetic life

title: Rishyashringa performs the Ashvamedha and Putrakameshti
description: Rishyashringa conducts Dasharatha's Ashvamedha on the Sarayu's north bank, then the son-desiring Putrakameshti to obtain heirs

title: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa bound by the Nāgapāśa
description: Indrajit binds both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with the serpent-weapon Nāgapāśa; they are freed when Garuḍa arrives and the snakes flee

title: Rāma surveys from Gandhamādana Parvatam
description: Rāma is said to have viewed the bridge-building and Laṅkā from the island's highest point, where his footprints (pādukā) are enshrined

title: Śūrpaṇakhā incites Rāvaṇa
description: Śūrpaṇakhā reaches Laṅkā and goads Rāvaṇa, describing Sītā's beauty and planting the desire that will doom him

title: Settling at Chitrakūṭa
description: On Bharadvāja's advice the exiles reach Chitrakūṭa on the Mandākinī, where Lakṣmaṇa builds a leaf hermitage and forest life begins

title: Sugrīva enthroned, lapse, and Lakṣmaṇa's wrath
description: Sugrīva is consecrated king of the vānaras with Aṅgada as heir, then lapses into pleasure forgetting his vow until Lakṣmaṇa's furious entry recalls him to duty

title: Svayamprabhā aids the southern party
description: Trapped in the magical cave Ṛkṣabila, the famished southern party is fed by the ascetic Svayamprabhā, who transports them out to the seashore

title: Tapas for and grant of the Ātma-liṅga
description: By fierce tapas offering his heads, Rāvaṇa wins from Śiva the Ātma-liṅga to make Laṅkā invincible, on condition it never touch the ground (with the Vaidyanātha head-healing variant)

title: The cast-off coverings become subsidiary shrines
description: Rāvaṇa hurls away the casket, lid, string, and cloth, which fall to form the Dhāreśvara, Guṇavanteśvara, Murudeśvara, and Śejjeśvara liṅgas

title: The false cry and Sītā sending Lakṣmaṇa away
description: Dying Mārīca cries out in Rāma's voice; Sītā drives Lakṣmaṇa to leave her, the moment later elaborated as the Lakṣmaṇa-rekhā

title: The four-quarter search and Sampāti's tidings
description: Sugrīva dispatches vānara parties to the four quarters; the southern party, after the Svayamprabhā cave, learns from the vulture Sampāti that Sītā is held in Laṅkā

title: The Lava-Kuśa war (capture of the sacrificial horse)
description: In the Purāṇic/folk amplification the boys seize the wandering horse and defeat Rāma's army and brothers, binding Hanumān, before the truth emerges

title: The ātman discourse — 'for love of the Self'
description: Yājñavalkya teaches Maitreyī that the husband, wife, wealth and worlds are dear not for their own sake but for love of the Self (ātman), which alone is to be seen, heard, reflected on and meditated upon; illustrated by the lump-of-salt simile

title: Triśaṅku cursed to become a cāṇḍāla
description: King Triśaṅku, wishing to ascend bodily to heaven, is refused by Vasiṣṭha and cursed to outcaste form by Vasiṣṭha's insulted sons

title: Twenty-one-fold extermination of the kṣatriyas
description: Paraśurāma vows to rid the earth of kṣatriyas twenty-one times and slaughters the tyrannical warrior kings worldwide

title: Vishvamitra's hundred sons split and the elder fifty cursed
description: Vishvamitra orders his hundred sons to accept Devarata as eldest; the fifty younger agree and are blessed, the fifty elder refuse and are cursed to father the border peoples

title: Vishvamitra's request & slaying of Tataka and Subahu
description: Vishvamitra takes Rama and Lakshmana to guard his sacrifice; Rama kills the rakshasi Tataka, gets celestial astras, hurls Marica and slays Subahu

title: Viśvāmitra confers the divine astras
description: Pleased by the slaying, Viśvāmitra bestows on Rāma the full arsenal of celestial weapons and their recall mantras, initiating him into divine weapon-craft

title: Viśvāmitra takes Rāma to guard his sacrifice
description: The sage Viśvāmitra arrives at Ayodhyā and demands the boy Rāma to protect his sacrifice from rākṣasas; Daśaratha relents on Vasiṣṭha's counsel

title: Viśvāmitra wins the title Brahmarṣi
description: Having conquered his wrath, Viśvāmitra is humbly acknowledged by Vasiṣṭha as a brahmarṣi, the sole kṣatriya to earn the rank

title: Vālī humiliates Rāvaṇa
description: The vānara king Vālī tucks Rāvaṇa under his arm during his sandhyā worship, humbling the rākṣasa emperor

title: Bharata's Gandharva conquest and city-foundings
description: At Yudhājit's prompting Bharata wars on the Gandharvas of Gāndhāra and founds Takṣaśilā for his son Takṣa and Puṣkalāvatī for Puṣkala

title: Bharata's Regency with Rama's Sandals
description: Refusing the throne, Bharata installs Rama's sandals as regent and rules as caretaker until Rama's return

title: Bharata's repudiation of Kaikeyī
description: Bharata denounces his mother, refuses the throne, and installs Rāma's sandals as sovereign at Nandigrāma

title: Birth of Vasiṣṭha and Agastya from Urvaśī's catalyst
description: At the sight of Urvaśī the seed of Mitra-Varuṇa spills into a pot, producing the sages Vasiṣṭha and Agastya — a cross-myth with Urvaśī as catalyst

title: Daśaratha recalls the Śravaṇa-kumāra curse
description: The dying king recalls killing the boy Śravaṇa by sound while hunting, and the boy's blind parents' curse that he too would die of grief for a son

title: Daśaratha's confession of the Śravaṇa curse
description: The dying king tells Kausalyā how he killed the ascetic boy Śravaṇa and was cursed to die of grief for a son

title: Death of Rohitāśva and the test at the pyre
description: The boy Rohitāśva dies of snakebite, and at the cremation ground Hariścandra, bound by duty to his master, demands the cremation fee even from his unrecognized grieving wife — the supreme test of his truth

title: Defeat of her sons at Siddhāśrama
description: At Viśvāmitra's sacrifice Rāma hurls Mārīca into the sea with the Mānava astra and kills Subāhu with the Āgneya astra, completing the confrontation with Tāṭakā's line

title: Five blood-lakes at Samanta-pañcaka
description: At Samanta-pañcaka (Kurukṣetra) Paraśurāma fills five pools with kṣatriya blood and offers tarpaṇa to his ancestors, who bid him relent

title: Gaṇeśa's trick and the rooting at Gokarṇa
description: The devas send Gaṇeśa as a cowherd-boy and Viṣṇu fakes dusk; the boy sets the liṅga down, rooting it at Gokarṇa as Mahābaleśvara, with the scattered-wrappings coastal liṅga-chain as a variant

title: Hanuman burns Lanka
description: After uprooting the Ashoka grove, slaying Aksha, and being captured by Indrajit's Brahmastra, Hanuman has his tail set ablaze and uses it to set the golden city aflame

title: Hanumān's leap to Laṅkā
description: Reminded of his powers by Jāmbavān, Hanumān leaps the sea to Laṅkā, carrying the epic into the Sundara-kāṇḍa

title: Indrajit beheads the illusory Māyā-Sītā
description: To demoralize the army Indrajit conjures an illusory Sītā and beheads her before Hanumān, until Vibhīṣaṇa reveals it was sorcery

title: Indra steals Ambarisha's sacrificial victim (Ramayana variant)
description: In the epic retelling, Indra carries off King Ambarisha's consecrated victim and the priest demands a human substitute be procured

title: Kuśika line gains the sage-seed
description: The queen-mother bears Viśvāmitra, a kṣatriya by birth driven by brāhmaṇa-tejas to win brahmarṣi rank, completing the mirror cross-over of the two clans
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva 116–117; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa

title: Lakṣmaṇa felled and revived by the Sañjīvanī herb
description: Indrajit's weapon leaves Lakṣmaṇa mortally wounded; Hanumān carries the entire Droṇagiri mountain so the physician Suṣeṇa can revive him with the Sañjīvanī herb

title: Launch of the four-direction search and Sampāti's revelation
description: Sugrīva dispatches vānara parties to the four quarters to find Sītā; the southern party under Aṅgada, Hanumān and Jāmbavān learns from the dying vulture Sampāti that Sītā is held in Laṅkā

title: Mārīca becomes the golden deer
description: Coerced by Rāvaṇa, Mārīca becomes a dazzling golden deer to lure Rāma away from the hermitage

title: Murder of Jamadagni
description: In Paraśurāma's absence the sons of Kārtavīrya behead the meditating, unresisting Jamadagni and carry off his head; Reṇukā strikes her breast twenty-one times, fixing the number of the vengeance

title: Paraśurāma's Vengeance and the Annihilation of the Kṣatriyas
description: Paraśurāma severs Kārtavīrya's thousand arms and beheads him; after the king's sons murder Jamadagni, he vows to rid the earth of kṣatriyas and exterminates the warrior race twenty-one times

title: Rāma allies with Sugrīva and kills Vālī
description: Rāma allies with the monkey-king Sugrīva, slays his usurping brother Vālī from concealment, and gains the vānara army; Hanumān becomes chief agent

title: Rāma's Pañcavaṭī exile on the Godāvarī
description: Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa settle at Pañcavaṭī (Nāsik) on the Godāvarī, the stage of the Śūrpaṇakhā mutilation, golden-deer ruse and Sītā's abduction

title: Sampāti reveals Sītā's location
description: Hearing of his brother Jaṭāyu's heroic death, the aged vulture Sampāti uses his far-sight to descry Sītā captive in Rāvaṇa's Aśoka grove in Laṅkā, and his wings regrow as a dharmic reward

title: Sarasvatī confounds Mantharā's tongue (deva-instrument variant)
description: In Tulsīdās and devotional traditions the gods prompt Sarasvatī to turn Mantharā's intellect so the exile—needed for Rāvaṇa's death—is set in motion

title: Shurpanakha mutilated and Sita abducted (Ramopakhyana)
description: In the Dandaka forest Shurpanakha is mutilated, Khara and Dushana's host destroyed, Marica's golden-deer ruse draws Rama away, Ravana abducts Sita, and Jatayu falls defending her

title: Sītā gives Hanumān the cūḍāmaṇi and secret sign
description: Declining to be carried back, Sītā gives Hanumān her crest-jewel and recalls the Kākāsura crow-demon episode as a private sign only Rāma would know

title: Sītā-haraṇa (abduction by Rāvaṇa)
description: Rāvaṇa, disguised as a sannyāsin, seizes the undefended Sītā and carries her off in the puṣpaka — the pivot of the epic, seated at Pañcavaṭī

title: Sītā's agni-parīkṣā
description: After Rāvaṇa's fall Rāma voices public doubt; Sītā enters a pyre to prove her purity, and Agni rises bodily to return her unharmed

title: Sītā's second public oath and return to the Earth
description: Asked to swear her purity once more, Sītā calls on her mother the Earth, who rises on a nāga-borne throne and receives her forever, her unanswerable verdict

title: The divine payasa and birth of the four princes
description: The Yajna-purusha rises from the fire bearing payasa, which divided among the queens produces Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, Vishnu's incarnation to slay Ravana

title: The miraculous feast for Bharata's army
description: When Bharata halts with the army of Ayodhya, Bharadvaja conjures by tapas a divine feast, palace and entertainers to host the entire host

title: The preserved body, Bharata's repudiation, and the funeral
description: With heirs absent the king's body is preserved until Bharata returns, performs the rites, denounces Kaikeyī, and rules as regent for Rāma's sandals

title: Śukra blinded blocking Vāmana's water-pot
description: When Bali insists on granting Vāmana three paces, Śukra shrinks into the water-pot spout to void the vow, and Vāmana's grass blade pierces and blinds his eye, sealing the gift

title: Vedavatī's curse on Rāvaṇa
description: Accosted by Rāvaṇa, the ascetic Vedavatī cuts off her defiled hair, enters the fire, and curses that she will be reborn (as Sītā) to destroy him

title: Vision of Śiva's cosmic form (viśvarūpa)
description: Śiva grants Rāma divine sight and reveals his all-pervading cosmic form containing all worlds — the Śaiva answer to Bhagavad Gītā ch. 11

title: Viśvāmitra as guru of Rāma
description: The now-serene brahmarṣi takes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to guard his sacrifice, gifts them divine astras, and leads them to Sītā's svayaṃvara

title: Viśvāmitra creates a counter-heaven for Triśaṅku
description: Viśvāmitra raises Triśaṅku bodily skyward; rejected by Indra, the enraged sage begins a parallel universe of new stars until the gods fix Triśaṅku head-down as a constellation

title: Agastya Equips Rama in Dandaka
description: At his southern ashram Agastya gifts Rama the bow of Vishnu, an inexhaustible quiver, a divine arrow and sword, and directs the exiles to Panchavati

title: Agastya teaches Rāma the Aditya Hṛdayam
description: On the battlefield before the final duel with Rāvaṇa, sage Agastya teaches the fatigued Rāma the 31-verse solar hymn Aditya Hṛdayam, whose chanting restores him to victory

title: Ambarisha buys Sunahshepa from Richika (Ramayana variant)
description: Ambarisha buys the middle son Sunahshepa from the sage Richika for a hundred thousand cows to serve as the human victim

title: Bestowal of the Pāśupata weapon and boon
description: Śiva confers the Pāśupata-astra on Rāma, assures him he will slay Rāvaṇa and recover Sītā, and departs

title: Bharata curses Urvaśī (Vikramorvaśīya)
description: In Kālidāsa's play, Urvaśī blurts 'Purūravas' instead of 'Puruṣottama' during a celestial drama and the sage Bharata curses her to fall to earth

title: Birth of Hanumān on Añjanādri (claimed)
description: Regional and Vijayanagara-era tradition claims the Tuṅgabhadrā hill Añjanādri as the birthplace of Hanumān, son of Añjanā and Vāyu — one of several rival janma-sthāna claims

title: Birth of Kumbhakarṇa
description: Second-born of the sage Viśravas and the daitya princess Kaikasī, the pot-eared Kumbhakarṇa is born so enormous he devours living creatures by the thousands as an infant

title: Birth of Meghanāda (Indrajit)
description: Born in Laṅkā to Rāvaṇa and Mandodarī as crown prince, named Meghanāda because his infant cry boomed like a thundercloud

title: Birth of Rama and his brothers (Putra-kameshti yajna)
description: Childless King Dasharatha of Ayodhya performs a son-granting sacrifice whose sacred porridge yields four sons — Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna

title: Death of Daśaratha
description: Calling for Rāma, Daśaratha dies of grief at midnight, the Śravaṇa-kumāra curse fulfilled; his body is preserved in oil to await Bharata

title: Earth-gift to Kaśyapa and retirement to Mahendra
description: Paraśurāma performs an Aśvamedha, gifts the whole earth to Kaśyapa as dakṣiṇā, and withdraws to Mahendra mountain

title: Hanuman fetches the Sanjivani mountain
description: When Lakshmana is felled in battle, Hanuman flies to the Himalayas and, unable to identify the herb, carries the entire Dronagiri mountain back to Lanka

title: Hanumān's leap to Laṅkā and burning of the city
description: Hanumān leaps the ocean, finds Sītā in the Aśoka grove, delivers Rāma's ring, burns Laṅkā with his tail, and returns with news

title: Hanumān wrecks the Aśoka grove and slays the guards
description: To provoke the enemy, Hanumān lays waste the Aśoka grove and kills waves of guards including the 80,000 kiṅkaras, Jambumālī, and five generals

title: Jaṭāyu's fall
description: Jaṭāyu attacks Rāvaṇa in mid-air and is felled when his wings are cut, surviving only to reveal Sītā's flight-direction to Rāma
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 50–51, 67–68; Sarvatīrtha/Ṭākeḍ regional tradition

title: Jāmbavān awakens Hanumān for the leap
description: The bear-king Jāmbavān reminds Hanumān of his forgotten divine origin and might; roused, Hanumān swells to colossal size on Mount Mahendra to spring across the sea

title: Kaikeyī's remorse and the Citrakūṭa reconciliation
description: Stricken with shame, Kaikeyī joins Bharata's procession to Citrakūṭa to beg Rāma's return; Rāma forgives her

title: Lakṣmaṇa slays Indrajit at Nikumbhilā
description: Guided by Vibhīṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa disrupts Indrajit's invincibility-granting fire-sacrifice at Nikumbhilā and beheads him with the Aindrāstra

title: Nalakūbara's curse for the rape of Rambhā
description: After Rāvaṇa rapes the apsarā Rambhā, Nalakūbara curses that his head will shatter into seven pieces if he ever again forces an unwilling woman — why he cannot touch Sītā

title: Rama allies with Sugriva and slays Valin (Ramopakhyana)
description: Rama allies with the exiled vanara Sugriva, slays Valin, and gains the monkey army

title: Rama's return halt at the ashram
description: Flying home in the Pushpaka vimana after the war, Rama alights again at Bharadvaja's ashram, where the sage grants out-of-season fruiting along his path and confirms Ayodhya's welfare

title: Rāma slays Śambūka
description: Told a śūdra's out-of-order penance caused a brāhmaṇa boy's premature death, Rāma beheads the ascetic Śambūka and the boy revives, the cycle's most contested act

title: Rāma slays Mārīca and the false cry
description: Rāma pierces the deer; dying, Mārīca resumes demon form and cries out in Rāma's voice, drawing Lakṣmaṇa away from Sītā

title: Rāma slays Tāḍakā
description: At Viśvāmitra's command Rāma kills the yakṣiṇī-turned-rākṣasī Tāḍakā ravaging the forest — his first kill and a famous dharmic crux of slaying a female

title: Rāma's Penance for Brahmahatyā at Rishikesh
description: Folk tradition has Rāma perform penance at Rishikesh to expiate the brahmahatyā of slaying Rāvaṇa, with Lakṣmaṇa crossing the Gaṅgā on a jute-rope bridge (the Lakṣmaṇ Jhūlā legend)

title: Śūrpaṇakhā's mutilation
description: At Pañcavaṭī the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā lusts after Rāma and lunges at Sītā; Lakṣmaṇa cuts off her nose and ears, igniting the war

title: Sampāti shields Jaṭāyu and loses his wings
description: The young vulture brothers fly toward the sun; when Jaṭāyu's wings begin to scorch, Sampāti spreads his own wings as a shield, his wings are burnt away, and he falls to the Vindhyas

title: Shukra blinded at the Vamana episode
description: Shukra hides in the spout of Bali's water-pot to block the donation pour, and Vamana pierces it with a blade of grass, putting out Shukra's eye and making him one-eyed

title: Shurpanakha and the Golden Deer; Abduction of Sita
description: In the Dandaka forest the episode of Shurpanakha and the golden deer Marica leads to Ravana's abduction of Sita

title: Sita svayamvara & breaking of Shiva's bow
description: At Mithila Rama lifts and breaks Shiva's bow Pinaka to win Janaka's earth-born daughter Sita; the four brothers marry

title: Slaying of Indrajit at the Nikumbhilā rite
description: Vibhīṣaṇa reveals the secret Nikumbhilā yajña that would make Indrajit invulnerable; Lakṣmaṇa disrupts it and beheads Indrajit in the ensuing duel

title: Sons of the brothers and the dynasty's passing
description: Śatrughna and Śrutakīrti's sons (Subāhu and Śatrughātī/Śūrasena) are set over Mathurā and an adjacent realm as the brothers share in the dynasty's final departure from the world

title: Sītā becomes Mahākālī and slays Sahasra-Rāvaṇa
description: In the Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa the thousand-headed Sahasra-Rāvaṇa fells Rāma, so Sītā assumes the form of Mahākālī and severs his thousand heads, revealing her supreme Śakti

title: The gods restore Hariścandra and revive his son
description: At the instant of his unbroken truth the devas led by Indra, Yama/Dharma, and Viśvāmitra descend, declare the ordeal passed, revive Rohitāśva, restore the family and kingdom, and Hariścandra wins heaven while sharing it with his subjects

title: The vow and twenty-one-fold extermination of the kṣatriyas
description: Paraśurāma vows to rid the earth of kṣatriyas twenty-one times and circuits the world slaughtering tyrannical warrior kings and their lines

title: Vamana subdues the three worlds (Bali story)
description: Vishnu's manvantara-avatara Vamana subdues the three worlds and returns them to Indra Purandara, pushing the demon-king Bali to the netherworld

title: Viśvāmitra confers the divine astras on Rāma
description: Pleased, Viśvāmitra gives Rāma the entire array of celestial weapons and recall-mantras, which appear as embodied beings pledging service

title: Viśvāmitra eats dog-flesh in the twelve-year famine
description: In a drought at the Tretā–Dvāpara junction the starving sage Viśvāmitra steals dog-meat from a Caṇḍāla, eats to preserve his life and the Veda he carries, then makes rain by penance and is purified, establishing that life-preservation can override caste and dietary law

title: Vāmana subdues Bali
description: Viṣṇu as the dwarf Vāmana subdues the asura king Bali — the Treta-Yuga avatāra framing the Vāmana Purāṇa

title: Widowhood and the fourteen-year wait
description: Daśaratha dies of grief; Kausalyā endures as widowed queen-mother in Ayodhyā under Bharata's regency

title: Abduction of Sītā and slaying of Jaṭāyu
description: Inflamed by Śūrpaṇakhā, Rāvaṇa uses Mārīca's golden-deer ruse to draw Rāma away, abducts Sītā in the Puṣpaka, and slays Jaṭāyu who tries to stop him

title: Agastya Teaches Rama the Aditya-Hridaya
description: On the eve of the final duel with Ravana, Agastya appears on the battlefield and teaches the war-weary Rama the Aditya-Hridayam hymn, by whose power Rama slays Ravana

title: Anasūyā counsels and gifts Sītā
description: At Atri's hermitage Anasūyā instructs Sītā in pātivratya-dharma and gifts her celestial unfading garments, ornaments, and cosmetics

title: Battle of Janasthāna
description: Roused by Śūrpaṇakhā, Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras attack with fourteen thousand rākṣasas; Rāma alone destroys the host

title: Bharata denounces Kaikeyī and refuses the throne
description: Recalled to Ayodhyā, Bharata learns of his father's death and his mother's plot, condemns Kaikeyī, refuses the kingdom, and performs the funeral rites

title: Building of the bridge to Laṅkā
description: The vānaras build the Setu (Rāma Setu) bridge across the ocean to invade Laṅkā

title: Hanuman slays Ahiravana in Patala
description: When Ahiravana abducts the sleeping Rama and Lakshmana to Patala, Hanuman assumes his five-faced Panchamukha form to extinguish the demon's five life-lamps at once and slays him

title: Hanuman's leap to Lanka and Avindhya's protection of Sita
description: Hanuman crosses the ocean, finds Sita in the Ashoka grove and comforts her, while the sympathetic old rakshasa minister Avindhya counsels restraint and protects Sita's morale

title: Hanumān kills Akṣa-kumāra
description: Rāvaṇa's young son Akṣa attacks valiantly; Hanumān, admiring his courage, seizes him by the feet and dashes him to death

title: Kumbhakarṇa's penance and the mis-spoken boon
description: During Kumbhakarṇa's extreme penance, Sarasvatī ties his tongue at Indra's request so he asks for sleep instead of sovereignty/destruction of the gods, and Brahmā grants perpetual slumber

title: Lakṣmaṇa declines the crown-prince office
description: After the return to Ayodhyā and Rāma's coronation, Lakṣmaṇa declines the Yuvarāja position in deference to Bharata

title: Lakṣmaṇa struck by the Vāsavī Śakti and healed
description: Rāvaṇa hurls Indra's infallible javelin at Lakṣmaṇa, who falls mortally wounded; Hanumān again brings the whole Droṇagiri and Suṣeṇa's Sañjīvanī heals him before dawn

title: Meghanāda conquers and binds Indra
description: Meghanāda overpowers the devas in war on Svarga, binds Indra and carries him captive to Laṅkā; Brahmā ransoms Indra and the gods hail him 'Indrajit.'

title: Parashurama confrontation & transfer of power
description: Parashurama challenges Rama over the broken bow; Rama strings the Vishnu-bow, draining his power, and the 6th avatara cedes to the 7th

title: Raghu's Digvijaya and the Vishvajit Sacrifice
description: Raghu conquers the world and gives away all his wealth after the Vishvajit sacrifice, becoming so illustrious the line is renamed Raghuvamsha

title: Rama slays Tataka and guards Vishvamitra's sacrifice
description: Sage Vishvamitra takes Rama and Lakshmana to guard his sacrifice; Rama kills the rakshasi Tataka, receives celestial weapons, routs Marica and slays Subahu

title: Ravana's Tapas and Shiva Heals His Heads at Vaidyanath
description: Ravana offers his ten heads one by one into fire to win Shiva's favor and the Atma-linga, and Shiva appears as the divine physician to reattach his heads, founding the Vaidyanath jyotirlinga where the linga was tricked into being set down

title: Reclaiming the western coast
description: Forbidden to dwell on the gifted earth, Paraśurāma hurls his axe into the sea; Varuṇa recedes and the Konkan/Kerala coast (Paraśurāma-kṣetra) emerges as his abode
source: Padma, Skanda, Brahmāṇḍa Puranas; Keralolpatti; Konkan/Tuluva legends (regional)

title: Rāma flings Mārīca into the sea
description: Defending Viśvāmitra's sacrifice, Rāma hurls Mārīca 800 miles into the sea with the Mānavāstra and spares his life

title: Rāma hurls Mārīca and slays Subāhu
description: Defending Viśvāmitra's sacrifice, Rāma flings Mārīca into the ocean with the Mānava astra and kills Subāhu with the Āgneya astra

title: Rāvaṇa abducts Sītā
description: Disguised as a mendicant, Rāvaṇa reveals himself, seizes Sītā, places her in the Puṣpaka chariot, and flies south toward Laṅkā as she screams

title: Sacrifice of Lakṣmaṇa
description: To honour his word after Lakṣmaṇa breaks Kāla's sealed audience to spare the realm from Durvāsā's curse, Rāma abandons him; Lakṣmaṇa enters the Sarayū as Śeṣa/Ananta

title: Savitri Wins Satyavan Back from Yama
description: When Yama personally takes the soul of Satyavan, his devoted wife Savitri follows and cleverly extracts boons until Yama, bound by his own word, must restore Satyavan to life

title: Sītā's banishment to Vālmīki's hermitage
description: A washerman's slander prompts Rāma to send the pregnant Sītā away; Lakṣmaṇa leaves her near Vālmīki's āśrama, who shelters her

title: The five blood-lakes at Samanta-pañcaka
description: Paraśurāma fills five pools at Samanta-pañcaka (Kurukṣetra) with the blood of the slain and offers tarpaṇa; the pacified Bhṛgu ancestors appear and bid him relent

title: Urvaśī transformed into a vine in Kumāra's grove
description: In Kālidāsa's play a jealous Urvaśī strays into Kārtikeya's forbidden grove and is turned into a creeper, later restored by the union-gem

title: Vishnu Measures the Worlds as Trivikrama (Sirkazhi)
description: At Kazhicheerama Vinnagaram and other Trivikrama sthalas, Vishnu as Vamana/Trivikrama measures the three worlds with raised foot

title: Vishvamitra teaches Sunahshepa hymns and Indra spares him (Ramayana variant)
description: At Pushkara Vishvamitra teaches his nephew Sunahshepa secret mantras to Indra and Vishnu; reciting them, the boy is granted long life and spared, while Vishvamitra curses his own refusing sons

title: Viśvāmitra curses Rambhā to stone
description: Detecting Indra's next seductress, Viśvāmitra curses Rambhā to become stone, but the angry curse burns up his tapas, his moral turning point toward conquering wrath

title: Agastya teaches Rāma the Āditya-Hṛdayam
description: As Rāma flags in the final duel, the sage Agastya appears and teaches him the Āditya-Hṛdayam hymn to Sūrya, renewing his vigor

title: Ahalya cursed to stone and freed by Rama
description: The sage Gautama curses his wife Ahalya to stone, and she is later freed by the touch of Rama

title: Aja and the Death of Indumati
description: Raghu's son Aja wins Indumati at her svayamvara; her death from a falling celestial garland plunges Aja into grief

title: Bharata marches to Chitrakūṭa to recall Rāma
description: Bharata leads an army and the queens to Chitrakūṭa to bring Rāma back; the brothers reunite and Rāma performs water-offerings for their father

title: Brahmā's boon of the fire-sacrifice chariot
description: Refused immortality, Meghanāda is granted that whenever he completes a fire-sacrifice before battle a celestial chariot rises from the fire, and while fighting from it he cannot be slain

title: Breaking Śiva's bow and the Rāmāyaṇa encounter
description: Paraśurāma confronts Rāma Dāśarathi after the breaking of Śiva's bow, challenges him to draw Viṣṇu's Śārṅga, and yields his tejas to the younger avatāra

title: Death of Jaṭāyu
description: Jaṭāyu challenges Rāvaṇa in mid-air, wounds him and wrecks his chariot, but Rāvaṇa severs his wings and the great bird falls dying

title: Hanuman's Leap to Lanka and Burning of Lanka
description: Hanuman leaps across the ocean to Lanka, finds Sita in the Ashoka grove, and burns the city

title: Hariścandra's truth-test (wager of the sages)
description: In a wager over Hariścandra's truthfulness Viśvāmitra strips him of kingdom and forces him to sell wife, son and himself to a cāṇḍāla before his truth is vindicated and all restored

title: Indrajit captures Hanumān with the Brahmāstra
description: Rāvaṇa's eldest son Indrajit binds Hanumān with the Brahmāstra; Hanumān submits in reverence and feigns captivity to enter Rāvaṇa's court

title: Kaikeyi's two boons & the exile decree
description: Manthara poisons Kaikeyi's mind; she invokes two old boons demanding Bharata's crown and Rama's 14-year exile

title: Lakṣmaṇa escorts the banished Sītā to the forest
description: Charged by Rāma after the public slander, Lakṣmaṇa in anguish escorts the pregnant Sītā to Vālmīki's hermitage

title: Liberation of Ahalya
description: Rama's presence restores Ahalya, wife of Gautama cursed to stone for Indra's deception, to human form

title: Mārīca's deer and Sītā's abduction
description: Rāvaṇa uses Mārīca as a golden deer to lure Rāma away, then seizes Sītā and bears her toward Laṅkā; Jaṭāyu falls fighting him

title: Rama installs the Ramanatha jyotirlinga at Setu
description: Rama builds the Rama-Setu bridge and installs the Ramanatha jyotirlinga at Rameshvaram, the founding legend of the Setu pilgrimage

title: Rāma enthrones Kuśa and Lava
description: Rāma installs Kuśa at Kuśāvatī (continuing the Ikṣvāku line) and Lava at Śrāvastī, settling his brothers' sons over many realms

title: Rāma slays Rāvaṇa with the Brahmāstra
description: After Rāvaṇa's heads regrow, Agastya teaches Rāma the Āditya-hṛdaya and Rāma looses the Brahmāstra into Rāvaṇa's navel/chest where the regenerating nectar was stored, killing him

title: Rāma slays Subāhu
description: Subāhu, who with Mārīca rains flesh and blood on Viśvāmitra's yajña, is killed by Rāma's Āgneyāstra

title: Rāvaṇa softens the sleep-curse
description: Dismayed his mighty brother would be useless asleep, Rāvaṇa pleads and the curse is commuted to a cycle of six months' sleep and a day's waking during which he can be roused for war

title: Sita blesses Hanuman with immortality
description: Sita blesses Hanuman to live as long as Rama's story is told on earth, making him a Chiranjivi who remains through the Kali Yuga

title: The bridge to Lanka and Vibhishana's defection (Ramopakhyana)
description: The vanaras build the causeway and cross, and Ravana's righteous brother Vibhishana defects to Rama, receiving his sovereignty from Kubera

title: The earth-gift to Kaśyapa and retirement to Mahendra
description: Paraśurāma performs an Aśvamedha, gifts the whole earth to Kaśyapa as dakṣiṇā, is bidden to quit the land, and withdraws to Mahendra mountain as a deathless ascetic

title: Birth of Makaradhvaja at Bet Dvaraka
description: Hanuman's son Makaradhvaja is born of Hanuman's sweat swallowed by a fish, enshrined at the Hanuman Dandi temple on Bet Dvaraka

title: Bridge to Lanka and the Great War
description: Rama's army builds the bridge to Lanka and wages the great war culminating in the slaying of Ravana

title: Dasharatha Kills Shravana and Is Cursed
description: Dasharatha accidentally kills Shravana Kumara and is cursed to die from grief at separation from his own son

title: Fall of the rakshasa champions and slaying of Ravana (Ramopakhyana)
description: The siege brings the fall of Kumbhakarna, Indrajit, and the rakshasa champions, and Rama kills Ravana in single combat, fulfilling the man-and-monkey loophole

title: Hanumān burns Laṅkā
description: His tail set alight on Vibhīṣaṇa's plea against killing an envoy, Hanumān leaps roof to roof torching the golden city, then quenches the flame in the sea

title: Hariścandra's vow and the Śunaḥśepa sacrifice
description: Childless Hariścandra vows his first-born to Varuṇa; the purchased victim Śunaḥśepa is freed by Ṛgvedic hymns at the stake and adopted by Viśvāmitra as Devarāta

title: Jābāli's heterodox argument rejected
description: The minister-sage Jābāli advances a near-materialist argument that the dead father is gone and vows are empty, urging Rāma to take the throne; Rāma vehemently rejects it

title: Kuvalashva slays the demon Dhundhu
description: At Uttanka's tapas Vishnu foretells and the Ikshvaku king Kuvalashva and his sons slay the sand-buried fire-breathing asura Dhundhu, earning the king the title Dhundhumara

title: Lakṣmaṇa's self-sacrifice and end in the Sarayū
description: Guarding Rāma's private audience with Kāla, Lakṣmaṇa interrupts it to admit the threatening Durvāsas, accepts the death-sentence as banishment, and gives up his body in the Sarayū — precipitating Rāma's own departure

title: Mārīca becomes the golden deer; slain by Rāma
description: Coerced by Rāvaṇa, Mārīca becomes the golden deer that lures Rāma away so Sītā can be abducted; slain by Rāma's arrow, he dies mimicking Rāma's voice

title: Rama Installs the Rameshwaram Linga
description: To expiate the brahma-hatya of killing Ravana, Rama installs and worships a Shiva linga at Setubandha; with Hanuman delayed fetching one from Kailasa, Sita fashions a linga from sand, founding the Rameshwaram jyotirlinga

title: Rama's forest departure & death of Dasaratha
description: Rama accepts exile with Sita and Lakshmana; Dasaratha dies of grief, fulfilling the Shravana-kumara curse

title: Rāma finds the dying Jaṭāyu and performs his rites
description: Returning to an empty hermitage, the grieving Rāma finds Jaṭāyu, who names Rāvaṇa as abductor and expires; Rāma performs his funeral rites and the bird attains the higher worlds

title: Rāma slays Rāvaṇa
description: With Indra's chariot and Mātali's aid, Rāma looses the Brahmāstra into Rāvaṇa's amṛta-filled navel, drying the nectar and finally killing him; Rāvaṇa is given honorable cremation

title: Rāma's Mahāprasthāna (jala-samādhi)
description: Rāma walks into the Sarayū, resumes his form as Viṣṇu and ascends to Vaikuṇṭha with all who followed, closing the avatāra in collective liberation

title: Rāvaṇa's cremation and Vibhīṣaṇa's coronation
description: Rāma honors the fallen Rāvaṇa with full cremation rites, declaring enmity ends with death, and crowns Vibhīṣaṇa king of Laṅkā

title: Sita svayamvara and breaking of Shiva's bow
description: At Mithila Rama lifts and breaks Shiva's bow Pinaka to win Sita, daughter of Janaka, and marries her, while his brothers marry Janaka's and Kushadhvaja's daughters

title: Slaying of Rāvaṇa and the war's end
description: In the great battle Kumbhakarṇa and Indrajit fall and Rāma finally kills Rāvaṇa, ending the war

title: Sītā's return to the Earth
description: Summoned to swear her chastity again, Sītā instead calls on her mother the Earth, who opens, rises on a golden throne, and draws her down — her final vindication

title: Aditi's Penance for the Birth of Vāmana (Kurukṣetra)
description: The Vāmana Purāṇa's Kurukṣetra-māhātmya ties the field to Aditi's penance that brings about the birth of the Vāmana avatāra

title: Bharata's refusal & the sandals (paduka)
description: Bharata refuses the throne, takes Rama's sandals as tokens of sovereignty, and rules as regent from Nandigrama

title: Hanumān granted deathlessness
description: In the Vaiṣṇava telling, at Rāma's departure Hanumān is granted cirañjīvitva to remain on earth as long as the Rāma-kathā is told

title: Hanumān returns and reports to Rāma
description: Hanumān leaps back, announces 'I have seen Sītā,' the vānaras raid the Madhuvana in joy, and he presents the cūḍāmaṇi to a weeping Rāma, who resolves on the march to Laṅkā

title: Parashurama confronts Rama
description: On the journey home Parashurama challenges Rama over the broken bow; Rama effortlessly strings Parashurama's Vishnu-bow, draining his power as the 6th avatar cedes to the 7th

title: Rama, 7th Avatara of Vishnu
description: Rama's exile, the abduction of Sita by Ravana, alliance with Sugriva and Hanuman, war at Lanka, and the establishment of Ramarajya mark the apex of the Solar dynasty

title: Rama's return/coronation (Gudi Padwa charter)
description: An alternate Gudi Padwa charter commemorates Rama's return and coronation, the raised Gudi serving as a banner of triumph

title: Reunion and Rama's coronation (Ramopakhyana ending)
description: Sita is restored, the party returns to Ayodhya, and Rama is crowned king in a righteous reign, the tale ending at the coronation with no Uttara-Kanda banishment

title: Rāma annihilates Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras and 14,000 rākṣasas
description: After Śūrpaṇakhā's mutilation, Khara leads 14,000 rākṣasas with Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras against Rāma, who annihilates the whole host single-handedly

title: Rāma gives his sandals to Bharata
description: Defeated in argument, Bharata takes Rāma's gold-adorned wooden sandals as tokens of sovereignty, vowing to rule only as their deputy and enter fire if Rāma does not return on time

title: Rāvaṇa composes the Śiva Tāṇḍava Stotra
description: The supreme Śiva-devotee Rāvaṇa composes the thunderous Śiva Tāṇḍava Stotra, traditionally sung while pinned beneath Kailāsa

title: Sita's Agni-pariksha and Rama's Coronation
description: After the war Sita undergoes the fire-ordeal (agni-pariksha) and Rama is crowned at his pattabhisheka

title: Slaying of Kabandha
description: The brothers sever the arms of the monster Kabandha and cremate him; from the pyre rises a gandharva who counsels Rāma to ally with Sugrīva

title: Sītā's fire-ordeal and Rāma's coronation
description: Sītā undergoes the agni-parīkṣā fire-ordeal; Rāma returns to Ayodhyā and is crowned, inaugurating Rāma-rājya

title: Viśvāmitra's sons split over Devarāta
description: Ordered to accept Devarāta as senior, Viśvāmitra's fifty elder sons refuse and are cursed to become border tribal peoples; the younger fifty obey

title: Śabarī's devotion and ascent
description: The aged tribal devotee Śabarī offers Rāma fruit, is blessed by his darśana, enters the fire and ascends, directing him to Lake Pampā and Sugrīva

title: Akampana flees to incite Rāvaṇa
description: The Janasthāna survivor Akampana flees to Laṅkā to inform Rāvaṇa and incite the abduction of Sītā

title: Banishment of Sītā
description: Stung by a washerman's slander about a wife who dwelt in another's house, Rāma orders the pregnant Sītā conveyed to the forest and abandoned near Vālmīki's hermitage

title: Banishment of Sītā and birth of Lava and Kuśa
description: Rāma banishes the pregnant Sītā over a washerman's gossip; in Vālmīki's hermitage she bears Lava and Kuśa, who later challenge Rāma's Aśvamedha horse

title: Bharata's regency from Nandigrāma
description: Bharata enthrones the sandals and governs as an ascetic from Nandigrāma, sharing Rāma's exile in spirit

title: Kaikeyi's boons and the exile decree
description: On the eve of Rama's coronation, the maid Manthara poisons Kaikeyi's mind; Kaikeyi invokes two old boons demanding Bharata be crowned and Rama exiled fourteen years

title: Kusha and Lava Inherit the Kingdom
description: Rama's twin sons Kusha and Lava inherit Kosala and found Shravasti/Lavapura respectively

title: Rāvaṇa loses the Ātma-liṅga at Gokarṇa
description: Śiva grants Rāvaṇa the Ātma-liṅga to carry to Laṅkā if never set down, but the boy Gaṇeśa tricks him into setting it at Gokarṇa, where it roots as Mahābaleśvara

title: Shiva descends as Hanuman (11th Rudra)
description: In Shaiva tradition, when Vishnu was to descend as Rama, Shiva took birth as Hanuman, the 11th Rudra, to serve him on earth

title: Sita's Banishment and Birth of Lava and Kusha
description: In the Uttara Kanda Sita is banished, shelters with Valmiki, and gives birth to the twins Lava and Kusha, who are taught the epic

title: Slaying of Viradha & forest sages
description: In Dandaka Rama buries the man-eating rakshasa Viradha, vows to clear the forest of demons, and meets Agastya and Jatayu

title: Sītā's fire-ordeal (Agni-parīkṣā)
description: After Rāma's harsh disavowal, Sītā enters the fire; Agni rises bearing her unburned and testifies to her chastity, and the gods reveal Rāma's divinity

title: Viśvāmitra hailed Brahmarṣi by Vasiṣṭha
description: Having conquered his anger, Viśvāmitra humbly approaches Vasiṣṭha, who embraces him and publicly confers the title brahmarṣi, the only kṣatriya so to rise

title: Anasūyā honors Sītā
description: At Atri's hermitage the chaste sage-wife Anasūyā instructs Sītā in wifely dharma and gifts her divine unfading garments and ornaments

title: Birth of Lava and Kuśa
description: In Vālmīki's hermitage Sītā bears twin sons, Kuśa and Lava, whom the sage names and trains to chant the 24,000-verse Rāmāyaṇa, ignorant it is their father's tale

title: Rama's forest departure and Dasharatha's death
description: Rama accepts exile and Sita and Lakshmana accompany him to the forest; Dasharatha dies of grief, recalling the curse of Shravana-kumara's blind parents

title: Sita's Return to the Earth and Rama's Departure
description: Sita returns into the earth and Rama departs the world, closing the Uttara Kanda

title: Sītā swallowed by the Earth; Rāma departs into the Sarayū
description: Sītā is taken back by the Earth, her mother, and Rāma ends his earthly life by entering the Sarayū river, returning to Vaikuṇṭha

title: Surpanakha mutilated
description: Rama's spurned suitor Surpanakha attacks Sita; Lakshmana cuts off her nose and ears, sparking the war

title: The fallen vānaras restored to life
description: The gods grant a boon by which the dead vānaras and ṛkṣas are restored to life

title: Viradha buried alive; redemption
description: The giant Viradha seizes Sītā; unkillable by weapon, he is buried alive by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and his death releases him back to heaven as the cursed gandharva Tumburu

title: Adbhuta-variant: Sītā as Mahākālī slays the thousand-headed Rāvaṇa
description: In the Śākta Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa, when Rāma faints Sītā becomes the active power (Mahākālī) and slays a thousand-headed Rāvaṇa

title: Bharata's refusal and the sandals
description: Bharata returns, refuses the throne, pursues Rama to Chitrakuta, and rules as regent in Rama's name with Rama's sandals on the throne at Nandigrama

title: Kabandha freed and directs Rāma to Sugrīva
description: The headless rākṣasa Kabandha grabs Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; they sever his arms, and cremated he resumes his celestial form and directs Rāma to Sugrīva and Hanumān

title: Khara, Dushana & Trishiras army destroyed
description: Rama single-handedly annihilates Khara, Dushana, Trishiras and the 14,000 rakshasas of Janasthana

title: Renuka beheaded and restored by Parashurama
description: Renuka, chaste wife of sage Jamadagni, is beheaded on his order and restored by her son Parashurama; her severed-and-rejoined head is the etiology of the goddess Yellamma/Mariyamman
source: Mahabharata/Purana Renuka tale; South Indian folk variants

title: Rāma's Aśvamedha and the twins' recital
description: Rāma performs a horse-sacrifice using a golden image of Sītā; at it Lava and Kuśa recite the Rāmāyaṇa, and their resemblance reveals them as his sons

title: Rāma's coronation at Ayodhyā
description: Flying north in the reclaimed Puṣpaka, Rāma reunites with Bharata at Nandigrāma and is consecrated King of Ayodhyā, inaugurating the ideal age of Rāma-rājya

title: Golden deer & abduction of Sita; death of Jatayu
description: Marica as a golden deer lures Rama away; Ravana abducts Sita to Lanka, and Jatayu is mortally wounded trying to stop him

title: Lakṣmaṇa disfigures Ayomukhī
description: The rākṣasī Ayomukhī lusts after Lakṣmaṇa, who disfigures her, paralleling the Śūrpaṇakhā episode

title: Mutilation of Shurpanakha
description: Ravana's sister Shurpanakha lusts after Rama and Lakshmana; spurned and attacking Sita, she has her nose and ears cut off by Lakshmana

title: Sītā returns to the Earth
description: Asked to publicly swear her purity again, Sītā calls on her mother Bhūmi-Devī, who rises on a golden throne and receives her into the ground forever

title: Viśvāmitra guides the young Rāma
description: The serene brahmarṣi takes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to guard his sacrifice, has them slay Tāṭakā and the rākṣasas, gifts divine astras and leads them to Sītā's svayaṃvara

title: Destruction of Khara and Dushana's army
description: Shurpanakha's brothers attack with 14,000 rakshasas; Rama annihilates them, prompting Shurpanakha to incite Ravana

title: Hanumān slays Kālanemi
description: Rāvaṇa's uncle Kālanemi is sent to delay Hanumān fetching the Saṃjīvanī herb by posing as a hermit, and is killed by Hanumān

title: Kabandha slain & Shabari's devotion
description: Rama frees the cursed Kabandha, who directs him to Sugriva; the devotee Shabari offers fruit and ascends, pointing him to Pampa

title: Sita Found in the Furrow by Janaka
description: The philosopher-king Siradhvaja Janaka finds Sita in a plough-furrow and later hosts the bow-svayamvara won by Rama, joining the two Ikshvaku branches

title: The Ramopakhyana retold
description: To console Yudhishthira, Markandeya narrates the whole Ramayana in brief, from Ravana's boon to the slaying of Ravana and recovery of Sita

title: Fire-witnessed alliance with Sugriva
description: Rama and the exiled vanara prince Sugriva swear mutual aid with Agni as witness, brokered by Hanuman

title: Indrajit binds Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with the Nāgapāśa
description: Fighting invisible from the air, Indrajit fires the Nāgapāśa whose serpent-arrows bind both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, dropping them senseless — the lowest point of the war

title: Jaṭāyu challenges Rāvaṇa over Sītā's abduction
description: Roused by Sītā's cries as Rāvaṇa carries her south, the aged Jaṭāyu rebukes him for stealing another's wife and demands he release her or fight

title: Lakṣmaṇa's doom and abandonment
description: To save the realm from Durvāsā's curse, Lakṣmaṇa interrupts Rāma's sealed meeting with Kāla, accepts the death-penalty, enters the Sarayū, and is taken up as Śeṣa

title: Nīla slays Prahasta
description: Prahasta, Rāvaṇa's prime minister and commander-in-chief, is slain by the vānara Nīla in the Laṅkā war

title: Rama slays Ravana (Dussehra/Ramlila)
description: Rama kills the ten-headed Ravana to recover Sita, the climax of the Yuddha Kanda commemorated as Vijayadashami with the burning of Ravana effigies

title: The awakening of Kumbhakarṇa
description: Roused as the ultimate weapon after Rāvaṇa's humiliation, Kumbhakarṇa is woken only by mountains of food, war-drums, maces, and a herd of elephants trampling over his body, then consumes a colossal meal

title: The golden deer and abduction of Sita
description: Marica as a golden deer lures Rama away and Lakshmana off too; Ravana disguised as an ascetic abducts Sita to Lanka, and the vulture Jatayu fights Ravana and is mortally wounded telling Rama the direction

title: Vamana reclaims the three worlds from Bali
description: The Dwarf avatara reclaims the three worlds from the asura-king Bali in three strides (Trivikrama)

title: Alliance with Sugriva and slaying of Vali
description: Rama meets Hanuman and the exiled vanara-prince Sugriva, allies with him, and kills Sugriva's brother Vali from concealment, restoring Sugriva to the throne of Kishkindha

title: Garuḍa frees the princes from the serpent-bonds
description: Garuḍa, enemy of all serpents, descends and at his mere approach the snake-bonds flee, freeing and healing Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa

title: Jaṭāyu's aerial duel and mutilation by Rāvaṇa
description: Jaṭāyu tears at Rāvaṇa's bow, armor and chariot, forcing him to the ground, until Rāvaṇa severs the great bird's wings, feet and sides and flies on with Sītā

title: Kumbhakarṇa counsels Rāvaṇa to return Sītā
description: Roused for the war, the dharma-aware Kumbhakarṇa tells Rāvaṇa that abducting Sītā was adharma and that he should return her, warning that Rāma is no ordinary man, yet vows to fight for his brother

title: Maya-Sita Substitution (Shadow Sita)
description: Foreknowing Ravana's plot, Rama has the true Sita hidden in Agni's fire and an illusory maya-Sita put in her place; only the shadow is abducted, and the true Sita re-emerges from the fire at the agni-pariksha

title: Rāma's Great Departure (Mahāprasthāna)
description: After enthroning Kuśa and Lava, Rāma walks into the Sarayū followed by his kin and people, resumes his form as Viṣṇu, and ascends to Vaikuṇṭha

title: Slaying of Vali
description: Rama kills Sugriva's brother Vali with a concealed arrow, the epic's most-debated act of dharma, restoring Sugriva to the throne

title: Four-quarter search for Sita & Sampati
description: Vanara armies search the four directions; the dying vulture Sampati reveals Sita is captive in Ravana's Ashoka grove in Lanka

title: Indrajit wounds Lakṣmaṇa; the Sañjīvanī herb
description: In a later sally Indrajit gravely wounds Lakṣmaṇa, who is saved when Hanumān flies to the Himālaya and brings back the life-restoring Sañjīvanī herb, lifting the whole mountain

title: Jaṭāyu's dying testimony and Rāma's last rites
description: The dying Jaṭāyu tells Rāma that Rāvaṇa carried Sītā south; Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa cremate the bird and perform the filial funeral rites of a son toward a father, declaring he has won the heavenly worlds

title: Kumbhakarṇa devastates the vānara army
description: Awake and armed, Kumbhakarṇa storms the field slaughtering thousands of vānaras, stuns and carries off Sugrīva (who bites off his nose and ears to escape), and battles Hanumān and Lakṣmaṇa

title: Rama avatara (condensed Ramayana)
description: Rama, the apex of the Solar line, descends and enacts the condensed Ramayana narrative in skandha 9

title: The search for Sita
description: Vanara armies are dispatched in four directions; the southern party learns from Sampati that Sita is held in Lanka across the ocean

title: Hanuman's leap across the ocean
description: Roused by Jambavan, Hanuman grows colossal and leaps 100 yojanas across the sea, passing the tests of Mainaka, Surasa, and Simhika

title: Hanuman's leap to Lanka and burning of the city
description: Hanuman leaps the ocean, finds Sita in the Ashoka-vatika, gives Rama's ring, burns Lanka with his tail after being captured, and returns with Sita's crest-jewel

title: Indrajit's illusory slaying of Sītā
description: To break morale Indrajit conjures a phantom Sītā and beheads 'her' before the vānaras; Rāma collapses in grief until Vibhīṣaṇa exposes the illusion as cover for the Nikumbhilā yajña

title: Parasurama clears the kṣatriyas twenty-one times
description: The warrior-brahmana avatara Parasurama rids the earth of the kṣatriya class twenty-one times

title: Rama Teaches the Rama-Hridaya to Hanuman
description: In the inset Rama-Hridaya ('Heart of Rama'), Hanuman is taught Rama's true Brahman-nature

title: Rāma slays Kumbhakarṇa
description: Rāma severs Kumbhakarṇa's arms and legs with celestial astras and finally decapitates the giant with the supreme Indra-astra; his death breaks Rāvaṇa, marking the turn toward his own end

title: Vamana's Three Steps and Bali's Surrender
description: The dwarf-avatara Vamana measures the cosmos in three steps and Bali surrenders himself, ceding his sovereignty

title: Hanuman finds Sita in the Ashoka grove
description: Hanuman finds Sita in the Ashoka-vana, gives Rama's ring as proof, and receives her crest-jewel (chudamani) as a return token

title: Kanyakumari Consecrated by Parashurama
description: Consecration of the Kanyakumari shrine at the subcontinent's southern tip is attributed to Parashurama

title: Kumbha and Nikumbha die in the war
description: Kumbhakarṇa's sons Kumbha and Nikumbha fight and die against Rāma's forces in the Laṅkā war

title: Rama Teaches the Rama-Gita to Lakshmana
description: After the coronation Rama instructs Lakshmana in pure Advaita Vedanta in the inset Rama-Gita, modelled on the Bhagavad-Gita

title: Setu-bandha (building the bridge to Lanka)
description: The vanaras led by Nala build a causeway to Lanka over the ocean, which yields after Rama threatens it with arrows

title: Sītā's earth-birth from the furrow
description: Janaka relates that Sītā was found ayonijā in the ploughed sacrificial field, a daughter of the Earth

title: The Nikumbhilā sacrifice interrupted
description: Guided by Vibhīṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa and Hanumān break into the Nikumbhilā grove and shatter Indrajit's sacrifice before the chariot manifests, denying him invulnerability

title: Burning of Lanka
description: Captured by Indrajit's Brahmastra and his tail set alight, Hanuman breaks free and torches the golden city of Lanka

title: Lakṣmaṇa slays Indrajit with the Aindrāstra
description: In the final duel Lakṣmaṇa beheads Indrajit with the Aindrāstra, the weapon of the very god Indra the rākṣasa had once conquered, breaking the back of the rākṣasa army

title: Rāma breaks the bow of Śiva and wins Sītā
description: At Mithilā Rāma lifts and strings Janaka's colossal Śiva-bow (Pināka), snapping it with a thunderclap, and so wins Sītā by the bride-price of valour

title: Vibhishana defects to Rama
description: Ravana's righteous brother Vibhishana joins Rama after counselling Ravana in vain to return Sita

title: Deaths of Kumbhakarna and Indrajit; Lakshmana revived
description: In the great battle Kumbhakarna and Indrajit/Meghanada fall, and Lakshmana, felled by Indrajit's weapon, is revived when Hanuman fetches the Sanjivani herb by carrying the whole Dronagiri mountain

title: Saubhari Weds Mandhata's Fifty Daughters
description: The sage Saubhari, disturbed by mating fish, multiplies his body to wed all fifty daughters of King Mandhata, then renounces everything

title: Sulocanā becomes satī on Indrajit's pyre
description: In later tradition Indrajit's wife Sulocanā, daughter of Śeṣa-nāga, becomes satī on his funeral pyre, celebrated as a model pativratā

title: The four-fold marriage at Mithilā
description: Rāma weds Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa weds Ūrmilā, and Bharata and Śatrughna wed Kuśadhvaja's daughters Māṇḍavī and Śrutakīrti in a quadruple fire-wedding

title: Vibhishana's defection (sharanagati)
description: Spurned by Ravana, his righteous brother Vibhishana surrenders to Rama, who accepts him and pre-crowns him king of Lanka

title: Building of the bridge (Nala-Setu / Rama-Setu)
description: Under Nala's direction the vanaras build a 100-yojana causeway across the ocean, and the army crosses to Lanka

title: Paraśurāma confronts Rāma and yields his power
description: The wrathful Paraśurāma challenges Rāma with Viṣṇu's Śārṅga bow; Rāma strings it, Paraśurāma recognizes him as Viṣṇu, surrenders his tapas, and withdraws

title: Rama slays Ravana
description: Rama kills the ten-headed Lanka-king Ravana with the Brahmastra, preceded by the Aditya-hridaya hymn taught by Agastya

title: Trishanku Hung Between Worlds
description: King Trishanku seeks heaven in his mortal body and is left suspended between earth and sky

title: Death of Kumbhakarna
description: Ravana's colossal sleeping brother Kumbhakarna is roused, rampages through the vanaras, and is dismembered and beheaded by Rama

title: Sagara's Sons Burnt and the Descent of Ganga
description: Sagara's 60,000 sons are burnt to ash by Kapila's glance, and Bhagiratha's tapas brings Ganga down to liberate their ashes

title: Sita's fire ordeal (Agni-pariksha)
description: Sita proves her chastity by entering fire, and Agni returns her unharmed

title: Agastya Releases the Kaveri
description: In a famine, the gods via Ganesha as a crow tip Agastya's water-pot so the maiden Kaveri flows out to relieve the drought, becoming the life-river of Tamil country

title: Khatvanga's Liberation in One Muhurta
description: King Khatvanga, granted a single muhurta of life on returning from aiding the devas, attains liberation in that hour by total surrender

title: Kārtavīrya steals Kāmadhenu from Jamadagni
description: Kārtavīrya Arjuna's theft of the wish-cow Kāmadhenu from the sage Jamadagni triggers Paraśurāma's vengeance

title: Rama's return and coronation (Rama-rajya)
description: Rama flies home in the Pushpaka-vimana and is crowned at Ayodhya, inaugurating the ideal reign of Rama-rajya, later celebrated as Dipavali/Vijayadashami

title: Sanjivani herb & revival of Lakshmana
description: Lakshmana felled by Indrajit's/Ravana's weapons is revived when Hanuman fetches the Sanjivani herb, carrying the whole Dronagiri mountain

title: Indrajit slain by Lakshmana
description: Guided by Vibhishana, Lakshmana disrupts the Nikumbhila sacrifice and beheads Indrajit (Meghanada) with the Aindrastra

title: Rāvaṇa wins the Ātma-liṅga and is tricked at Gokarṇa
description: Rāvaṇa wins Śiva's Ātma-liṅga by tapas on condition it never touch ground before Laṅkā; Gaṇeśa as a cowherd-boy and Vishnu's false dusk make him set it down at Gokarṇa, where it roots immovably as Mahābaleśvara, and the hurled wrappings spring up as the Sajjeśvara, Dhāreśvara, Guṇavanteśvara and Mūrudeśvara liṅgas

title: Sampāti reveals Sītā's location in Laṅkā
description: Hearing the mourning vānaras name his dead brother, the wingless Sampāti descends and, with his far-sight, declares Sītā held across the sea in Rāvaṇa's Laṅkā in the Aśoka grove, converting a hopeless search into the ocean-leap mission

title: Vasiṣṭha's brahmadaṇḍa swallows Viśvāmitra's Brahmāstra
description: Vasiṣṭha's defensive brahmadaṇḍa absorbs the Brahmāstra hurled by king Viśvāmitra, the humiliation that turns the warrior-king toward brahminhood

title: Lava-Kusha and the Ashvamedha
description: Lava and Kusha, taught the Ramayana by Valmiki, recite it at Rama's horse-sacrifice and capture the sacrificial horse, confronting their father

title: Nandinī conjures armies against Viśvāmitra
description: When king Viśvāmitra (then Kauśika) tries to seize Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Nandinī, she conjures whole armies (Pahlavas, Śakas, Yavanas, Kāmbojas) to rout him, setting him on the path to brahmin-hood
source: Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva

title: Niśākara's prophecy and Sampāti's wings restored
description: Fulfilling the sage Niśākara's prophecy that telling the vānaras of Sītā would be his great deed, Sampāti's feathers sprout and his wings regrow after he serves Rāma's cause, and he flies off rejoicing

title: Parashurama Clears the Earth of Kshatriyas
description: The Bhrigu avatara Parashurama clears the earth of kshatriyas twenty-one times in the Kartavirya/Jamadagni cycle

title: Rāma marks the Setu's start at Dhanuṣkoḍi
description: At the south-eastern sandspit of Rāmeśvaram island Rāma marks the start of the Nala-setu to Laṅkā with the tip (koḍi) of his bow (dhanuṣ) — and in the return-telling breaks the now-needless bridge there at Vibhīṣaṇa's request — giving Dhanuṣkoḍi its name and its sankalpa-snāna tīrtha and Kodaṇḍarāma shrine

title: Slaying of Ravana
description: Renewed by the Aditya-Hridayam, Rama looses the Brahmastra into Ravana's navel, drying the amrita that sustained him and killing the ten-headed king

title: Agni-pariksha (fire ordeal)
description: Sita enters fire to prove her chastity; Agni rises bearing her unharmed and testifies to her purity

title: Bharata enthrones Rāma's pādukās to rule Ayodhyā
description: Bharata enthrones Rāma's sacred sandals (pādukās) to rule Ayodhyā in his stead during Rāma's exile, an emblem of surrender at the lotus-feet

title: Rama's departure into the Sarayu
description: Rama renounces the world and walks into the Sarayu river to return to Vaikuntha as Vishnu, ending the avatar

title: Return to Ayodhya & coronation (Rama-rajya)
description: Rama flies home in the Pushpaka-vimana, reunites with Bharata, and is crowned king, inaugurating the ideal reign of Rama-rajya

title: Treta Yuga — the Age of Three-Quarter Dharma
description: Dharma declines by one leg; sacrifice (yajna), kingship, agriculture, and the first wars arise, with humans living ~10,000 years

title: Descent of the Ganga (Gangavatarana)
description: King Bhagiratha does immense penance to bring the celestial Ganga down to liberate the ashes of Sagara's 60,000 sons; Shiva breaks the river's fall in his hair and Ganga flows to Patala to redeem the ancestors, earning the epithet Bhagirathi
source: Ramayana Bala Kanda; Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana 9.8-9; Mahabharata

title: Rise of Ravana & Brahma's boon
description: The rakshasa brothers do great tapas; Ravana wins invulnerability to all beings except men and monkeys, seizes Lanka from Kubera, and conquers the three worlds

title: Valmiki composes the Rāmāyaṇa
description: The adi-kavi Valmiki composes the Rāmāyaṇa, the chronicle of Rāma's exile, Sītā's abduction, the war in Laṅkā and the return to Ayodhyā

title: Ahalya Cursed to Stone and Redeemed by Rama
description: Gautama's wife Ahalya is cursed to stone and redeemed by the touch of Rama, linking the sage-line Gautama to the Solar epic

title: Harishchandra's trial of truth
description: The Ikshvaku king Harishchandra, to honor a debt to sage Vishvamitra, surrenders his kingdom, sells his wife and son, and becomes a chandala's servant at the cremation ground; his unbroken truthfulness restores all and elevates him to heaven
source: Markandeya Purana; Aitareya Brahmana; Devi Bhagavata

title: Śiva gifts the Chandrahāsa sword to Rāvaṇa
description: Śiva gifts his curved sword Chandrahāsa to Rāvaṇa for his devotion; it returns to harm the wielder if used unjustly

title: Kārtavīrya Arjuna's sons slay Jamadagni
description: The sons of Kārtavīrya Arjuna slay the sage Jamadagni over the wish-cow Kāmadhenu, triggering Paraśurāma's vengeance

title: Vedavati's curse (reborn as Sita)
description: Ravana molests the chaste ascetic Vedavati, who immolates herself vowing to be reborn as the cause of his death, i.e. as Sita

title: Banishment of Sita
description: A washerman's slander prompts Rama to exile the pregnant Sita to Valmiki's hermitage, where she bears twins Lava and Kusha

title: Jaṭāyu fights Rāvaṇa and dies telling Rāma of Sītā
description: The vulture-king Jaṭāyu fights Rāvaṇa to save the abducted Sītā, has his wings severed, and dies telling Rāma the direction of her captor; Rāma performs his funeral rites as for a father

title: Paraśurāma clears the earth of kṣatriyas 21 times
description: The axe-bearing 6th avatāra of Viṣṇu, Paraśurāma, avenges his father by clearing the earth of corrupt kṣatriyas 21 times and reclaims Konkan/Kerala from the sea

title: Vishvamitra Becomes Brahmarshi
description: Born a Kshatriya king Kaushika, Vishvamitra earns brahmarshi status, tests Harishchandra, and trains Rama and Lakshmana, bridging Kshatriya and Brahmana lines

title: Lava-Kusha & the Ashvamedha
description: Vālmīki teaches the Rāmāyaṇa to Sita's twins Lava and Kusha, who recite it at Rama's horse-sacrifice and are revealed as his sons

title: Hanumān leaps the ocean to Laṅkā and finds Sītā
description: Hanumān, son of Vāyu and partial aṃśa of Śiva, leaps the ocean to Laṅkā and finds the captive Sītā, in supreme devotion to Rāma

title: Killing of Shambuka
description: Rama beheads the shudra ascetic Shambuka for performing tapas forbidden to his varna in Treta, reviving a dead brahmana boy; a highly disputed passage

title: Rāma slays Vālin and allies with Sugrīva
description: Rāma slays the usurping vānara Vālin (son of Indra) with his arrow and allies with Sugrīva (son of Sūrya), restoring him as king of Kiṣkindhā

title: Sita's return to the earth
description: Asked to prove her purity again, Sita calls on her mother Bhumi (Earth), who opens and receives her forever

title: Agastya presses down the Vindhya mountains
description: Agastya humbles the growing Vindhya range, pressing it down and opening the southward spread of Vedic culture

title: Nala and Nīla architect Rāma's bridge to Laṅkā
description: The engineer-vānaras Nala and Nīla architect the floating bridge (Setu) by which Rāma's monkey host crosses to storm Laṅkā

title: Rama returns to Ayodhya (Diwali)
description: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana return to Ayodhya after fourteen years' exile; the city lights lamps to guide them, the charter of Diwali night

title: Rama's departure (Mahaprasthana)
description: Rama enters the Sarayu river in jala-samadhi, resumes his form as Vishnu, and ascends to Vaikuntha; Hanuman is granted deathlessness

title: Ahalya's Redemption by Rama's Touch
description: In Kamban's devotional reframing, Rama's touch delivers Ahalya as an act of divine grace

title: Jain variant: Lakṣmaṇa slays Rāvaṇa, Rāma attains mokṣa
description: In Vimalasūri's Jain Paümacariya, the non-violent Rāma (Padma) does not kill Rāvaṇa — Lakṣmaṇa does — and Rāma attains mokṣa as a Jain layman

title: Viśvāmitra attains Brahmaṛṣi rank
description: Born a kṣatriya king, Viśvāmitra forces his way to Brahmaṛṣi rank by colossal tapas, the only Saptarṣi who was not a born brahmin

title: Hanumān carries the Sañjīvanī mountain to revive Lakṣmaṇa
description: Unable to identify the resurrection-herb Sañjīvanī on Droṇagiri, Hanumān carries the whole mountain to revive the wounded Lakṣmaṇa

title: Kapila incinerates the sons of Sagara
description: The wrathful sage Kapila's glance incinerates the 60,000 sons of Sagara in the Ganga-descent story, referenced from the Sankhya profile

title: Viśvāmitra creates Triśaṅku's heaven
description: Viśvāmitra builds a separate heaven for King Triśaṅku in his contest of tapas

title: Puṣpaka Vimāna flies Rāma home to Ayodhyā
description: The self-moving flying palace Puṣpaka — made by Viśvakarmā, passing Brahmā to Kubera to the seizing Rāvaṇa — finally flies Rāma, Sītā and the army home to Ayodhyā, then is returned to Kubera

title: Matali drives Indra's chariot for Rāma against Rāvaṇa
description: Indra's charioteer Matali drives the celestial ratha lent to Rāma for the duel with Rāvaṇa (and later to Arjuna for his heaven-journey)

title: Vasiṣṭha-Viśvāmitra cow-war and death of Vasiṣṭha's sons
description: The arch-rivalry of Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra over the wish-cow erupts in war, and Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons (including Śakti) are killed by Viśvāmitra's agency

title: Gautama curses Ahalyā to stone
description: The sage Gautama curses his wife Ahalyā (the Indra-deception myth) to become stone, later restored by Rāma's touch

title: Akal-bodhan — Rama's Autumn Worship of Durga
description: With Chandika shielding Ravana, Brahma counsels Rama to propitiate Durga out of season in autumn; Rama performs the untimely worship from Sashthi to Dashami, the mythic charter of Sharadiya Durga Puja

title: The 108 Blue Lotuses and Rama's Eye
description: Hanuman fetches 108 celestial blue lotuses for the worship; Durga hides one to test Rama, who prepares to pluck out his own lotus-eye to complete the count, whereupon Durga stays his hand and grants victory

title: Mahiravana Abducts Rama and Lakshmana; Hanuman's Patala Rescue
description: The sorcerer-king Mahiravana of Patala abducts the sleeping Rama and Lakshmana; Hanuman descends to the netherworld, learns the demon's life resides in bees, and slays him to rescue them

title: Śeṣa incarnates as Lakṣmaṇa
description: When Viṣṇu becomes Rāma, Śeṣa accompanies him as the ever-devoted younger brother Lakṣmaṇa

title: Martyrdom of Taranisen
description: Taranisen, the Rama-devotee son of Vibhishana, fights for Ravana's side out of duty while chanting Rama's name and is slain by Rama — a poignant martyrdom motif

title: Birth of Bhagiratha from Two Co-widows
description: In a Krittivasi accretion, Bhagiratha (later bringer of the Ganga to earth) is born of King Dilipa's two co-widows by divine blessing — a rare premodern parthenogenic/same-sex generation motif

title: Sita Slays Sahasra-Ravana as Mahakali (Adbhuta Ramayana)
description: When the thousand-headed Sahasra-Ravana of Pushkara fells Rama on the battlefield, Sita assumes the form of Mahakali and slays him, inverting hero and heroine roles

title: Vamana pushes Bali to the netherworld (Bali Pratipada/Onam)
description: Vamana, after the three-strides boon, pushes the asura-king Bali/Mahabali to Patala, who is granted one yearly return celebrated as Onam and Bali Pratipada

title: Sita Born to Mandodari (Adbhuta Ramayana)
description: In the Shakta Adbhuta Ramayana, Sita — the supreme Shakti — is born to Ravana's queen Mandodari rather than discovered by Janaka

title: Ravana Abducts Kausalya (Ananda Ramayana)
description: In the Ananda Ramayana, foretold that Kausalya's son by Dasharatha will kill him, Ravana abducts Kausalya but fails to keep her — a peripheral back-story

title: Vasishtha Instructs Young Rama (Yoga-Vasishtha)
description: A young, world-weary Rama is instructed by the sage Vasishtha in radical Advaita (ajatavada, non-origination) across hundreds of nested parables in the Yoga-Vasishtha

title: Vamana's three strides subdue Bali
description: Vishnu as the dwarf Vamana begs three paces of land from the asura king Bali, then swells to cosmic size (Trivikrama), covering earth and heaven in two strides and pushing Bali to the netherworld with the third
source: Rig Veda 1.154; Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23; Vishnu Purana

title: Parashurama exterminates the kshatriyas
description: After King Kartavirya Arjuna steals his father Jamadagni's wish-cow and kills the sage, the axe-bearing Parashurama annihilates the tyrant and the entire kshatriya class twenty-one times over
source: Mahabharata Vana Parva; Bhagavata Purana 9.15-16; Vishnu Purana

title: Rama slays Ravana and recovers Sita (Ramayana)
description: Rama, exiled prince of Ayodhya, allies with Hanuman and the vanaras, builds a bridge to Lanka, slays the rakshasa king Ravana, and recovers his abducted wife Sita

title: Lakshmana Kills Ravana (Jain Ramayanas)
description: In the Jain tradition the Vasudeva Lakshmana, not the non-violent Baladeva Rama, slays the Prativasudeva Ravana — and consequently falls to hell, while Rama attains moksha

title: Vali Renounces and Attains Nirvana (Paumacariya)
description: In Vimalasuri's Paumacariya, after the conflict with Sugriva, Vali renounces to become a muni and attains nirvana instead of being shot dead by Rama

title: Sita Born of Ravana and Mandodari, Then Abandoned (Gunabhadra/Sanghadasa)
description: In the Gunabhadra and Sanghadasa Jain strands, Sita is born to Ravana and Mandodari and exposed because of a prophecy of family destruction, making Ravana's later abduction unwitting near-incest

title: Rama Attains Kevala-jnana and Moksha (Jain ending)
description: The Jain epic closes with Rama attaining omniscience (kevala-jnana) and liberation at Tungi Giri, Lakshmana and Ravana going to hell, and Sita becoming a nun and ascending to heaven

title: Rāvaṇa drives Kubera from Laṅkā
description: Rāvaṇa drives his half-brother Kubera from Laṅkā and seizes his flying chariot, after which Kubera removes to Alakā in the Himālayas

title: Rāvaṇa steals the Puṣpaka Vimāna
description: Kubera's self-moving aerial chariot, a gift of Brahmā, is stolen by Rāvaṇa and later used by Rāma to return to Ayodhyā

title: Nalakūbara curses Rāvaṇa
description: Kubera's son Nalakūbara, consort of Rambhā, curses Rāvaṇa that his head will burst if he forces a woman, a curse that later protects Sītā

title: Suketu's daughter Tāḍakā born by boon and cursed by Agastya
description: The yakṣa king Suketu obtains a daughter Tāḍakā by boon, who, cursed by Agastya, becomes a man-eating ogress later slain by Rāma

title: Birth of Rama (Rama Navami)
description: Rama, the 7th dashavatara, is born to Dasharatha of Ayodhya, opening the Bala Kanda; commemorated on Chaitra Shukla Navami

title: Birth of Hanuman (Hanuman Jayanti)
description: Hanuman, the vanara devotee of Rama and a partial incarnation of Shiva/Vayu, is born, commemorated on Hanuman Jayanti

title: Lakshmi ties a thread on Bali (Raksha Bandhan)
description: Lakshmi, disguised as a poor woman, ties a protective thread on Bali to win back her husband Vishnu, a Raksha Bandhan charter linked to the Vamana cycle

title: Birth of Parashurama / descent of the Ganga (Akshaya Tritiya)
description: Akshaya Tritiya stacks charters including the birth of Parashurama, the descent of the Ganga, the start of Treta Yuga, and Vyasa beginning the Mahabharata

title: Yudhājit's embassy to Ayodhyā
description: Kaikeyī's brother Yudhājit, king of the Kekayas, sends the brahmin Gārgya to urge Rāma to conquer the rich, unclaimed country of the Gandharvas on both banks of the Sindhu

title: Abdication to the forest
description: remorseful and barred from fatherhood, Pāṇḍu renounces the throne to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and retires with Kuntī and Mādrī to ascetic life at Śataśṛṅga

title: Abduction of Draupadī by Jayadratha
description: Jayadratha, smitten, carries Draupadī off by force from the Pāṇḍava forest hermitage while the brothers hunt

title: Abduction of the Kāśi princesses
description: Bhīṣma storms the svayaṃvara of Kāśī and carries off Ambā, Ambikā, and Ambālikā by force as war-brides for Vicitravīrya

title: Abduction of the three Kāśī princesses
description: Bhīṣma seizes Ambā, Ambikā and Ambālikā by force from the Kāśī svayaṃvara as brides for Vicitravīrya, defeating the assembled kings including Śālva

title: Abhimanyu Born to Arjuna and Subhadra
description: Abhimanyu is born at Indraprastha to Arjuna and Subhadra as the incarnation of Varcas son of Soma, fated to return after only sixteen years

title: Acchodā reborn as Kālī/Satyavatī from the fish Adrikā
