description: The decree detonates: Uparicara Vasu's seed falls into the Yamunā, the cursed apsarā-fish Adrikā bears the dark fisher-girl Kālī (Satyavatī), a king's daughter fostered at the ferry

title: Aditi's earrings and boon
description: after the Naraka-vadha Kṛṣṇa flies with Satyabhāmā on Garuḍa to Amarāvatī to restore Aditi's stolen earrings, and Aditi grants Satyabhāmā unfading youth and beauty beside Kṛṣṇa

title: Aditi's mediation and Indra's condition
description: Aditi reconciles her son with Kṛṣṇa and Indra yields the tree on the condition that it bloom on earth only while the avatāra walks it, returning to Svarga at his departure

title: Akrūra summoned to Vraja
description: Kaṃsa sends the devotee-noble Akrūra to fetch Krishna and Balarāma to Mathurā for the bow-sacrifice festival
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.36–38; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa proclaimed as Nara-Nārāyaṇa
description: Paraśurāma closes the tale by identifying Arjuna as Nara and Kṛṣṇa as Nārāyaṇa, the eternal sages born among men, and urges Duryodhana to make peace before Gāṇḍīva's arrows fall

title: Arjuna redeems the five crocodile-apsarās at Mahīsāgara-saṃgama
description: on his pilgrimage-exile Arjuna drags cursed crocodile-apsarās from the Mahī–sea confluence and restores their forms, proving the tīrtha's redeeming power
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Kaumārikā-khaṇḍa; cf. Mbh Ādi Parva

title: Aśvatthāman leads the Sauptika night massacre
description: Consecrated as the last Kaurava senāpati and empowered by Śiva at the camp gate, he slaughters Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the Upapāṇḍavas, Śikhaṇḍin and the sleeping Pāñcāla host

title: Aśvins father Nakula and Sahadeva
description: by Kuntī's boon-mantra the twin physician-gods father the twin Pāṇḍavas Nakula and Sahadeva on Mādrī, wife of Pāṇḍu

title: Balarāma hears the Sarasvatī fords' legends
description: on his war-neutral forty-two-day Sarasvatī pilgrimage, Balarāma visits the Sārasvata and Vṛddhakanyā tīrthas whose upākhyānas are recited to him

title: Balarāma slays the ape Dvivida
description: The mountain-hurling gorilla Dvivida, ravaging Ānarta to avenge Naraka, is battered to death by Balarāma on Raivataka hill

title: Balarāma slays the other King Haṃsa
description: after an eighteen-day battle Balarāma kills a king who merely shares Haṃsa's name, seeding the fatal false report

title: Balarāma slays the rogue ape Dvivida
description: the Aśvin-born vānara, avenging Narakāsura by ravaging Ānarta, is battered to death on Raivataka hill

title: Balarāma's serpent-exit departure
description: at Prabhāsa after the Yādava fratricide, Balarāma gives up his body in yoga and a great white serpent issues from his mouth into the sea, Saṅkarṣaṇa returning to Śeṣa

title: Balarāma's tīrtha-yātrā — Romaharṣaṇa and Balvala
description: Sitting out the war, Balarāma tours the sacred fords, kills the unrising sūta Romaharṣaṇa with a kuśa blade at Naimiṣāraṇya, installs Ugraśravas as reciter, and slays the demon Balvala

title: Belālasena's severed head witnesses Kurukṣetra
description: Bhīma's son gives Kṛṣṇa his head before the war, watches all eighteen days, and testifies that only Kṛṣṇa's cakra did the killing [regional]

title: Bhānumatī wedded to Sahadeva
description: Nārada reveals Durvāsas' curse fulfilled and discharged, and the rescued maiden is bestowed on Mādrī's son Sahadeva

title: Bhīma reaches the Lauhitya
description: in the eastern digvijaya Bhīma subdues Prāgjyotiṣa and levies tribute from the mleccha kings beyond the Lauhitya

title: Bhīṣma narrates Mucukunda on the bed of arrows
description: dying after Kurukṣetra, the grandsire teaches Yudhiṣṭhira rājadharma through the tale of Mucukunda and Vaiśravaṇa, that a king's sword is empty without a priest's fire

title: Bhīṣma teaches the mānasa-tīrthas
description: within the arrow-bed instruction cycle, the 'tīrthas of the heart' are taught: truth their water, restraint and compassion their ghāṭs, above all outer fords

title: Bhīṣma tells the Sṛñjaya story
description: dying on his bed of arrows, Bhīṣma answers Yudhiṣṭhira's grief with the old Nārada–Sṛñjaya dialogue, a consolation-inset framing the roll of the Sixteen Kings

title: Bhīṣma tells the Uñchavṛtti-upākhyāna
description: on the arrow-bed after Kurukṣetra the dying grandsire closes the Mokṣadharma by narrating to Yudhiṣṭhira the tale of Dharmāraṇya and the Nāga Padmanābha, exalting the gleaner's life as the surest dharma

title: Bhīṣma's minor Śānti-Parva insets
description: from his bed of arrows the dying Bhīṣma answers Yudhiṣṭhira with five small didactic tales on japa, deliberation, dharma-over-wealth, hope, and enmity

title: Bhīṣma's twin varṇa-upākhyānas
description: on the bed of arrows Bhīṣma answers Yudhiṣṭhira's questions on caste with two adjacent, opposed tales — Mātaṅga (Brāhmaṇahood refused) and Vītahavya (Brāhmaṇahood conferred)

title: Bhīṣma-pañcaka instituted
description: Bhīṣma expounds dharma from the arrow-bed through Kārttika's last five days, and Kṛṣṇa charters the five-day fast in his honor

title: Bhūriśravas slays the ten sons of Sātyaki
description: In the fighting of the Jayadratha-vadha day Bhūriśravas kills Sātyaki's ten sons, sharpening the feud inherited from Śini and Somadatta

title: Birth of Aśvatthāman with the forehead gem
description: Droṇa and Kṛpī's son is born crying like the horse Uccaiḥśravas, named by a sky-voice, and bearing a protective gem in his forehead

title: Birth of Haṃsa and Ḍimbhaka by Śiva's boon
description: childless Brahmadatta of Śālva wins two weapon-proof sons after ten years' worship, while his brāhmaṇa friend Mitrasaha gains the Viṣṇu-named Janārdana

title: Birth of Nakula and Sahadeva by the Aśvins
description: Mādrī, lent Kuntī's mantra once, summons the twin Aśvins and bears twin sons in a single birth on Mount Śataśṛṅga, a bodiless voice declaring they will surpass their fathers in beauty and energy

title: Birth of Śuka from the araṇi
description: Vyāsa's tapas for a son pure as the five elements bears fruit when, at the sight of the apsarā Ghṛtācī in she-parrot form, his seed falls on the fire-drill sticks and Śuka is born from them, bathed by Gaṅgā in person

title: Chandra Tāl claimed as Yudhiṣṭhira's ascent-place
description: Himalayan tradition localizes the Mahāprasthānika climax at the Spiti moon-lake, holding that Indra's chariot descended to Chandra Tāl to carry the eldest Pāṇḍava bodily to Svarga (the epic itself names only Meru's slope)
source: Mahābhārata, Mahāprasthānika Parva 2–3; Spiti regional tradition

title: Cowherd boys sent to beg from the sacrifice
description: herding cattle far from Vraja, Krishna's hungry friends are told to ask food of the brāhmaṇas performing a Vedic sacrifice nearby, invoking the names of Krishna and Balarāma

title: Dantavakra and Vidūratha slain
description: Dantavakra attacks on foot with a mace to avenge Śiśupāla and Śālva and is crushed by Kaumodakī; his brother Vidūratha is beheaded, closing the Jaya–Vijaya cycle

title: Death by forest fire
description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī sit in yogic composure as the conflagration consumes the hermitage; Sañjaya escapes and Nārada brings the news

title: Destruction of Saubha and death of Śālva
description: the Sudarśana cakra cleaves the flying city in two into the ocean and then beheads Śālva, blazing like the sun

title: Devakī's petition
description: hearing that Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma raised Sāndīpani's dead son, the grieving Devakī begs to see once more the six sons Kaṃsa killed

title: Dhanvantari born into the Kāśī royal line
description: The ocean-born physician-god is reborn as a king of the Kāśī dynasty (son of Dīrghatapas), promulgating Āyurveda in eight divisions
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.17.4–5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.8

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra hears the Gītā and viśvarūpa through Sañjaya
description: refusing the divine eye for himself, the blind king receives Sañjaya's report of the war, the Bhagavad-Gītā, and the cosmic form

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra passed over for the Kuru throne
description: the blind eldest prince is set aside and the younger Pāṇḍu is consecrated king of Hāstinapura

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra restored as Gandharva king
description: in Yudhiṣṭhira's tour of the hereafter the blind king is seen glorious among the Gandharvas, the station of his origin

title: Digvijaya of Pāṇḍu
description: the young king slays Dīrgha of Magadha and reduces the Daśārṇas, Mithilā, Kāśī, Suhma and Puṇḍra, returning to Hāstinapura laden with tribute

title: Ḍimbhaka drowns in the Yamunā on false news
description: hearing "Haṃsa is slain," Ḍimbhaka believes his brother dead and kills himself in the river, untouched by any weapon

title: Ḍimbhaka's suicide in the same waters (Harivaṃśa variant)
description: pursued by Balarāma and taunted to "ask the river" for his brother, Ḍimbhaka laments and kills himself in the Yamunā

title: Dragging of Hastināpura
description: slighted by the Kurus holding Sāmba captive, Balarāma hooks his plough into the city's ramparts and drags Hastināpura toward the Gaṅgā until the couple is released

title: Dragging of the Yamunā
description: visiting Vraja alone for two months, the wine-flushed Balarāma hooks his plough into the Yamunā and drags the river-goddess from her course until she submits

title: Draupadī and the eight queens
description: Draupadī asks each of Kṛṣṇa's aṣṭa-mahiṣī how she was won, gathering the marriage-narratives of Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Jāmbavatī, Kālindī, Mitravindā, Satyā, Bhadrā and Lakṣmaṇā

title: Durvāsas curses Bhānumatī in the Raivata garden
description: the offended sage dooms Bhānu's daughter to be carried off by an enemy, then softens the curse to promise her purity and a good husband

title: Dushyanta weds Śakuntalā near Kaṇva's āśrama at Nandaprayag
description: Garhwal tradition localizes the gāndharva marriage that produced Bharata to this valley [folk] [regional]
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva base; Wikipedia, Panch Prayag

title: Dvārakā sinks and Vajra inherits the remnant
description: After Kṛṣṇa's departure by the hunter Jarā's arrow and Balarāma's yogic death, the sea swallows Dvārakā; Arjuna evacuates the survivors and Kṛṣṇa's great-grandson Vajra is installed as the last Yādava king
source: Mahābhārata Mausala Parva 4-8; Bhāgavata XI.30-31; Viṣṇu Purāṇa V.38

title: Dvivida-vadha
description: the rogue mountain-hurling ape Dvivida, avenging Narakāsura by ravaging Ānarta, is battered to death by Balarāma on Raivataka hill

title: Forest retirement of the old king
description: fifteen years after the war, Dhṛtarāṣṭra retires with Gāndhārī, Kuntī, Vidura and Sañjaya to a Gaṅgā-side hermitage

title: Fourfold division of Vajranābha's kingdom
description: Kṛṣṇa and Indra share the demon realm among Vijaya son of Jayanta and the newborn sons of Pradyumna, Sāmba and Gada, and the Yādavas return to Dwārakā

title: Funeral rites at Hāstinapura
description: the Śataśṛṅga ascetics deliver Kuntī, the five boys and the remains of Pāṇḍu and Mādrī to the capital, where Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Bhīṣma and Vidura perform the śrāddha

title: Gāndharva marriage of Pradyumna and Prabhāvatī
description: entering her apartments as a black bee in a garland, Pradyumna weds Prabhāvatī before a self-blazing fire; Gada and Sāmba secretly wed her cousins Candrāvatī and Guṇavatī

title: Gonanda I of Kashmir falls to Balarāma
description: The Kashmir king Gonanda I, kinsman-ally of Jarāsandha, joins the siege of Mathurā and is slain in battle by Balarāma

title: Gopīs of Vraja canonized as the paradigm of parā bhakti
description: their prema for Kṛṣṇa is named the living exemplar of supreme love, defended as no mere paramour's passion

title: Govardhan Annakūṭa — the mountain of food
description: Kṛṣṇa redirects Indra's sacrifice to Govardhana Hill heaped with food and lifts the hill to shelter Vraja from Indra's flood, founding the annakūṭa / chappan-bhoga offering

title: Haṃsa drowns after him; Jarāsandha turns home "with an empty heart"
description: the real Haṃsa, learning of Ḍimbhaka's suicide, enters the Yamunā, and the bereft Jarāsandha abandons his Mathurā campaign

title: Hanumān humbles Bhīma on the Gandhamādana path
description: the surviving vānara chirañjīvi tests his Vāyu-born brother with his immovable tail

title: Installation of Jñāna Sarasvatī at Vyāsapurī
description: the sand-mūrtis are consecrated with Sarasvatī as presiding goddess, founding the Basara Śākta Tridevī kṣetra

title: Jāmbavān fights Kṛṣṇa over the Syamantaka jewel
description: after a cave-battle of many days the bear-king recognizes Rāma returned, surrenders the gem and gives Jāmbavatī in marriage

title: Jantu immolated over the mothers' resistance
description: the queens seize and drag Jantu away weeping, but the priest wrests him free, slays him, offers his fat into the fire, and the swooning mothers are made to breathe the smoke

title: Kaṃsa slays the six infants
description: fulfilling the curse, the tyrant Kaṃsa dashes Devakī's first six newborns to death, the atrocity the Ṣaḍgarbha arc later resolves

title: Kaṃsa usurps Mathurā and imprisons Ugrasena
description: The Andhaka prince Kaṃsa jails his father King Ugrasena and, warned that Devakī's eighth son will kill him, imprisons Vasudeva and Devakī and slays their first six infants
source: Bhāgavata X.1-4; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa V.1-4

title: Kaṇva narrates the Mātali-upākhyāna
description: during Kṛṣṇa's failed peace-embassy the sage Kaṇva tells Duryodhana the tale of Mātali and Garuḍa as a warning against pride and irreconcilable enmity

title: Karṇa and Draupadī charter-variants of Chhath
description: folk aetiologies place the first riverside sun-vrata to Sūrya and Chhathī Maiyā with Sūrya's son Karṇa, or with Draupadī and the Pāṇḍavas seeking their kingdom [folk]

title: Karṇa spares Nakula
description: Defeating Nakula in single combat on Day 17, Karṇa honours his promise to Kuntī and dismisses him alive with a taunt and a touch of the bow

title: Karṇa's tapas at Karnaprayag
description: Karṇa worships his father Sūrya at the Piṇḍar–Alaknandā confluence and obtains the golden kavacha-kuṇḍala; Garhwal localization of the epic episode [regional]
source: Mahābhārata, Vana Parva base; Wikipedia, Panch Prayag

title: Kashmir sits out the Kurukṣetra war
description: Because the infant Gonanda II is too young to be courted by either side, no king of Kashmir is summoned to the Bhārata war — the question that frames the whole Nīlamata

title: Kāśī withholds alms from Vyāsa
description: to test the sage, Śiva has Pārvatī see that no household in the city gives Vyāsa or his disciples any alms

title: King Nanda's yajña at Nandaprayag
description: a King Nanda, identified by tradition with Krishna's Yādava foster-father, performs a great sacrifice at the Nandākinī confluence, giving the prayāga its name [regional]

title: King Nṛga freed from chameleon-form
description: Krishna lifts a giant chameleon from a dry well and it resumes the form of King Nṛga, cursed for misgiving a brāhmaṇa's cow; released, he ascends

title: Krishna blesses their love and sends them home
description: receiving their offering in the grove, Krishna praises the wives' devotion as life's highest fruit but bids them return to complete their husbands' rite, teaching that hearing and remembering him suffice without bodily nearness

title: Krishna descends to Varuṇa-loka
description: hearing the cowherds cry "Kṛṣṇa! Rāma!", Krishna understands his father has been taken and goes down into the watery abode of Varuṇa to reclaim him

title: Krishna performs Karṇa's last rites near Karnaprayag
description: a local variant extends the site's claim from Karṇa's penance to his post-Kurukṣetra obsequies [folk] [disputed]
source: local tradition, per Wikipedia, Panch Prayag

title: Krishna redirects the boys to the wives
description: unruffled by the refusal, Krishna sends the boys to the yajña-patnīs, the sacrificers' devoted wives, announcing that he and Balarāma have come and are hungry

title: Kṛṣṇa becomes Raṇacchoḍa
description: quitting Mathurā's battlefield for the western sea, Kṛṣṇa earns the epithet *Raṇchhoḍa* borne by the Dvārakā image later enshrined at Ḍākor

title: Kṛṣṇa beheads Nikumbha with the discus
description: discerning the true dānava amid his phantom doubles, Kṛṣṇa cuts off Nikumbha's head and the demon falls like an uprooted tree

title: Kṛṣṇa bilocates for Śrutadeva and Bahulāśva
description: Visiting Mithilā, Krishna simultaneously guests with the poor brāhmaṇa Śrutadeva and King Bahulāśva, honoring the equal devotion of pauper and monarch

title: Kṛṣṇa cites the drownings in the Rājasūya counsel
description: with Haṃsa, Ḍimbhaka, and Kaṃsa dead, Kṛṣṇa tells Yudhiṣṭhira that Jarāsandha is stripped of his supports and can now be slain, but only in single combat by Bhīma

title: Kṛṣṇa declares Mārgaśīrṣa his vibhūti
description: "Of months I am Mārgaśīrṣa," spoken in the vibhūti-yoga at Kurukṣetra, the epic's own month-consecration

title: Kṛṣṇa destroys Śālva's Saubha
description: Śiśupāla's ally Śālva besieges Dwārakā with the Śiva-granted aerial fortress Saubha; Krishna shatters the machine and beheads Śālva

title: Kṛṣṇa distinguishes sannyāsa from tyāga
description: at Kurukṣetra Kṛṣṇa rules that sannyāsa is giving up desire-driven rites while tyāga is giving up the fruits of all action

title: Kṛṣṇa follows Rukmiṇī to Diṇḍīrvan
description: in the Dvārakā-frame variant, Kṛṣṇa comes from Dvārakā seeking the estranged Rukmiṇī sulking in the Diṇḍīravana grove near Pandharpur, rooting the Deccan kṣetra in his Dvāpara life

title: Kṛṣṇa kicks Haṃsa into the Kāliya pool (Harivaṃśa variant)
description: routed by the Vaiṣṇava weapon, Haṃsa flees into the Yamunā abyss where Kāliya once lived and Kṛṣṇa's kick sends him to the serpent-deeps, never to rise

title: Kṛṣṇa narrates the Ekādaśī-māhātmyas to Yudhiṣṭhira
description: the master frame of the year-cycle: Yudhiṣṭhira asks the name, method, and fruit of each month's Ekādaśī and Kṛṣṇa answers with its kathā

title: Kṛṣṇa prescribes the Ananta vrata to Yudhiṣṭhira
description: after the dice-game dispossession, Kṛṣṇa teaches the fourteen-knot Ananta Chaturdaśī vow as the means to recover the kingdom

title: Kṛṣṇa seeks a son at Upamanyu's hermitage
description: Grieving Jāmbavatī's sonlessness, Kṛṣṇa travels to the Himālayan hermitage of the ageless sage Upamanyu to win a son by tapas to Śiva
source: Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva XIV; Śiva Purāṇa, Umā-saṃhitā 1

title: Kṛṣṇa slays Dāmodara and crowns the widow Yaśovatī
description: Gonanda's avenging son Dāmodara is killed by Kṛṣṇa's discus at a Gāndhāra svayaṃvara, and Kṛṣṇa has the pregnant queen Yaśovatī consecrated because Kashmir is Pārvatī herself

title: Kṛṣṇa slays Kaṃsa and restores Ugrasena
description: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma kill the usurper at Mathurā and reinstall Ugrasena as king, keeping Yadu's curse — no Yādava takes the throne himself
source: Bhāgavata X.44-45; Viṣṇu Purāṇa V.20-21; Harivaṃśa

title: Kṛṣṇa teaches the jaṅgama-tīrtha doctrine to Akrūra
description: Kṛṣṇa declares that saints are 'moving tīrthas' who purify the tīrthas themselves, since the Lord dwells in their hearts

title: Kṛṣṇa worships his own image at Dvārakā and charges Uddhava
description: Kṛṣṇa keeps the mūrti in his Dvārakā shrine and, before departing, tells Uddhava it will float free of the coming flood for Bṛhaspati to secure

title: Kṛṣṇa's confession at Kāmyaka
description: visiting the exiled Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa narrates the whole Saubha war in the first person to explain his absence from the dice-game

title: Kṛṣṇa's rāsa-līlā becomes the archetype of danced worship
description: the Vṛndāvana rāsa is the charter-myth later embodied in Manipuri Rāsa-līlā and the rāsa folk-dances

title: Kṛṣṇa's Rukmiṇī-marriage rejoins Jyāmagha's two branches
description: Kṛṣṇa (descended from Vidarbha's son Kratha via Sātvata) carries off Rukmiṇī of the Vidarbha house, marrying back within Jyāmagha's own posterity
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12–13, V.26; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.24, X.52–54

title: Kṛṣṇa's teaching to the gopīs
description: in private he consoles the gopīs with jñāna, declaring himself the one all-pervading Self so that their separation is only apparent and their love-longing is itself yoga

title: Kṛṣṇa's war with Indra (Indra-yuddha)
description: Indra pursues with the Ādityas, Maruts and Vasus and hurls the Vajra, but the deva-rāja is worsted by his own supreme source, Viṣṇu incarnate on Garuḍa

title: Kuntī's counter-precedent
description: refusing to be sent to a stranger's bed, Kuntī answers Pāṇḍu with the ancient tale of Vyuṣitāśva and asks him instead to beget children by his own ascetic power

title: Lomaśa leads the Pāṇḍavas' tīrtha-yātrā
description: the exiled Pāṇḍavas walk the all-India ford-circuit under the sage Lomaśa, dramatizing pilgrimage as the poor person's yajña

title: Mādrī's anumaraṇa on Pāṇḍu's pyre
description: The junior queen wins the contest of devotion against Kuntī and ascends her husband's funeral pyre by her own insistent choice

title: Many rasas at Kaṃsa's arena
description: Kṛṣṇa appears differently to each beholder (thunderbolt to wrestlers, death to Kaṃsa, child to the elders), the proof-text for devotion refracted through bhāva

title: Mokṣadā Ekādaśī as Gītā Jayantī
description: tradition fixes the speaking of the Bhagavad-gītā at Kurukṣetra to the Mārgaśīrṣa śukla Ekādaśī, doubling Mokṣadā as Gītā Jayantī
source: traditional identification; Padma Purāṇa Ekādaśī cycle

title: Muṣṭika slain in Kaṃsa's arena
description: Balarāma crushes the champion wrestler Muṣṭika and then Kaṃsa's eight avenging brothers at Mathurā

title: Nakula questions Bhīṣma on escaping Yama
description: on the field at Kurukṣetra the youngest Pāṇḍava asks his dying grandsire how a soul is freed from death's authority, and Bhīṣma repeats Yama's secret charge

title: Nakula slays the sons of Karṇa
description: In the Day 18 fighting Nakula kills Citrasena, Satyasena, and Suṣeṇa, three sons of Karṇa

title: Nakula's western digvijaya
description: For Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya, Nakula subdues Rohītaka, the Śibis and the western peoples and receives the affectionate submission of his uncle Śalya of Madra, returning with tribute borne by ten thousand camels

title: Nanda seized by Varuṇa's servant
description: bathing in the Yamunā at a forbidden pre-dawn hour on the Dvādaśī after his Ekādaśī fast, Nanda is carried off to the undersea court of the water-lord by a demoniac servant of Varuṇa

title: Nanda's report and the cowherds' silent wish
description: Nanda describes the honour Varuṇa paid to Krishna, and the cowherds inwardly wonder whether their boy can grant them his own supreme abode

title: Nārada retells the Nimi–Yogendra dialogue to Vasudeva
description: at Dvārakā on the eve of Kṛṣṇa's departure, Vasudeva asks about bhāgavata-dharma and Nārada answers with the ancient Videha saṃvāda

title: Nārada's Pārijāta blossom
description: Nārada brings a single Pārijāta flower to Kṛṣṇa's court and Kṛṣṇa gives it to Rukmiṇī, then goads Satyabhāmā that the whole tree stands in Indra's heaven, igniting the co-wife rivalry

title: Navaguñjara theophany to Arjuna
description: a composite beast of nine animals appears to Arjuna during his penance on Maṇibhadra hill; recognizing that no natural creature could exist in such a form, he lowers the Gāṇḍīva and worships it as Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa

title: Nikumbha abducts Bhānumatī
description: while the Yādava warriors sport at the festival, the illusion-wielding dānava snatches Bhānu's daughter from the palace garden and flies to Ṣaṭpura

title: Niyoga birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra
description: Ambikā closes her eyes before Vyāsa during the levirate rite and her son is born blind

title: Niyoga birth of Pāṇḍu
description: Ambālikā turns pale before the sage Vyāsa during the levirate rite, so her son is born pale and named Pāṇḍu

title: Outrage at Puṣkara
description: Haṃsa and Ḍimbhaka wreck the ascetics' hermitage and defile it with meat-cooking, and Durvāsas leads five thousand sages to Dvārakā to lay the sacrilege before Kṛṣṇa

title: Pāṇḍu crowned past his blind elder brother
description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra is set aside for blindness and Pāṇḍu is consecrated king of Hāstinapura, seeding the Kaurava grievance

title: Pāṇḍu seen among the risen dead
description: Vyāsa raises the departed to sight for one night on the Gaṅgā, and Pāṇḍu appears before his sons and widows

title: Pāṇḍu's plea for offspring
description: barred from fatherhood by the Kindama curse, Pāṇḍu invokes the ancient liberty of women and Śvetaketu's reform to urge Kuntī to raise up heirs for his line

title: Paraśurāma tells the Dambhodbhava tale in the Kaurava court
description: during Kṛṣṇa's peace embassy, Rāma Jāmadagnya narrates the world-conqueror's humbling as a warning against Duryodhana's pride

title: Partition of the Kuru kingdom
description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra grants the Pāṇḍavas the wilderness of Khāṇḍavaprastha, which they raise into Indraprastha

title: Patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyam — the offering charter
description: Kṛṣṇa declares he accepts a mere leaf, flower, fruit or water given with devotion, and that eaters of the remnant of sacrifice are freed from sin, converting every meal into naivedya and prasāda

title: Pauṇḍraka joins the anti-Kṛṣṇa axis
description: Pauṇḍraka-Vāsudeva, lord of the Puṇḍras/Vaṅgas/Kirātas, is named among Jarāsandha's allied kings and later escorts Śiśupāla to Rukmiṇī's wedding

title: Pauṇḍraka slain and Kāśī burned
description: Krishna beheads the imposter 'Vāsudeva' Pauṇḍraka and the Kāśī king; when Sudakṣiṇa's abhicāra fire-demon attacks Dwārakā, the Sudarśana cakra drives it back and incinerates Kāśī

title: Pauṇḍraka-vadha at Kāśī
description: Kṛṣṇa breaks the five akṣauhiṇīs of the impostor and his ally, beheads Pauṇḍraka with the Sudarśana cakra, and hurls the Kāśī king's severed head into his own city

title: Poigai's cosmic lamp
description: the first Āḻvār kindles a lamp of earth-vessel, ocean-ghee and sun-flame while Bhūtam lights one of love and Pey sees Śrī before Viṣṇu, composing the earliest 300 verses of the Prabandham

title: Pradyumna's stand and the charioteer's dharma
description: Pradyumna champions the city's defense, is struck senseless, rebukes the charioteer who saved him, then is stopped from killing Śālva, whose death is fated for Kṛṣṇa

title: Pūjanī blinds Brahmadatta's prince
description: the palace bird Pūjanī, whose chick the infant prince crushed, tears out his eyes in revenge and refuses the king's peace, declaring that kindled enmity never dies

title: Pulastya recites the tīrtha catalogue to Bhīṣma
description: the sage Pulastya teaches young Bhīṣma the roster of fords and their phala, with the warning that only the self-controlled gain the fruit

title: Rādhā's birth at Barsānā/Rāval
description: Rādhā is born (or found on a lotus) as daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā in Braj
source: Padma Purāṇa late portions; Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa

title: Rādhā's māna–separation–reunion arc (Gīta-Govinda narrative)
description: Jayadeva's lyric recentres Kṛṣṇa's Vṛndāvana rāsa on the single beloved Rādhā, through jealous pride (yāhi mādhava), Kṛṣṇa's plea to place her foot on his head (dehi pada-pallavam), and reunion where God serves the beloved (kuru yadunandana) [late text]

title: Rantideva among the sixteen dead kings
description: recited amid the consolation for Abhimanyu, Vyāsa names Rantideva a cakravartin at whose table two thousand cattle were dressed daily, yet who died — teaching the vanity of grief

title: Rāsa-līlā as the paradigm of madhurya-rasa
description: the gopīs' autumn-night dance with Kṛṣṇa becomes the archetypal event of conjugal devotional rasa, with Rādhā's mahābhāva its summit

title: Robbers murder the golden boy for an empty hoard
description: believing Suvarṇaṣṭhīvin's body full of gold, robbers slay and cut him open, find nothing, and perish, leaving Sṛñjaya bereft of both son and gold at a stroke

title: Sahadeva offers the arghya to Kṛṣṇa
description: At the Rājasūya Sahadeva, at Bhīṣma's direction, presents the first-honour offering to Kṛṣṇa, triggering Śiśupāla's fatal outburst

title: Sahadeva slays Ulūka and Śakuni
description: On the afternoon of Day 18 Sahadeva kills Śakuni's son Ulūka and then beheads Śakuni with a broad-headed arrow, reminding him of the dice and fulfilling his dice-hall vow

title: Sahadeva's southern digvijaya and the fire at Māhiṣmatī
description: Sahadeva conquers the south for the Rājasūya, propitiating Agni who defends king Nīla's city, and levies tribute from the Pāṇḍyas, Dravidas, and by envoys from Vibhīṣaṇa of Laṅkā

title: Śakuni's bone-dice vengeance
description: the Kauravas starve Śakuni's Gāndhāra kin to death; dice carved from his father's bones drive his covert engineering of the Kauravas' ruin [regional]

title: Śālva besieges Dvārakā
description: avenging Śiśupāla's death at the Rājasūya, Śālva assaults Dvārakā from the airborne Saubha while Kṛṣṇa is away at Indraprastha

title: Śālva wins the Śiva-boon and the Saubha
description: after a year-long vow to Paśupati, Śālva receives the Maya-built flying iron city Saubha, unassailable by devas, asuras or men

title: Śalya marches to join the Pāṇḍavas
description: Śalya sets out from Madra with his army intending to fight for his sister's sons, the Pāṇḍavas

title: Arjuna and the Gandharva — the 'Tāpatya' frame
description: Arjuna defeats the gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa/Citraratha on the Gaṅgā, is hailed as 'Tāpatya,' and asks why — prompting the Saṃvaraṇa–Tapatī tale

title: Arjuna Conceived by Indra
description: Kunti uses the Durvasa boon-mantra to invoke Indra, who begets Arjuna, the third Pandava, in the Shatashringa hermitage

title: Arjuna reaches Maṇipura on his tīrtha-yātrā
description: During the twelfth year of his exile-pilgrimage, Arjuna arrives at the kingdom of Maṇipura and beholds the princess Citrāṅgadā

title: Arjuna sees Subhadrā at Dvārakā
description: During his tīrtha-pilgrimage Arjuna comes to Dvārakā/Raivataka and is smitten by Subhadrā at the Vṛṣṇi festival

title: Bāṇa's boon of war
description: The thousand-armed asura Bāṇāsura, vain of his arms, begs Śiva for a worthy battle; Śiva foretells his humbling when his banner-staff breaks
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.62; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Bṛhadaśva Begins the Tale of Nala
description: In exile Yudhiṣṭhira asks if any king suffered worse than he; the sage Bṛhadaśva answers with Nala's story and teaches him the secret of dice

title: Bṛhadaśva narrates Nala's tale to Yudhiṣṭhira
description: Sage Bṛhadaśva consoles the exiled Yudhiṣṭhira with the Nala story and teaches him the akṣa-hṛdaya (secret of dice)

title: Bhima Born of Vayu
description: Kunti uses the Durvasa-mantra to summon Vayu, who begets Bhima, the second Pandava endowed with superhuman strength

title: Bhishma's terrible vow
description: Devavrata renounces the throne and vows lifelong celibacy so Satyavati's line may inherit, earning the name Bhishma and the boon of death-at-will

title: Bhīma Catches the Bull-Form Shiva at Guptakāśī
description: Fleeing the Pandavas seeking expiation for the Kurukshetra slaughter, Shiva as a bull is recognized by Bhima at Guptakashi; seized by the tail, the bull dives into the earth to re-emerge in five parts across Garhwal

title: Bhīṣma Delivers the Mokṣadharma
description: From his bed of arrows the dying Bhīṣma teaches Yudhiṣṭhira the dharma of liberation, the largest philosophical block of the epic

title: Bhīṣma Recites the Nārāyaṇīya
description: In the aftermath of Kurukṣetra, the dying Bhīṣma teaches Yudhiṣṭhira the Nārāyaṇīya, systematizing Kṛṣṇa-Vāsudeva as supreme Brahman and Pāñcarātra theology

title: Birth and primacy of Citrāṅgada
description: Citrāṅgada is born as the firstborn son of Śāntanu and Satyavatī, becoming eldest heir after Bhīṣma's renunciation of the throne
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~101; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: Birth as an aṃśa of Dvāpara
description: Śakuni, son of Subala and brother of Gāndhārī, is born of a portion of the age-spirit Dvāpara, the embodiment of the gambling-die

title: Birth from the fish
description: Born of King Uparicara Vasu's seed and the cursed apsarā-fish Adrikā, the girl twin is raised by the fisher-chief and carries a fish-smell (Matsyagandhā)

title: Birth of Babhruvahana to Arjuna and Chitrangada
description: Babhruvahana is born to Chitrangada of Manipura during Arjuna's tirtha-exile, bound by pact to remain as matrilineal heir of Manipura

title: Birth of Barbarīka
description: Barbarīka is born to Ghaṭotkaca and Maurvī/Kāmakaṇṭakaṭā, grandson of Bhīma, carrying both rākṣasa and Pāṇḍava blood
source: Skanda Purāṇa (Kāmārika Khaṇḍa); folk Mahābhārata traditions

title: Birth of Duhshasana from the flesh-ball
description: Duhshasana is born as the second of the hundred Kauravas, the second piece to ripen from Gandhari's divided ball of flesh

title: Birth of Irāvān to Arjuna and Ulūpī
description: During his exile Arjuna unites with the Nāga princess Ulūpī (daughter of Kauravya) beneath the Gaṅgā, begetting Irāvān, who is reared in the serpent-realm

title: Birth of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana on the island
description: Parāśara fathers Vyāsa on the fisher-maiden Satyavatī on a Yamunā island; he is born dark and island-born, matures instantly, and vows to come whenever remembered
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4

title: Birth of Kripa and Kripi from Sharadvat's seed
description: Sage Sharadvat's seed falls on shara-grass at the sight of the apsara Janapadi and splits into twin children, Kripa and Kripi

title: Birth of Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa
description: Vyasa is born on a river island to sage Parashara and Satyavati, dark-complexioned and regarded as a partial amsha incarnation of Vishnu

title: Birth of Kuru to Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī
description: Kuru is born to the Pauravā king Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī, daughter of Sūrya, grafting a solar strand onto the Lunar line
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (Caitraratha-parvan ~167–173); Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19

title: Birth of Pradyumna as Kāmadeva reborn
description: Rukmiṇī bears Kṛṣṇa's eldest son at Dwārakā, declared to be the god of love Kāma re-embodied after Śiva burnt him

title: Birth of Shishupala with three eyes and four arms
description: Shishupala, son of Damaghosha and Shrutashrava, is born deformed with an extra eye and two extra arms, his abandonment forbidden by an aerial voice

title: Birth of Vikarṇa among the hundred Kauravas
description: Vikarṇa, third son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī, ripens from the māṃsapeśī flesh-ball split by Vyāsa, born an aṃśa of the Paulastya rākṣasas

title: Birth of Vyasa
description: Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa is born on a Yamuna island to Parashara and Satyavati, a partial amsha of Vishnu

title: Birth of Yuyutsu from the vaishya serving-woman
description: Yuyutsu is born to Dhritarashtra by a vaishya serving-woman (Sughada/Sauvali) during Gandhari's failed two-year pregnancy, set apart from the hundred Kauravas by birth

title: Boon of Durvasa to Kunti
description: The sage Durvasa, pleased by Kunti's year of service, grants her a mantra to summon any deity and beget a child sharing his nature

title: Boyhood friendship with Droṇa and the half-kingdom vow
description: Young Drupada, schooled beside Droṇa at Bharadvāja's āśrama, vows to share half his future kingdom with him

title: Bride-price marriage of Mādrī to Pāṇḍu
description: Bhīṣma secures the Madra princess Mādrī as Pāṇḍu's second queen by paying the customary bride-price (śulka) to her people

title: Building of Indraprastha
description: Granted the wild tract Khāṇḍavaprastha, the Pāṇḍavas transform it into the splendid capital Indraprastha, its assembly-hall built by the asura architect Maya

title: Composition of the Bhagavata Purana
description: Narada finds Vyasa unsatisfied after dividing the Veda and composing the Mahabharata and prescribes singing Hari's lila, leading Vyasa to compose the Bhagavata Purana

title: Curse of Mahābhiṣa and Gaṅgā
description: King Mahābhiṣa and the goddess Gaṅgā exchange desire in Brahmā's court and are cursed to mortal birth, fixing Mahābhiṣa's rebirth as Śāntanu

title: Death of Shalya
description: On Day 18 Shalya rampages as fourth commander until Yudhishthira, fated to kill him, hurls a mantra-consecrated dart that pierces his chest, ending the Madra resistance

title: Departure for the Kamyaka forest and the Akshaya-patra
description: The exiles leave Hastinapura for the Kamyaka forest, and Surya grants Yudhishthira the inexhaustible vessel that yields unlimited food daily

title: Descent of portions (amshavatarana)
description: Devas and asuras incarnate on earth to relieve its burden, with key heroes declared portions of gods

title: Devāpi's birth as eldest son of Pratīpa
description: Devāpi is born firstborn of King Pratīpa of the Kuru line, ahead of brothers Bāhlīka and Śāntanu, making him rightful heir to Hastināpura
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sleeplessness and summons of Vidura
description: Tormented by foreboding of war over the Pāṇḍavas' kingdom, the blind king cannot sleep and summons Vidura, framing the Prajāgara discourse

title: Droṇa rejects Ekalavya
description: The Niṣāda prince Ekalavya approaches Droṇa for archery training and is refused on account of his low birth and Droṇa's vow that none would surpass Arjuna

title: Drona consecrated as Kaurava commander
description: On Bhishma's counsel Duryodhana installs Drona as commander-in-chief; Drona promises to capture Yudhishthira alive if Arjuna can be drawn away

title: Duryodhana consecrates Ashvatthaman as final commander
description: The three surviving Kaurava warriors reach the dying Duryodhana, who with his last strength consecrates Ashvatthaman as the final commander-in-chief

title: Earth appeals to the gods and Viṣṇu plucks two hairs
description: Oppressed by demonic kings, Earth appeals to the gods; Viṣṇu agrees to descend, and the plucking of a dark and a light hair becomes Krishna and Balarāma

title: Ekalavya Surrenders His Thumb
description: The Nishada prince Ekalavya learns archery before Drona's clay image and surrenders his right thumb as guru-dakshina

title: Entry into Kāmyaka-vana
description: The Pāṇḍavas leave Hāstinapura after the dice-game and settle first in Kāmyaka on the Sarasvatī's desert-edge, attended by Dhaumya and brahmins

title: Eternal Vrindavana rasa-lila (scriptural backdrop)
description: Krishna and the gopis dance the nightly rasa-lila in Vrindavana, held in tradition to continue eternally in the Nidhivana groves

title: Fire-birth of Dhṛṣṭadyumna
description: Born full-grown and armed from Drupada's putrakāmeṣṭi revenge-sacrifice, named by a sky-voice as the fated slayer of Droṇa

title: Gāndhārī's curse on Krishna
description: The bereaved Kuru queen Gāndhārī, having lost all hundred sons, curses Krishna that his Vrishni-Andhaka kinsmen will perish in fratricidal strife and he himself will die ignobly alone in the wilderness 36 years hence

title: Govardhana-dhāraṇa līlā
description: Boy Kṛṣṇa lifts Govardhana hill on his little finger for seven days to shelter Braj from Indra's deluge — the act the Nathdwārā icon eternally depicts

title: Indra and Agni test King Shibi (dove and hawk)
description: Indra as a hawk and Agni as a dove fall upon King Shibi, testing whether he will protect a refugee at any cost

title: Jarasandha's seventeen sieges of Mathura
description: Jarasandha of Magadha, Kamsa's father-in-law, besieges Mathura seventeen times to avenge Kamsa and is repelled each time, Krishna deliberately sparing him
source: Bhagavata Purana X.50; Vishnu Purana V.22; Harivamsha (Vishnu Parva)

title: Kṛṣṇa commissions Uddhava as envoy to Vraja
description: From Mathurā, Kṛṣṇa sends his cousin and minister Uddhava to console the grieving cowherds and gopīs of Vṛndāvana with a consoling message

title: Karna consecrated as third Kaurava commander
description: With Bhishma and Drona fallen, Duryodhana installs Karna as the third commander-in-chief; Karna vows to slay Arjuna or die and demands Shalya as a charioteer equal to Krishna

title: Kaṃsa dispatches the last wave of demons to Vraja
description: Forewarned the Vraja boy is his foretold killer, Kaṃsa sends his final relay of asuras — the bull Ariṣṭa and the horse Keśin — to Vṛndāvana
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.36–37; Harivaṃśa (Viṣṇu Parva); Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Kṛṣṇa slays Mura at the Prāgjyotiṣa moat-fortress
description: Kṛṣṇa, attacking Narakāsura's capital Prāgjyotiṣa/Kāmarūpa, first confronts and slays the thousand-armed (five/seven-headed) Dānava general Mura, who guards the moat-fortress with his many sons; Kṛṣṇa decapitates/destroys him with the Sudarśana chakra immediately before reaching Narakāsura. This slaying yields Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa's devotional epithets Murāri, Murahara, and Murabhid

title: King Vareṇya's question to Gajānana
description: Troubled by worldly sorrow and the problem of right action, King Vareṇya asks the Gajānana incarnation of Gaṇeśa for the highest knowledge, mirroring Arjuna's despondency

title: King Śveta's self-directed giving
description: A righteous, generous king performs every rite and gives lavishly but heaps all his gifts and feasts upon himself, never feeding guests or the needy

title: Kāliya's flight to the Yamunā
description: The nāga Kāliya, fleeing Garuḍa from Ramaṇaka Dvīpa, takes refuge in a Yamunā pool barred to Garuḍa by Saubhari's curse

title: Krishna curses Ashvatthama to deathless wandering
description: After the night-massacre and the Brahmastra aimed at Uttara's womb, Krishna revives Parikshit and curses Ashvatthama to wander 3,000 years suffering until Kali's end

title: Krishna Narrates the Vrikasura Tale
description: Krishna tells Yudhishthira the cautionary tale of Vrikasura after the Rajasuya/Ashvamedha sacrifices, answering why Shiva-worshippers gain wealth

title: Krishna's Flight West and Founding of Dvaraka
description: Harried repeatedly by Jarasandha and threatened by Kalayavana, Krishna abandons Mathura and leads the Yadava clans west to the sea-girt safety of Saurashtra, earning the epithet Ranchhod

title: Kṛtavarma's lineage as a Bhoja-Vṛṣṇi chief
description: Kṛtavarma, son of Hṛdika (hence Hārdikya), is a Bhoja-branch chief of the Vṛṣṇi/Yādava confederacy of Dvārakā and kinsman of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma

title: Kuntī adopted by Kuntibhoja
description: Śūrasena gives his firstborn daughter Pṛthā in adoption to his childless cousin Kuntibhoja, who renames her Kuntī and rears her

title: Maṇḍavya's impalement and his curse on Yama
description: Falsely accused, the silent ascetic Maṇḍavya is impaled but survives; learning his torment stemmed from a boyhood insect-piercing, he reforms cosmic law on the age of innocence and curses Yama to be born among men as a Śūdra

title: Markandeya tells the Ramopakhyana to console Yudhishthira
description: After Jayadratha's attempt to abduct Draupadi, the deathless sage Markandeya narrates the whole Rama story to console the humiliated Yudhishthira that even greater men suffered and recovered

title: Marriage and self-blindfolding
description: Gāndhārī of Gandhāra weds the blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra and binds her own eyes for life to share his darkness

title: Maya builds the illusory assembly hall
description: In gratitude, Maya raises a peerless hall of optical illusion at Indraprastha with materials from Lake Bindusaras

title: Mārkaṇḍeya narrates the Dharma-vyādha tale
description: During the forest exile Mārkaṇḍeya answers Yudhiṣṭhira on whether women and the low-born can be wise by telling the story of Kauśika and the butcher

title: Mudgala lives by uñchavṛtti at Kurukṣetra
description: The brāhmaṇa-sage Mudgala subsists only on gleaned fallen grain, owning nothing in reserve, sustaining a fortnightly iṣṭi sacrifice and his family

title: Mudgala's uñchavṛtti livelihood
description: The brāhmaṇa Mudgala of Kurukṣetra subsists solely by gleaning fallen grain, yet performs the new/full-moon Iṣṭi and feeds gods, ancestors and guests before himself

title: Naraka's tyranny and theft from heaven
description: Bhaumāsura plunders the worlds, stealing Aditi's earrings, Varuṇa's parasol and the Maṇi-parvata jewel-seat and imprisoning 16,100 royal women

title: Onset of autumn (śarad ṛtu-varṇana)
description: The rains cease and autumn clears the skies, waters and groves of Vṛndāvana, setting the stage for the flute-song

title: Pandavas choose Matsya for ajnata-vasa
description: As the 12 forest years close, the Pandavas decide to spend their 13th incognito year at King Virata's prosperous kingdom of Matsya

title: Pandavas take service at Virata's Matsya court
description: The five Pandavas and Draupadi pass their thirteenth incognito year disguised as servants in King Virata's prosperous, dharmic kingdom of Matsya

title: Piṅgalā's night of futile waiting
description: Piṅgalā, a courtesan of Mithilā, waits adorned at her door all night for a wealthy patron who never comes
actors: Piṅgalā (courtesan of Mithilā); the awaited wealthy lover

title: Pārijāta-haraṇa (Kṛṣṇa carries off the Pārijāta tree from Nandana)
description: To please his queen Satyabhāmā, Kṛṣṇa uproots the Pārijāta (coral/night-jasmine) wish-tree from Indra's celestial pleasure-grove Nandana in Amarāvatī and carries it to Dvārakā, defeating Indra who pursues to recover it

title: Pūtanā and the poison-breast (and her mokṣa)
description: The child-killing demoness sent by Kaṃsa suckles the infant Krishna with a poisoned breast and is drained of life, yet is granted liberation for coming in the form of a mother
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.6; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Pūtanā–Baka–Agha sibling triad
description: The Bhāgavata binds the demoness Pūtanā, the crane Bakāsura, and the python Aghāsura into one demon-family, motivating Aghāsura's revenge
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.6, X.11–12; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Raivataka festival & the abduction of Subhadrā
description: At the Vṛṣṇi-Andhaka spring festival on the Raivataka slopes, Arjuna abducts Subhadrā on Kṛṣṇa's counsel

title: Rukmī blocks the match and pledges Rukmiṇī to Śiśupāla
description: Rukmiṇī's arrogant brother Rukmī, hating Kṛṣṇa, vetoes the desired marriage and betroths her to Śiśupāla, ally of Jarāsandha
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.52; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu-parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.26

title: Sāmba is born of the Śaiva boon
description: Jāmbavatī bears Sāmba, the son "won from Śiva" through Upamanyu's initiation and Kṛṣṇa's tapas

title: Sāmba's capture and the dragging of Hastināpura
description: Sāmba abducts Duryodhana's daughter Lakṣmaṇā and is captured; Balarāma hooks his plough into Hastināpura's ramparts and drags the city toward the Gaṅgā until the Kurus release the couple

title: Sañjaya as Dhṛtarāṣṭra's court sūta and truth-teller
description: The sūta Sañjaya Gāvalgaṇi serves as the blind king's charioteer-bard, minister, and confidant, openly blaming Dhṛtarāṣṭra's partiality and Duryodhana's greed for the coming war

title: Sanjaya granted divine sight
description: Vyasa grants the charioteer-bard Sanjaya the eye of the gods (divya-drishti) so he can narrate the entire war to the blind king Dhritarashtra

title: Sāmba's curse and leprosy
description: Sāmba, Kṛṣṇa's son by Jāmbavatī, is cursed (via Nārada's contrivance) and afflicted with leprosy

title: Sāmba's leprosy and cure by Sūrya
description: Sāmba, son of Kṛṣṇa, is cursed with leprosy (by Durvāsā or Nārada), performs a twelve-year penance to Sūrya, recovers a Sun-image from the Candrabhāgā river, installs it, and is healed
source: Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (Brahma Parva); Sāmba Purāṇa; Varāha Purāṇa

title: Śaṅkhacūḍa the guhyaka scatters the gopīs
description: a wealthy Yakṣa follower of Kubera, drunk on pride, drives the women of Vraja away northward before the eyes of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma

title: Satyabhāmā's former birth as Guṇavatī
description: at Dvārakā Kṛṣṇa reveals that his queen won him as husband by the merit of a flawless Kārtika-vrata kept in an earlier life as the poor brāhmaṇa girl Guṇavatī
source: Padma P., Uttara-khaṇḍa; Skanda P., Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya

title: Satyabhāmā's Puṇyaka-vrata
description: to keep Kṛṣṇa across lifetimes Satyabhāmā performs the Pārijāta-requiring vow, formally gifting Kṛṣṇa away to Nārada and then redeeming him by his weight in gold and gems

title: Sātyaki beheads the fasting Bhūriśravas
description: After Arjuna's arrow severs Bhūriśravas's sword-arm mid-duel, Sātyaki beheads the disarmed warrior seated in prāya, a breach of the war-code both armies condemn

title: Sātyaki dies in the Mausala fratricide at Prabhāsa
description: Taunting Kṛtavarma over the Sauptika massacre, Sātyaki beheads him and is then killed by the Bhoja-Andhaka mob with Pradyumna at his side, igniting the Yādava self-slaughter
source: Mahābhārata, Mausala Parva 3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa XI.30

title: Sātyaki kills Śalva and spares Sañjaya
description: In the final rout Sātyaki slays the mleccha king Śalva and captures Sañjaya, releasing him at Vyāsa's intervention so the epic's eyewitness survives

title: Sātyaki named among the seven Pāṇḍava marshals
description: Yudhiṣṭhira appoints seven leaders over the seven Pāṇḍava akṣauhiṇīs, Sātyaki among them, while his kinsman Kṛtavarma leads Yādavas for the Kauravas

title: Sātyaki rebuts Balarāma's peace counsel
description: At the Upaplavya war-council Sātyaki angrily answers Balarāma's conciliatory speech, declaring war the only reply to the dice-hall outrage

title: Sātyaki serves at the Rājasūya
description: The Vṛṣṇi chief Sātyaki attends Yudhiṣṭhira's imperial consecration at Indraprastha and holds the royal umbrella in the coronation rites

title: Sātyaki survives the Sauptika night
description: Away from the camp with the Pāṇḍavas and Kṛṣṇa during Aśvatthāman's night-massacre, Sātyaki stands among the seven survivors of the Pāṇḍava side

title: Sātyaki's Day-14 drive through Droṇa's array
description: Sent by Yudhiṣṭhira on Arjuna's trail, Sātyaki circumvents Droṇa, defeats Kṛtavarma and Duryodhana, and kills Jalasandha and Sudarśana, one of only three cars to cross the Kaurava host

title: Satyavatī bears Vyāsa, fulfilling the Pitṛs' promise
description: By the sage Parāśara the reborn river-maiden bears the island-born Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, divider of the Veda — the redemption clause of her sentence

title: Satyavatī weds Śāntanu and bears Citrāṅgada and Vicitravīrya
description: The final terms of the decree play out as the Pitṛ-daughter becomes Kuru queen and mother of the doomed heirs whose deaths force the niyoga

title: Śiva and Pārvatī feed the cursing sage
description: disguised as householders, Pārvatī (Annapūrṇā/Viśālākṣī) and Śiva feast Vyāsa and his disciples lavishly, then expose the hypocrisy of a dharma-teacher who curses over food

title: Śiva and Umā grant Kṛṣṇa sixteen boons
description: After months of the vow Śiva appears with Umā and grants eight boons each, including the promised son

title: Slaying of Dhenuka and Pralamba
description: the boy Balarāma kills the ass-demon of Tālavana and fist-smashes the disguised cowherd-demon Pralamba

title: Slaying of Vajranābha
description: revived from a club-blow by the blast of Kṛṣṇa's Pāñcajanya, Pradyumna beheads Vajranābha with Kṛṣṇa's discus; Gada slays Sunābha and Nikumbha flees to Ṣaṭpura

title: Somaka refuses heaven without his priest
description: dying, Somaka learns his chaplain burns in hell for Jantu's killing and demands to share or wholly assume the punishment, overriding Yama's law that each soul reaps its own deed alone

title: Somaka's hundred wives and single son
description: the Pāñcāla king Somaka, long childless despite a hundred queens of equal rank, at last begets in old age one frail son, Jantu, on whom every mother's whole hope hangs

title: Sudakṣiṇa's abhicāra against Dwārakā
description: the Kāśī prince Sudakṣiṇa wins a conditional boon from Śiva at Avimukta and raises the Dakṣiṇāgni as a blazing kṛtyā fire-demon that marches on Dwārakā

title: Sudarśana freed by Kṛṣṇa's touch
description: Kṛṣṇa touches the python with his foot, and it sheds its reptile body to rise as the radiant vidyādhara Sudarśana, cursed into a snake by the Āṅgirasa sages for mocking them in pride

title: Śuka critiques prāyaścitta as incomplete
description: asked by Parīkṣit how to escape the narakas, Śukadeva gives the orthodox answer of penance, then judges it partial — like an elephant that bathes and again throws dust — for it removes the act but not the sinful propensity

title: Śuka sent to Janaka's court
description: Vyāsa sends his born-perfect son Śuka to king Janaka as final examiner of his liberation-knowledge; Janaka confirms renunciation is knowledge, not costume

title: Śuka's flight — bodiless liberation
description: Śuka rises by yoga through the parting peaks of Himavat and merges into all creation; the grieving Vyāsa calls "O Śuka!" and the whole world echoes back in his son's voice, Śiva consoling him with a shadow-Śuka
source: Mahābhārata XII, Mokṣadharma, close of the Śuka-carita

title: Sulabhā tests Janaka's liberation
description: The mendicant yoginī Sulabhā enters king Janaka Dharmadhvaja's mind by yoga-power; his gendered rebuke proves he still identifies with body and office, and she teaches that the ātman is not gendered

title: Sūrya gives the Syamantaka to Satrājit
description: The sun-god rewards his votary Satrājit with the radiant Syamantaka jewel that yields gold daily and wards off calamity

title: Sudama and Krishna at Sandipani's gurukula
description: The poor brahmin Sudama (Kuchela) and Krishna study together under guru Sandipani at Avanti, forming a boyhood friendship

title: Sudāmā's poverty and the wife's urging
description: The poor brāhmaṇa Sudāmā, boyhood schoolmate of Kṛṣṇa, is urged by his starving wife to seek aid from his now-royal friend at Dvārakā

title: Sweetness of the Braj *līlā*
description: The hymn's subject: the flute-playing cowherd Kṛṣṇa of Vṛndāvana — his lips, smile, gait, *veṇu*, the Yamunā, gopīs and cows — each contemplated as *madhuram*

title: The ant-bite that shamed a kingdom
description: an ant stings Jantu on the hip and all hundred queens spring up wailing at once, an uproar that convinces Somaka one son among a hundred women is a curse, not a blessing

title: The aṣṭamī–caturdaśī concession
description: Pārvatī intercedes and wins Vyāsa leave to enter Kāśī only on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, after which he settles on the east Gaṅgā bank south-east of Lolārka

title: The battle of Ṣaṭpura (Six-Cities)
description: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, and Pradyumna storm the dānava stronghold; Nikumbha's māyā multiplies him into thousands, fells Pradyumna, and bears Arjuna skyward

title: The Bhāṇḍīravana wedding
description: Kṛṣṇa weds Rādhā in the Bhāṇḍīra forest with Brahmā himself officiating, making the pair an eternally wedded divine couple

title: The Brahma-hrada vision of Vaikuṇṭha
description: reading their hearts, Krishna dips the cowherds in the Brahma-hrada of the Yamunā and lifts them up to behold the effulgent abode beyond material darkness, where he is praised by the personified Vedas

title: The Brāhmaṇa's araṇi stolen by a deer
description: As the exile nears its end a deer bounds off with a Brāhmaṇa's fire-churning sticks, robbing him of his agni-hotra and setting the Yakṣa-praśna in motion

title: The brāhmaṇas repent their ritual pride
description: shamed by their wives' example, the sacrificers curse their own birth, learning and ritual expertise as worthless without devotion, yet dare not approach Krishna for fear of Kaṃsa

title: The Brahmaśiras aimed at Uttarā's womb
description: Unable to recall the Brahmaśiras he launched on a blade of grass against Arjuna's counter-weapon, Aśvatthāman redirects it into the wombs of the Pāṇḍava women to end the line

title: The court-parables fail and the embassy collapses
description: despite Paraśurāma's tale, Kaṇva's Mātali story, and Nārada's Gālava story, Duryodhana refuses to yield and the war the tales were told to avert follows

title: The crest-jewel to Balarāma
description: Kṛṣṇa overtakes the fleeing Yakṣa, strikes off his head with a fist-blow, and gives the shining crest-jewel from his head to his elder brother Balarāma

title: The crocodile-tīrthas of the southern sea (epic original)
description: in the Mahābhārata's Ādi Parva Arjuna frees the apsarās Vargā, Saurabheyī, Samīcī, Budbudā and Latā at five southern-ocean tīrthas — the tale the Purāṇa relocates to the Gulf of Khambhāt

title: The curse of Kindama
description: Pāṇḍu shoots a mating pair of deer who are the sage Kindama and his wife; the dying sage curses him to die the moment he approaches a wife in desire

title: The descent to Sutala and Bali's worship
description: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma pass by yoga-māyā into the netherworld Sutala, where Bali Mahārāja worships them as the Soul of the universe and yields the six infants held in his keeping

title: The dice-game assents
description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra overrides Vidura to authorize Śakuni's rigged game, grants Draupadī's boons after evil omens, then permits the second exile-stake throw

title: The digging of Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa
description: Kṛṣṇa digs a pond in atonement for slaying the bull-demon Ariṣṭāsura and Rādhā with her sakhīs digs its twin, creating the holiest Gauḍīya tīrtha near Govardhana

title: The divine-father decision
description: Kuntī reveals Durvāsā's invocation-mantra and at Pāṇḍu's direction bears Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma and Arjuna of Dharma, Vāyu and Indra, then lends one use to Mādrī for the Aśvin twins

title: The Durvāsā-mantra resolution
description: unable to father sons himself, Pāṇḍu is freed of the deadlock when Kuntī discloses the deva-invoking mantra, leading to the divine births of Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma and Arjuna

title: The elephant-lie breaks Droṇa
description: Bhīma slays an elephant named Aśvatthāman and Yudhiṣṭhira's half-truth convinces Droṇa his son is dead, leading to his beheading in yoga by Dhṛṣṭadyumna

title: The embassy of the false Vāsudeva
description: Pauṇḍraka of Karūṣa, decked in counterfeit conch, discus, Śrīvatsa and Garuḍa banner, sends an envoy to Dwārakā demanding Kṛṣṇa renounce the name and emblems of Vāsudeva; Ugrasena's assembly laughs and Kṛṣṇa promises to 'release the emblem' upon him

title: The final parting of Vraja and Dvārakā
description: after the sacrifice Nanda stays some months, then returns with the Vraja folk to Vṛndāvana while the Vṛṣṇis go back to Dvārakā, never to meet again

title: The flowers fall in Rukmiṇī's yard
description: planted at Satyabhāmā's door, the Pārijāta lets its blossoms drift into Rukmiṇī's courtyard, a sign that quiet devotion outdraws proud possession
source: popular Vaiṣṇava retelling; cf. Bhāgavata X.59

title: The forest picnic after Aghasura
description: Krishna, Balarama and the cowherd boys take their lunch into the forest the morning after Aghasura's death; the calves stray and Krishna goes to fetch them

title: The gem surrendered and Kṛṣṇa's 3,000-year curse
description: Aśvatthāman's forehead-gem is cut away leaving an unhealing wound, and Kṛṣṇa curses him to wander deathless for 3,000 years, diseased and shunned, while vowing the struck embryo shall live as Parīkṣit

title: The gopīs' Kātyāyanī month-vrata
description: through Hemanta's first month (Mārgaśīrṣa) the maidens of Vraja bathe at dawn in the Yamunā and worship Kātyāyanī to win Kṛṣṇa

title: The haṃsa embassy to Vajrapura
description: Indra's celestial swans enter the sealed city; the she-swan Śucimukhī kindles Prabhāvatī's love for the unseen Pradyumna and baits Vajranābha with tales of a wonder-working actor

title: The hundred sons and the golden-marked eldest
description: every queen conceives and bears a son, and Jantu returns as the firstborn to his own mother Kausalyā, known by the golden mark on his left side foretold by the priest

title: The impostor's liberation by meditation
description: because Pauṇḍraka had constantly meditated on the Lord's form by wearing His emblems, his bonds are cut and he attains absorption in Kṛṣṇa, glossed by commentators as sārūpya/sāyujya mukti

title: The interrupted Indra-yajña and Kṛṣṇa's argument
description: Kṛṣṇa questions Nanda's annual Indra-sacrifice and argues for worshipping Govardhana, the cows and brāhmaṇas instead, on karma/svadharma grounds
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.24; Harivaṃśa (Viṣṇu Parva); Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 5

title: The iron statue of Bhima
description: Intending to crush Bhima in revenge for Duryodhana, the blind Dhritarashtra is given an iron effigy by Krishna; he crushes it to powder and weeps with remorse before learning of the substitution

title: The iron-Bhīma embrace
description: Kṛṣṇa substitutes Duryodhana's practice statue for Bhīma, and the grieving king crushes it to pieces before accepting the Pāṇḍavas

title: The Janaka householder-test
description: sent on foot to Mithilā to settle whether the āśramas are mandatory, Śuka stays equanimous through neglect at the gates and through offered luxuries, and Janaka declares him already free by knowledge
source: Mahābhārata XII, Mokṣadharma; Yoga Vāsiṣṭha, Vairāgya Prakaraṇa variant

title: The Kurukṣetra eclipse pilgrimage
description: a great solar eclipse draws the Vṛṣṇis from Dvārakā and the Vraja folk from Vṛndāvana to Samanta-pañcaka to bathe at the sacred field

title: The māyā-beheading of 'Vasudeva'
description: in the sea-battle Śālva's illusion shows Kṛṣṇa his father seized and beheaded; Kṛṣṇa grieves a moment, then pierces the deceit

title: The milk of liberation
description: restored to Dvārakā, the six infants sip Devakī's breast-milk — remnant of Kṛṣṇa's own touch — regain their divine forms, and ascend liberated to the abode of the gods, closing the infanticide arc

title: The Mudal Āḻvārs at Tirukkōvilūr
description: three lotus-born saints crowd a narrow storm-porch (one lies, two sit, three stand) and feel Viṣṇu jostle in as an unseen fourth, sparking the three Tiruvandhādhis

title: The musala-curse at Piṇḍāraka
description: At the Saurāṣṭra coastal tīrtha of Piṇḍāraka near Dvārakā, the sages Viśvāmitra, Kaṇva and Nārada, mocked by Yādava youths who disguised Sāmba as a pregnant woman, curse that Sāmba will bear an iron pestle (musala) that will annihilate the Vṛṣṇi–Andhaka race — the trigger of the Yādava self-slaughter and Kṛṣṇa's departure at the Dvāpara–Kali hinge

title: The Nārāyaṇāstra unleashed and neutralised
description: After Droṇa's death Aśvatthāman releases the once-only Nārāyaṇāstra, which Kṛṣṇa defeats by ordering the whole army to lay down arms and offer no resistance

title: The pīṣṭodaka humiliation
description: The boy Aśvatthāman drinks rice-flour water believing it milk, and the shame drives Droṇa to seek patronage at the Kuru court

title: The priest prescribes the sacrifice of Jantu
description: Somaka's ṛtvij reveals a rite by which, if Jantu is offered in the fire and the queens inhale the smoke of his burning fat, each will bear a son and Jantu be reborn eldest with a golden mark

title: The python at Ambikāvana
description: on the Vraja pilgrimage to worship Śiva by the Sarasvatī, a hungry python seizes the sleeping Nanda and begins to swallow him, unmoved by the cowherds' firebrands

title: The Raivataka festival and abduction of Subhadrā
description: On the Raivataka (Girnar) festival slopes beside Dvārakā, Arjuna abducts Kṛṣṇa's sister Subhadrā on Kṛṣṇa's counsel

title: The ritualists refuse the hungry boys
description: engrossed in ritual scruple and contemptuous of a request made in a cowherd's name, the sacrificing brāhmaṇas give no food and no answer, and the Bhāgavata condemns their devotionless learning

title: The sages' tīrtha discourse at Kurukṣetra
description: before Vyāsa, Nārada and a great company of ṛṣis, Kṛṣṇa teaches that the living sādhu, not clay or water, is the true place of pilgrimage

title: The salt-tribute embassy
description: the brothers send Janārdana to demand tribute and salt from Kṛṣṇa for Brahmadatta's Rājasūya; Kṛṣṇa's laughing refusal in the Sudharmā hall makes war inevitable

title: The secret breaks; night battle in Vajrapura
description: the wonder-born sons of the hidden marriages are spotted, Vajranābha orders their seizure, and Prabhāvatī herself arms Pradyumna for the night-long fight

title: The shared term of hell, then heaven together
description: Yama grants Somaka the measured term of Naraka needed to exhaust the priest's demerit, after which king and priest ascend to the higher worlds together

title: The Sixteen Kings and the revival
description: Nārada consoles the grieving Sṛñjaya with the deaths of sixteen supreme emperors of old, then, exceeding his own lesson, restores the slain Suvarṇaṣṭhīvin to a full span of life
source: Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva ch. ~31; Ganguli XXXI

title: The Śruti-gīta (Veda-stuti)
description: Answering how the Vedas can indicate the nirguṇa Brahman, Śuka relays Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi's account of the personified śrutis hymning the Lord at the dawn of creation

title: The Sudarśana burns Kāśī
description: Kṛṣṇa dispatches the Sudarśana cakra from his dice-game; the repelled kṛtyā rebounds to consume Sudakṣiṇa and his priests, and the pursuing discus incinerates the whole city of Vārāṇasī before returning to Kṛṣṇa's side

title: The twins in disguise at Virāṭa's court
description: For the incognito thirteenth year Nakula serves as Granthika the horse-keeper and Sahadeva as Tantipāla the superintendent of cattle

title: The twins' vows after the dice-fraud
description: Amid the dice-hall vows Sahadeva swears to slay Śakuni, architect of the crooked game, and Nakula vows to slay the partisan sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra

title: The Vasus Steal Nandini and Are Cursed
description: The eight Vasus steal the wish-cow Nandini from Vasishtha, who curses them to be born as mortals, with the chief offender Dyaus to live a full long human life

title: The Vidura-nīti night
description: the sleepless king summons Vidura for an all-night discourse on dharma and statecraft, praises it, and follows none of it

title: The Vrishni widows enter the fire
description: After the clan's destruction, Vasudeva's four wives Devakī, Rohiṇī, Bhadrā and Madirā mount his pyre, and several of Krishna's and Balarāma's wives follow at the great cremations while Satyabhāmā retires to the forest

title: The Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas annihilate one another at Prabhāsa
description: Doubly cursed by Gāndhārī and the sages of Piṇḍāraka, the drunken clans seize the iron-turning erakā reeds and slaughter each other, Sātyaki beheading Kṛtavarmā over the Sauptika massacre
source: Mahābhārata Mausala Parva 1-4; Bhāgavata XI.30; Viṣṇu Purāṇa V.37

title: The Vyadha-gita: the righteous butcher teaches Kaushika
description: A proud brahmana is humbled by a housewife and a righteous butcher who teaches that liberation lies in honestly doing one's appointed work

title: The Vyāsa–Śuka anupraśna
description: Śuka questions his father on the highest good and Vyāsa teaches the path to Brahman, the Śānti Parva's central renunciation-cycle

title: The war-council at Upaplavya
description: With the exile fulfilled, the allied kings assemble; Krishna declares the Pandavas want their rightful kingdom and that an envoy should be sent, while Balarama counsels moderation and Satyaki force

title: The wife delivered in meditation
description: one wife, held back in the house by her husband, absorbs herself wholly in Krishna, sheds her body of the three guṇas and attains him directly without ever seeing him

title: The wives defy their menfolk to carry the feast
description: hearing Krishna's name, the brāhmaṇa wives seize the four kinds of food and rush to him like rivers to the sea, disobeying husbands, fathers, brothers and kin who forbid them

title: The Yādava migration to Dvārakā
description: Under Jarāsandha's seventeen sieges and Kālayavana's advance, Kṛṣṇa evacuates the Vṛṣṇi-Andhaka-Bhoja federation from Mathurā to the new sea-fort of Dvārakā in Saurāṣṭra
source: Bhāgavata X.50-52; Viṣṇu Purāṇa V.22-23; Harivaṃśa

title: The Yādava sea-excursion to Piṇḍāraka
description: Kṛṣṇa leads the clan from Dvārakā on a pleasure voyage of sweetened seas, water-sports, and the celestial Chālikya song near Raivataka

title: The Yādavas infiltrate Vajrapura as actors
description: Pradyumna, Sāmba and Gada enter the demon city with Bhadra's troupe and stage a Rāmāyaṇa play and the Rambhābhisāra — among the earliest theatre-within-story scenes in Sanskrit

title: Three handfuls of sand become the Tridevī
description: each day Vyāsa moulds three fistfuls of Godāvarī sand that take form as Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī and Mahākālī

title: Ulūpī abducts Arjuna into the Gaṅgā
description: During Arjuna's twelve-year tīrtha-exile, the Nāga princess Ulūpī draws the bathing Arjuna down beneath the Gaṅgā into her father Kauravya's serpent-palace

title: Umpire of the mace-duel
description: returning from pilgrimage, Balarāma referees the Bhīma–Duryodhana duel of his two pupils and raises his plough in fury at the illegal thigh-blow before Kṛṣṇa restrains him

title: Upamanyu initiates Kṛṣṇa into the Pāśupata vow
description: The sage gives Kṛṣṇa dīkṣā into the pāśupata-vrata with ash and mantra and directs his austerity
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Umā-saṃhitā 1–4; Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva

title: Upamanyu teaches Kṛṣṇa Śiva-tattva
description: The Kṛṣṇa–Upamanyu dialogues expound Pāśupata doctrine and Śiva's greatness, framing the Umā- and Vāyavīya-saṃhitās

title: Upanayana of Krishna and Balarama
description: After Kamsa's death the brothers receive the sacred thread from the priest Garga, entering brahmacarya

title: Uprooting of the Pārijāta
description: Kṛṣṇa uproots the celestial coral-tree from Indra's Nandana grove over the protest of Śacī, to plant it in Satyabhāmā's Dwārakā courtyard

title: Urvaśī's curse converted to asset
description: her curse of eunuch-hood on Arjuna is capped by Indra at one chosen year, becoming the Bṛhannaḍā disguise at Virāṭa

title: Uttaṅka's quest for the celestial earrings
description: The disciple Uttaṅka journeys to fetch a queen's earrings as guru-fee, swallowing dung that is secretly amṛta and surviving a curse-duel

title: Uttanka's guru-fee demand for the celestial earrings
description: After completing his studies Uttanka is set the impossible gurudakshina of fetching the queen's celestial earrings within a fixed time

title: Vajra, the last Yādava, crowned
description: after the Yādavas destroy themselves at Prabhāsa and Kṛṣṇa departs, Arjuna installs Kṛṣṇa's great-grandson Vajra (Pradyumna → Aniruddha → Vajra) as king, the sole heir of the ruined clan

title: Vajranābha's boon and the sealed city Vajrapura
description: the dānava wins from Brahmā an impregnable city that not even the wind may enter unbidden, then claims Indra's three worlds

title: Varuṇa worships the cowherd boy
description: the lokapāla of the waters, overwhelmed with joy, worships Krishna as the Supreme Person, apologizes for his ignorant servant, and returns Nanda

title: Vasiṣṭha foretells Kṛṣṇa's teaching of Arjuna
description: Within the Tretā-frame discourse Vasiṣṭha prophesies that in Dvāpara Viṣṇu will descend as Kṛṣṇa and give Arjuna the non-dual battlefield teaching, in verses echoing the Bhagavad-Gītā [late text]

title: Vasu's tapas and Indra's intervention
description: The devout Cedi king Vasu Uparicara performs severe tapas; Indra, fearing rivalry, lures him back to kingship with gifts

title: Śvetaki's twelve-year sacrifice and Agni's indigestion
description: King Śvetaki's unbroken sacrifice gorges Agni on ghee until the fire-god grows sick and dyspeptic

title: Vasudeva and Devakī inherit the icon; Kṛṣṇa's four-armed birth-vision
description: the image passes to the Yadu couple, and the newborn Kṛṣṇa reveals the four-armed form the mūrti depicts

title: Vasudeva's great sacrifice
description: confessing bondage despite fathering the Lord, Vasudeva asks the sages the means of release and is led by Nārada through a mahā-yajña on the eclipse-field

title: Veṇu-gītā (Song of the Flute)
description: The gopīs rapturously describe Kṛṣṇa's flute-playing as the autumn season opens, the lyric overture that kindles desire for the rāsa

title: Vidura summons Sanatsujata to teach Dhritarashtra
description: On the war's eve the sleepless Dhritarashtra asks for higher wisdom; Vidura, pleading his shudra birth, meditates upon and summons the deathless sage Sanatsujata to teach in his stead

title: Vishvamitra's penance broken by Menaka
description: Fearing Vishvamitra's severe tapas, Indra sends the apsara Menaka, who with Vayu and Kamadeva breaks the sage's penance, and he unites with her

title: Viṣṇu concedes Śiva's supremacy
description: Viṣṇu appears secretly, tells the humbled Vyāsa that Śiva is supreme, restores his speech, and Vyāsa sings the Vyāsāṣṭaka and installs the Vyāseśvara liṅga

title: Viṣṇu dispatches Yoganidrā/Yogamāyā
description: Viṣṇu sends his sleep-power Yogamāyā to transfer Balarāma to Rohiṇī and be born to Yaśodā as the substitute for the infant Kṛṣṇa

title: Viśvakarmā fashions the bāla-Kṛṣṇa icon for Rukmiṇī
description: The Udupi churning-child Kṛṣṇa mūrti is made by the cosmic craftsman Viśvakarmā and worshipped by Rukmiṇī at Dvārakā in Kṛṣṇa's own lifetime

title: Vraja meets Dvārakā
description: Vasudeva and Nanda embrace, Devakī and Rohiṇī weep with Yaśodā, and Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma bow to their foster-parents in the one reunion of his two worlds

title: Vṛkāsura wins the incinerate-by-touch boon from Śiva
description: After a flesh-offering penance at Kedāra, the asura Vṛka extracts a death-by-touch boon and turns it on Śiva, who flees to Vaikuṇṭha

title: Vāraṇāvata escape into the forest
description: The Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī flee the burning lac-house and halt exhausted in the rākṣasa-haunted forest where Bhīma keeps watch

title: Vyāsa banished from Kāśī as a Rudra-piśāca
description: declared unworthy to dwell in the city, Vyāsa is expelled from the kṣetra by the householder-Śiva

title: Vyasa Divides the Veda into Four
description: Krishna-Dvaipayana Veda-Vyasa, the 28th and current Vyasa, splits the single Veda into Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva and teaches them to four pupils, also authoring the Mahabharata
actors: Krishna-Dvaipayana Vyasa; Paila; Vaishampayana; Jaimini; Sumantu
source: Vishnu Purana 3.3-3.4; Bhagavata Purana 1.4; Mahabharata Adi Parva

title: Vyāsa and Kṛṣṇa prescribe the Aśvamedha to console Yudhiṣṭhira
description: Yudhiṣṭhira sinks back into grief over the slain kinsmen; Vyāsa and Kṛṣṇa console him and prescribe the horse-sacrifice as expiation and a seal of universal sovereignty

title: Vyāsa institutes the Nirjalā (Bhīmasenī) Ekādaśī
description: unable to fast twice a month, Bhīma is prescribed a single absolute waterless fast whose merit equals all 24 Ekādaśīs of the year

title: Vyāsa narrates the Devī Bhāgavata to Janamejaya
description: Vyāsa instructs King Janamejaya in the Goddess's Bhāgavata at the Naimiṣa assembly so the listener may attain mukti through Goddess-devotion

title: Vyāsa's arm paralysed at Jñānavāpī
description: proclaiming Viṣṇu's supremacy in Śiva's own city, Vyāsa raises his hand to swear the point and Nandin freezes it "playfully"

title: Vyāsa's curse on Kāśī rebounds
description: enraged, Vyāsa curses the city to lose learning, wealth, and liberation for three generations, but the eternal Avimukta kṣetra cannot be bound and the curse recoils on him

title: Vyāsa's southward sojourn after Kurukṣetra
description: grieved by the war's carnage, the Veda-arranger wanders down the Deccan seeking peace and settles to do tapas on the Godāvarī at the future Basara

title: Vyāsa's tīrthas and cave on the Godāvarī
description: the sage's penance seats the aṣṭa-tīrtha bathing-fords and the Vyāsa-guṇḍam cave-shrine around Basara

title: Vyāsapurī → Vāsara → Basara
description: the town takes its name from Vyāsa's stay, worn down to Vāsara and softened to Basara under Marāṭhī v→b speech

title: Vyoma steals the sheep-boys
description: in the boys' game of thieves and shepherds, Vyoma the son of the asura Maya, disguised as a cowherd, carries off most of the boys playing sheep and seals them in a mountain cave

title: Vyomāsura crushed at the cave
description: Kṛṣṇa detects the magician-thief, seizes him as a lion seizes a jackal, crushes him despite his mountain-sized form, and breaks open the cave to free the trapped boys

title: Womb-transfer of Saṅkarṣaṇa
description: Yogamāyā draws Devakī's seventh embryo to Rohiṇī's womb in Gokula, and Balarāma is born as Rauhiṇeya

title: Yadavas destroy themselves at Prabhasa
description: Cursed by the brahmanas and maddened by drink, the Yadavas slaughter one another at Prabhasa as Krishna's avatara nears its end

title: Yoga-māyā transfers the six to Devakī's womb
description: Viṣṇu's deluding potency carries the six cursed souls into Devakī's womb to be born one by one in Mathurā's prison

title: Yudhiṣṭhira approaches the dying Bhīṣma
description: After Kurukṣetra, the grief-struck new king approaches Bhīṣma on his bed of arrows for instruction on dharma and liberation

title: Yudhiṣṭhira asks Bhīṣma for the thousand names of Śiva
description: Having heard the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma, Yudhiṣṭhira requests the thousand names of Mahādeva/Śiva

title: Yudhiṣṭhira chooses Nakula at the Yakṣa's lake
description: Offered one dead brother back after answering the Yakṣa's questions, Yudhiṣṭhira revives Nakula so that Mādrī's line, like Kuntī's, keeps a living son, and Dharma restores all four

title: Yudhiṣṭhira resolves to renounce the kingdom
description: Sickened by the slaughter of kin and elders, Yudhiṣṭhira declares the kingdom worthless and resolves to abandon it for the forest as an ascetic

title: Abhimanyu Learns the Cakravyuha in the Womb
description: While in Subhadra's womb Abhimanyu overhears Arjuna narrate how to penetrate the cakravyuha but not how to exit it, as Subhadra falls asleep mid-telling

title: Śakaṭāsura the cart-demon
description: A demon enters a heavy handcart to crush the babe, who overturns and smashes it with a kick of his tiny foot
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.7; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Akrūra's vision in the Yamunā
description: Bathing en route, Akrūra sees Krishna and Balarāma within the river as Viṣṇu on Śeṣa, confirming their divinity

title: Śambara abducts the infant and casts him into the sea
description: The asura Śambara, fated to die by Pradyumna, steals the ten-day-old child and flings him into the ocean, where a fish swallows him

title: Ambā released to wed Śālva
description: Ambā confesses she had chosen Śālva; Bhīṣma honorably releases her to her beloved while her sisters wed Vicitravīrya

title: Arjuna and Duryodhana seek Krishna's aid
description: Both go to Dvaraka; Krishna offers either himself unarmed or his Narayani army; Arjuna chooses Krishna (who becomes his charioteer and vows to bear no weapon), Duryodhana takes the army

title: Arjuna and the Eye of the Bird
description: In Drona's archery test only Arjuna sees nothing but the wooden bird's eye, and Drona declares his one-pointedness the mark of a master

title: Arjuna Defeats Chitraratha (Aṅgāraparṇa)
description: The gandharva-king Chitraratha challenges the Pāṇḍavas at the Gaṅgā; Arjuna burns his chariot with the Āgneyāstra and, sparing him, exchanges weapons and receives the Cākṣuṣī-mantra

title: Aśvamedha horse reaches Manipura
