description: Yudhishthira's sacrificial horse, guarded by Arjuna, enters Manipura, where King Babhruvahana greets his father with homage rather than battle

title: Bhīṣma defers and Kṛṣṇa recites the Śiva Sahasranāma
description: The dying Bhīṣma declines to expound Śiva's names himself and names Kṛṣṇa as the fit reciter, who then recites them

title: Bhīṣma resumes teaching the still-grieving Yudhiṣṭhira
description: Despite all of the Śānti Parva, Yudhiṣṭhira remains crushed by guilt, so Bhīṣma resumes his deathbed teaching on dāna-dharma, fate and effort

title: Birth and abandonment of Shakuntala
description: A daughter is born to Menaka on the Malini river and abandoned; sheltered by shakunta birds, she is found and adopted by sage Kanva, who names her Shakuntala

title: Birth of Vidura by niyoga
description: When Ambikā sends her handmaid in her place, Vyāsa begets upon the gracious maid the supremely wise Vidura, born of a Śūdra-status mother and barred from the throne — the incarnation of Dharma fulfilling Maṇḍavya's curse

title: Boyhood warnings against Duryodhana's plots
description: As the one righteous Kaurava insider, Yuyutsu (in retelling tradition) alerts the Pandavas/Vidura to Duryodhana's schemes against Bhima, including the poisoning at Pramanakoti

title: Brahma asks Krishna to return to his abode
description: Brahma with the gods comes to Dvaraka and asks Krishna to return home; Krishna consents and turns to settle his devotees

title: Brahma's curiosity and test
description: Astonished by the slaying of Aghasura, Brahma resolves to test Krishna's divinity

title: Brahmā prescribes the burning of Khāṇḍava
description: Brahmā tells Agni he must consume the Khāṇḍava forest to cure his digestion, but only with Nara-Nārāyaṇa's aid

title: Charvaka the rakshasa reviles Yudhishthira
description: A rakshasa disguised as a brahmin named Charvaka denounces Yudhishthira after the Kurukshetra war and is destroyed by the assembled brahmins

title: Conception of Droṇa from Bharadvāja and Ghṛtācī
description: At the Gaṅgā the sage Bharadvāja sees Ghṛtācī; a breeze disrobes her, his seed escapes, and he catches it in a wooden trough (droṇa) from which the ayonija boy Droṇa develops, making Ghṛtācī ancestress of the weapons-master line

title: Consecration of Citrāṅgada
description: On Śāntanu's death, Bhīṣma installs the young Citrāṅgada as king of Hastināpura while acting as protecting elder

title: Disqualification by skin-affliction and forest renunciation
description: A skin-disease (kuṣṭha/skin-blemish) bars Devāpi from royal consecration; he withdraws to the forest as an ascetic, clearing the throne for Śāntanu
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva

title: Division of the Veda
description: Vyasa splits the one Veda into Rig, Yajur, Sama, Atharva and teaches them to four disciples

title: Division of the Veda into four
description: Vyasa splits the primordial Veda into Rig, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva for the declining age and teaches them to his four disciples Paila, Vaishampayana, Jaimini, and Sumantu

title: Draupadi Born of Fire
description: The Panchala princess Draupadi is born from the sacrificial fire and becomes common wife of the five Pandavas

title: Drupada humiliates the impoverished Droṇa
description: Now a proud king, Drupada repudiates the boyhood promise and insults Droṇa, declaring friendship exists only between equals

title: Duhshasana drags Draupadi by the hair
description: After Draupadi is lost at dice, Duhshasana seizes her by the hair and hauls her, menstruating and in one garment, into the men's assembly

title: Durvāsa grants Kuntī the deity-invocation mantra
description: After Kuntī serves the volatile sage Durvāsa flawlessly, he grants her an ātharvaṇa mantra to summon any deity to beget a child upon her

title: Durvāsā arrives to test Mudgala
description: The irascible sage Durvāsā comes feigning madness, naked and reviling, deliberately to break Mudgala's reputed equanimity and hospitality

title: Durvāsā tests Mudgala by devouring his food
description: Durvāsā arrives repeatedly in a mad/naked guise, consumes Mudgala's entire gleaned store each fortnight, mocks him, and leaves the family starving

title: Duryodhana's hospitality trap and the boon
description: Duryodhana serves Śalya's marching army lavishly in disguise; Śalya, thinking the host was Yudhiṣṭhira, grants a boon and is bound to fight for the Kauravas

title: Ekalavya self-trains before a clay Droṇa
description: Undeterred, Ekalavya fashions an earthen image of Droṇa as his guru and practises archery before it with total devotion until he attains the highest skill, entirely self-taught

title: Enrollment at Sandipani's gurukula
description: Krishna and Balarama choose the sage Sandipani of Avanti (Ujjayini) as their teacher and serve him as model pupils

title: Four Pāṇḍavas fall dead at the lake
description: Chasing the deer and parched, each brother in turn ignores the guardian voice's warning, drinks from the lake, and dies, until four lie dead

title: Gaṇeśa breaks his tusk as Mahābhārata scribe
description: Serving as Vyāsa's scribe for the Mahābhārata, Gaṇeśa snaps off his own tusk to keep writing when his pen breaks, becoming Ekadanta

title: Gajānana's teaching of the yogas
description: Gajānana instructs Vareṇya in karma-, jñāna-, and bhakti-yoga across the discourse, declaring himself the imperishable self and Para-brahman, with ~90% of verses adapted from the Bhagavad Gītā

title: Gandhari's glance scorches Yudhishthira
description: As Yudhishthira approaches, Gandhari's wrath escapes through her blindfold and scorches the king's nails; Vyasa and Krishna restrain her and she relents before her grandsons' killer

title: Hiding the weapons in the shami tree
description: Before entering the city the Pandavas wrap their celestial weapons in a corpse-shroud and bind them high in a shami tree, claiming it is a relative's body so none will touch it

title: Hiḍimba sends Hiḍimbī to fetch prey
description: The man-eating rākṣasa Hiḍimba smells the sleeping humans and dispatches his sister Hiḍimbī to kill and bring them as food

title: Import of the eighteen Maga families from Śākadvīpa
description: Unable to find a local brāhmaṇa to tend the Sun-image, Sāmba uses Garuḍa to bring eighteen Maga priest families from Śākadvīpa, founding the Bhojaka Sun-temple priesthood

title: Indra's appeal to Kṛṣṇa
description: Indra, robbed of his mother Aditi's earrings, comes to Dwārakā and begs Kṛṣṇa to destroy Naraka

title: Infant Bhima Shatters a Rock
description: As an infant Bhima falls from Kunti's lap onto a rock and smashes it to powder while remaining unhurt, the first omen of his strength

title: Kṛṣṇa counsels abduction
description: Kṛṣṇa advises Arjuna to seize Subhadrā by rākṣasa-form capture, pre-empting Balarāma's plan to wed her to Duryodhana

title: Kṛṣṇa drives the cows into the forest
description: Kṛṣṇa, with Balarāma and the cowherd boys, leads the cattle into the flowering autumn woods of Vṛndāvana

title: Kalayavana marches on Mathura
description: The invincible Yavana king Kalayavana, a vengeance-son born of the sage Gargya, advances on Mathura with a vast mleccha host, posing a threat Krishna cannot meet by force
source: Bhagavata Purana X.50-51; Vishnu Purana V.23; Harivamsha

title: Kaṃsa imprisons Devakī and slays her children
description: On the prophecy that Devakī's eighth child will kill him, Kaṃsa imprisons Devakī and Vasudeva and slays their first children

title: Kṛṣṇa's request for the gem refused
description: Kṛṣṇa asks Satrājit to give the jewel to King Ugrasena for the common good; the greedy Satrājit refuses, sowing suspicion

title: Kṛṣṇa Subdues Kāliya (Kāliya-mardana)
description: The poison-spewing nāga Kāliya infests a Yamunā pool until the boy Kṛṣṇa leaps into his coils and dances upon his hoods, subduing but sparing him and banishing him back to Ramaṇaka Dvīpa

title: Kauśika burns the crane with his gaze
description: The proud ascetic Kauśika, soiled by a bird while reciting, burns it to ashes with an angry glance and is elated, the flaw the parable exists to cure

title: Ākāśavāṇī Prophesies Kaṃsa's Death
description: At the wedding of Devakī to Vasudeva a heavenly voice warns Kaṃsa that her eighth child will kill him, triggering the whole birth-cycle of Kṛṣṇa

title: Kirmīra-vadha
description: Bhīma slays the cannibal rākṣasa Kirmīra (kin of Baka and Hiḍimba) bare-handed at the threshold of Kāmyaka forest

title: Kunti summons Surya and conceives Karna
description: Testing the mantra out of curiosity, Kunti invokes Surya, who begets a son in her and restores her virginity afterward

title: Maṇipura succession pact
description: By marriage-pact the son stays in Maṇipura as its king and never joins the Pāṇḍava household

title: Maitreya's curse on Duryodhana
description: The mocked sage Maitreya curses that Bhima will smash Duryodhana's thigh in war, sealing the Sabha-Parva oath

title: Marriage to Vicitravīrya
description: Ambikā and Ambālikā are wed to Vicitravīrya at Hastināpura after the eldest sister Ambā is released

title: Nala and Damayantī Fall in Love by Reputation
description: Each hearing the other endlessly praised, Nala and Damayantī fall in love before ever meeting

title: Nala and Damayantī fall in love via the golden swan
description: Nala and Damayantī fall in love by reputation; a golden haṃsa carries Nala's praise to Vidarbha

title: Narada describes the celestial sabhas
description: Narada describes the assembly-halls of Indra, Yama, Varuna, Kubera, and Brahma, noting Hariscandra alone among humans sits with the gods for completing the Rajasuya, planting Yudhishthira's ambition

title: Niyoga births of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura
description: Vyasa fathers Dhritarashtra (blind), Pandu (pale), and Vidura (Dharma incarnate) on the widowed Kashi princesses and a maidservant

title: Nārada and Dhaumya lay out the four-quarter pilgrimage plan
description: Nārada and the Pāṇḍava priest Dhaumya describe the east-south-west-north circuit of fords as a route-plan for the exiled Yudhiṣṭhira

title: Parāśara, the boons, and the birth of Vyāsa
description: The sage Parāśara unites with her under a mist, restores her virginity and turns her fish-smell to a yojana-fragrance (Yojanagandhā); on a Yamunā island she bears Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, who promises to come whenever she remembers him
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~57, ~63; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa

title: Piṅgalā's sudden vairāgya (turn to detachment)
description: Crushed by disappointment, Piṅgalā grows disgusted with desire itself and perceives that the Self/Lord within is the true neglected beloved

title: Prophecy of Shishupala's slayer
description: An aerial voice foretells that the child's surplus eye and arms will vanish when his future slayer takes him on his lap

title: Pursuit, capture, and sparing of Jayadratha
description: The Pāṇḍavas overtake and capture Jayadratha; Yudhiṣṭhira spares his life for Duḥśalā's sake

title: Renaming of the Bhārata clan as Kuru
description: After Kuru, the dynasty formerly called Bhārata becomes the Kuru clan, naming both Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19

title: Rescue and naming by Shantanu
description: King Shantanu finds the abandoned twins, is moved to pity (kripa), rears them and names them Kripa and Kripi

title: Retirement to the Himālaya
description: Pāṇḍu renounces the throne and withdraws to the Himālaya as an ascetic, accompanied by both queens Kuntī and Mādrī

title: Reunion of Arjuna and Irāvān in Indraloka
description: Father and son meet in Indra's heaven; Irāvān pledges to fight for the Pāṇḍavas and rides to Kurukṣetra

title: Rukmiṇī's secret love-letter via the Brāhmaṇa messenger
description: Rukmiṇī sends a trusted Brāhmaṇa to Dwārakā with a secret letter declaring her love and begging Kṛṣṇa to abduct her before the wedding, dictating the temple-procession plan

title: Sahadeva slays Shakuni
description: Sahadeva confronts Shakuni, the dice-master architect of the war, and severs his head, fulfilling his dice-hall vow; Shakuni's son Uluka is also slain

title: Sanatsujata delivers the teaching that heedlessness is death
description: Sanatsujata expounds that death is pramada (heedlessness) not extinction, that the deathless state is vigilance, and that the Vedas alone do not save without realization of the Self

title: Sarayū named as a tīrtha in the Mahābhārata pilgrim-lists
description: The Sarayū and its Gopratāra ford are listed in the Tīrtha-yātrā catalogue recited to Yudhiṣṭhira as sin-destroying, heaven-conferring fords

title: Satyavatī's virginity and fragrance restored
description: Parāśara restores Satyavatī's virginity and changes her fish-odor to musk, enabling her later marriage to Śantanu and the Kuru line

title: Saṃvaraṇa beholds Tapatī on the mountain
description: King Saṃvaraṇa, hunting, sees Sūrya's daughter Tapatī on a mountain; they fall in mutual love but she vanishes

title: Shalya undermines Karna with the crow-and-swan parable
description: Forced to drive Karna's chariot, Shalya repeatedly praises Arjuna and belittles Karna, mocking him with the fable of the arrogant crow who challenged a swan, fulfilling his secret promise to demoralize him

title: Shibi offers his own flesh on the scale
description: To resolve the dove's claim to sanctuary against the hawk's claim to food, Shibi cuts flesh equal to the dove's weight onto a balance and finally offers his whole body

title: Slaughter of the first six children and transfer of Balarama
description: Kamsa kills Devaki's first six infants; the seventh, Balarama, is mystically transferred by Yogamaya to Rohini's womb in Gokula

title: Slaying of Ariṣṭāsura the bull-demon
description: Krishna seizes the rampaging bull-demon by the horns, hurls him back, and wrings his neck until he vomits blood and dies
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.36; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5; Harivaṃśa

title: Sulabhā Debates Janaka from Within
description: Testing Janaka's claim of liberation, the yoginī Sulabhā enters his mind by yoga-bala and argues the self is ungendered and unembodied, exposing his lingering identification

title: Takṣaka steals the earrings; Uttaṅka burns Nāgaloka
description: Takṣaka snatches the earrings into the serpent-world; Uttaṅka digs after them, sees the cosmic loom-vision, and floods Nāgaloka with fire from Agni's horse until the nāgas return the jewels

title: The boon of the crystal vimāna, Vaijayantī garland, and bamboo staff
description: Indra grants Vasu a crystal aerial car (whence 'Uparicara'), an unfading Vaijayantī garland, and a protective bamboo staff

title: The brahmacarya debate and one-night marriage
description: Ulūpī woos Arjuna, who objects on his celibacy vow; she argues the vow binds him only regarding Draupadī and that refusing a desiring woman breaches dharma, and they wed for one night

title: The brothers and Draupadī argue against renunciation
description: Arjuna, Bhīma, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī, and Devasthāna refute Yudhiṣṭhira's wish to renounce, defending kṣatriya duty, wealth, and righteous rule over barren asceticism

title: The double cattle-raid and Virata's capture
description: Susharma of Trigarta strikes from the south and captures Virata while the Kauravas raid from the north; Bhima routs Trigarta and frees the king

title: The first Annakūṭa and the śailo 'smi self-manifestation
description: The Vrajavāsīs redirect the offerings to Govardhana with parikramā and a mountain of food; Kṛṣṇa manifests a colossal form on the summit and eats it, declaring 'I am the hill.'

title: The Five Re-Emergences and Founding of the Pancha Kedar
description: The bull-form Shiva's body-parts surface at five Garhwal sites where the Pandavas raise the Pancha Kedar temples (hump-Kedarnath, arms-Tungnath, face-Rudranath, navel-Madhyamaheshwar, hair-Kalpeshwar), freeing them of sin

title: The Gandhāra grievance (variant backstory)
description: In late/folk tradition the Kurus starve the imprisoned Subala family, and Śakuni survives to avenge them with dice made from his father's bones; absent from the critical text
source: Regional/televised retellings [folk] [late text]; not in BORI Critical Edition

title: The gift of flattened rice (pṛthuka/poha)
description: Having nothing, the wife begs four fistfuls of flattened rice from neighbours and ties them in a tattered cloth as Sudāmā's gift for Kṛṣṇa

title: The Gita teaches nishkama karma and the three margas
description: In the Bhagavad Gita the teaching of desireless action and of karma-, jnana- and bhakti-yoga as complementary paths to liberation is delivered

title: The gold expedition to recover King Marutta's hoard
description: To fund the impoverished kingdom's sacrifice, a party journeys near Mount Meru/Himavat to recover King Marutta's ancient buried gold, worshipping Śiva and the guardian Yakṣas

title: The infant swap at Gokula
description: Vasudeva carries Kṛṣṇa to Gokula and exchanges him for Yaśodā's newborn daughter, the goddess, returning her to Kaṃsa's prison

title: The Kama-gita: Desire sings of its indestructibility
description: Desire personified sings that he cannot be slain by force and is transcended only by knowledge, an inset in Krishna's instruction

title: The matrilineal heir-pact and marriage
description: King Citravāhana gives his only daughter Citrāṅgadā (a putrikā) to Arjuna on the condition that her son remain in Maṇipura as Citravāhana's heir; Arjuna accepts and weds her

title: The owl-omen inspires the night raid
description: Sleepless under a banyan, Ashvatthaman watches an owl kill sleeping crows one by one, which gives him the plan to massacre the sleeping enemy camp

title: The poisoned pool
description: Kāliya's venom boils a reach of the Yamunā, killing birds, cattle, and people who touch the water

title: The sages curse Samba's iron club
description: At Pindaraka, idle Yadava princes dress Krishna's son Samba as a pregnant woman to mock visiting rishis (Vishvamitra, Kanva, Narada and others), who curse that Samba will deliver an iron club that destroys the whole Vrishni-Andhaka race

title: The Sañjaya-yāna peace-embassy to the Pāṇḍavas
description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra sends Sañjaya as envoy to the Pāṇḍava camp at Upaplavya with a hollow peace-offer; Yudhiṣṭhira and Kṛṣṇa see through it, and Sañjaya reports back faithfully, rebuking the king

title: The Samshaptaka oath and Arjuna drawn off
description: The Trigarta king Susharman and his brothers swear a death-pact to kill Arjuna or die, challenging him to a separate sector to pull him from Yudhishthira

title: The six questions
description: Yudhiṣṭhira asks the one supreme deity, the highest goal, whom to worship for the auspicious, and the greatest/easiest dharma

title: The summons of the flute
description: On the autumn full-moon night Kṛṣṇa's flute draws the gopīs from their homes, some leaving their bodies through love-meditation

title: The Syamantaka conspiracy against Satrājit
description: A spurned suitor of Satyabhāmā, Kṛtavarma joins Akrūra in inciting Śatadhanvā to murder the sleeping Satrājit and seize the Syamantaka jewel

title: The three infallible arrows
description: Through tapas Barbarīka earns three infallible arrows (Tīn Bāṇ) from Śiva and/or the Goddess that mark and annihilate any target, making him unconquerable

title: The Vasus' bargain with Gaṅgā
description: The eight Vasus, cursed by Vasiṣṭha for stealing his cow, ask Gaṅgā to be their mortal mother and drown them to free them

title: The wife's urging and the gift of flattened rice
description: Sudama's starving wife begs a few fistfuls of prithuka (flattened rice) from neighbours and ties them in a cloth as his only gift for Krishna

title: Twelve-year tapas to Sūrya at Candrabhāgā
description: Counselled that only the Sun can cure disease, Sāmba performs severe penance to Sūrya at Mitravana on the Candrabhāgā

title: Twin-birth of Draupadī
description: Draupadī (Kṛṣṇā) rises unasked from the same altar immediately after Dhṛṣṭadyumna, his fire-born twin

title: Uddhava consoles Nanda and Yaśodā
description: Reaching Vraja at sunset, Uddhava hears Nanda and Yaśodā pour out their parental grief and reassures them that Kṛṣṇa as the Supreme Self is never truly absent

title: Uṣā's boon-dream
description: Granted a boon by Gaurī/Pārvatī, Uṣā dreams of and makes love to an unknown youth, then wakes longing for the lover she cannot name

title: Uttanka eats the bull's dung (Indra's amrita)
description: On the road a giant on a bull bids Uttanka eat dung and urine, which are secretly amrita given by Indra on Airavata, making him proof against death

title: Varuṇa gives Arjuna the Gāṇḍīva at Khāṇḍava
description: At the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest Varuṇa bestows on Arjuna the great bow Gāṇḍīva, two inexhaustible quivers, and a divine chariot

title: Vatsāsura the calf-demon slain
description: A demon disguised as a stray calf is seized by the hind legs, whirled, and dashed against a wood-apple tree by Krishna
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.11; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Śveta condemned to devour his own body
description: After death Śveta is punished by being made to eat his own flesh repeatedly, because his gifts fed only himself and never another

title: Vikarṇa's protest in the dice-hall
description: Alone among the hundred Kauravas, Vikarṇa rises and argues that Draupadī was never lawfully staked, since Yudhiṣṭhira had already lost himself before wagering her

title: Vishnu deceives Vrinda and the origin of Tulsi
description: To break the invincible asura Jalandhara, Vishnu deceives his chaste wife Vrinda in his guise; she curses Vishnu and self-immolates, reborn as the tulsi plant (origin of Tulsi Vivaha)

title: Vishvakarman Builds Dvaraka in a Single Day
description: Krishna asks the ocean-god Samudra for land and Vishvakarman raises the golden sea-fortress city of Dvaraka in a single day on reclaimed sea-land

title: Viṣṇu tricks the asura into destroying himself
description: Viṣṇu (as a brāhmaṇa boy, or as Mohinī in the Bhasmāsura folk version) dupes the demon into laying his own hand on his head, killing himself

title: Viśvāvasu fathers Pramadvarā by Menakā
description: The gandharva Viśvāvasu fathers Pramadvarā by the apsarā Menakā; the abandoned child is reared by the sage Sthūlakeśa and betrothed to the Bhārgava Ruru, setting up the half-lifespan revival and ahiṃsā parable

title: Vyāsa's boon of a hundred sons
description: The pleased sage Vyāsa grants Gāndhārī the boon of a hundred sons equal to her husband

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya and the killing of Jarāsandha
description: To claim sovereignty Yudhiṣṭhira performs the Rājasūya yajña; on Kṛṣṇa's counsel the obstacle-king Jarāsandha is killed by Bhīma before the rite

title: Yudhishthira honours the elders before battle
description: Yudhishthira lays down his weapons and walks unarmed across to touch the feet of Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Shalya, seeking their leave to fight; each blesses him with victory

title: Yudhishthira's tour of Naraka
description: In the Svargarohana Parva, Yudhishthira is given a brief tour of the hells before the final reckoning

title: Abduction of Subhadrā
description: Arjuna carries Subhadrā off in his chariot as she returns from worship at Raivataka, scattering the guards

title: Abhimanyu Weds Uttara
description: Abhimanyu marries Uttara, daughter of King Virata, sealing the Matsya-Panchala-Yadava alliance for the coming war

title: Arjuna Captures Drupada
description: As Drona's guru-fee Arjuna defeats and binds King Drupada of Panchala, sowing the enmity that produces Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna

title: Arjuna rebukes Babhruvahana
description: Bound by kshatriya code, Arjuna reproaches his son as unwarriorlike for offering submission and demands combat

title: Arjuna's despondency between the armies
description: Arjuna has Krishna drive between the armies; seeing his kin arrayed to kill one another he is overcome with grief, his limbs failing and Gandiva slipping from his hand

title: Arjuna's tapas and battle with Śiva-as-Kirāta on Indrakīla
description: During the Pāṇḍavas' forest exile Arjuna performs severe tapas on Mount Indrakīla, fights Śiva disguised as a Kirāta hunter over a slain boar, and on recognising the god is granted the Pāśupatāstra — the episode dramatised in Bhāravi's Kirātārjunīya

title: Ashvatthaman slays the Pandya king
description: On the 16th day Ashvatthaman, bent on vengeance, slays the mighty Pandya king Malayadhvaja in a long archery duel, cutting off his head and arms

title: Ashvatthaman worships Shiva at the camp gate
description: Blocked by a divine three-eyed guardian, Ashvatthaman offers his own body as oblation to Shiva, who grants him a celestial sword and enters his body so Rudra's destructive energy works through him

title: Attempted disrobing of Draupadi (vastraharana)
description: Duhshasana tries to strip Draupadi in open court, but endless garments appear until he collapses exhausted, unable to bare her

title: Avatara of Gajanana
description: Ganesha descends in Dvapara Yuga as the mouse-mounted Gajanana, born to Shiva and Parvati, slaying the demon of greed/ego (Sindura)

title: Bakāsura the crane-demon torn at the beak
description: A giant crane swallows Krishna, is forced to disgorge him by burning heat, then is split apart by his beak
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.11; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Balarama marries Revati and shrinks her with his plough
description: On Brahma's counsel Revati weds Balarama, who taps her with his plough-tip to reduce her to the stature of his own era

title: Bhima Poisoned and Given the Naga-nectar
description: Duryodhana feeds Bhima poison and casts him into the Ganga, but the Naga king Vasuki gives him eight jars of nectar conferring immense strength

title: Bhima slays Kirmira
description: In the Kamyaka woods Bhima kills the man-eating rakshasa Kirmira bare-handed

title: Bhishma's Terrible Vow and the Boon of Icchha-mrityu
description: Devavrata renounces the throne and takes the dreadful vow of lifelong celibacy so Satyavati's son may rule, earning the name Bhishma and the boon of death-at-will

title: Bhīṣma names Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva as supreme refuge
description: Bhīṣma answers that Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva is the supreme deity and that praising Him by the thousand names is the highest and easiest dharma

title: Birth of Babhruvāhana and Arjuna's departure
description: After three years at Maṇipura, Citrāṅgadā bears Babhruvāhana, who is left in Maṇipura as crown-prince per the pact, and Arjuna resumes his pilgrimage alone

title: Birth of Karna in armor
description: Karna is born already wearing a golden kavacha and kundala fused to his skin, dipped in amrita, making him invulnerable while he keeps them

title: Birth of Karna to Kunti and Surya
description: Using Durvasa's mantra Kunti summons Surya and bears Karna armored with kavacha-kundala, then sets the infant adrift on the river

title: Birth of Krishna
description: Krishna is born at midnight on Janmashtami as the dark-hued eighth child, displaying his four-armed Vishnu form before assuming infant shape

title: Birth of Krishna and the substituted goddess
description: Balarāma's embryo is moved to Rohiṇī and Krishna is born and carried across the Yamunā to Nanda and Yaśodā, swapped for the infant goddess Ekānaṃśā/Nidrā who escapes Kaṃsa's hand and prophesies his doom

title: Brahma abducts and hides the calves and boys
description: Brahma secretly carries off first the calves and then the cowherd boys, hiding both in a mountain cave in yogic sleep

title: Capture by Arjuna and loss of half Pāñcāla
description: As Droṇa's teaching-fee, Arjuna defeats and binds Drupada; Droṇa seizes the northern half of Pāñcāla

title: Citralekhā's magical portraiture
description: The yoginī Citralekhā paints likenesses of gods and Yādavas, and Uṣā identifies her dream-lover as Aniruddha, Kṛṣṇa's grandson

title: Citrāṅgada's pride and the gandharva's challenge
description: The proud warrior-king Citrāṅgada is challenged by a gandharva king of the same name who takes the shared title as an affront

title: Co-architect of the lacquer house
description: Śakuni helps Duryodhana and Purocana plan the Lākṣāgṛha at Vāraṇāvata to burn the Pāṇḍavas alive; the plot is foiled

title: Composition of the Mahabharata
description: Vyasa authors the 100,000-verse Mahabharata, dictated to Ganesha as scribe on the condition that Vyasa never pause and Ganesha never write without understanding

title: Curse of the sage Kindama
description: Pāṇḍu shoots the sage Kindama mating in deer form and is cursed to die the instant he approaches a wife in desire, barring natural fatherhood

title: Damayantī's svayaṃvara and the five identical Nalas
description: At the svayaṃvara the four Lokapālas mimic Nala's form; Damayantī picks the true Nala by divine signs and the gods grant him boons

title: Death of Prasena and the lion
description: Satrājit's brother Prasena wears the gem hunting and is killed with his horse by a lion, which carries off the jewel

title: Death of Vicitravīrya, widowhood
description: After seven years Vicitravīrya dies childless of consumption, leaving both queens young widows and the Kuru line near extinction

title: Departure from Vraja and gopīs' grief
description: The brothers leave Vṛndāvana on Akrūra's chariot; the gopīs' separation (viraha) is left unresolved

title: Descent of Vishnu as Krishna
description: Vishnu descends as Krishna at the close of the Dvapara Yuga of this 28th Mahayuga, the defining reason this cycle matters above all others

title: Dhanvantari reborn as king of Kashi
description: A later Dhanvantari is reborn into the royal house of Kashi (identified with Divodasa), where he systematizes and publicly teaches the Ayurvedic system
source: Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Brahmanda Purana; Sushruta Samhita

title: Durvāsā's mantra-boon to Kuntī and the birth of Karṇa
description: Pleased by a year of flawless service from the young princess Kuntī, Durvāsā grants her a mantra to summon any deity and beget a child of his nature; testing it on Sūrya, she bears Karṇa before marriage, seeding the Kuru tragedy

title: Duryodhana hides in Lake Dvaipayana
description: With his army destroyed, Duryodhana flees and by yogic power solidifies the waters of Lake Dvaipayana, lying hidden beneath the surface to regather strength

title: Dushyanta meets Shakuntala at Kanva's ashrama
description: King Dushyanta, hunting from Hastinapura, enters Kanva's hermitage in the sage's absence, is received and smitten by Shakuntala, and the two fall in mutual love

title: Duṣyanta & Śakuntalā Wed by Gandharva Rite
description: Duṣyanta and Śakuntalā marry by gandharva vivāha (mutual consent without ritual) in Kaṇva's forest hermitage — the locus classicus of the love-match marriage

title: Ekalavya seals the dog's mouth with arrows
description: On a hunt Ekalavya fires seven arrows by sound alone (śabda-vedha) into a barking dog's open mouth, sealing it without drawing blood, astonishing the Kuru princes

title: Gandhari's panoramic lament over the slain
description: By her divine eye Gandhari surveys all of Kurukshetra and describes the carnage corpse by corpse to Krishna, naming Duryodhana, Abhimanyu, Karna, Drona, Jayadratha and the slaughtered warrior aristocracy

title: Gods reveal themselves and boon Shibi a son
description: Indra and Agni resume true form, heal Shibi, and promise him a glorious son Kapotaroma, proving dharma upheld without limit overrides death

title: Hiḍimbī falls for Bhīma
description: Sent to seize the sleepers, the shape-shifting Hiḍimbī is smitten with desire for Bhīma, takes human-woman form, warns him of her brother, and offers love and rescue

title: Humiliation of Jayadratha
description: Bhīma shaves Jayadratha's head leaving five tufts and forces him to declare himself the Pāṇḍavas' slave before release

title: Indra's seven quenchings of the forest
description: Indra, protector of Khāṇḍava and friend of Takṣaka, douses Agni's blaze with rain seven times

title: Indra's Sāṃvartaka deluge
description: The slighted Indra commands the dissolution-clouds to destroy Vraja with a pralaya-like flood of rain, hail and gale
actors: the people and cattle of Vraja
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.25; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 5

title: Institution of the Indra-dhvaja festival
description: Vasu founds the annual Indra-maha / Indra-dhvaja banner-pole festival and bequeaths it to all kings as a royal rite of prosperity
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (~63); Varāhamihira Bṛhat-saṃhitā (historical rite)

title: Irāvān's cavalry exploits at Kurukṣetra
description: Mounted, Irāvān routs the cavalry of Śakuni's Gāndhāra brothers, slaying several in the early days of the war

title: Journey to Dvārakā
description: Sudāmā walks the long road to the opulent island-city of Dvārakā, desiring only the darśana of Kṛṣṇa

title: Kama reborn as Pradyumna and slays Sambara
description: Kama is reborn as Pradyumna, son of Krishna and Rukmini; stolen by Sambara and raised by Mayavati (Rati), the grown Pradyumna slays Sambara and weds her

title: Kṛṣṇa names Upamanyu as his source for the hymn
description: Kṛṣṇa explains he learned the thousand names and Śiva-worship from the sage Upamanyu during his own austerities

title: Karṇa overrules Vikarṇa
description: Karṇa angrily rebukes the young Vikarṇa, rules Draupadī lawfully won and a slave, and orders her stripped, overruling the lone dharmic voice

title: Kṛṣṇa revives the stillborn Parikṣit
description: Parikṣit, struck in Uttarā's womb by Aśvatthāman's Brahmāstra and born seemingly dead, is restored to life by Kṛṣṇa's act of truth, securing the continuity of the Kuru line

title: Kṛṣṇa rides to Kuṇḍina; the hostile kings gather
description: Kṛṣṇa drives to Vidarbha with Dāruka; Balarāma follows with the Yādava army; Śiśupāla's coalition (Jarāsandha, Śālva, Dantavakra and others) awaits

title: Karkoṭaka Bites and Disguises Nala
description: The black nāga Karkoṭaka bites and disfigures King Nala in a benign bite that hides him from Kali's persecution and later lets him resume his form

title: Kaṃsa Deposes and Imprisons Ugrasena
description: Kaṃsa deposes and imprisons his father Ugrasena, king of Mathurā, ruling as a despot allied to Jarāsandha of Magadha

title: Krishna absorbs the Vaishnavastra; Arjuna slays Bhagadatta
description: Bhagadatta of Pragjyotisha hurls the Vaishnavastra, which Krishna absorbs onto his chest as the Vaijayanti garland; Arjuna then slays Bhagadatta on his elephant Supratika

title: Krishna delivers the Uddhava Gita
description: At the eve of Kali Yuga Krishna gives Uddhava his final systematic teaching (the Uddhava/Hamsa Gita) synthesizing bhakti, jnana, yoga and Samkhya before departing

title: Krishna's Departure and Onset of Kali
description: Krishna passes away and the Yadava line ends, after which Kali personified enters the world, marking the turn into the Kali Yuga

title: Krishna's exodus and the building of Dwaraka
description: Krishna abandons Mathura and has Vishvakarma build the island-city Dwaraka on land reclaimed from the ocean, transferring the citizens there by yogic power
source: Bhagavata Purana X.50.49-57; Vishnu Purana V.23; Harivamsha

title: Krishna's lap fulfils the sign
description: When Shrutashrava places the child on Krishna's lap the third eye and extra arms drop away, revealing Krishna as the appointed killer

title: Krishna Slays Shankhasura at Bet Dvaraka
description: At Shankhoddhara (Bet Dvaraka) Krishna slays the conch-demon Shankhasura and recovers the Vedas, the myth tied to his Panchajanya conch

title: Kṛtavarma enrolled as a Kaurava general
description: The Yādava clan splits for the war; Kṛtavarma brings a Vṛṣṇi-Bhoja contingent to fight for Duryodhana while Sātyaki fights for the Pāṇḍavas

title: Kuntī invokes Sūrya and bears Karṇa
description: Testing the mantra, Kuntī summons Sūrya, who is compelled to beget Karṇa upon her, born with natural golden armor and earrings, while restoring her virginity

title: Kuntī invokes Vāyu and conceives Bhīma
description: Using Durvāsā's mantra, Queen Kuntī invokes Vāyu and conceives Bhīma, strongest of the Pāṇḍavas, Vāyu's might made mortal

title: Lomaśa leads the Pāṇḍavas on the walked tīrtha-circuit
description: The sage Lomaśa conducts the exiled Pāṇḍavas around the ford-network, the catalogue dramatised as a journey with inset legends at each station

title: Maha-Rasa — Krishna's circle-dance with the gopis
description: On the Sharad full-moon night Krishna's flute summons the gopis to the rasa-lila, multiplying himself to partner each; tradition stretches the night to a night of Brahma

title: Marriage to Śāntanu and the bride-price
description: Śāntanu seeks her in marriage; the fisher-chief demands that her son inherit the throne, prompting Devavrata's renunciation and terrible vow of celibacy that makes him Bhīṣma, after which she is wed as queen

title: Mastery of all knowledge in sixty-four days
description: The brothers master the Vedas, weapons, and sixty-four arts on single hearings, completing their education in sixty-four days

title: Mudgala endures without anger; Durvāsā blesses him
description: Through repeated ruin Mudgala remains serene and free of resentment; Durvāsā, won over, declares his anger-free virtue and pronounces he will ascend bodily to heaven

title: Māyāvatī (Rati) finds and rears Pradyumna
description: The netted fish is given to Śambara's cook Māyāvatī, who finds the living boy; Nārada reveals he is Kāma and she, as Rati, secretly raises him

title: Nārada reveals Krishna's birth-secret to Kaṃsa
description: After Ariṣṭa's fall Nārada visits Kaṃsa, discloses that Devakī's child survives as the Vraja boy, and sets the Keśin mission in motion

title: Śāntanu's accession seeds the Kuru succession crisis
description: With Devāpi disqualified and Bāhlīka settled abroad, Śāntanu is consecrated at Hastināpura, setting up the later Kuru succession crisis
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: Peace through abandoning hope ('āśā hi paramaṃ duḥkham')
description: The instant Piṅgalā gives up hope she finds deep calm and sleeps in peace, declaring hope the supreme misery and hopelessness the supreme bliss; she resolves on renunciation

title: Ploughing of Kurukṣetra with the golden share
description: Kuru ploughs the Samanta-pañcaka plain on the Sarasvatī with a golden ploughshare as prolonged tapas, in the Vāmana Purāṇa yoking Yama's buffalo and Śiva's bull and sowing the dharmic virtues
source: Mahābhārata Śalya Parva (Kurukṣetra-māhātmya stratum); Vāmana Purāṇa Kurukṣetra-māhātmya

title: Pratīpa's boon and the naming of Śāntanu
description: Gaṅgā sits on Pratīpa's right thigh and is promised to his son; Pratīpa later begets in tranquillity a son named Śāntanu
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~97; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: Prince Uttara's boast and panic
description: Left alone in the city, Prince Uttara boasts he would scatter the Kuru host, then panics at the sight of the army and flees, only to be dragged back by Brihannala

title: Revival of the poisoned cowherds and cattle
description: Krishna revives cowherd boys and cows killed by the tainted water with his nectarean glance

title: Śārṅga passes to Kṛṣṇa (Śārṅgapāṇi)
description: Viṣṇu's bow Śārṅga is borne by Kṛṣṇa, giving rise to his epithets Śārṅgin and Śārṅgapāṇi ('Śārṅga-in-hand'), the latter enshrined as the dedicatory name of the Sārangapāni temple at Kumbhakoṇam

title: Samba cured by worshipping Surya
description: The leprous Samba, son of Krishna, is cured by worshipping Surya, founding solar worship at Mitravana/Multan

title: Saṃvaraṇa's penance on the mountain
description: The lovesick king performs austerities to win Tapatī, who insists her father Sūrya must give her in proper marriage

title: Self-revealed Sūrya image and the cure
description: Pleased Sūrya cures Sāmba, who recovers a divine Sun-image fashioned by Viśvakarmā from the river and installs it, founding Arka Kṣetra

title: Shalya tricked to the Kaurava side
description: The Madra king Shalya, intercepted by Duryodhana's hospitality, is bound by gratitude to fight for the Kauravas but secretly promises Yudhishthira to dishearten Karna as charioteer

title: Sharadvat teaches Kripa the science of arms
description: Sharadvat returns to Shantanu's court and imparts the full dhanurveda to his son, making Kripa a complete acharya

title: Slaying of Jarasandha by Bhima
description: Disguised as brahmanas, the three reach Magadha; Krishna's leaf-splitting hint lets Bhima tear Jarasandha in two and fling the halves apart, freeing the captive kings

title: Sūrya's gift of the Akṣaya-pātra
description: Yudhiṣṭhira propitiates Sūrya, who gives the inexhaustible cooking-vessel that yields unlimited food daily until Draupadī has eaten

title: Sudama's journey to Dwaraka
description: Longing only for darshana, Sudama walks the long road and enters the opulent island-city of Dwaraka to reach Krishna's palace

title: The agra-pūjā to Kṛṣṇa and beheading of Śiśupāla
description: Yudhiṣṭhira awards the first-worship of the Rājasūya to Kṛṣṇa; when Śiśupāla protests and exhausts his hundred allotted offenses, Kṛṣṇa beheads him with his discus

title: The double rejection of Ambā
description: Śālva spurns Ambā as won by another; Vicitravīrya and the vow-bound Bhīṣma also refuse her, leaving her abandoned and fixing blame on Bhīṣma

title: The faithful housewife humbles Kauśika
description: A devoted wife tending her husband tells the impatient Kauśika she is no crane to be burnt, that household duty done in love is itself the path, and sends him to the butcher of Mithilā

title: The flute sounds
description: Kṛṣṇa sets the veṇu to his lips and fills the forest with music; the gopīs hear it and begin praising it to one another

title: The Garuḍa-flight to Prāgjyotiṣa
description: Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā mount Garuḍa and cross the mountain-girt, weapon-warded defences in an aerial assault

title: The Golden Swan Carries Nala's Suit
description: A captured golden swan, released by Nala, flies to Vidarbha and extols him to Damayantī, kindling her longing

title: The infant dashed on the rock rises as eight-armed Devī
description: Kaṃsa seizes the infant girl to smash her on a stone; she slips free and rises into the sky as an eight-armed armed goddess
source: Harivaṃśa Āryā-stava; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.1; Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.4

title: The iron club ground to powder and the eraka grass born
description: Samba produces the cursed iron club; on Ugrasena's order it is ground to powder and cast into the sea, but one unground lump is swallowed by a fish (whose splinter the hunter Jara takes as an arrowhead) and the filings wash ashore to grow into the sharp eraka reed

title: The Pandavas take disguises at Virata's court
description: The five brothers and Draupadi assume hidden identities (Kanka, Vallabha, Brihannala, Granthika, Tantipala, Sairandhri) and enter service at Virata's court, Arjuna's eunuch disguise fulfilling Urvashi's curse

title: The provocation cycle — Durvāsā devours all the food repeatedly
description: Durvāsā eats Mudgala's entire gleaned store and abuses him across successive visits (six in the tale); Mudgala re-gleans and feeds him afresh each time without anger

title: The secret pact with Yudhiṣṭhira
description: Śalya promises Yudhiṣṭhira to demoralize Karṇa from the charioteer's seat when the decisive duel comes

title: The testing dialogue
description: Kṛṣṇa feigns propriety and tells the gopīs to return to their husbands; they argue the supremacy of prema over social dharma

title: The water-boon
description: At parting Ulūpī grants Arjuna invincibility in water and the obedience of all aquatic creatures

title: The Yakṣa-praśna (riddles of dharma)
description: Yudhiṣṭhira chooses to answer rather than drink, and the disguised guardian poses a rapid catechism of dharma — the mother heavier than earth, the greatest wonder being men's denial of death, conduct over birth

title: Trained by Droṇa
description: Knowing the prophecy, Droṇa accepts his destined killer as a pupil and teaches him the full dhanurveda

title: Tṛṇāvarta the whirlwind-demon
description: A demon in whirlwind form carries the child into the sky; Krishna grows immovably heavy and throttles him, crashing him dead onto a rock
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.7; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Two-year pregnancy and the flesh-ball miscarriage
description: Jealous of Kuntī, Gāndhārī strikes her womb and miscarries a lifeless ball of flesh after carrying it two years

title: Uddhava delivers Kṛṣṇa's message to the gopīs
description: At dawn the gopīs gather around Uddhava, who conveys Kṛṣṇa's impersonal jñāna-yoga consolation that the Lord is the Self of all and never separated from them

title: Urvashī curses Arjuna to be a eunuch
description: When Arjuna refuses her advances, Urvashī curses him to spend a year as the eunuch Bṛhannala

title: Uttanka and King Paushya trade and retract curses
description: Over a perceived insult Uttanka curses King Paushya to blindness and Paushya curses Uttanka to childlessness, then both retract

title: Śveta released by a sage at the tīrtha
description: A sage/ascetic intervenes at the holy ford and frees Śveta from the cycle of self-devouring, establishing the site's sanctity and the charter on charitable giving

title: Vidura's coded warning of the lac-house
description: As the Pāṇḍavas depart for Vāraṇāvata, Vidura warns Yudhiṣṭhira in coded Mleccha speech of the planned arson and arranges a miner's tunnel and a boat for their escape

title: Vow to fight for the losing side
description: Barbarīka vows to his mother to always fight for whichever side is losing, then rides toward Kurukṣetra to join the war

title: Vyāsa, Devala and Nārada console Yudhiṣṭhira
description: The sages console the grieving king, with Vyāsa arguing the slain went to heaven by kṣatriya-dharma and that expiation, not flight, is the king's path

title: Vyāsa grants Sañjaya divine sight (divya-dṛṣṭi)
description: After Dhṛtarāṣṭra declines restored eyesight, Vyāsa confers divya-dṛṣṭi on Sañjaya, making him invulnerable, unwearied, and able to perceive every act and thought on the battlefield so he can narrate the war

title: Yājñavalkya Teaches Janaka the Tattvas
description: Yājñavalkya expounds the Sāṃkhya enumeration of 24 tattvas, the 25th puruṣa, and the supreme 26th Īśvara to King Janaka

title: Yudhishthira's pre-war call for defectors
description: On the first day at Kurukshetra, Yudhishthira crosses to honor the elders and publicly invites anyone on the Kaurava side to join him

title: Abandonment of the infant Karṇa on the river
description: To hide her disgrace, Kuntī sets the armored infant Karṇa adrift in a basket; he is found and raised by the charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Rādhā

title: Abhimanyu breaks into the cakra-vyuha
description: Day 13: Drona forms the spinning cakra-vyuha; Abhimanyu, knowing only how to enter, breaks in while Jayadratha (by Shiva's boon) seals the gap behind him, trapping the boy alone

title: A celestial messenger offers bodily ascent to svarga
description: A devadūta arrives in a flying chariot to escort Mudgala in his own body to heaven, his merit having ripened

title: Aghāsura the python killed from within
description: The python-demon swallows the boys and calves; Krishna enters and swells until it chokes, and Aghāsura's liberated spirit merges into Krishna

title: Agni petitions Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna at the Yamunā
description: Agni, disguised as a tawny brāhmaṇa, asks Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna by the Yamunā to satisfy his hunger

title: Śalya made Karṇa's charioteer
description: Karṇa demands a driver equal to Kṛṣṇa and names Śalya; insulted at driving for a sūta, Śalya consents only on the condition he may say what he wishes

title: Among the six who killed Abhimanyu
description: Kṛtavarma is one of the six warriors who jointly broke and slew the lone Abhimanyu inside the Cakravyūha

title: Arjuna's Brihannala reveal at the cattle-raid
description: Brihannala retrieves the hidden Gandiva from the shami tree, takes the reins with Uttara as charioteer, and single-handedly routs the Kuru army with the Sammohana astra

title: Arjuna wins the Pashupatastra from Shiva
description: Performing fierce tapas, Arjuna duels Shiva disguised as a Kirata over a slain boar and is granted the supreme Pashupata weapon

title: Balarama returns from his Saraswati pilgrimage
description: Having stayed neutral on a tirtha-yatra along the Saraswati for the war's duration, Balarama returns to Kurukshetra exactly in time to preside as referee over his two pupils' mace-duel

title: Balarāma's fury and Kṛṣṇa's mediation
description: Balarāma rages at the seizure; Kṛṣṇa pacifies him and the Yādavas, and the marriage is celebrated openly

title: Bhima Carries the Pandavas from the Lacquer-House
description: When the Kauravas set the flammable house at Varanavata ablaze, Bhima carries Kunti and his four brothers out through the escape tunnel

title: Bhima's twin vows and Draupadi's vow
description: Bhima vows to tear open Duhshasana's chest and drink his blood and to break Duryodhana's thigh; Draupadi vows to leave her hair unbound until washed in Duhshasana's blood

title: Bhishma's vow
description: King Shantanu weds Ganga who bears Devavrata (Bhishma); to enable Shantanu's marriage to Satyavati, Bhishma takes the vow of lifelong celibacy and renounces the throne, earning the boon of death-at-will

title: Bhīṣma recites the Piṅgalā parable to Yudhiṣṭhira
description: From the bed of arrows, Bhīṣma quotes Piṅgalā's song as a Mokṣa-dharma proof-text on the cessation of craving

title: Bhīṣma refuses to continue the line
description: Satyavatī begs Bhīṣma to beget heirs or take the throne; he refuses both, bound by his vow of celibacy

title: Birth and rearing of Irāvān
description: Ulūpī bears Arjuna's son Irāvān (Tamil Arāvāṇ) and rears him in the Nāga world after Arjuna departs

title: Birth of Kṛṣṇa at Mathurā
description: Krishna is born in the prison of his uncle Kamsa at Mathura on the Yamuna in the Dvapara Yuga, later slaying Kamsa
source: Garuda Purana; Bhagavata Purana 10; Vishnu Purana

title: Boon from Śiva
description: After austerities Jayadratha wins from Śiva the power to check the four Pāṇḍavas (not Arjuna) for one day in battle

title: Chitrasena Captures Duryodhana
description: The gandharva Chitrasena, who taught Arjuna music in Amarāvatī, defeats and captures Duryodhana at the Ghoṣa-yātrā, only for the Pāṇḍavas to rescue him

title: Conscience without defection
description: Despite his dice-hall righteousness, Vikarṇa never crosses to the Pāṇḍavas like Yuyutsu; he stays loyal and fights for Duryodhana in the war

title: Death of Irāvān by Alambuṣa
description: The rākṣasa Alambuṣa beheads Irāvān through illusion-war; his fall (placed on the first or eighth day) grieves Arjuna

title: Devāpi and Bāhlīka set aside
description: Elder brother Devāpi (blemished/ascetic) and Bāhlīka are barred from Hastināpura's throne, which passes to Śāntanu
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22

title: Dhanvantari teaches Sushruta surgery
description: Sages led by Sushruta approach the Kashi king-physician to learn medicine, and he teaches them Shalya-tantra (surgery), transmitted as the Sushruta Samhita

title: Division of the one Veda into four and the four disciples
description: Vyāsa splits the single Veda into Ṛg, Yajur, Sāman and Atharva and entrusts each to Paila, Vaiśampāyana, Jaimini and Sumantu, with the itihāsa-purāṇa to Romaharṣaṇa
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva

title: Durvāsā declares Mudgala conquered and blesses bodily ascent
description: Defeated by the gleaner's unbroken forbearance and charity, Durvāsā praises his titikṣā and dāna and pronounces that he will ascend to heaven in his own body

title: Ekalavya surrenders his thumb as guru-dakṣiṇā
description: When Arjuna protests being outclassed, Droṇa demands Ekalavya's right thumb as his teaching-fee, and Ekalavya without hesitation severs his thumb, permanently crippling his archery and preserving Arjuna's primacy

title: First dance and disappearance
description: Kṛṣṇa dances with the gopīs but vanishes to curb the pride (garva) that arose in them

title: Gandhari's curse on Krishna
description: Charging Krishna with allowing the slaughter, Gandhari curses that in the thirty-sixth year his Yadava kin will destroy one another as the Kurus did and that he will die alone in the wilderness; Krishna accepts it as his own will

title: Ganesha Gita spoken to King Varenya
description: As Gajanana, Ganesha reveals the Ganesha Gita to King Varenya, teaching karma-, jnana-, and bhakti-yoga in a Ganesha-fied Bhagavad Gita

title: Garga's naming and the vision of the universe in his mouth
description: Sage Garga secretly names the child Kṛṣṇa, and Yaśodā, checking for eaten dirt, beholds the entire cosmos within his mouth before Yogamāyā restores her maternal love — the locus of vātsalya-rasa

title: Herald at Draupadī's svayaṃvara
description: Presides over his sister's bride-choice and secretly tracks the disguised Pāṇḍavas, identifying them to Drupada

title: Her sons and the dynastic collapse
description: Satyavatī bears Śāntanu two sons, Citrāṅgada (killed young) and Vicitravīrya, who dies childless of consumption, leaving her royal line on the brink of extinction

title: Hiḍimba-vadha (slaying of Hiḍimba)
description: Enraged by his sister's betrayal, Hiḍimba attacks; Bhīma fights him hand to hand and kills him, the first demon Bhīma slays

title: Indra's boon consecrating Kurukṣetra
description: Moved by Kuru's austerity, Indra (or Viṣṇu) grants that whoever dies at Kurukṣetra attains heaven, fixing it as the supreme dharma-kṣetra

title: Jāmbavān seizes the Syamantaka
description: The bear-king Jāmbavān slays the lion, takes the gem, and gives it to his infant to play with in his cave

title: Kṛṣṇa delivers the Anugītā to Arjuna
description: Arjuna confesses he has forgotten the Gītā's wisdom; unable to repeat it verbatim, Kṛṣṇa relays an old conversation of the same import (the Anugītā) on transmigration, karma, the guṇas, and mokṣa

title: Kali vows to destroy Nala and possesses him
description: The age-demon Kali, enraged Nala won the bride, waits twelve years for a ritual lapse then enters Nala; Dvāpara possesses the dice

title: Karna cast on the river
description: Fearing disgrace, Kunti seals the infant in a basket and floats him down the rivers to the Ganga

title: Karna defeats but spares the lesser Pandavas
description: Karna overpowers Nakula, Sahadeva and Yudhishthira but spares each, honoring his promise to Kunti to kill none of her sons but Arjuna

title: Kṛṣṇa's leaf-test
description: Disguised as a brāhmaṇa, Kṛṣṇa tests Barbarīka; the marking arrow pierces every leaf of a Pīpala tree and hovers over Kṛṣṇa's foot where a leaf is hidden

title: Kṛṣṇa's penance and boon of sons from Śiva
description: Kṛṣṇa narrates having propitiated Śiva by tapas to obtain sons (notably Sāmba) and boons, framing the Śaiva material

title: Kṛṣṇa's visit and Draupadī's grievance
description: Kṛṣṇa comes to Kāmyaka; Draupadī recounts the dice-hall outrage and the resolve for eventual war is renewed

title: Kṛṣṇa's welcome and the washing of feet
description: Kṛṣṇa rises from Rukmiṇī's couch, embraces his ragged friend, washes his feet and honours him as an equal while Rukmiṇī fans him

title: Kicaka's harassment of Sairandhri
description: Kicaka, the queen's brother and army-commander, becomes inflamed with lust for Sairandhri (Draupadi), assaults her, and humiliates her by kicking and dragging her in the assembly hall

title: Kripi married to Drona; birth of Ashvatthaman
description: Kripi is wedded to Drona, making Kripa the brother-in-law of Drona and uncle of their son Ashvatthaman

title: Krishna, Balarama and Sudama Study at Sandipani's Gurukula
description: Krishna, Balarama and the poor brahmin Sudama study the Vedas, 64 arts and weaponry at Rshi Sandipani's gurukula in Ujjain, where the Krishna-Sudama friendship begins

title: Krishna multiplies himself into every boy and calf
description: Krishna expands himself to become every missing cowherd boy and every calf, identical in form, voice, dress, habit and relationships

title: Krishna's boon to forgive a hundred offenses
description: At Shrutashrava's plea Krishna vows to pardon a full hundred offenses of Shishupala before exacting any penalty

title: Krishna's Vṛndāvana demon-slayings
description: Growing among the cowherds, Krishna and Balarāma slay the pastoral demons Pūtanā, Śakaṭa, the twin Arjuna trees, Kāliya, Dhenuka, Pralamba, Ariṣṭa, and Keśin in early form

title: Krishna welcomes and honours the beggar
description: Krishna rises from Rukmini's couch, embraces Sudama, seats him on his own bed, washes his feet, and Rukmini fans him

title: Kuntī lends Mādrī the Durvāsa mantra
description: At Pāṇḍu's request Kuntī shares one use of her deity-summoning invocation-mantra with Mādrī so the junior queen may also bear sons

title: Mahabharata War and Krishna's Departure
description: The Mahabharata war is fought near the Dvapara-Kali junction; Krishna's departure (3102 BCE) marks Kali Yuga fully entering, the traditional onset of the present age
source: Bhagavata Purana 1.15; Mahabharata; Surya Siddhanta epoch

title: Nahuṣa freed by Yudhiṣṭhira's riddles
description: Ages later the python Nahuṣa seizes Bhīma; Yudhiṣṭhira answers his dharma-riddles, freeing both Bhīma and the cursed king, who ascends to heaven

title: Nocturnal abduction of Aniruddha
description: Citralekhā flies by yogic power to Dwārakā and bears the sleeping Aniruddha through the air to Uṣā's apartment in Śoṇitapura

title: Omens at Dwarka and the divine weapons depart
description: Portents multiply at Dwarka as the 36th year comes; Krishna's Sudarshana Chakra, conch Panchajanya, chariot and horses, and Balarama's plough rise and vanish, the instruments of the avatar leaving first, and Krishna orders the fatal pilgrimage to Prabhasa

title: Pañcaśikha Instructs Janaka
description: Pañcaśikha teaches Janaka an austere atheistic Sāṃkhya of guṇas and discriminative knowledge, witnessing the Kapila-Āsuri-Pañcaśikha lineage

title: Paraśurāma's duel with Bhīṣma
description: Ambā appeals to Bhīṣma's guru Paraśurāma, who fights Bhīṣma in a multi-day stalemate at Kurukṣetra ended by the gods' and Nārada's intervention

title: Prabhasa praised in the Tirtha-yatra Parva
description: Pulastya and Lomasa/Dhaumya name Prabhasa as the foremost western tirtha, where gods and Soma bathe, during the Pandavas' forest pilgrimage

title: Proposing the dice-game
description: After Duryodhana's humiliation at the Rājasūya, Śakuni proposes a rigged dice-game and offers to play as proxy, knowing the secret of the dice

title: Rati reveals herself and teaches māyā
description: Grown Pradyumna recoils from Māyāvatī's courtship until she explains he is Kāma and she his wife Rati, then teaches him illusion-magic to defeat Śambara

title: Recitation of the thousand names
description: Bhīṣma recites the one thousand names of Viṣṇu (the sahasranāma) to Yudhiṣṭhira as the surest path freeing one from sorrow
source: Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva XIII.135 (Viṣṇu Sahasranāma main body)

title: Sañjaya narrates the war and recites the Bhagavad Gītā
description: Answering Dhṛtarāṣṭra's question 'dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre', Sañjaya frames the entire battle-narrative, reciting the Bhagavad Gītā verbatim ('Sañjaya uvāca'), narrating the Viśvarūpa, and pronouncing its closing benediction

title: Sanjaya's peace-embassy fails
description: Dhritarashtra sends Sanjaya with a message offering no land; Yudhishthira and Krishna expose its emptiness, refusing to surrender their birthright

title: Slaying of Keśin the horse-demon
description: Krishna thrusts his arm down the gaping throat of the giant horse-demon, swelling it until the demon bursts and splits in two
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.37; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5; Harivaṃśa

title: Slaying of the washerman
description: Krishna kills Kaṃsa's arrogant washerman who refuses festive garments, then dresses in the cloth

title: Sudama's Reunion with Krishna at Bet Dvaraka
description: The poor brahmin Sudama's pinch of beaten rice is repaid with untold wealth at Bet Dvaraka, a key bhakti parable of Krishna's love for the lowly

title: Takshaka steals the earrings
description: Takshaka, disguised as a naked mendicant, snatches the earrings Uttanka has set down and dives into a hole leading to Nagaloka

title: The avadhuta's teaching of the 24 gurus
description: Within the Uddhava Gita Krishna retells how a wandering avadhuta-brahmana, questioned by King Yadu, named 24 natural gurus as the source of his serene bliss

title: The Aśvamedha prescribed as expiation
description: To purge the sin of the war, Yudhiṣṭhira is told he must rule and later perform the horse-sacrifice as prāyaścitta

title: The Bhagavad Gita spoken
description: Krishna delivers his 700-verse teaching resolving Arjuna's paralysis through the imperishable atman, nishkama-karma, and the yogas of knowledge, action and devotion, climaxing in the Vishvarupa-darshana

title: The Bhramara-gītā — the gopī's Song to the Bee
description: A bumblebee alights and the chief gopī (read as Rādhā by later tradition), mad with love-in-separation, addresses it as Kṛṣṇa's fickle messenger, alternately rebuking and praising the absent Kṛṣṇa

title: The chariot-seizure at the goddess temple
description: As Rukmiṇī emerges from worshipping the goddess outside the city, Kṛṣṇa lifts her onto his chariot before the assembled kings and drives off toward Dwārakā

title: The deer and forest creatures enchanted
description: Does, birds, cows and calves are stilled and transfixed by the flute-song, drawing near Kṛṣṇa in love

title: The Dharma-vyādha teaches Kauśika
description: The righteous butcher of Mithilā delivers the Vyādha-gītā — that no duty is impure, svadharma done without malice does not defile, ahiṃsā is intention, and service to parents is the highest dharma

title: The Digvijaya: conquest of the four quarters
description: The four younger Pandavas subdue the four directions, bringing back vast tribute that ignites Duryodhana's envy

title: The fallen seed and the hawk
description: Called to the śrāddha hunt on his queen Girikā's fertile day, Vasu's seed falls; he sends it to her by a hawk, but it is dropped into the Yamunā during an aerial fight

title: The Four Gods Make Nala Their Messenger
description: En route to the svayaṃvara the four Lokapālas compel the truthful Nala to plead their suit to the very woman he loves

title: The gandharva marriage with the heir-condition
description: Dushyanta argues gandharva marriage lawful and weds Shakuntala on her binding condition that her son shall be heir-apparent; he departs giving no token, and Kanva blesses the union on his return

title: The guru-dakshina request
description: Asked his fee, Sandipani requests the return of his young son drowned in the sea at Prabhasa
source: Bhagavata Purana X.45; Harivamsha; Vishnu Purana 5

title: The horse reaches Maṇipura at the Aśvamedha
description: Years later the consecrated horse of Yudhiṣṭhira's sacrifice enters Maṇipura, where the grown Babhruvāhana greets Arjuna peaceably and is rebuked as unwarriorlike

title: The Kashi Abduction of Amba, Ambika, Ambalika
description: Bhishma storms the Kashi svayamvara and carries off the three princesses by force as brides for Vicitravirya, defeating the assembled kings and Shalva

title: The leap from the kadamba tree
description: Krishna climbs a kadamba on the bank and leaps into the venomous pool to purge the river

title: The lifting of Mount Govardhana for seven days
description: Kṛṣṇa uproots Govardhana and holds it aloft on his left little finger as an umbrella for seven days, sheltering the cowherds, gopīs and cattle until Indra's storm is spent
actors: the cowherds and cattle of Vraja
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.25; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 5

title: The meeting of Hanumān and Bhīma
description: Seeking the saugandhika flower, Bhīma cannot lift an old monkey's tail blocking his path; the monkey reveals himself as Hanumān, his elder half-brother, and blesses him

title: The night massacre of the sleeping camp
description: Ashvatthaman strangles Dhrishtadyumna, slays the five sons of Draupadi, cuts Shikhandin in two, and butchers the Panchala chiefs and host as they sleep while Kripa and Kritavarman fire the camp gates

title: The Pāṇḍavas reach Prabhāsa and the western Sarasvatī-mouth fords
description: Lomaśa's circuit reaches the western arc — Dvārakā, Piṇḍāraka and the radiant sea-ford of Prabhāsa where the Sarasvatī meets the ocean

title: The prophecy of Kaṃsa's doom
description: From the air the goddess mocks Kaṃsa that his slayer is already born elsewhere, sealing his fate

title: The putrakāmeṣṭi and the fire-birth of Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Draupadī
description: Seeking revenge on Droṇa, Drupada has Yāja and Upayāja perform a son-desiring sacrifice from which fire-born Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Draupadī arise

title: The Ranachhoda flight
description: Krishna walks out of Mathura unarmed and flees Kalayavana on foot, earning the epithet Ranachhoda ('deserter of battle') as bait for a trap
source: Bhagavata Purana X.51.1-6; Vishnu Purana V.23

title: The slaying of Mura
description: Kṛṣṇa beheads the five-headed daitya Mura with the Sudarśana cakra, earning the epithet Murāri; Mura's sons and Pīṭha are also slain

title: The three-year duel and death of Citrāṅgada
description: The two Citrāṅgadas duel for three years at Kurukṣetra; the gandharva slays the Kuru prince, who dies young and childless
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~101; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22.20; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: The Vasus Steal Nandinī; Vasiṣṭha's Curse
description: The eight Vasus steal Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Nandinī, and the enraged sage curses them to be born as mortals, with the instigator Dyaus condemned to a long mortal life

title: The viśvarūpa (cosmic-form) theophany
description: Gaṇeśa grants Vareṇya divine sight and reveals his all-pervading universal form containing all worlds and beings — the Gāṇapatya answer to Bhagavad Gītā 11

title: Transfer of Balarāma to Rohiṇī's Womb
description: The seventh embryo Śeṣa/Balarāma is mystically transferred by Yoga-māyā from Devakī's womb to Rohiṇī at Gokula, giving Balarāma the epithet Saṃkarṣaṇa

title: Ulupi goads Babhruvahana to fight
description: The Naga princess Ulupi rises from the earth and incites Babhruvahana to take up arms against his father, overriding his reluctance

title: Uttaṅka beholds Kṛṣṇa's Viśvarūpa and the Uttaṅka-megha boon
description: In the Āśvamedhika doublet Uttaṅka would curse Kṛṣṇa for the war, is shown the Universal Form, fails the Caṇḍāla-amṛta test, and is granted desert rain-clouds

title: Vasiṣṭha ascends to Sūrya and wins Tapatī's hand
description: The purohita Vasiṣṭha rises to the solar orb, asks Vivasvān for Tapatī on Saṃvaraṇa's behalf, and Sūrya consents

title: Vasudeva carries Krishna across the Yamuna
description: Vasudeva bears the newborn across the flooding Yamuna to Gokula, swapping him for Yashoda's just-born daughter Yogamaya

title: Vidura delivers the Vidura-nīti
description: Over eight chapters Vidura, incarnation of Dharma, pours out aphoristic counsel on the wise and the fool, kingship, truth and forgiveness, urging restraint of Duryodhana

title: Vidura protests Draupadī's outrage at the dice-game
description: At the rigged dice-game Vidura alone rises to denounce the assembly and the king as Draupadī is dragged in and disrobed, warning that adharma will consume the house

title: Vyāsa incubates the Kauravas in jars
description: Vyāsa divides the flesh-mass into 101 pieces sealed in ghee-pots, yielding the hundred Kauravas and Duḥśalā

title: Yudhiṣṭhira chooses Nakula
description: Offered one brother's life, Yudhiṣṭhira passes over Bhīma and Arjuna and asks for Nakula so that both his father's wives have a living son, prizing impartiality

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's fall at the dice-game
description: Lured into a rigged dice-game played by the cheating Śakuni, Yudhiṣṭhira loses wealth, kingdom, his brothers, himself, and finally Draupadī, triggering the disrobing

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's imperial Aśvamedha completed
description: After Arjuna's year-long horse-campaign the consecrated horse returns and Yudhiṣṭhira performs the full Aśvamedha with lavish gifts, proclaiming him cakravartin

title: Yuyutsu defects to the Pandavas
description: Yuyutsu alone of the entire Kaurava host answers Yudhishthira's invitation, renounces Duryodhana's cause, and crosses to fight on the Pandava side

title: Abhimanyu slain by six warriors
description: Inside the formation Abhimanyu kills thousands and slays Duryodhana's son Lakshmana, but is ganged upon by six maharathis and finally clubbed to death by Duhshasana's son, an open breach of the war-code

title: Adrikā the fish swallows the seed and bears twins
description: The apsarā Adrikā, cursed to be a fish, swallows the seed; caught by fishermen, she yields a boy and a girl and is freed from her curse

title: Śalya demoralizes Karṇa and the crow-and-swan parable
description: From the driver's seat Śalya praises Arjuna, predicts Karṇa's death, and mocks him with the haṃsa-kāka fable, sapping his spirit before the fatal duel

title: Ambā's tapas, Śiva's boon, and self-immolation
description: Out of human remedies, Ambā performs fierce austerities; Śiva grants she will cause Bhīṣma's death and remember her past life, and she immolates herself to hasten rebirth

title: Appointed Pāṇḍava commander-in-chief
description: Chosen as senāpati of the seven-akṣauhiṇī Pāṇḍava host on the strength of his destiny to break Droṇa

title: Arjuna nearly kills Yudhishthira; Krishna intervenes
description: When the wounded Yudhishthira reviles Arjuna and insults the Gandiva, Arjuna draws his sword to honor a vow to kill any who insults it; Krishna resolves the dilemma through casuistry without bloodshed

title: Arjuna's departure for the divine weapons
description: From Kāmyaka Arjuna journeys north to win the Pāśupata from Śiva and celestial astras from Indra and the world-guardians
source: Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Kairāta / Indralokābhigamana Parva ~38–41

title: Ashwatthama's night slaughter of the Pandava camp
description: Born as a Rudra-portion to Drona, the immortal cursed warrior Ashwatthama slaughters the Pandava camp by night

title: Balarama's Sarasvati tirtha-yatra
description: Declining to fight at Kurukshetra, Balarama makes a pilgrimage up the Sarasvati from its mouth at Prabhasa to its source

title: Balarāma routs the pursuing coalition
description: The Yādava force under Balarāma turns and shatters the pursuing army of Jarāsandha's allies, covering the escape of Kṛṣṇa's chariot

title: Bhima Slays Hidimba and Weds Hidimba
description: Bhima kills the cannibal rakshasa Hidimba in a wrestling match and weds his sister Hidimba, fathering Ghatotkaca

title: Bhima slays Kicaka
description: Lured to a night tryst in the dance-hall where Bhima lies in Sairandhri's place, Kicaka is seized and crushed into a shapeless ball of flesh, avenging Draupadi's humiliation

title: Birth and boyhood of Sarvadamana (Bharata)
description: Shakuntala bears a son of extraordinary power, Sarvadamana, raised in the hermitage, so strong he ties up lion and tiger cubs in play

title: Birth of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura
description: After Satyavati's sons die heirless, Vyasa fathers by niyoga the blind Dhritarashtra, the pale Pandu, and the wise Vidura (an incarnation of Dharma) on the widowed queens and a maid

title: Birth of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura
description: By niyoga, Vyasa fathers the blind Dhritarashtra, pale Pandu, and wise Vidura on the Kuru queens

title: Birth of Kṛṣṇa in Kaṃsa's Prison
description: Kṛṣṇa is born at midnight on Janmāṣṭamī in the prison cell as Devakī and Vasudeva's eighth child; the chains fall and the guards sleep

title: Birth of the twins Nakula and Sahadeva by the Aśvins
description: Mādrī cleverly invokes the twin Aśvins, who beget twin sons Nakula and Sahadeva in a single act, matching two of Kuntī's god-sons with one invocation

title: Blessing of Sudāmā the garland-maker
description: The flower-seller Sudāmā joyfully garlands the brothers and is blessed with wealth and devotion

title: Brahma-vimohana motivated by Aghāsura
description: Astonished by the Aghāsura feat, Brahmā steals the calves and boys, and Krishna multiplies himself to replace them for a year

title: Chitrasena teaches Arjuna music in Amarāvatī
description: During Arjuna's sojourn in Indra's heaven, Indra appoints the gandharva Chitrasena to teach him music, song and dance — training Arjuna later uses while disguised at Virāṭa's court

title: Citrāṅgadā's lament and the gem-revival
description: After Ulūpī goads Babhruvāhana into slaying Arjuna, Citrāṅgadā grieves and reproaches Ulūpī; Arjuna is revived by the Nāgamaṇi and the Vasus' curse is disclosed, and Citrāṅgadā is later invited to Hastināpura

title: Composition of the Mahābhārata, dictated to Gaṇeśa
description: Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata; Gaṇeśa scribes on condition of unbroken dictation, Vyāsa seeds knotted kūṭa-ślokas, and Gaṇeśa breaks his tusk to write

title: Damayantī Chooses Nala at the Svayaṃvara
description: Confronted with five identical Nalas, Damayantī recognizes the true mortal by his shadow, sweat and dusty feet and garlands him

title: Day 1 — Bhishma slays Shveta; Shalya slays Uttara
description: On the first day Bhishma kills Shveta son of Virata with a celestial weapon and Shalya kills prince Uttara, two of Virata's sons falling in a single day

title: Death of Vikarṇa and Bhīma's lament
description: Bhīma kills Vikarṇa among the hundred but uniquely mourns him, recalling his lone stand for Draupadī and praising him as a knower of dharma

title: Descent to the ocean and the sea-god's report
description: At Prabhasa the sea-god Varuna reports the boy was seized by a demon dwelling in the ocean

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra rejects the counsel
description: The blind king concedes Vidura's wisdom is just yet cannot break his love for Duryodhana and resigns to fate, the epic's tragedy in miniature

title: Discovery and imprisonment of Aniruddha
description: Bāṇa discovers the lovers, Aniruddha beats back the guards with an iron club, and Bāṇa binds him with the serpent-noose (nāgapāśa)
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.62; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Dāmodara — the butter-theft and binding to the mortar
description: Krishna breaks the butter-pot and steals butter; Yaśodā tries to bind him to a grinding-mortar but the rope always falls two finger-widths short until he consents to be bound, earning the name Dāmodara

title: Draupadi's vow of vengeance for the gem
description: Learning all her sons and kin are dead, Draupadi vows to fast to death unless Ashvatthaman is killed and the invulnerability-gem on his forehead is brought to her; Bhima races ahead in pursuit

title: Draupadī's svayaṃvara and the Pāṇḍava alliance
description: Drupada sets a bow-and-target test; Arjuna wins Draupadī, who becomes the common wife of the five Pāṇḍavas, sealing the Pāñcāla–Pāṇḍava alliance

title: Durvasa's Curse Separating Rukmini
description: Sage Durvasa, yoked to Rukmini's chariot by Krishna and Rukmini, curses that she will thirst and dwell apart, explaining her temple's location outside Dvaraka town

title: Durvāsā's kheer-test and Kṛṣṇa's mortal heel
description: Durvāsā orders Kṛṣṇa to smear boiling kheer over his body; Kṛṣṇa leaves only his soles unanointed, and the sage's boon makes his body invulnerable except at the unanointed sole — the fatal point later struck by the hunter Jara's arrow
source: Mausala Parva tradition with later Purāṇic/folk glosses (not in core Critical Edition, where Gāndhārī's and the Pindāraka sages' curses cause the doom)

title: Duryodhana's ill-omened birth spared
description: Despite evil omens and sages' warning to abandon him, Gāndhārī and Dhṛtarāṣṭra rear Duryodhana

title: Ekalavya allies with Jarāsandha against the Yādavas
description: As king of the Niṣādas, Ekalavya fights alongside Jarāsandha of Magadha in his invasions of Mathurā, hurling himself against the Yādavas

title: False accusation against Kṛṣṇa
description: Dwārakā suspects Kṛṣṇa of murdering Prasena for the gem after his request was refused; the slander spreads

title: Gaṅgā Bears the Vasus; Birth of Bhīṣma
description: To discharge Vasiṣṭha's curse, Gaṅgā bears the eight Vasus by King Śāntanu, drowning seven at birth to free them; the eighth, Dyaus, survives as Devavrata-Bhīṣma

title: Ganesha scribes the Mahabharata and breaks his tusk
description: Ganesha agrees to write Vyasa's Mahabharata; when his pen breaks mid-dictation he snaps off his own tusk to keep writing, becoming Ekadanta

title: Indra's submission and the Govinda-abhiṣeka
description: Humbled Indra descends, praises Kṛṣṇa with the Indra-stuti, and with the cow Surabhi anoints him, conferring the title Govinda
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.26–27; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 5

title: Jayadratha Seals the Breach
description: Jayadratha, using a boon from Shiva, holds the entry-point and turns back the other Pandavas, stranding Abhimanyu alone inside the formation

title: Kṛṣṇa lodges with Vidura during the embassy
description: Arriving as peace-envoy, Kṛṣṇa declines Duryodhana's lavish feast and stays at the humble home of the righteous Vidura

title: Kṛṣṇa restores Bhīṣma's faculties for the teaching
description: Kṛṣṇa grants the dying Bhīṣma freedom from pain and clarity of mind for the duration of his instruction, and Bhīṣma sings a hymn to Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa

title: Kṛṣṇa reveals the Viśvarūpa to Arjuna
description: Kṛṣṇa reveals his cosmic all-form (Viśvarūpa) to Arjuna on the battlefield, an infinite theophany of all worlds and time devouring the armies
source: Bhagavad Gītā 11; Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva; Bhāgavata 10.7

title: Karna found and raised by the suta couple
description: The childless charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Radha recover the basket at Campa and raise Karna as their own, branding him Sutaputra

title: King Pāṇḍu's Penance and the Birth of the Pandavas at Pandukeshwar
description: King Pandu does penance at Yogadhyan Badri to be cleansed of killing two mating deer; the Pandavas are born there and Pandu attains salvation

title: Kāliya's coiling and Krishna's release
description: Kāliya binds Krishna in his coils; the cowherds and parents swoon, Balarāma reassures them, and Krishna expands his body to break free

title: Kripa appointed first preceptor of the Kuru princes
description: Bhishma appoints Kripa as the first formal weapons-master of the Kaurava and Pandava boys, before Drona's arrival

title: Krishna earns the name Keśava
description: The slaying of Keśin becomes the narrative etiology of the epithet Keśava, 'slayer of Keśin', alongside the older lexical 'fine-haired' gloss

title: Krishna lifts Mount Govardhana
description: Krishna persuades the cowherds to worship Mount Govardhana instead of Indra, and when Indra sends rains he lifts the mountain as an umbrella, after which Indra consecrates him as Govinda

title: Krishna Restores Sandipani's Dead Son as Guru-Dakshina
