description: As guru-dakshina, Krishna and Balarama slay the demon Pancajana (taking the Pancajanya conch) and descend to Yama's realm to restore Sandipani's son lost in the sea at Prabhasa

title: Kuntī and Yudhiṣṭhira sanction the marriage
description: Hiḍimbī presses her suit; Kuntī and Yudhiṣṭhira assent on conditions, treating duty to a benefactor-suppliant as dharma

title: Kunti reveals Karna's birth to the Pandavas
description: Kunti discloses that Karna, whom they killed, was their eldest brother born to her by Surya before her marriage, overwhelming the Pandavas with fresh grief and remorse

title: Kuntī's svayaṃvara and marriage to Pāṇḍu
description: At her self-choice ceremony Kuntī garlands the Kuru king Pāṇḍu, becoming his senior queen (Mādrī being the second)

title: Kurukṣetra as the field of the Bhārata war
description: The consecrated ground becomes the battlefield of the eighteen-day war, named dharma-kṣetre kurukṣetre in the Bhagavad Gītā

title: Lakshmi incarnates as Rukmini with Krishna
description: When Vishnu descends as Krishna, Lakshmi incarnates as his chief queen Rukmini (and as Radha in devotional tradition)

title: Luring Kalayavana into the cave
description: Krishna leads the pursuing Kalayavana into a mountain cave where the ancient king Muchukunda sleeps, then slips aside

title: Marriage and arrival at Indraprastha
description: With dowry from the Vṛṣṇis, Arjuna brings Subhadrā to Indraprastha, where she wins over an initially displeased Draupadī

title: Marriage of Revati and Balarama
description: On Brahma's counsel Revati is married to Balarama, who taps her with the tip of his plough to reduce her from her earlier-yuga height to the stature of his own age

title: Marriage of Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī
description: Vasiṣṭha conveys Tapatī down; the two are wed on the mountain, and Saṃvaraṇa dwells there twelve years

title: Maya spared at the Khāṇḍava fire
description: Fleeing Agni's conflagration of the Khāṇḍava forest, Maya takes refuge with Arjuna, who with Kṛṣṇa spares his life

title: Mudgala questions the messenger about heaven's nature
description: Rather than accept blindly, Mudgala interrogates the envoy about svarga's joys and defects, learning that merit is exhausted and the soul falls back into rebirth

title: Nala loses his kingdom at dice and is exiled
description: Possessed Nala gambles away his entire kingdom to his brother Puṣkara and is stripped and exiled into the wilderness

title: Nara and Nārāyaṇa reborn as Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa
description: The twin sages take their final earthly descent as Arjuna (Nara) and Kṛṣṇa (Nārāyaṇa), their cross-yuga friendship explaining the inseparable Kurukṣetra bond
source: Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva / Nārāyaṇīya; Bhagavad Gītā

title: Śāntanu's accession at Hastināpura
description: Śāntanu is consecrated king of Hastināpura, ruling justly as a famed hunter-sovereign

title: One of the four Kaurava survivors of Day 18
description: After the eighteenth day only Duryodhana (dying), Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa and Kṛtavarma survive of the Kaurava host

title: Pandu's curse and birth of the Pandavas
description: Cursed by sage Kindama, Pandu cannot father children; Kunti and Madri invoke gods to bear Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva

title: Pāṇḍavas Worship Śiva at Sthāneśvar before the War
description: The Pāṇḍavas worship Śiva at Sthāneśvar Mahādev in Thanesar to secure victory before the Kurukṣetra war

title: Plot to seize Krishna
description: Duhshasana joins the cabal of Duryodhana, Shakuni, and Karna to arrest Krishna during the peace embassy; Krishna foils it with his cosmic form

title: Prime mover of the niyoga
description: After Bhīṣma twice refuses to take the throne or beget heirs, Satyavatī reveals her secret son Vyāsa, summons him by thought, and in haste arranges the niyoga that produces blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra, pale Pāṇḍu, and the maid's son Vidura

title: Pulastya Names Pushkar First of Tīrthas to Bhīṣma
description: In the Tirtha-yatra Parva sage Pulastya instructs Bhishma on holy fords, opening with Pushkar where Brahma and the gods are ever present, the textual root of its Adi Tirtha rank

title: Release of the sacrificial horse and Arjuna's campaign begins
description: The consecrated stallion is set loose to roam for a year; Arjuna is appointed its protector, instructed to conquer without needless slaughter, and follows it with an army

title: Reminiscence of the gurukula storm
description: The two friends recall their student days, especially the night they were caught in a forest storm gathering firewood for the guru

title: Rivers, clouds, trees and hill respond
description: Rivers halt to embrace Kṛṣṇa's feet, a cloud canopies him, the trees thrill with horripilation, and Govardhana is blessed by his touch

title: Sañjaya reports the war-books and carries each great death's news
description: Through the Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa and Śalya Parvas the battle is delivered as Sañjaya's running report to the king, including the news of the falls of Bhīṣma, Abhimanyu, Droṇa, Karṇa and finally Duryodhana

title: Satyavatī summons Vyāsa for niyoga
description: Satyavatī calls her pre-marital son Vyāsa to father heirs on the widows by niyoga, warning the queens to bear his fearsome appearance

title: Sealing the cakravyūha mouth
description: Using Śiva's boon, Jayadratha holds the formation's entrance shut, stranding Abhimanyu alone inside to be killed

title: Sparing Maya the Architect
description: Arjuna and Krishna spare the asura-architect Maya, who in gratitude builds the Pandavas' illusion-hall at Indraprastha

title: The butcher's past-life curse revealed
description: The butcher reveals he was a learned Brāhmaṇa in a former life, brought to the butcher's caste by a curse, now re-ascending through faultless duty and filial service

title: The celestial chariot descends for Mudgala
description: A devadūta arrives with a divine swan-drawn chariot to carry Mudgala bodily to svarga as reward for his merit

title: The death of Naraka
description: Kṛṣṇa severs Naraka's head with the cakra; Bhūmi returns the stolen treasures and Bhagadatta is installed; a variant has Satyabhāmā as the slayer

title: The dāna of the head
description: Recognising the danger of the vow, Kṛṣṇa begs Barbarīka's head as alms; bound by dāna-dharma Barbarīka offers it, asking to witness the war before he dies

title: The exile-stake and second dice-game
description: After Dhṛtarāṣṭra's boons free the Pāṇḍavas, a single decisive throw lost commits them to twelve years' forest exile and a thirteenth incognito year

title: The goddess departs to dwell on the Vindhyas
description: Having prophesied, the goddess declares she will take her abode on the Vindhya mountains and departs—the origin of Vindhyavāsinī

title: The gopīs reproach the absent Kṛṣṇa
description: Returning to Uddhava, the gopīs reproach Kṛṣṇa for abandoning them and ask only whether he remembers Vraja; Uddhava again assures them of his presence and return

title: The half-golden mongoose denounces the sacrifice
description: A mongoose with one golden side and a human voice declares the entire Aśvamedha worth less than a poor brāhmaṇa's single prastha of barley-flour

title: The kaḷappali — Aravān's self-sacrifice to Kālī
description: In the Tamil tradition Aravān, one of three flawless warriors bearing the thirty-two perfections, freely offers his own head to Kālī before the war to secure Pāṇḍava victory

title: The Lokapalas arm Arjuna
description: The world-guardians appear and bestow the danda, pasha, and antardhana weapons, and Indra invites Arjuna to heaven

title: The mace-duel and Duryodhana's broken thighs
description: In the gada-yuddha Bhima cannot beat the more skilled Duryodhana fairly; on Krishna's thigh-slapping cue he strikes a forbidden blow below the navel, shattering Duryodhana's thighs to fulfill his dice-hall vow

title: The mothers' and cows' affection deepens
description: Re-entering Vraja as all the boys and calves, Krishna is fondled by the mothers and cows whose love grows even more intense

title: The Pandavas Pursue Shiva as a Bull (Pancha Kedar)
description: Seeking absolution after Kurukshetra, the Pandavas pursue Shiva, who flees as a bull and dives into the earth, re-emerging in five parts to form the Pancha Kedar shrines

title: The Pāṇḍavas ascend to Badarī and the Nara-Nārāyaṇa-Gandhamādana heights
description: The northern leg of the circuit brings the Pāṇḍavas to the Himalayan hermitage of Nara-Nārāyaṇa at Badarī and the Kailāsa/Gandhamādana fords

title: The phala-śruti
description: The closing 'fruit of hearing' promises freedom from sin, sorrow, and fear and the attainment of eternal Brahman for the devotee of Vāsudeva

title: The Rajasuya sacrifice performed
description: Yudhishthira is consecrated samrat in the grand Rajasuya, the high-water mark of Pandava fortune

title: The rigged dice-game and Yudhiṣṭhira's total loss
description: Playing as Duryodhana's proxy with loaded dice, Śakuni wins Yudhiṣṭhira's wealth, kingdom, brothers, self, and finally Draupadī

title: The search and Kṛṣṇa-anukaraṇa
description: Maddened by separation the gopīs wander Vṛndāvana questioning nature and imitating Kṛṣṇa's deeds in total identification with him

title: The Yadava clan self-destructs in the brawl at Prabhasa
description: At a drunken festival Satyaki beheads Kritavarma after mutual taunts; the mob kills Satyaki and Pradyumna, and every Yadava who grabs the eraka reeds finds it transformed into an iron club, so brother slays brother until almost the entire Vrishni-Andhaka race lies dead, fulfilling the curse

title: The Yakṣa revealed as Dharma; brothers revived
description: Pleased by the son's equitable virtue, the Yakṣa reveals himself as Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira's divine father, restores all four brothers and returns the firesticks

title: Ulūpī goads Babhruvāhana against Arjuna
description: During Yudhiṣṭhira's Aśvamedha the horse reaches Maṇipura; Ulūpī rises from the earth and incites the reluctant Babhruvāhana to fight his father Arjuna

title: Ulūpī Weds Arjuna and Bears Irāvān
description: The nāga princess Ulūpī of the Airāvata line weds Arjuna in Nāgaloka and bears Irāvān, later reviving Arjuna after his death by Babhruvāhana

title: Uttanka descends into Nagaloka and burns it with the Agni-horse
description: Indra's vajra tunnels Uttanka into the serpent-world where, after the cosmic loom-vision, he blows into the fire-horse Agni, flooding Nagaloka with flame until the serpents return the earrings

title: Varuṇa grants the Gāṇḍīva, quivers, chariot, and Kṛṣṇa's weapons
description: Via Agni and Varuṇa, Arjuna receives the Gāṇḍīva bow, inexhaustible quivers and the kapi-dhvaja chariot; Kṛṣṇa receives the Sudarśana-cakra and Kaumodakī mace

title: Vicitravīrya consecrated as boy-king
description: With Citrāṅgada dead and heirless, the minor Vicitravīrya is consecrated king with Bhīṣma governing as regent
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~102; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: Vidura-niti delivered
description: During Dhritarashtra's sleepless night Vidura delivers a long aphoristic treatise on statecraft and ethics, urging the king to restrain Duryodhana and return the Pandavas' share

title: Virata's dice-blow and the reveal
description: Mistakenly crediting his son, Virata strikes Yudhishthira's face with a die; the disguises then fall and Virata becomes the Pandavas' first great royal ally

title: Vyasa Fathers the Kuru Heirs by Niyoga
description: When Vicitravirya dies childless and Bhishma refuses the widows, Satyavati summons Vyasa, who by niyoga fathers Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura

title: Vyāsa divides the Veda into four
description: At the Dvāpara–Kali junction Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana Vyāsa splits the single Veda into four for the diminished memory of Kali-Yuga humans

title: Vyāsa Teaches Śuka, Who Merges into Brahman
description: Vyāsa teaches his son Śuka the path to Brahman; perfected, Śuka ascends and merges into the all-pervading Brahman

title: Yogamaya escapes Kamsa as the goddess
description: Kamsa dashes the substituted girl on a rock, but she rises as the eight-armed goddess, declares his slayer is born, and vanishes

title: Yuyutsu fights the eighteen-day war on the Pandava side
description: Yuyutsu serves through the Kurukshetra war under Yudhishthira as the hundred sons of Gandhari are slain one by one

title: Abduction of the Kashi princesses
description: Bhishma seizes the three Kashi princesses for Vicitravirya; Amba, in love with Shalva, is released and vows vengeance, reincarnating as Shikhandin

title: Abhimanyu Slays Lakshmana
description: Trapped within the array, Abhimanyu wreaks havoc and slays Lakshmana, Duryodhana's son, enraging the king

title: Śalya appointed fourth and final Kaurava commander
description: After Karṇa's death the Kauravas make Śalya — who broke Karṇa's morale — the fourth generalissimo on Day 18
source: Mahābhārata, Karṇa Parva close / Śalya Parva (Śalya-vadha)

title: Ambikā shuts her eyes; birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra
description: Terrified, Ambikā keeps her eyes shut during the niyoga, and Vyāsa decrees her son will be born blind — Dhṛtarāṣṭra

title: Aravān's three last wishes and the Mohinī marriage
description: Granted last wishes, Aravān asks not to die unmarried; Kṛṣṇa takes the female form Mohinī to wed him for one night

title: Arjuna ascends to Indra's heaven
description: Matali carries Arjuna to Amaravati, where he learns the vajra and celestial weapons and is taught song and dance by Citrasena

title: Arjuna's sunset vow (Pratijñā)
description: Arjuna swears to slay Jayadratha before sunset the next day or enter the fire, for barring the rescue of Abhimanyu

title: Arjuna subdues the Trigartas
description: The surviving grandsons of the Trigarta kings attack to avenge their war-dead elders; Arjuna subdues them after a hard fight

title: Arjuna's vow to slay Jayadratha
description: Learning of his son's death, Arjuna swears to slay Jayadratha by next sunset or enter the fire himself; Drona walls Jayadratha off with three nested formations

title: Babhruvāhana kills Arjuna
description: In the duel Babhruvāhana's arrows strike Arjuna dead; Citrāṅgadā laments and reproaches Ulūpī

title: Babhruvāhana slays Arjuna
description: In the duel before Maṇipura, Babhruvāhana's arrows strike Arjuna dead, while Citrāṅgadā reproaches Ulūpī for engineering the parricide

title: Balarama perceives the secret
description: Puzzled by the increased affection, Balarama perceives that all the boys and calves are Krishna's self-manifestations and Krishna reveals the truth to him

title: Balarama's fury and Krishna's justification
description: Enraged at the illegal thigh-blow, Balarama raises his plough-weapon against Bhima and must be restrained by Krishna, who justifies the blow as retribution for Duryodhana's own adharma

title: Balarama's yogic departure as Shesha-Ananta
description: Krishna finds Balarama seated in yoga giving up his body; a great white serpent issues from his mouth and glides into the sea received by Ocean and the Nagas, Balarama returning to his nature as the cosmic serpent Shesha/Ananta

title: Balarāma's Sārasvata tīrtha-yātrā ending at Samanta-pañcaka
description: To avoid taking sides in the Kurukṣetra war, Balarāma undertakes an upstream pilgrimage along the Sarasvatī, touching Prabhāsa, Vinaśana, Saptasārasvata, Kapālamocana, Pṛthūdaka and the other fords in sequence, arriving back at Samanta-pañcaka just as the war closes; his route fixes the literary spine of Kurukṣetra's inner tīrtha-ring

title: Bhṛgu Teaches Bharadvāja on Cosmogony and Varṇa
description: Bhṛgu teaches the Mind-born primeval Being and a color-coded varṇa, but Bharadvāja's objection resolves that caste is by conduct, not birth

title: Bhima kills Duhshasana and drinks his blood
description: Bhima seizes Duhshasana, tears open his chest and drinks his blood, fulfilling his dice-hall vows; Draupadi at last binds up the hair she had left loose since her disrobing

title: Bhima Slays Bakasura of Ekachakra
description: Bhima eats the food tribute meant for the man-eating rakshasa Baka and breaks his back across his knee, freeing the town

title: Bhima slays the 105 Upakicakas
description: When Kicaka's kinsmen seize Sairandhri to burn her on his pyre, Bhima uproots a tree, charges in, and kills all 105 Upakicakas, freeing her

title: Bhīṣma accepts the role of teacher on the arrow-bed
description: Empowered by Kṛṣṇa, the dying Bhīṣma agrees to instruct Yudhiṣṭhira in rāja-, āpad-, and mokṣa-dharma until the sun turns north

title: Birth of Abhimanyu
description: Subhadrā bears Abhimanyu at Indraprastha, the prodigy who will die breaking the cakravyūha

title: Birth of Matsya, founder of the Matsya line
description: The male twin is kept by Vasu and becomes the righteous king Matsya, ancestor of the Cedi/Matsya royal stock

title: Birth of the Pandavas
description: Cursed Pandu's heirs are born via Kunti's mantra summoning gods — Yudhishthira (Dharma), Bhima (Vayu), Arjuna (Indra), and via Madri the twins Nakula and Sahadeva (Ashvins); Kunti's earlier secret son by Surya is Karna

title: Breaking the twin arjuna trees — liberation of Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva
description: Bound to the mortar, Krishna crawls between two arjuna trees and uproots them, freeing the Yakṣa sons of Kubera, Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva, whom Nārada had cursed to be trees
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.10–11; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Bāṇāsura Defeated by Kṛṣṇa
description: The thousand-armed Śiva-devotee Bāṇāsura, whose daughter Uṣā loved Aniruddha, is defeated by Kṛṣṇa, his arms shorn to four, and spared at Śiva's plea

title: Building and Rule of Dvārakā by Kṛṣṇa
description: Krishna builds and rules the golden many-gated sea-fortress city of Dwarka after leading the Yadavas out of Mathura
source: Garuda Purana; Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana

title: Challenge to Karna at the graduation tournament
description: Kripa challenges Karna to declare his royal lineage before combat with Arjuna, exposing his unknown birth

title: Chitrasena captures Duryodhana at the Ghoṣa-yātrā
description: At the Ghoṣa-yātrā the gandharva Chitrasena defeats and captures Duryodhana and his retinue; in a dharma-inversion the exiled Pāṇḍavas rescue their persecutor, Arjuna invoking his friendship with Chitrasena

title: Compilation of the eighteen Purāṇas and the Bhāgavata
description: Vyāsa compiles the eighteen Mahā-Purāṇas; reproached by Nārada for not glorifying the Lord, he composes the Bhāgavata and teaches it to Śuka

title: Counsel before the war
description: Gāndhārī protests Draupadī's outrage and refuses Duryodhana victory, saying where there is dharma there is victory

title: Day 3 — Krishna's first wheel-charge against Bhishma
description: Seeing Arjuna fight half-heartedly while Bhishma devastates the army, Krishna breaks his vow, seizes a chariot-wheel and rushes at Bhishma; Arjuna restrains him and swears to fight in earnest

title: Dharma's boon of non-recognition
description: Dharma grants that during the coming thirteenth year of incognito living the Pāṇḍavas pass unrecognized, plus inner conquest over the six foes, easing the year in Virāṭa's kingdom

title: Dhenukāsura the donkey-demon of the Tālavana slain
description: Balarāma shakes down palm fruit, is kicked by the donkey-demon, and kills it and its herd by flinging them into the palms, opening the Tālavana
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.15; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Draupadī's disrobing triggered by the dice-loss
description: Śakuni's victory leads directly to Draupadī being dragged and stripped in the assembly, seeding the war-vows including Sahadeva's vow to kill Śakuni

title: Dushyanta's denial and the celestial voice naming Bharata
description: At court Dushyanta publicly disowns Shakuntala, who rebukes him with a fierce dharma speech; a sky-voice declares the child his and decrees the name Bharata, after which the king reveals his denial was a deliberate strategy

title: Forest retirement and death
description: Having secured the next generation, Satyavatī withdraws to the forest in vānaprastha with Ambikā and Ambālikā—warned by Vyāsa not to witness the coming Kuru doom—and there ends her life

title: Freeing and marriage of the 16,100
description: Kṛṣṇa frees the 16,100 captive women and weds them so they live with honour, totalling 16,108 with the eight principal queens

title: Gaṅgā marriage and the secret-vow condition
description: Śāntanu weds Gaṅgā on the condition that he never question or restrain her

title: Grief of Chitrangada and Babhruvahana
description: Babhruvahana resolves to die beside his slain father while Chitrangada laments and reproaches Ulupi for engineering the parricide

title: Śikhaṇḍin, the instrument of Bhīṣma's fall
description: Drupada raises Śikhaṇḍin (rebirth of Ambā) as a son; the yakṣa sex-exchange makes the loophole by which Bhīṣma is felled

title: Incineration of Kalayavana by Muchukunda's glance
description: Kalayavana kicks the sleeper, mistaking him for Krishna; the wakened Muchukunda's first glance burns Kalayavana to ashes by an old boon
source: Bhagavata Purana X.51.13-14; Vishnu Purana V.23; Harivamsha

title: Kṛṣṇa eats the pinch of rice; Rukmiṇī stays his hand
description: Kṛṣṇa snatches the hidden bundle and eats a fistful of flattened rice with relish; Rukmiṇī (Lakṣmī) catches his hand as he reaches for a second, the love-gift sufficing to grant Sudāmā all fortune

title: Karna becomes Parashurama's disguised pupil
description: Rejected by Drona, Karna goes to Parashurama claiming to be a brahmana to learn brahmastra-grade weapons

title: Kṛṣṇa slays Ekalavya
description: Kṛṣṇa kills Ekalavya in battle, commonly by crushing him with a hurled boulder; in the Harivaṃśa's kinship framing this is the slaying of a lost Yādava cousin

title: Kṛṣṇa tracks the gem to the cave
description: To clear his name Kṛṣṇa traces Prasena's route, finds the bodies and the dead lion, and follows bear-tracks to a cave

title: Kauśika sent home to serve his parents
description: The butcher tells Kauśika he neglected his aged parents for tapas; the twice-humbled ascetic returns home, tends them, and is reconciled to true dharma

title: Krishna abducts Rukmini
description: Krishna elopes with Rukmini on the eve of her wedding to Shishupala, publicly humiliating him and seeding his enmity

title: Krishna eats the pinch of flattened rice
description: Krishna snatches the hidden bundle, declares that even a leaf or fruit offered with love satisfies Him, and eats a fistful of rice; Rukmini stays His hand at the second

title: Krishna slays Kaṃsa at Mathurā
description: Summoned to Mathurā's bow-festival, Krishna and Balarāma kill the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa and the wrestlers Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika, then Krishna drags Kaṃsa from his throne and kills him, reinstating Ugrasena

title: Kuntī refuses a further mantra-use
description: When Pāṇḍu asks for one more invocation so Mādrī might have more sons, Kuntī refuses, unwilling to be outdone, fixing the Pāṇḍava count at five

title: Loss of divine sight; capture and release by Sātyaki
description: At Duryodhana's fall Vyāsa's boon lapses and Sañjaya loses his divine sight; seized by Sātyaki and about to be killed, he is freed at Vyāsa's intervention and returns to the king

title: Marriage of Abhimanyu and Uttaraa
description: Arjuna declines Uttaraa for himself (his dance-pupil) and weds her to his son Abhimanyu at Upaplavya, sealing the Matsya-Pandava-Yadava alliance

title: Marriage of Bhīma and Hiḍimbī
description: Bhīma weds Hiḍimbī on terms: she has him by day but he returns nightly to the Pāṇḍavas, and the union lasts only until a son is born — the first non-human marriage of the exile

title: Mass cremation and water-offering for the dead
description: At Yudhishthira's command Vidura cremates the slain warriors with full Vedic rites, and both armies' survivors descend to the Ganga to offer water-libations, Kunti openly making the offering for Karna

title: Maya fetches treasure from the Himalayan Lake Bindusaras
description: Spared from the Khandava fire, the asura architect Maya brings gem-quality stone, a mace, and the conch Devadatta from Lake Bindusaras (once Vrishaparvan's) to build the Mayasabha at Indraprastha

title: Mudgala refuses heaven and seeks mokṣa
description: Learning that even paradise ends in a fall, Mudgala declines the chariot, abandons the gleaning-rite, cultivates supreme equanimity, and pursues the imperishable supreme station beyond rebirth

title: Nala deserts Damayantī in the forest
description: Tormented by Kali, Nala cuts away half his sleeping wife's garment and abandons her in the night

title: Nemīnātha's renunciation, omniscience and liberation on Girnar
description: The 22nd Tīrthaṅkara Nemīnātha (Ariṣṭanemi), Kṛṣṇa's cousin, attains dīkṣā, kevala-jñāna and nirvāṇa on the Ujjayanta peak

title: Nārada brings news; Yādava march on Śoṇitapura
description: Nārada reveals Aniruddha is Bāṇa's captive; Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and Pradyumna lead the Vṛṣṇi host (on Garuḍa) to besiege Śoṇitapura

title: Nārada's Keśava-stuti prophecy
description: Nārada hails the victorious Krishna with a hymn foretelling Kaṃsa-vadha, the Mathurā and Dvārakā deeds, and his unburdening role at Kurukṣetra

title: Pāṇḍu's curse by the sage Kindama
description: Pāṇḍu kills the sage Kindama mating in deer form and is cursed to die the instant he approaches a wife in desire, making natural fatherhood impossible

title: Rebirth as Drupada's child Śikhaṇḍin(ī)
description: Ambā is reborn to King Drupada of Pāñcāla as a daughter raised secretly as a son, Śikhaṇḍin, precipitating a marriage crisis with Daśārṇa

title: Return to Dwārakā and recognition
description: Māyāvatī flies Pradyumna back to Kṛṣṇa's palace; his likeness to Kṛṣṇa and Nārada's narration reveal him as Rukmiṇī's lost son, to the city's joy

title: Rukmī defeated, spared at Rukmiṇī's plea, and disfigured
description: Kṛṣṇa overpowers the pursuing Rukmī and is about to behead him; Rukmiṇī intercedes, so Kṛṣṇa instead shaves his head in patches as disgrace; Balarāma reconciles the family

title: Sanatsujatiya teaching
description: The boy-sage Sanatsujata teaches the still-sleepless king that death is not annihilation but ignorance, expounding Brahman, true knowledge, and liberation

title: Slaying of Duhshasana and blood-drinking
description: On the 17th day Bhima smashes Duhshasana from his chariot, tears open his chest, and drinks his blood, fulfilling the twin dice-hall vow

title: Slaying of Putana
description: The demoness sent with poisoned breast-milk is drained of life by the suckling infant Krishna and granted liberation

title: Slaying of Sisupala
description: After Sisupala exceeds his hundred forgiven offenses objecting to Krishna's first-honour, Krishna beheads him with the Sudarsana Cakra and his radiance merges into Krishna

title: Slaying of the conch-demon Panchajana
description: Krishna kills the asura Panchajana, who lived in the sea in the form of a conch and had swallowed the boy
source: Bhagavata Purana X.45; Harivamsha; Vishnu Purana 5

title: Sole surviving son of Dhritarashtra
description: After Kurukshetra every Kaurava is dead by Bhima's vow; Yuyutsu alone of Dhritarashtra's sons survives, having crossed sides and slept outside the doomed camp

title: Straightening of Trivakrā (Kubjā)
description: Krishna straightens the deformed hunchback maidservant Trivakrā, who had anointed him with sandal-paste
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.42 (visit X.48); Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: The 18-Day Mahābhārata War at Kurukṣetra
description: Eighteen akṣauhiṇīs assemble between the Sarasvatī and Dṛṣadvatī and fight the 18-day Kaurava–Pāṇḍava war that seals the Dvāpara–Kali yuga-turn

title: The Brahmashiras duel and Vyasa's intervention
description: Cornered at Vyasa's hermitage, Ashvatthaman invokes the Brahmashiras on a blade of grass; Arjuna counters with his own Brahmastra, and Vyasa and Narada step between to halt the world-ending collision

title: The brahmin's curse and the iron pestle
description: Sages cursed by Yadava youths' prank decree that Samba will bear an iron pestle destroying the clan; ground to powder and cast into the sea, it returns as eraka reeds and an iron splinter

title: The burning of Khāṇḍava and the slaughter of fleeing creatures
description: Agni blazes on every side while Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa drive escaping beasts and beings back into the flames

title: The dance upon the hoods (Kāliya-nartana)
description: Krishna mounts the serpent's heads and dances upon them, crushing each rearing hood as gods drum and shower flowers

title: The footprints and the favoured gopī
description: The gopīs find paired footprints showing Kṛṣṇa led one favoured gopī away, then find her abandoned for her own pride; commentators read Rādhā here

title: The Gods Grant Nala Boons and the Marriage
description: Pleased, the four gods grant Nala gifts of fire, water, dharma and cooking; the couple marries and bears Indrasena and Indrasenā

title: The gopīs envy the flute (veṇu-asūyā)
description: The gopīs voice jealousy of the bamboo flute that drinks the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's lips, wondering what austerities it performed to earn the touch

title: The Iron-Club Curse on the Yadavas
description: Sages mocked when young Yadavas disguised Samba as a pregnant woman curse that he will bear an iron club destroying the clan; Samba births an iron bolt ground to powder and cast into the sea

title: The Kāśī svayaṃvara abduction
description: Bhīṣma raids the joint svayaṃvara of the three Kāśī princesses and carries off Ambā, Ambikā, and Ambālikā by force as brides for Vicitravīrya

title: The messenger's honest account of svarga's defects
description: Asked to describe heaven truthfully, the messenger reveals svarga is earned by merit, exhausted by enjoyment, accrues no new karma, breeds discontent, and ends in a sorrowful fall to rebirth

title: The Mārkaṇḍeya discourses
description: The deathless sage Mārkaṇḍeya recounts to Yudhiṣṭhira the pralaya-vision, Naḷa–Damayantī, Sāvitrī, the Matsya-flood, the Dharma-vyādha and the Kali-yuga prophecy

title: The Parashurama-Bhishma Duel
description: Spurned Amba appeals to Parashurama, who fights Bhishma a multi-day duel at Kurukshetra that ends inconclusively when the gods intervene

title: The Pāṇḍavas Visit Pushkar
description: The Pandavas visit Pushkar on their pilgrimage from the Kamyaka forest, attesting its established sanctity by the Pandava era

title: The Python Seizes Bhīma
description: Ages later during the Pāṇḍava exile, the boon-strengthened serpent Nahuṣa seizes Bhīma in a mountain cave and drains his strength

title: The third Sauptika night-raider
description: Kṛtavarma, after Kṛpa's failed dissent, guards the camp gates and sets the fires while Aśvatthāman slaughters the sleeping Pāñcāla–Pāṇḍava camp

title: The Uñchavṛtti gleaner-family's fourfold gift to Dharma
description: A starving Kurukṣetra gleaner-brāhmaṇa, his wife, son and daughter-in-law each give their own portion of barley-flour to a guest who is Dharma in disguise, dying of hunger but ascending to heaven

title: The witnessing head over Kurukṣetra
description: Kṛṣṇa immortalises Barbarīka's head and sets it on a high hill to watch the entire eighteen-day war

title: The yoga of liberation and surrender
description: The Gītā closes with total surrender (prapatti/śaraṇāgati) to Gaṇeśa as the supreme secret and the promise of release, adapting Bhagavad Gītā 18

title: Twelve-year drought and ruin of the kingdom
description: During the king's absence Indra withholds rain for twelve years; famine and disorder weaken Hastināpura

title: Uddhava departs for Badarikashrama
description: After the final bhakti teaching Uddhava, overwhelmed, takes leave of Krishna and proceeds to Badarikashrama to practice renunciation

title: Uddhava is humbled and exalts the gopīs' love
description: After months in Vraja Uddhava declares the gopīs' unlettered love supreme over all jñāna and yoga, praying to be reborn as a shrub of Vṛndāvana to receive the dust of their feet

title: Unbroken generalship through the 18-day war
description: Holds supreme Pāṇḍava command from day 1 to the end, arranging the army's daily counter-formations

title: Uttanka discharges the fee before sunset
description: The fire-horse carries Uttanka back to deliver the earrings in time, and Veda explains all the omens he met

title: Vasudeva Carries Kṛṣṇa Across the Yamunā to Gokula
description: Vasudeva carries the infant Kṛṣṇa across the flooding Yamunā to Gokula, exchanging him for Nanda and Yaśodā's newborn daughter Yoga-māyā, who announces Kaṃsa's doom

title: Vidura speaks the Vidura-nīti and resigns his post
description: On the eve of war Vidura pours out his eight-chapter aphoristic discourse on nīti to the sleepless king, and renounces his ministerial post and weapons to take no part in the war

title: Vyāsa relays the Haṃsa-gītā to Yudhiṣṭhira
description: In the post-war Mokṣadharma frame, Vyāsa recalls and recounts the ancient swan-Brahmā discourse to Yudhiṣṭhira as a purātana itihāsa on the highest good

title: Yudhiṣṭhira receives the akṣaya-pātra from Sūrya
description: In exile Yudhiṣṭhira propitiates Sūrya, who grants the inexhaustible vessel that feeds the Pāṇḍavas' guests until Draupadī finishes her daily meal

title: Śalya's Day 18 rampage
description: Śalya fights furiously, scattering the Pāṇḍavas and wounding Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Sātyaki and the twins, fighting like Yama

title: Amba's Rebirth as Shikhandin
description: After tapas and Shiva's boon to be the cause of Bhishma's death, Amba immolates herself and is reborn as Shikhandin, child of Drupada, who obtains manhood by exchanging sex with a yaksha

title: Ambālikā turns pale; birth of Pāṇḍu
description: Ambālikā blanches with dread at Vyāsa, and her son is born pale — Pāṇḍu, the pallid king

title: Ambā released and the marriages
description: Ambā is freed after revealing her prior pledge to Śālva; Ambikā and Ambālikā are wed to Vicitravīrya at Hastināpura

title: Arjuna defeats Vajradatta of Prāgjyotiṣa
description: Vajradatta, son of the slain Bhagadatta, rides his war-elephant against Arjuna; a fierce three-day duel ends in Vajradatta's submission

title: Arjuna slays Karna's son Vrishasena
description: Keeping his fresh vow to avenge Abhimanyu, Arjuna kills Karna's son Vrishasena before his eyes with razor-arrows, breaking the grief-stricken Karna's spirit

title: Ashvatthaman redirects the weapon into Uttara's womb
description: Unable to withdraw his weapon, Ashvatthaman redirects it into the wombs of the Pandava women, especially Uttara, to extinguish the line; Krishna vows to revive the slain embryo and names him Parikshit

title: Authorship of the Brahma Sūtras (Bādarāyaṇa)
description: Under the name Bādarāyaṇa, Vyāsa is the traditional author of the Brahma Sūtras founding the Vedānta darśana, with a scholarly debate over the identity

title: Bharata crowned Cakravartin and namesake of the land
description: Dushyanta installs Bharata as crown prince; Bharata becomes a universal sovereign whose conquests give his name to the Bharatas and the subcontinent Bharatavarsha, continuing the Paurava-Kuru line

title: Bhima kills Jarasandha
description: Jarasandha of Magadha is slain by Bhima, clearing the way for Yudhishthira's Rajasuya

title: Bhima Slays Kirmira and Jatasura
description: During the exile Bhima kills the rakshasa Kirmira in the Kamyaka forest and later slays Jatasura who abducted his kin

title: Birth of Ghaṭotkaca
description: By rākṣasa speed Hiḍimbī conceives and bears Ghaṭotkaca the same day; he matures at once and departs with the boon to come at a thought

title: Birth of Satyavatī / Matsyagandhā
description: The female twin, fish-scented, is given to the fisherman-chief and grows up as Satyavatī (Matsyagandhā), secretly carrying royal Lunar blood

title: Birth of the Kauravas
description: Gandhari bears from a mass of flesh divided into a hundred jars the hundred Kauravas led by Duryodhana, plus a daughter Duhshala

title: Birth of Yudhiṣṭhira by Dharma
description: At Pāṇḍu's request Kuntī invokes Dharma and bears Yudhiṣṭhira, the eldest Pāṇḍava and embodiment of righteousness

title: Breaking of Kaṃsa's bow
description: Krishna strings and snaps the great ceremonial bow of the Dhanur-yajña, then beats off the guards
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.42; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Condensed Mahābhārata and Kṛṣṇa carita
description: The Agni Purāṇa gives a précis of the Yādava birth of Kṛṣṇa, his Vṛndāvana/Mathurā exploits, and the Pāṇḍava–Kaurava conflict and war

title: Damayantī curses the hunter and reaches Chedi
description: Abandoned Damayantī curses a lustful hunter dead by her chastity, then is taken in as an attendant in Chedi and recognized by her lotus-mark

title: Day 8 — Iravan beheaded by Alambusha
description: Iravan, Arjuna's son by the Naga princess Ulupi, fights brilliantly but is beheaded by the rakshasa Alambusha, while Ghatotkaca dominates the field with illusions

title: Death of Ketumāna at Kurukṣetra
description: Ekalavya's son Ketumāna, a Niṣāda warrior, fights and is slain on the Kaurava side in the great Kurukṣetra war

title: Death of Pāṇḍu by Mādrī's embrace
description: Overmastered by desire in spring, Pāṇḍu embraces Mādrī despite her warning, and the Kindama curse strikes him dead at the touch

title: Deaths of Uttara and Virata in the war
description: Prince Uttara is slain by Shalya on the first day (his brother Shveta by Bhishma); Virata is killed by Drona on the 17th day, ending the Matsya royal house

title: Draupadi Becomes Wife to the Five Pandavas
description: On Kunti's unseeing instruction to 'share it among you,' Draupadi becomes the common wife of all five Pandavas

title: Draupadi binds her hair in Duhshasana's blood
description: Bhima carries the blood to Draupadi, who at last binds the hair loosed since the dice-hall, completing the vengeance loop

title: Drowning of the seven Vasus
description: Gaṅgā drowns her first seven newborn sons (the released Vasus) while the vow-bound Śāntanu watches in silence

title: Duryodhana humiliated in the Mayasabhā
description: Duryodhana mistakes the illusion-floor for water and falls into a pool, his shame seeding the dice-game and the Kurukṣetra war

title: Duryodhana left dying appoints Ashvatthaman
description: Mortally wounded but still alive at the lake, Duryodhana reviles Krishna for the unfair killings and survives into the night to appoint Ashvatthaman as the last commander

title: Ekalavya's thumb as guru-dakshina
description: The self-taught Nishada prince Ekalavya surpasses Arjuna, and Drona demands his right thumb to preserve Arjuna's supremacy

title: False-sunset slaying of Jayadratha
description: Kṛṣṇa veils the sun to feign sunset; Jayadratha exposes himself and Arjuna beheads him as the sun reappears

title: Founding of Dvārakā
description: To escape Jarāsandha's relentless sieges and Kālayavana, Krishna leads the Yādavas west and builds with Viśvakarman the island-fortress city of Dvārakā in the sea

title: Held off during Abhimanyu's death
description: On day 13 he and the Pāṇḍava leaders are blocked by Jayadratha and cannot reach Abhimanyu trapped in the cakravyūha

title: Indra's failed defense of the forest
description: Indra leads the gods and pours rain to save Khāṇḍava, but Arjuna's arrow-canopy holds them off until Indra desists

title: Kṛṣṇa Delivers the Bhagavad Gītā at Jyotisar
description: As the armies face off at Jyotisar, Kṛṣṇa speaks the Bhagavad Gītā to Arjuna and grants the viśvarūpa-darśana under the immortal banyan

title: Kali Vows to Destroy Nala
description: Arriving too late and enraged that a mortal won the bride the gods coveted, the age-demon Kali vows to destroy Nala and lurks twelve years for an opening

title: Kṛṣṇa's Infant Līlās at Gokula
description: At Gokula the infant Kṛṣṇa slays Pūtanā, Śakaṭāsura and Tṛṇāvarta, steals butter, and is bound to the mortar in the damodara-līlā

title: Kṛṣṇa subdues Śiva (Hari–Hara combat)
description: Śiva sallies on Nandin to defend his devotee Bāṇa; Kṛṣṇa neutralizes him with the Jṛmbhaṇāstra (yawn-weapon) without insult

title: King Nala Released from Śani's Affliction
description: Under Saturn's malefic grip King Nala loses his kingdom and is parted from Damayanti; bathing in the Nala Tirtham and worshipping at Tirunallar, he is freed from Sani's affliction and regains throne and queen

title: Kripa present at the dice-hall
description: Kripa is among the elders present at the dice game and the disrobing of Draupadi but does not prevent it

title: Krishna's false sunset and the slaying of Jayadratha
description: Day 14: Krishna covers the sun feigning sunset; Jayadratha exposes himself and Arjuna beheads him, shooting the head into his meditating father Vriddhakshatra's lap so the boon recoils and bursts the father's head

title: Krishna's peace embassy to Hastinapura
description: Krishna goes personally to ask for only five villages; he lodges with Vidura, visits Kunti, and pleads in the Kaurava court, but Duryodhana refuses even a needle-point of land

title: Krishna sustains the substitution for a full year
description: Krishna maintains himself as all the boys and calves for one complete earthly year, a mere moment on Brahma's time-scale

title: Launch of the Tīrtha-yātrā
description: From the exile-forest the Pāṇḍavas begin the great pilgrimage of Bhārata's fords, catalogued by Pulastya/Nārada and guided by Lomaśa

title: Manu Instructs Bṛhaspati on the Self
description: Bṛhaspati questions Manu, who teaches the field and knower of the field, the supremacy of jñāna, and the ascent to the supreme Self

title: Marriage at Dwārakā and Rukmiṇī as Lakṣmī-incarnate chief queen
description: Kṛṣṇa weds Rukmiṇī with full rites; she becomes paṭṭa-mahiṣī, identified as Lakṣmī/Śrī incarnate

title: Marriage to Rukmavatī and birth of Aniruddha
description: Pradyumna weds Rukmī's daughter Rukmavatī and begets Aniruddha; at the wedding-festivities Balarāma kills Rukmī in a dice-quarrel

title: Migration from Gokula to Vṛndāvana
description: Alarmed by the prodigies and demon-deaths, the cowherds under Upananda move the community from Gokula to Vṛndāvana, closing the infancy arc

title: Mohinī's widowhood and mourning
description: After Aravān is sacrificed at dawn, Kṛṣṇa-as-Mohinī mourns him as a widow before resuming male form

title: Mārkaṇḍeya narrates the upākhyāna to Yudhiṣṭhira
description: Within the forest exile, the deathless sage Mārkaṇḍeya tells the Mudgala parable to Yudhiṣṭhira as the epic's definitive teaching that even svarga is to be renounced for Brahman

title: Muchukunda Incinerates Kalayavana
description: Awakened from his boon of long sleep in Dvapara, Muchukunda's glance incinerates Kalayavana, linking the Solar line to Krishna's story

title: Mudgala refuses heaven and turns the chariot away
description: Learning that svarga is impermanent (anitya), Mudgala reasons a reward that must be lost is no true gain and dismisses the chariot, declining bodily ascent

title: Niyoga and the births of Dhritarashtra, Pandu, Vidura
description: Vyasa fathers Dhritarashtra (born blind), Pandu (born pale), and Vidura (born wise to a maidservant) on the widows by niyoga

title: Nārada's tour of the 16,108 palaces
description: Nārada finds Kṛṣṇa simultaneously present in all 16,100 palaces, each wife believing him hers alone, demonstrating his yoga-māyā

title: Pandavas recover weapons from the shami tree (Ayudha Puja gloss)
description: The Pandavas retrieve their hidden weapons from the shami tree at the close of their incognito year, linked to Ayudha Puja's Shami-puja strand

title: Parashurama's curse on Karna
description: After Karna endures a worm boring his thigh without flinching, Parashurama deduces his kshatriya birth and curses that his memory of the supreme astra will fail at his greatest need

title: Pāñcāla seizure and forest exile
description: Sudāsa of Pāñcāla drives Saṃvaraṇa from Hastināpura; the king lives in forest exile on the Sindhu for twelve years
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Sambhava/Tāpatya strata; Pauravā genealogy

title: Pralambāsura slain by Balarāma's fist
description: A demon disguised as a cowherd carries Balarāma off in a play-game, then is smashed dead by a single fist-blow to the head
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.18; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Pre-war counsel and embassy
description: Drupada urges diplomacy, sending his purohita as envoy to Hastināpura, and is named a commander-candidate of the Pāṇḍava host

title: Procession to Kurukṣetra and scorched nails
description: On the field her grief-glance through the blindfold scorches Yudhiṣṭhira's nails before she relents

title: Recitation of the thousand Rudra-Śiva names and phala-śruti
description: Kṛṣṇa utters the thousand names (Sthāṇu, Hara, Mahādeva, etc.) closing with the fruit-promise of release and union with Śiva

title: Revival by the Nāgamaṇi
description: Ulūpī summons the serpent-realm resurrection jewel (Mṛtasaṃjīvanī / Nāgamaṇi) and revives the slain Arjuna

title: Revival of Arjuna by the Nagamani
description: Ulupi supplies the Naga revival-gem (Sanjivana/Nagamani), placed on Arjuna's chest, and Arjuna is restored to life

title: Sañjaya follows the king to the forest and departs to the Himālaya
description: Sañjaya consoles the broken Dhṛtarāṣṭra, accompanies him, Gāndhārī and Kuntī into forest vānaprastha, escapes the forest fire that kills them, and finally goes north to the Himālaya to end his days in asceticism

title: Sex-change via the yakṣa Sthūṇa
description: The yakṣa Sthūṇakarṇa exchanges sex with Śikhaṇḍin; Kubera's curse fixes the maleness on Śikhaṇḍin for life, defusing the Daśārṇa war

title: Shiva Flees as a Bull at Kedarnath
description: The Pandavas seek Shiva at Kedarnath to expiate the Kurukshetra slaughter; Shiva flees as a bull and dives into the ground, leaving the worshipped hump and the Panch Kedar

title: Slaying of Shakatasura
description: Baby Krishna overturns and destroys the cart-demon with a kick

title: Sātyaki beheads Kṛtavarma at Prabhāsa
description: In the drunken Yādava brawl at Prabhāsa, Sātyaki taunts Kṛtavarma over the night-massacre and beheads him, igniting the Mausala self-slaughter of the clan
source: Mahābhārata, Mausala Parva 3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa XI.30

title: Submergence of Dvārakā
description: After Krishna's departure the city of Dwarka sinks into the sea, marking the hinge into the present Kali Yuga

title: Sudama departs without begging
description: Content merely to have seen Krishna, Sudama never voices his poverty and leaves having received (he thinks) only the Lord's affection

title: Sudāmā departs without begging
description: Too abashed to voice his poverty, Sudāmā never asks for anything and leaves content merely to have seen Kṛṣṇa

title: Susharma's Trigarta cattle-raid
description: The Trigarta king Susharma raids Matsya's cattle and captures King Virata; the four Pandavas rescue Virata, rout the Trigartas, and capture Susharma, whom Yudhishthira mercifully frees

title: The 28-day cave-fight with Jāmbavān
description: Kṛṣṇa duels the bear-king Jāmbavān alone for twenty-eight days until Jāmbavān's strength fails

title: The first game of dice
description: Playing for Duryodhana, the cheating Shakuni wins everything from Yudhishthira in escalating stakes down to his brothers, himself, and finally Draupadi

title: The Gopī-gītā
description: Reassembled on the Yamunā bank the gopīs sing the 19-verse Song of the Gopīs of longing, the locus classicus of love-in-separation

title: The half-heard cakravyūha womb-lesson
description: In the folk motif, Subhadrā falls asleep during Arjuna's narration, so the unborn Abhimanyu learns only how to enter the cakravyūha, not exit

title: The hunter Jara's arrow and Krishna's departure
description: As Krishna lies in meditation, the hunter Jara mistakes his raised foot for a deer and shoots him with the very iron splinter from the cursed club; Krishna consoles and blesses Jara, then withdraws into his supreme abode, ending the Krishna avatar and marking the onset of Kali Yuga

title: The Killing of Abhimanyu
description: A ring of Kaurava maharathis disarms the weaponless sixteen-year-old Abhimanyu and Duhshasana's son strikes him dead with a mace, the moral nadir of the war

title: The mongoose gilded by the gleaners' crumbs
description: Rolling in the scattered leftover flour turned half the mongoose to gold; it wanders sacrifices ever after seeking to gild its other half, but no rite matches the gleaners' gift

title: The pleas of the Nāga-wives (Nāga-patnī-stuti)
description: Kāliya's wives bow and hymn Krishna as the Supreme, begging mercy, and Kāliya himself submits

title: The second dice-game and the exile-stake
description: Śakuni wins a second match staking thirteen years' exile, sending the Pāṇḍavas into the forest

title: The verdict — Sudarśana alone won the war
description: After the war the witnessing head declares it saw no human warrior win, only Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana cakra and the Goddess's tongue drinking blood; the heroes were mere instruments

title: The Yadava Massacre at Prabhasa
description: Drunk on maireya at the Prabhasa festival, the Yadavas quarrel and uproot the lethal eraka reeds as clubs, slaughtering one another until nearly all the Vrishnis die

title: The Yadava mausala at Prabhasa
description: The Vrishni-Andhaka chiefs migrate to Prabhasa, fall to drink and quarrel, and slaughter one another with iron clubs sprung from the eraka reeds, annihilating the Yadava race

title: The Yakṣa Praśna
description: After his four brothers drink and die at a guarded lake, Yudhiṣṭhira answers a Yakṣa's riddles, chooses to revive Nakula for impartial dharma, and the Yakṣa — his father Dharma — revives all four and grants undetected passage of the thirteenth year

title: Third demonic birth: Sisupala and Dantavakra slain
description: The pair are reborn as the human kings Sisupala (beheaded by the Sudarsana Cakra) and Dantavakra (killed by Krishna), their radiance merging into Krishna to discharge the curse

title: Tulādhāra Instructs Jājali
description: A heavenly voice tells the penance-proud ascetic Jājali he is unequal to the humble grocer Tulādhāra, who expounds ahiṃsā and honest livelihood as true dharma

title: Uddhava's farewell and report to Kṛṣṇa
description: Bowing to the gopīs and declaring their devotion the rarest thing in the three worlds, Uddhava returns to Mathurā and reports their love to Kṛṣṇa

title: Urvashi's curse on Arjuna
description: Spurned by Arjuna, the apsara Urvashi curses him to be a eunuch, which Indra softens to last only one year of his choosing

title: Uttanka receives Krishna's Vishvarupa darshana
description: In the Ashvamedhika version, an enraged Uttanka makes to curse Krishna for the war's carnage but is shown the Universal Form and taught the war's necessity for dharma

title: Veṇu-gītā as overture to the rāsa cycle
description: The flute-song kindles the gopīs' longing that the rāsa-līlā will consummate, opening the mādhurya song-cycle before the vastra-haraṇa intervenes

title: Vidura's death and merger into Yudhiṣṭhira
description: In forest penance Vidura casts his life-breaths and tejas into Yudhiṣṭhira by yogic power, both being portions of Dharma; a heavenly voice forbids cremating the yogin's body, closing Yama's curse-arc

title: Viśvakarmā raises Dvārakā in a single night
description: At Kṛṣṇa's request Viśvakarmā raises the sea-girt capital Dvārakā in a single night on land reclaimed from the ocean

title: Winning of the conch Panchajanya
description: From the slain demon's shell Krishna takes the conch Panchajanya, his lifelong emblem and war-conch
source: Bhagavata Purana X.45; Harivamsha; Vishnu Purana 5

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's Dharma-Catechism Frees Nahuṣa
description: Yudhiṣṭhira answers the serpent's riddles on dharma and varṇa, satisfying Nahuṣa, who releases Bhīma, sheds the serpent body, and ascends to heaven

title: Yuyutsu made steward of Hastinapura
description: In the war's aftermath Yuyutsu is given charge of the surviving women, the treasury, and governance of a depopulated Hastinapura under Yudhishthira's reign

title: Abhimanyu's death and Uttaraa widowed pregnant
description: Abhimanyu is killed in the cakravyuha on the 13th day, leaving Uttaraa widowed while carrying his only child

title: Arjuna destroys the Nivatakavachas and Hiranyapura
description: As guru-dakshina to Indra, Arjuna destroys the Nivatakavacha danavas of the sea and the flying demon-city Hiranyapura

title: Arjuna's Oath to Kill Jayadratha
description: Finding his son dead, Arjuna swears to kill Jayadratha before sunset the next day or enter fire, a feat Krishna later engineers

title: Arjuna spares the Saindhava forces at Duḥśalā's plea
description: In the Sindhu country of the dead Jayadratha, the bereaved widows and boy-heir give battle; Arjuna spares them when Duḥśalā pleads and her grandson faints

title: Arjuna's Union with Ulupi
description: During his pilgrimage-exile Arjuna is drawn under the Ganga by the Naga princess Ulupi, fathering Iravan

title: Balarama's Departure at Prabhasa
description: Balarama withdraws into yoga on the Prabhasa shore and the white serpent Shesha, whose portion he was, issues from his mouth into the sea, his return to source

title: Balarama's yogic departure
description: Balarama gives up his body in yoga on the Prabhasa shore; the serpent Shesha issues from his mouth into the sea

title: Banishment of Kāliya to Ramaṇaka Dvīpa
description: Krishna spares Kāliya and orders him with his kin back to Ramaṇaka, the footprint-mark protecting him from Garuḍa; the Yamunā is cleansed

title: Beheading of Droṇa
description: After the Aśvatthāman half-truth makes Droṇa lay down arms in yoga, Dhṛṣṭadyumna seizes him by the hair and severs his head, fulfilling the birth-prophecy

title: Bhima Splits Jarasandha
description: Bhima wrestles Jarasandha for many days and, on Krishna's split-leaf hint, rends him in two and hurls the halves apart so they cannot rejoin, freeing the captive kings

title: Bhishma Appointed Kaurava Commander
description: Duryodhana names Bhishma supreme commander; Bhishma accepts on condition he not kill the Pandavas and will not fight while Karna is in the field

title: Birth of Bhīma by Vāyu
description: Kuntī invokes the wind-god Vāyu and bears the immensely strong Bhīma, making him a brother of Hanumān

title: Birth of Pradyumna
description: Rukmiṇī's first son Pradyumna is born, recognized as Kāmadeva reborn, continuing the Vṛṣṇi line through his son Aniruddha

title: Brahma's return and the theophany of four-armed Vishnu-forms
description: Brahma returns to find both companies coexisting and sees every boy and calf revealed as a four-armed Narayana worshipped by all beings, falling into total vimohana

title: Condensed Kṛṣṇa biography (Brahma Purāṇa)
description: A compact Kṛṣṇa-carita: birth at Mathurā, Gokula childhood, slaying of Kaṃsa, the Dvārakā years, and his role in the Mahābhārata era

title: Day 9 — Krishna's second wheel-charge
description: In despair at Arjuna's reluctance to kill his grandfather, Krishna again leaps down and charges Bhishma with a wheel; Arjuna restrains him a second time and vows to slay Bhishma next day

title: Death in the Mausala fratricide
description: Thirty-six years after Kurukṣetra, Pradyumna falls at Prabhāsa in the cursed club-slaughter of the Vṛṣṇi-Andhakas with almost the whole clan

title: Death of Śalya by Yudhiṣṭhira's dart
description: At midday Yudhiṣṭhira hurls a consecrated golden śakti that pierces Śalya's chest, killing the last Kaurava commander; his brother and son fall soon after

title: Death of Drupada at Droṇa's hands
description: On the fifteenth day Drupada is slain by his lifelong enemy Droṇa, just before Droṇa is beheaded by Drupada's son Dhṛṣṭadyumna

title: Death of Kālayavana by Mucukunda's gaze
description: Krishna lures the foreigner Kālayavana into the cave of the sleeping king Mucukunda, whose boon-given gaze incinerates him — the origin of Krishna's epithet Raṇchoḍ

title: Disclosure of the Vasus' curse and expiation of Bhishma's death
description: Ulupi reveals the death was orchestrated so Arjuna would fall by his son's hand, expiating the Vasus' curse for slaying Bhishma unfairly behind Shikhandi

title: Disclosure of the Vasus' curse and reconciliation
description: Ulūpī reveals she orchestrated the death to expiate the Vasus' and Gaṅgā's curse for Arjuna's unfair slaying of Bhīṣma; the family is reconciled and invited to the Hastināpura sacrifice

title: Dissolution of the marriage and Hiḍimbī's return
description: The compact fulfilled by the son's birth, Hiḍimbī takes Ghaṭotkaca to the rākṣasa realm to raise him while Bhīma rejoins the Pāṇḍavas

title: Drona defeats Drupada via his pupils
description: Drona demands as guru-dakshina that his pupils defeat Drupada; Arjuna captures him and Drona takes half his kingdom, sowing Drupada's hunger for a son to kill Drona

title: Drona vs Drupada and the guru-dakshina war
description: Humiliated by Drupada, Drona has his pupils capture him and takes half Panchala, sowing Drupada's hunger for a son to kill Drona

title: Durvasa's curse and the lost ring (Kalidasa's version)
description: In Abhijnanashakuntalam, Durvasa curses the distracted Shakuntala that the king will forget her until he sees his signet ring, which she then loses in a river, leading to Dushyanta's blameless rejection

title: Ekalavya's thumb
description: Drona trains the princes in archery and demands Ekalavya's thumb as guru-dakshina

title: Escape of Aśvasena the serpent
description: The Nāga Aśvasena, son of Takṣaka, escapes the fire by his mother's aid and Indra's wind, beginning his enmity with Arjuna

title: Fall of Bhīṣma on the Bed of Arrows
description: On day 10 Bhīṣma is felled by Arjuna (with Śikhaṇḍin before him) and lies on a bed of arrows at Bhīṣma-kund, withholding death until uttarāyaṇa

title: Fathering Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura by niyoga
description: Summoned by Satyavatī, Vyāsa begets Dhṛtarāṣṭra (blind), Pāṇḍu (pale) and Vidura (by the maidservant) on Vicitravīrya's widows by levirate

title: Fulfillment of the companion thigh-vow on Duryodhana
description: The twin vow's other half is discharged when Bhima breaks Duryodhana's bared thigh in the Shalya Parva, closing the oaths sworn over Draupadi's outrage

title: Goading against peace and the plot to seize Kṛṣṇa
description: Śakuni stands with the war-party, hardens Duryodhana against reconciliation, and joins the scheme to arrest Kṛṣṇa during the peace embassy

title: Śikhaṇḍin as instrument of Bhīṣma's fall on day 10
description: Refusing to fight one born a woman, Bhīṣma lowers his weapons before Śikhaṇḍin; Arjuna, shielded behind him, fells Bhīṣma onto the bed of arrows, fulfilling Ambā's vow of vengeance

title: Journey to Yama's realm
description: The boy not found in the demon, Krishna and Balarama go to Yama's city Samyamani and Krishna blows the Panchajanya to summon him

title: Kali Possesses Nala and Rigs the Dice
description: Catching a ritual impurity, Kali enters Nala's body while Dvāpara possesses the dice, and goads Puṣkara to challenge Nala to gambling

title: Killing of the elephant Kuvalayāpīḍa
description: At the arena gate Krishna fells Kaṃsa's rogue war-elephant and its mahout, tearing out a tusk
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.43; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Kāliya-Damana
description: Kṛṣṇa subdues the many-hooded serpent Kāliya in the poisoned Yamunā pool and dances on his hoods

title: Kripa among the killers of Abhimanyu
description: On day 13 Kripa is one of the warriors who surround and kill the disarmed Abhimanyu inside the Chakravyuha

title: Krishna honored with the agra-puja at the Rajasuya
description: At Yudhishthira's consecration Bhishma nominates Krishna for the foremost guest-honor and Sahadeva performs the arghya to him

title: Krishna manifests the Vishvarupa in court
description: When Duryodhana's faction moves to seize the unarmed envoy, Krishna laughs and reveals his cosmic universal form, terrifying the court; the embassy formally fails

title: Krishna's curse on Ashvatthaman
description: The head-gem is cut from Ashvatthaman's forehead leaving an unhealing wound, and Krishna curses him to wander the earth alone for 3,000 years, friendless and diseased, an immortal misery

title: Krishna's Worship-Image Survives Dwaraka's Flood
description: Krishna foretells that his worship-image will float free when the sea engulfs Dwaraka at the Dvapara-Kali hinge; Guru (Brhaspati) and Vayu recover it and install it at Guruvayur with Parashurama's aid

title: Maya builds the illusion-hall of Indraprastha
description: The asura-architect Maya Dānava designs the wondrous illusion-hall (Māyā-sabhā) for Yudhiṣṭhira at the Pāṇḍavas' capital Indraprastha

title: Mādrī entrusts the twins to Kuntī
description: Mādrī commits Nakula and Sahadeva to Kuntī's care, asking she raise all five boys impartially, making Kuntī mother of five though she bore three

title: Medhāvin Urges His Father to Renounce
description: The precocious son Medhāvin urges his complacent father to renounce now since death does not wait, reversing the expected hierarchy

title: Muchukunda's awakening, hymn, and departure to penance
description: Waking in the Dvapara, Muchukunda recognizes Krishna, offers the Muchukunda-stuti, and departs north to Gandhamadana/Badarikashrama for austerities

title: Mudgala seeks mokṣa beyond heaven and rebirth
description: Renouncing his livelihood and all desire, Mudgala fixes on the changeless supreme state, attaining the highest perfection (mokṣa) from which there is no return

title: Narakāsura slain by Kṛṣṇa
description: The tyrant Narakāsura, who imprisoned 16,000 women, is slain by Kṛṣṇa with Satyabhāmā, commemorated as Naraka Caturdaśī (Diwali)

title: Pandavas Pursue Shiva and Kedarnath Hump Forms
description: Seeking absolution for kin-slaying after the Mahabharata war, the Pandavas pursue Shiva, who flees as a bull and dives into the ground leaving his hump at Kedarnath, founding the jyotirlinga

title: Pradyumna routs Skanda
description: Pradyumna wounds Skanda (Kārttikeya), who flees the field bleeding, while Balarāma scatters Bāṇa's ministers

title: Regent during the elders' forest-retreat
description: When Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, and Vidura withdraw to the forest, Yuyutsu is left to look after Hastinapura as trusted caretaker-regent

title: Satyaki beheads the meditating Bhurishravas
description: Arjuna shoots off Bhurishravas's sword-arm to save Satyaki; Bhurishravas sits in praya, and Satyaki, against all protests, beheads the one-armed meditating man, a flagrant Pandava breach of the war-code

title: Seizure of the Pārijāta and defeat of Indra
description: Kṛṣṇa returns Aditi's earrings to Svarga, uproots the celestial Pārijāta tree for Satyabhāmā, and defeats Indra and the Devas who resist

title: Slaying of Trinavarta
description: The whirlwind-demon carries Krishna aloft, but the child grows heavy and strangles him

title: Sparing of the eighth son and Gaṅgā's departure
description: Śāntanu breaks his vow to save the eighth child (Dyaus, the future Bhīṣma); Gaṅgā explains the curse, names him Devavrata, and departs with him

title: Subhadrā's grief at Abhimanyu's death
description: After Abhimanyu is killed on the 13th day, Subhadrā laments alongside the widowed Uttarā

title: Substituted maid; birth of Vidura
description: Asked to approach Vyāsa again, Ambikā sends her handmaid in her place; the unafraid maid is blessed with the wisest son, Vidura, the incarnation of Dharma

title: The Brahmana's cow-curse on Karna
description: Karna accidentally kills a brahmana's cow and is cursed that his chariot-wheel will sink into the earth when he most needs to be steady in battle

title: The Chandala-amrita test and the Uttanka-megha clouds
description: Uttanka refuses water (secretly amrita) offered by Indra disguised as a Chandala, failing the test of equanimity; Krishna then grants that desert rain-clouds, the Uttanka-megha, will rise at his wish

title: The disrobing of Draupadi
description: Duhshasana drags Draupadi into the assembly and attempts to strip her, but endless garments appear so she cannot be disrobed; she poses her unanswered question on dharma

title: The divine-eye threnody
description: With a boon of divine sight Gāndhārī surveys the corpse-strewn field and laments the slain corpse by corpse to Kṛṣṇa

title: The falling-head boon recoils on Vṛddhakṣatra
description: Arjuna shoots Jayadratha's severed head into his meditating father's lap; it rolls to the ground and Vṛddhakṣatra's own head bursts

title: The Ghoṣa-yātrā — capture and rescue of Duryodhana
description: Duryodhana's cattle-expedition to Dvaitavana ends with the gandharva Citrasena capturing him; Arjuna and Bhīma rescue their enemy on Yudhiṣṭhira's order

title: The homeward reflection
description: On the road back Sudāmā marvels at the Lord's love and concludes Kṛṣṇa withheld wealth lest prosperity make him forget God

title: The hovel transformed into a palace
description: On returning, Sudama finds his hut turned into a resplendent jewelled palace and his wife radiant, Krishna having silently granted untold wealth unasked

title: The Kaurava cattle-raid (Go-grahana)
description: The Kauravas strike undefended Matsya from the north to rustle the cattle and flush out the Pandavas, forcing the disguised Arjuna to come to its defense as charioteer to prince Uttara

title: The Nagastra deflected by Krishna
description: Karna looses a serpent-arrow animated by the snake Ashvasena; Krishna presses the chariot down with his foot so it strikes Arjuna's diadem instead of his head, and Karna refuses to fire it twice

title: The return and consolation
description: Kṛṣṇa reappears, explains he withdrew to deepen their love, and confesses he can never repay it (na pāraye 'ham)

title: Vasiṣṭha restores Saṃvaraṇa to the throne
description: Returning as purohita, Vasiṣṭha re-consecrates Saṃvaraṇa, who recovers Hastināpura and the kingship from the Pāñcālas

title: Vasudeva's death and the funerals at Dwarka
description: Krishna's father Vasudeva gives up his life in yoga; Arjuna performs his funeral and the last rites for Balarama, Krishna and the slain Yadavas, and four of Vasudeva's wives and some of Krishna's and Balarama's wives mount the pyre as sati

title: Vasu's sons seed the Cedi and Magadha dynasties
description: Vasu's sons found regional kingdoms; Bṛhadratha establishes the Magadha (Bārhadratha) line leading to Jarāsandha, while another holds Cedi
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (~63); Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19

title: Vicitravīrya's death of consumption, childless
description: After seven years of marriage Vicitravīrya dies young of consumption (rāja-yakṣma), leaving both queens widowed and heirless and the Kuru line at the brink of extinction
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~103; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22.21

title: Yudhiṣṭhira as Kaṅka at Virāṭa's court
description: In the incognito year Yudhiṣṭhira serves King Virāṭa as the brāhmaṇa dice-master Kaṅka, surviving undetected through the term

title: Annihilation of Drupada's line in the night-raid
description: Aśvatthāman massacres the sleeping Pāñcālas, including Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, ending Drupada's house and his vengeance

title: Arjuna defeats Meghasandhi of Magadha
description: Meghasandhi, grandson of Jarāsandha, challenges Arjuna at Rājagṛha and is defeated, then submits

title: Arjuna retrieves his weapons and reveals himself
description: Arjuna drives to the shami tree, recovers the hidden arms, strings the Gandiva and blows the conch Devadatta, then discloses his true identity to the astonished prince Uttara

title: Arjuna's Arrow Springs Bāṇgaṅgā for Bhīṣma
description: Arjuna shoots an arrow into the earth at Narkatari and a jet of Gaṅgā-water springs up to slake the fallen Bhīṣma's thirst, naming the Bāṇgaṅgā

title: Arjuna spares Maya Dānava
description: The asura architect Maya flees Kṛṣṇa's discus to Arjuna, who grants him safety, sparing him from fire and Kṛṣṇa

title: Arjuna Weds Citrangada
description: Arjuna marries the warrior-princess Citrangada of Manipura on terms that their son Babhruvahana inherits her matrilineal throne

title: Ashvatthaman's Brahmastra and Krishna's Revival of Parikshit
description: Ashvatthaman directs the Brahmastra at Uttara's womb to end the line; the child is stillborn and Krishna revives him as Parikshit

title: Ashvatthaman's Brahmastra on Uttaraa's womb
description: After the war Ashvatthaman aims the Brahmastra/Aishika weapon at Uttaraa's womb to extinguish the Kuru line, striking the unborn heir dead

title: Bhima Meets Hanuman in the Kadalivana
description: On the Saugandhika lotus-quest Bhima cannot lift the tail of an old monkey, recognizes his half-brother Hanuman, and is blessed with added strength

title: Bhishma Reveals the Secret of His Death
description: Stalemated, the Pandavas come by night to Bhishma, who reveals he will lay down arms before Shikhandin, consenting to his own fall

title: Bhishma reveals the secret of his own death
description: At night the Pandavas ask the invincible Bhishma how to kill him; he reveals he will not raise a weapon against Shikhandin (born a woman), telling them to set Shikhandin before him

title: Birth of Arjuna by Indra
description: Kuntī invokes Indra, king of the devas, and bears the supreme archer Arjuna

title: Birth of Karṇa by Sūrya's boon
description: Kuntī, using a boon-mantra before her marriage, conceives Karṇa by Sūrya, born with divine armour and earrings (kavaca-kuṇḍala)

title: Birth of Kuru — the solar graft onto the lunar line
description: Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī beget Kuru, eponym of the Kuru clan and Kurukṣetra, grafting Sūrya's solar blood onto the Lunar Pauravā line
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Caitraratha- & Sambhava-parvans; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19

title: Birth of Śuka
description: Vyāsa fathers the supreme renunciate Śukadeva by his austerity (variant: of the apsarā Ghṛtācī), who later recites the Bhāgavata to Parīkṣit

title: Curse on Kṛṣṇa setting the 36-year clock
description: Gāndhārī curses Kṛṣṇa that in 36 years his Yādava kin will destroy each other and he will die alone; Kṛṣṇa accepts

title: Death in the Sauptika night-raid
description: Found asleep, Dhṛṣṭadyumna is trampled and strangled to death by Aśvatthāman, denied an honourable weapon-death in revenge for Droṇa's beheading

title: Duel of the two fevers (Jvara)
description: Bāṇa's three-headed Māheśvara-jvara scorches the Yādavas; Kṛṣṇa's Vaiṣṇava-jvara defeats it, and the praising Jvara is released

title: Duryodhana born of a portion of Kali
description: The Aṃśāvataraṇa lists Duryodhana as born of a portion of the asura Kali, spirit of the dark age, framing the war as a clash of incarnate cosmic forces

title: Dwarka swallowed by the sea
description: As Arjuna leads out the last surviving Yadava women, children and elders, the sea rises and submerges Dwarka behind them, reclaiming every part except the spot where Krishna had dwelt

title: Ekalavya's thumb demanded
description: The self-taught Nishada prince surpasses Arjuna; Drona demands his right thumb as dakshina to preserve Arjuna's supremacy

title: Eternal Rāsa-līlā in Goloka and on earth
description: The Rāsa-līlā is presented first as an eternal event in Goloka between Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā, then re-enacted on earth at Vṛndāvana in the Dvāpara Yuga

title: Jara's arrow at Bhalka Tirtha
description: The hunter Jara, mistaking Krishna's raised foot for a deer, pierces it with the last pestle-fragment arrow at Bhalka Tirtha
source: Mahabharata Mausala Parva 4; Bhagavata Purana 11.30; Vishnu Purana 5.37

title: Jayadratha's abduction of Draupadī
description: Jayadratha of Sindhu carries off Draupadī from the hermitage; the brothers defeat him and shave his head leaving five tufts, sparing his life
source: Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Draupadī-haraṇa / Jayadratha Parva ~248–256

title: Karna spends the Vasavi Shakti on Ghatotkaca
description: In the night battle Ghatotkaca devastates the Kauravas until Karna is forced to hurl the one-use Vasavi Shakti (hoarded for Arjuna), killing him instantly; Krishna rejoices that the only weapon certain to kill Arjuna is now spent

title: Kripa one of the last three Kaurava survivors
description: After Duryodhana falls, only Ashvatthaman, Kripa, and Kritavarman remain alive of the Kaurava host

title: Krishna persuades Vraja to worship Govardhana
description: The boy Krishna argues that Mount Govardhana and the cows sustain the cowherds, not Indra, and persuades them to worship the hill instead, interrupting the Indra-puja

title: Krishna reveals Karna's parentage
description: Leaving Hastinapura, Krishna takes Karna aside and reveals he is Kunti's firstborn by Surya and the rightful heir, offering him kingship and Draupadi if he joins his brothers; Karna refuses out of loyalty to Duryodhana

title: Krishna Shot by the Hunter Jara and His Ascension
description: The hunter Jara mistakes Krishna's raised foot for a deer and shoots him in the sole with the iron-bolt fish-nub; Krishna consoles Jara, casts off his body and ascends, ending the Yuga

title: Liberation of Nalakubara and Manigriva (Yamalarjuna)
description: Cursed by Narada to become two arjuna trees, Kubera's sons Nalakubara and Manigriva are liberated when the infant Krishna, tied to a mortar, drags it between them and uproots them

title: Marriage to Jāmbavatī
description: Jāmbavān gives his daughter Jāmbavatī to Kṛṣṇa; she becomes a chief queen and mother of Sāmba

title: Mādrī's sati on Pāṇḍu's pyre
description: Winning the contest of devotion against Kuntī, Mādrī immolates herself on Pāṇḍu's funeral pyre; ascetics then escort Kuntī and the five boys to Hāstinapura

title: Mothers of the warring generation
description: Through Dhṛtarāṣṭra come the hundred Kauravas and through Pāṇḍu come the five Pāṇḍavas, making Ambikā and Ambālikā the grandmothers of both warring sides

title: Mārkaṇḍeya narrates the tale to the exiled Yudhiṣṭhira
description: Within the Pāṇḍavas' forest exile, the sage Mārkaṇḍeya recites Mudgala's story to console Yudhiṣṭhira, teaching contentment, forbearance, and the renunciation of even heaven

title: Mudgala Declines Heaven
description: The gleaner-sage Mudgala feeds the testing Durvāsā without anger and, offered bodily ascent to heaven, declines it on learning svarga ends, choosing mokṣa

title: Nala Gambles Away His Kingdom
description: Maddened, Nala loses gold, chariots and his entire kingdom to Puṣkara; he and Damayantī are stripped and exiled with one garment each

title: Nārada's embassy in the Sabhā Parva
description: Nārada visits Yudhiṣṭhira's new assembly-hall, describes the celestial sabhās, and prompts the Rājasūya sacrifice by relaying Pāṇḍu's wish, setting the imperial-rivalry chain in motion

title: Prophecy against Kamsa
description: A voice warns Kamsa that Devaki's 8th child will kill him; he imprisons the couple and slays their first six infants

title: Reconciliation and Babhruvahana's matrilineal succession
description: Arjuna is reconciled with his son; Babhruvahana remains king of Manipura as matrilineal heir while the Kuru line passes through Parikshit

title: Relocation of the Cowherds to Vṛndāvana
description: Troubled by demons and ill omens at Gokula, Nanda relocates the whole cowherd community by bullock-cart to Vṛndāvana

title: Restoration of Sandipani's son
description: Yama yields the boy's soul; Krishna recovers the living son and presents him to the overjoyed Sandipani, who blesses them
source: Bhagavata Purana X.45; Harivamsha; Vishnu Purana 5

title: Return of the grown prince Devavrata
description: Gaṅgā restores the grown, fully-trained Devavrata to Śāntanu, who installs him as crown prince

title: Satyavatī becomes the genealogical hinge of the Kuru line
description: Vasu's daughter Satyavatī weds Śāntanu and, via Vyāsa, becomes ancestress of the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas, making Vasu the upstream root of the Kuru tragedy

title: Saudasa-Kalmashapada spares Uttanka (Ashvamedhika variant)
description: To reach Queen Madayanti, Uttanka confronts her man-eating husband Saudasa cursed into cannibalism by Vasishtha, pledges to return to be eaten, and is let go

title: Shishupala's outburst and insults
description: Shishupala rejects honoring Krishna as a mere cowherd, abuses Bhishma, and rallies kings to walk out, exhausting Krishna's hundred pardons

title: Slaying of Kirmira at the forest threshold
description: Bhima kills the rakshasa Kirmira haunting the edge of the Dvaita/Kamyaka forest as the exiled Pandavas enter

title: Swallowing the forest fire (davāgni)
description: Krishna saves the cowherds and cattle trapped by a wildfire near the purified river by swallowing the blaze

title: The Ashta-Vasu steal Vasishtha's cow
description: The eight Vasus steal sage Vasishtha's wish-cow Nandini, and he curses them to be born as mortals

title: The Brahma-stuti — Brahma's hymn of surrender
description: Brahma offers the celebrated hymn of 10.14, confessing bhakti over jnana (jnane prayasam udapasya) and the inconceivability of Bhagavan, and begs forgiveness for his test

title: The complete life of Krishna
description: Krishna is born at Mathura to Devaki and Vasudeva, performs the bala- and gopa-lila (Putana, Kaliya, Govardhana, rasa), slays Kamsa, founds Dvaraka, marries, and plays his Mahabharata-era role

title: The death of Karna
description: As Karna's chariot-wheel sinks (Earth-goddess's curse) and the Brahmastra incantation fails him (Parashurama's curse), Krishna rejects his appeal to dharma and Arjuna severs his head with the Anjalika-astra

title: The eight principal queens (Aṣṭa-bhāryā) of Dwārakā
description: Consolidated account of Kṛṣṇa's eight chief wives — Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Jāmbavatī, Kālindī, Mitravindā, Satyā/Nāgnajitī, Bhadrā, Lakṣmaṇā — each won by a distinct episode

title: The graduation tournament and Karna crowned king of Anga
description: Karna matches Arjuna but is mocked as a charioteer's son; Duryodhana crowns him king of Anga, forging their lifelong alliance

title: The graduation tournament and Karna's challenge
description: At the Kuru princes' martial display Karna matches every feat of Arjuna and challenges him, but is humiliated as a Sutaputra when his lineage is demanded

title: The Kuru line preserved through Parīkṣit
description: Abhimanyu's posthumous son Parīkṣit, saved by Kṛṣṇa, survives as sole Kuru heir, making Subhadrā the genealogical bridge of the dynasty

title: The leap from Pravarshana hill and founding of the Yadava capital
description: Pursued again by Jarasandha, Krishna and Balarama leap from the burning Pravarshana mountain and reach Dwaraka, which becomes the Yadava capital and a sacred tirtha
source: Bhagavata Purana X.52.1-13; Vishnu Purana V.23

title: The mahā-rāsa and the multiplication
description: The great circle-dance: Kṛṣṇa multiplies himself between each pair of gopīs so each believes he dances at her side alone, the summit of mādhurya-bhakti

title: The niyoga of Vyāsa producing the war generation
description: Triggered by Vicitravīrya's childlessness and Bhīṣma's refusal, Satyavatī summons Vyāsa, whose niyoga on the widows produces Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and Vidura, all reckoned as Vicitravīrya's line
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~103–106; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22.22

title: The peace embassy fails over five villages
