description: Yudhiṣṭhira asks for a mere five villages to avert war, but Duryodhana refuses even a needlepoint of land, making the Kurukṣetra war unavoidable

title: The ring-in-the-fish recognition and heavenly reunion (Kalidasa)
description: A fisherman finds the ring inside a fish, restoring Dushyanta's memory; aiding the gods, he later finds Bharata taming a lion cub at Marica's celestial hermitage and is reunited with Shakuntala

title: The Sage and the Worm (Kīṭa-saṃvāda)
description: A sage tells a terrified worm crossing a road that even its humble life is precious and can climb the chain of rebirths toward liberation

title: The Syamantaka jewel and Krishna's marriages
description: Accused of stealing the sun-gem Syamantaka, Krishna tracks it through Prasena's death and wrests it from the bear Jāmbavān, winning Jāmbavatī, clearing his name, and marrying Satyabhāmā

title: The terrible vows in the hall
description: Bhima vows to break Duryodhana's thigh and drink Duhshasana's blood; Draupadi vows to leave her hair unbound until washed in Duhshasana's blood

title: The transformed palace — untold wealth granted unasked
description: Sudāmā finds his hovel turned into a jewelled palace and his wife radiant, Kṛṣṇa having silently bestowed everything without a word

title: Ulūka's insulting embassy
description: Śakuni's son Ulūka carries Duryodhana's provocative message to the Pāṇḍava camp on the eve of war

title: Vyasa grants Sanjaya divine sight
description: Vyasa bestows divya-cakshus (divine sight) on Sanjaya so he can relay the distant Kurukshetra battlefield to the blind Dhritarashtra, framing the whole Gita as a vision-within-a-recitation

title: Wealth without attachment and the supreme abode
description: Sudama enjoys the bounty without pride, ascribes all to Krishna, and through unbroken devotion attains the supreme abode; Shuka gives the moral to Parikshit

title: Wrestling deaths of Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika
description: Krishna kills the champion wrestler Cāṇūra and Balarāma kills Muṣṭika, with other wrestlers dispatched
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.44; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Arjuna Abducts Subhadra
description: On Krishna's counsel Arjuna abducts Subhadra from the Raivataka festival; she bears Abhimanyu, through whose son the Kuru line survives

title: Arjuna and the Kirata; winning the Pashupatastra
description: Arjuna's austerities win a duel with Shiva disguised as a mountain-hunter, earning the Pashupatastra

title: Arjuna single-handedly defeats the Kuru host
description: Alone, Arjuna defeats Karna, Kripa, Drona, Ashvatthaman, Bhishma and Duryodhana in succession, finally invoking the Sammohana-astra to swoon the entire Kuru army

title: Babhruvāhana slays Arjuna in battle
description: At Maṇipura, Arjuna rebukes his peaceful son Babhruvāhana as unmanly; goaded by the Nāga princess Ulūpī, Babhruvāhana fights and kills Arjuna with his arrows

title: Bhima's Two Great Vows at the Dice-Hall
description: After Draupadi's disrobing and Duryodhana's bared-thigh taunt, Bhima vows to drink Duhshasana's blood and to shatter Duryodhana's thigh

title: Bhishma Falls on the Bed of Arrows
description: On the tenth day Bhishma lowers his weapons before Shikhandin and Arjuna pierces him until he topples onto the sharashayya, choosing to await the uttarayana

title: Bhīṣma recites the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma
description: Asked the supreme refuge and easiest path to liberation, Bhīṣma answers that meditating on Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva is best and recites the thousand names of Viṣṇu, the key Vaiṣṇava stotra

title: Birth of Ghaṭotkaca to Bhīma and Hiḍimbā
description: After Bhīma slays the rākṣasa Hiḍimba and weds his sister Hiḍimbā in the forest, she bears Ghaṭotkaca the same day by rākṣasa speed, born bald with a pot-shaped head

title: Citralekhā abducts Aniruddha
description: The apsarā Citralekhā, skilled in magic and friend of Ūṣā, abducts Aniruddha by her arts in the Ūṣā-Aniruddha episode

title: Conception of Droṇa in a pot
description: The sage Bharadvāja's seed escapes at the sight of the apsarā Ghṛtācī and is caught in a wooden trough, from which the ayonija boy Droṇa develops, named for the vessel of his birth

title: Damodara and the liberation of the Yakshas
description: Bound to a mortar by Yashoda, Krishna drags it between two arjuna trees, freeing the cursed Yakshas Nalakubara and Manigriva

title: Day 10 — the fall of Bhishma on the bed of arrows
description: With Shikhandin screening him, Arjuna pierces Bhishma over his whole body; he falls but is held off the ground by the arrows themselves, the celebrated shara-shayya

title: Death of Śakuni at Sahadeva's hands
description: On Day 18 Sahadeva beheads Śakuni Saubala after an arrow-duel, fulfilling his dice-hall vow; Śakuni's son Ulūka falls in the same engagement

title: Dharmavyādha Teaches Kauśika (Vyādha-Gītā)
description: The arrogant ascetic Kauśika, humbled by a butcher of Mithilā, receives the Vyādha-Gītā teaching that dharma lies in selfless svadharma over ritual purity

title: Dhritarashtra's opening question to Sanjaya
description: On the field of dharma at Kurukshetra, the blind king Dhritarashtra asks his bard Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas did, the single question that launches the entire Gita

title: Draupadi's boons free the Pandavas
description: Frightened by ill omens, Dhritarashtra grants Draupadi boons that free Yudhishthira and her other husbands and restore their kingdom

title: Drupada's vengeance-sacrifice for a son
description: Humiliated and stripped of half his kingdom by Droṇa via Arjuna, King Drupada commissions the brahmins Yāja and Upayāja to perform a great fire-rite to obtain a son who will kill Droṇa

title: Duryodhana crowns Karna King of Anga
description: Duryodhana crowns Karna King of Anga on the spot so he may duel Arjuna, binding Karna to him in lifelong gratitude

title: Forest retirement of the elders
description: The aged Kuru elders withdraw to the forest in vānaprastha; the matriarchs' deaths are folded into this general account and not individually dwelt upon

title: Gandhari's vow of blindfolding
description: Gandhari blindfolds herself for life to share her blind husband's condition

title: Ganga marries Shantanu on a condition
description: Ganga agrees to bear the cursed Vasus and marries King Shantanu only on condition that he never question any act of hers

title: Gāndhārī's flesh-ball and the hundred-and-one pots
description: After a two-year pregnancy Gāndhārī strikes her womb and expels a lifeless ball of flesh; Vyāsa divides it into a hundred and one thumb-sized pieces sealed in ghee-pots to incubate

title: Jaiminiya underworld quest variant
description: In the later Jaiminiya Ashvamedha, Babhruvahana descends into Patala and wages war on the serpents to seize the amrita/Sanjivani jewel to revive Arjuna

title: Jambavan battles Krishna over the Syamantaka jewel
description: The bear-king Jambavan fights Krishna 21 days over the Syamantaka jewel, recognizes him as Rama returned, surrenders the gem and gives his daughter Jambavati in marriage

title: Kṛṣṇa restores the gem and is vindicated
description: Kṛṣṇa returns to Dwārakā and hands the Syamantaka back to Satrājit in open assembly, clearing the murder charge

title: Kṛṣṇa's birth and Vraja bāla-līlā
description: Retelling of Kṛṣṇa's Mathurā birth, the move to Gokula/Vṛndāvana, childhood marvels, demon-slayings, and the Kaṃsa cycle, framed by Rādhā-bhakti

title: Kripa argues against the night-raid
description: Kripa urges Ashvatthaman to abandon the massacre of the sleeping Panchalas, warning it is sinful and damning

title: Krishna and Draupadi's grievance at Kamyaka
description: Krishna visits the exiles at Kamyaka and Draupadi pours out her grief over the dice-hall outrage, renewing the resolve for war

title: Krishna beheads Shishupala with the Sudarshana
description: When Shishupala insults past the hundredth offense, Krishna releases the Sudarshana Chakra and beheads him in the assembly

title: Krishna teaches the parampara charter (Gita 4.1-3)
description: Krishna recounts that the yoga was handed down by succession from Vivasvan to Manu to Ikshvaku, was lost, and is re-spoken by him to Arjuna

title: Kunti's appeal to Karna on the Ganges
description: Kunti confesses she is Karna's mother and begs him to spare his brothers; Surya confirms her words from the sky, and Karna vows to kill only Arjuna so Kunti will keep five living sons

title: Mādrī bears the Aśvin twins Nakula and Sahadeva
description: Kuntī teaches the mantra to Mādrī, who summons the twin Aśvins and bears Nakula and Sahadeva in a single act

title: Nala Abandons Damayantī
description: Tormented by Kali within, Nala cuts away half her single garment and steals away from the sleeping Damayantī into the night

title: Nala reunites with Damayantī and wins back his kingdom
description: Through the second-svayaṃvara ruse Nala resumes his true form, reunites with Damayantī, and wins back his throne from Puṣkara at dice

title: Pradyumna slays Śambara
description: Krishna's son Pradyumna (incarnation of Kāmadeva), stolen as an infant by the demon Śambara and raised unknowingly, learns the truth from Māyāvatī (Rati) and slays Śambara before returning to Dvārakā

title: Prophecy and imprisonment by Kamsa
description: A voice warns Kamsa, tyrant of Mathura, that the 8th child of his sister Devaki will kill him; he imprisons Devaki and Vasudeva and slays their first six infants

title: Restoration of the original boys and calves
description: Brahma departs and Krishna brings back the original boys and calves from the cave; to them no time has passed and the day's play resumes seamlessly

title: Shalya named fourth Kaurava commander
description: With Karna fallen and the army broken, the demoralized Kauravas turn to Shalya as the fourth and last generalissimo

title: Shearing of Bāṇa's thousand arms
description: Kṛṣṇa with the Sudarśana cakra lops off Bāṇa's thousand arms in succession, leaving only four (or two); his banner-staff breaks per Śiva's omen

title: Slaying of Droṇa
description: On day 15 Droṇa is beheaded by Dhṛṣṭadyumna after the 'Aśvatthāmā is dead' stratagem

title: Subhadrā survives the Yādava end
description: Subhadrā outlives the Mausala destruction of the Vṛṣṇis, is escorted from Dvārakā by Arjuna, and ends her days with the Pāṇḍavas at Hastināpura

title: Sudama the fellow-pupil
description: The poor brahmin Sudama (Kucela) was a classmate at Sandipani's school, seeding their later Dvaraka reunion

title: Survival of the Śārṅgaka birds (Mandapāla-Jaritā upākhyāna)
description: The four nestling sons of the sage Mandapāla and the bird Jaritā are spared by Agni's earlier pledge

title: Takshaka kills King Parikshit
description: Doomed by the sage-boy Shringin's curse, King Parikshit is bitten and killed by the serpent-king Takshaka

title: The death of Drona by the half-lie
description: Day 15: Bhima kills an elephant named Ashvatthaman and Yudhishthira affirms 'Ashvatthaman is dead'; grief-stricken Drona lays down his arms and Dhrishtadyumna beheads the disarmed, meditating brahmin

title: The half-truth that fells Droṇa
description: To break the invincible Droṇa, Yudhiṣṭhira declares 'Aśvatthāmā is dead — man or elephant,' the qualifier drowned out; the grieving Droṇa lays down arms and is beheaded, and Yudhiṣṭhira's chariot descends to earth

title: The house of lac (Lakshagriha)
description: Duryodhana's agent Purocana builds a combustible mansion at Varanavata; warned by Vidura, the Pandavas escape via a tunnel and burn it

title: The Rāsa-Līlā
description: On the Śarad Pūrṇimā full-moon night Kṛṣṇa dances the rāsa with the gopīs on the Yamunā sands, multiplying himself to dance with each, the supreme emblem of divine love

title: The Satyavatī match and dowry demand
description: Śāntanu loves the fisher-maiden Satyavatī, but the Dāśarāja demands her sons inherit the throne, leaving Śāntanu pining
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~100; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22

title: The Sea Engulfs Dvaraka
description: As Arjuna leads the surviving women and elders out, the ocean rushes in and engulfs Dvaraka leaving no trace, fixing the Dvapara-Kali hinge at 3102 BCE

title: The Yakṣa-praśna at the Dvaita lake
description: Dharma in the guise of a Yakṣa quizzes Yudhiṣṭhira after the other four brothers drink and fall dead; Yudhiṣṭhira answers the riddles on dharma

title: Śuka's apologia
description: Narrator Śuka defends the transcendent rāsa to King Parīkṣit against the charge of impropriety, warning it is not to be imitated

title: Vadha of Kaṃsa
description: Krishna leaps the royal dais, drags Kaṃsa by the hair into the arena, and slays the tyrant
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.44; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: Wealth without attachment and final liberation
description: Sudāmā enjoys the bounty without pride, attributes all to Kṛṣṇa, and through unbroken devotion attains the supreme abode; Śuka gives the moral

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya at Indraprastha
description: After the Pāṇḍavas conquer the four quarters and Jarāsandha is slain, Yudhiṣṭhira performs the royal-consecration Rājasūya sacrifice at Indraprastha to become samrāṭ

title: Arjuna frees the cursed apsarā-crocodiles
description: Five apsarās led by Vargā, cursed to become crocodiles, are freed by Arjuna in the southern tīrthas during his pilgrimage

title: Arjuna's departure for divine weapons
description: From Kamyaka Arjuna sets out north to win the Pashupata from Shiva and celestial astras from Indra

title: Arjuna's last rites and the drowning of Dvaraka
description: Arjuna performs the Yadava funeral rites and evacuates survivors; the ocean reclaims Dvaraka and his Gandiva-power fails, closing the heroic age

title: Ashvatthaman unleashes the Narayanastra
description: Enraged at his father's death, Ashvatthaman invokes the Narayanastra; Krishna orders the army to drop all weapons and submit, so the weapon, denied resistance, dissipates harmlessly

title: Bhima meets Hanuman over the saugandhika lotus
description: Seeking the celestial lotus, Bhima cannot lift the tail of his half-brother Hanuman, who shows his cosmic Setu-bandha form and promises to roar on Arjuna's banner

title: Bhima Slays Kichaka
description: Disguised as the cook Ballava, Bhima ambushes Kichaka for molesting Draupadi and pounds him into a shapeless ball of flesh, then kills the 105 Upakichakas

title: Bhishma chooses death-by-will at uttarayana
description: By his father Shantanu's boon Bhishma resolves not to die until the sun turns north, lingering on the arrow-bed through the rest of the war

title: Bhishma's Dharma Teachings and the Vishnu Sahasranama
description: From the bed of arrows the dying Bhishma delivers the epic's longest dharma-instruction to Yudhishthira and recites the Vishnu Sahasranama

title: Bhīṣma's double vow
description: Devavrata renounces the throne and swears lifelong celibacy to win Satyavatī for his father, becoming Bhīṣma; Śāntanu grants him death-at-will

title: Birth of Duryodhana amid ill omens
description: Duryodhana emerges first from the pots as jackals howl and fires blaze in evil directions; Vidura and the sages warn that he portends the dynasty's destruction, but Dhṛtarāṣṭra spares him

title: Birth of the hundred Kauravas
description: Gandhari's flesh-lump is divided by Vyasa into 101 ghee-jar pieces, producing Duryodhana (born amid evil omens), 99 more sons, and the daughter Duhshala

title: Conception of Drona in a pot
description: Seeing the apsara Ghritachi, Bharadvaja's seed escapes and is caught in a wooden trough (drona), from which his son Drona develops, ayonija

title: Crossing of the Yamuna
description: Vasudeva carries baby Krishna across the parted, flooded Yamuna to Nanda and Yashoda, swapping for their newborn girl (Yogamaya)

title: Damayantī's Trials in the Forest
description: Abandoned, Damayantī is seized by a python, freed by a hunter whom she curses dead for lusting after her, then survives a caravan's destruction

title: Death of Pāṇḍu and Mādrī
description: Pāṇḍu dies when he embraces Mādrī (fulfilling Kindama's curse), Mādrī follows him on the pyre, and Kuntī alone rears all five boys

title: Draupadi rejects Karna at her svayamvara
description: Karna rises to attempt Drupada's bow-test but Draupadi refuses him as a charioteer's son, hardening his hatred (treated as later interpolation in the Critical Edition)

title: Drupada's boyhood vow to share half his kingdom
description: Reared together in Bharadvāja's āśrama, the boy Drupada vows in affection that as king he will share half his realm with Droṇa

title: Duryodhana surveys the armies and speaks to Drona
description: Seeing the Pandava army marshalled by Dhrishtadyumna, Duryodhana approaches his teacher Drona and recites the enemy's strength and his own champions to reassure himself

title: Fire-birth of Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Draupadī
description: From Drupada's fire-altar springs Dhṛṣṭadyumna armored and prophesied to slay Droṇa, and immediately after Draupadī, a full-grown dark maiden born of pure fire (ayonijā), destined to destroy the kṣatriyas

title: Ganga drowns her seven sons
description: Ganga bears and drowns seven newborn sons in the river in succession, each drowning releasing a Vasu from the curse, while the silent Shantanu watches

title: Ghaṭotkaca's summon-at-a-thought boon
description: Grown to full youth within a day, Ghaṭotkaca takes leave of his parents with the boon that he will come to the Pāṇḍavas the moment they think of him

title: Indra consecrates Krishna as Govinda
description: Defeated, Indra descends with the cow Surabhi and consecrates Krishna as Govinda, confessing his pride

title: Śiva's intercession and Hari–Hara reconciliation
description: Śiva pleads for his devotee's life; Kṛṣṇa spares Bāṇa and grants him fearlessness, the two gods reconciled in Hari–Hara non-difference

title: Kṛṣṇa recites the Śiva Sahasranāma
description: Asked for the names of Śiva, Bhīṣma defers and Kṛṣṇa recites the thousand names, having learned them from the sage Upamanyu

title: Karna institutes Surya-worship (Chhath charter)
description: An alternate Chhath charter holds that Karna, son of Surya, instituted the sun-worship that became Chhath Puja

title: Killing of Kaṃsa's brothers
description: Kaṃsa's eight brothers rush to avenge him and are killed by Balarāma

title: Kāma reborn as Pradyumna
description: The ash-reduced Kāmadeva is reborn in body as Pradyumna, son of Kṛṣṇa and Rukmiṇī, in the Dvāpara age

title: Kripa guards the gate during the Sauptika massacre
description: Yielding to his nephew, Kripa and Kritavarman guard the camp gates and fire the camp while Ashvatthaman slaughters the sleepers

title: Marriage to Satyabhāmā
description: A remorseful Satrājit gives Kṛṣṇa his daughter Satyabhāmā; Kṛṣṇa accepts the bride but returns the jewel

title: Maya builds the Mayasabhā at Indraprastha
description: In repayment Maya Dānava raises the wondrous assembly-hall for Yudhiṣṭhira on the cleared ground, with the Devadatta conch and Bhīma's mace

title: Panchajanya as the Kurukshetra war-conch
description: Generations later Krishna blows the same conch Panchajanya to open the Bhagavad-gita at Kurukshetra

title: Shishupala's radiance merges into Krishna
description: A light rises from the slain body and enters Krishna before the court, marking the end of Jaya's curse and liberation by merger (dvesha-bhakti)

title: Shiva as the Kirata and the Pashupata-astra
description: Arjuna's tapas on Indrakila brings Shiva disguised as a hunter; after a duel Arjuna worships him and receives the supreme Pashupata weapon

title: Slaying of Śiśupāla
description: During Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya, the rite culminates in the killing of Śiśupāla

title: Slaying of Karṇa
description: On day 17 Arjuna slays Karṇa while he lifts his mired chariot-wheel, the spot marked at Karṇa-vadh

title: Slaying of Keśī
description: Kṛṣṇa slays the horse-demon Keśī at Keśī-ghāṭa in Vṛndāvana

title: Slaying of Vatsasura and Bakasura
description: Krishna slays the calf-demon and the crane-demon at Vrindavana

title: Sāmba founds sun-worship at Multan
description: Sāmba, son of Krishna, founds sun-worship at Mitravana/Mūlasthāna (Multan) after Sūrya cures his leprosy, establishing the Maga Brahmin solar priesthood

title: The armies muster at Kurukshetra and commanders named
description: Eighteen akshauhinis march to Kurukshetra; Dhrishtadyumna is made Pandava commander and Bhishma the Kaurava commander on conditions, with rules of dharma-yuddha agreed

title: The Bāṇāsura war (Aniruddha and Uṣā)
description: After Uṣā's companion magically brings Aniruddha to Bāṇa's city and Bāṇa imprisons him, Krishna, Balarāma, and Pradyumna ride Garuḍa to war, Krishna fights even Śiva and Skanda, and shears off Bāṇa's arms before taking the couple to Dvārakā

title: The choice of Nakula and boon of concealment
description: Granted one brother's revival, Yudhiṣṭhira chooses Nakula so both mothers have a living son; Dharma revives all four and grants undetected ajñātavāsa

title: The Pativratā Humbles Kauśika
description: A devoted housewife rebukes Kauśika's anger by reading his mind, showing wifely devotion equals a sage's power, and directs him to the Dharmavyādha

title: The second dice game and the exile sentence
description: A single decisive throw lost by Yudhishthira sends the Pandavas and Draupadi into 12 years' forest exile plus a 13th incognito year

title: Ulūpī revives Arjuna with the Nāga gem
description: Ulūpī summons the serpent-realm jewel of resurrection (Mṛtasaṃjīvanī) and places it on Arjuna's chest, returning him to life, then reveals she engineered the death to expiate the Vasus' curse over Bhīṣma's unfair slaying

title: Uttanka incites Janamejaya to the snake-sacrifice
description: Bearing an undying grudge against Takshaka, Uttanka incites King Janamejaya to undertake the sarpa-satra to avenge his father Parikshit

title: Virata strikes Yudhishthira with a dice
description: Believing his son won the battle, Virata hurls a dice that bloodies Yudhishthira's face when Kanka credits Brihannala; Draupadi catches the blood lest it fall and cause drought

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's Aśvamedha and the golden mongoose
description: To expiate the war's bloodshed Yudhiṣṭhira performs the horse-sacrifice, at whose climax a half-golden mongoose declares a poor man's gift of barley-flour greater than the whole royal rite

title: Yugala-gītā
description: A paired song of the gopīs in two half-choruses praising Kṛṣṇa's flute-play, sometimes counted with the gopī song-cluster

title: Bhima slays Bakasura
description: At Ekachakra Bhima goes in a brahmin's place and kills the cannibal-demon Baka, freeing the town from its daily tribute

title: Bhima slays Jatasura
description: The rakshasa Jatasura, disguised as a brahmana, abducts Yudhishthira, the twins, and Draupadi, and Bhima returns to slay him

title: Bhima Slays the Hundred Kauravas
description: Across the eighteen-day war Bhima personally slays every one of the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra, leaving Duryodhana last

title: Bhishma blows his conch (the Kaurava war-signal)
description: To cheer Duryodhana, the aged Bhishma roars like a lion and blows his conch, sounding the first battle-signal from the Kaurava side and triggering a tumult of war-instruments

title: Bhishma-Karna reconciliation at the arrow-bed
description: With Bhishma fallen, Karna comes to the arrow-bed; Bhishma reveals he knew Karna was Kunti's eldest son and urges him to join his brothers or fight nobly, but Karna returns to the field

title: Bhishma's Death at Uttarayana
description: When the sun turns north Bhishma withdraws his life-breaths by yogic will and his spirit rises to the heavens, on the day observed as Bhishma Ashtami

title: Bhramara-gītā (Song to the Bee)
description: After Kṛṣṇa leaves for Mathurā, Uddhava visits the grieving gopīs; the chief gopī addresses a bumblebee in delirium of separation, humbling Uddhava's jñāna with the gopīs' love

title: Birth of Bhishma and Ganga's departure
description: At the eighth birth Shantanu breaks his vow; Ganga reveals her identity, takes the boy Devavrata (future Bhishma) to be reared, and later returns him grown

title: Celestial voice at Draupadī's birth
description: An aśarīravāṇī announces at Draupadī's birth that this dark woman will lead the kṣatriya race to ruin and accomplish the gods' purpose

title: Damayantī Recognized in Chedi
description: Taken in as a sairandhrī at Subāhu's court, Damayantī is recognized by the Brahmin Sudeva via the lotus-mark on her brow and sent home

title: Droṇa obtains Paraśurāma's celestial weapons
description: Arriving after Paraśurāma's wealth is gone, Droṇa asks for his celestial astras with the secret of their recall and discharge, and is made unmatched in astra-vidyā

title: Duryodhana poisons Bhīma in the Gaṅgā
description: Duryodhana feeds Bhīma poison, binds him, and throws him into the Gaṅgā at Pramāṇakoṭi; in the Nāga realm the serpents' nectar grants Bhīma the strength of ten thousand elephants, backfiring the plot

title: Escape from the house of lac and slaying of Hiḍimba
description: The family escapes the burning lac-house through Vidura's tunnel; Bhīma slays the rākṣasa Hiḍimba and Kuntī sanctions his union with Hiḍimbā

title: Fall of Duryodhana and the Sauptika Night-Massacre
description: On day 18 Bhīma fells Duryodhana with a mace-blow to the thigh, followed by Aśvatthāmā's night-massacre of the sleeping Pāṇḍava camp

title: Founding of Indraprastha on the cleared land
description: The burnt Khāṇḍava tract (Khāṇḍava-prastha) becomes the Pāṇḍava capital Indraprastha

title: Kṛṣṇa obtains sons and boons from Śiva through penance
description: Kṛṣṇa narrates how, through austerity and Upamanyu's Śiva-bhakti, he obtained sons and boons from Śiva, framing the Śaiva material

title: Karna's digvijaya for Duryodhana
description: As Angaraja, Karna conquers the four quarters subduing many kings for Duryodhana's Rajasuya/Vaishnava sacrifice

title: Krishna slays Dantavakra
description: Shishupala's cousin Dantavakra attacks Krishna to avenge him and is killed, completing the third Jaya-Vijaya birth-pair

title: Markandeya's discourses in the forest
description: The deathless sage Markandeya recounts the pralaya vision, Nala-Damayanti, Savitri, the Matsya flood, the righteous butcher, and the Kali-yuga prophecy to Yudhishthira

title: Marriage to Satyavatī
description: Śāntanu weds Satyavatī and brings her to Hastināpura as queen
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~100; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: Murder of Satrājit by Śatadhanvā
description: Incited by Akrūra and Kṛtavarman, Śatadhanvā kills Satrājit in his sleep and steals the Syamantaka while Kṛṣṇa is away

title: Pandavas/Draupadi perform Chhath to regain their kingdom
description: Another Chhath charter holds the Pandavas and Draupadi performed the sun-vrata to regain their lost kingdom

title: Pandu's curse by Kindama
description: Pandu kills the sage Kindama coupling in deer-form and is cursed to die if he ever embraces a wife

title: Release of Devakī and Vasudeva
description: Krishna and Balarāma free their imprisoned birth-parents after Kaṃsa's death

title: Slaying of Aghasura
description: The python-demon swallows the cowherd boys, and Krishna kills him from within

title: The crossing of the Yamuna
description: Vasudeva carries baby Krishna across the flooded Yamuna (Shesha shielding with his hood) to Gokula, exchanging him for Nanda and Yashoda's newborn daughter, who slips from Kamsa's grasp and foretells his doom

title: The Pandavas' identities revealed
description: On the third day the brothers take royal seats and reveal that Kanka is Yudhishthira, Vallabha Bhima, Brihannala Arjuna, the grooms the twins, and Sairandhri is Draupadi; Virata begs forgiveness and offers alliance

title: The Usha-parinaya (marriage and return to Dwārakā)
description: Aniruddha is freed from the nāgapāśa, weds Uṣā, and is brought in triumph to Dwārakā; Bāṇa becomes a Gaṇa of Śiva

title: Transmission of weapons-science and the Drona-Drupada boyhood
description: Bharadvaja transmits the agneyastra and dhanurveda (received from Agnivesha) to Drona, and rears Drona alongside Drupada in his ashram

title: Vastra-haraṇa (Hiding the Gopīs' Clothes)
description: Kṛṣṇa hides the gopīs' clothes at Cīra-ghāṭa while they bathe

title: Vyāsa re-compiles the Vedas at the Dvāpara–Kali junction
description: In the orthodox frame, all Upaniṣads are eternal Śruti seen by ṛṣis and re-compiled by Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana Vyāsa at the Dvāpara–Kali junction (~3102 BCE)

title: Yudhiṣṭhira performs the grand Aśvamedha at Hastināpura
description: The returned horse is sacrificed in the full rite with Vyāsa officiating and lavish gifts, proclaiming Yudhiṣṭhira cakravartin and universal sovereign

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's Aśvamedha (post-war atonement)
description: Yudhiṣṭhira performs the horse sacrifice after the Kurukṣetra war as imperial atonement, the wandering stallion leading to the Babhruvāhana episode and the golden-mongoose appearance

title: Arjuna Slays the Nivatakavachas
description: As Indra's champion Arjuna destroys the ocean-demon Nivatakavachas and the city Hiranyapura, earning the diadem and the name Kiritin

title: Balarāma Ends His Sarasvatī Pilgrimage; Post-War Śrāddha
description: Baladeva (Balarāma) ends his Sarasvatī pilgrimage at Aujas-ghāṭ, where post-war śrāddha for the slain is performed

title: Balarāma Slays Dhenukāsura at Tālavana
description: Balarāma slays the ass-demon Dhenukāsura at the palm-forest Tālavana, freeing the tāla fruits

title: Bhīṣma awaits the winter solstice by icchā-mṛtyu
description: Bhīṣma uses his boon of death-at-will to delay his death until the sun turns north (uttarāyaṇa), the auspicious gate to the deathless worlds

title: Births of Citrāṅgada and Vicitravīrya
description: Satyavatī bears Śāntanu two sons, Citrāṅgada and Vicitravīrya, both later dying young and childless
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~100–102; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.20

title: Births of the three eldest Pandavas
description: Using Durvasas' boon, Kunti bears Yudhishthira by Dharma, Bhima by Vayu, and Arjuna by Indra

title: Brahma's bewilderment
description: Brahma steals the cowherd boys and calves to test Krishna, who multiplies himself into identical copies of all of them for a year

title: Draupadi's svayamvara and Arjuna's win
description: Disguised as a brahmin, Arjuna strings the bow and pierces the revolving fish-target to win Draupadi; Karna is rebuffed as a suta

title: Droṇa weds Kṛpī
description: Droṇa marries Kṛpī, sister of Kṛpa, tying him to the Kuru court before he enters it

title: Duel with Bhīṣma over Ambā
description: As guru-in-arms, Paraśurāma fights an indecisive multi-day duel with Bhīṣma over the cause of Ambā

title: Duryodhana crowns Karṇa king of Aṅga
description: At the graduation tournament Duryodhana crowns the unknown Karṇa king of Aṅga to legitimize a champion against Arjuna, sealing the lifelong Karṇa–Duryodhana friendship

title: Ghosha-yatra: Pandavas rescue Duryodhana
description: Duryodhana on a cattle-expedition to Dvaitavana is captured and humiliated by the gandharva Citrasena, and Arjuna and Bhima rescue their enemy on Yudhishthira's order

title: Hanuman humbles Bhima in the forest
description: In the Gandhamadana forest the aged Hanuman lies with his tail across Bhima's path; unable to move it, the proud Bhima is humbled and recognizes his half-brother

title: Indra begs Karna's armor and earrings
description: Disguised as a brahmana, Indra exploits Karna's charity-vow to ask for his invulnerable kavacha-kundala; warned by Surya, Karna cuts them from his body and becomes mortal

title: Janamejaya's Sarpa-Sattra (snake sacrifice)
description: Janamejaya performs the year-long snake sacrifice to annihilate all serpents in vengeance for his father Parikṣit's death by Takṣaka's bite; the sage Āstīka halts it, sparing Takṣaka, and the Mahābhārata is narrated during the rite

title: Killing of Śatadhanvā
description: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma pursue Śatadhanvā, who hands the gem to Akrūra; Kṛṣṇa beheads him with the Sudarśana cakra but finds no jewel

title: Kirata grants the Pashupatastra to Arjuna
description: In hunter form Shiva battles Arjuna over a slain boar and, after the duel, grants him the supreme weapon Pashupatastra

title: Krishna and Arjuna blow their celestial conches
description: From the white-horsed chariot Krishna blows Panchajanya and Arjuna blows Devadatta, joined by the Pandava champions, the answering blast tearing through earth and sky and shattering the Kauravas' hearts

title: Kārkoṭaka Transforms Nala into Bāhuka
description: Nala rescues the nāga-king Kārkoṭaka from a fire; the serpent's bite torments Kali, disguises Nala as a dwarf, and gives him form-restoring garments

title: Kuntī's word makes Draupadī the common wife
description: After Arjuna wins Draupadī, Kuntī unseeingly tells her sons to 'share it among yourselves,' and her binding command becomes the chief sanction for Draupadī's polyandry

title: Marriage of Abhimanyu and Uttara
description: Arjuna takes Virata's daughter Uttara as daughter-in-law, marrying her to his son Abhimanyu in a great wedding at Upaplavya; their union will produce Parikshit

title: Reinstatement of Ugrasena
description: Krishna recoronates his deposed grandfather Ugrasena as Yādava king, declining the throne himself
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.44–45; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5

title: The golden-headed mongoose deflates the Aśvamedha
description: A half-golden mongoose with a human voice declares the grand sacrifice not equal to a poor brahmin's handful of barley flour, recounting how a starving gleaner family gave their last meal to a guest who was Dharma in disguise and ascended to heaven

title: Uluka delivers Duryodhana's insulting message
description: Duryodhana sends Uluka to the Pandava camp with a deliberately humiliating war-mongering message; each Pandava returns a defiant reply, ending any last hope of peace

title: Vidura Counsels Dhṛtarāṣṭra (Vidura-nīti)
description: Vidura counsels the sleepless Dhṛtarāṣṭra with fables and maxims on statecraft and dharma, including the man-in-the-well allegory of the soul ensnared in saṃsāra

title: Vision of the universe in Krishna's mouth
description: Yashoda, checking for eaten dirt, sees the entire cosmos within infant Krishna's mouth

title: Yudhishthira frees Bhima and Nahusa from the python-curse
description: The serpent Nahusa seizes Bhima and releases him only after Yudhishthira answers his questions on dharma, freeing Nahusa from his curse

title: Balarāma Slays Pralambāsura at Bhāṇḍīravana
description: Balarāma slays the demon Pralamba at Bhāṇḍīravana, the forest of the great banyan

title: Balarāma's rift and the gem left with Akrūra
description: Balarāma, suspecting concealment, leaves for Mithilā; Kṛṣṇa traces the gem to Akrūra, proves his innocence, and lets Akrūra keep it

title: Bhima Shatters Duryodhana's Thigh
description: In the final mace-duel Bhima, on Krishna's thigh-slap cue, delivers the forbidden below-the-navel blow that shatters Duryodhana's thighs, fulfilling his second vow

title: Bhishma ranks the warriors and demotes Karna
description: Bhishma classifies the host into rathi, atiratha and maharatha grades and pointedly rates Karna only an ardha-ratha, prompting Karna to vow not to fight until Bhishma is slain

title: Bhīṣma dies by yoga and his soul ascends
description: With the teaching complete and the solstice reached, Bhīṣma withdraws his life-breaths by yogic concentration; the arrows fall away, flowers rain from heaven, and his soul rises like a meteor

title: Bhīma slays the rākṣasa Baka at Ekacakrā
description: Sheltering with a brāhmaṇa family at Ekacakrā, Kuntī volunteers Bhīma to take the household's place and kill the demon Baka

title: Bāhuka Serves King Ṛtuparṇa
description: Disguised as Bāhuka, Nala becomes charioteer and cook at Ṛtuparṇa's court to obtain the secret of dice

title: Birth and naming of Aśvatthāman
description: Droṇa and Kṛpī's son is born neighing like the divine horse Uccaiḥśravas; a sky-voice names him Aśvatthāman, the beloved and lethal heir destined to be a Cirañjīvī

title: Births of the twins Nakula and Sahadeva
description: Madri uses the mantra once to invoke the twin Ashvins, bearing Nakula and Sahadeva

title: Damodara and the twin trees
description: Yashoda binds the butter-thief to a mortar; Krishna drags it through twin arjuna trees, freeing two cursed Yakshas

title: Damodara and the Yamala-Arjuna trees
description: Yashoda binds the butter-stealing toddler Krishna to a mortar, and he uproots the twin Yamala-Arjuna trees, freeing two cursed Yakshas; he also shows the universe in his mouth to Yashoda

title: Draupadi's polyandrous marriage
description: On Kunti's word and Vyasa's sanction, Draupadi becomes wife to all five Pandava brothers

title: Hanuman rides Arjuna's banner at Kurukshetra
description: Hanuman resides on the flag of Arjuna's chariot throughout the Kurukshetra war, protecting it and giving Arjuna the epithet Kapidhvaja

title: Indra grants the Vasava-shakti
description: In exchange for the armor, Indra gives Karna the infallible one-use Vasava-shakti dart, which he later must spend on Ghatotkaca

title: Jarāsandha's vendetta seeded
description: Kaṃsa's father-in-law Jarāsandha of Magadha vows revenge, opening the cycle of sieges on Mathurā

title: Jayadratha's abduction of Draupadi
description: Jayadratha of Sindhu carries off Draupadi from the hermitage; the Pandavas pursue, defeat and shave his head as humiliation

title: Kṛṣṇa identifies himself as Uccaiḥśravas
description: In the Bhagavad-gītā (10.27) Kṛṣṇa declares 'Among horses know Me as Uccaiḥśravas, born of nectar,' the key teaching of the Vibhūti-yoga

title: Krishna slew the demon Panchajana (conch origin)
description: Krishna's conch Panchajanya was made from the bones of the demon Panchajana whom he slew, recalled in the naming of the conches before the war

title: Mārkaṇḍeya Counsels Yudhiṣṭhira in Exile
description: During the forest exile the deathless sage consoles the Pāṇḍavas with stories of dharma, devoted women, and cosmic time

title: Śāntanu's reign and death
description: Śāntanu reigns long and justly and dies in old age while his sons are young, leaving Bhīṣma as guardian of the throne

title: Piṅgalā the Courtesan Attains Detachment
description: Wearied of waiting for a paying lover, the courtesan Piṅgalā suddenly attains detachment, realizing desire causes misery and the inner Lord is the only beloved

title: Slaying of Dhenukasura
description: Balarama kills the donkey-demon of the Talavana palm-grove

title: Teaching Droṇa
description: Paraśurāma gives Droṇa his entire stock of celestial astras and the science of arms

title: The lacquer house plot at Vāraṇāvata
description: Duryodhana builds a mansion of lac and ghee to burn the Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī alive, but warned by Vidura they escape through a tunnel, leaving substitute corpses

title: Urvashi Curses Arjuna
description: Arjuna refuses the apsara Urvashi by calling her 'mother,' and she curses him to become a eunuch-dancer, softened by Indra to one year of his choosing

title: Yama Fathers Yudhishthira
description: As Dharma, Yama fathers Yudhishthira on Kunti via the boon-mantra, producing the truthful eldest Pandava

title: Abduction of the Kashi princesses (Amba backstory)
description: Recounted backstory: Bhishma carried off Amba, Ambika and Ambalika from their svayamvara for Vicitravirya; Amba, in love with Shalva and rejected by him, becomes vengeful against Bhishma

title: Arjuna as Brihannala Routs the Kauravas
description: In his concealment year as the eunuch Brihannala, Arjuna becomes Uttara's charioteer, retrieves his arms, and single-handedly routs the Kaurava raiders in the Gograhana

title: Bhīṣma's cremation and Kṛṣṇa consoles Gaṅgā
description: The Pāṇḍavas and Dhṛtarāṣṭra perform the funeral; Gaṅgā rises grieving from her river and Kṛṣṇa consoles her, revealing Bhīṣma's true nature as the Vasu Dyaus/Prabhāsa cursed to be born human

title: Birth and Renunciation of Śuka
description: Vyāsa's son Śuka, born already liberated, tarries in the womb fearing māyā and at birth walks straight to the forest, later becoming reciter of the Bhāgavata

title: Damayantī's Second-Svayaṃvara Ruse
description: Suspecting Bāhuka is Nala, Damayantī proclaims an impossible second svayaṃvara, knowing only Nala's charioteering could reach Kuṇḍina in time

title: Death of Pandu and Madri's sati
description: Pandu dies by the curse embracing Madri in spring; Madri immolates herself, entrusting her twins to Kunti

title: Drupada rebuffs Droṇa and Droṇa's vow of revenge
description: Impoverished Droṇa claims the boyhood promise but the now-proud King Drupada insults and turns him away; Droṇa leaves vowing to humble him, his private feud becoming the hidden engine of the epic

title: Duryodhana humiliated at Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya
description: Dazzled by Maya's illusory palace, Duryodhana mistakes water for floor and is laughed at, the humiliation that triggers the dice-plot

title: Krishna drives the chariot between the two armies
description: At Arjuna's request Krishna halts the chariot before Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings, telling Arjuna to behold the assembled Kurus so that he sees not enemies but his own family

title: Krishna's secret offer to Karna
description: On the war's eve Krishna reveals Karna's birth and offers him the throne and the Pandavas' allegiance, but Karna refuses to betray Duryodhana

title: Kuntī's war-message via Kṛṣṇa (Vidulā-ākhyāna)
description: When Kṛṣṇa's peace-embassy fails, Kuntī sends through him the inset tale of Vidulā to goad Yudhiṣṭhira to fight for his right rather than live on charity

title: Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa Wedded by Brahmā at Bhāṇḍīravana
description: In one tradition Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are wedded by Brahmā under the bhāṇḍīra-vaṭa banyan

title: Subduing of Kaliya
description: Krishna subdues the many-hooded serpent poisoning the Yamuna, dancing on his hoods and banishing him to Ramanaka

title: Teaching and cursing Karṇa
description: Paraśurāma teaches Karṇa (disguised as a brahmin) the Brahmāstra, then curses him to forget its mantra at his hour of greatest need

title: The Yaksha-Prashna
description: Yama, disguised as a Yaksha at a lake, kills the four younger Pandavas, then revives them after testing Yudhishthira with riddles on dharma and revealing himself as his father

title: The Yaksha-prashna at the Dvaitavana lake
description: Four Pandavas fall dead drinking from a Yaksha-guarded lake; Yudhishthira answers Dharma's riddles, revives them, chooses Nakula, and wins the boon of concealment for the ajnatavasa

title: Vyasa Divides the Eternal Veda into Four
description: Krishna-Dvaipayana Vyasa re-divides the single eternal Veda into four at the Dvapara-Kali junction (c. 3102 BCE), establishing the Rig, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva recensions

title: Abduction and marriage of Subhadra
description: With Krishna's blessing Arjuna carries off Subhadra at Dvaraka; their son is Abhimanyu

title: Amba's tapas, Shiva's boon, and rebirth as Shikhandin
description: After Parashurama's indecisive duel with Bhishma fails to win her redress, Amba wins Shiva's boon to cause Bhishma's death, immolates herself, is reborn as Drupada's child, and becomes male via the yaksha Sthunakarna

title: Arjuna's despair and collapse on the chariot
description: Seeing kinsmen, teachers, and elders arrayed on both sides, Arjuna is overcome with pity, his limbs fail and his bow Gandiva slips, and he casts aside his bow and sinks onto the chariot seat refusing to fight

title: Brihadbala Slain by Abhimanyu
description: Brihadbala, the last great Suryavamshi of the epic age, fights for the Kauravas and is slain by Abhimanyu in the Mahabharata war, pinning the two dynasties' timelines together

title: Death of Krishna at Prabhasa
description: The death-place lore of Krishna at Prabhasa-kshetra is recorded in the Prabhasa-khanda

title: Droṇa appointed preceptor of the Kuru princes
description: After Droṇa retrieves the princes' ball and ring from a well with a chain of grass-arrows, Bhīṣma recognizes his mastery and appoints him ācārya of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava princes

title: Duryodhana poisons Bhima
description: Duryodhana poisons Bhima and throws him into the Ganga, but he sinks to the naga realm where serpent-nectar gives him the strength of ten thousand elephants

title: Duryodhana's thigh-slap at the disrobing
description: Duryodhana orders Draupadī dragged and stripped and bares his left thigh inviting her to sit on it — the obscene gesture Bhīma vows to avenge by breaking that thigh

title: Exchange of Dice and Horse Secrets; Kali Expelled
description: Nala trades the horse-secret for the dice-secret with Ṛtuparṇa; the instant the dice-knowledge enters him, Kali is vomited out and takes refuge in the Vibhītaka tree

title: Govardhana-Dhāraṇa (Lifting the Hill)
description: After Kṛṣṇa redirects worship from Indra to Govardhana, the affronted Indra looses catastrophic rains; Kṛṣṇa lifts the hill on his little finger for seven days to shelter all Braj

title: Govardhana-lila
description: Krishna stops Indra-worship, and when the enraged Indra sends torrential rain, Krishna lifts Mount Govardhana on his finger for seven days as an umbrella protecting Vraja, until Indra submits

title: Kunti's plea and Karna's vow to spare four brothers
description: Kunti reveals she is his mother; Karna vows to fight only Arjuna and spare the other four Pandavas so Kunti will keep five living sons

title: Kuntī reveals herself to Karṇa
description: Before the war Kuntī goes to Karṇa at his Sūrya-worship and reveals she is his mother, begging him to join the Pāṇḍavas; Sūrya corroborates but Karṇa refuses, vowing to fight only Arjuna and spare her other sons

title: Sāmba founds the Maga sun-cult
description: Kṛṣṇa's son Sāmba founds the Maga/Sāmba sun-worship cult, recorded in the Sāmba Upapurāṇa

title: Subduing Kaliya
description: Krishna subdues and dances on the hoods of the poison-serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna, banishing him

title: Swallowing the forest fire
description: Krishna twice consumes a forest conflagration to save the herders

title: Tirtha-yatra launched from the exile-forest
description: From the forest the Pandavas undertake the great pilgrimage tour narrated by Pulastya/Narada and Lomasha, threading Bharata's holy fords

title: Vaishampayana Curses Yajnavalkya to Disgorge the Yajus
description: Vaishampayana, quarreling with his pupil Yajnavalkya, orders him to vomit up all the Yajus he was taught; the rejected knowledge is pecked up by disciples who became partridges (tittiri), forming the Taittiriya/Krishna Yajurveda

title: Arjuna Slays Karna
description: Across the war Arjuna fells Bhishma, Jayadratha, and finally Karna with the Anjalika arrow when Karna's chariot-wheel sinks on the 17th day

title: Duryodhana captured by the gandharva Citrasena
description: During the Ghoṣa-yātrā Duryodhana clashes with the gandharva Citrasena, is defeated and taken prisoner, and is humiliatingly rescued by the very exiled Pāṇḍavas

title: Gandiva given to Arjuna by Varuna at the Khandava burning
description: Arjuna's divine bow Gandiva, which slips from his hand in despair, was given by Varuna via Agni at the burning of the Khandava forest

title: Karna consecrated Kaurava commander-in-chief
description: After Drona's death Duryodhana makes Karna the third Kaurava senapati for days 16-17, with Shalya as his sabotaging charioteer

title: Kṛṣṇa Summons the Gaṅgā to Form Mānasī-Gaṅgā
description: Kṛṣṇa mentally summons the Gaṅgā to purify the cowherds, forming the lake Mānasī-Gaṅgā at Govardhana

title: Lifting Mount Govardhana
description: Krishna stops Indra-worship; enraged Indra sends torrential rain and Krishna lifts Govardhana on his finger for 7 days to shelter Vraja

title: Nala and Damayantī Reunited
description: Through the children's recognition and his resumed radiant form, Nala reunites with Damayantī, the Wind-god affirming her chastity from the sky

title: Post-war disclosure of Karṇa's parentage
description: After victory Kuntī reveals Karṇa was her firstborn and the Pāṇḍavas' eldest brother; the horrified brothers perform his obsequies and Yudhiṣṭhira reproaches her concealment

title: Rasa-lila
description: Krishna performs the circular moonlit dance with the gopis, the supreme devotional episode, with Radha as the foremost beloved

title: Slaying of Pralambasura
description: Balarama kills the demon disguised as a cowherd with a fist

title: Surya Reveals the Shukla Yajurveda to Yajnavalkya
description: Stripped of his learning, Yajnavalkya worships Surya, who in horse form (vajin) — in some tellings as Narayana — teaches him a fresh, untransmitted White (Shukla) Yajus, named Vajasaneyi after the equine revelation

title: The House of Lac plot and the fire
description: Duryodhana's combustible mansion at Varanavata is foiled by Vidura's coded warning and escape tunnel; the Pandavas fire it over Purocana and flee, deceiving the Kauravas into thinking them dead

title: The wooden-bird test confirms Arjuna supreme
description: Droṇa tests the princes by asking what each sees aiming at a wooden bird's eye; only Arjuna answers 'the eye alone' and shoots true, confirming him the supreme pupil

title: Vyāsa compiles and disseminates the Purāṇas
description: Vyāsa composes the Purāṇas at the start of Kali Yuga and disseminates them through his pupil Romaharṣaṇa and the bard Ugraśravas to the Naimiṣa-forest sages

title: Arjuna surrenders as Krishna's disciple
description: Stricken with faint-heartedness and confused about dharma, Arjuna formally takes refuge in Krishna as his disciple, converting his battlefield refusal into the teaching occasion of the Gita

title: Babhruvahana Slays Arjuna
description: During Yudhishthira's Ashvamedha, Arjuna's son Babhruvahana, goaded by Ulupi, looses an arrow that kills Arjuna, fulfilling the Vasus' curse

title: Bhima slays Hidimba; birth of Ghatotkaca
description: Bhima kills the rakshasa Hidimba, weds his sister Hidimba, and she bears the mighty son Ghatotkaca who vows to come whenever needed

title: Bhīṣma completes the discourse and dismisses the assembly
description: Having covered rāja-, āpad-, and mokṣa-dharma, Bhīṣma blesses Yudhiṣṭhira and dismisses the assembly until the sun's northward turn, still alive on the arrow-bed

title: Birth of Rādhā at Barsānā
description: Rādhā (Rādhārāṇī) is born/found at Vṛṣabhānupura (Barsānā), daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu and Queen Kīrtidā

title: Droṇa rejects Ekalavya and claims his thumb
description: Droṇa refuses the Niṣāda prince Ekalavya instruction; when the self-taught boy surpasses Arjuna, Droṇa claims his right thumb as guru-dakṣiṇā to preserve Arjuna's primacy

title: Durvāsā's test averted by the Akṣaya-pātra
description: At Duryodhana's instigation the sage Durvāsā with ten thousand disciples descends on the forest-Pāṇḍavas, but Kṛṣṇa saves them via a single grain in the Akṣaya-pātra

title: Jayadratha abducts Draupadi
description: Jayadratha carries off Draupadi from the hermitage; the Pandavas overtake and humiliate him, and he wins a boon from Shiva enabling Abhimanyu's later death

title: Karna spares the four lesser Pandavas
description: True to his vow, Karna defeats but spares Yudhishthira, Bhima, Nakula, and Sahadeva in turn

title: Killing of Kamsa
description: Summoned to Mathura, Krishna and Balarama break Kamsa's sacrificial bow, kill the elephant Kuvalayapida and the wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika, then Krishna drags Kamsa from his throne and kills him, restoring Ugrasena

title: Kuntī's retirement and death in the forest fire
description: In old age Kuntī retires to the forest with the Kuru elders and perishes with them in a wildfire

title: Maya builds the assembly hall
description: The spared asura-architect Maya raises a wondrous illusory maya-sabha at Indraprastha for Yudhishthira

title: Nala Wins Back His Kingdom
description: Armed with the dice-secret, Nala wins all back from Puṣkara at a single throw, spares him, and is restored to his throne with Damayantī

title: The vastra-harana (stealing the gopis' clothes)
description: Krishna takes the bathing gopis' garments to a kadamba tree, teaching surrender of ego

title: Yajnavalkya Teaches Maitreyi, Gargi, and Janaka
description: The sage Yajnavalkya delivers his dialogues with Maitreyi, Gargi, and King Janaka in the Brihadaranyaka, articulating 'neti neti' and the early Atman=Brahman doctrine

title: Arjuna captures Drupada as guru-dakṣiṇā
description: Droṇa demands the princes capture Drupada; the Kauravas fail but Arjuna defeats and drags him bound to Droṇa, who seizes half of Pāñcāla in repayment

title: Arjuna Revived by the Nagamani
description: Ulupi fetches the Naga Sanjivana gem and lays it on Arjuna's breast, reviving him, reconciled with his son

title: Arjuna routs the Kauravas at the Virāṭa cattle-raid
description: In the incognito year Duryodhana joins the Kaurava raid on Matsya's cattle; Arjuna as Bṛhannalā routs the whole host single-handed and strips off Duryodhana's robe as a trophy

title: Death of Karna
description: In the final duel Karna's curses converge as his wheel sinks and his astra-memory fails; on Krishna's word Arjuna beheads the defenseless Karna with the Anjalika arrow

title: Exodus to Dvaraka
description: After Jarasandha attacks Mathura seventeen times, Krishna builds and relocates the Yadavas to the sea-fortress Dvaraka, earning the epithet Ranachhoda

title: Govardhana-dharana
description: Krishna persuades the cowherds to abandon Indra-worship; the enraged Indra sends rain, and Krishna lifts Mount Govardhana on his finger for seven days as an umbrella
source: Bhagavata Purana X.24-25; Harivamsa; Vishnu Purana 5

title: Kṛṣṇa Slays Narakāsura
description: Narakāsura, son of Bhūmi and Varāha, tyrant of Prāgjyotiṣa who imprisoned 16,000 women and stole Aditi's earrings, is slain by Kṛṣṇa with Satyabhāmā — commemorated as Naraka Caturdaśī

title: Krishna begins the Gita teaching (Samkhya of the deathless self)
description: Smiling, Krishna begins his discourse, teaching the imperishability of the atman, reincarnation as a change of garments, and the duty of the kshatriya, planting the seeds of nishkama-karma

title: Kuntī's prayer (Kunti-stuti)
description: As Kṛṣṇa departs Hastināpura, Kuntī sings a hymn paradoxically asking for more calamities so her mind stays fixed on him — a touchstone of bhakti

title: Mudgala rejects heaven for Brahman
description: The gleaner-sage refuses bodily ascent to heaven on learning it too is impermanent, choosing the imperishable Brahman

title: Slaying of Ariṣṭāsura and Digging of the Twin Kuṇḍas
description: To atone for slaying the bull-demon Ariṣṭāsura, Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā each dig a pond, creating the twin Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa, holiest tīrtha of Braj for Gauḍīyas

title: Śaṅkhacūḍa Beheaded by Śiva
description: The Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa, protected by his wife Tulsī/Vṛndā's chastity, terrorizes the gods until Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu breaks the vow and Śiva beheads him, his conch-jewel passing to Kṛṣṇa

title: Arjuna defeats the gandharva Citraratha
description: Crossing the Ganga at night, Arjuna defeats and spares the gandharva king, who teaches him celestial lore and gifts horses

title: Draupadī's svayaṃvara — the rotating-fish test
description: Drupada sets a near-impossible mark; Arjuna, disguised as a brahmin, strings the colossal bow and pierces the eye of the revolving fish seen only in reflection, winning Draupadī's hand

title: Droṇa accepts his destined killer Dhṛṣṭadyumna as pupil
description: Told the fire-born Dhṛṣṭadyumna is fated to kill him, Droṇa nonetheless takes him as a pupil and teaches him all his science, knowing his own death-instrument

title: Duryodhana chooses Kṛṣṇa's army over Kṛṣṇa
description: Offered a choice between Kṛṣṇa unarmed and his Nārāyaṇī army, Duryodhana eagerly takes the army while Arjuna takes Kṛṣṇa as charioteer — a fatal preference of force over the divine

title: Ekalavya learns from a clay image and gives his thumb
description: Ekalavya, refused tuition by Drona, learns archery by worshipping a clay image of him, surpasses Drona's students, and surrenders his right thumb as guru-dakshina

title: Ghaṭotkaca slays Alāyudha
description: Ghaṭotkaca duels and kills rākṣasa champions including Alambuṣa and beheads Alāyudha, who had entered the war to avenge Hiḍimba, hurling the head before Duryodhana

title: Indra's submission and Govinda consecration
description: Indra and the cow Surabhi consecrate Krishna as Govinda

title: Jarasandha's invasions and founding of Dwaraka
description: Jarasandha attacks Mathura 17 times; Krishna relocates the Yadavas to the sea-fortress Dwaraka, earning the name Ranachhoda

title: Kaṃsa-Vadha and Restoration of Ugrasena
description: The grown Kṛṣṇa, summoned to Kaṃsa's bow-sacrifice, kills the wrestlers Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika, then drags Kaṃsa from his throne and slays him, restoring Ugrasena to the throne of Mathurā

title: Krishna lifts Govardhana (recalled)
description: The Varaha Purana's Govardhana-tirtha glorification recalls Krishna's lifting of Govardhana hill against Indra's rain

title: Krishna teaches Karma-yoga and action as yajna
description: Krishna delivers the Karma Yoga teaching, declaring action inescapable, framing all work as sacrifice (yajna) in the cosmic wheel begun by Prajapati, and naming desire and anger as the great enemy

title: Marriage to Rukmini
description: Krishna elopes with Princess Rukmini of Vidarbha from the temple, defeating her brother Rukmi; their son is Pradyumna (Kamadeva reborn)

title: Posthumous revelation of Karna's parentage
description: After the war Kunti reveals Karna was the Pandavas' eldest brother; the anguished Yudhishthira curses all women never again to keep a secret

title: Svetaki's sacrifice sickens Agni
description: King Svetaki's colossal twelve-year sacrifice gorges Agni on ghee until he falls ill and loses his lustre and appetite; Brahma prescribes consuming the Khandava forest as the cure

title: The Anugita Spoken
description: Back at Indraprastha Arjuna confesses the Gita has slipped from memory and Krishna retells its essence as the Anugita through ancient narratives

title: Vyāsa dictates the Mahābhārata to Gaṇeśa
description: Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata, dictating it to Gaṇeśa who writes it down on the condition Vyāsa never pause, prompting knotty kūṭa verses

title: Yamuna Parts at Krishna's Birth
description: On the storm-night of Krishna's birth, the flooding Yamuna rises to touch his feet and parts to make a path as Vasudeva carries the infant to safety in Gokula

title: Yudhishthira's Rajasuya consecration
description: After the four brothers' digvijaya conquest, Yudhishthira is consecrated samrat in a grand sacrifice, the high-water mark of Pandava fortune

title: Agni recruits Krishna and Arjuna for Khandava
description: Disguised as a Brahmana, Agni asks Krishna and Arjuna to help him burn the Khandava forest by holding off Indra's protective rain, since Indra repeatedly extinguishes the fire to shield the Naga Takshaka

title: Arjuna wins Draupadi at the svayamvara
description: Disguised as a brahmin, Arjuna strings Drupada's bow and pierces the revolving fish-target to win Draupadi, after Karna is rebuffed

title: Bhīma slays Hiḍimba
description: The cannibal rākṣasa Hiḍimba sends his sister to fetch the sleeping Pāṇḍavas as food; Bhīma kills him in a wrestling-match when she falls in love instead

title: Births of the Kuru line and the Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas
description: The Ādi Parva narrates the births of Bhīṣma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and the Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas, founding the rival lines

title: Duryodhana refuses the five villages
description: When Yudhiṣṭhira reduces his claim to five villages to avert war, Duryodhana refuses to yield even a needle-point of land without war

title: Kaliya-Damana (Taming of the Serpent)
description: The boy Krishna leaps into the Yamuna pool poisoned by the Naga Kaliya, dances on his many hoods, and banishes him to Ramanaka, restoring the river

title: Karṇa spends the Vāsavī Śakti on Ghaṭotkaca
description: On the 14th night Kṛṣṇa sends Ghaṭotkaca against the rampant Karṇa; forced to save his army, Karṇa hurls his once-only Vāsavī Śakti, killing Ghaṭotkaca but spending the dart hoarded for Arjuna

title: Karna surrenders his armor to Indra
description: Warned by Surya, Karna cuts his inborn armor and earrings from his body and gives them to the disguised Indra, receiving the one-use Vasavi Shakti in exchange

title: Krishna declares the avatara doctrine (yada yada hi dharmasya)
description: Krishna reveals that though birthless he descends by his own maya age after age whenever dharma declines, to protect the good, destroy the wicked, and re-establish dharma, the charter of the Dashavatara

title: Kuntī's accidental command and Draupadī's polyandrous marriage
description: Kuntī unseeingly tells her sons to share what they brought; Yudhiṣṭhira rules Draupadī wife of all five and Vyāsa sanctions the unprecedented polyandry by revealing her prior-birth boons

title: Maya Builds the Mayasabhā
description: The asura architect Maya, spared by Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa from the Khāṇḍava fire, builds the illusion-palace Mayasabhā for Yudhiṣṭhira at Indraprastha, where Duryodhana's humiliation seeds the Mahābhārata war

title: Slaying of Narakasura and freeing of 16,100 women
description: Krishna with Satyabhama slays the demon Narakasura and frees the 16,100 captive women (festival Naraka Chaturdashi)

title: Slaying of Shishupala
description: When Shishupala's insults exceed Krishna's vowed hundred pardons, Krishna beheads him with the Sudarshana Chakra and his radiance merges into Krishna

title: The Rasa-lila
description: On the autumn full-moon night Krishna summons the gopis with his flute and multiplies himself to dance the circle-dance with each, the theological heart of bhakti-rasa

title: Agni gifts divine weapons to Krishna and Arjuna
description: To enable them, Agni (via Varuna) gives Arjuna the bow Gandiva, two inexhaustible quivers, and a divine chariot, and gives Krishna the Sudarshana Chakra and the mace Kaumodaki

title: Akrura's mission to bring Krishna to Mathura
description: Kamsa sends Akrura to lure Krishna and Balarama to Mathura for a bow sacrifice; Akrura sees Krishna as Vishnu in the Yamuna

title: Ambopakhyana: Amba reborn as Shikhandin
description: Scorned by Bhishma, Amba immolates herself to be reborn as Shikhandin, the instrument of Bhishma's fall

title: Draupadi married to the five Pandavas
description: On Kunti's accidental word and Yudhishthira's ruling, Vyasa sanctions Draupadi's marriage to all five brothers, justified by her former-birth boon from Shiva

title: Duryodhana's plot to seize Kṛṣṇa and the Viśvarūpa
description: Duryodhana plots to arrest Kṛṣṇa in court; Kṛṣṇa reveals his cosmic Viśvarūpa form before the assembly and departs, ending hope of peace

title: Ghaṭotkaca's dying body crushes an akṣauhiṇī
description: Mortally struck, Ghaṭotkaca magnifies his body to colossal size and falls upon the Kaurava ranks, crushing a full akṣauhiṇī of troops in death

title: Hiḍimbā weds Bhīma; birth of Ghaṭotkaca
description: The rākṣasī Hiḍimbā weds Bhīma by rākṣasa union and bears Ghaṭotkaca, then releases Bhīma to rejoin his brothers

title: Krishna teaches the renunciation-of-action and meditation yogas
description: Krishna reconciles renunciation with selfless action and delivers a practical meditation manual (posture, moderation, steadying the restless mind) plus the reassurance that the fallen yogi is reborn favorably and perfected across many births

title: Lac-house plot and Draupadī's svayaṃvara
description: The Kauravas' lac-house (Lākṣāgṛha) assassination plot fails, and Draupadī's svayaṃvara leads to her marriage to the five Pāṇḍavas

title: Nārada sets the rotation rule for Draupadī
description: Warning of the Sunda–Upasunda strife, Nārada decrees Draupadī dwell one year with each husband in turn, any intruder going into exile — the rule that later sends Arjuna wandering

title: Saubhari's Curse on Garuda
description: The sage Saubhari curses Garuda so he cannot enter Vrindavana, which is why Kaliya was able to hide in the Yamuna there

title: Syamantaka jewel and Jambavati
description: Krishna clears himself of stealing the gem, fights bear-king Jambavan for 28 days, and wins Jambavati and Satyabhama

title: The game of dice and Draupadi's disrobing
description: Shakuni's foul dice strip Yudhishthira of kingdom, brothers and Draupadi; Duhshasana drags her in but the disrobing is foiled by endless cloth

title: The Yaksha Prashna at the lake
description: After four brothers drink and fall dead, Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles on dharma; the Yaksha (Dharma in disguise) revives them and grants a boon for their coming disguise

title: Bhīma kills Duryodhana's ninety-nine brothers
description: Bhīma systematically kills all ninety-nine Kaurava brothers, most gruesomely tearing open Duḥśāsana's chest and drinking his blood in fulfillment of his dice-hall vow

title: Bhīma slays Bakāsura
description: At Ekacakrā, Bhīma in disguise eats the food meant for the extorting cannibal Baka and breaks his back, freeing the town

title: Birth of the Upapāṇḍavas (Draupadeyas)
description: Draupadī bears one son by each husband — Prativindhya, Sutasoma, Śrutakarman, Śatānīka, Śrutasena — all later slain asleep in Aśvatthāman's night-raid

title: Brahma-vimohana-lila — the Bewilderment of Brahma
description: The Brahma of our universe steals child-Krishna's cowherds and calves; Krishna duplicates them all and reveals countless universes each with its own Brahma, humbling his pride

title: Burning of the Khandava forest
description: Agni surrounds Khandava with his seven flames while Krishna and Arjuna ring the forest and shoot down every fleeing creature and beat back Indra and the gods until Agni is fully sated

title: Founding of Indraprastha
description: Dhritarashtra grants the Pandavas the wild tract Khandavaprastha, which they transform into the splendid capital Indraprastha

title: Kṛṣṇa rejoices that Karṇa is disarmed
description: Kṛṣṇa alone rejoices and embraces Arjuna, explaining that with the once-only dart spent on Ghaṭotkaca, Karṇa can no longer kill Arjuna — the strategic pivot of the war

title: Krishna reveals his two natures and the four kinds of devotees
description: Krishna distinguishes his lower (material) and higher (conscious) prakritis, declares all is strung on him like pearls, names the four classes of devotees, and teaches that maya is crossed only by taking refuge in him

title: Krishna straightens Kubja
description: Krishna straightens the deformed maidservant who gives him sandalwood

title: Krishna Weds Kalindi (Yamuna)
description: The river-goddess Kalindi does austerities longing to wed Vishnu; Krishna finds her and takes her as the fourth of his eight chief queens, who bears him ten sons

title: Lakshagriha (House of Lac) escape
description: Duryodhana plots to burn the Pandavas alive in a lac palace at Varanavata; warned by Vidura, they escape via a tunnel and fake their deaths

title: Slaying Narakasura and freeing the 16,100
description: Krishna with Satyabhama slays Narakasura of Pragjyotisha and frees 16,100 captive women, later accepting them as wives

title: The dice game and Draupadī's disrobing
description: In the rigged dice match against Śakuni, Yudhiṣṭhira loses kingdom, brothers, self, and Draupadī, whose attempted disrobing is foiled by Kṛṣṇa's miracle, leading to 13 years' exile

title: The terrible vows and the 13-year exile sentence
description: Bhima vows to drink Duhshasana's blood and break Duryodhana's thigh; the second dice game sends the Pandavas to 12 years' exile plus one incognito

title: Añjanaparvan slain by Aśvatthāman
description: Ghaṭotkaca's son Añjanaparvan is slain by Aśvatthāman during the war

title: Arjuna's self-exile and marriages to Ulupi and Citrangada
description: Arjuna breaks Narada's rule and exiles himself on pilgrimage, wedding the naga princess Ulupi (mother of Iravan) and Citrangada (mother of Babhruvahana)

title: Bhīma slays Kirmīra
description: Kirmīra, brother of Baka, ambushes the Pāṇḍavas entering the Kāmyaka forest to avenge his kin and is killed bare-handed by Bhīma

title: Breaking the bow and killing Kuvalayapida
description: Krishna snaps Kamsa's great bow and slays the rogue elephant Kuvalayapida at the arena gate

title: Draupadi's svayamvara
description: Arjuna in Brahmin disguise wins Draupadi by stringing the bow and hitting the fish-eye target; by Kunti's word and a past boon Draupadi becomes the common wife of all five Pandavas

title: Duryodhana hides in Dvaipāyana lake
description: After his army's annihilation the weaponless Duryodhana solidifies the lake's waters by yogic power and hides submerged until the Pāṇḍavas taunt him out

title: Krishna teaches death, the kalpa-clock, and the two after-death paths
description: Krishna teaches that the last thought at death determines one's destiny, reckons Brahma's day and night as a thousand yugas with the cosmic out-breath and in-breath of beings, and names the bright devayana and dark pitryana routes

title: The Pāṇḍavas' forest exile
description: The Pāṇḍavas spend twelve years in the forest amid pilgrimages and sub-tales; Arjuna performs penance and wins divine weapons

title: The six survivors of Khandava; Maya spared
description: Khandava's destruction spares only six, including Takshaka's son Ashvasena, the architect-demon Maya (saved by Arjuna), and four sharngaka birds; the spared Maya later builds the Mayasabha at Indraprastha

title: War with Banasura over Aniruddha and Usha
description: Krishna's grandson Aniruddha weds Usha; Krishna battles the asura Bana and Shiva's forces

title: Abduction of Subhadra
description: With Krishna's blessing Arjuna carries off Subhadra; their son is Abhimanyu

title: Arjuna in Indra's heaven and Urvashi's curse
description: Arjuna ascends to Amaravati for celestial weapons; spurning the apsara Urvashi, he is cursed to be a eunuch for a year of his choosing

title: Bhīma slays Jaṭāsura
description: Jaṭāsura, disguised as a brahmin, abducts Yudhiṣṭhira, Nakula, Sahadeva and Draupadī and is slain by Bhīma on his return

title: Birth of Kṛṣṇa in Kamsa's prison
description: Kṛṣṇa is born to Vasudeva and Devaki in Kamsa's prison and is smuggled to Nanda and Yasoda in Gokula

title: Kamsa's Tyranny and Krishna's Birth
description: Following the prophecy that Devaki's eighth son will kill Kamsa, Krishna is born in prison and raised in Gokula/Vrindavana
source: Bhagavata X; Harivamsha; Vishnu Purana V

title: Killing of Chanura and Mushtika
description: Krishna and Balarama kill Kamsa's champion wrestlers in the arena

title: Krishna proclaims the sovereign secret and accessible devotion
description: Krishna declares the king of sciences, his immanent-yet-transcendent pervasion of all, that he accepts a leaf-flower-fruit-water offered in love, and that even the lowly-born and worst sinner who worship him reach the supreme goal

title: The mace-duel and the foul thigh-blow
description: In a fair mace-duel Duryodhana is the superior fighter until Kṛṣṇa signals Bhīma, who strikes below the navel and shatters Duryodhana's thighs, the forbidden blow that fulfills his vow

title: The year in disguise at Virāṭa's court
description: In the 13th incognito year the Pāṇḍavas serve King Virāṭa; Bhīma kills Kīcaka and Arjuna as Bṛhannalā repels the Kaurava cattle-raid

title: Death of Ghaṭotkaca by Karṇa's Śakti
description: At Kurukṣetra Ghaṭotkaca is slain on the 14th night by Karṇa's one-use divine Śakti weapon, which Karṇa had hoarded for Arjuna, thereby saving Arjuna's life

title: Death of Shishupala
description: At the Rajasuya, Shishupala insults Krishna past 100 forgiven offenses and is beheaded by the Sudarshana chakra

title: Duryodhana anoints Aśvatthāman commander
description: The half-dead Duryodhana's final act is to anoint Aśvatthāman commander, who that night slaughters the sleeping Pāṇḍava camp

title: Karna surrenders his armour to Indra
description: Indra, disguised as a brahmin, begs away Karna's invulnerable kavacha-kundala, giving in exchange the one-use Vasavi Shakti dart

title: Kṛṣṇa's demon-slayings in childhood
description: The infant and boy Kṛṣṇa slays Putana, Tṛnavarta, Sakatasura, Aghasura, Bakasura, and Dhenukasura

title: Kṛṣṇa's failed peace embassy
description: Kṛṣṇa's peace mission to Hastināpura fails when Duryodhana refuses even five villages, and the armies muster for war; Karṇa's parentage is revealed to him

title: Krishna, 8th Avatara of Vishnu
description: Krishna slays Kamsa, founds Dvaraka, allies with the Pandavas and teaches the Bhagavad Gita; his departure marks the start of Kali Yuga in 3102 BCE

title: Krishna declares his divine glories (Vibhuti Yoga)
description: Krishna enumerates his vibhutis as the foremost of every class (Vishnu among Adityas, the Ganges among rivers, the letter A, Time itself), declaring he supports the whole universe with a single fragment of himself

title: Rajasuya sacrifice and Duryodhana's humiliation
description: Yudhishthira performs the imperial Rajasuya sacrifice; Duryodhana, humiliated in the illusory hall, nurses revenge

title: Slaying of Kamsa
description: Krishna drags Kamsa by the hair and kills him, freeing his parents and reinstating the deposed king Ugrasena
source: Bhagavata Purana X.44; Harivamsa; Vishnu Purana 5

title: The burning of the Khandava forest
description: Agni, to cure his indigestion, devours the Khandava forest while Krishna and Arjuna (newly armed with Gandiva and Sudarsana) ring the blaze and repel Indra and the gods

title: Duryodhana's death and flower-rain
description: Felled and broken, Duryodhana accuses Kṛṣṇa of every deceit and proclaims he dies a true kṣatriya bound for heroes' heaven; a flower-rain from the gods falls on him

title: Education under Sandipani and recovery of his son
description: Krishna and Balarama study at Avanti and as guru-dakshina recover Sandipani's drowned son from the demon Panchajana and Yama's realm

title: Ghaṭotkaca slays Alambuṣa
description: Alambuṣa, son of Jaṭāsura, fights for the Kauravas at Kurukṣetra to avenge his father and is finally killed by Ghaṭotkaca

title: Kaliya-damana
description: Kṛṣṇa subdues the venomous serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna, dancing on its hoods

title: Krishna grants Arjuna the divine eye to behold the Vishvarupa
description: At Arjuna's request Krishna confers a divya-cakshus and reveals his Universal Form containing all worlds, gods, and infinite radiance like a thousand suns

title: Maya Danava spared at Khandava
description: The asura-architect Maya is spared by Arjuna at Krishna's word and pledges to build the assembly hall at Indraprastha

title: Sudama's visit
description: Krishna's poor Brahmin friend Sudama brings flattened rice; Krishna honors him and silently grants him wealth

title: The Bhagavad Gītā is spoken
description: Before battle Kṛṣṇa delivers the Bhagavad Gītā to Arjuna, synthesizing karma-, bhakti- and jñāna-yoga — the pivotal teaching of the epic

title: The game of dice
description: Shakuni plays dice for Duryodhana and Yudhishthira gambles away wealth, kingdom, his brothers, himself, and finally Draupadi

title: The Yadava Self-Destruction (Mausala)
description: Cursed by sages, the Vrishnis kill each other with iron maces at Prabhasa, Krishna and Balarama depart, and Dvaraka sinks into the sea, ending the Yadava line

title: Bhīṣma's abduction of the Kāśī princesses (rākṣasa-vivāha exemplar)
description: Bhīṣma carries off Ambā, Ambikā and Ambālikā by force, the epic exemplar of the rākṣasa marriage-by-capture sanctioned for kṣatriyas

title: Draupadi's disrobing
description: Duhshasana drags Draupadi by the hair and attempts to strip her, but Krishna miraculously extends her sari; Bhima vows to break Duryodhana's thigh and drink Duhshasana's blood

title: Duryodhana seen enthroned in heaven
description: Ascending to heaven, Yudhiṣṭhira first sees Duryodhana radiant among the heroes; Nārada explains he earned svarga by dying fearlessly in battle, fulfilling kṣatriya-dharma

title: Dushyanta and Shakuntala
description: King Dushyanta meets and marries Shakuntala in Kanva's hermitage; after a ring-curse of forgetting, their son becomes the emperor Bharata

title: Fall of Bhīṣma
description: After ten days as commander, Bhīṣma falls onto the bed of arrows at Kurukṣetra

title: House of Lac escape
description: Duryodhana plots to burn the Pandavas in a lac palace at Varanavata; they escape via a tunnel and fake their deaths

title: Jarasandha's invasions of Mathura
description: Kamsa's father-in-law Jarasandha attacks Mathura seventeen times and is repelled

title: Kṛṣṇa lifts Mount Govardhana
description: Kṛṣṇa lifts Mount Govardhana to shelter Vṛndavana, displacing Indra-worship with devotion

title: The Anu-gita delivered
description: After the war Krishna gives Arjuna a different, more austere restatement of the Gita's teaching, framed by inset tales

title: The Vishvarurupa devours the warriors; Krishna declares 'I am Time'
description: Arjuna beholds Bhishma, Drona, Karna and the kings rushing into the flaming mouths of the terrible form, and Krishna reveals himself as Time the destroyer of worlds, the warriors already slain, bidding Arjuna be the mere instrument

title: Bharata, the Eponymous Emperor
description: The cakravartin Bharata, after whom Bharata-varsha (India) is named, gives rise to the Bharata clan

title: Death of Abhimanyu and slaying of Droṇa
description: Abhimanyu is killed in the cakra-vyūha and Jayadratha is slain; Droṇa is killed via the 'Aśvatthāmā is dead' ruse

title: Founding of Dwaraka and death of Kalayavana
description: Facing Kalayavana, Krishna withdraws and builds the island-city Dwaraka, luring Kalayavana into the cave of the sleeping Mucukunda whose gaze incinerates him

title: Kṛṣṇa carries off Rukmiṇī (rākṣasa-vivāha exemplar)
description: Kṛṣṇa's carrying-off of Rukmiṇī is cited as the epic exemplar of marriage by seizure permitted to the warrior class

title: Krishna offered Krishna-unarmed vs his army
description: Arjuna chooses the unarmed non-combatant Krishna as charioteer while Duryodhana takes the Narayani army

title: Krishna withdraws the cosmic form and resumes his human shape
description: At the awe-struck Arjuna's plea, Krishna withdraws the terrible cosmic form, shows the four-armed Vishnu form, then resumes his gentle two-armed human shape, declaring this vision attainable by undivided devotion alone

title: The half-golden mongoose at the Ashvamedha
description: A half-golden mongoose declares Yudhishthira's imperial Ashvamedha worth less than a starving family's gift of barley-flour

title: The thirteen-year exile
description: The Pandavas spend twelve years in the forest plus one year incognito at King Virata's court in disguised roles

title: Yudhiṣṭhira cremates Duryodhana
description: After the war Yudhiṣṭhira himself performs the funeral rites for Duryodhana and the fallen Kauravas amid Gāndhārī's grief

title: Abduction of Rukmini
description: Krishna abducts Rukmini from her own wedding to Sisupala at her secret request and defeats her brother Rukmi

title: Arjuna kills Karṇa
description: With his chariot wheel sunk, Karṇa is slain by Arjuna
