title: Arjuna obtains the Pashupatastra
description: During the forest exile Arjuna performs penance and obtains the Pashupatastra from Shiva (the Kiratarjuniya episode) and celestial weapons from the gods

title: Bhishma's Vow of Celibacy
description: Shantanu's son Devavrata vows lifelong celibacy and renounces the throne so his father can marry Satyavati, becoming Bhishma with the boon of death-at-will

title: Bhishma teaches Yudhishthira on ahimsa
description: Bhishma, on his deathbed, instructs Yudhishthira that non-violence is the highest dharma in the Anushasana Parva

title: Droṇa appointed Kaurava commander after Bhīṣma's fall
description: On day 11, after Bhīṣma falls, Droṇa is made Kaurava senāpati and holds the post for five days, vowing to capture Yudhiṣṭhira alive

title: Kṛṣṇa slays Kamsa
description: Kṛṣṇa goes to Mathura and slays the tyrant king Kamsa

title: Krishna revives Parikshit in the womb
description: Krishna revives the still-born Parikshit struck by Ashvatthaman's Brahmastra, saving the dynastic line

title: Krishna's peace embassy and the Vishvarupa
description: Krishna's plea for five villages is rejected by Duryodhana; when seized he manifests his cosmic universal form, and the embassy fails

title: Krishna teaches the supremacy of devotion and the beloved devotee
description: Krishna affirms that worship of the personal Lord is easier and superior to meditation on the formless Absolute, gives a descending ladder of practice, and portrays the qualities of the devotee dear to him

title: Pandavas retrieve weapons from the shami tree
description: On Vijayadashami the Pandavas recover their hidden weapons from the shami tree, ending their incognito year, basis of Shami-puja

title: Sun cures Samba of leprosy; founding of the Multan sun-temple
description: Samba, Krishna's son, is cured of leprosy by the Sun and founds the great sun-temple at Mulasthana/Multan, introducing the Maga Brahmin sun-priests into Hindu society

title: The rigged dice game and staking of Draupadī
description: Śakuni plays for Duryodhana; Yudhiṣṭhira loses kingdom, wealth, brothers, himself, and finally stakes and loses Draupadī

title: Building of Dvaraka
description: Amid conflicts with Jarasandha and Kalayavana, Kṛṣṇa builds the fortress-city of Dvaraka

title: Draupadī dragged into the assembly by Duḥśāsana
description: Duḥśāsana seizes the menstruating Draupadī, clad in a single cloth, by the hair and hauls her into the men's assembly

title: Fall of Duryodhana in the mace-duel
description: Śalya is killed and Bhīma smashes Duryodhana's thigh in the mace-duel, mortally wounding him on the war's final day

title: Karna's parentage revealed; the vow to spare four
description: Krishna and Kunti reveal Karna is Kunti's firstborn; loyal to Duryodhana he refuses the throne but vows to kill only Arjuna among the brothers

title: Krishna's failed peace embassy
description: Krishna goes as peace envoy but Duryodhana refuses to yield even five villages and tries to seize Krishna, who reveals his cosmic Vishvarupa, making war inevitable

title: Krishna teaches the field and its knower (kshetra/kshetrajna)
description: Krishna distinguishes the body-field from its conscious knower, names himself the universal knower of all fields, and describes the indwelling supreme Witness whose right perception yields liberation

title: The Cakravyūha and death of Abhimanyu
description: Droṇa marshals the wheel-formation; Abhimanyu, knowing only how to break in, is sealed inside by Jayadratha and killed many-against-one by a coordinated assault against the rules of combat

title: The Syamantaka jewel and marriages to Jambavati and Satyabhama
description: Krishna fights the bear-king Jambavan 28 days to recover the Syamantaka gem, winning Jambavati, and is given Satyabhama by the vindicated Satrajit

title: Vyasa's Niyoga Fathers the Kuru Heirs
description: After Vicitravirya dies heirless, sage Vyasa fathers Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura by niyoga, continuing the dynasty

title: Arjuna's vow fulfilled — Jayadratha beheaded
description: On day 14 Arjuna vows to kill Jayadratha before sundown; despite Droṇa's shielding formations, Kṛṣṇa's feigned sunset draws Jayadratha out and Arjuna beheads him

title: Aśvatthāmā's night massacre and curse
description: Aśvatthāmā, Kṛpa and Kṛtavarmā slaughter the sleeping Pāṇḍava camp; the Brahmāstra duel ensues and Aśvatthāmā is cursed

title: Commanders named and rules of war agreed
description: Bhishma is made Kaurava senapati and Dhrishtadyumna the Pandava commander; dharma-yuddha conventions are settled and Yuyutsu defects

title: Divine Paternity of the Pandavas
description: Pandu cursed to die if he embraces a wife, Kunti's mantra summons gods to father Yudhishthira, Bhima, and Arjuna, while Madri bears Nakula and Sahadeva by the Ashvins

title: Draupadī's unanswerable dharma question
description: Draupadī demands whether Yudhiṣṭhira, having already lost himself, could lawfully wager her; the silent sabhā cannot rule, and only Vikarṇa speaks in her defense

title: Kṛṣṇa's marriages and defeat of Narakasura
description: Kṛṣṇa marries Rukmini, Satyabhama, and the 16,100, and defeats the demon Narakasura

title: Krishna delivers the Bhagavad Gita
description: On the battlefield, as Arjuna collapses in despair at fighting kin, Krishna delivers the 700-verse Bhagavad Gita teaching karma, bhakti, and jnana yoga and revealing his universal form, and Arjuna resolves to fight

title: Krishna teaches the three gunas and the guna-transcender
description: Krishna expounds how sattva, rajas, and tamas bind the embodied self and shape rebirth, and portrays the gunatita who, by unswerving devotion, crosses the gunas to attain immortality

title: Slaying of Narakasura and freeing the 16,100
description: Krishna with Satyabhama on Garuda slays Narakasura of Pragjyotisha and frees the 16,100 imprisoned royal women, later taking them as wives
source: Bhagavata Purana X.59; Vishnu Purana 5; Harivamsa

title: Amba/Shikhandin back-story
description: Abducted and rejected, Amba immolates herself vowing Bhishma's death and is reborn as Drupada's child Shikhandin who becomes male

title: Destruction of the Yadava clan
description: A brahmana-curse causes the Yadava clan to annihilate itself in a drunken brawl at Prabhasa

title: Fall of Bhishma
description: On the tenth day, with Shikhandi shielding Arjuna, Bhishma falls on a bed of arrows, choosing to wait for the winter solstice to die

title: Gāndhārī curses Kṛṣṇa
description: Mourning the dead, Gāndhārī curses Kṛṣṇa, foreshadowing the ruin of the Yādavas

title: Krishna teaches the inverted cosmic tree and Purushottama
description: Krishna figures samsara as an inverted ashvattha tree to be cut by detachment, traces the jiva as an eternal fragment of himself, and names himself Purushottama, the Supreme Person beyond the perishable and imperishable

title: Kurukshetra War and Revival of Parikshit
description: The 18-day war nearly annihilates the Kuru host; Parikshit, Arjuna's grandson, is revived in the womb by Krishna and becomes the post-war king opening the historical Kali Yuga

title: The 13-year exile
description: The Pandavas spend 12 years in forest exile plus 1 year incognito at King Virata's court

title: The endless cloth — Kṛṣṇa's grace at the disrobing
description: As Duḥśāsana pulls at her single garment, it multiplies without end until he collapses exhausted and Draupadī stays covered — in devotional tellings Kṛṣṇa supplies the infinite cloth

title: The Nārāyaṇāstra crisis neutralized
description: In grief and rage Droṇa and Aśvatthāman unleash the Nārāyaṇāstra; Kṛṣṇa saves the army by having all warriors throw down their weapons, neutralizing it

title: The Parijata episode
description: To please Satyabhama, Krishna takes the celestial Parijata tree from Indra's heaven, defeating Indra

title: Bhīma's and Draupadī's vows at the dice-hall
description: Bhīma swears to break Duḥśāsana's chest and drink his blood and to smash Duryodhana's thigh; Draupadī vows to leave her hair unbound until she binds it with Duḥśāsana's blood

title: Bhīṣma teaches dharma and dies at the solstice
description: On his arrow-bed Bhīṣma instructs Yudhiṣṭhira on rāja-, āpad- and mokṣa-dharma and delivers the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma, then departs at the winter solstice

title: Birth and return of Pradyumna
description: Krishna and Rukmini's son, Kamadeva reborn, is stolen by Shambara, raised by Mayavati, and returns to slay him

title: Death of Abhimanyu
description: On the thirteenth day Arjuna's son Abhimanyu penetrates the Chakravyuha but cannot exit and is cornered and killed by six maharathis

title: Dvapara Yuga — the Age of Half Dharma
description: Virtue and vice balance evenly; disease and discord appear and Vyasa divides the Vedas as human intellect weakens, with humans living ~1,000 years

title: Krishna contrasts divine and demonic natures
description: Krishna catalogs the divine and demonic endowments, portrays the demonic mentality and its fate of being hurled into ever-lower wombs, and names lust, anger, and greed as the threefold gate to hell

title: Krishna's Birth and the Slaying of Kamsa's Demons
description: Devaki's eighth child Krishna is carried across the river to Yashoda and as an infant slays Putana, Trinavarta, Shakatasura and the Yamala-Arjuna twins

title: The Bhagavad Gita delivered
description: Arjuna's despondency between the armies triggers Krishna's 700-verse teaching on dharma, karma-yoga and bhakti, restoring his resolve

title: The lie of Aśvatthāman's death
description: Bhīma slays an elephant named Aśvatthāman and Yudhiṣṭhira confirms 'Aśvatthāman is dead — the elephant,' the qualifier drowned by Kṛṣṇa's conches, breaking Droṇa; Yudhiṣṭhira's floating chariot thereafter touches earth

title: Uddhava Gita delivered
description: Kṛṣṇa delivers his final teaching, the Uddhava Gita (Hamsa Gita), to his friend Uddhava on jnana, bhakti, and renunciation

title: Aniruddha weds Usha and the war with Banasura
description: Krishna's grandson Aniruddha weds Usha, daughter of the asura Bana, and Krishna battles Bana and Shiva's forces

title: Arjuna's despondency
description: Surveying his kin arrayed for battle, Arjuna's limbs fail and his bow slips; he refuses to fight, posing the Gita's central crisis

title: Death of Iravan
description: On day 8 Arjuna's naga-born son Iravan fights brilliantly but is beheaded by the rakshasa Alambusha

title: Death of Jayadratha
description: Arjuna vows to kill Jayadratha by sunset; Krishna conceals the sun to draw him out then reveals it, and Arjuna beheads him

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra grants Draupadī two boons
description: Frightened by evil omens, the blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra grants Draupadī two boons, freeing Yudhiṣṭhira and then all the Pāṇḍavas with their arms; she refuses a third

title: Droṇa beheaded by Dhṛṣṭadyumna
description: Crushed by the false report, Droṇa lays down his bow and sits in yoga; Dhṛṣṭadyumna seizes the defenseless brahmin by the hair and severs his head, fulfilling his birth-purpose

title: Kaliya-damana and the Lifting of Govardhana
description: Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya, swallows the forest-fire, slays Aghasura, Bakasura and Dhenukasura, and lifts Mount Govardhana to snub Indra

title: Kṛṣṇa's disappearance, struck by Jara
description: Kṛṣṇa is struck in the heel by the hunter Jara and departs the earth, marking the full onset of Kali Yuga

title: Krishna teaches the three kinds of faith and Om Tat Sat
description: Krishna analyzes faith, food, sacrifice, austerity, and charity by the three gunas and expounds the threefold designation of Brahman, Om Tat Sat, used since creation to consecrate sacred acts

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's Aśvamedha and the Anu-Gītā
description: Yudhiṣṭhira performs the horse sacrifice to expiate the war, and Kṛṣṇa recaps his teaching in the Anu-Gītā

title: Aśvatthāman's grief-driven night-massacre
description: Learning of his father's deceitful beheading, Aśvatthāman slaughters the sleeping Pāñcālas including Dhṛṣṭadyumna and is cursed by Kṛṣṇa to wander deathless for 3,000 years

title: Death of Ghatotkacha
description: Bhima's rakshasa son Ghatotkacha rampages by night and Karna spends his infallible Shakti spear, reserved for Arjuna, to kill him — a decisive turn

title: Death of the elders in the forest fire
description: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī retire to the forest and perish in a wildfire

title: Fall of Bhishma on the bed of arrows
description: On day 10 Arjuna, shielded by Shikhandin, fells Bhishma, who lies on a bed of arrows choosing to die only at uttarayana

title: Krishna delivers the final teaching of surrender (Charama Shloka)
description: In the grand synthesis Krishna distinguishes sannyasa from tyaga, grades all things by the gunas, and gives the supreme final word, sarva-dharman parityajya, calling Arjuna to abandon all dharmas and take refuge in him alone

title: Slaying of Jarasandha
description: Krishna with Bhima and Arjuna engineers Bhima's wrestling victory that kills Jarasandha, freeing the kings he imprisoned and clearing the way for the Rajasuya
source: Bhagavata Purana X.72; Mahabharata Sabha Parva

title: The second dice game and thirteen-year exile
description: A fresh dice game sends the Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī into thirteen years' exile, the casus belli of Kurukṣetra

title: Arjuna's delusion is dispelled and he resolves to fight
description: Arjuna declares his delusion destroyed and his memory regained by Krishna's grace, standing firm and vowing to carry out Krishna's word, fulfilling the teaching's purpose of moving him from despair to resolved action

title: Death of Abhimanyu in the cakra-vyuha
description: Day 13: the 16-year-old Abhimanyu breaks into the wheel formation but cannot exit and is killed by six warriors ganging up unfairly

title: Death of Drona
description: Through Krishna's stratagem of the ambiguous report of Ashvatthama's death, the grieving Drona lays down arms and is beheaded by Dhrishtadyumna

title: Death of Sisupala at the Rajasuya
description: At the Rajasuya, honored first, Krishna beheads Sisupala with the Sudarsana cakra after he exceeds the hundred forgiven offenses
source: Bhagavata Purana X.74; Mahabharata Sabha Parva

title: Fall of the Yādavas and death of Kṛṣṇa
description: Gāndhārī's curse ripens as the Yādavas slay each other at Prabhāsa, Kṛṣṇa is killed by the hunter Jarā (marking Kali's onset) and Dvārakā sinks into the sea

title: Krishna Slays Kamsa at Mathura
description: Akrura brings Krishna to Mathura, where he breaks the great bow and kills the tyrant Kamsa

title: The Vishvarupa theophany
description: Granted a divine eye, Arjuna beholds Krishna's Universal Form, Time the world-destroyer, with all beings rushing into its mouths

title: Sanjaya's epilogue benediction
description: Sanjaya, having relayed the whole dialogue to blind Dhritarashtra, marvels at the wondrous discourse and pronounces the closing benediction that wherever Krishna and Arjuna are, there are fortune, victory, and morality

title: Slaying of Jayadratha at false sunset
description: Day 14: Krishna feigns sunset with his discus so Arjuna can fulfil his vow and behead Jayadratha, the boon recoiling on his father

title: Sudama's visit and reward
description: Krishna's impoverished boyhood friend brings flattened rice and is silently granted lavish wealth, the paradigm of devotion and divine reciprocity

title: Uddhava's Mission to Vraja
description: Krishna sends Uddhava to console the grieving gopis, occasioning the Bhramara-gita addressed to a bee

title: Death of Bhurishravas
description: Bhurishravas, about to behead Satyaki, loses his arm to Arjuna and is then beheaded by Satyaki while sitting in praya-fast

title: Deaths of Shalya and Shakuni
description: On the eighteenth day Shalya is killed by Yudhishthira and Shakuni by Sahadeva as the last Kaurava brothers fall

title: Krishna Beheads Shishupala at the Rajasuya
description: Krishna's Sudarshana beheads the rival cousin Shishupala when his hundred offences are filled at Yudhishthira's Rajasuya

title: Reunion at Kurukshetra during the eclipse
description: On an eclipse pilgrimage the Vraja folk and the Pandavas reunite with Krishna at Samanta-panchaka

title: Arjuna's despondency at Kurukshetra
description: Seeing kin arrayed for battle, Arjuna lays down his bow in moral crisis over killing teachers and family, opening the Gita's vishada-yoga

title: Arjuna wins the Pāśupatāstra from Śiva
description: After single combat with Śiva in his Kirāta hunter form, Arjuna wins the Pāśupatāstra — the central boon of his Himālayan tapas

title: Bhishma waits for Uttarayana to die
description: Bhishma famously withholds his death until the auspicious northward course of the Sun (Uttarayana) begins, illustrating the devayana half-year

title: Birth and childhood of Kṛṣṇa (Harivaṃśa)
description: The Harivaṃśa appendix supplies Kṛṣṇa's birth and childhood, absent from the main epic, bridging itihāsa to the Kṛṣṇa-centric Purāṇas

title: Death of Ghatotkaca and spent Vasavi Shakti
description: In the night battle Karna is forced to spend his one-use Vasavi Shakti on the rampaging Ghatotkaca, secretly saving Arjuna's life

title: Duryodhana's fall
description: Drawn out of hiding in a lake, Duryodhana fights Bhima with maces and Bhima smashes his thigh with an unfair blow on Krishna's hint, fulfilling his vow

title: Jayadratha's attempted abduction of Draupadī
description: The Sindhu king Jayadratha tries to carry Draupadī off from the forest hermitage; the brothers rescue her and shave his head in shame

title: Maya Builds the Pandavas' Hall at Indraprastha
description: The asura architect Maya constructs the Pandavas' illusory assembly hall at Indraprastha, cited as a foundational feat of Sthapatyaveda architecture

title: Recovering a Brahmin's dead sons from Maha-Vishnu
description: Krishna and Arjuna travel beyond the world to retrieve a Brahmin's lost children, revealing Krishna's supreme identity to Arjuna

title: The Mausala Destruction of the Yadus
description: The Yadava sages are cursed, and the iron-club fratricide at Prabhasa destroys the Yadavas as Krishna withdraws

title: Vyasa divides the Vedas
description: In Dvapara Yuga the Vedas are divided by Vyasa because human memory and intellect have weakened

title: Bhīma slays Kīcaka for harassing Sairandhrī
description: Serving as the maid Sairandhrī in Virāṭa's court, Draupadī lures the lustful Kīcaka to a night tryst where Bhīma pounds him into a shapeless ball; the Upakīcakas who try to burn her on the pyre are also killed

title: Curse of the sages and Gandhari on the Yadava clan
description: Yadava boys mock the rishis who curse the clan to destruction by an iron club, and the bereaved Gandhari also curses Krishna's line to perish

title: Sauptika night massacre and revival of Parikshit
description: Ashvatthama with Kripa and Kritavarma raid the sleeping camp slaughtering Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandi, and Draupadi's five sons, then loose the Brahmashiras at Uttara's womb; Krishna revives the unborn Parikshit and curses Ashvatthama to wander 3,000 years

title: Aravan's battlefield self-sacrifice
description: Aravan, son of Arjuna and the Naga princess Ulupi, offers himself to Kali before the Mahabharata war for Pandava victory, asking to be wed for one night; Krishna as Mohini weds and mourns him
source: Tamil Aravan Kalappali; Parata Venpa (9th c.); Villiputturar Makaparatam

title: Dattatreya's Twenty-Four Gurus Recounted
description: Within the Uddhava-gita, Krishna recounts the avadhuta Dattatreya's dialogue with King Yadu listing the twenty-four gurus he took from nature

title: Narayanastra released and countered
description: Ashvatthama unleashes Vishnu's Narayana weapon; Krishna has the army submit unresisting so it dissipates harmlessly

title: The Uddhava-Gita delivered
description: Krishna gives his last great discourse to Uddhava on jnana, bhakti, and the avadhuta's 24 gurus, then sends him to Badarikashrama

title: Death of Duhshasana
description: Bhima tears open Duhshasana's chest and drinks his blood, fulfilling his dice-hall vow; Draupadi binds her hair in the blood

title: Krishna's Departure by the Hunter Jara
description: The hunter Jara mistakes Krishna's foot for a deer and shoots him; Krishna ascends and Dvaraka sinks beneath the sea

title: Yadava fratricide at Prabhasa
description: Drunken Yadavas turn the cursed reeds-turned-clubs on each other and almost the whole clan dies at Prabhasa

title: Yudhishthira's reign and the Ashvamedha
description: Yudhishthira is crowned at Hastinapura, Bhishma delivers the Shanti and Anushasana teachings before dying at the solstice, and a horse-sacrifice is performed

title: Departure of Balarama
description: Balarama merges into yoga by the sea as a great white serpent issues from his mouth into the ocean

title: Fall of Duryodhana
description: Drawn from a lake, Duryodhana duels Bhima with maces; Bhima smashes his thigh on Krishna's hint, fulfilling his vow

title: The sages' curse on Samba
description: Krishna's son Samba, dressed as a pregnant woman to mock visiting sages, is cursed to bear an iron club that will doom the Yadava clan; ground to powder it regrows as deadly reed-grass

title: Death of Krishna marks onset of Kali Yuga
description: The death of Krishna, traditionally on 17/18 February 3102 BCE, marks the onset of the Kali Yuga and the epoch of the Kali-samvat era

title: Karṇa born with the Kavaca-Kuṇḍala; Indra extracts it
description: Karṇa is born with invulnerable golden armor and earrings fused to his body, the gift of his father Sūrya; Indra extracts them by guile to make Karṇa killable

title: The Mahabharata war and Krishna's departure mark the Dvapara-Kali transition
description: The great Mahabharata war and Krishna's departure mark the turn from Dvapara into Kali Yuga, traditionally dated to 3102 BCE

title: The Sauptika night massacre
description: Ashvatthama raids the sleeping camp, killing Draupadi's five sons; his Brahmashiras aimed at Parikshit's womb is countered by Krishna, who curses him

title: Yadava civil war at Prabhasa
description: On pilgrimage the drunken Yadavas quarrel, the reeds turn to iron clubs in their hands, and the entire clan slaughters itself

title: Death of Balarama
description: Balarama withdraws into yoga at the seashore and Shesha-naga issues from his mouth into the ocean as he departs the world

title: Death of Shakuni
description: Sahadeva beheads Shakuni, the dice-master architect of the war, fulfilling his own dice-hall vow

title: Garga names Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma
description: The Yādava family-priest Garga performs the naming rite for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma

title: Planets align in conjunction at the start of Kali Yuga
description: The Surya Siddhanta sets all planets in conjunction at the start of Kali Yuga (18 Feb 3102 BCE), synchronizing the planetary clock with the cosmological clock

title: Submersion of Dwaraka
description: As Krishna departs the sea reclaims Dwaraka; Arjuna evacuates the surviving women and children, who are raided by bandits en route

title: Death of Krishna
description: Krishna sits in meditation under a pipal tree and the hunter Jara, mistaking his reddish sole for a deer, shoots an arrow piercing it; Krishna ascends to his abode, ending the avatar and marking the onset of Kali Yuga

title: Onset of Kali Yuga at Krishna's departure
description: Krishna's departure (traditionally 3102 BCE) marks the start of Kali Yuga and the Pandavas' final journey

title: The mace-duel and fall of Duryodhana
description: In the gada-yuddha Bhima, cued by Krishna, breaks Duryodhana's thighs with a foul below-the-belt blow, effectively ending the war

title: The Uddhava-Gita
description: Krishna gives his last great discourse to his devotee Uddhava on jnana, bhakti, and the avadhuta's 24 gurus before the end

title: Viṣṇu slays the demon Pañcajana and takes the conch
description: In the Mahābhārata/Skanda variant, Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa slays the demon Pañcajana (in whale-form, who had swallowed Sāndīpani's son) and seizes the conch he dwelt in, naming it Pāñcajanya

title: Ashvatthama's night massacre
description: Empowered by Shiva, Ashvatthama with Kripa and Kritavarman slaughters the sleeping Pandava camp, killing Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin and the Upapandavas

title: Curse of the sages on Samba
description: Krishna's son Samba is dressed as a pregnant woman to mock sages, who curse the clan to be doomed by an iron club

title: Krishna's Vishvarupa theophany — 'I am Time'
description: At the climax of the universal-form vision Krishna declares 'kalo'smi' — I am Time, the world-destroyer — revealing the cosmic person as the cosmic clock and Arjuna as its instrument

title: Submergence of Dvaraka
description: As Krishna leaves, the sea swallows Dvaraka; Arjuna evacuates the survivors but is robbed en route, his powers fading with the age

title: Sudarśana Cakra beheads Śiśupāla
description: Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana Cakra beheads Śiśupāla after his hundred offenses are exhausted

title: Brahmashiras duel and curse of Ashvatthama
description: Ashvatthama aims the Brahmashiras at Uttara's womb; Krishna vows to revive the child Parikshit, takes Ashvatthama's gem and curses him to wander 3,000 years

title: Brahma-vimohana-lila (Bewilderment of Brahma)
description: Doubting child-Krishna, the Brahma of our universe steals Krishna's cowherd boys and calves; Krishna duplicates them all for a year and reveals countless universes each with its own Brahma, humbling his pride

title: Draupadī demands Aśvatthāman's head after the night-raid
description: After all five Draupadeyas are slain in the night-raid, Draupadī demands Aśvatthāman's head but accepts the gem from his crest instead

title: Karṇa loses his Nāgāstra against Arjuna
description: Karṇa looses the nāgāstra (the serpent Aśvasena) at Arjuna's head, but Kṛṣṇa presses the chariot into the earth so it strikes only Arjuna's crown

title: Krishna delivers the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna
description: Krishna answers Arjuna's crisis by teaching svadharma, niskama-karma, and the imperishable atman, reconciling the warrior's duty with ahimsa

title: Krishna slays Narakasura (Naraka Chaturdashi)
description: Krishna with Satyabhama slays the asura Narakasura of Pragjyotishapura and frees 16,000 captives, the South Indian Deepavali charter

title: Posthumous revelation of Karna's birth
description: After the war Kunti reveals Karna was the eldest Pandava; the anguished Yudhishthira curses all women never to keep a secret

title: Bhagadatta's Vaiṣṇavāstra absorbed by Kṛṣṇa
description: Bhagadatta looses the infallible Vaiṣṇavāstra at Arjuna, but Kṛṣṇa absorbs it onto his own chest, where it becomes the Vaijayantī garland

title: Draupadī's death on the Himālayan ascent
description: On the great departure toward heaven, Draupadī is the first of the six to fall dead, attributed by Yudhiṣṭhira to her partiality for Arjuna

title: Sage's curse on Samba's iron club
description: Yadava princes mock rishis with Samba dressed as a pregnant woman; the cursed iron club is ground to powder that becomes the deadly eraka grass

title: Aśvatthāman looses the Nārāyaṇāstra; Pāṇḍavas survive by submission
description: Aśvatthāman discharges Viṣṇu's Nārāyaṇāstra, and Kṛṣṇa has the Pāṇḍava host drop their weapons and dismount so the auto-multiplying barrage finds no resistance

title: Draupadī restored as Śrī in heaven
description: In heaven Yudhiṣṭhira finds Draupadī revealed as the goddess Śrī/Lakṣmī, closing her prior-birth incarnation

title: Submergence of Dwaraka
description: As Krishna leaves, the sea swallows Dwaraka; Arjuna evacuates survivors but is robbed en route as his powers fade

title: The Yadava clan self-destructs at Prabhasa
description: Thirty-six years after the war the drunken Vrishni-Andhakas slay one another with eraka-turned-iron clubs, fulfilling Gandhari's and the sages' curses

title: Death of Balarama and Krishna; sinking of Dvaraka
description: Balarama departs as Shesha; the hunter Jara's arrow pierces Krishna's foot and he ascends, after which the sea swallows Dvaraka, ending the Dvapara Yuga

title: Śeṣa incarnates as Balarāma
description: When Viṣṇu descends as Kṛṣṇa, Śeṣa descends as his elder brother Balarāma, whose serpent-nature departs his mouth as a white nāga at his death

title: Indra gives Karṇa the Vāsava-śakti for his kavaca-kuṇḍala
description: Indra trades his one-use infallible dart, the Vāsava-śakti, to Karṇa in exchange for his birth-armor and earrings (kavaca-kuṇḍala)

title: Karṇa spends the Vāsava-śakti on Ghaṭotkaca
description: Forced by Ghaṭotkaca's rampage, Karṇa expends his one-use Vāsava-śakti dart (reserved for Arjuna) to kill Bhīma's son Ghaṭotkaca

title: Arjuna beheads Karṇa with the Añjalikāstra
description: Arjuna uses Indra's crescent-bladed Añjalikāstra to behead Karṇa, who had lost his Bhārgavāstra knowledge to a curse at the decisive moment

title: Śiva grants Barbarīka the three infallible arrows
description: Śiva grants Ghaṭotkaca's son Barbarīka three infallible arrows able to end the entire war in a moment — one marks targets to destroy, one to save, the third destroys/binds the marked

title: Sudarśana obscures the sun to trap Jayadratha
description: Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana Cakra obscures the sun at Kurukṣetra to trick Jayadratha into the open so Arjuna can fulfill his vow

title: Brahmaśiras duel of Arjuna and Aśvatthāman; killing and revival of Parīkṣit
description: After Kurukṣetra, Arjuna and Aśvatthāman loose Brahmaśiras at each other; Vyāsa and Nārada intervene, Arjuna withdraws his but Aśvatthāman cannot, redirecting it at Uttarā's womb to kill the unborn Parīkṣit, whom Kṛṣṇa revives

title: Aśvatthāman cursed for the Brahmaśiras misuse
description: For aiming the unwithdrawable Brahmaśiras at the Pāṇḍava line, Aśvatthāman is cursed with the loss of his head-jewel and a festering wound enduring for millennia

title: Burning of the Khāṇḍava forest and gift of the Gāṇḍīva to Arjuna
description: When Agni begs Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa to help him consume the Khāṇḍava forest, Varuṇa gives Arjuna the bow Gāṇḍīva (made by Brahmā) with two inexhaustible quivers

title: Pārijātaharaṇa — Kṛṣṇa steals the Pārijāta from Indra
description: Kṛṣṇa uproots the Pārijāta tree from Indra's heaven and plants it in Satyabhāmā's courtyard, provoking a brief war with Indra

title: Sūrya gifts the Syamantaka gem to Satrājit
description: The sun-gem Syamantaka, source of Sūrya's brilliance and yielding eight bhāras of gold daily, is gifted by Sūrya to the Yādava king Satrājit

title: The Syamantaka affair — Kṛṣṇa fights Jāmbavān and weds Jāmbavatī
description: Falsely accused of stealing the Syamantaka after Prasena is killed by a lion and the gem taken by Jāmbavān, Kṛṣṇa fights the bear-king for 28 days (or 21), who yields the gem and his daughter Jāmbavatī in marriage; Kṛṣṇa returns it and weds Satyabhāmā

title: Kṛṣṇa sounds the Pāñcajanya to open the Kurukṣetra war
description: Kṛṣṇa blows his conch Pāñcajanya, with Arjuna's Devadatta and the Pāṇḍava conches, to open the Bhagavad-gītā and the Kurukṣetra war

title: Sūrya gives Yudhiṣṭhira the Akṣaya-pātra
description: After Yudhiṣṭhira's penance in the Gaṅgā, Sūrya gives the Pāṇḍavas the inexhaustible food-vessel Akṣaya-pātra, yielding unlimited food each day until Draupadī takes her own meal

title: Kṛṣṇa sates Durvāsā with a single rice-grain from the Akṣaya-pātra
description: When Durvāsā and his thousand disciples arrive after Draupadī has eaten, Kṛṣṇa eats a single clinging rice-grain from the empty pot and thereby sates the sage's whole party

title: Kāliya-mardana — Kṛṣṇa dances on the serpent Kāliya
description: The boy Kṛṣṇa leaps into the Yamunā at Vṛndāvana, is coiled by the venomous Nāga Kāliya, then dances on his hoods until he submits and departs, sparing him at his wives' plea

title: Kṛṣṇa masters the 64 kalās and 14 vidyās in 64 days
description: After slaying Kaṃsa and his upanayana, Kṛṣṇa (with Balarāma) studies under guru Sāndīpani at Avantī/Ujjayinī and masters the 14 vidyās and 64 kalās within 64 days

title: Kṛṣṇa restores Sāndīpani's drowned son as guru-dakṣiṇā
description: As guru-dakṣiṇā, Kṛṣṇa restores Sāndīpani's drowned son from the sea/Yama's realm

title: Krishna's life and the Bhagavad Gita
description: Krishna slays his tyrant uncle Kamsa, lifts Govardhana hill, and as Arjuna's charioteer at Kurukshetra delivers the Bhagavad Gita; his departure in 3102 BCE marks the start of Kali Yuga

title: Balarama's deeds
description: Balarama, incarnation of the serpent Shesha and Krishna's elder brother, slays the asuras Dhenuka and Pralamba and drags the Yamuna river with his plow

title: Kṛṣṇa destroys Śālva's flying fortress Saubha
description: Kṛṣṇa destroys Saubha, the airborne fortress-city of the asura king Śālva, after it attacks Dvārakā

title: Vyāsa redacts the Vedas at the Dvapara–Kali junction
description: Vyāsa (Krishna Dvaipayana) arranges and redacts the four Vedas at the Dvapara–Kali junction (~3102 BCE in the scriptural frame), earning the title Veda-Vyāsa

title: Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata
description: Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata, chronicling the Kuru succession war at Kurukṣetra and containing the Bhagavad Gītā, with Krishna's departure marking the start of Kali Yuga

title: The eight Vasus steal Vasiṣṭha's cow Nandinī
description: The eight Vasus, led by Prabhāsa at his wife's urging, steal the wish-cow Nandinī from the sage Vasiṣṭha and are cursed to be born among mortals

title: Gaṅgā drowns seven Vasu-newborns; the eighth becomes Bhīṣma
description: The river-goddess Gaṅgā bears the cursed Vasus by King Śāntanu and drowns the first seven at birth to release them; Śāntanu stays her hand at the eighth, Prabhāsa, who lives on as Bhīṣma

title: Arjuna requests the Gita teaching again (Anugita frame)
description: After the Kurukshetra war, as Krishna prepares to leave for Dvaraka, Arjuna confesses he has forgotten the supreme teaching of Kurukshetra and begs Krishna to repeat it

title: Krishna smears color on Radha and the gopis (Holi)
description: Krishna playfully smears color on Radha and the gopis in Vrindavan, the devotional origin of Holi's play of colors

title: Krishna declines to repeat the Gita verbatim
description: Krishna rebukes Arjuna's lapse and declares he cannot reproduce the original discourse word-for-word since it was uttered in a yogic trance, choosing instead to convey the same truths through an old narrative

title: Krishna speaks the Anugita to Arjuna
description: In peacetime after the war, Krishna delivers the Anugita, a jnana-and-Samkhya seminar restating the Gita through embedded ancient stories, within the Ashvamedhika Parva

title: Yudhishthira performs the Ashvamedha horse-sacrifice
description: To expiate the slaughter of the war, Yudhishthira performs the ashvamedha (horse-sacrifice) that gives Book 14 of the Mahabharata its name

title: Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva cursed to become trees
description: Kubera's sons Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva are cursed by Nārada to become trees, later liberated by the infant Kṛṣṇa in the yamalārjuna episode

title: The Yakṣa Praśna and revival of the Pāṇḍavas
description: A yakṣa guarding a lake kills the four younger Pāṇḍavas who drink without answering him; Yudhiṣṭhira alone answers the dharma-catechism, and the yakṣa — revealed as Yama-Dharma — restores his brothers to life

title: Sthūṇa exchanges sex with Śikhaṇḍin
description: The yakṣa Sthūṇa compassionately exchanges his sex with Śikhaṇḍinī so she can become male; Kubera curses the exchange permanent, enabling the fall of Bhīṣma

title: Astika halts Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice (Nag Panchami)
description: The sage Astika stops King Janamejaya's sarpa-satra and saves the serpent race, the Adi Parva frame-story commemorated at Nag Panchami

title: Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya
description: Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna, recalled in western Nag Panchami strands

title: Birth of Krishna (Janmashtami)
description: Krishna, the 8th avatar, is born at midnight in Mathura's prison to Devaki and Vasudeva, commemorated by Krishna Janmashtami

title: Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill (Govardhan Puja)
description: Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill on one finger to shelter Vrindavan from Indra's rains, teaching worship of nature over Indra; commemorated as Annakut

title: Vyasa dictates the Mahabharata to Ganesha
description: Ganesha serves as scribe to whom Vyasa dictates the Mahabharata, invoked at Ganesh Chaturthi as lord of letters and beginnings

title: Bhishma chooses death at Uttarayana (Makar Sankranti)
description: Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows with the boon of icchamrityu, waits for Uttarayana before releasing his life, commemorated at Makar Sankranti

title: Draupadi binds her sari on Krishna's finger
description: Draupadi binds her torn sari on Krishna's bleeding finger and he vows lifelong protection, repaid at the vastra-haran; a Raksha Bandhan charter

title: Krishna speaks the Gita on Mokshada Ekadashi
description: Vaikuntha/Mokshada Ekadashi marks the day the Bhagavad Gita was spoken by Krishna to Arjuna

title: Birth of Vyasa / division of the Veda (Guru Purnima)
description: Guru Purnima honors the birth and Veda-division day of Veda Vyasa, the Adi Guru who split the one Veda into four and composed the Mahabharata and Puranas

title: The Avantī Brāhmaṇa's Song of Forbearance (Bhikṣu-gītā)
description: Recited by Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava in his farewell teaching: a rich but miserly brāhmaṇa of Avantī (Ujjain), who hoarded wealth and neglected gods, guests, and ancestors, is stripped of everything by fate (relatives, thieves, time, fire, accident); reduced to begging he is mocked, beaten, and reviled by the townsfolk, yet bears it without anger. Reflecting, he realizes that neither other people, the body, the planets (graha), time (kāla), nor fate/karma cause his suffering — the mind alone (manas) is the cause of bondage and liberation; he vows forbearance (titikṣā), crosses the ocean of material existence, and attains peace
actors: the unnamed miserly brāhmaṇa of Avantī (Ujjain)
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.23 (Bhikṣu-gītā / Avantī-brāhmaṇa-gītā), within the Uddhava-gītā (11.6.40–11.29)

title: Acyutānanda's Mālikā foretells Kali's end
description: palm-leaf Bhaviṣya Mālikā prophecies of calamity, the sea entering Purī, Jagannātha leaving the Śrīmandira, and Kalki's advent [folk] [disputed]

title: Aśvatthāman's weapon against the embryo
description: After Kurukṣetra, Aśvatthāman hurls the Brahmaśiras/Aiṣīka weapon to abort the unborn last Kuru heir in Uttarā's womb
source: Mahābhārata Sauptika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.7–8

title: Ātmadeva retires to the forest with the Tenth Skandha
description: Counselled in vairāgya by Gokarṇa, the grieving Ātmadeva renounces home at sixty, daily recites the Bhāgavata's Tenth Skandha, and attains the Lord

title: Bhakti revived by Bhāgavata recitation
description: Bhakti personified, wandering with her fainting sons Jñāna and Vairāgya, is restored in Kali-yuga by recitation of the Bhāgavata, with the Gokarṇa–Dhundhukārī ghost-liberation tale

title: Bharata ascends by one funeral-rite merit and Puṣkara's grace
description: the sinner, saved by having once carried a stranger's dead child to the Gaṅgā bank and performed its funeral rites, rises to heaven in a celestial vehicle, crediting the grace of Puṣkara

title: Bharata dies confessing at Puṣkara
description: Puṇḍarīka finds his sinful younger brother mortally wounded at the lake and hears his confession of the prostitute Prabhāvatī, gambling, theft, and a brāhmaṇa's killing

title: Bhartṛhari and the immortality-fruit
description: given an amṛta-phala, Bhartṛhari watches it circle from queen to stable-master to courtesan and back to him, grasps the vanity of desire, cedes the throne of Ujjayinī to Vikramāditya, and turns yogin

title: Bhīmā glorified as Candrabhāgā
description: the Pāṇḍuraṅga-māhātmya sanctifies the crescent bend of the Bhīmā at Pandharpur as the Candrabhāgā tīrtha whose bath destroys sins, with Puṇḍalīka's shrine on its sands

title: Binduga forsakes Cañculā
description: a base brahmin of the seaside village Bāṣkala abandons his faithful, beautiful wife Cañculā for a prostitute, squandering himself in a courtesan's house

title: Binduga the wind-eating piśāca
description: Pārvatī reveals that Binduga, after death and hell, has become a piśāca bound to the Vindhya mountains, feeding only on wind, from the residue of his sins

title: Binduga's salvation by recitation
description: at Cañculā's intercession the Gandharva-king Tumburu recites the whole Śiva Purāṇa (saṃhitās 1–7) to the bound ghost, who sheds his sins and piśāca-body and ascends by aerial chariot to Śiva's abode

title: Birth of Naravāhanadatta
description: from the restored marriage of Udayana and Vāsavadattā is born the son destined to become cakravartin of the Vidyādharas, the frame-hero of the rest of the ocean of story

title: Bṛhadratha's Renunciation
description: King Bṛhadratha, judging body and world impermanent, installs his son and retires to the forest for austerity

title: Bhīma's unforgiving taunt drives the elders to renounce
description: During fifteen years of concord, Bhīma alone cannot forgive and openly boasts of slaying the Kaurava sons and drinking Duḥśāsana's blood, wounding Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī and pushing them toward renunciation

title: Brahman identified as Kṛṣṇa-Gopāla
description: The Upaniṣad opens by declaring the supreme Brahman to be Kṛṣṇa, the eternal cowherd (Gopāla) of Vṛndāvana, cause of all causes

title: Cañculā's adultery and the pimping contract
description: neglected, the once-chaste Cañculā takes a paramour; discovering it, Binduga strikes a nefarious mutual contract, profiting from his wife's adultery until her youth fades

title: Cañculā's disillusion at Gokarṇa
description: at the Gokarṇa temple Cañculā chances to hear a discourse describing the tortures of adulterous women, trembles with fear, and falls at the reciting brahmin's feet begging to be lifted from her plight

title: Cañculā's salvation
description: instructed in the Śiva Purāṇa she takes up Śaiva asceticism — bark, matted hair, ash, rudrākṣa, Śiva's names — casts off her body, assumes the form of Gaurī, and becomes an attendant of Pārvatī in Śiva's city

title: Caṇḍamahāsena's artificial elephant
description: the Ujjayinī king traps the elephant-charmer Udayana of Vatsa by a mechanical wooden elephant hiding armed men in the Vindhya forest, carrying him captive to Ujjayinī

title: Citraketu's sonlessness
description: The mighty emperor of Śūrasena grieves that none of his many wives bears him a son

title: Codification of the tālamāna unit system
description: The śilpa-śāstras define the aṅgula, mānāṅgula and the face-based tāla (12 aṅgulas) as the modular units of all image-measure
actors: śilpins (image-makers); compilers of the Mānasāra and Mayamata

title: Composition of the Nṛsiṃha-anuṣṭubh (Mantrarāja)
description: After Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu, the terrified gods and ṛṣis compose the thirty-two-syllable anuṣṭubh 'king of mantras' to pacify and praise the Man-Lion

title: Coronation of Parīkṣit at Hastināpura
description: Renouncing the throne, Yudhiṣṭhira installs Parīkṣit, the lone Kuru heir revived by Kṛṣṇa in the womb, as King of Hastināpura with Kṛpa as his preceptor, and leaves Yuyutsu as regent

title: Devarāja's catalogue of sins
description: a Kirāta brahmin turned liquor-seller robs all four varṇas by murder, kills his own mother, father, and first wife for wealth, and dissipates the family fortune with the courtesan Śobhāvatī

title: Devasmitā and the red lotus of fidelity
description: armed with Śiva's chastity-token, a merchant's wife sees through the nun Yogakaraṇḍikā's weeping-bitch ruse, brands four seducers with a dog's-foot mark, and reclaims her honor disguised as a merchant

title: Dhaneśvara saved by a single Kārtika lamp
description: a lifelong sinner is present when a lamp is lit before Viṣṇu in Kārtika, and that one accidental dīpa outweighs his sins so his soul is saved at death
source: Skanda P., Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya; Padma P., Uttara-khaṇḍa

title: Dharmadatta frees the piśācī Kalahā
description: a drop of Tulasī-sanctified water from the brāhmaṇa's Kārtika worship cleanses the quarrel-ghost Kalahā and releases her from ghost-hood

title: Dhundhukārī murdered by the five harlots; becomes a preta
description: His prostitutes strangle him with ropes and kill him with burning coals, burying the body secretly; dead by violence without rites, he becomes a tormented wind-form ghost

title: Durvāsas commissioned to revive the Śaiva teaching
description: the śāstras lost in deepening Kali Yuga, Śiva as Śrīkaṇṭha orders Durvāsas to restore them; his mind-born son Tryambaka founds the non-dual line claimed by Kashmir Śaivism
source: lineage account with Tantrāloka 36, Jayaratha's Viveka

title: Founding of the Four Vaishnava Sampradayas
description: To anchor valid initiation in Kali Yuga, four authorized disciplic lines are inaugurated by Shri, Brahma, Rudra and the Kumaras, whose acharyas are prophesied to appear at Purushottama-kshetra

title: Gāṇḍīva surrendered at the Lauhitya waters
description: on the Pāṇḍavas' final journey Agni bars the way and Arjuna casts the Gāṇḍīva and quivers back into the Lauhitya sea for Varuṇa

title: Gayā-śrāddha fails and Sūrya counsels the saptāha
description: Gokarṇa's śrāddha at Gayā and every tīrtha cannot free the preta, who appears in shifting terrible forms; appealed to, the Sun-god prescribes a seven-day hearing of the Bhāgavata

title: Gokarṇa born of the cow
description: The cow that ate the sannyāsī's fruit gives birth to a perfect human child with cow's ears, named Gokarṇa, raised alongside the wicked Dhundhukārī

title: Guru and Vāyu install Kṛṣṇa at Guruvāyūr
description: as Dvārakā sinks at the Dvāpara–Kali hinge, Bṛhaspati and Vāyu recover the floating icon, are guided by Paraśurāma, and enshrine it by Rudratīrtha where Śiva cedes the spot and withdraws to Mammiyūr

title: Indra's dance-contest & the gift of the throne
description: summoned to Amarāvatī to judge whether Rambhā or Urvaśī dances better, Vikramāditya renders a flawless verdict and Indra rewards him with the jewelled lion-throne borne by thirty-two apsara statuettes

title: Janamejaya questions Vaiśampāyana about Kashmir
description: In the generation after the war, Janamejaya asks why no Kashmir king fought at Kurukṣetra, and Vaiśampāyana's answer unfolds into the whole Nīlamata — Kashmir's origins and Nīla's ordinances

title: Kali Yuga Begins
description: Kali Yuga starts at 3102 BCE the moment Kali fully enters, reckoned from Krishna's departure from earth
source: Bhagavata Purana 1.15.36, Vishnu Purana 5.38, Surya Siddhanta 1.15-20

title: Katamaraju crowned Pasuvulanna
description: the Yadava cattle-chief, reckoned 74th from Vishnu and 23rd from Krishna and himself an incarnation of Vishnu, is crowned sovereign over all the Yadava herds and vows lifelong brahmacarya
source: Katamaraju Kathalu, Coronation of Katama Raju

title: Katamaraju's duel with Goddess Ganga at the Paleru
description: driven south by drought, the herder-king argues with the goddess Ganga who bars his herds at the Paleru, finally salutes and worships her, and is blessed to cross

title: King Cola vs Viṣṇudāsa & the freed brahma-rākṣasa
description: rich king and poor bhakta each donate a Kārtika-observance to liberate a tree-haunting brahma-rākṣasa, then quarrel to the edge of war over whose merit freed him until Viṣṇu judges their bhakti equal

title: King Tuṅgadhvaja spurns the cowherds' prasāda
description: the king refuses the vrata prasāda of cowherds worshipping under a tree, loses his hundred sons and wealth, and regains all by joining the vrata and eating the prasāda

title: Kṣāntiśīla's gem-fruits oblige the king
description: The mendicant Kṣāntiśīla presents King Trivikramasena a fruit daily for years, each hiding a priceless gem, and summons him to the cremation ground by night

title: Lakṣmī chooses Karavīra as her earthly seat
description: Mahālakṣmī takes up permanent earthly residence at Karavīra, glorified by the māhātmya as the foremost of all tīrthas

title: Lakṣmī expelled from the Śrīmandira
description: Balabhadra brands the goddess polluted for entering a caṇḍāla's house and Jagannātha, deferring to his elder brother, casts her out

title: Lakṣmī's conditions and the Mahāprasād charter
description: Lakṣmī returns to the temple only after Jagannātha concedes that no caste distinction shall attach to his food, the story Odia tradition tells for Purī's caste-free Mahāprasād
source: Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa, conclusion

title: Lakṣmī's Gurubāra inspection of Purī
description: on a Mārgaśira Thursday Lakṣmī leaves the Śrīmandira, finds high-caste houses negligent, and accepts the worship of the outcaste devotee Śriyā
source: Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa, opening

title: Lavaṇāsura tyrannises the Lonār country
description: The salt-asura Lavaṇāsura/Lonāsura oppresses the region, sages and gods from his lair in the crater basin
source: Skanda Purāṇa Lonar-māhātmya tradition; Lonar sthala-purāṇa

title: Lineage transmission from Brahmā to Śaunaka
description: Brahmā teaches Brahma-vidyā to Atharvan, passed down through Aṅgiras and Satyavaha until Śaunaka the householder asks Aṅgiras what, once known, makes all known

title: Lohajaṅgha impersonates Viṣṇu at Mathurā
description: a cast-off Brāhmaṇa lover, enriched from a jewel-island after riding a dead elephant's carcass, disguises as four-armed Viṣṇu on a Garuḍa to disgrace the greedy bawd and reclaim the courtesan Rūpiṇikā

title: Madanavega deceives Kaliṅgasenā and Madanamañcukā is born
description: the Vidyādhara Madanavega weds Kaliṅgasenā in Udayana's borrowed form after minister Yaugandharāyaṇa blocks the real match, fathering Madanamañcukā, future chief queen of Naravāhanadatta

title: Mahidasa Aitareya redacts the Aitareya Brahmana
description: The sage Mahidasa Aitareya, favoured by the Earth-goddess Mahi, is credited with redacting the Hotr's Rigvedic Brahmana

title: Mahānārāyaṇa = Taittirīya Āraṇyaka prapāṭhaka 10
description: The Mahānārāyaṇa (Yājñikī) Upaniṣad is identified as prapāṭhaka 10, the concluding theistic forest-layer of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda
source: Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10; Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad; Muktikā Upaniṣad

title: Mālava's gift to Puṇḍarīka at the Godāvarī
description: the Viṣṇu-devoted brāhmaṇa of Vidarbha, bathing at the Godāvarī with ten thousand palas of gold, gives half to his sister's son Puṇḍarīka as the "crest-jewel of worthy recipients," and Puṇḍarīka gives a fourth of it onward to learned brāhmaṇas

title: Malayadhvaja's putra-kāmeṣṭi
description: The childless Pāṇḍya king Malayadhvaja and queen Kāñcanamālai perform a son-desiring fire-sacrifice at Madurai

title: Mandodarī fixed in the Pañcakanyā verse
description: the sin-destroying remembrance verse *Ahalyā Draupadī Kuntī Tārā Mandodarī tathā…* enshrines her among the five ideal women [late text]

title: Mantroddhāra — coded extraction of mantras
description: The Tantric manuals encode mantras in coded epithets and prastāra syllable-grids so they must be decoded by an initiate rather than read plainly

title: Mārkaṇḍeya instructs King Vajra
description: at the dawn of Kali the deathless sage Mārkaṇḍeya answers the young king's plea with a total curriculum — cosmology, statecraft, the sciences, and the arts of divine image-making

title: Muktikā groups the ~20 Yoga Upaniṣads
description: The Muktikā Upaniṣad's 108-text canon contains a cluster of about twenty minor Śruti texts unified by yoga practice rather than pure Brahman-metaphysics
actors: Muktikā Upaniṣad; Upaniṣad-Brahma-Yogin; A. Mahadeva Sastri
source: Muktikā Up.; Mahadeva Sastri, The Yoga Upaniṣads (1920)

title: Naciketas Questions His Father's Gift
description: Watching his father give away useless cattle, the boy Naciketas asks three times to whom he himself will be given

title: Naciketas sent to the house of Death
description: Vājaśravasa angrily gives his son Naciketas to Yama; the boy waits three nights and is granted three boons

title: Nāma-saṅkīrtana declared the yuga-dharma of Kali
description: the intelligent worship the kṛṣṇa-varṇa yet non-black-lustered Lord with His associates by sacrifices consisting chiefly of congregational chanting, the Gauḍīya proof-text for Caitanya

title: Namuci slain and the panakam-offering origin
description: The asura Namuci, unslayable by dry or wet weapon, is destroyed by Vishnu/Indra through foam/stratagem, the 'neither dry nor wet' theme read into the liquid panakam rite

title: Narada chides Vyasa, Bhagavata composed
description: Despondent after compiling the Vedas and Mahabharata, Vyasa is told by Narada to glorify Hari directly, and so composes the Bhagavata Purana

title: Nārada finds Bhakti with her aged sons on the Yamunā
description: Touring a Kali-ridden earth, Nārada meets the young mother Bhakti beside her decrepit sons Jñāna and Vairāgya at Vṛndāvana, who recounts her Draviḍa-to-Gujarat journey

title: Nārada's petition and the vrata's revelation
description: grieved by earthly suffering, Nārada asks Viṣṇu for an easy remedy, and Nārāyaṇa prescribes the Satyanārāyaṇa vrata as the fit rite for the Kali age

title: Nārada–Pañcacūḍā saṃvāda
description: The sage Nārada encounters the apsarā Pañcacūḍā and interrogates her about the true inner nature and conduct of women; her unsparing reply on strī-svabhāva becomes a much-cited and contested gnomic discourse, later reported by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira from the bed of arrows

title: Onset of Kali Yuga
description: Kali Yuga begins at midnight 17/18 February 3102 BCE, the moment of Krishna's departure, when the bull of Dharma is reduced to standing on one leg
source: Surya Siddhanta; Vishnu Purana 5.38; Bhagavata Purana 1.15.36

title: Parāśara teaches Maitreya the exemption
description: asked how a man may be exempt from Yama, the sage Parāśara transmits to his pupil the layered Yama-Gītā he had from Bhīṣma through Nakula

title: Parīkṣit liberated at Takṣaka's bite
description: after Śuka's final teaching that the self cannot be burned, Parīkṣit fixes his mind on Kṛṣṇa and attains liberation at the instant of the serpent's strike

title: Pratardana storms Indra's abode
description: Pratardana, son of Divodāsa of Kāśī, reaches Indra's world by fighting and virility and receives the teaching that Indra is prāṇa, the conscious self

title: Puṇḍalīka's brick halts the Lord
description: the devoted son, unwilling to interrupt service to his parents, tosses a brick for the visiting Lord to wait on, and Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa remains standing on it as Viṭṭhala of Pandharpur for the whole Kali Yuga

title: Puṇḍarīka's sāyujya at Puṣkara
description: on the Māgha full moon Viṣṇu promises absorption, carries the devotee back to Puṣkara on Garuḍa, and a flash with Puṇḍarīka's vital breath leaves his body and merges into Viṣṇu's own form

title: Rain of golden lotuses and the founding of Madurai
description: Nectar drips from Śiva's locks over the new city, naming it Madhurā/Maturai; Madurai laid out as a lotus around the svayambhū liṅga

title: Rājadharma taught for the new age
description: Mārkaṇḍeya lays out for Vajra the duties of a sovereign — law and punishment, judicial procedure, army and diplomacy, expiation and gift — the governance of the remnant Yādava world as Kali opens

title: Redaction of the Kauṣītaki (Śāṅkhāyana) Brāhmaṇa
description: The second Brāhmaṇa of the Ṛgveda is preserved and arranged by the Kauṣītaki/Śāṅkhāyana school as a 30-adhyāya prose manual of the Hotṛ's ritual
actors: Kauṣītaki / Kuṣītaka teacher-line; Śāṅkhāyana school; Hotṛ priesthood

title: Sādhu's deferred vow and imprisonment at Ratnasārapura
description: the merchant Sādhu vows the vrata for a child, twice defers it, and is framed for the theft of King Candraketu's treasure until Līlāvatī's vrata prompts the king's dream and his release with doubled wealth

title: Sahadeva and Nakula fall on the final journey
description: On the mahāprasthāna Sahadeva falls second for thinking none his equal in wisdom and Nakula third for believing none equalled him in beauty, Yudhiṣṭhira naming each flaw without looking back

title: Śani puts Vikramāditya through the sāḍe-sātī
description: slighted in the Ujjain court, Saturn strands the king maimed and nameless at an oil-press for 7½ years, then restores him and grants that Saturday worshippers who hear the Māhātmya pass his transits lightly

title: Sannyāsa listed among the kalivarjyas
description: medieval smṛti digests declare the acceptance of sannyāsa forbidden in the Kali Yuga, a ruling the living monastic orders reject [disputed] [late text]
source: kalivarjya lists, per Kane, History of Dharmaśāstra II

title: Śiva becomes the mother (Thāyumānavar)
description: with the Kāverī in flood stranding her real mother on the far bank, the devotee Ratnāvatī goes into labour, and Śiva of the Rock Fort takes the exact form of her absent mother to comfort and midwife the childbirth

title: Six seekers approach Pippalāda
description: Six Brahman-devoted seekers come fuel-in-hand to sage Pippalāda, who bids them dwell a year in austerity and faith before questioning

title: Śṛṅgi's seven-day curse on Parīkṣit
description: the death-countdown by Takṣaka's bite creates the frame-audience for the Bhāgavata Purāṇa's recitation

title: Story of Uttanka and the snake-sacrifice trigger
description: Uttanka's quest for his guru's wife's earrings and duel with Takshaka leads him to urge Janamejaya to the snake-sacrifice, the hinge that triggers the epic's recitation

title: Śuka cites Khaṭvāṅga to the doomed Parīkṣit
description: instructing the king who has seven days to live, Śuka names Khaṭvāṅga — freed with only a muhūrta left — as the charter of taking shelter of Vāsudeva at the last hour

title: Sundarar Claimed as Bondsman at Tiruvennainallur
description: At Tiruvennainallur, Shiva claims the saint Sundarar as his bondsman (the tozhan episode), beginning Sundarar's career

title: Taṇḍula-kusuma-balivikāra named in the 64 Kalās
description: Vātsyāyana lists rice-and-flower offering-designs as the 7th of the sixty-four classical arts, the textual anchor of the floor-art tradition

title: The curse ripens in the Kali age
description: the cursed brāhmaṇas are sentenced to Kumbhīpāka hell until Kṛṣṇa's incarnation, then reborn in the Kali age devoid of the three sandhyās and of Gāyatrī-devotion — the Devī-Bhāgavata's charter for why brāhmaṇas neglect the Goddess

title: The cursed cirañjīvi wanders Kali Yuga
description: First-named of the eight immortals and the only one whose deathlessness is a punishment, Aśvatthāman is held by folk tradition to roam still, offering a daily flower to Śiva at Asirgarh fort and seeking oil for his unhealing wound [folk]

title: The Draviḍa-rivers devotee prophecy
description: great devotees of Vāsudeva will abound in Kali along the Tāmraparṇī, Kṛtamālā, Payasvinī, Kāverī and Mahānadī, read by Śrīvaiṣṇavas as foretelling the Āḻvārs

title: The elopement from Ujjayinī
description: contrived by minister Yaugandharāyaṇa, Udayana and Vāsavadattā flee on the swift she-elephant Bhadravatī to Kauśāmbī, while her father Caṇḍamahāsena secretly consents to the match he had engineered

title: The first Bhāgavata saptāha at Haridvāra revives Bhakti's sons
description: The Four Kumāras conduct the seven-day Bhāgavata recitation at Ānanda-ghāṭ on the Gaṅgā, Bhakti and her sons appear rejuvenated, and Bhakti is installed in the hearts of devotees

title: The goddess's boycott strips the temple
description: departing, Lakṣmī vows the brothers will find neither food nor water, and all wealth and abundance leave the Śrīmandira with her

title: The Great Puzzle silences the king
description: The kinship-tangle of the father and son who married a daughter and her mother defeats even Trivikramasena, and the satisfied vetāla reveals Kṣāntiśīla's plot to sacrifice him

title: The Jagannātha Triad and Sudarśana Pillar
description: Purī's sanctum holds the abstract wooden busts of Jagannātha (Kṛṣṇa), Balabhadra, Subhadrā and the Sudarśana post — deliberately armless and unfinished

title: The liberation of Devarāja
description: dying of fever at Pratiṣṭhāna, Devarāja involuntarily overhears a Śiva-discourse; Yama's messengers seize him but four ash-smeared trident-bearing gaṇas drive them off and bear him to Kailāsa, instantly liberated

title: The lie to the sannyāsī and Kalāvatī's abandoned prasāda
description: Sādhu calls his cargo "leaves and creepers" before the disguised god and finds it so, and Kalāvatī's uneaten prasāda sinks her husband's boat until she returns and eats it

title: The lute behind the curtain
description: set to teach Vāsavadattā the vīṇā while each is told the other is deformed, Udayana and the princess break the screen, behold each other, and fall in love

title: The poor brahmin of Kāśī and the woodcutter
description: Satyanārāyaṇa in disguise teaches the vrata to a starving brahmin, and a woodcutter who copies it sells his load at double price; both rise to wealth

title: The revelation and reunion
description: his purpose secured, Yaugandharāyaṇa discloses the ruse and produces Vāsavadattā alive, restored as senior queen with Padmāvatī her junior co-wife

title: The sannyāsī's fruit and Dhundhulī's fraud
description: Childless Ātmadeva receives a son-granting fruit, but his wife Dhundhulī feeds it to the cow and passes off her sister's newborn as her own son Dhundhukārī

title: The seven knots burst and Dhundhukārī is liberated
description: Listening from inside a seven-knotted bamboo as Gokarṇa reads the Bhāgavata seven days, the preta bursts one knot per day and emerges in divine form, borne to Vaikuṇṭha by the Lord's attendants

title: The seven-day Bhāgavata recitation
description: the sixteen-year-old Śuka arrives unbidden at Parīkṣit's fast unto death on the Gaṅgā and recites the entire Bhāgavata over the king's last seven days

title: The Śīkṣā-vallī convocation charge
description: A teacher dismisses the graduating student with the famous injunctions to speak truth, practise dharma, neglect not study, and revere mother, father, teacher and guest as gods
actors: the ācārya (teacher) and the graduating Vedic student (snātaka); the four 'gods': mother

title: The Opening Question (Keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ)
description: A disciple asks by whose will the mind, breath, speech, eye and ear go forth to their objects

title: The Sannyāsa Upaniṣad group within the Muktikā canon
description: A thematic cluster of ~17–19 minor Upaniṣads, grouped by the subject of renunciation rather than parent Veda, forms the Śruti charter of Hindu monasticism

title: The Self Alone in the Beginning
description: The Ātman alone exists before creation and resolves to bring forth the worlds

title: The Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya frame
description: Sūta expounds to Śaunaka at Naimiṣāraṇya the seven-chapter Glory of the Śiva Purāṇa, three phala-śruti tales proving that merely hearing the Purāṇa liberates the vilest Kali-age sinner

title: The Śrāvaṇa saptāha takes the whole town to Goloka
description: Gokarṇa repeats the seven-day reading with disciplined listeners, the Lord himself appears and embraces him, and the entire assembly ascends in divine form to Goloka

title: The starving brothers eat in the outcaste's house
description: begging in vain through Purī, Jagannātha and Balabhadra finally eat rice cooked by Lakṣmī herself in a caṇḍāluṇī's home, the very act for which she was expelled

title: The tale told to Janamejaya
description: within the Devī Bhāgavata's Book III celebration of the Devī-yajña and Navarātra, the Satyavrata story is narrated to King Janamejaya as an exhortation to worship the Goddess

title: The treacherous mendicant beheaded
description: Asked to prostrate before the corpse, the king makes Kṣāntiśīla demonstrate and beheads him; the vetāla grants the tales world-fame and apotropaic power, and Śiva bestows the sword Aparājita and future Vidyādhara emperorship

title: The twelve-year sattra of Śaunaka at Naimiṣa
description: 88,000 ṛṣis led by Kulapati Śaunaka assemble in Naimiṣa forest for a perpetual sacrificial session, hearing the old stories during ritual intervals
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 1.1; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4; Vāyu Purāṇa 1.11–12

title: The twins seated among the Aśvins in heaven
description: Touring heaven in the epic's last book, Yudhiṣṭhira beholds Nakula and Sahadeva shining in the station of the Aśvins, their divine fathers

title: The Two Paths After Death (devayāna/pitṛyāna)
description: Citra Gāṅgyāyani questions Uddālaka/Śvetaketu; the dead pass to the moon, which sorts souls to the upward path of the gods or rebirth as rain

title: The vanishing and the naming
description: when the flood subsides and the true mother arrives, the Śiva-form disappears, and the Lord is thereafter called Thāyumānavar / Mātṛbhūtēśvara, 'he who became even the mother'

title: The vetāla's twenty-four riddle-tales
description: Carrying the corpse from the śiṃśapā tree in silence, the king answers dilemma after dilemma (transposed heads, three suitors, Unmādinī, Vīravara) and each answer sends the corpse flying back

title: Udayana's grief and the Padmāvatī marriage
description: believing his queen dead, the inconsolable Udayana is counselled to wed Padmāvatī of Magadha, sealing the alliance and army with which he recovers Vatsa

title: Upakośā and the chest of blackened dignitaries
description: the faithful wife of Vararuci lures four would-be seducers into a dark chest, has them smeared with lamp-black, and exposes them at the Nanda king's court to recover her husband's deposit

title: Vaṭapatraśāyī enshrined as a Divya Desam
description: Viṣṇu reclines as Vaṭapatraśāyī on a banyan leaf at Srivilliputhur, counted among the 108 Divya Desams hymned in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham
source: Sthala-purāṇa of Srivilliputhur; Nālāyira Divya Prabandham

title: Āśvalāyana petitions Brahmā for brahma-vidyā
description: The sage Āśvalāyana approaches Brahmā the Grandsire asking to be taught the highest secret knowledge of Brahman by which the wise cast off evil and attain the supreme Puruṣa

title: Vedas and Gītā fail; the ākāśavāṇī prescribes a sat-karma
description: Nārada's recitation of Vedas, Vedānta and Gītā cannot rouse Jñāna and Vairāgya, and a bodiless voice announces that only a specific good work will revive them

title: Vikrama gives away the philosopher's stone
description: granted the pāras-maṇi that turns iron to gold, Vikramāditya hands it at once to a poor Brahmin, the recurring pattern by which he acquires only to give

title: Vikramāditya offers his own head to the Goddess
description: to fulfil another man's vow of a perfect human sacrifice, Vikrama lays his own head on Devī's altar and is restored to life by the awestruck Goddess, the cycle's chief proof of his fearless self-sacrifice

title: Vikramāditya vs. Śālivāhana and the two eras
description: the child Śālivāhana of Pratiṣṭhāna, son of the nāga Śeṣa, animates a clay army to repel Vikrama's invasion, the folk etiology of the Vikrama Saṃvat (57 BCE) and Śālivāhana Śaka (78 CE) reckonings

title: Vipula guards Ruci from Indra by yoga
description: The sage Devaśarman, leaving on a sacrifice and knowing Indra covets his beautiful wife Ruci, charges his disciple Vipula to guard her chastity. Vipula enters Ruci's body by yoga, binding her senses from within so she cannot respond to a seducer; when Indra arrives in disguise he finds her warded and Vipula's tapas blazing, and departs foiled. Vipula withdraws, restores Ruci unaware, and reports his success to his returning guru. A didactic inset on guarding a teacher's trust, the burdens of a guru-kārya, and yogic self-mastery, with contested ethics read variously as pious devotion or as coercive violation of Ruci's consent

title: Viṣṇu dwells a month in Puṇḍarīka's house
description: answering Puṇḍarīka's bath-wish at Puṣkara, Viṣṇu in his original form resides in the devotee's adorned home for the whole month of Māgha, worshipped with tulasī, flowers and incense while two hundred brāhmaṇas are fed

title: Viṣṇu's Kali-yuga refuge promise on Veṅkaṭa hill
description: At the dawn of Kali-yuga Viṣṇu agrees to remain standing and visible on the Seven Hills so the merit-poor may win liberation by darśana alone, making Tirumala Bhū-Vaikuṇṭha

title: Vājaśravasa's flawed Viśvajit sacrifice
description: The father Vājaśravasa gives away only old, barren cows in the all-giving Viśvajit sacrifice, a defective dāna noticed by his son
source: Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.1–3; cf. Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.11.8

title: Īśāvāsyam idaṃ sarvam — all is pervaded by the Lord
description: The opening mantra declares the whole moving universe pervaded by the Lord (Īśa), to be enjoyed by renunciation and non-coveting

title: Viṣṇudāsa cooks his own flesh
description: the poor Vaiṣṇava, bound by a Kārtika vow of hospitality and with no food, cuts and cooks flesh from his own body to honour an arriving guest

title: Vyāsa composes the Purāṇas, recited by the Sūta at Naimiṣa
description: All 18 Mahāpurāṇas and 18 Upapurāṇas are ascribed to Vyāsa and recited by the sūta Ugraśravas/Romaharṣaṇa to the sages at the Naimiṣa forest in this Kali Yuga

title: Vyāsa on the ego of the enlightened
description: answering Janamejaya's paradox of why sages fought for a thousand years, Vyāsa teaches that even liberated beings retain ahaṃkāra, bridging to the tale of Bhṛgu's curse on Viṣṇu

title: Vyāsa teaches Jaimini the kriyā-yoga for Kali-yuga
description: asked how beings of the degenerate age can reach Viṣṇu, Vyāsa prescribes devotional action (pūjā, Gaṅgā-snāna, Ekādaśī, tulasī) illustrated by the Manobhadra, Mādhava–Sulocanā, Kālakalpa, Indra–Padmagandhā, Cakrikā and Bhadratanu tales

title: Yaugandharāyaṇa's fire-ruse at Lāvāṇaka
description: to force the Magadha alliance, the minister stages a fire and reports Vāsavadattā and himself burned, secretly hiding the disguised queen under rival princess Padmāvatī's own protection

title: Yoga Narasiṃha cooled on Ghaṭikācala
description: After slaying Hiraṇyakaśipu the fierce Narasiṃha withdraws to the Periya-malai and settles into yoga-mudrā as the pacified Yoga Narasiṃha

title: Yudhiṣṭhira finds Duryodhana enthroned in heaven
description: Carried to Svarga, Yudhiṣṭhira sees his arch-enemy Duryodhana enthroned in glory; he recoils, but Nārada explains that earthly hatred ceases in heaven and Duryodhana earned the seat by dying bravely on the field of Kurukṣetra

title: Aṅgiras's son-boon
description: Sage Aṅgiras performs a Tvaṣṭṛ sacrifice for the king, warning the son will bring both joy and grief

title: Bhāskararāya's uddhāra of the Śrīvidyā pañcadaśākṣarī
description: Bhāskararāya's Varivasyā-rahasya decodes the fifteen-syllable Lalitā-Tripurasundarī mantra from its coded designations, differing by Kādi and Hādi schools

title: Birth of Taḍātakai (Mīnākṣī) from the fire
description: A three-breasted, fish-eyed girl rises fully formed from the yajña fire, born to rule, named Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī

title: Birth of Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī from the sacrificial fire
description: A three-breasted girl, the future Mīnākṣī, rises from the Pāṇḍya fire-altar, born crowned to rule, with a prophecy of her third breast vanishing at meeting her lord

title: Birth of Viṣṇucitta (Periyāḻvār) and his garland service
description: The brahmin Viṣṇucitta is born at Srivilliputhur and weaves daily garlands from his tulasī garden for Vaṭapatraśāyī

title: Brahman as the Ear of the Ear
description: The teacher answers that Brahman is the mind of the mind, speech of speech, eye of the eye and breath of breath — the unseen ground of all faculties

title: Brahmā teaches the path of renunciation
description: Brahmā answers that immortality is won not by works, progeny or wealth but by renunciation (tyāga) joined with faith, devotion and meditation, practised by forest ascetics
source: Kaivalya Upaniṣad 2-3 (renunciation half-verse shared with Mahānārāyaṇa Up.)

title: Definition of Brahman as Satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ Brahma
description: The Brahmānanda-vallī declares Brahman to be the Real, Knowledge and the Infinite, set in the cave of the heart, and unfolds the elements from the Self

title: Demons made invincible by Vedic dharma
description: The daityas defeat the devas because their rigorous Vedic observance and tapas make them unconquerable; the gods appeal to Vishnu

title: Dharma Bull Stands on One Leg
description: With Kali's onset only one quarter of virtue remains; Earth and Dharma lament as cow and bull

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī depart for the forest
description: Grief-worn, the blind king and Gāndhārī take leave to retire as vānaprasthas; to the Pāṇḍavas' shock Kuntī chooses to accompany them, and the elders cast off royal robes for bark and deerskin at Vyāsa's hermitage on the Gaṅgā

title: End of the Barhadratha line
description: The last Barhadratha king Puranjaya (Ripunjaya) is assassinated by his minister Shunaka, who enthrones his own son, beginning the prophesied Kali dynasties of Magadha

title: Establishment of the tāla-schemes ranking deities by height
description: The aṣṭa-, nava- and daśa-tāla schemes assign taller, more elongated proportions to higher deities and squatter ones to lesser/fierce beings
source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā 58; Viṣṇudharmottara Citrasūtra; Mānasāra 65; Śukranīti 4

title: Exposition of the haviryajña fire-rites
description: Chapters 1–6 lay out the Agnyādheya, Agnihotra, Darśapūrṇamāsa, Cāturmāsya and Agrayaṇa offerings in a single systematic sequence

title: Indradyumna founds the Jagannath deities
description: King Indradyumna, instructed in a dream, recovers Krishna's imperishable remains (a sacred daru log washed ashore) and has Vishvakarma carve the three stub-armed deities from neem wood, the carving left unfinished

title: Kṛṣṇa revives Parīkṣit in the womb
description: Born stillborn and scorched, the infant is revived by Kṛṣṇa entering the womb, the Bhāgavata's proof-text of Kṛṣṇa as protector of the embryo
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.8.13–33; Mahābhārata Āśvamedhika Parva

title: King Indradyumna's Quest for Nīla Mādhava
description: The pious king Indradyumna seeks the hidden forest form of Viṣṇu, Nīla Mādhava, and sends Brahmins to find it

title: Kurvann eveha karmāṇi — action-renunciation synthesis
description: The text endorses doing works while wishing to live a hundred years, holding that disinterested action does not bind

title: Lakṣmī departs Vaikuṇṭha
description: Śrī-Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha after estrangement from Viṣṇu and descends to dwell at Karavīra

title: Naciketas Consigned to Death
description: Provoked, the father angrily declares 'To Death I give you,' and the boy must go to Yama's house

title: Naciketas demands the secret of death from Yama
description: Rejecting all worldly bribes, Naciketas holds firm to his third boon and Yama teaches him the deathless Self, śreyas/preyas, OM and yoga

title: Naciketas given to Death
description: Naciketas thrice asks 'to whom will you give me?'; the angry father vows 'Unto Death (Yama) I give you,' and the boy goes willingly to Yama's abode

title: Parikshit Cursed by Shringi
description: Abhimanyu's son Parikshit, last of the Kuru line, garlands a meditating sage with a dead snake and the sage's son curses him to die of Takshaka's bite in seven days, occasioning the Bhagavata's recitation

title: Prahlāda and the Man-Lion descent localized at the hill
description: The māhātmya draws the Prahlāda–Hiraṇyakaśipu cycle and the Narasiṃha descent onto the auspicious hill as the seat of the Lord's grace

title: Praśna 1 — origin of creatures from rayi and prāṇa
description: Pippalāda teaches Kabandhī that Prajāpati produced the pair rayi (matter/moon) and prāṇa (life/sun), from whose union all creatures arise

title: Projection of the Four Worlds
description: The Self emits the four worlds ambhas, marīci, mara, and āpas

title: Revelation of the Gopāla (eighteen-syllable) mantra
description: The Pūrva-tāpanī expounds the eighteen-syllable Gopāla-mantra syllable by syllable as the supreme means of realizing Kṛṣṇa

title: Revelation of the Narasiṃha-Sāvitrī and Yajus with nyāsa
description: The Pūrva-tāpanī supplies the Narasiṃha gāyatrī/Sāvitrī, the Yajus formula, and the six aṅga-mantras for installing the Mantrarāja's syllables on the body

title: Self-manifestation of the Kūrma tortoise-icon at Śrīkūrmam
description: The sage/king Śveta performs tapas and Vishnu reveals himself as the svayam-vyakta tortoise-stone on the Bay of Bengal shore, with the icon later lost and refound

title: Shiva Grants Sundarar the Padikasu at Tiruvarur
description: Shiva grants Sundarar a daily gold coin (padikasu) at the Tiruvarur Thyagaraja temple, dramatizing his intimate friend-of-Shiva status

title: Suta recites Bhagavata at Naimisa
description: The bard Ugrasrava (Suta Gosvami) recites the entire Bhagavata to the sages of the Naimisa forest during Kali Yuga, opening the outer frame

title: The 28 Yogeshvaras incarnate to teach Pashupata-yoga
description: Shiva incarnates once in every Kali Yuga across the 28 mahayugas of the present manvantara as the 28 Yogeshvaras, each with four disciples, transmitting the yoga of liberation

title: The ghaṭikā boon of mental clarity
description: Worship on the hill bears fruit within one ghaṭikā (~24 min), granting clarity of intellect and relief from mental affliction — naming the hill Ghaṭikācala / Tirukkaḍigai
source: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, Ghaṭikācala-māhātmya; Śrī Vaiṣṇava tradition

title: The Lament on Transience
description: Bṛhadratha pours out a vanitas lament: the body is a foul frame and even great kings, seas, mountains and gods perish

title: The Paryaṅka-vidyā — ascent to Brahmaloka and dialogue at the throne
description: The liberated soul travels the devayāna up through cosmic worlds, crosses the river Vijarā and reaches Brahmā's couch Amitaujas, where Brahmā asks 'Who are you?' and the soul answers with self-identification as Brahman

title: The saṃnyāsa renunciation rite (praiṣa)
description: The candidate performs his own symbolic funeral, recites the praiṣa formula freeing all beings of fear of him, and discards sacred fire, thread, and tuft
source: Jābāla Up.; Āruṇi Up.; Sannyāsa group

title: The two knowledges: parā vs. aparā vidyā
description: Aṅgiras teaches that two knowledges exist — the lower (aparā: the four Vedas and Vedāṅgas) and the higher (parā) by which the imperishable Brahman is known

title: Tirumūlar enters the cowherd's corpse
description: The Kailāsa-yogī Sundaranātha animates the dead cowherd Mūlan's body to tend cattle, cannot return, and becomes the Siddhar Tirumūlar

title: Two recensions (Āndhra/Drāviḍa vs Atharvan)
description: The Upaniṣad survives in a longer South-Indian Āndhra recension (~64 anuvākas) and a shorter Northern/Atharvan recension, causing anuvāka numbering to vary by edition

title: Ugraśravas Sauti recites the epic at Naimiṣa Forest
description: The bard Ugraśravas arrives at the Naimiṣa Forest where ṛṣis led by Śaunaka perform a 12-year sacrifice and recites the whole Mahābhārata as he heard it at Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice (the outer frame narrative)

title: Ugraśravas Sūta recites the Mahābhārata and Purāṇas
