description: The bard Ugraśravas (son of Romaharṣaṇa), Vyāsa's disciple, narrates the Mahābhārata and the eighteen Purāṇas to Śaunaka's sages — the outermost narrative frame of the corpus
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 1.1–1.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.1; Vāyu Purāṇa 1.16

title: Vajra crowned at Indraprastha
description: Yudhiṣṭhira enthrones Vajra, the surviving Yādava prince and great-grandson of Kṛṣṇa, over Indraprastha and the Śūrasena lands, preserving the Yādava line after the Mausala fratricide

title: Varāha's prior ownership of the hill
description: Varāha already owns Veṅkaṭa hill from a prior age; Śrīnivāsa must ask his leave to settle and ordains Varāha's darśana be taken first

title: Viṣṇu-Daityasūdana slays the asura
description: Viṣṇu descends as Daityasūdana and slays the asura, burying him in the crater basin

title: Yogatattva names the four yogas
description: The Yogatattva Upaniṣad gives the earliest neat Śruti statement of mantra-, laya-, haṭha- and rāja-yoga, the eight aṅgas, āsanas, prāṇāyāma and the siddhis in a Viṣṇu/Hiraṇyagarbha frame

title: Yudhiṣṭhira descends into hell and chooses to remain
description: Led down a foul path through the iron-thorned hells (Asipatravana, Vaitaraṇī), Yudhiṣṭhira hears the agonized voices of his brothers, Karṇa and Draupadī and, declaring his presence eases their suffering, resolves to stay in hell with them rather than enjoy heaven with their tormentors

title: Astika halts the snake-sacrifice
description: Janamejaya's serpent-sacrifice burns thousands of Nagas until the boy-brahmin Astika wins a boon and halts the rite, the frame at which the epic is recited

title: Birth of Mayamoha the deluder
description: Vishnu emits Mayamoha, a mendicant deluder, and sends him to the asuras on the Narmada banks

title: Birth of Sambandar at Sirkazhi
description: The child-prodigy saint Sambandar, largest contributor of pathigams to the Tevaram canon, is born at Sirkazhi (Brahmapureeswarar)

title: Birth of the prince
description: Kṛtadyuti bears a son; the king's possessive love provokes the co-wives' jealousy

title: Boon and Request for Ātma-vidyā
description: The sage Śākāyanya, pleased by the austerities, grants a boon; the king asks for knowledge of the Self rather than the body

title: Brahmā's penance on the hill
description: Brahmā performs tapas on the hill and gains darśana of the yogic Narasiṃha, marking the kṣetra as divinely revealed

title: Chanakya uproots the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta
description: A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) uproots the Nanda dynasty and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty in the Puranic king-prophecy

title: Dhyāna on Śiva in the heart-lotus
description: The seeker is instructed to meditate in a pure secret place on the Lord (Īśa) of the nature of Oṃ within the heart-lotus, contemplating the three-eyed, blue-throated, tranquil Śiva

title: Doctrine of the five sheaths (pañca-kośa)
description: Man is described as enveloped in five nested sheaths — food, breath, mind, intellect and bliss — each inner and other than the last, leading to the bliss-Self
actors: the Upaniṣadic teacher; the embodied self

title: Drawing Forth of the Cosmic Puruṣa
description: The Self draws a cosmic Person from the waters and shapes him as the matrix of the organs

title: Exposition of the Soma sacrifices
description: Chapters 7–30 expound the Agniṣṭoma/jyotiṣṭoma Soma rites, multi-day ahīna and sattra sessions, the Gavām-ayana and Mahāvrata, and the Hotṛ's śastras

title: Formulation of the āyādi ṣaḍvarga calculations
description: Six divinatory formulae (āya, vyaya, yoni, ṛkṣa, vāra, tithi) test an icon's or temple's dimensions for auspicious remainders before construction
actors: śilpa architects; Mānasāra and Mayamata compilers

title: Lakulisha as the 28th avatara founds the Pashupata sect
description: Shiva descends at Kayavarohana as the wandering ascetic Lakulisha, the 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples Kushika, Garga, Mitra, and Kaurushya who spread the Pashupata cult

title: Markandeya's Kali Prophecy
description: Sage Markandeya foretells the apocalyptic decline of Kali: mleccha kings, 16-year lifespans, cannibalism, barren earth

title: Meditation on the Vṛndāvana maṇḍala
description: Meditation locates Kṛṣṇa at the centre of a lotus/maṇḍala in Vṛndāvana-Goloka, surrounded by gopas, gopīs, cows and wish-trees, beyond the material worlds

title: Naciketas Waits Three Nights in Yama's House
description: Yama being absent, Naciketas waits three nights unfed; to atone for the un-hosted guest Yama grants three boons

title: Naming and birth-omens
description: The child is named Parīkṣit (and Viṣṇurāta) and astrologers foretell a pious Ikṣvāku-like Aśvamedha-king devoted to Kṛṣṇa

title: Panguni Uthiram divine marriages
description: On the Uttara-phalguni (Uthiram) full moon of Tamil Panguni, a cluster of celestial weddings is solemnized across South Indian temples on a single day — Shiva-Meenakshi/Parvati, Murugan-Deivanai, Rama-Sita, and Andal-Ranganatha — the nakshatra of marital union (ruled by Bhaga/Aryaman); also a great kavadi day at the Murugan abodes

title: Pānakāla Narasiṃha drinks only panakam (half left)
description: The open-mouthed hilltop Narasiṃha accepts only jaggery-water poured in, gurgles as he drinks, and mysteriously leaves about half uncons­umed however much is offered
source: Maṅgalagiri sthala-māhātmya; Wikipedia (Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple)

title: Praśna 2 — supremacy of prāṇa
description: Answering Bhārgava, Pippalāda shows via the bee-king parable that prāṇa is chief among the body's powers, sustaining all the faculties

title: Prāṇa-upāsanās and the father-to-son transmission rite
description: Meditations worshipping prāṇa as Brahman, the inter-sensory internal offering, and the dying father's sampradāna handing of his powers to his son

title: Prophecy of the vanishing third breast
description: A divine voice foretells the supernumerary breast will disappear when she meets her destined consort, making it a recognition device

title: Self-manifestation of the Mūla-virāṭ mūrti
description: The standing four-armed Veṅkaṭeśvara image arises svayam-vyakta, not carved by human hands, with Śrī resting on his chest; later fixed as Viṣṇu by Rāmānuja

title: Shrinivasa Weds Padmavati at Tirumala
description: Vishnu as Shrinivasa dwells in a termite-mound on Venkata hill, meets Padmavati (reborn Lakshmi) while hunting, and weds her, founding the Tirumala-Tirupati cult

title: Spark-from-fire creation simile
description: As thousands of sparks of like form leap from a blazing fire, so manifold beings arise from and return into the Imperishable Brahman

title: Sudarśana-cakra association and protective kavaca
description: The Pūrva links the Mantrarāja to the Sudarśana-cakra and a protective maṇḍala/yantra, founding the apotropaic Sudarśana-Narasiṃha worship

title: That Which the Mind Cannot Think
description: The text declares Brahman to be that which the mind cannot think but by which the mind thinks, unknown to those who know and known to those who do not

title: The asura's being becomes the saline water
description: The blood/dissolved being of the slain asura becomes the lake's saline (lavaṇa) water, explaining the brine and the name Lonār

title: The Bhāgavata's opening question on the dawning Kali Yuga
description: Troubled by the onset of Kali Yuga, the Naimiṣa sages ask Sūta for the essence of all scriptures; he answers with the Bhāgavata he heard from Śuka

title: The Bhṛgu-kick trigger (separated-couple variant)
description: Sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest, the offended Lakṣmī quits Vaikuṇṭha and settles at Kolhapur while Viṣṇu settles at Tirupati, reading the two shrines as the separated divine couple

title: The four (and six) grades of renouncer
description: Ascetics are graded as kuṭīcaka, bahūdaka, haṃsa, and paramahaṃsa, with later texts adding turīyātīta and avadhūta above
source: Bhikṣuka Up.; Nāradaparivrājaka Up.; Turīyātītāvadhūta Up.

title: The hell dissolves as māyā; the final test passed
description: At Yudhiṣṭhira's choice Indra, Yama and the gods appear and the hell instantly vanishes as illusion; Dharma reveals this was the third and last trial, explains that all must briefly taste hell to exhaust residual karma (his caused by the half-lie about Aśvatthāmā), and Yudhiṣṭhira bathes in the celestial Ganges to shed his human body

title: The joyless asura-worlds and the slayers of the Self
description: Those who slay the Self go after death to sunless worlds wrapped in blind darkness

title: The Madurai debate and the Tiruppallāṇḍu
description: Viṣṇucitta wins the Pāṇḍya court debate on Viṣṇu's supremacy and sings the Tiruppallāṇḍu, earning the title Periyāḻvār

title: The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī begin the mahāprasthāna
description: After final rites and distribution of wealth, the five brothers and Draupadī cast off royalty for ascetic garb and set out walking north toward death with no intention of return, a faithful dog attaching itself to the company

title: The six-limbed viniyoga (anatomy of a mantra)
description: Every mantra is specified by ṛṣi, chandas, devatā, bīja, śakti and kīlaka, each touched to a body-point before recitation as a prerequisite for efficacy

title: Three nights unhosted at Yama's house
description: Naciketas waits three nights without food or welcome while Yama is absent, an unhonoured Brahmin guest who 'burns up' the host's merit

title: Uttaṅka incites Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice
description: Uttaṅka's grudge against Takṣaka goads King Janamejaya into the sarpa-satra, the frame at which the Mahābhārata is first recited

title: Vaiśampāyana narrates the epic at Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice
description: At King Janamejaya's Sarpa Satra, held to avenge his father Parīkṣit's death by the serpent Takṣaka, Vyāsa's pupil Vaiśampāyana narrates the Mahābhārata at Vyāsa's bidding (the middle frame narrative)

title: Vidura merges into Yudhiṣṭhira and dies
description: Found wasted by tapas, Vidura by yogic power casts his life-breaths and being into Yudhiṣṭhira's body and drops dead, the two merged because both are portions of Dharma; Vyāsa forbids cremating his body and explains the Aṇī-Māṇḍavya curse that made Dharma born as Vidura

title: Vidyāpati, Viśvāvasu and the Mustard-Seed Trail
description: The Brahmin Vidyāpati finds Nīla Mādhava worshipped by the Śabara chief Viśvāvasu, marries his daughter Lalitā, and traces the secret path with mustard seeds

title: World-conquest and the Tirukalyāṇam (divine wedding)
description: Mīnākṣī's dig-vijaya reaches Kailāsa, her third breast vanishes at sight of Śiva, who weds her at Madurai as Sundareśvara with Viṣṇu giving her away

title: Yogaśikhā: Śiva teaches integrated haṭha-rāja yoga
description: The longest Yoga Upaniṣad has Śiva expound the union of prāṇa and mind, the nāḍīs, chakras and kuṇḍalinī, integrating haṭha and rāja yoga toward the jīvan-mukta

title: Appar Reconverts from Jainism to Shaivism
description: Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), formerly the Jain Dharmasena, reconverts to Shaivism and composes Tirumurai 4–6, famed for his hoe-service temple cleaning

title: Arjuna surrenders the Gāṇḍīva to Agni
description: At the red-watered sea Agni appears blocking the path and demands Arjuna return the celestial bow Gāṇḍīva and quivers to Varuṇa; Arjuna casts them into the waters, formally ending the kṣatriya phase of their lives

title: Bhṛgu's kick and Lakṣmī's departure from Vaikuṇṭha
description: Sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest in a test; affronted that her seat was struck, Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha and descends to earth

title: Brahmā receives and transmits the Gopāla knowledge
description: Brahmā receives the highest secret of the Gopāla-mantra and transmits it down through a divine paramparā

title: Coronation as reigning Pāṇḍya queen
description: On Malayadhvaja's death Taḍātakai is crowned queen regnant of Madurai, ruling and bearing the sword in her own name

title: Critique of sacrifice — the leaky boats
description: The fire-sacrifices are declared unsteady boats (plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajña-rūpāḥ); those who hail them as highest return to old age and death, like the blind led by the blind

title: Divergence from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa
description: As the Bāṣkala/Kauṣītaki śākhā's manual it preserves an independent, more unified Hotṛ tradition, omitting the Aitareya's Rājasūya block and Śunaḥśepa legend
source: Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa vs. Aitareya Brāhmaṇa; Keith HOS 25

title: Emergence of Organs and Presiding Deities
description: From the brooded-over Puruṣa break forth the organs, their faculties, and the cosmic deities (Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, the Quarters, herbs, Moon, Death, Waters)

title: Establishment of the Daityasūdana temple cult
description: Viṣṇu under the epithet Daityasūdana is enshrined beside the crater, commemorating the slaying and anchoring the māhātmya to a living shrine

title: First Boon — A Reconciled Father
description: Naciketas asks that his father be freed of anger and welcome him gladly on his return, and Yama grants it

title: Āṇḍāḷ found in the tulasī garden
description: Periyāḻvār discovers the infant Gōdai beneath a tulasī plant and raises her as Āṇḍāḷ, held to be an avatāra of Bhū-devī

title: Installation on the Hāstinapura throne
description: On the Pāṇḍavas' mahāprasthāna, Yudhiṣṭhira installs the boy Parīkṣit as emperor at Hāstinapura
source: Mahābhārata Mahāprasthānika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.15

title: Śiva identified with the entire pantheon
description: The text declares the meditated Śiva to be Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, the imperishable supreme self-ruler, breath, time, fire and moon — collapsing the Trimūrti and all gods into one

title: Jaratkāru sees his ancestors hanging in the pit
description: The celibate ascetic Jaratkāru finds his forefathers dangling over a chasm and is told his line will end unless he marries and begets a son

title: Jābāla Upaniṣad teaches immediate renunciation
description: Yājñavalkya rules that the very day detachment dawns one may go forth (yad ahar eva virajet tad ahar eva pravrajet), bypassing the āśrama sequence; the only text of the group cited in the corpus

title: King's tapas and the self-manifest Pānakāla form
description: A royal devotee's penance on the hill draws the Lord to manifest svayam in the open-mouthed Pānakāla form, establishing the hilltop worship

title: Śākāyanya's Teaching of the Two-Fold Brahman
description: Śākāyanya expounds Brahman in two forms — the guṇa-bound bhūtātman and the supreme tranquil Self

title: Lakṣmī waits for Viṣṇu (tāyār theology)
description: Karavīra is the place where Lakṣmī abides awaiting Viṣṇu's reconciliation, linking Kolhapur and Tirupati darśana

title: Muktinath sung as Tiru Śālagrāmam by the Ālvārs
description: The Ālvār poet-saints give the maṅgalāśāsanam of Tiru Śālagrāmam, fixing Muktinath as the only Divya Deśam outside India

title: Nama-Sankirtana — Kali's One Virtue
description: Though an ocean of faults, Kali offers liberation through mere chanting of God's name, hard-won in earlier ages

title: Nārada counsels Vyāsa to compose the Bhāgavata
description: The despondent Vyāsa is visited by Nārada, who diagnoses his lack and prompts him to compose the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, telling his own life-story as encouragement

title: Nyāsa — installation of sound on the body
description: Through ṣaḍaṅga-, kara-, aṅga-, vyāpaka- and mātṛkā-nyāsa the practitioner installs mantra-syllables onto the body to become the deity before worship

title: Poisoning of the heir
description: The jealous co-wives poison the infant prince to death, collapsing the king into grief

title: Praśna 3 — origin, five-fold division and departure of prāṇa
description: Pippalāda tells Kausalya that prāṇa arises from the Ātman, divides into five vital airs, moves in 101 nāḍīs, and departs upward via udāna at death

title: Pratardana and Indra — prāṇa as prajñā
description: Pratardana son of Divodāsa wins a boon from Indra, who reveals himself as prāṇa and the conscious self (prajñātman), teaching that life-breath and consciousness are one and the lord of all the senses

title: Pūrva phala-śruti
description: The knower-reciter of the Mantrarāja is promised protection from fear, demons, untimely death, and saṃsāra, purified as by all Vedic sacrifices

title: Śrīmuṣṇam reckoned among the Aṣṭa svayam-vyakta kṣetras
description: Vaiṣṇava tradition counts Śrīmuṣṇam among the eight self-manifest abodes of Vishnu alongside Tirumala, Śrīraṅgam, Naimiṣāraṇya, Puṣkara, Badari, Śālagrāma and Toṭādri

title: Seduction of the asuras off the Vedic path
description: Mayamoha preaches non-Vedic (Jain/Buddhist) heterodoxy until the asuras abandon the Veda, lose protective merit, and are destroyed by the devas

title: Selling bangles to the women of Madurai
description: Śiva walks the streets disguised as a bangle-seller to grace the cowherd women of Madurai

title: Shrinivasa Borrows Wedding Wealth from Kubera
description: To pay the bride-price Shrinivasa borrows immense wealth from the treasurer-god Kubera, a perpetual divine debt that devotees' Tirumala offerings repay

title: Specification of aṅga-pratyaṅga proportions and bhaṅga flexions
description: Texts fix limb-by-limb sub-measures, the three-part face division, canonical eye-shapes, and the postural axes sama-/ā-/tri-/ati-bhaṅga

title: Tad-vanam Doctrine
description: Brahman is named Tad-vanam, the Yearned-for that all beings long for, and is to be worshipped under that name

title: The calculus of bliss (ānanda-mīmāṃsā)
description: A graded scale measures bliss a hundredfold up through human, gandharvas, pitṛs, devas, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Prajāpati to Brahman, equating it with the desireless Veda-knower's joy
actors: the Upaniṣadic teacher; ranks of gandharvas

title: The Devī-Bhāgavata recited at Naimiṣa
description: The Śākta Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa is framed as recited at Naimiṣa, binding the Goddess-tradition to the same recitation-forest

title: The heroes reunited and dissolved into their source deities
description: In his new divine body Yudhiṣṭhira beholds each hero returned to source: Bhīma to the Maruts, Arjuna among Indra's host (as Nara), Nakula and Sahadeva to the Aśvins, Draupadī as Śrī/Lakṣmī, Karṇa into Sūrya, Bhīṣma to the Vasus, Droṇa into Bṛhaspati, Abhimanyu to Soma, and Kṛṣṇa beheld in his supreme Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa form

title: The nadir king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste
description: The prophesied king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste, shows no reverence to Vedas or brahmanas, and reduces the twice-born to outcaste status — the symbolic floor of the dynastic prophecy

title: The three boons granted
description: Yama offers three boons in amends: reconciliation with the father, knowledge of the heaven-leading Naciketas-fire (named after the boy), and the secret of what survives death

title: The unmoving mover and the indwelling Ātman
description: The Self is described as immanent-yet-transcendent — unmoving yet swifter than mind, far and near, within and outside all; the seer of oneness transcends grief

title: The Vanished Deity and the Floating Dāru-brahma
description: Nīla Mādhava disappears into the sand before the king arrives; a divine voice promises return as a fragrant log (Dāru-brahma) that washes ashore at Purī

title: The Vratya-stomas
description: Four soma-chants prescribed to consecrate roving outsider Vratya bands and absorb them into the orthodox sacrificial community, redistributing their distinctive gear

title: Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār sings Tirukkaḍigai
description: Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār offers maṅgalāśāsanam on Tirukkaḍigai, enrolling it among the 108 Divya Desams in the Tondai-nāḍu group

title: Vyāsa raises the slain warriors from the Gaṅgā for one night
description: At Gāndhārī's and Kuntī's plea, Vyāsa by ascetic power calls up all the slain warriors of both armies from the river for one reconciled night with the living; Dhṛtarāṣṭra is granted celestial sight to behold his hundred sons, and at dawn the dead re-enter the Gaṅgā

title: Yogacūḍāmaṇi maps the six chakras
description: A concise manual lays out the ṣaṭ-cakra, nāḍīs, prāṇas, bandhas, mudrās and the haṃsa (so'ham) mantra — an early chakra-list text

title: Aniconic yoni-cleft worship
description: The Goddess is worshipped not as an image but as a natural yoni-shaped rock cleft kept moist by an underground spring

title: Attachment of the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka and Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad
description: The Brāhmaṇa's school-corpus extends into the Śāṅkhāyana (Kauṣītaki) Āraṇyaka, which embeds the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad with its Paryaṅka-vidyā and Pratardana–Indra dialogues
actors: Kauṣītaki school; Pratardana; Indra; Bālāki; Ajātaśatru

title: Avatara of Dhumraketu
description: Ganesha will descend as the smoke-colored horse-mounted Dhumraketu at the end of Kali Yuga to destroy the wicked mleccha hordes, a Ganapatya parallel to Kalki

title: Barhadratha Line Ends
description: Last Barhadratha king Puranjaya (Ripunjaya) is assassinated by his minister Shunaka, who enthrones his own son

title: Becoming a fish-seller
description: Śiva takes the guise of a fisherman/fish-vendor, echoing Mīnākṣī's fish-eyed name and the Pāṇḍya fish-emblem

title: Bālāki and Ajātaśatru — the king teaches a brahmin
description: Proud Gārgya Bālāki offers to expound Brahman to King Ajātaśatru of Kāśī, names a series of cosmic/bodily 'persons' each rejected as mere aspects, then is taught the prajñātman via a sleeping man — a parallel of Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.1

title: Brahman Wins a Victory; the Gods Grow Proud
description: Brahman secures a victory for the devas, who exult thinking the glory was their own

title: Brahmā's hurled discus names the forest (nemi/cakra)
description: Brahmā releases his mind-made wheel and bids the sages settle where its rim (nemi) falls; the rim sinks here, naming the forest Naimiṣa and opening the Chakra-tīrtha spring

title: Definition of the identity-grammar (āsana, mudrā, āyudha, vāhana, dhyāna-śloka)
description: Pratimā-lakṣaṇa rules fix a deity's identity through posture, gesture, held attributes, mount and meditation-verse, generating named forms by attribute-permutation
actors: Purāṇic compilers; Mārkaṇḍeya–Vajra dialogue of the Citrasūtra
source: Agni Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Garuḍa Purāṇa pratimā-lakṣaṇa chs.; Viṣṇudharmottara III

title: Deities Afflicted by Hunger Seek an Abode
description: The emitted deities fall into the cosmic ocean, suffer hunger and thirst, and ask the Self for a dwelling
actors: Ātman; the presiding deities; hunger and thirst

title: Descent of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (Closing-Age Teacher)
description: In Gaudiya tradition the next descent after Krishna in this Mahayuga is Chaitanya Mahaprabhu within the present Kali Yuga, propagating the nama-sankirtana yuga-dharma

title: Digvijaya conquest of the eight directions
description: As warrior-queen she conquers the eight quarters, subduing kings, the dik-pālas, Indra and the devas

title: Durvāsas, the gopīs, and the parting of the Yamunā
description: The gopīs cross the Yamunā to feed Durvāsas after the river parts at the claim that Kṛṣṇa is a perpetual brahmacārin, dramatizing His transcendence of His own līlā

title: Kṛṣṇa's Viśvarūpa Darśana to Janamejaya
description: Viṣṇu as Kṛṣṇa the Pāṇḍava-envoy grants the cosmic-form darśana to king Janamejaya, commemorated at the Pāṇḍava Dūta temple of Kāñcī

title: Marriage of Jaratkāru and Vāsuki's sister (Manasā)
description: Vāsuki gives his sister, also named Jaratkāru (later Manasā), to the ascetic so her son can halt the snake-sacrifice

title: Nārada and Aṅgiras console
description: The two sages come to teach the king that worldly relations are transient configurations of karma

title: Oṃkāra-turīya identification of Narasiṃha-Brahman
description: The Uttara analyses AUM and its fourth soundless mātrā, mapping the four states of consciousness to Narasiṃha as turīya, the supreme non-dual Self

title: Praśna 4 — sleep, dream and deep sleep
description: Pippalāda explains to Sauryāyaṇī how the senses rest in the mind in sleep, the mind projects dreams, and in deep sleep all merge in the imperishable Ātman

title: Śrīnivāsa's descent and the anthill austerity
description: Viṣṇu follows Lakṣmī to earth as Śrīnivāsa and dwells in austerity on Veṅkaṭa hill, in some tellings nursed within an anthill

title: Āruṇi questions Prajāpati on abandoning rites
description: The sage Āruṇi (Uddālaka) asks Prajāpati how to relinquish all rites, and is told the physical renunciations (sons, wealth, sacred thread, study)

title: Sambandar's Confrontation with the Jains at Madurai
description: At the Meenakshi/Madurai shrine, Sambandar confronts the Jains in the legends focused on the Pandya capital

title: Second Boon — The Nāciketa Fire
description: Naciketas asks the heavenward fire-sacrifice; Yama expounds the Nāciketa fire-altar, names it after the boy, and adds a necklace

title: Slaying of Kolhāsura
description: The Goddess slays the demon Kolhāsura, who dying begs that the city bear his name and that she remain as Mahālakṣmī of Kolhāpura

title: The Bhṛgu–Varuṇa inquiry into Brahman
description: Bhṛgu asks his father Varuṇa to teach Brahman and, through repeated tapas, ascends from food to breath, mind, knowledge and finally bliss as Brahman — that from which beings are born, live, and into which they return

title: The Bhūtātman Bound by the Guṇas
description: The elemental self, overcome by prakṛti's three guṇas, fails to perceive the indwelling Lord and wanders through births

title: The bow-and-arrow praṇava meditation
description: Oṃ is the bow, the self the arrow, Brahman the target; drawn by a mind absorbed in That, one strikes the Imperishable

title: The epic closes with its phala-śruti
description: The book declares Vyāsa composed a six-million-verse poem distributed across the worlds, proclaims the merit of reciting the Mahābhārata, and gives the closing self-praise that what is here is found elsewhere and what is not here is nowhere, with benediction to Nārāyaṇa, Nara and Sarasvatī

title: The five fall one by one on the slopes of Meru
description: As they cross the high snow, Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, and Bhīma each fall in turn, Yudhiṣṭhira naming the single fault (partiality, pride in wisdom, vanity of beauty, arrogance in prowess, gluttony and boasting) that bars each from bodily ascent, never looking back

title: The Hidden Carpenter and the Unfinished Images
description: Viśvakarmā (or Ananta-mahārāṇā) carves the log behind locked doors; the door is opened early, leaving Jagannātha armless and unfinished, and Brahmā consecrates the temple

title: The 'I am Śiva' (śivo'ham) realization
description: The meditator declares his identity with Śiva-Brahman — all is born, established and dissolved in Me; that non-dual Brahman am I; for Me there is no death, fear, caste, birth, father or mother

title: The righteous reign
description: Parīkṣit rules as a cakravartin at the Dvāpara→Kali cusp, marries Irāvatī, fathers Janamejaya, and performs three Aśvamedhas

title: The sixteen mantra-saṃskāras and mantra-caitanya
description: A received mantra is purified by sixteen saṃskāras and 'awakened' (caitanya), since a mantra may be asleep or cursed and thus inert without it

title: The vidyā/avidyā and saṃbhūti/asaṃbhūti balanced pairs
description: Devotion to either knowledge or ignorance alone leads to darkness; one crosses death by holding both vidyā and avidyā (and saṃbhūti and asaṃbhūti) together
source: Īśa Upaniṣad 9–14 (Kāṇva & Mādhyandina recensions; Śaṅkara bhāṣya)

title: The worn-garland miracle (Cūḍikkoḍutta Nācciyār)
description: Gōdai secretly wears the Lord's garlands; Viṣṇu declares he will accept only garlands she has first worn, giving her the epithet Cūḍikkoḍutta Nācciyār

title: War-widows enter the Gaṅgā to rejoin their husbands
description: Vyāsa tells the widows that any who wish to rejoin their dead husbands may enter the river; women who do so cast off their bodies in the Gaṅgā and ascend to their husbands' worlds

title: Yama's test — wealth offered and refused
description: Yama tries to deflect the third boon with sons, herds, gold, long life and apsarases; Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds Yama to the knowledge of the Self

title: Yogakuṇḍalinī rouses the serpent power
description: The text describes rousing kuṇḍalinī by bhastrikā breath and bandhas, the khecarī-mudrā and drinking cranial amṛta, culminating in union with Śiva at the sahasrāra

title: Ambubāchī Melā — annual menstruation
description: Each Āṣāḍha the Goddess menstruates; the temple closes three days and reopens with red-cloth prasāda, drawing tantric pilgrims

title: Birth of Āstīka
description: After Jaratkāru abandons his pregnant wife, the half-brahmin half-nāga boy Āstīka is born and reared by Vāsuki to save the snakes

title: Brahma founds the Tirumala Brahmotsavam
description: Brahma is said to have first performed the nine-day utsavam on Venkatachala hill to thank Vishnu for descending as Venkateshwara in the Kali Yuga, establishing the paradigm South-Indian brahmotsava form with its sequence of daily vahana processions culminating in Garuda Seva, Rathotsavam and the Chakra-snanam
source: Venkatachala Mahatmya / Varaha Purana; Vaikhanasa-Pancharatra Agama; TTD

title: Composition of the Tiruppāvai and Nācciyār Tirumoḻi
description: At Srivilliputhur Āṇḍāḷ composes the thirty-verse Tiruppāvai and the 143-verse Nācciyār Tirumoḻi, vowing to wed only Raṅganātha
source: Nālāyira Divya Prabandham — Tiruppāvai, Nācciyār Tirumoḻi

title: Cow and Horse Rejected, Man Accepted
description: The deities reject cow and horse as dwellings but accept the human form, exclaiming su-kṛtam ('well made')

title: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī die in the forest fire
description: After two more years of harsh tapas, a wildfire sweeps the wood; too weak to flee, the three elders choose not to escape and the blind king sits in yoga as the flames take all three; Nārada announces their deaths to Yudhiṣṭhira

title: Divergence of sectarian Āgamic iconometric canons
description: Śaiva, Vaikhānasa and Pāñcarātra Āgamas establish sect-specific bera/pratimā-lakṣaṇa distinguishing dhruva-bera from utsava icons by distinct measures

title: Doctrine of the Good vs. the Pleasant (śreyas/preyas)
description: Satisfied by the test, Yama teaches that the wise choose the Good (śreyas) over the Pleasant (preyas), and that the Self is gained only by the one it chooses

title: Dvā suparṇā — two birds on one tree
description: Two companion birds on one tree: the jīva eats the sweet fruit while the witnessing Self looks on; seeing the Lord, the grieving jīva's sorrow departs

title: Enrollment among the 18 Mahā Śakti Pīṭhas
description: Mahālakṣmī of Kolhapur is fixed as the seventh of the Aṣṭādaśa Śakti Pīṭhas in the stotram attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara

title: Gokarna-Dhundhukari ghost-liberation (Bhagavata-Mahatmya)
description: The allegory of Bhakti as a mother with sons Jnana and Vairagya, with the ghost Dhundhukari liberated by recitation of the Bhagavata

title: Hiraṇmayena pātreṇa — the golden vessel over Truth's face
description: A prayer to Pūṣan/the solar deity to unveil the golden disc hiding the face of Truth, and the identity 'that Person in the sun, He am I.'
actors: Pūṣan / Sūrya / Yama; the dying seeker

title: King Indradyumna founds the Jagannātha cult at Puri
description: King Indradyumna recovers the divine dāru-brahman image, which Viśvakarmā carves into the Jagannātha–Balabhadra–Subhadrā triad at Puruṣottama-kṣetra (Puri)

title: Marriage of Śrīnivāsa and Padmāvatī
description: Śrīnivāsa falls in love with and marries Padmāvatī (Alamēlu-maṅgā), lotus-born daughter of King Ākāśarāja and a form of Lakṣmī, enshrined at Tiruchanūr

title: Medha-sūktas invoke intelligence and memory
description: Short hymns beg Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, Agni, Indra and the Aśvins to grant medhā (intellect/memory), recited by students before Vedic study

title: Nabakalebara — Periodic Re-embodiment
description: The perishable wooden images are periodically replaced and the secret Brahma-padārtha life-essence transferred; historical rites span 1969–2015

title: Nanda Dynasty — Exterminator of Kshatriyas
description: Mahapadma Nanda, born of a shudra woman, founds the first non-kshatriya empire, styled 'exterminator of all kshatriyas'

title: Nādabindu and Haṃsa systematize inner sound (nāda/laya-yoga)
description: Laya-yoga dissolves the mind in the ten unstruck inner sounds; the Haṃsa Upaniṣad sets the haṃsa-vidyā/ajapā-gāyatrī in a Sanatkumāra–Gautama dialogue

title: Nārada questions Prajāpati on the paramahaṃsa
description: Nārada asks Prajāpati to define the supreme renouncer, who casts off staff, tuft, and thread and wears only knowledge as his mark

title: Praśna 5 — meditation on Oṃ (one, two, three mātrās)
description: Pippalāda teaches Śaibya that meditating on Oṃ's one/two/three mātrās wins the world of men, the moon, or Brahma-loka and the supreme Puruṣa

title: Prophesied Descent of Kalki
description: Vishnu is prophesied to descend as Kalki at the end of Kali Yuga to end the age of strife and restore Satya Yuga

title: Puraścaraṇa — the preparatory regimen
description: Before a mantra becomes siddha the sādhaka completes a cascade of japa, homa, tarpaṇa, abhiṣeka and brāhmaṇa-bhojana in a one-tenth decadal ratio

title: Takṣaka Slays King Parīkṣit
description: The serpent-chief Takṣaka, having been cursed-upon by Śṛṅgin's word against Parīkṣit, slays the king with his venom on the seventh day, triggering Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice

title: Taming and regulating personified Kali
description: Parīkṣit catches Kali beating the bull Dharma and cow Earth, spares the suppliant, and confines adharma by assigning Kali fixed abodes (gambling, drink, illicit sex, slaughter, gold)

title: The dead boy's soul revived to speak
description: Nārada summons the departed jīva back into the corpse; the soul discourses on the deathless self and its countless past kin

title: The dog reveals himself as Dharma and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends in the body
description: Indra offers to carry Yudhiṣṭhira to Svarga but forbids the dog; Yudhiṣṭhira refuses to abandon the faithful creature, whereupon the dog reveals himself as Dharma (his divine father) who praises his compassion, and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends to heaven in his living mortal body, an unprecedented feat

title: The food-hymns and 'I am food' realization-chant
description: The Bhṛgu-vallī closes with injunctions never to despise food and the liberated knower's exultant chant 'I am food, I am the eater of food.'
actors: the liberated knower (Bhṛgu); the Taittirīya tradition

title: The gopīs question the nature of the Deity
description: The gopīs and sages ask who Kṛṣṇa truly is, how to worship Him, and what His mantra and abode are; the answers reaffirm Kṛṣṇa as the one Brahman behind all gods

title: The Nimiṣa demons slain in a wink
description: A host of Nimiṣa demons is destroyed at the site in an instant (nimiṣa), an alternative etymology for the name Naimiṣa

title: The storming of Kailāsa
description: Mīnākṣī marches on Śiva's Kailāsa, routs his gaṇas including Nandi and Vīrabhadra, drawing Śiva onto the field

title: The Three Guṇas Mapped to the Trimūrti
description: The Upaniṣad names sattva, rajas, tamas explicitly and maps them to Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Rudra as the One's threefold unfolding

title: The Yakṣa Appears
description: Brahman manifests as an unrecognizable yakṣa (spirit) before the gods to humble them

title: Third Boon — The Secret of Death Requested
description: Naciketas asks the great doubt of whether a man exists after death, the Upaniṣad's metaphysical innovation

title: Two-birds image and turīya analysis
description: The text re-quotes the two-birds (dvā suparṇā) verse and the witness of waking-dream-deep-sleep, weaving Māṇḍūkya-style turīya analysis into the Śaiva meditation
actors: the jīva (eating bird); the Lord (witnessing bird)

title: Unity of Mantrarāja and Praṇava; Uttara phala-śruti
description: The Uttara teaches that the man-lion Mantrarāja and the Oṃkāra are one, and that knowing this Oṃkāra-Narasiṃha grants liberation, crossing death into turīya

title: Vandi-koṇḍa līlā — carrying earth for piṭṭu and taking the cane-blow
description: Śiva labours as a coolie for the piṭṭu-seller Vandi to dam the Vaikai; the king's cane-blow on the lazy labourer is felt by every living being

title: Agni Fails to Burn the Straw
description: Agni is sent first and cannot burn a single blade of grass set before him by the yakṣa

title: Andal Composes the Tiruppavai at Srivilliputhur
description: Andal (Goda) is born at Srivilliputhur, birthplace also of Periyalvar, where the Tiruppavai originates

title: Bindu-texts interiorize Oṃ (praṇava)
description: Amṛtabindu, Dhyānabindu, Amṛtanāda and Brahmavidyā resolve Oṃ into bīja, bindu, nāda and kalā and into the soundless turīya, teaching that the mind alone binds and frees
source: Amṛtabindu (Brahmabindu) Up.; Dhyānabindu Up.; Amṛtanāda Up.; Brahmavidyā Up.

title: Canonization as northernmost Jyotirliṅga
description: Kedarnath is fixed as the northernmost of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, 'Himālaye tu Kedāram,' in the Śiva Purāṇa and Śaṅkara's stotra

title: Chanakya Uproots the Nandas
description: A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) overthrows the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty

title: Doctrine of māna-doṣa and canonical efficacy
description: The texts hold that a correctly-measured image is prāsādika while a proportion-fault (māna-doṣa) brings harm, making the canon a ritual necessity rather than aesthetics

title: Initiation and the Saṅkarṣaṇa mantra
description: Freed of grief, Citraketu receives the Saṅkarṣaṇa mantra from Nārada and purifies himself by seven days of discipline

title: Janamejaya's Sarpa-Satra (Snake-Sacrifice)
description: Janamejaya vows to exterminate the serpent race and undertakes the sarpa-satra, whose oblations draw nāgas of every size from across the worlds into the flames

title: Kaṇṇappa's Eye-Offering at Srikalahasti
description: The hunter-saint Kannappa, worshipping the linga his untaught way, gouges out his own eyes to stop the linga's bleeding eye; Shiva seizes his hand, restores his eyes and grants liberation, proving devotion outranks ritual

title: Kubera's wedding-loan to Śrīnivāsa
description: To meet bridal expenses Śrīnivāsa borrows a vast sum from Kubera, vowing repayment with interest through all of Kali-yuga — the basis of the temple hundi donations

title: Lakulisha prophecy, last of the 28 Yogeshvaras
description: The Purana prophesies Maheshvara descending in Kali Yuga as the ascetic Lakulisha, 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples who found the Pashupata sect

title: Opening the rock / staying the flood for the Pāṇḍya
description: Śiva cleaves a rock or stays the Vaikai flood for the Pāṇḍya, delivering the city

title: Parikṣit insults sage Śamīka with a dead snake
description: The lone Kuru heir Parikṣit, thirsty while hunting, loops a dead snake on the silent meditating sage Śamīka

title: Phala-śruti and Śatarudriya benediction
description: The closing fruit-of-recitation verses promise that whoever recites this knowledge, chanting it with the Śatarudriya, is purified of the great sins and attains kaivalya, oneness with Śiva
source: Kaivalya Upaniṣad closing verses 23-24 (cf. Yajurveda Śatarudriya/Rudram)

title: Praśna 6 — the Person of sixteen parts (ṣoḍaśa-kala puruṣa)
description: Pippalāda answers Sukeśā that the sixteen kalās arise from the Person within the body and dissolve back into him as rivers lose name-and-form in the sea

title: Rudhirādhyāya blood-offering rite
description: The Kālikā Purāṇa's blood-chapter prescribes the animal (and ideal human) sacrifice continued at Kāmākhyā

title: Sañjaya escapes the fire and departs for the Himālaya
description: Before the fire closes in, Dhṛtarāṣṭra orders his faithful charioteer Sañjaya to save himself; bereft of his master, Sañjaya retires to the Himālaya to perform penance and is never heard of again

title: Satyam eva jayate — Truth alone triumphs
description: The verse 'satyam eva jayate nānṛtaṃ' declares truth alone triumphs over falsehood; later adopted as the national motto of India under the Lion Capital of Aśoka
source: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.6; State Emblem of India

title: Āṇḍāḷ's bridal procession and merging at Śrīraṅgam
description: Viṣṇu commands that Gōdai be brought in bridal procession to Śrīraṅgam, where she enters the sanctum and merges into Raṅganātha

title: The ṣaṭkarma — six applied prayogas
description: The six acts (śānti, vaśīkaraṇa, stambhana, vidveṣaṇa, uccāṭana, māraṇa) deploy a perfected mantra, each with assigned deity, season, direction and seat
source: Mantra-mahodadhi; Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Agni Purāṇa; Tantrarāja Tantra

title: The Chakra-tīrtha discus-ford established
description: The central tank at Nīmsār marks where the wheel's rim (or Viṣṇu's Sudarśana/Manomaya Cakra) struck the earth, opening a perennial spring said to well up from Pātāla
source: Vāyu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa Naimiṣa-khaṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4

title: The chariot allegory of the Self
description: Yama teaches the ratha-kalpanā: the Self as rider, body as chariot, intellect as charioteer, mind as reins, senses as horses, sense-objects as roads

title: The cremation prayer — body to ashes, Agne naya supathā
description: The dying invocation releasing breath to the immortal Wind and body to ashes, and the closing prayer to Agni to lead by the good path
actors: Agni; the dying person / cremation officiant

title: The Devas approach and learn Kṛṣṇa's supremacy
description: The gods led by Brahmā and Indra approach the supreme Person and learn He is the inner Self and Lord of all the Devas, who themselves worship Him

title: The Gods Enter Their Seats in Man
description: Each deity enters its station in the human body, becoming the corresponding sense-faculty

title: The Ratha Yātrā Chariot Festival
description: On Āṣāḍha dvitīyā the triad rides three giant chariots (Nandighoṣa, Tāḷadhvaja, Darpadalana) to the Guṇḍicā temple; the Gajapati king performs Chera Paṅharā
source: Brahma Purāṇa māhātmya layer; temple tradition

title: The Sannyāsa corpus as charter of the Daśanāmī orders
description: The group supplies the Śruti backing for the ekadaṇḍin Daśanāmī monastic system traditionally organised under Ādi Śaṅkara, who read his order back into these texts

title: The Six-Limbed Ṣaḍaṅga-Yoga
description: Śākāyanya sets out the sixfold yoga — prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi — prefiguring Patañjali

title: The third breast vanishes at the sight of Śiva
description: Facing Śiva, her third breast disappears and her battle-fury turns to a bride's modesty, marking him as her destined lord

title: The thirsty hunt and dead-snake insult
description: Exhausted and parched, and with Kali entered through his gold crown, Parīkṣit drapes a dead snake on the silently meditating sage Śamīka
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.18

title: Yama Tests Naciketas with Bribes
description: Yama offers sons, cattle, gold, lands, long life and celestial maidens instead, but Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds to the third boon

title: Birth of Nammalvar at Azhwarthirunagari
description: Nammalvar (Maran/Satakopan), foremost of the Alvars who sang the most Divya Desams, is born at Tirukkurugur/Azhwarthirunagari

title: Buddha absorbed as Vishnu's 9th avatara (Mayamoha rationale)
description: Puranic tradition folds the Buddha into the Dashavatara as a deluder (Mayamoha) sent to lead the unworthy/asuras away from the Veda, both absorbing and discrediting Buddhism

title: Citraketu becomes lord of the Vidyādharas
description: He attains vidyādhara lordship, beholds Saṅkarṣaṇa/Ananta, and wanders the heavens for an age

title: Creation and Pursuit of Food
description: The Self creates food, which flees, and is finally seized only by the down-breath (apāna)

title: Dadhīci gives his bones at the kṣetra to forge the Vajra
description: At the Naimiṣa kṣetra (Misrikh/Dadhīci-kuṇḍa) the sage Dadhīci surrenders his bones to forge the Vajra that slays Vṛtra

title: Declaration of Goloka/Vṛndāvana as the supreme abode and phala-śruti
description: Kṛṣṇa is declared cause of all causes with Goloka-Vṛndāvana as His eternal transcendent abode; the text closes with the worship-method and a phala-śruti promising His abode and liberation

title: Frame-dialogue Yoga Upaniṣads transmit aṣṭāṅga/tāraka yoga
description: Maṇḍala-brāhmaṇa (Sun to Yājñavalkya), Triśikhi-brāhmaṇa (Sun to Triśikhi), Darśana (Dattātreya to Sāṃkṛti) and Varāha (Viṣṇu-Boar to Ṛbhu) transmit full eight-limbed/tāraka yoga with chakras and kuṇḍalinī
actors: Sun-Puruṣa; Yājñavalkya; Triśikhi; Dattātreya; Sāṃkṛti; Viṣṇu (Varāha); Ṛbhu
source: Maṇḍala-brāhmaṇa Up.; Triśikhi-brāhmaṇa Up.; Darśana Up.; Varāha Up.

title: Śṛṅgin's curse on Parikṣit
description: Śamīka's son Śṛṅgin curses the king to die within seven days from Takṣaka's bite; Parikṣit retreats to a guarded pillar-palace

title: Śṛṅgī's seven-day death-curse
description: Śamīka's boy-son Śṛṅgī curses the king to die within seven days by the bite of the nāga Takṣaka; Śamīka rebukes his son and sends a warning
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.18

title: Hunting the boar (Pandi līlā)
description: Śiva pursues a great boar through Pāṇḍya country, founding shrines along the chase

title: Śiva pledges the Madurai wedding
description: Śiva bids her return to her capital and promises to come as Sundareśvara to wed her at Madurai

title: Liberation as Union in the Self
description: By the sixfold yoga the yogī beholds the golden Person and his stilled thought subsides into its source, attaining unity in the Ātman

title: River-into-ocean simile of liberation
description: As rivers lose name and form in the ocean, the knower freed from name and form attains the supreme Puruṣa

title: Śrīnivāsa remains bodily on the hill
description: Bound by marriage and debt, Śrīnivāsa stays on Tirumala rather than returning to Vaikuṇṭha, grounding the Kali-yuga refuge promise

title: Sambandar's Madurai episode
description: The child-saint Sambandar cures the Pāṇḍya king's fever with holy ash, defeats the Jains in debate and ordeal, and reconverts the king to Śaivism

title: Sannyāsa mantras and the tyāga-immortality verse
description: Supplies the renunciation formulae (praiṣa, 'fearlessness to all beings') and the verse 'na karmaṇā... tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ' exalting renunciation as the path to immortality

title: Sarayū established as life-purifier and death-liberator tīrtha
description: The Ayodhyā-māhātmya fixes the bathing/dying mokṣa-formula on the Sarayū and catalogues its riverfront fords (Svargadvāra, Gopratāra, Rāmkī Paiṛī) for ongoing pilgrimage
actors: Pilgrims of Ayodhyā; the Skanda/Padma Purāṇa redactors
source: Skanda Purāṇa Ayodhyā-māhātmya; Padma Purāṇa; pilgrimage tradition

title: Āstīka Halts the Snake-Sacrifice
description: Vāsuki sends his nephew Āstīka, who praises the sacrifice so eloquently that Janamejaya grants a boon to cease it, sparing Takṣaka and the surviving nāgas and ending the enmity

title: The distinct Liṅga Purāṇa Śiva Sahasranāma
description: A separate thousand-name recension with its own selection and frame, used in liṅga worship and not to be merged with the Mbh list

title: The Pūrṇam śānti-mantra
description: The peace-invocation 'Oṃ pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam' declaring the infinite Absolute undiminished in manifesting the world, conventionally attached to the Īśa
actors: recitation tradition of the Śukla Yajurveda
source: Śukla Yajurveda śānti-pāṭha; cf. Bṛhadāraṇyaka V.1.1

title: The razor's-edge path and 'arise, awake'
description: Yama exhorts Naciketas to awaken, declaring the spiritual path hard to cross as a razor's sharp edge (kṣurasya dhārā), above a ladder of subtlety culminating in the Puruṣa

title: Vishvasphurji Abolishes Caste
description: The nadir king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste, scorns Vedas and brahmanas — the symbolic floor of the dynastic prophecy

title: Vāyu Fails to Move the Straw
description: Vāyu is sent next and cannot blow away the same blade of grass

title: Yama Teaches the Knowledge of the Self
description: Yama discloses śreyas vs preyas, the unborn Self, OM, the chariot of the body, and yoga as steadiness of the senses

title: Ahalyā among the Pañcakanyā
description: Ahalyā heads the traditional list of five ideal women (Pañcakanyā) invoked in daily sin-destroying remembrance, paragons of virtue despite irregular sexual histories

title: Entry of the Self Through the Suture of the Skull
description: The Self cleaves the crown of the head and enters the body through the suture, the place of bliss, becoming the indwelling seer (cryptically named Indra)

title: Gokarṇa as the western Tīrtha-yātrā ford
description: The Mahābhārata Tīrtha-yātrā Parva names Gokarṇa among the holy western/southern coastal tīrthas where bathing yields great merit

title: Indra Approaches and the Yakṣa Vanishes
description: Indra goes last; the yakṣa disappears, and Indra alone waits at the spot

title: Mockery of Śiva and Pārvatī
description: Citraketu carelessly jests at Śiva for holding Pārvatī on his lap before an assembly of sages

title: Naciketas Attains Brahman
description: Having received the knowledge of the Self and the whole rule of yoga from Death, Naciketas becomes free of passion and death and attains Brahman

title: Naimiṣa named a supreme ford in the Tīrtha-yātrā Parva
description: Pulastya (to Bhīṣma) and Nārada/Dhaumya (to Yudhiṣṭhira) rank Naimiṣa on the Gomatī among the supreme pan-sectarian fords, a month's bathing yielding horse-sacrifice merit

title: Renunciation and hearing the Bhāgavata from Śuka
description: Accepting the curse, Parīkṣit fasts on the Gaṅgā and hears the entire Bhāgavata Purāṇa recited by Śukadeva over seven days (vs the epic's fortified-tower resistance)
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.19–XII.5; Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva

title: Sandhyā, prāṇāyāma and expiation liturgy
description: Furnishes a large share of daily twilight-prayer (sandhyā-vandana), the prāṇāyāma vyāhṛti-formula, and aghamarṣaṇa/prāyaścitta expiation mantras of the Yajurvedin

title: Takṣaka kills Parikṣit
description: Takṣaka turns back the healer Kāśyapa, enters the fortress hidden in a fruit, and bites Parikṣit, who burns to death
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 40–43; cf. Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.16–19

title: The hunter and the elephant
description: Śiva as a hunter subdues a rogue/demon elephant sent against the city or his devotees

title: The thumb-sized Person and yoga of sense-restraint
description: Yama reveals the aṅguṣṭha-mātra puruṣa dwelling in the heart, the self-luminous abode, the eleven-gated body-city and the inverted cosmic tree, defining yoga as the firm holding-back of the senses
source: Kaṭha Upaniṣad II.1.12–13, II.2.1, II.2.15, II.3.1, II.3.10–17

title: The Tirukalyāṇam — the divine wedding
description: Śiva as Sundareśvara weds Mīnākṣī in the great Tirukalyāṇam at Madurai, the theological centre of the temple

title: Vaiśampāyana First Recites the Mahābhārata
description: At Janamejaya's sarpa-satra, Vaiśampāyana, pupil of Vyāsa, first recites the Mahābhārata to the king — the epic's outermost narrative frame

title: Arjuna's Gandiva fails against the Abhira robbers
description: Escorting the Yadava column, Arjuna is ambushed by Abhira bandits and finds his strength gone, unable to string Gandiva or summon his astras; the widows are carried off and the loss of his invincibility signals the divine age has closed

title: Death by Takṣaka
description: Takṣaka turns back the physician Kaśyapa, hides as a worm in a fruit, and bites the king, who dies liberated; the death triggers Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa XII.6

title: Doctrine of the Threefold Birth
description: The teaching that a man is born three times: in the womb, at delivery, and through his offspring / spiritual rebirth, exemplified by Vāmadeva

title: Forest retreat and the dead raised
description: Gāndhārī retires to a forest hermitage where Vyāsa raises the slain from the Gaṅgā for one night

title: Gokarṇa as mukti-kṣetra, the Kāśī of the South
description: Gokarṇa is glorified as a liberation-tīrtha with the Koṭi-tīrtha tank and direct touch-darśana of the Ātma-liṅga, styled Dakṣiṇa-Kāśī

title: Janamejaya vows the sarpa-satra
description: On learning how his father died, Janamejaya vows a snake-sacrifice to summon and burn every serpent, with Takṣaka the chief target

title: Pārvatī's curse
description: The offended Goddess curses Citraketu to take a demon's birth as corrective humiliation

title: Revelation by Umā Haimavatī
description: The goddess Umā Haimavatī appears and reveals to Indra that the yakṣa was Brahman, whose victory the gods had wrongly claimed

title: The First Three Alvars Meet at Tirukkovilur
description: The first three (Mudhal) Alvars — Poigai, Bhutha, and Pey — meet in a storm-narrowed corridor at Tirukkovilur, where the Iyarpa Prabandham begins

title: The Kali-yuga king-list prophecy
description: Parashara prophesies the post-Parikshit dynasties of Magadha (Pradyotas, Shaishunagas, Nandas, Mauryas, Shungas, Kanvas, Andhras) and foretells the rise of mleccha and low-born kings

title: The stone elephant that ate sugarcane
description: Śiva makes a carved stone elephant come alive and eat sugarcane to confound rivals and vindicate a devotee

title: Tiru Naimiśāraṇyam sung as a Divya Desam
description: Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār sings Naimiṣāraṇya (Devarāja Perumāḷ, with Puṇḍarīkavalli Thāyār) as one of the 108 Divya Desams in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham

title: Venkateshvara's marriage to Padmavati and loan from Kubera
description: The self-manifest Venkateshvara (Balaji/Srinivasa) of Tirumala marries Padmavati and takes a loan from Kubera, the founding legend of the Tirupati shrine

title: Vishnu Stands on Pundalika's Brick at Pandharpur
description: While serving his parents, the reformed son Pundalika tosses a brick for the arriving Vishnu to wait upon; pleased, the Lord stays standing on the brick as Vitthala

title: Viṣṇu/Aḻagar gives the bride away
description: Her brother Viṣṇu (Aḻagar/Kallaḻagar) performs the kanyādāna; in the festival variant he arrives at the Vaikai too late

title: Vyāsa recounts the 108 Śakti Pīṭhas
description: Vyāsa recounts to Janamejaya 108 seats of the Goddess with their locations and the local form of the Devī at each — the most-cited Purāṇic pīṭha-list

title: Citraketu's serene acceptance
description: He bows and calmly accepts the curse as God's will, treating blessing and curse with equal vision; Śiva extols him

title: Co-sovereignty and worship-precedence established
description: By the marriage Mīnākṣī remains co-sovereign and is worshipped before Sundareśvara, the union re-enacted yearly at the Cittirai festival

title: Death in the forest wildfire
description: A forest conflagration consumes Gāndhārī together with Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Kuntī; Sañjaya survives to report it

title: Disputed canonical status — the Vāyu/Śiva seat
description: Vāyu is counted among the 18 Mahāpurāṇas by Matsya/Bhāgavata lists but replaced by the Śiva Purāṇa in others; al-Bīrūnī already recorded the two rival lists

title: Hierarchy of the Gods Established
description: Because Agni, Vāyu and Indra drew nearest to Brahman, they are held to excel the other gods, Indra most of all

title: Naimiṣa counted among the Aṣṭa Svayaṃ-vyakta Viṣṇu kṣetras
description: Vaiṣṇava tradition lists Naimiṣa among the eight self-manifested shrines of Viṣṇu where the deity appeared without human installation
source: Pāñcarātra tradition; Vaiṣṇava sthala-purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4

title: Prajñānaṃ Brahma — Consciousness Is Brahman
description: The inquiry into the Self identifies all faculties and all gods and beings with Prajñāna and declares the Ṛgvedic mahāvākya 'Consciousness is Brahman.'

title: The burning of the nāgas
description: Priests' mantras drag serpents by the thousand into the sacrificial fire, fulfilling Brahmā's sanctioned cull

title: Turning jackals into horses (and back)
description: Śiva transforms jackals into cavalry horses to rescue Māṇikkavācakar, then turns them back into jackals before vindicating his devotee

title: Vajra installed as king at Indraprastha
description: Arjuna reaches Kurukshetra with a remnant and installs Krishna's grandson Vajra as king at Indraprastha, preserving the Yadava line

title: Vajranabha Re-founds Dvaraka Worship
description: Krishna's lineage through Aniruddha and Vajra is credited with re-founding worship and raising the original Hari-griha shrine after the city's submergence

title: Astika halts the sarpa-satra and the Mahabharata is recited
description: The young brahmana Astika stops Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, sparing Takshaka, and it is at this sattra that Vaishampayana first recites the Mahabharata

title: Establishing/convening the Tamil Saṅgam
description: Śiva sanctions and presides over the Madurai Tamil Saṅgam, legitimising Tamil as a sacred language

title: Rebirth as Vṛtrāsura
description: By the curse Citraketu is reborn through Tvaṣṭṛ's sacrifice as the saintly demon Vṛtra, bridging into the Indra–Vṛtra–Dadhīci war

title: Survival, reconciliation, and tutorship of Parikshit
description: Kripa survives the war uncursed, is re-accepted at Hastinapura, and becomes the weapons-teacher of Parikshit

title: Takṣaka flees to Indra; Indra abandons him
description: Takṣaka coils round Indra's throne; the intensified mantra begins to drag Indra and Takṣaka together, and Indra lets him slide toward the fire

title: The Great Departure and the test of the dog
description: After Kṛṣṇa's death Yudhiṣṭhira crowns Parikṣit and journeys north; his companions fall one by one, and he refuses Indra's heaven rather than abandon a faithful dog who proves to be Dharma

title: The Lalitā / Liṅgadhāriṇī Devī seat
description: The kṣetra hosts the Devī Liṅgadhāriṇī (identified with Lalitā), counted in several Śakti Pīṭha rosters, with Bhairava Mahārudra as guardian

title: Vyāsa counsels the Pāṇḍavas to renounce the kingdom
description: The grief-stricken Arjuna goes to Vyāsa, who explains all happened by destiny and the ripening of curses, and counsels that the heroes' age is over and the time has come for the Pāṇḍavas to renounce and depart

title: Kali-Yuga prophecy (Bhaviṣya Parva)
description: The Bhaviṣya Parva forecasts the degenerate age to come — the moral and social decline of Kali Yuga, beginning by tradition at Krishna's departure

title: Kalki's Epic Wars and Reign (Kalki Purana)
description: Kalki marries Padma and Rama, wars against Koka and Vikoka, defeats the demon Kali personified, then reigns and ascends

title: The final test of heaven and hell
description: Seeing Duryodhana in heaven and his loved ones in hell, Yudhiṣṭhira chooses to remain in Naraka with them; the illusion lifts, he sheds his body in the celestial Gaṅgā, and is reunited in true Svarga

title: The miraculous Saṅgam bench (palakai)
description: Śiva grants a floating plank that expands or contracts to seat only true poets, rejecting the unworthy

title: Vāsuki sends Āstīka to the sacrifice
description: Watching his clan burn, Vāsuki dispatches his grown nephew Āstīka to the sacrificial ground to plead for the snakes

title: Kali Yuga prophecy of the Viṣṇu Purāṇa
description: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa closes its king-lists with a famed prophecy of the moral decline of Kali Yuga

title: Āstīka halts the rite and saves Takṣaka
description: Āstīka's eulogy wins a boon from Janamejaya; he asks that the sacrifice cease, and Takṣaka—suspended over the fire—and the surviving nāgas are saved

title: The contest with Nakkīrar
description: The critic Nakkīrar faults a verse authored by Śiva himself; Śiva opens his third eye but finally pardons the fearless scholar

title: Bhima's Fall on the Great Departure
description: On the final Himalayan march Bhima falls, his flaw named as gluttony and pride in his strength

title: Gaṇeśa-caturthī moon-curse aetiology
description: A vrata-kathā frame explains Kṛṣṇa's slander as the fruit of seeing the moon on Gaṇeśa-caturthī, and prescribes reciting the Syamantaka story to avert false accusation
source: Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa / vrata-kathā tradition attached to Bhāgavata 10.56–57

title: Sending the seven clouds and the great flood
description: Śiva commands the seven clouds to deluge the land (the Vaikai flood), showing mastery of the elements over the Pāṇḍya realm

title: Āstīka's snakebite-protection blessing
description: The grateful serpents grant Āstīka a boon; he decrees that whoever recalls his name shall fear no snakes—the charm tied to Nāga Pañcamī
source: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 58; Nāga Pañcamī folk tradition

title: Grace-sports: curing the king, granting children, restoring devotees
description: A cluster of miracle-sports in which Śiva heals the Pāṇḍya, grants heirs, and answers devotees' vows

title: Recitation of the Mahābhārata at the sacrifice
description: With the snakes spared, Vyāsa's pupil Vaiśampāyana narrates the entire Mahābhārata to Janamejaya at this very session, and Sauti later retells it at Naimiṣāraṇya

title: Disciplining rival sects / the Jain (Samaṇa) contests
description: Sports vindicating Śaivism against Jain (Samaṇa) opponents at Madurai, the sectarian-polemic layer of the cycle

title: The Dharma Daivas Appear at Birmanna Pergade's House
description: Four guardian spirits of Dharma test and are pleased by the Jain chieftain Birmanna Pergade's hospitality, then ask him in a dream to dedicate his home to their worship, founding Dharmasthala

title: Arjuna Returns Gandiva to the Waters
description: After Krishna's death, his powers gone, Arjuna casts Gandiva back into Varuna's waters on the final journey and ascends north toward Svarga

title: Birth of Hariharaputra (Shiva + Mohini)
description: After the Samudra Manthana, Vishnu reassumes the Mohini form for Shiva, and from their union the divine child Sasta/Ayyappa is born, deliberately to produce the being able to slay the demoness Mahishi
source: Brahmanda Purana, Bhutanatha Upakhyana; Bhagavata Purana 8; Keralan tradition

title: Mahishi's boon of unslayability
description: The buffalo-demoness Mahishi, sister of Mahishasura, does penance and Brahma grants that she can be killed only by a being born of both Vishnu and Shiva — the engine of Ayyappa's birth

title: The infant Ayyappa left on the Pampa
description: The divine child is left on the banks of the Pampa river with a golden bell at his neck, to be found and adopted as Manikandan by the childless King Rajashekhara of Pandalam

title: The tiger's-milk plot against Manikandan
description: Resentful of the favored foundling, the queen feigns an illness curable only by tigress's milk, sending Manikandan on a seemingly fatal forest errand

title: Ayyappa slays Mahishi
description: In the forest Manikandan confronts and kills the demoness Mahishi (often on the Azhutha river), fulfilling his cosmic mission; her death-dance is commemorated

title: Janamejaya's Snake-Sacrifice
description: Avenging his father Parikshit, killed by Takshaka, Janamejaya holds the sarpasatra, the occasion at which the Mahabharata is first recited by Vaishampayana

title: Ayyappa returns riding a tiger
description: Manikandan returns to Pandalam astride a tiger (Indra and the devas in tiger-forms), revealing his divinity and fulfilling the milk-errand

title: Kali Yuga begins (3102 BCE)
description: The Age of Strife begins at Krishna's departure with dharma on a single leg; chanting the divine name becomes the prescribed yuga-dharma

title: Founding of the Sabarimala shrine
description: Ayyappa shoots an arrow and ordains a temple be built where it lands — at Sabari, where the Ramayana ascetic Sabari awaited Rama — then merges into the deity-form

title: Onset of Kali Yuga, Parikṣit restrains personified Kali
description: Kali Yuga formally begins as Kṛṣṇa leaves the earth (traditionally 3102 BCE); Parikṣit confronts and restrains a personified Kali

title: Curse of Leela into demonic form
description: The celestial woman Leela is cursed to buffalo/demonic form (becoming Mahishi) after refusing to return to the divine realm with sage Dattatreya, and is freed upon her death at Ayyappa's hands

title: Parikṣit cursed to die in seven days
description: Parikṣit is cursed by the boy-brahmana Sṛṅgi to die in seven days by the snake Takṣaka, the dramatic engine for the rest of the Bhagavata

title: Malikappurathamma's deferred marriage proposal
description: The goddess Malikappurathamma wishes to marry Ayyappa, who replies he will wed her only when no first-time pilgrim comes to Sabarimala — forever deferring the marriage and preserving his celibacy

title: Suka teaches Parikṣit on the Ganga
description: Sukadeva Gosvami speaks the bulk of the Bhagavata to King Parikṣit on the bank of the Ganga during the seven days before his death

title: The great departure of the Pāṇḍavas
description: The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī walk toward Mount Meru and fall one by one; only Yudhiṣṭhira and a dog (Dharma in disguise) reach heaven's gate

title: Ayyappa defeats the bandit Udayanan
description: Aided by his companion Vavar and local forces, Ayyappa defeats the forest robber-chief Udayanan

title: Yudhiṣṭhira's heaven-test and ascension
description: Yudhiṣṭhira is tested by an illusion of his kin in hell/heaven, then reconciled, and the heroes attain their celestial states

title: Ugrashravas recites the Mahabharata to the Naimisha sages
description: The outermost frame of the Gita is Ugrashravas' recitation of the epic to the sages of the Naimisha forest, nesting Vaishampayana's and Sanjaya's reports within it

title: Future-dynasty prophecy
description: Suka foretells the post-Mahabharata kings (Magadha, Nanda, Maurya, Sunga, Andhra) down into Kali in the prophetic past tense

title: Death of Parikshit by Takshaka
description: King Parikshit fearlessly meets death by the serpent Takshaka's bite, closing the frame, followed by Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice

title: Manu's law-code narrated to the sages
description: The Manava-Dharmasastra (Laws of Manu) is narrated by Manu to the sages, codifying dharma, varna, and ashrama for the current age

title: The Pandavas' Great Departure (Mahaprasthana)
description: Hearing of Krishna's death, the Pandavas crown Parikshit and walk north toward the Himalayas, all dying on the way except Yudhishthira, who ascends to heaven with a dog who is Dharma in disguise

title: Kalki avatara ends Kali Yuga
description: Kali Yuga closes with the Kalki avatara, who destroys adharma and ushers in a new Satya Yuga, restarting the Mahayuga
source: Bhagavata Purana 12.2; Kalki Purana; Vishnu Purana 4.24

title: Śeṣa incarnates as Patañjali
description: Ādiśeṣa takes birth as the sage Patañjali, falling as a tiny serpent into the cupped hands of his mother Goṇikā, to witness Śiva's Tāṇḍava and honour him as first teacher of yoga

title: Buddha avatar deludes the asuras
description: Vishnu descends in ascetic Buddha form, in one reading to delude the asuras away from the Vedic path so the devas can defeat them, and in another to stop Vedic animal sacrifice out of compassion
source: Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24; Vishnu Purana 3.17-18; Gita Govinda

title: Jīmūtavāhana offers his body to Garuḍa
description: The compassionate Vidyādhara prince Jīmūtavāhana offers his own body to Garuḍa in place of a Nāga victim, halting Garuḍa's serpent-slaughter

title: Naravāhanadatta consecrated emperor of the Vidyādharas
description: The mortal-born prince Naravāhanadatta wins the vidyās and is consecrated Cakravartin emperor of the Vidyādharas across the Kathāsaritsāgara

title: Tulasī Vivāha — annual marriage of Tulsī to Viṣṇu
description: The ceremonial marriage of Tulsī to Viṣṇu/Śālagrāma is performed each year from Prabodhinī Ekādaśī to Kārttika Pūrṇimā, ending Cāturmāsya and opening the wedding season

title: Vaishampayana recites the Anugita to Janamejaya
description: The Anugita reaches the world as Vaishampayana's recitation to King Janamejaya at the snake-sacrifice, reporting the postwar exchange between Krishna and Arjuna

title: Caṇḍeśa made lord of the gaṇas' provisions
description: In the Nāyanār tradition the boy-saint Caṇḍeśa strikes his own father to defend Śiva-worship and is made steward and lord of the gaṇas' provisions

title: "Call your son to the table"
description: the Bhairava refuses to eat unless a child of the house joins him, so the mother goes to the door and calls Cīrāḷaṉ by name exactly as on any other day

title: "Elders full of Udayana tales"
description: Kālidāsa's Meghadūta finds at Avantī the village elders skilled in the tales of Udayana, proof the romance was already proverbial by the 4th–5th c. CE

title: "I will go tomorrow"
description: longing to see Naṭarāja at Chidambaram yet held back by awe and unworthiness, Nandanar keeps deferring the pilgrimage with "nāḷai-p-pōvēṉ," earning the name Tirunāḷaippōvār

title: "Kaṇikaṇṇaṉ pōha" — the rolled-up serpent-bed
description: banished for his disciple's sake, Tirumaḻiśai Āḻvār bids the reclining Lord of Tiruveḵkā roll up His snake-couch and follow, and Viṣṇu obeys, earning the epithet Yathoktakāri

title: "One of only two Sarasvatī temples"
description: Basara's fame rests on its rarity, styled the southern counterpart of Kashmir's Śāradā Pīṭha (or Śṛṅgerī's Śāradāmbā)

title: 'Adharaṃ Madhuram' — the sweetness refrain
description: Each of the eight stanzas closes on *madhurādhipater akhilaṃ madhuram*, 'everything about the Lord of Sweetness/Mathurā is sweet,' the hymn's fixed anaphoric device

title: 'Summā iru' — initiation into silence
description: Murugan silences the overwhelmed poet with 'Be still, beyond words', a wordless initiation memorialised in Kandar Anubhūti v. 4

title: Abhinanda's Laghu-Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha abridgement (c. 9th–10th c. CE)
description: The Kashmiri paṇḍit Abhinanda condenses the work to ~6,000 verses, the form in which it traveled most widely [scholarly]

title: Abhinavagupta completes the Tantrāloka and Tantrasāra
description: 37 āhnikas (~5,800 verses) synthesising Āgama, Spanda and Pratyabhijñā on the base of the Mālinīvijayottara, with his own prose digest (c. 950–1016 CE [scholarly])

title: Acchoda lake in Bāṇa's Kādambarī
description: Bāṇabhaṭṭa sets Mahāśvetā's hermitage on the luminous Acchoda lake, giving the Purāṇic clear-water lake a celebrated literary afterlife (7th c. CE) [scholarly]

title: Achyuta Menon edits the Ballads of North Malabar (1935)
description: C. Achyuta Menon collects and publishes the oral Vaṭakkan Pāṭṭukaḷ as Ballads of North Malabar (University of Madras, 2 vols.), the standard critical gathering that fixed the corpus's received shape

title: Ādi Śaṅkara organizes the Daśanāmī ekadaṇḍi order
description: the ten-named single-staff renunciate order with four cardinal maṭhas is traditionally founded (8th c. CE)

title: Adi Shankara Organizes the Greater Char Dham
description: Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) is traditionally credited with organizing the four pan-India abodes (Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram) into one pilgrimage to bind the subcontinent

title: Adi Shankara Renounces as a Boy at Kaladi
description: Born at Kaladi to an aged childless couple, the precocious Shankara renounces as a boy after a crocodile seizes his leg, forcing his mother's consent to sannyasa

title: Adoption by the Vaṇiya household
description: the Vaṇiya headman Muchilōṭṭu Paḍanāyar and his wife recognize her divinity and install her, making her the kuladevata of the oil-presser community
source: Muchilottu Bhagavathy thoṭṭam-pāṭṭu; Kannur kāvu tradition

title: Adoption of Dali Bai
description: Ramdev finds and adopts the Meghwal (Dalit) girl Dali Bai as his sister; she becomes his foremost devotee and the cult's anti-untouchability charter

title: Afzal Khan desecrates the shrine (1659 CE)
description: the Bijapur general raids Tuljapur before marching on Shivaji; the goddess assures victory, fulfilled at Pratapgad on 10 Nov 1659

title: Afzal Khan's raid on Tuljapur and Pratapgad (1659 CE)
description: the Bijapur general desecrates the Tuljapur shrine (the true mūrti hidden, in the devotional telling) and is killed at Pratapgad on 10 Nov 1659, read by tradition as Bhavānī's assured victory

title: Agama Hindu Bali wins state recognition; Parisada founded (1958–1959)
description: Balinese leaders codify Sang Hyang Widhi Wasa monotheism and the Panca Sradha to gain recognition under Pancasila, creating the Parisada Hindu Dharma council [scholarly]

title: Ahobila Maṭha founded
description: Ādivaṇ Śaṭhakopa Jīyar establishes the Vaḍakalai seat in 1398, initiated per tradition by Narasiṃha of Ahobilam himself [traditional]

title: Ajātaśatru's survey of the six heretical teachers
description: King Ajātaśatru of Magadha reports to the Buddha that he had previously questioned each of the six rival śramaṇa teachers (Pūraṇa Kassapa, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta, Ajita Kesakambali, Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta/Mahāvīra, Makkhali Gosāla) about the visible fruits of the ascetic life and found their answers unsatisfying — the canonical doxographic frame of the 6th–5th c. BCE heterodox field

title: Ajmal's plunge at Dwarka and Krishna's boon
description: the childless Ajmal Tanwar of Pokaran leaps into the sea at Dwarka and Krishna promises to be born in his house

title: Akṣara-abhyāsam at Basara
description: families across the southern Deccan bring toddlers to trace their first letters before Jñāna Sarasvatī, the regional form of the Vidyārambha saṃskāra

title: Akṣobhya Tīrtha's *tat tvam asi* debate at Mulbāgal
description: Madhva's direct disciple debates the Advaitin Vidyāraṇya with Vedānta Deśika as arbiter, the verdict-verse declaring Akṣobhya victor, 14th c. CE [traditional] [disputed]
source: Dvaita matha tradition; Sharma, History of the Dvaita School

title: Āḻvār bridal mysticism anticipates madhurya
description: Nammāḻvār's nāyakī-bhāva and Āṇḍāḷ's bridal poems pour devotion into Tamil akam love-conventions centuries before Rūpa (c. 7th–9th c. CE [scholarly])

title: Ambedkar burns the Manusmṛti (1927)
description: during the Mahad Satyāgraha B. R. Ambedkar publicly burns the code as the charter of caste hierarchy and untouchability, commemorated as Manusmṛti Dahan Din

title: Angkor turns Buddhist under Jayavarman VII
description: the Vaiṣṇava temple-mountain city is superseded by Mahāyāna Angkor Thom and the Bayon, and Angkor Wat itself becomes a Theravāda shrine

title: Angkor Wat built as Vishnuloka
description: Sūryavarman II raises the largest religious monument on earth, a moated Meru dedicated to Viṣṇu and named Parama-viṣṇuloka, in the Khmer capital Yaśodharapura

title: Appar's ordeals and the Pallava king's conversion (7th c. CE)
description: the ex-Jain monk Dharmasēna survives lime-kiln, poison, elephant and drowning, converting Mahendravarman I [scholarly]

title: Appayya Dīkṣita's 104 works
description: the 16th-c. Śaiva polymath of Adayapalam writes the Advaita doxography Siddhānta-leśa-saṅgraha, the Śiva-Advaita Śivārka-maṇi-dīpikā, and the poetics manual Kuvalayānanda under Cinna Bomma Nāyaka's patronage

title: Ārōmaluṇṇi avenges his father
description: Ārōmal's posthumous son, reared and drilled in the kaḷari by the Puttūram elders, grows into a champion and hunts down and kills the traitor Cāntu, redeeming the family's blood-debt

title: Aruṇagiri's ruin
description: a dissolute youth of Tiruvaṇṇāmalai squanders his family's wealth on courtesans and, diseased and destitute, is broken by shame at his sister Adhi's devotion

title: Aśvaghoṣa composes the earliest surviving mahākāvyas
description: the Buddhacarita and Saundarananda show ornate court epic already mature, c. 1st–2nd c. CE [scholarly]

title: Āyurveda adopts the Brahma-muhūrta rising rule
description: the dinacaryā chapters prescribe rising in Brahma-muhūrta 'to protect the life-span', classical Āyurvedic compendia c. 600 CE [scholarly]

title: Ayya Vaikundar inaugurates Ayyavazhi
description: After the 1833 Tiruchendur sea-bath tradition holds transformed him into the avatar-son of Nārāyaṇa, Vaikundar preaches caste equality and the coming Dharma Yukam from Swamithope, his teaching fixed in the Akilattirattu Ammanai (1841)
actors: Ayya Vaikundar; Hari Gopalan Citar; Swathi Thirunal of Travancore

title: Baitāl Pacīsī and the birth of literary Hindi
description: Ṣūrat Kabīshwar's Braj rendering (1719–49) is turned into Hindustani by Lallū Lāl under John Gilchrist in 1805, a foundational text of literary Hindi [scholarly]

title: Balarāma Dāsa composes the Odia Lakṣmī Purāṇa
description: the eldest of the Pañcasakhā writes the vrata-charter poem of Lakṣmī and Śriyā in early 16th-century Purī, a founding text of caste-critique bhakti [scholarly]
source: Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa; Odia literary histories

title: Balarāma Dāsa writes the Jagamohana (Daṇḍī) Rāmāyaṇa and Lakṣmī Purāṇa
description: the first Odia Rāmāyaṇa and the caste-critique poem chartering the Māṇabasā Gurubāra vrata, early 16th century CE [scholarly]

title: Bāmākhepā Born at Āṭlā
description: the future cremation-saint Bāmācaraṇ Caṭṭopādhyāy is born (1837) at midnight on Śivarātri in Āṭlā village, Birbhum, near Tārāpīṭha

title: Bāmākhepā's Cremation-Ground Sādhanā
description: under Kailāśpati Bābā, Bāmākhepā perfects yoga and Tantric practice living in Tārāpīṭha's mahāśmaśāna and 'sweetens' the fierce Ugra-Tārā into an intimate nursing Mother

title: Bāmākhepā's Samādhi (1911)
description: Bāmākhepā dies in 1911 and his samādhi is set within the Tārāpīṭha complex beside the burning-ground, making the pīṭha a living saint-shrine worshipped alongside Tārā

title: Bandhu Mohanty arrives too late
description: the poor devotee, having saved for years to offer bhoga, reaches Purī after the deities are put to rest for the night and sits weeping at the shut temple, his lifetime's hope undone

title: Basara temple attributed to a Deccan king
description: the built Jñāna Sarasvatī shrine is raised in the early-medieval centuries, traditionally by a Karnataka/Chalukya ruler named Bijjaḷa

title: Batu Caves dedicated to Murugan
description: the trader K. Thamboosamy Pillai develops the Kuala Lumpur cave-temple that becomes the global focus of Thaipūsam kāvaḍi, later crowned by a 42.7 m Murugan statue

title: Baṭuk Bhairav in Nepal and North India
description: the boy-form spreads as a Newar Kathmandu-Valley guardian and a North Indian household Bhairav Bābā, propitiated on Kālāṣṭamī and Bhairavāṣṭamī

title: Belanjong pillar erected at Sanur (914 CE)
description: earliest dated Balinese inscription, in Sanskrit and Old Balinese, attesting an Indic royal cult on Bali [scholarly]

title: Bengal Sati Regulation XVII abolishes satī (4 Dec 1829)
description: Governor-General Bentinck declares the burning or burying alive of widows culpable homicide after Rām Mohan Roy's campaign; the orthodox Privy Council appeal is dismissed in 1832 [scholarly]

title: Bhadrācala Rāmadāsu builds the Rāma temple and is imprisoned
description: The tahsildar Kancherla Gopanna builds the Bhadrāchalam Rāma temple with diverted revenue and, imprisoned ~12 years in Golconda fort, composes his anguished Rāma-kīrtanas; legend has Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa repay the sultan Tānīśā to free him
actors: Bhadrācala Rāmadāsu (Kancherla Gopanna); Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tānīśā)

title: Bhadravarman founds Bhadreśvara at My Son
