description: The commentator Kaundinya (4th–5th c.) writes the Pañcārtha-bhāṣya on the Pāśupata-sūtra, fixing the pati–paśu–pāśa triad inherited by all later Śaiva schools

title: Life as dāsī and the household-labor devotional idiom
description: Janābāī serves as maidservant in Nāmdev's home, turning menial chores (grinding, sweeping, gathering dung, fetching water) into continuous devotion and signing her verse 'Dāsī Janī'

title: Lorik and Candā love-and-war saga
description: The cowherd-hero Lorik and his beloved Candā/Mañjarī elope, go into exile and fight cattle-feuds and single combats, the great martial-romantic oral epic of the Ahīr/Yādav (and Gond) herding communities, sung as Lorikāyan in the Bhojpurī/Awadhī belt and as Canainī/Candainī in Chhattisgarh

title: Madhva calms the storm and claims the gopīcandana ballast
description: Madhva stills a storm off the Malpe coast and asks the rescued Dvārakā ship only for two lumps of sacred gopīcandana clay used as ballast

title: Manasollāsa treats metal images among royal arts
description: Someśvara III's Abhilaṣitārtha-cintāmaṇi (Mānasollāsa), a dated 12th-c. royal encyclopedia, sets out dhātu-pratimā proportions and ornament

title: Marriage of Mirabai to Bhojraj of Mewar
description: In 1516 Mira weds Bhojraj, crown prince of Mewar and son of Rana Sanga, marrying into the Sisodiya dynasty of Chittor

title: Nammalvar's sixteen years of silence under the tamarind
description: Nammalvar sits in padmasana in a hollow of a tamarind tree at the Adinatha temple for sixteen years, eyes closed in absorption, neither speaking nor eating

title: Nimbarka founds the Nimbarka Sampradaya
description: Nimbarka founds the Kumara/Nimbarka Sampradaya, propounds Dvaitadvaita, elevates Radha to full divine status worshipped inseparably with Krishna as the Yugala, and authors the Vedanta-parijata-saurabha

title: Nivṛttināth initiated by Gahinīnāth
description: The eldest sibling, separated from family near Brahmagiri/Tryambakeśvar, receives Nāth dīkṣā from Gahinīnāth, entering the line Gorakṣanātha → Gahinīnāth → Nivṛttināth

title: Pey Alvar First Sees Lakshmi Beside Vishnu
description: Pey Alvar, third of the Mudhal Alvars, is said to have first 'seen' Lakshmi beside Vishnu, recorded in his Munram Tiruvandhadhi

title: Pox-as-grace and neem cooling
description: Smallpox/chickenpox/cholera treated as the goddess's presence in the body, cooled with neem, turmeric and buttermilk rather than only medicated

title: Raising of the ~66 m vimāna and monolithic capstone
description: The ~216 ft Drāviḍa śrī-vimāna (Dakṣiṇa Meru) is built and crowned by a single-block capstone, by tradition hauled up a 6 km ramp from Sārapallam
actors: Chola masons and engineers under Rājarāja I
source: Chola inscriptions; Tamil Śaiva sthala folk tradition

title: Ramanuja breaks with Yadava Prakasha
description: Ramanuja first studies Advaita under Yadava Prakasha at Kanchi but breaks with him over the kapyasam scriptural-interpretation dispute, then aligns with the Yamuna line

title: Ravidas envisions Begampura
description: The Chamar sant-poet Ravidas of Varanasi sings his nirguna devotion and articulates the utopia of Begampura, an egalitarian city 'without sorrow or tax,' a great social image of the bhakti movement

title: Re-composition of the Ramakien under Rama I
description: After Ayutthaya-era versions were lost in the 1767 Burmese sack, King Rama I re-composes the standard Thai national Rama epic (1782-1809)
actors: King Rama I of the Chakri dynasty

title: Śrīpādarāja systematizes the Dāsa-kūṭa
description: Mulbāgal pontiff (c. 1422–1480) shapes the suḷādi form and composes under aṅkita 'Raṅga Viṭṭhala', first major systematizer of Dāsa-kūṭa song

title: Rukmiṇī withdraws to Diṇḍīrvan; Viṭṭhal follows
description: Angered, Rukmiṇī (Rakhumāī) withdraws to nearby Diṇḍīrvan and Viṭṭhal follows her to Pandharpur, explaining the two separate shrines in the temple complex

title: Sambandar's Pandya reconversion contest
description: Summoned by queen Maṅgaiyarkkaracī, Sambandar cures the Pandya king's fever, defeats the Jains in contests of fire and water, and reconverts the king and realm to Śaivism

title: Sangam Avvaiyār contributes to the anthologies
description: The earliest Avvaiyār, a Sangam-age court poet (c. 1st–3rd c. CE), composed akam/puṟam verses surviving in Puṟanāṉūṟu and other Eṭṭuttokai anthologies
source: Puṟanāṉūṟu; Eṭṭuttokai; Avvaiyar (Sangam poet) — Wikipedia; Sangam literature — Wikipedia

title: Sangili Karuppaṉ, the chained subform
description: Karuppu fans into named local subforms including Sangili Karuppaṉ, shown bound in chains because his power must be restrained

title: Shankara Initiated by Govinda Bhagavatpada
description: Journeying north, Shankara meets and is initiated by his guru Govinda Bhagavatpada on the banks of the Narmada, inheriting the proto-Advaita teaching of Gaudapada

title: Sharad Navaratri Shakta substrate
description: Gujarat's garba/dandiya sits on the pan-Hindu nine-night autumn worship of Durga/Amba and her victory over Mahishasura

title: Snana Yatra / Snana Purnima and the Anavasara seclusion
description: On Jyeshtha Purnima, Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are bathed on the Snana Bedi with 108 pots of scented water (Mahasnana) and given the elephant-form Gajavesha (Ganesha) darshan; afterward the deities ritually fall ill with fever (jvara) and enter the Anavasara/Anasara seclusion, treated with herbal remedies, reappearing at the Nava-yauvana/Netrotsava darshan just before the Rath Yatra
source: Wikipedia (Snana Yatra, Anavasara); Jagannath Temple Puri [traditional]

title: Sāriputta and Moggallāna leave Sañjaya for the Buddha
description: The two future chief disciples Sāriputta and Moggallāna, originally pupils of the skeptic teacher Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta, abandon his 'eel-wriggling' equivocation and join the Buddhist saṅgha

title: Svami Haridasa's life at Nidhivana
description: The rasika singer-saint Svami Haridasa (c.1480-1573, dates disputed), reckoned an incarnation of the sakhi Lalita, lives as an ascetic in Nidhivana and founds the Haridasi Sampradaya

title: The cruel mother-in-law and the stone-in-the-plate
description: Her harsh mother-in-law starves her, hiding a stone under a thin layer of rice, giving rise to a Kashmiri proverb of endurance

title: The destitute woman's single āmalaka
description: A desperately poor Brahmin woman, having nothing else, gives Śaṅkara her one possession — a single gooseberry (āmalaka)

title: The divine child found
description: Padikutty Amma finds a baby boy by the river and the couple raise the divine foundling as their son

title: The donkey-broom-winnowing-fan-water-pot dhyāna
description: The Śītalāṣṭaka fixes her iconography: she rides a donkey and carries a broom, winnowing-fan and cooling water-pot, often worshipped aniconically as a pot or stone under a neem tree

title: The famine and Tukārām's turn to devotion
description: A c. 1629 famine kills Tukārām's first wife Rakhumābāī and a son and ruins his trade, the collapse that turns the failing grocer toward total Viṭṭhal-devotion

title: The Five Siddhāntas
description: Five early-CE astronomical schools (Sūrya, Paitāmaha, Vāsiṣṭha, Romaka, Pauliśa) absorbing Greco-Babylonian geometry and the 12-sign zodiac into India

title: The forty-day prayer on the Indus
description: The despairing Sindhi Hindus fast and pray for forty days on the bank of the Indus to Varuna / the water-god for deliverance
source: Sindhi folk tradition; prototype of the Chaliho observance

title: The four-part dawn liturgy fixed
description: Annan arranges the morning service as four sequential texts — Suprabhatam (awakening), Stotram (praise), Prapatti (surrender), Mangalasasanam (benediction)

title: The Garland Legend (Sudikkodutta Nacciyar)
description: Kodai secretly wears the temple garlands as the Lord's bride; when Periyalvar withholds the 'polluted' offering, Vishnu appears in his dream declaring he prefers the worn garlands, earning her the epithet Sudikkodutta Nacciyar

title: The Kailasa author-legend
description: Legend that Shankara found the first 41 verses (Ananda-lahari) inscribed at Shiva's abode, had them snatched away by Nandin/Ganesha, and supplied the remaining 59 verses himself

title: The miracle of the two mangoes
description: Puṉitavati gives a mango to a Śiva-devotee, then miraculously produces a second mango by prayer to serve her husband

title: The Moovar Sing the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams
description: The Nayanar saint-poets Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar (6th-9th c. CE) compose the Tevaram, qualifying 275/276 Shiva temples as Paadal Petra Sthalams

title: The ṣoḍaśa-śṛṅgāra sixteen-adornment complex
description: Tradition fixes a sixteen-item maṅgala-śṛṅgāra of bridal/married adornment (bindī, sindūr, mehndi, āltā, ornaments) as the complete auspicious adorned state of a wife

title: The periphery guardian-shrine
description: Ayyaṉār is enshrined at the village edge (tank-bund, field-boundary, grove, cremation-fringe) facing outward, served by non-Brahman priests with animal offering

title: The rebuke and composition of the refrain
description: Śaṅkara sings 'bhaja govindam... nahi nahi rakṣati ḍukṛñ-karaṇe', warning that grammar cannot save one at death — only devotion to Govinda can

title: The rival twins Arjan and Surjan
description: The boon-sweet is shared with or seized by Bāchhal's co-sister Kāchhal, who bears the twins Arjan and Surjan, Gugga's cousins and lifelong rivals

title: The runaway bridegroom
description: At c. age 12, on hearing the priest's 'sāvadhān', he fled the wedding mandap and renounced household life

title: Traditional blindness of Sūrdās
description: Sūr remembered as blind (often from birth), the sightless poet who 'sees' Kṛṣṇa inwardly; scholars debate literal congenital blindness given his visual detail

title: Traditional discipleship under Rāmānanda
description: Ravidās is remembered, like Kabīr, as one of the disciples of Svāmī Rāmānanda of Vārāṇasī, a link doubted by scholars

title: Turn to Viṭṭhal and refusal of suitors
description: Renowned for her beauty, she refuses all men and fixes her heart on Viṭhobā of Pandharpur as her only lord

title: Vidyāraṇya replaces the Śāradā image with gold
description: Vidyāraṇya (Mādhava, 14th c. Śṛṅgerī pontiff) replaces Śaṅkara's original sandalwood Śāradā mūrti with the gold/pañcaloha image and is credited with rebuilding the Śāradāmbā temple in stone, alongside the Vidyāśaṅkara temple

title: Śaṅkara composes the Dvādaśa-mañjarikā
description: Śaṅkara expands the song into the twelve-verse 'twelve-blossom' core (Dvādaśa-mañjarikā Stotra) on renunciation, impermanence, satsaṅga, and surrender to Govinda

title: Śaṅkara composes the hymn to Lakṣmī
description: Moved by the woman's self-giving in poverty, Śaṅkara spontaneously praises Lakṣmī in ~18-21 verses, begging her mercy

title: Śaṅkara composes the Saundarya-laharī proper (vv. 42–100)
description: Śaṅkara completes the hymn with the head-to-foot (keśādi-pādānta) poetic adoration of the goddess's body, forming the 100-verse Saundarya-laharī

title: Śaṅkara mounts the Sarvajña-pīṭha at the Kashmir Śāradā shrine
description: In the dig-vijaya hagiography Śaṅkara ascends the Sarvajña-pīṭha ('seat of omniscience') at the Kashmir Śāradā Pīṭha, linking the northern learning-seat of the goddess to his southern Śṛṅgerī installation as the two poles of one Śāradā cult of letters

title: Andal Composes the Tiruppavai
description: Andal composes the 30-verse Tiruppavai, dramatizing the Margali pavai vow with herself as a gopi waking companions and the household of Krishna, the most-recited portion of the Prabandham

title: Aniconic and fierce-head iconography
description: Māri worshipped as plain stone, anthill, trident, pot under a neem tree, or as a fierce ground-level severed head, versus the seated red four-armed temple form

title: Ayyaṉār as lord of the bhūta-host
description: Ayyaṉār leads a retinue of attendant spirits and lieutenant guardians (Karuppu, Muṉīśvaraṉ, Maturai-Vīraṉ) at the village edge, mirroring the Purāṇic Bhūtanātha

title: Bhadrabāhu–Sthūlabhadra famine migration and the Digambara–Śvetāmbara split
description: Facing a twelve-year famine in Magadha, the elder Bhadrabāhu leads monks south to Karnataka (Śravaṇabeḷagoḷa); the monks who stayed north under Sthūlabhadra relaxed the nudity-rule and convened a council at Pāṭaliputra to fix the canon. The returning southern monks rejected both the clothed practice and the northern recension, the legendary seed of the Digambara/Śvetāmbara cleavage

title: Blood sacrifice and the buffalo-bali
description: The defining grāmadevatā offering is animal blood, above all the buffalo, re-enacting the goddess's slaying of a buffalo-demon

title: Bond with the chieftain Atiyamāṉ and the gooseberry boon
description: Avvaiyār served the chieftain Atiyamāṉ Neṭumāṉ Añci as poet, friend, and peace-envoy; he gave her a life-prolonging nelli (gooseberry) fruit, seeding her 'immortal old age' legend, and she mourned him in puṟam elegies

title: Bridal and festival mehndi (henna) custom
description: Henna paste is painted on hands and feet at weddings and festivals as an auspicious sign of saubhāgya, with folk beliefs on colour-depth and the hidden groom's name
source: Wikipedia Mehndi/Henna; wedding and festival custom

title: Composes the abhangas of caste-protest and surrender
description: Chokhamela composes his canonical abhangas including 'Us donga pari rasa nohe donga' (the cane is crooked but the juice is not), fusing protest at exclusion with total surrender to Vitthal

title: Composition of the Dvādaśa-mañjarikā core
description: Śaṅkara composes the twelve-blossom core verses on vairāgya, impermanence of wealth/body/kin, and satsaṅga leading to liberation

title: Composition of the Pāṇḍuraṅga-māhātmya
description: The Sanskrit sthala-purāṇa glorifying the Pandharpur kṣetra, the Candrabhāgā river, and the Puṇḍalīka legend is transmitted in Skanda and Padma Purāṇa recensions

title: Composition of the Rigveda
description: The Rigveda, oldest layer of the four Vedas with hymns to Agni, Indra, Soma, Varuna and Ushas, is composed c. 1500-1200 BCE (traditionally held eternal and authorless)

title: Composition of the Tirumantiram
description: Tirumūlar sings the ~3,000-verse Tirumantiram, canonized as the Tenth Tirumuṟai and the foundational Tamil scripture of Yoga and Tantra (scholarly c. 6th–10th c. CE)

title: Coomaraswamy's reading of the Face of Glory as Death-Time the All-Devourer
description: A. K. Coomaraswamy interprets the kīrtimukha mask as the iconic All-devourer, Death-and-Time (kāla), consumed-and-transcended at the deity's threshold, paralleling the Upaniṣadic Death-as-devourer theme

title: Dakshin Ray's claim over the forest
description: The tiger-demon Dakshin Ray claims the jungle as his domain and demands human flesh, rivaling Bonbibi's authority

title: Dattila composes the Dattilam
description: Dattila's concise gāndharva compendium restates śruti, svara, grāma, mūrcchanā, jāti and tāna alongside the Nāṭya Śāstra

title: Dayananda Saraswati founds the Arya Samaj
description: Swami Dayananda founds the Arya Samaj at Bombay on 10 April 1875, preaching return to the sole authority of the Vedas and pioneering the shuddhi reconversion rite, and authors the Satyarth Prakash

title: Deification of Kaṇṇaki as Paṭṭiṉi
description: Kaṇṇaki is deified as the goddess of chastity Paṭṭiṉi/Kaṇṇaki Amman, and King Ceṅkuṭṭuvaṉ builds her temple, founding the Paṭṭiṉi cult

title: Emergence of the Drāviḍa order with storeyed vimāna and towering gopurams
description: The South Indian pyramidal storeyed vimāna within concentric walled enclosures develops under Pallava, Cōḻa, Pāṇḍya and later dynasties, with gateway-gopurams eventually out-scaling the central shrine
source: Mānasāra; Mayamata; Wikipedia (Dravidian architecture, Vimana, Gopuram)

title: Flight to Pandharpur
description: She leaves Mangalveḍhā for Pandharpur, joins the Vārkarī devotees, and gives herself to kīrtana and dance before Viṭṭhal-Rukmiṇī

title: Founding of the Anubhava Mantapa
description: Basava founds the Anubhava Mantapa at Kalyana, a casteless 'first religious parliament' open to all and to women, presided over spiritually by Allama Prabhu on the Shunya-simhasana, becoming the crucible of the vachana corpus

title: Gangamma reveals her fierce form and slays the Pālegāḍu
description: Gangamma manifests her terrifying true form and kills the Pālegāḍu, the climactic act commemorated by the great clay form

title: Husband's awe and withdrawal
description: Awed and fearful at the vanishing divine mango, Paramatattaṉ withdraws, flees on a voyage, remarries, and names his daughter Puṉitavati in reverence

title: Initiation by guru Viṣobā Khecara
description: The Nāth-influenced teacher Viṣobā Khecara corrects Nāmdev's belief that the divine is confined to the Pandharpur image, teaching all-pervading formless presence

title: Installation of the giant monolithic Nandi
description: A single-granite-block Nandi (~25 t), one of India's largest, is set before the sanctum

title: Jhūlana Yātrā / Hindolā Utsava
description: The monsoon swing festival up to Śrāvaṇa Pūrṇimā, when Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are placed on flower-decked swings and rocked amid kīrtana, rooted in the Bhāgavata Vṛndāvana swing-līlā
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa Kṛṣṇa-līlā; Wikipedia (Jhulan Yatra/Hindola); ISKCON/Krishna.com; Puṣṭimārg sevā tradition

title: Kabir's trick-initiation by Ramananda
description: Kabir lies across the Panchganga ghat steps before dawn; Ramananda trips over him crying 'Ram! Ram!', and Kabir seizes that involuntary cry as his initiating mantra, proclaiming himself the saint's disciple

title: Kinnaur Kailāsh ~79-ft natural Śivaliṅga
description: A ~79-ft svayambhū rock-Śivaliṅga near the Kinnaur Kailāsh summit, held to change colour through the day and reached by an arduous parikramā, worshipped as Śiva's winter abode

title: Living regional floor-art forms diverge
description: The art differentiates into Rangoli, Kōlam (incl. pulli/sikku), Muggu, Ālpana, Maṇḍana and other named regional traditions with distinct media and grammars
source: Wikipedia: Rangoli, Kolam, Muggu, Alpana, Mandana [regional]

title: Madhūcchiṣṭa-vidhāna lost-wax single-pour casting
description: The sthapati models the icon in beeswax, invests it in clay, de-waxes by firing, casts solid in one continuous pour, then breaks the mould and chases the bronze
source: Sivaramamurti, South Indian Bronzes; Dehejia, Chola: Sacred Bronzes

title: Madhurakavi breaks Nammalvar's silence
description: Following a southern light to the tamarind tree, Madhurakavi poses a riddle and the boy's first-ever words answer it, declaring the soul's total dependence on God; Madhurakavi becomes his disciple on the spot

title: Manifestation (prakatya) of Banke Bihari
description: At Haridasa's song the divine pair Radha-Krishna appear and merge into the single dark tribhanga icon of Banke Bihari, self-manifested from the soil of Nidhivana

title: Marriage to Jaratkāru and birth of Āstīka
description: Manasā marries the sage Jaratkāru, who deserts her on the wedding night; she bears the sage Āstīka

title: Matsyendranāth receives the secret yoga
description: 9th–10th c. first human Nāth guru and Kaula founder overhears Śiva's hidden yoga; revered in Nepal as Avalokiteśvara/Karuṇāmaya (Red Matsyendranāth)

title: Maturai-Vīraṉ the warrior takes service under the Madurai king
description: The warrior of low/outcaste birth enters the service of the Madurai Nāyak king, who appoints him kāval-kāraṉ (watchman) of the city

title: Meeting and initiation by Vallabhācārya
description: Vallabha hears Sūr's self-pity songs, tells him to sing Kṛṣṇa's līlā instead, and initiates him into the Puṣṭimārga via Brahma-sambandha
source: Caurāsī Vaiṣṇavan kī Vārtā; Hawley; Wikipedia Surdas

title: Nabakalebara (renewal of Jagannath's wooden bodies)
description: Every 12-19 years, when an Adhika Ashadha falls, the wooden bodies of the Puri deities are ritually replaced and the Brahma-padartha soul-substance transferred in secret

title: Nivṛttināth initiates and guides Jñāneśvar
description: Nivṛttināth becomes his own brother's guru and commands Jñāneśvar to compose the Jñāneśvarī (1290), the founding text of Marathi spirituality

title: Ostracism as children of a renunciant
description: Orthodox Brāhmaṇas brand the children saṃnyāsī-putra, deny them the sacred thread and excommunicate the family

title: Parshvanatha, 23rd Tirthankara
description: Parshvanatha establishes the Jain path as the 23rd Tirthankara, traditionally c. 9th-8th c. BCE, the earliest ford-maker most scholars treat as plausibly historical

title: Pratisarga 'prophecy' of Adam, Noah, Moses
description: The interpolated Pratisarga Parva narrates a Genesis-derived cycle of Ādhama and Havyavatī, Nyūha (Noah) and the flood, and Mūsā (Moses) — an 18th–19th-c. fabrication

title: Rañjāvatī's ordeal and the birth of Lausen
description: Rañjāvatī, wife of Karṇasena of Maina, wins the boon of a son Lausen from Dharma Ṭhākur through extreme hook-swinging self-offering ordeal

title: Ramanuja Heads the Shri Sampradaya
description: Ramanuja (trad. 1017-1137) is appointed head acharya of the Lakshmi-founded Shri Sampradaya, crystallizing it into the Vishishtadvaita school of qualified non-dualism

title: Ramanuja systematizes Vishishtadvaita and reorganizes Srirangam
description: Ramanuja settles at Srirangam, reorganizes its Ranganatha temple worship, propounds prapatti as the supreme means to moksha, and writes the Shri Bhashya refuting Shankara sutra by sutra
source: Shri Bhashya; Vedartha Samgraha; Gadya Trayam

title: Śrīdhar's bhanḍārā
description: The brahmin devotee Śrīdhar holds a kanyā-pūjā feast at which the girl Vaiṣṇavī appears and miraculously feeds the whole assembly without the food running short

title: Recovery of the Kṛṣṇa icon from the gopīcandana
description: Washing the clay reveals Rukmiṇī's lost Bālagopāla icon, which Madhva carries to Udupi and installs (a Balarāma image is said to go to Malpe)

title: Renunciation and the wandering naked dancer
description: In her mid-20s Lallā abandons marriage and home, wandering as an ascetic, going about naked, dancing and singing her vākhs in God-intoxication

title: Restoration of the Jñāneśvarī text (c. 1584)
description: Eknāth collates and purifies the corrupted Jñāneśvarī, producing the standard reliable recension underlying the modern printed text; legend ties this to finding Jñāneśvar's Āḷandī samādhi

title: Rigveda Composed
description: Oldest Veda layer composed c. 1500-1200 BCE (scholarly); tradition holds the Vedas eternal and authorless

title: Sambandar raises Pūmpāvai from death
description: Sambandar raises the merchant's daughter Pūmpāvai from death by his hymn and is given a pearl palanquin, parasol and cymbals by Śiva

title: Self-manifestation of Devadamana on Govardhana
description: The raised arm of the icon emerges from Govardhana hill near Āniyor/Jatipura and reveals itself as the self-manifest Govardhana-dhāraṇa form

title: Self-naming colophon
description: The closing verses embed Tulsidas's poetic signature (tulasidasa sada hari cera) naming the author within the text

title: Shankara Recovers the Badrinath Image from the Alaknanda
description: Adi Shankara is said to have recovered the self-manifest black shaligram image of Badrinarayan from the Alaknanda river, establishing the northern dham

title: Siri and her four-generation line apotheosised
description: The Tuḷu goddess-heroine Siri suffers abandonment and is deified as a daiva, her saga continuing across four generations of women (Siri, Sonne, the twins Abbaga-Daraga); recorded by Lauri Honko as the ~15,000-line Siri epic and re-embodied annually at the Siri jātre mass group-possession of women
actors: Siri; Sonne; twins Abbaga and Daraga; (recorder Gopala Naika / Lauri Honko)
source: Siri-paddana; Lauri Honko, The Siri Epic as Performed by Gopala Naika

title: Sūrya Siddhānta
description: Cornerstone of Hindu mathematical astronomy revealed by Sūrya to Maya; planetary motions, Earth's sphericity, and the 4,320,000-year Mahāyuga synchronising all planets

title: Staging of the Cihna Yātrā
description: Śaṅkaradeva stages the Cihna Yātrā, the first theatrical/visual-art presentation of the movement and seed of aṅkīyā nāṭ drama

title: Surdas composes the Sursagar
description: The blind Braj-bhasha master Surdas, supreme of the Ashtachhap, composes the Sursagar 'Ocean of Sur,' a vast song-anthology on Krishna's childhood and youth

title: Śītalā-aṣṭamī / Basoda cold-food vrata
description: On Caitra (or regional Śrāvaṇa) aṣṭamī the hearth-fire is doused and only cold/stale Basoda food eaten and offered, enacting the cooling worship

title: Testing the saints with the thāpaṭṇe (potter's mallet)
description: Goroba taps each saint's head with his potter's mallet as one tests a pot for firing, declaring Nāmdev still 'unbaked' for lacking a living guru

title: The cousins' feud
description: Gugga and his cousins Arjan and Surjan quarrel over inheritance, cattle, or a slight to his bride, escalating into open war among the kinsmen

title: The curse of impotence on Bāpiyā
description: Dying by tragu, Bahucharā curses Bāpiyā with impotence and loss of manhood for assaulting a Cāraṇ woman

title: The Digvijaya (Conquest of the Directions)
description: Shankara undertakes a pan-Indian debate-tour, defeating and converting rival schools, reordering monastic life and establishing his pithas

title: The Gaṅgā-in-the-cobbler's-tub saying
description: Ravidās declines a Ganges pilgrimage with 'Man changā to kaṭhautī meṅ Gaṅgā', asserting inner purity over sacred geography

title: The 'Kausalya supraja Rama' opening verse
description: The hymn opens by addressing the Lord as Rama, son of Kausalya, transplanting the Ramayana dawn-waking of Rama onto Venkateshvara
actors: Annan; Venkateshvara identified with Rama; (echoing Vishvamitra and Rama)
source: Venkatesha Suprabhatam v.1; Valmiki Ramayana Bala-kanda

title: The voice from the river
description: A voice answers from the waters promising a deliverer will be born to Devaki, wife of Ratanchand Lohano, at Nasarpur

title: The wild hunter boy
description: The boy takes to non-Brahmanical ways — forest hunting with bow and arrow, toddy-drinking, and eating fish and meat

title: Tiruppan Alvar Carried into the Srirangam Sanctum
description: The low-born Panar bard saint Tiruppan Alvar is carried into the Srirangam sanctum and composes the Amalanadipiran, a head-to-foot vision of Ranganatha, emblem of bhakti transcending caste

title: Tukārām's dream-initiation by Bābājī Caitanya
description: Having no living guru, Tukārām receives dream-dīkṣā when a teacher named Bābājī Caitanya lays a hand on his head and gives the mantra 'Rām Kṛṣṇa Hari.'

title: Twelve years of austerity at Ṭākaḷī
description: Performed ~12 years of tapas (c. 1620–1632) on the Godāvarī at Ṭākaḷī near Nāśik, reciting the Rāma mantra 13 crore times

title: Vallabha founds the Pushtimarg
description: Vallabha founds the Pushtimarg 'Path of Grace' and systematizes Shuddhadvaita, teaching salvation by divine grace and sevA through Brahma-sambandha self-dedication to Krishna, and authors the Anubhashya and Subodhini

title: Vasugupta receives the Śiva-Sūtras
description: Śiva reveals the Śiva-Sūtras (77 aphorisms) to Vasugupta, inscribed on a rock at Mahādeva mountain, seeding Kashmir Śaivism and the Spanda doctrine
source: New World Encyclopedia, Kasmir Saivism; SUNY

title: Viṭṭhal helps Janī with her chores
description: Legend has Viṭhobā/Viṭṭhal himself descend to help Janī at the quern, sweep, gather cow-dung, comb her hair and bathe her, the Lord lowering himself to the servant-girl's labor

title: Vyāsatīrtha institutionalizes the Haridāsa movement
description: Dvaita dialectician and Vijayanagara rāja-guru (c. 1460–1539), bridges Vyāsa-kūṭa and Dāsa-kūṭa, mentors Purandara and Kanaka; signature 'Sirī Kṛṣṇa'

title: Wandering household
description: Economic hardship forces the family to move repeatedly through Maharashtra towns, framing her spiritual turn

title: Widowing of Mirabai
description: Bhojraj, wounded in battle c.1518, dies c.1521 before succeeding to the throne, leaving Mira widowed young and never reigning as queen

title: Xuanzang Records the Prayag Assembly under Harsha
description: The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang records a great bathing-and-almsgiving assembly at Prayag convened by King Harsha in 644 CE, often cited as the earliest historical witness to the Kumbh

title: Abhinavagupta receives the Kaula transmission
description: Abhinavagupta (c. 975–1025) receives the Kaula transmission from his guru Śambhunātha and fuses Krama's Kālī-core into a Kaula-Trika synthesis in the Tantrāloka

title: Alaktaka / āltā red lac foot-dye in literature and bridal rite
description: Lac-derived red dye paints the feet and hands, a kāvya beauty-convention and a Bengali/Odia bridal item leaving auspicious Lakṣmī-like footprints
source: Sanskrit kāvya; Mahābhārata Lākṣā-gṛha; Wikipedia Alta (dye)

title: All-India pilgrimage
description: Wandered the subcontinent on foot c. 1632–1644, concluding that dharma needed physical strength and organization

title: Andal Dreams Her Wedding to Vishnu (Varanam Ayiram)
description: In the Varanam Ayiram decad of the Nacciyar Tirumoli, Andal dreams her marriage to Vishnu in vivid ritual detail, the textual core of her dream-wedding identity

title: Annual Gangamma Jātara re-enacts the veṣams
description: The week-long Tirupati festival re-performs the goddess's disguises day by day, culminating in the colossal fierce clay form which is then broken
source: Tirupati festival tradition; Handelman/Krishnamurthy/Dawson and Flueckiger ethnography [regional/scholarly]

title: Basava's reform program and the ishtalinga
description: Basava abolishes caste in worship and table-fellowship, rejects temple-icon ritual and animal sacrifice, and gives every devotee regardless of birth or sex the ishtalinga to wear, making the body the temple

title: Battle of the 1760 Haridwar Kumbh
description: At the 1760 Haridwar Kumbh, competition over bathing primacy erupts into a deadly battle between Shaiva Gosains and Vaishnava Bairagis, leaving hundreds dead

title: Bhairavnāth's pursuit
description: The tantric yogī Bhairavnāth lusts after Vaiṣṇavī and demands marriage; she refuses and flees up the Trikūṭa mountain with him in pursuit

title: Bhasmāsura–Mohinī legend at Shrīkhaṇḍ Mahādev
description: The demon Bhasmāsura, granted a head-touch incineration boon, is tricked by Viṣṇu-as-Mohinī into laying his own hand on his head and burning to ash — localized at the ~5,155–5,227 m Shrīkhaṇḍ massif with its ~75-ft rock Śivaliṅga
source: Bhāgavata / Śiva-purāṇic Bhasmāsura cycle; Shrīkhaṇḍ sthala-purāṇa; Wikipedia (Shrikhand Mahadev)

title: Bhogar casts the Palani navapāṣāṇa Murugan image
description: The alchemist-Siddhar Bhogar is traditionally credited with casting the Palani Murugan mūrti from nine minerals/poisons (navapāṣāṇa)

title: Birth of Uderolal at Nasarpur
description: The child Uderolal is born at Nasarpur on the Indus amid marvels and hailed as the avatara of Varuna

title: Bāṅke Bihārī Jhūlana (Vṛndāvana)
description: At the Bāṅke Bihārī temple the veiled deity is brought to a golden hindolā (svarṇa-hindolā) for the jhūlana days, one of Braj's most thronged darśanas
source: Wikipedia (Banke Bihari Temple); Braj temple tradition

title: Brāhmaṇa-challenge and floating-stone miracles
description: Challenged by Brāhmaṇas who scorn an untouchable's worship, Ravidās produces the sacred thread from his chest and makes a stone float

title: Caste-transgressing acts of compassion
description: Eknāth defies caste norms by feeding untouchables at śrāddha, bathing a sick outcaste, and (in legend) pouring sacred Rāmeśvaram water down a dying donkey's throat, drawing orthodox censure

title: Codification of the temple threshold-ornament canon in the Śilpa/Āgama corpus
description: The Mānasāra, Mayamata and Śaiva/Vaikhānasa-Pāñcarātra Āgamas systematize the doorway, pillar and gateway ornament — kīrtimukha, makara-toraṇa, vyāla/yāḷi pillars, dvārapālas and gajalakṣmī lintels — as protective alaṅkāra distinct from cult-image iconometry, codifying older guild practice c. 5th–13th c. CE
source: Mānasāra; Mayamata; Śaiva/Vaikhānasa/Pāñcarātra Āgama dvāra-lakṣaṇa; T. A. Gopinatha Rao

title: Co-founding of Vārkarī kīrtana with Jñāneśvar
description: Nāmdev, contemporary and companion of Jñāneśvar, helps establish communal nāma-saṅkīrtana as the devotional engine of the Vārkarī movement

title: Composition of Later Vedic Corpus and Upanishads
description: The Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas plus Brahmanas, Aranyakas and principal Upanishads are composed c. 1200-500 BCE, shifting from sacrificial ritualism to Atman-Brahman metaphysics
source: Vedic corpus; Brihadaranyaka and Chandogya Upanishads

title: Composition of the Mahishasura Mardini Stotra
description: A medieval Devi hymn versifying the buffalo-demon slaying is composed, traditionally ascribed to Adi Shankara
actors: Adi Shankara (traditional attribution); disputed later medieval poet

title: Composition of the Saundarya-laharī as a Śrīvidyā work (text-critical)
description: By the text-critical clock the developed Tantric Saundarya-laharī, presupposing the mature Śrī Cakra system, is composed in the medieval Śrīvidyā efflorescence by a later author under Śaṅkara's name
actors: later Śrīvidyā author (disputed); attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara

title: Council of Valabhī redacts the Śvetāmbara Āgama canon
description: The Śvetāmbara Jain canon of Āgamas (the Aṅgas and allied texts) is redacted at the Council of Valabhī (c. 5th c. CE) as the surviving word descending from Mahāvīra's gaṇadharas; the Digambaras reject this, holding the original canon lost and revering instead the Ṣaṭkhaṇḍāgama
actors: Śvetāmbara saṅgha; (against) the Digambaras; Puṣpadanta & Bhūtabali (Ṣaṭkhaṇḍāgama authors)

title: Counted among the Aṣṭachāp under Viṭṭhalanātha
description: Sūr is reckoned greatest of the eight Aṣṭachāp poet-singers, organized into a singing collegium by Vallabha's son Viṭṭhalanātha

title: Daily dawn threshold-drawing as Lakṣmī-invitation
description: Women renew the rice-flour kōlam/muggu at dawn on the swept doorstep to invite Śrī-Lakṣmī, feed small creatures, and seal the home's boundary

title: Dandiya Rasa as Krishna's rasa-lila echo
description: The paired stick-dance dandiya is read as an echo of Krishna's rasa-lila with the gopis, tying the Goddess and Krishna threads into one festival
source: Bhagavata Purana 10.29-33; classical Tala/Danda rasa repertoire

title: Development of the Vesara hybrid order in the Deccan
description: The intermediate Deccan order fuses Nāgara and Drāviḍa — storeyed articulation pulled into a rounded, often stellate profile — under the Cālukyas, Rāṣṭrakūṭas and Hoysaḷas; its very name and definition remain disputed (geographic hybrid vs. apsidal/round-plan)
source: Wikipedia (Vesara, Badami Chalukya architecture); Vāstu Śāstra; Mānasāra

title: Dhona's bargain abandons Dukhe
description: Merchant Dhona, unable to gather honey, is promised wealth by Dakshin Ray in exchange for abandoning the poor boy Dukhe on the Kedokhali flats as a human offering

title: Disciples add the Caturdaśa-mañjarikā verses
description: Fourteen of Śaṅkara's disciples (trad. Padmapāda, Toṭaka, Hastāmalaka, Sureśvara, etc.) each contribute a verse, expanding the hymn

title: Disciples contribute the Caturdaśa-mañjarikā verses
description: Inspired by the master, fourteen disciples (traditionally Padmapāda, Toṭakācārya, Hastāmalaka, Sureśvara, et al.) each add a verse, forming the 'fourteen-blossom' set and the composite ~31-verse hymn

title: Establishment as flagship of the suprabhata genre
description: The hymn becomes the most famous and most-imitated awakening-hymn, the template for later suprabhatam compositions for other deities
actors: Sri Vaishnava tradition; later suprabhata composers

title: Founding of Ekaśaraṇa Dharma
description: Śaṅkaradeva founds the Ekaśaraṇa ('single refuge') monotheistic Kṛṣṇa/Nārāyaṇa devotion, structuring it around the cāri vastu (Nāma, Deva, Guru, Bhakat)

title: Gorakṣa rouses Matsyendra at Kadalī
description: Disciple Gorakṣa enters the enchanted women's kingdom of Kadalī in disguise and wakes his bewitched guru with the cry 'Cala Macchindra, Gorakh āyā!'

title: Hirapur Chausaṭh Yoginī Temple Built
description: The Bhauma-Kara queen Hīrādevī builds the small circular hypaethral Chausaṭh Yoginī temple at Hirapur c. 864 CE with 64 black-stone yoginī images and a central Kālī/Mahāmāyā shrine
source: ASI; Wikipedia: Chausath Yogini Temple, Hirapur

title: Initiation by Sed Bāyu / Siddha Śrīkaṇṭha
description: Lallā is initiated into Trika non-dualism by her guru Sed Bāyu (Siddha Śrīkaṇṭha), and in some vākhs surpasses her teacher

title: Jñāneśvar and the Jñāneśvarī
description: Jñāneśvar (c.1275–1296 CE) founds the Vārkarī poetic stream with the Marathi Jñāneśvarī Gītā-commentary, Haripāṭh and abhaṅgas, taking samādhi at Āḷandī

title: Kabir's double critique of Hindu and Islamic orthodoxy
description: Kabir delivers his iconoclastic teaching attacking idol-worship, pilgrimage, caste and the sacred thread on the Hindu side and the muezzin's call, namaz, hajj and circumcision on the Muslim side, declaring independence from both religions

title: Kaumudi Mahotsava — classical moonlight festival
description: The classical-period autumn full-moon festival of moonlight and revelry (kaumudi), the courtly observance-layer beneath the Puranic charters, surviving in the name Kaumudi Purnima
actors: Classical courts/cities; literary tradition (Kaumudi-mahotsava nataka attributed to Vijjika)
source: Kaumudi Mahotsava in classical Sanskrit sources [scholarly/disputed]

title: Koṭi and Cennaya martyred and deified as daivas
description: The Billava twin warrior-brothers Koṭi and Cennaya of medieval Tuḷu Nāḍu die fighting injustice and are deified as daivas/bhūtas, worshipped in Bhūta-Kōla possession ritual across coastal Karnataka with their own garaḍi shrines
source: Koṭi-Cennaya paddana; Koti and Chennaya — Wikipedia

title: Lakṣmī's reluctance over merit
description: In an expansion, Lakṣmī demurs that the woman lacks accumulated puṇya; Śaṅkara argues her last-gift act is supreme merit, moving the goddess to relent

title: Lausen makes the sun rise in the west
description: To prove Dharma's power, Lausen offers his own body and worships until the god makes the sun rise in the west, then restores him

title: Śālivāhana meets Īśā (Jesus)
description: King Śālivāhana is said to encounter in the Himalayas a teacher calling himself Īśā-putra, born of a virgin — a late Christian interpolation

title: Madhva founds the Krishna Matha and appoints eight disciples
description: Madhva enshrines Kṛṣṇa, digs the Madhva-sarovara, founds the Dvaita headquarters c. 1285 CE, and appoints eight sannyāsī disciples to worship in turn

title: Madhva Founds the Udupi Seat and Dvaita School
description: Madhva (1238-1317), held to be the third avatara of Vayu, heads the Brahma Sampradaya, founds the Udupi seat-cluster, and systematizes the realist Dvaita / Tattvavada doctrine

title: Maṇimēkalai renounces the world and gains the alms-bowl
description: Maṇimēkalai, daughter of Kōvalaṉ and Mādhavi, renounces the world for the Buddhist path and obtains the never-empty magic alms-bowl Amuta-curapi

title: Makkhali Gosala founds the Ajivika order (niyati-vada)
description: Makkhali Gosala leads the Ajivika ascetic movement teaching strict fatalism (niyati), and breaks with his former associate Mahavira

title: Mataṅga defines and names rāga in the Bṛhaddeśī
description: The Bṛhaddeśī gives the first surviving definition of rāga ('raṅjayati iti rāgaḥ'), shifting theory from jāti to rāga and formalizing the deśī melodic types and the mārga/deśī divide

title: Maturai-Vīraṉ's loves with Bommi and Vellaiyammāḷ
description: Maturai-Vīraṉ weds Bommi, a palace dancing-girl, and is bound to Vellaiyammāḷ; the scandalous affair turns the king against him

title: Milarepa Flies to the Kailāsa Summit
description: In the Bön/Buddhist legend the yogi Milarepa flies to the summit of Kailāsa on a sunbeam, winning the mountain for Buddhism through devotion rather than climbing

title: Mirabai defies widow-propriety and caste
description: Rejecting Rajput widow seclusion, Mira sings and dances publicly before Krishna's image and consorts with low-caste sadhus, the core scandal driving the persecution legends

title: Mucalinda Shelters the Buddha
description: The nāga Mucalinda coils seven times and spreads his hood to shelter the meditating Buddha from a seven-day storm

title: Muktābāī composes the Tāṭīce Abhaṅga
description: When the hurt Jñāneśvar shuts the door (tāṭī), the young Muktābāī coaxes him out with a celebrated abhaṅga-cycle teaching the bhakti ethic of forbearance

title: Nammalvar composes the Tiruvaymoli and his four works
description: Nammalvar composes his four Tamil works totaling 1,296 verses — the Tiruvaymoli, Tiruviruttam, Tiruvaciriyam and Periya Tiruvandhadhi — revered as the Tamil Veda equated with the four Vedas

title: Narsinh Mehta composes Vaishnava Jana To
description: The Adi Kavi of Gujarati, Narsinh Mehta, sings Krishna's rasa-lila and composes 'Vaishnava Jana To,' which became Gandhi's favorite bhajan and a near-anthem of the freedom movement

title: Nāmdev sent to complete his realization under Viṣobā Khecara
description: Stung by the 'unbaked' verdict, Nāmdev appeals to Viṭhobā, who confirms it and directs him to the living guru Viṣobā Khecara to be 'fired to completion'

title: Parents' self-sacrifice and the Paithan purification quest
description: Viṭṭhalapant and Rukmiṇībāī end their lives to lift the curse; the boys seek a śuddhi-patra from the pundits of Paithan

title: Possession and oracle cult
description: The goddess mounts chosen devotees who shake, dance and prophesy at the jātara, centred on possession and pot-carrying

title: Purandara Dāsa codifies Carnatic pedagogy
description: 'Father of Carnatic music' (c. 1484–1564) creates the graded piḷḷāri gītes and Māyāmāḷavagauḷa exercises and vast devaranāma under 'Purandara Viṭṭhala'

title: Raja Jagat Singh installs Raghunath as Kullu's sovereign
description: As penance for a curse, King Jagat Singh installed an idol of Raghunath (Rama) brought from Ayodhya as Kullu valley's true king and ruled as his regent, founding Kullu Dussehra

title: Ramakrishna's multi-path realization at Dakshineswar
description: The Dakshineswar Kali priest Ramakrishna attains experiential realization through multiple paths — Tantra, Vaishnava bhakti, Advaita, Islam and Christianity — grounding the doctrine that all religions lead to the same God

title: Ramanuja's exile to Melkote
description: Fleeing Chola Shaiva-aligned persecution, Ramanuja takes refuge at Melkote in the Hoysala Karnataka country, founding institutions there before returning to Srirangam

title: Rebuke and self-revelation as god
description: Rebuked for his caste-breaking habits, the boy reveals his true divine (cosmic) form, showing he is god, and the couple worship him

title: Reception as the foremost short Vedantic stotra
description: The Atma Shatkam becomes the most-quoted short Advaita hymn, chanted across mathas, Yoga schools and Vedanta movements with its Shivo'ham refrain set to music
source: Nirvana Shatkam recitation and commentary tradition

title: Release only through worship in female guise
description: The curse can be lifted only by worshipping Bahucharā in female guise; this clause becomes the charter for those who renounce or transcend male gender

title: Rāmānuja's flight to the Hoysaḷa country
description: Fleeing Cōḻa Śaiva persecution at Śrīraṅgam, Rāmānuja crosses into Karnataka for a ~12-year exile centered on Melkote (early–mid 12th c. CE)

title: Āryabhaṭa and the Āryabhaṭīya (499 CE)
description: Founding dated astronomical text giving π≈3.1416, sine tables, and the radical doctrine of Earth's axial rotation; midnight vs sunrise reckoning schools

title: Samayapuram temple cult
description: The largest Māriyammaṉ temple near Tiruchirappalli, with an unanointed clay-and-sand mūla-vigraha and mass Cittirai festivals

title: Sambandar merges into the jyoti at his wedding
description: At his own marriage at Nallūr-Perumaṇam, Sambandar prays and merges into the divine effulgence, taking the entire wedding party into Śiva

title: Sambandar Turns the Pandya King Back to Shaivism
description: The child-prodigy saint Tirugnana Sambandar, fed divine milk by Parvati, composes hymns that lead the Pandya king back to Shaivism from Jainism

title: Shankara Debates Mandana Mishra
description: Shankara challenges the Mimamsa ritualist Mandana Mishra at Mahishmati with his wife Ubhaya Bharati as umpire; Shankara prevails and Mandana takes sannyasa as Sureshvaracharya

title: Somānanda founds the Pratyabhijñā school
description: Early 10th c., Somānanda founds the Pratyabhijñā ('recognition') school with his Śiva-dṛṣṭi and teaches Utpaladeva

title: Svāmimalai/Thañjāvūr Viśvakarma sthapati lineages
description: Hereditary bronze-caster guilds of the Kāveri delta, tracing craft to Viśvakarman, transmit and still practise the pañca-loha lost-wax rite

title: Tansen, Akbar and Haridasa
description: Disputed tradition makes the Mughal court-musician Tansen a disciple of Haridasa, with Akbar coming incognito to hear him sing

title: The Bidar/Bedar sultan's summons to his harem
description: The Sultan of Bidar, hearing of her beauty, sends soldiers to bring her to his harem; she refuses the royal patronage

title: The calf legend
description: Bahiṇā's beloved calf collapses and dies in devotional rapture at a kīrtan and she falls near death in grief, a turning point into bhakti

title: The composing household sings abhangas
description: Chokhamela's Mahar household produces a roster of poet-saints: wife Soyarabai on bodily impurity and caste-pollution, son Karmamela's bitter abhangas questioning his untouchable birth, sister Nirmala, and brother-in-law Banka
source: Soyarabai/Karmamela/Banka/Nirmala abhanga corpus; Tharu & Lalita, Women Writing in India; Zelliot

title: The drowned manuscripts miracle
description: Ordered by Rāmeśvar Bhaṭṭ to destroy his poems, Tukārām sinks his manuscripts in the Indrāyaṇī and fasts 13 days, after which they float up intact, vindicating a Śūdra's right to scripture

title: The giant terracotta-horse votive offering
description: Potters (Kuyavar/Vēlar) make and consecrate avenues of enormous fired-clay horses (and elephants, bulls) as mounts pledged to Ayyaṉār in fulfilment of vows
source: Terracotta-horse cult lore; Tamil folk tradition

title: The great endowment inscriptions
description: Rājarāja I endows the temple with lands, gold, and ~400 devadāsīs and staff, recorded in one of India's most detailed economic inscriptions
actors: Rājarāja Chola I; temple personnel and devadāsīs

title: The slaying of the cousins
description: Gugga kills his rival cousins Arjan and Surjan in battle, carrying off their heads in the grimmest recensions

title: The stolen-necklace false accusation and deliverance
description: Janī is falsely accused of stealing the temple necklace and condemned to death, but Viṭṭhal intervenes to save his devotee and the charge dissolves

title: The vrata-kathā of the cold-food woman
description: In the standard tale a woman who kept Basoda is spared the fire/pox while a neighbour who cooked fresh and offended Śītalā is stricken until she submits
actors: Śītalā; the pious cold-food woman; the offending cooking woman

title: Twelve-year drought caused by the elder being passed over
description: Śaṃtanu's kingdom suffers a twelve-year drought because the rightful elder Devāpi was passed over for the throne, offending dharma so the gods withhold rain

title: Upanishads & Later Vedic Corpus
description: Brahmanas, Aranyakas and principal Upanishads c. 1200-500 BCE shift focus to Atman-Brahman metaphysics

title: Vallabha discovers and serves Shrinathji
description: Vallabha discovers and serves the self-manifest Shrinathji image — Krishna as a child lifting Mount Govardhana — on Govardhana hill in Braj, the central icon of the Pushtimarg

title: Vallabhācārya recognises and establishes Śrīnāthajī
description: c. 1493 CE Vallabhācārya encounters the deity on Govardhana, names him Śrī Nāthajī, builds the first shrine and institutes formal sevā

title: Vināyaka (Gaṇeśa) devotion and the Vināyagar Agaval
description: Avvaiyār composed the Vināyagar Agaval, an akaval-metre adoration of Vināyaka fusing bhakti with kuṇḍalinī-yoga imagery, central to Tamil Gaṇeśa worship

title: Worshipped as a goddess by her husband
description: Brought to her husband, Paramatattaṉ and his new family fall at Puṉitavati's feet, confirming he regards her as divine, not as wife

title: Śaṅkara composes the Dakṣiṇāmūrti Stotra
description: Ādi Śaṅkara hymns Dakṣiṇāmūrti as nirguṇa Brahman, with the mirror/world-as-reflection verse, making him the iṣṭa-deva of Advaita

title: Ambaji temple and the major centres
description: Ambaji (aniconic Sri Yantra shrine of Amba Mata) is the spiritual heart while Ahmedabad and Vadodara host stadium-scale garba/dandiya grounds

title: Apotheosis and the seat at Becharājī
description: Bahucharā is recognized as an āvataraṇa of the great Devī and her sthāna at Becharājī in Mehsāṇā becomes her great pilgrimage temple

title: Appar's healing and reconversion to Śaivism
description: After a Jain phase as Dharmasena, Appar is struck by incurable colic, returns to his sister Tilakavatiyār who applies sacred ash, is healed, and embraces Śaivism for life

title: Appar Survives the Shaiva Ordeals
description: Appar, converted to Jainism then back to Shaivism, survives ordeals of poison, an elephant and the sea, and establishes the sacred-ash (Tiruniru) devotion

title: Ayyaṉār flanked by Pūrṇā and Puṣkalā
description: In his married village form Ayyaṉār-Śāstā stands with twin consorts Pūrṇā (fullness) and Puṣkalā (abundance), the married iconography distinguishing him from the celibate Ayyappa
source: Tamil grāma-devatā tradition; Śāstā temple iconography

title: Bāṇagaṅgā arrow-river
description: Thirsty during the flight, Vaiṣṇavī shoots an arrow into the earth releasing a stream and washes her hair, creating the Bāṇagaṅgā waypoint

title: Bastar Dussehra instituted by the Bastar house
description: The Bastar ruling house instituted a ~75-day Dussehra honouring the guardian-goddess Danteshwari and clan goddess Maoli as a tribal-royal compact, with no Ravana-burning

title: Bhedaghat 81-Yoginī Temple Built
description: The Kalachuri king Yuvarāja II builds the largest Yoginī temple at Bhedaghat in the early 11th century with 81 cells following the Mūla-cakra scheme of 9 Mātṛkās each leading 8 yoginīs

title: Building of the medieval Daityasūdana temple and rim shrines
description: The visible Daityasūdana temple and rim-cluster of shrines (Kamalajā Devī, Rāma, Śiva, Hanumān) are built in the Yādava era and later

title: Caitanya and ISKCON propagation of the mahāmantra
description: Caitanya Mahāprabhu propagates the mantra as yuga-dharma saṅkīrtana and ISKCON later carries it worldwide as the most globally recognized Hindu chant

title: Caitanya Grafts the Gaudiya Line onto Madhva
description: Caitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534) and his Acintya-bheda-abheda theology are affiliated to the Brahma-Madhva line through Madhavendra Puri and Ishvara Puri, forming the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya Sampradaya

title: Chand Sadagar refuses Manasā's worship
description: The Śaiva merchant Chand Sadagar, protected by the Mahājñāna spell, refuses to worship the upstart goddess Manasā

title: Composition of Bhogar 7000
description: The seven-thousand-verse alchemical-yogic compendium Pōkar Ēḻāyiram on rasavāda, kāya-kalpa and Palani lore is ascribed to Bhogar

title: Composition of the Begampura hymn
description: Ravidās articulates Begampura, a utopian city without sorrow, rank, fear or taxation, the great anti-caste social vision of bhakti
source: Begampura hymn in Gurū Granth Sāhib; Gail Omvedt Seeking Begumpura

title: Composition of the Eknāthī Bhāgavata
description: Eknāth composes a Marathi ovī exposition of Skandha 11 (Uddhava-gītā) of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, partly at Vārāṇasī where pandits first oppose then honour it

title: Composition of the Kelimala and Siddhanta-ke-pad
description: Haridasa composes the Kelimala (Garland of Play, ~110 padas) and the Siddhanta-ke-pad (~18 doctrinal padas), the songbooks anchoring Haridasi dhrupad temple-music

title: Composition of the Kīrtana-ghoṣā
description: Śaṅkaradeva composes the Kīrtana-ghoṣā, his masterpiece of Assamese narrative Kṛṣṇa-verse for congregational singing and central scripture of Ekaśaraṇa

title: Composition of the Śītalāṣṭaka (Skanda Purāṇa)
description: The Eight Verses to Śītalā, framed as spoken by Śiva, become the core Sanskrit hymn fixing her form and promising protection from pox and fever

title: Composition of the Tukārām Gāthā
description: Tukārām composes the Tukārām Gāthā (c. 1632–1650), several thousand plain-Marathi abhaṅgas that become the culminating scripture of the Vārkarī canon

title: Composition of the vākhs (Lallā-vākyāni)
description: Lallā composes terse four-line vākhs teaching Trika Śiva-consciousness, kuṇḍalinī, the futility of ritual and the dissolving of Hindu-Muslim duality, founding the Kashmiri vernacular literary tradition

title: Confrontation with Mirkhshah
description: Jhulelal confronts Mirkhshah, manifests water and fire, and compels the tyrant to grant the Hindus freedom of worship

title: Construction of the Konārk stone-chariot temple
description: The Eastern Gaṅga king Narasiṃhadeva I builds the colossal chariot-temple of the Sun with twelve pairs of wheels and seven horses, c. 1241–1258 CE

title: Daily suprabhata-seva at Tirumala-Tirupati
description: The hymn becomes the first ritual service at brahma-muhurta in the Tirumala shrine, ceremonially waking the standing Lord each dawn

title: Death in the wall-collapse during corvee labour
description: Conscripted into corvee labour repairing a wall (told at Mangalvedhe), Chokhamela is killed when the wall collapses on the Mahar workers

title: Death of Kabir at Maghar and the body of flowers
description: Kabir deliberately dies at the inauspicious town of Maghar rather than Kashi; his quarreling Hindu and Muslim disciples lift the shroud to find the body vanished and only flowers, which they divide for cremation and burial

title: Death of Vallabha at Varanasi
description: Vallabha attains tirobhava at Varanasi in 1531, traditionally by entering the Ganga at Hanuman-ghat and vanishing in a flame

title: Departure and settling at Parassinikkadavu
description: Muthappan leaves the household and, by his arrow or wandering (and a sacred dog motif), comes to settle at Parassinikkadavu on the Valapattanam river where his madappura stands

title: Devāpi as purohita invokes Bṛhaspati and ends the drought
description: Serving as purohita for Śaṃtanu, the seer Devāpi Ārṣṭiṣeṇa propitiates Bṛhaspati and obtains rain, ending the twelve-year drought

title: Doddācārya installs Yoga Anjaneya on the Chinna-malai
description: The Śrī Vaiṣṇava ācārya Doddācārya consecrates/propitiates the meditative Yoga Anjaneya (Hanumān) on the small hill to guard the cooled Narasiṃha and the kṣetra
source: Śrī Vaiṣṇava sampradāya tradition; sthala tradition

title: Dukhe's cry and Bonbibi's rescue
description: As the tiger closes in, Dukhe cries out to Bonbibi, who hears him and sends Shah Jangali to defeat Dakshin Ray

title: Establishment of daily and weekly recitation tradition
description: The Chalisa enters living North-Indian practice as a daily, Tuesday/Saturday, and protective apotropaic recitation across the Hindu diaspora

title: Execution and apotheosis of Maturai-Vīraṉ
description: Condemned over the affair, Maturai-Vīraṉ is mutilated and executed; Bommi and Vellaiyammāḷ die with him, and the wronged hero is deified into a guardian-god whose worship the remorseful king institutes

title: Festival and vrata floor-art calendar
description: Elaborate designs mark Diwali, Mārgaḻi/Mārgaśīrṣa kōlam, Pongal/Saṅkrānti, Onam pookkalam, and Lakṣmī-pūjā/brata vows

title: First National Ayurveda Day
description: The Government of India designated Dhanteras as National Ayurveda Day, first observed 28 October 2016

title: Founding of the Baranagore Math
description: After Ramakrishna's death in 1886 his monastic disciples form the first Math at Baranagore, the seed of the Ramakrishna order

title: Founding of the Jānakī Mandir and the modern Sītā-cult
description: A Sītā image found at Janakpur in 1657 CE becomes the founding relic of the cult, enshrined in the Nau Lakhā Jānakī Mandir built 1910–11 CE, anchoring living Maithilī Janakī-bhakti
source: Temple history; Wikipedia (Janaki Mandir); regional Maithilī tradition

title: Gali Gopuram and hill-foot Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha temple built
description: The lower Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha temple and its towering open 'wind tower' (Gali Gopuram) are built and endowed under Vijayanagara-era and later patronage

title: Gorakṣanāth systematizes haṭha-yoga
description: Chief organizer of the order codifies haṭha-yoga, reputed author of the Gorakṣa-śataka, dating disputed across 9th–13th c

title: Gorakhnāth's penance and the Nāth seat at Girnar
description: Guru Gorakhnāth and the Kānphaṭa Nāth yogīs establish a primal seat on Girnar's peaks, co-opting Dattātreya into the lineage

title: Jayadeva's compassion reinterpretation
description: The Gita Govinda's Dashavatara-stotra recasts Buddha as the compassionate avatara who censures Vedic ritual and ends animal sacrifice out of mercy

title: Kanaka Dāsa, anti-caste poet-saint
description: Kuruba warrior-poet-saint (c. 1509–1609), author of Mohanataraṅgiṇī and Haribhaktisāra, the Uḍupi Kanakana Kiṇḍi legend; signature 'Kāginele Ādikeśava'

title: Kanakadāsa barred and the deity turns west
description: The low-caste saint Kanakadāsa, refused entry, sings from outside until Kṛṣṇa turns west and the back wall splits open so he can have darśana

title: Lakṣmīdhara writes the Saubhāgyavardhinī commentary
description: Lakṣmīdhara composes the influential Saubhāgyavardhinī commentary, reading the hymn through the Samaya (internal, right-hand) school against the Kaula reading and aligning it with orthodox Śaṅkara Śrīvidyā
source: Lakṣmīdhara, Saubhāgyavardhinī commentary on the Saundarya-laharī

title: Lausen's wars and the villain Mahāmada
description: Lausen, aided by the Ḍom hero Kālu, survives the plots of the minister Mahāmada and campaigns at Kāmrūp/Hākanda, establishing Dharma-pūjā

title: Madhvācārya, third descent of Vāyu
description: In Dvaita doctrine Vāyu descends a third time as Madhvācārya in the Kali Yuga to restore true dualist Vaiṣṇava Vedānta, completing the threefold avatāra after Hanumān and Bhīma
source: Madhva-vijaya of Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya; Mādhva exegesis of Ṛgveda 1.141

title: Mahavira, 24th Tirthankara, founds/reforms Jainism
description: Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara of the cycle, establishes the historical Jain order (c. 599-527 BCE by tradition), contemporary of the Buddha

title: Maṇimahesh Kailāsh and the unclimbed jewel-summit
description: The ~5,653 m Maṇimaheśvara peak above Maṇimahesh Lake in Chamba, never summited, bearing the 'jewel on Śiva's forehead', revered as Śiva's western-Himalayan abode
actors: Śiva as Maṇimaheśvara and Pārvatī as Maṇimaheśvarī
source: Wikipedia (Manimahesh Lake); Markaṇḍeya/Chamba Śaiva tradition; Skanda Purāṇa Himalayan khaṇḍa

title: Maruti (Hanumān) temple campaign
description: Installed Hanumān images and founded maṭhs (the eleven Akrā Mārutī and a wider network) as gymnasium-shrines across Maharashtra

title: Mass cross-dressing: men take the goddess's female veṣam
description: Men of Tirupati dress as women to take Gangamma's veṣam as a vow, ritually becoming the goddess and inverting everyday gender

title: Modern exposition and recitation tradition
description: Swāmī Cinmayānanda's 20th-c. commentary and M. S. Subbulakshmi's musical setting establish Bhaja Govindam as a staple of daily and congregational devotion

title: Modern revival through Cinmayānanda and musical settings
description: In the 20th century Swāmī Cinmayānanda's discourse-commentary and M. S. Subbulakshmi's sung rendition popularize Bhaja Govindam as a centerpiece of modern Vedānta and one of the most-quoted Advaita devotional poems
source: Swāmī Cinmayānanda, Bhaja Govindam (Central Chinmaya Mission Trust); recorded musical tradition

title: Muktābāī as guru to Cāṅgadeva
description: The aged occult-yogī Cāṅgadeva, humbled in the wall-riding contest and the blank 65-line letter, becomes disciple with the child Muktābāī as his guru; addressee of the Cāṅgadeva Pāsaṣṭī

title: Murugan and the hot-fruit/cold-fruit riddle
description: Murugan, disguised as a boy, humbles the proud poet Avvaiyār with the sutta-paḻam/sudāta-paḻam ('hot fruit or cold fruit') riddle, dramatizing wisdom bowing to grace

title: Nammalvar's ascent to Vaikuntha
description: After a brief life of about 35 years Nammalvar attains paramapada-prapti, ascending to Vaikuntha, commemorated annually as his apotheosis

title: Narahari Tīrtha reorganizes Śrīkūrmam as a Vaiṣṇava centre
description: The Madhva ascetic Narahari Tīrtha, regent of the Kaliṅga Gaṅga court, is tied by inscriptions to the temple's conversion from Śaiva to Vaiṣṇava worship in the late 13th c
source: Epigraphia Indica; South Indian Inscriptions; Dvaita tradition

title: Navaratri recitation tradition
description: The hymn enters living practice as a Navaratri/Durga Puja staple and a widely sung devotional piece

title: Nāmdev spreads Viṭṭhal-bhakti into the Punjab
description: The tailor-saint Nāmdev (c.1270–1350 CE) propagates the Pandharpur cult through abhaṅgas, 61 of which enter the Sikh Guru Granth Sāhib

title: Panini's Ashtadhyayi
description: Panini composes his Sanskrit grammar c. 5th-4th century BCE

title: Panini's Ashtadhyayi Composed
description: Panini composes the Ashtadhyayi, the foundational Sanskrit grammar, c. 5th-4th century BCE

title: Prayagwal Priests Rebrand the Magh Mela as Kumbh
description: In the mid-1800s the Prayagwal priests rebrand Prayag's annual Magh Mela as 'Kumbh' for socio-economic advantage, the name previously reserved for Haridwar

title: Prayer to shed beauty and become a pēy
description: Released from marriage, Puṉitavati prays to Śiva to strip her beauty and grant her the emaciated skeletal pēy form of a ghoul-attendant

title: 'Prophecy' of Mahāmada (Muhammad)
description: A polemical late insertion casts Muhammad as a piśāca/demon-incarnation whose followers are called musalmān

title: Punnainallur anthill foundation
description: The Thanjavur-area shrine said to arise when the goddess directed a devotee to an anthill image, a Sanskritized Māri seat

title: Queen Māyā Conceives the Buddha at Anavatapta
description: In Buddhist legend Queen Māyā conceives the Buddha at Mānasarovara (Anavatapta/Anotatta), the lake at the centre of the world

title: Ramaṇa Mahaṛṣi prizes and recites the Ribhu-Gītā
description: Bhagavān Śrī Ramaṇa Mahaṛṣi (1879–1950) singles out the Ribhu-Gītā as a supreme expression of Self-knowledge and has portions chanted daily at Sri Ramaṇāśramam, Tiruvaṇṇāmalai
source: Talks with Sri Ramana Maharshi; Ramaṇāśramam records

title: Recovery and re-consecration of the buried mūla-mūrti
description: Rāmānuja recovers the lost Celuvanārāyaṇa image from an anthill/thicket and re-founds regular worship at the ruined hill-temple

title: Śārṅgadeva composes the Saṅgīta-ratnākara
description: At the Yādava court of Devagiri the seven-chapter 'Ocean of Music' synthesizes svara, rāga, tāla, gamaka (nāda-brahman doctrine) authoritatively for both later Hindustani and Carnatic traditions, the last text common to both

title: Rājarāja I recovers and Nampi canonizes the Tirumurai
description: The lost early Śaiva hymns are rediscovered by Chola king Rājarāja I in a sealed Chidambaram chamber and arranged into the canon by Nampi Āṇṭār Nampi

title: Rāmprasād Sen opens Śākta-bhakti
description: Rāmprasād Sen (c. 1718–1775), Bengal's founding Śākta poet-saint, first addresses Kālī with tender intimacy as Mother in his Rāmprasādī Kālī-songs, reframing the fierce Goddess

title: Saundatti Yellammā cult and pan-Deccan identification
description: The Yellammā cult centers on the Saundatti hill shrine (Belagavi, Karnataka) with mass pilgrim jātre festivals; Reṇukā is identified with Yellammā, Ekvīrā, Māriyammaṉ, Padmākṣī and Aai as one pan-Deccan mother, and is the goddess of the contested jogtī/devadāsī dedication
source: Saundatti sthala tradition; grāmadevatā and ethnographic studies

title: Service as liturgical singer of Śrīnāthjī at Govardhan
description: Sūr serves as lead kīrtaniyā before Śrīnāthjī on Govardhan hill, his padas becoming the standing liturgical music of the Puṣṭimārga
source: Wikipedia Surdas; Grokipedia Shrinathji; Vraj Dwar

title: Shankara Enters King Amaruka's Corpse to Learn Kama
description: When Ubhaya Bharati questions the celibate Shankara on the art of love, he enters the corpse of the dead King Amaruka by parakaya-pravesha to learn the subject and win the debate

title: Siddhpur established as Matr-gaya, the mother-shraddha tirtha
description: Siddhpur's Bindu-sarovara becomes the foremost site for matr-shraddha (rites to the mother/maternal line), paired with Gaya for the father, with the medieval town developed under the Solankis

title: Standardization of the Burmese Yama Zatdaw
description: Myanmar's Rama epic is standardized under Konbaung-dynasty patronage in the 18th century, shaped by court contact with Thai Ayutthaya after 1767

title: Surrender and cry to Viṭṭhal as sole refuge
description: Pressed by the king's men, she comes before the image of Viṭṭhal and cries that the god alone is her refuge and protector

title: Teppotsavam / Float Festival (genre)
description: The South-Indian Āgama tank-procession in which the utsava-mūrti is rowed on an illuminated raft around the temple tank over several evenings, spanning both Vaiṣṇava and Śaiva temples
source: Vaikhānasa/Pāñcarātra Āgama utsava-repertoire; Wikipedia (Float Festival, Teppakulam)

title: Textual systematization of the tripartite classification in the śilpa/vāstu and Purāṇa corpus
description: Treatises and Purāṇa building-chapters codify the threefold Nāgara/Drāviḍa/Vesara scheme as a divinely-ordained typology, with the Bṛhat Saṃhitā giving an early pre-classification witness and the Agni and Matsya Purāṇas preserving prāsāda-types and the mythic architect-lineage
actors: Varāhamihira; Bhuvanadeva; Purāṇic compilers; Viśvakarmā and the eighteen vāstu-teachers (mythic)
source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā; Mānasāra; Mayamata; Aparājitapṛcchā; Sthāpatyaveda; Agni Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa

title: The buffalo reciting the Veda
description: Challenged at Paithan, the boy Jñāneśvar makes a water-buffalo recite the Ṛgveda, refuting Brahmin monopoly over scripture

title: The child trampled in the clay-pit during kīrtana
description: Absorbed in kīrtana while treading clay, Gorā fails to notice his infant child in the pit and tramples it, the measure of his total God-absorption

title: The cup of poison turned to nectar
description: The Rana sends Mira a cup of poison disguised as prasad; she drinks it as Krishna's gift and is unharmed, the poison turning to nectar

title: The Haralayya-Madhuvarasa inter-caste marriage crisis
description: A marriage between the son of the untouchable Sharana Haralayya and the daughter of the Brahmin Sharana Madhuvarasa enrages the orthodox; Bijjala orders the fathers blinded and executed, triggering Sharana unrest

title: The mother's repudiation
description: Grief-stricken Bāchhal rejects the kinslayer Gugga, bars him from the city, and wishes the earth would swallow him

title: The rain of golden āmalakas (kanaka-dhārā)
description: Pleased by the hymn, Lakṣmī showers golden gooseberry fruit — a stream of gold — into the woman's home, ending her poverty

title: The revolving-temple miracle
description: Barred as a low-caste man, Nāmdev sings from behind a shrine (often Auṇḍhā Nāgnāth) and the temple revolves to face him, dramatizing bhakti overriding caste

title: The Seven Sisters pattern
description: Village mothers cluster as seven sister-goddesses (saptakannimār / yedugurakkalu), later equated with the Purāṇic Sapta-Mātṛkā
source: Whitehead; Sapta-Mātṛkā village-mother studies; Devī-Māhātmya overlay

title: The Tenkalai-Vadakalai split
description: The Shri Sampradaya fractures by the late 14th c. into the Vadakalai (Vedanta Deshika, monkey-analogy effortful grace) and Tenkalai (Manavala Mamunigal, cat-analogy causeless grace) sub-sects over how prapatti and grace operate

title: The tilaka/sindūr painted-mark complex
description: Forehead tilaka/bindī, parting-sindūr and patra-lekhā tracery form the kindred painted marks of Viśeṣaka-cchedya, linked to Pārvatī, Sītā and Sāvitrī

title: The Twin Dream-Command to Bring Andal to Srirangam
description: Ranganatha appears in dreams to both Periyalvar and the Srirangam priests, commanding that Andal be brought in bridal attire to be wed to him

title: Tulsidas composes the Ramcharitmanas
description: Tulsidas composes the Ramcharitmanas in seven kandas in 1574-77, begun at Ayodhya on Rama-Navami, a devotional Awadhi retelling of the Ramayana that becomes the basis of the Ramlila and the 'Bible of north India.'

title: Tēvāram recovery and Tirumurai codification
description: Rājarāja I with Nambiyāṇḍār Nambi is said to recover the lost Tēvāram hymns from Chidambaram and codify them into the Tirumurai

title: Utpaladeva systematizes Pratyabhijñā
description: Utpaladeva (c. 925–975) systematizes the recognition philosophy in the Īśvara-pratyabhijñā-kārikā

title: Utsava-mūrti vs mūla-bera distinction
description: Portable festival bronze (utsava/kautuka-bera) is cast in metal to leave the sanctum and process, distinct from the fixed stone mūla/dhruva icon, by Vaikhānasa measure

title: Vaikuntha Ekadashi / Adhyayana Utsava (Paramapada Vasal opening)
description: On Mokshada/Vaikuntha Ekadashi in Margazhi, the Paramapada Vasal (gate of Vaikuntha) is opened at Srirangam, Tirupati and other Divya Desams within the 20-day Adhyayana Utsava — Pagal Pathu (ten days) and Ra Pathu (ten nights) of reciting the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, climaxing in the Iyarpa Sattrumurai and Nammalvar Moksham, the temple enactment of the heaven's-gate liberation myth
source: Wikipedia (Vaikuntha Ekadashi, Adhyayana Utsavam); Srirangam Temple [traditional/scholarly]

title: Varāhamihira
description: Sixth-century synthesiser whose Pañcasiddhāntikā summarises the five Siddhāntas and whose Bṛhat Saṃhitā and Bṛhat Jātaka anchor the saṃhitā and horā branches

title: Viṭṭhalanātha systematises the sevā
description: Gusāīṃjī (1515–1585) codifies the eightfold aṣṭa-yāma darśana, the Aṣṭachāp kīrtana and divides the deities among his seven sons (Sāt Gharānā)

title: Vijayanagara–Nāyaka building of the standing temple
description: The monumental Bhū-Varāha-svāmī temple with its carved ratha-maṇḍapa is founded and endowed under Vijayanagara and Tanjore/Senji Nāyaka patronage in the 16th c. CE
source: South Indian Inscriptions; ASI records; Wikipedia, Bhuvarahaswamy Temple Srimushnam

title: Vision and dream-dīkṣā from Tukārām
description: She receives a vision of the Śūdra sant Tukārām, who gives the mantra and accepts her as disciple, mirroring his own dream-initiation

title: Witness to the founding Vārkarī circle and Jñāneśvar's samādhi
description: Hagiographic strands place Janī within the circle of Nāmdev and Jñāneśvar, connecting her to foundational events such as Jñāneśvar's sañjīvana samādhi at Āḷandī (1296)

title: Worship in the guardian-cluster
description: Sudalaimāḍaṉ is worshipped alongside Karuppasāmi, Muṉiyāṇṭi and others as a kāval-deyvam attending a presiding goddess such as Māriyammaṉ

title: Abhinavagupta unifies the Kashmiri streams
description: Abhinavagupta (c. 950–1016) reconciles the Āgama, Spanda and Pratyabhijñā streams into a unified non-dualism in the Tantrāloka and other works

title: Akbar/Tānsen legend
description: Popular but disputed legend has Emperor Akbar or Tānsen seek out the blind singer; treated as later hagiography, not documented

title: Andal Merges into Ranganatha (Goda-Kalyanam)
description: Borne to Srirangam as a bride, Andal ascends to Ranganatha's couch and merges bodily into the deity in a burst of light, a paradigm of jiva-Brahman union

title: Appar survives the ordeals under Mahendravarman I
description: Appar survives a lime kiln, poison, a maddened elephant and being cast into the sea bound to a stone, convincing the Pallava king Mahendravarman I to reconvert to Śaivism

title: Assassination of Bijjala and the Kalyana dispersal
description: The marriage-crisis repression provokes Bijjala's assassination c.1167 and the violent scattering of the Kalyana Sharanas, who flee to Ulavi carrying the vachana manuscripts that preserve the movement

title: Aurangzeb's Braj temple destruction
description: Aurangzeb's 1670 demolition of the Mathurā Keśavadeva temple endangers the Govardhana deity, prompting its removal

title: Bhāskara I
description: Earliest commentator on Āryabhaṭa, author of Mahābhāskarīya and a rational sine approximation, and an early user of positional decimal notation with zero

title: Blood-sacrifice and possession at the jātara
description: Fierce-goddess buffalo-style blood offerings and possession (āveśam) channel Gangamma's presence, contrasting the vegetarian Agamic worship of Veṅkaṭeśvara

title: Bāmākhepā perfects Tantric sādhanā at Tārāpīṭha
description: Bāmākhepā (1837–1911) perfects yoga and Tantric sādhanā in the Tārāpīṭha cremation ground, becomes its spiritual head and 'sweetens' the terrifying Tārā into an intimate Mother

title: Cōḻa Naṭarāja bronze perfected
description: The Cōḻa atelier perfects the Ānanda-Tāṇḍava dancing-Śiva bronze, the supreme cast icon of the tradition

title: Caurangī / Pūraṇ Bhagat restored and perfected
description: The maimed prince of the Pūraṇ Bhagat legend is healed and perfected by Matsyendra/Gorakṣa, becoming the Nāth/Mahāsiddha Caurangī

title: Charaṇ Pādukā footprints
description: Vaiṣṇavī pauses to look back at Bhairavnāth, leaving her footprints imprinted on the rock at Charaṇ Pādukā

title: Civavākkiyar's iconoclastic songs
description: Civavākkiyar composes the Civavākkiyam, attacking caste, idolatry and ritual and insisting on the formless inner Śiva

title: Codification of the Dharma-gājan, ghaṭ and ordeal rites
description: The Dharma-pūjā/gājan festival with ghaṭ-sthāpana, vow-taking bhaktas, hook-swinging and fire-walking ordeals becomes the cult's central rite

title: Companionship and grief at Jñāneśvar's samādhi
description: Nāmdev tours pilgrimage sites with Jñāneśvar and composes verses memorializing Jñāneśvar's sañjīvana samādhi at Āḷandī (1296)

title: Compilation of the Bijak
description: The eastern Banaras branch compiles the Bijak ('seed/map of hidden treasure') in the 17th century as the holy scripture of the Kabir Panth, organizing Kabir's verse into Ramaini, Shabad and Sakhi

title: Composition of ~300+ abhaṅgas preserved in the Sakal Sant Gāthā
description: Janābāī composes some 300 or more abhaṅgas—grinding-songs, intimate Viṭhobā verses and verses about the sants—preserved in the Vārkarī Abhaṅga-gāthā / Sakal Sant Gāthā
source: Marathi abhaṅgas; Sakal Sant Gāthā; Wikipedia (Janabai)

title: Composition of the Bhāvārtha Rāmāyaṇa
description: Eknāth writes a devotional Marathi Rāmāyaṇa, leaving it incomplete at the Yuddha-kāṇḍa; his disciple Gāvbā completes it

title: Composition of the Jñāneśvarī
description: On Nivṛttināth's command Jñāneśvar dictates the ~9,000-ovī Marathi commentary-paraphrase of the Bhagavad Gītā in 1290

title: Construction of the Lingarāja temple
description: The mature Kaliṅga-architecture temple is built c. mid-11th c. CE under Somavaṃśī (Keśarī) patronage, later elaborated by the Eastern Gaṅgas
source: Madala Pañji; epigraphy and architectural history

title: Conversion and descent into the earth
description: When the ground refuses to open for a Hindu, Gugga takes the kalmā/becomes a pīr so the earth receives him, and he and his blue mare are swallowed alive into pātāla

title: Conversion of Hoysaḷa king Biṭṭideva to Viṣṇuvardhana
description: Rāmānuja converts the Hoysaḷa ruler Biṭṭideva from Jainism, who is restyled Viṣṇuvardhana and patronizes Melkote

title: Cross-border Mithilā pilgrimage circuit
description: Janakpur anchors a Nepal–Bihar Rāmāyaṇa circuit linking Dhanushadham, Jaleshwar, Sitamarhi and Punaura-dhām, walked at Vivāha Pañcamī, Rāma Navamī and Sītā Navamī, with the furrow birth-spot disputed between Janakpur and Sitamarhi
source: Pilgrimage tradition; Wikipedia (Janakpur, Mithila region); regional Sitamarhi/Punaura-dhām counterclaim

title: Death at the temple, choosing the god over the king
description: At the feet of Viṭṭhal she gives up her life in the temple rather than be carried to the sultan's harem

title: Ādi Śaṅkara institutes the South-Indian Bhaṭṭa priesthood
description: Ādi Śaṅkara is held to have reformed worship at Paśupati and decreed that only Dravida (southern) Brahmins serve as mūl-bhaṭṭa

title: Eastern Ganga construction of the Śrīkūrmam temple
description: The standing stone complex with its dual dhwaja-stambhas and pillared maṇḍapa is built in Kaliṅga style (13th–14th c.) with later Gajapati, Reddi and Vijayanagara additions
source: Wikipedia Srikurmam Temple; ASI; South Indian Inscriptions

title: Eastern Ganga construction of the stone temple
description: The standing Kaliṅga-style stone complex is built/rebuilt under Eastern Ganga king Narasiṃhadeva I (c. 1238–1264 CE) over an older Cōḷa-period core

title: Eknāth restores the Jñāneśvarī
description: Eknāth (c.1533–1599 CE) of Paiṭhaṇ produces a critical text of the Jñāneśvarī and composes the Eknāthī Bhāgavata and Rukmiṇī-svayamvara

title: Establishment of the Madurai Veeran temple cult
description: Maturai-Vīraṉ gains a firmly established temple following, his image flanked by Bommi and Vellaiyammāḷ and set as guardian at temple gateways across the Tamil south, worshipped alongside Karuppasāmi

title: First Organized Prayag Kumbh (1870)
description: The recognizably modern, administered Kumbh at Allahabad is held in 1870 under British supervision

title: Floor-art read as folk-yantra / maṇḍala geometry
description: The dot-grid kōlam and cauk are interpreted as the household counterpart of priestly yantra/maṇḍala, sharing bindu-centred bounded symmetric grammar and motifs (svastika, padma, śatkoṇa)

title: Foundation of the Banke Bihari temple (1864)
description: The Haridasi Goswamis build the present Banke Bihari Mandir in Vrindavana in 1864 CE, moving the icon from Nidhivana; it becomes the most-visited temple of Braj

title: Founding the Rāmdāsī Sampradāya
description: Established a non-Vārkarī order centred on Rāma and Hanumān, fusing practical Advaita Vedānta with civic activism and 'Mahārāṣṭra dharma'/swarājya

title: Gautama Buddha founds Buddhism
