description: Siddhartha Gautama, a Magadhan shramana, teaches anatman and rejects Vedic authority, founding Buddhism (6th-5th c. BCE)

title: Historical incorporation of Buddha into the avatar canon
description: By c. 8th c. CE Buddha is added as a Vishnu-avatara across several Puranas as a Brahmanical theological response subordinating Buddhism
source: Agni Purana 49, Garuda Purana 1.86, Padma Purana, Varaha Purana; Adivaraha inscription (7th c.)

title: Husband's opposition and the bhakti-vs-strīdharma conflict
description: Her discipleship to a Śūdra guru brings caste scandal and her husband's rage and threats; she holds wifely duty and devotion in unresolved tension rather than renouncing the household

title: Islamization of the Hikayat Seri Rama
description: The Malay prose Rama story is reframed within an Islamic cosmological frame (Allah, prophet-hierarchy) roughly 1300-1700 CE, one of the oldest Malay literary works

title: Jnaneshwar composes the Jnaneshwari and takes living samadhi
description: The Varkari founding luminary Jnaneshwar composes the Jnaneshwari Marathi paraphrase of the Bhagavad Gita in 1290, then dies at 21 by living sanjivana samadhi at Alandi

title: Karaikkal Ammaiyar Becomes a Ghoul-Attendant at Shiva's Dance
description: The earliest Nayanar renounces her beauty to become a skeletal pey (ghoul) attendant at Shiva's dance, composing some 143 verses

title: Later Dāsa-kūṭa revival
description: 18th-c. revival under Vijaya Dāsa, Gopāla Dāsa, and Jagannātha Dāsa (Harikathāmṛtasāra), extending the Haridāsa corpus

title: Madhva rejects Advaita and founds Dvaita
description: Initiated young under the Advaitin Acyutapreksha, Madhva rejects Advaita and launches Tattvavada (Dvaita), teaching the pancha-bheda five eternal distinctions and authoring the 37 Sarvamula granthas
source: Brahma Sutra Bhashya; Anuvyakhyana; Sarvamula granthas

title: Madurai Mariamman Teppakulam
description: The Vandiyur temple tank at Madurai with its float-festival, a Māri tank-cult beside the Mīnākṣī complex

title: Madurai Meenakshi Teppam
description: Mīnākṣī and Sundareśwara are floated on a raft around the central island of the Vāṇḍiyūr Teppakkuḷam on the Thai full moon, tied to the birth-anniversary of 17th-c. ruler Tirumalai Nāyak who dug the tank
source: Wikipedia (Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam, Meenakshi Temple); Madurai temple calendar

title: Mahavira and Buddha
description: Mahavira (Jainism) and Gautama Buddha flourish c. 6th-5th c. BCE, challenging Vedic ritual and caste

title: Maṇimahesh Yātrā (Chhaḍī procession, Janmāṣṭamī–Rādhāṣṭamī)
description: The major annual pilgrimage from Hadsar via Dhancho to Maṇimahesh Lake, climaxing in a holy dip when the sacred Chhaḍī mace procession from Bharmour/Chamba arrives during the Janmāṣṭamī-to-Rādhāṣṭamī fortnight
source: Wikipedia (Manimahesh Lake); Chamba Śaiva living tradition

title: Manasā destroys Chand's fortune and six sons
description: Manasā wrecks Chand's garden, fleet and friend and kills his six elder sons to break his resistance

title: Mediation by Bara Khan Gazi and partition of the forest
description: Dakshin Ray takes refuge with the pir Bara Khan Gazi; Bonbibi spares him, accepts him as a son, and partitions the forest's bounty rather than seizing it

title: Mitaoli Ekattarso Mahadeva Temple Built
description: The 64-celled circular Ekattarso Mahadeva yoginī temple is built at Mitaoli c. 1323 CE, often cited as inspiration for the Indian Parliament's circular plan

title: Mīrābāī remembered as Ravidās's disciple
description: The Rajput princess-saint Mīrābāī is traditionally tied to Ravidās as her guru, a boundary-crossing memory scholars treat as later accretion

title: M. S. Subbulakshmi's 1963 recording
description: M. S. Subbulakshmi records the canonical popular rendition for the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams, fixing the hymn's cadence in modern practice
actors: M. S. Subbulakshmi; Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams

title: Namdev recovers the chanting bones
description: Namdev identifies Chokhamela's remains in the rubble because his bones still chant 'Vitthal, Vitthal', confirming his sanctity past death

title: Nathamuni recovers the lost Divya Prabandham
description: Nathamuni recites Madhurakavi's eleven verses 12,000 times at Alvartirunagari until Nammalvar appears in yogic vision and reveals the entire 4,000 hymns with their music and esoteric meaning, which he institutes as the Dravida Veda

title: Nāthamuni recovers the Divya Prabandham
description: By legend Nāthamuni recovers the lost 4,000 Āḻvār verses through yogic meditation on Nammāḻvār, compiling the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham

title: Origin of Govardhana Pūjā and the Annakūṭa festival
description: The līlā becomes the charter for the Kārttika Śukla Pratipadā festival of Govardhana Pūjā / Annakūṭa, the Govardhana parikramā, and Giri-rāja / Śrī Nāthjī worship
source: Festival and sectarian tradition (Vallabha Puṣṭimārga; Braj practice)

title: Pilgrimage to Kailāsa walking on her head
description: She journeys to Mount Kailāsa, climbing on her hands/head downward in humility to avoid treading on the sacred mountain

title: Poturāju the buffalo-king escorts the mothers
description: The fierce male guardian-brother Poturāju escorts, controls and executes for the seven mother-goddesses, presiding over the buffalo-sacrifice

title: Prabhupada Founds ISKCON as 32nd Link
description: Prabhupada founds ISKCON (1966), reckoning himself the 32nd link in the Brahma-Madhva-Gaudiya parampara counted from Krishna

title: 'Prophecies' of Mughals, Timur, and the British
description: The Pratisarga Parva 'foretells' the Mughals, Timur, Akbar, Nādir Shāh, the English, Calcutta, and Queen Victoria — fabricated retrojections dating the layer to the 18th–19th c

title: Reconciliation of Mirkhshah (variant)
description: In a variant Jhulelal converts Mirkhshah's heart rather than destroying him, teaching one Lord under different names

title: Restoration of the child and the vow of stillness
description: In devotional variants Viṭhobā's grace restores the child to life, or Gorā vows never to tread clay again until the Lord intervenes

title: Rise of the Sixteen Mahajanapadas
description: Sixteen kingdoms and oligarchies arise c. 600-321 BCE with cities, coinage and the ascendancy of Magadha during the second urbanization

title: Rāmāmātya introduces the mela in the Svaramelakalānidhi
description: At Vijayanagara, Rāmāmātya's Svaramelakalānidhi introduces the mela parent-scale as a classifying device, seeding the melakarta system

title: Sealing of the jagamohana (1903)
description: After the main deul/śikhara collapsed and worship lapsed, the British fill and seal the surviving porch with sand in 1903 to prevent its fall

title: Sekkizhar Composes the Periya Puranam
description: Sekkizhar composes the Periya Puranam (12th c., the 12th Tirumurai), the hagiography of all 63 Nayanars narrating their temple-visits as miracle events

title: Shankara Establishes the Four Amnaya Pithas
description: Shankara installs four cardinal mathas (Shringeri, Puri, Dvaraka, Jyotirmatha), each with a Veda, mahavakya and first head, and reorganizes renunciants into the Dashanami order

title: Sibling Great Living Chola Temples
description: Rājendra Chola I extends the programme with the Gangaikoṇḍa Cholapuram Bṛhadīśvara and Airāvateśvara at Darasuram, forming the UNESCO triad
source: Chola inscriptions; UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples

title: Singraur excavations — the archaeological site
description: The site survives as the excavated mound at Singraur; ASI/B. B. Lal (1977–1986) exposed a brick water-tank/hydraulic complex of the Śuṅga–Kuṣāṇa horizon, part of the Archaeology of the Rāmāyaṇa Sites project
source: B. B. Lal, Excavations at Sringaverapura / Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites

title: Sopāndev's samādhi at Saswad
description: The third sibling, the abhaṅga-poet 'Sopān-kākā', takes samādhi at Saswad shortly after Jñāneśvar in 1296; his shrine anchors a Pandharpur pālkhī

title: Sureśvara's Mānasollāsa vārttika
description: Sureśvara (traditionally Maṇḍana Miśra) composes the authoritative Advaita commentary on Śaṅkara's Stotra

title: Systematisation of the Pañcha Sabhai fivefold set
description: Medieval Tamil Śaiva-Siddhānta tradition assembles the five long-independent dance-halls into a single canonical set modelled on Chidambaram's golden hall
source: Tamil Śaiva tradition; sthala-purāṇas of the five temples; Tirumantiram/Tēvāram milieu

title: Tamil rendering and English condensation circulated
description: The text spreads via a Tamil verse rendering and a widely-circulating ~122-verse English condensation (N. R. Krishnamoorthi Aiyer's Essence of Ribhu Gita) plus a complete SAT translation
source: Tamiḻ Ṛbhu-Gītai; The Essence of Ribhu Gita; SAT complete translation

title: Textual systematization of vastu
description: The science is set down in datable treatises — Varahamihira's Brihat Samhita (~6th c.), Mayamata, Manasara, and Bhoja's Samarangana Sutradhara (11th c.) — plus Puranic vastu chapters
source: Brihat Samhita; Mayamata; Manasara; Samarangana Sutradhara; Matsya, Agni & Garuda Puranas

title: The basket with the serpent
description: Mira is sent a covered basket said to hold a venomous snake but on opening it finds a garland of flowers or a Krishna image, the snake transformed

title: The Bengali Śītalā-maṅgal force-my-worship cycle
description: Maṅgal-kāvya poets (incl. Kṛṣṇarām Dās, 17th c.) narrate Śītalā compelling an unwilling king/merchant to worship her by visiting smallpox on his realm
actors: Śītalā; the resisting king/merchant; Bengali maṅgal poets

title: The borgeet fire and the 34 survivors
description: A fire destroys Śaṅkaradeva's 240 borgeet manuscripts; only ~34 are recovered from memory, after which, grieved, he stops composing and asks Madhavadeva to continue the genre

title: The didactic primers — Ātticcūṭi, Koṉṟai Vēntaṉ, Mūturai, Nalvaḻi
description: The medieval (Chola-era) Avvaiyār composed the alphabetic moral primers Ātticcūṭi and Koṉṟai Vēntaṉ and the verse counsels Mūturai (Vākkuṇṭa Ammai) and Nalvaḻi/Naṉneṟi — the foundational moral first-readers of Tamil schooling
source: Ātticcūṭi; Koṉṟai Vēntaṉ; Mūturai; Nalvaḻi; Auvaiyar — Wikipedia

title: The Girnar (Lili) Parikramā established
description: The annual ~36 km forest circumambulation of the massif runs from Kārttika Ekādaśī to Pūrṇimā, gathering pilgrims and sādhus through the Gir forest

title: The Kanakana Kindi becomes the principal darśana point
description: The small west-wall navagraha window named for Kanaka becomes the main mukha-darśana aperture, so every pilgrim sees Kṛṣṇa as the saint did

title: The kodai festival and possession
description: The annual kodai festival climaxes with the god descending into a cāmiyāṭi medium who dances, gives oracles and blesses devotees, with blood sacrifice and paḍaiyal offerings
source: Sudalaimāḍaṉ kodai festival tradition; Tamil possession-worship tradition

title: The Nund Rishi link
description: Tradition holds the infant Nund Rishi, founder of the Kashmiri Rishi Sufi order, was suckled or blessed by Lallā, symbolizing her bridging of both communities

title: The swapped head-and-body etiology
description: In folk variants Reṇukā's head is rejoined to an outcaste woman's body, producing the split high-caste/low-caste goddess linking Reṇukā to Mātaṅgī/Māriyammaṉ

title: The twelve Āḻvārs sing Śrīraṅgam
description: All twelve Āḻvārs glorify the shrine in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham, the only Divya Desam so sung

title: Thrissur Pooram founded by Sakthan Thampuran
description: Around 1796 Raja Rama Varma 'Sakthan Thampuran' of Cochin organized ten temples around Vadakkunnathan into the unified Thrissur Pooram after smaller temples were barred from the Aarattupuzha Pooram

title: Tukārām's bodily ascent to Vaikuṇṭha
description: At his end (1649/1650) Tukārām tells Avalī he is going to Vaikuṇṭha and is taken bodily in a radiant chariot before a crowd, leaving no corpse

title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage inscription (2023)
description: 'Garba of Gujarat' is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2023, recognizing one of the world's largest religious dance festivals

title: Variant: the tree-shrine revelation
description: In a parallel sthala-legend the goddess reveals herself at an aniconic seat under a sacred tree discovered by a devotee, coexisting with the tragu legend

title: Vikramaditya's Reign and the Vikrama Samvat Epoch
description: The legendary cakravartin Vikramaditya reigns at Ujjayini with his court of nine gems including Kalidasa, and the Vikrama Samvat era (57 BCE) is founded counting from his reign

title: Vitthalanatha forms the Ashtachhap
description: Vallabha's son Vitthalanatha completes his father's works, organizes temple seva and forms the Ashtachhap, the eight poet-saints (four his, four Vallabha's) whose Braj-bhasha songs become the sect's liturgical music

title: Vivekananda's Chicago address
description: Vivekananda delivers the 'Sisters and Brothers of America' address at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in September 1893, introducing Vedanta and Yoga to the West

title: Yatōktakāri Obeys Tirumaḻicai Āḻvār
description: The reclining Viṣṇu at Tiru-Veḷḷakkuḷam rises and leaves (then returns) at the command of Tirumaḻicai Āḻvār, becoming Yatōktakāri, 'he who did exactly as told'

title: Adi Śaṅkara recovers the image and re-establishes Badrinath
description: In the 8th c. CE Adi Śaṅkara recovers the Badrī mūrti from the Nārada-kuṇḍa, revives the temple as the northern pole of his pan-India Char Dhām, and sets the Nambūdiri Rāwal priesthood

title: Ajivikas receive Mauryan patronage (Barabar caves)
description: Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha dedicate the Barabar and Nagarjuni rock-cut caves to Ajivika ascetics, the school's main epigraphic footprint

title: Śaṅkara's commentary
description: Ādi Śaṅkara composes the standard Viṣṇu-sahasranāma-bhāṣya, reading the names as praise of the one non-dual Brahman

title: Śaṅkara's Taittirīya-bhāṣya
description: Ādi Śaṅkara (c. 8th c. CE) composes a full Advaita commentary on the Taittirīya, fixing the standard reading of the Brahman-definition, pañca-kośa and Bhṛgu inquiry

title: Aśokan and later rock-edicts at Girnar's foot
description: A boulder at Girnar's base carries Aśoka's fourteen Major Rock Edicts plus the Rudradāman and Skandagupta Sudarśana-lake inscriptions — the secular historical clock

title: Bhartṛhari renounces Ujjain
description: King Bhartṛhari abandons his throne and queen Piṅgalā to become a Nāth yogī, subject of north-Indian Jogī ballads

title: Bhartrhari Renounces the Ujjain Throne
description: The poet-king Bhartrhari, disillusioned by the tale of the immortality-fruit passed between king, queen and lover, renounces the Ujjain throne to become a yogin and compose the Shatakatraya

title: Bonalu and jātara festival complex
description: Telangana women carry decorated pots of cooked rice to the village mothers in Āṣāḍha amid drumming, possession and Poturāju's procession
source: Bonalu festival ethnography; Medaram jātara studies

title: Brahmagupta and the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta (628 CE)
description: First text to treat zero and negatives as numbers; carried the decimal system to Baghdad as the Zīj al-Sindhind; rejected Āryabhaṭa's rotating Earth

title: Building of the Jānakī Mandir
description: The discovered Sītā image (1657 CE) is enshrined and the great Nau Lakhā Jānakī Mandir is built in 1910-11 CE by Queen Vrishabhanu Kunwari, anchoring the modern cult

title: Building of the west-facing temple and Kiraṇotsava alignment
description: The medieval Cālukya/Śilāhāra stone temple is built with the west-facing svayambhū mūrti and a solar alignment that admits the setting sun onto the Goddess thrice yearly (Kiraṇotsava)
source: Wikipedia: Mahalaxmi Temple, Kolhapur; temple administration

title: Buta Malik's discovery of the cave
description: A shepherd given coals that turned to gold returns to find the cave and ice-liṅga, re-popularizing the shrine

title: Cēkkiḻār composes the Periya Purāṇam
description: In 1135 CE Cēkkiḻār composes the Periya Purāṇam, the hagiography of all 63 Nāyaṉārs, under Chola Kulottuṅga II

title: Composition of the Amṛtānubhava
description: Jñāneśvar writes an independent non-dual philosophical work expounding cidvilāsa and the unity of Śiva and Śakti

title: Composition of the autobiographical Abhaṅga-gāthā / Ātmanivedana
description: She composes a first-person abhaṅga cycle narrating her own life and inner struggle, a landmark of pre-modern Indian women's self-writing and a primary witness to Tukārām's circle
source: Feldhaus, Bahina Bai: A Translation of Her Autobiography and Verses; Tharu & Lalita

title: Composition of the Rukmiṇī Svayaṃvara
description: Eknāth composes a Marathi narrative poem on Kṛṣṇa winning and wedding Rukmiṇī, drawn from the Bhāgavata

title: Composition of the Sūr Sāgar
description: Sūr's vast Braj Kṛṣṇa-song anthology (Ocean of Sūr); small attested early core grew by centuries of accretion under his open signature

title: Death of Basava at Kudalasangama
description: Having withdrawn to Kudalasangama amid the crisis, Basava dies there, traditionally described as merging into the linga

title: Death of Ravidās
description: Ravidās dies c. 1520 CE (traditional) after a life as cobbler-saint of Vārāṇasī

title: Dense inscriptional endowments and Vijayanagara patronage
description: Hundreds of inscriptions record endowments by Eastern Ganga, Kakatiya, Reddi, Gajapati and Vijayanagara rulers, including Kṛṣṇadevarāya after his Kaliṅga campaign

title: Ādi Śaṅkara's Śrīśaila sojourn and the Śivānanda-laharī
description: Tradition holds Ādi Śaṅkara visited Śrīśaila, composed the Śivānanda-laharī before Mallikārjuna, and survived a Kāpālika seeking his head

title: Diaspora spread of the cult
description: Tamil emigration carries Sudalaimāḍaṉ shrines, kodai and firewalking observances into Malaysia, Singapore, Sri Lanka and beyond

title: Disputed guru association with Śivājī
description: Traditional accounts make Rāmdās the guru/rājguru of Chhatrapati Śivājī; modern historians regard the relationship as late and exaggerated

title: Double veneration as Lalleśvarī and Lal ʿĀrifa
description: Lallā is revered simultaneously by Hindus as Lalleśvarī / Lallā Yogīśvarī and by Muslims/Sufis as Lal ʿĀrifa / Lal Ded, becoming the great bridge between Trika Śaivism and Kashmiri Sufism
actors: Lallā; Kashmiri Hindu and Muslim communities

title: Dukhe enriched and worship established
description: Bonbibi sends Dukhe home laden with wealth and restores him to his mother, establishing her worship among the forest people

title: Enactment of Nammalvar's Vaikuntha-ascent at Srirangam
description: During the Adhyayana Utsava at Srirangam the full Tiruvaymoli is recited and Nammalvar's image is taken through the Paramapada Vasal into the sanctum, dramatically staging his liberation before the assembled devotees

title: Establishment of the daily all-caste cult
description: The non-Brahmanical, all-caste-and-faith Parassinikkadavu cult is established with daily theyyam performance, toddy/fish/meat offerings, and the trademark fish-curry-and-boiled-gram prasāda
source: Parassinikkadavu Muthappan temple lore; Kerala theyyam folklore

title: Firewalking, karagam and neem-vow festivals
description: Signature Māri rites — coal-bed firewalking (tīmiti), karagam pot-dance, neem-skirt vows and body-piercing austerities that 'cool' the goddess

title: Founding/glorification of the Koṇārka Sun Temple
description: The Brahma Purāṇa describes the great Sun Temple of Koṇārka (built 1241 CE) and its pilgrimage merit, a key dating anchor

title: Founding of the pādukā-pālkhī procession
description: In 1685 Tukārām's youngest son Nārāyaṇ Mahārāj begins the pādukā-pālkhī custom, carrying the saint's sandals in a palanquin from Dehu to Pandharpur

title: Garbha Joon / Ardh Kuwārī womb-cave
description: Vaiṣṇavī meditates nine months inside the narrow Garbha Joon cave at Ardh Kuwārī, then tears open its far end to emerge as Bhairavnāth nears

title: Gorakhnāth's penance and the Nāth siddha-seat
description: Guru Gorakṣanātha does penance on a Girnar summit, establishing it as a primal Nāth/Kānphaṭa yogī seat (9th-13th c. CE historical layer)

title: Household and the poet-maidservant Janābāī
description: The maidservant Janābāī lives in Nāmdev's household and becomes a celebrated abhaṅga-poet, repeatedly naming Nāmā in her verse

title: Iconography of the dvitiya-avatara
description: Kurma is depicted as a plain tortoise bearing Mandara or as a hybrid tortoise-bodied four-armed Vishnu holding shankha, chakra, gada and padma

title: Interment within the temple and the tarati samādhi-tree
description: She is buried within the Viṭṭhal-Rukmiṇī temple precinct—traditionally the only person so interred—and a tarati tree grows from her samādhi
source: Sri Vitthal-Rukmini temple tradition; Vārkarī hagiography

title: Iron bridal chamber with a hidden flaw
description: Chand builds an impenetrable iron nuptial chamber for Lakhindar and Behulā; Viśvakarmā, coerced by Manasā, leaves a needle-fine hole

title: Śiva names her 'Ammai' (Mother) and grants boons
description: On Kailāsa Śiva addresses her as 'Ammai'; she begs undying love, freedom from rebirth, never to forget Him, and to witness His cosmic dance forever

title: Kabir's verses entered into the Adi Granth
description: Guru Arjan Dev compiles the Adi Granth in 1604 at Kartarpur, incorporating Kabir's verses and making him the largest non-Sikh bhagat contributor to Sikh scripture

title: Kailāsanāthar Temple Built by Rājasiṃha
description: The Pallava king Rājasiṃha (Narasiṃhavarman II) builds the Kailāsanāthar temple c. 685–705 CE, the oldest standing temple in Kāñcī and foundational to the Dravidian style

title: Kannappar Offers His Own Eyes to Shiva
description: The tribal hunter Nayanar Kannappar offers his own eyes to a Shiva linga, becoming the archetype of devotion over ritual purity

title: Krishnadevaraya Composes the Amuktamalyada
description: The Telugu poet-king Krishnadevaraya retells Andal's life in the Amuktamalyada ('she who gives a worn garland'), an emperor's literary tribute

title: Lakshmidhara's Saubhagyavardhani commentary
description: The most authoritative commentary reads the hymn through the orthodox Samayacara lens, setting the chief interpretive divide against Kaula/prayoga readings

title: List-placement as ninth/twenty-first avatara
description: Buddha fixed as the 9th of ten in Krishna-as-8th lists and the 21st/23rd in the long Bhagavata schemas, contested against Balarama in other traditions
source: Agni Purana 49, Garuda Purana 1.86.10-11, Bhagavata Purana 1.3

title: Madhva obtains the Udupi Krishna icon and founds the Krishna Matha
description: Madhva miraculously obtains a Krishna murti encased in gopichandana from a ship off the Karnataka coast and enshrines it at Udupi, establishing the Krishna Matha and the Ashta Matha with their Paryaya worship rotation

title: Manasā as Bengali folk-goddess and the Behulā–Lakhindar legend
description: In eastern India the nāga-sister becomes the independent serpent-goddess Manasā, whose Manasā-maṅgala poems tell of the merchant Cānd Sadāgar's feud and Behulā's corpse-raft journey to revive Lakhindar
source: Bengali Manasā-maṅgala / Manasā-vijaya (c. 13th–18th c. CE); Purāṇic strata

title: Medieval/early-modern temple foundation and 1692 CE rebuild
description: The standing pagoda-roofed Paśupatinātha temple, on possibly Licchavi-era foundations, is rebuilt in 1692 CE and becomes the presiding national shrine of Nepal

title: Meykaṇḍar composes the Śivajñāna-bodham
description: In the 13th c. Meykaṇḍar authors the twelve-sūtra Śivajñāna-bodham, founding systematic Tamil Śaiva Siddhānta and the Meykaṇḍar Sampradāya

title: Muktābāī's disappearance in a storm
description: Unlike her brothers' entombed samādhis, Muktābāī is said to vanish into light during a thunderstorm on the Tāpī near Mehūn c. 1297; shrine at Muktainagar

title: Muṉīśvaraṉ's Śaiva pedigree and colour-forms
description: Muṉīśvaraṉ/Muṉiyāṇṭi, read as a form of Śiva, splits into Veḷḷai (white, milder) and Karu/Karuppu (black, fierce) Muṉīśvaraṉ forms in the kāval register

title: Namdev co-founds the Varkari kirtana tradition
description: The tailor sant Namdev of Pandharpur, Jnaneshwar's contemporary, co-founds the Varkari kirtana tradition and travels to the Punjab, his hymns entering the Guru Granth Sahib

title: Periya Purāṇam and the Chola bronze/Naṭarāja milieu
description: Under continuing Chola patronage the Nāyanār hagiography Periya Purāṇam is composed and the Naṭarāja bronze tradition is perfected as dynastic Śaiva emblem

title: Pāmbāṭṭi-cittar's kuṇḍalinī songs
description: The snake-charmer Siddhar composes verses refraining 'āḍu, pāmbē!' ('dance, O snake!'), coding the raising of kuṇḍalinī

title: Rajarāja I Bṛhadīśvara bronze commissions
description: Rājarāja I builds the Thañjāvūr Bṛhadīśvara temple; its inscriptions record numerous donated metal images (tirumēni) with specified metal-weight, among the earliest dated bronzes

title: Recovery of the Rāmapriya/Selvapiḷḷai utsava-mūrti from Delhi
description: Rāmānuja journeys north to retrieve the processional image carried to Delhi among temple plunder and found with the Sultan's daughter

title: Relocation of Śrīnāthajī from Braj to Mewār (1672)
description: The icon is carried by bullock-cart out of Braj (c.1669–70); at Siṅhāḍ the cart sinks and will not move, taken as the deity's choice to settle

title: Relocation of Shrinathji to Nathdwara
description: In 1672, fleeing Aurangzeb, the Shrinathji image is moved from Govardhana to Nathdwara in Rajasthan, which becomes the chief Pushtimarg shrine

title: Rise of Mahavira and the Buddha
description: Mahavira (Jainism) and Gautama Buddha flourish c. 6th-5th century BCE, their critique of Vedic ritual and caste reshaping the religious field Hinduism later defines itself against

title: Rukuṇā Rath Yātrā of Lingarāja
description: On Aśokāṣṭamī the deity is carried in chariot to the Rāmeśvara temple, an Odishan parallel to Purī's Ratha Yātrā

title: Samadhi set at the foot of the temple steps
description: Namdev builds Chokhamela's samadhi at the foot of the Vithoba temple steps, so the saint barred in life rests at the threshold every pilgrim touches

title: Samādhi shrine at Ter and pālkhī tradition
description: Gorā's samādhi at Ter becomes a Vārkarī pilgrimage point, his palanquin joining the wārī to Pandharpur

title: Scholarly disambiguation from Sabarimala Ayyappa
description: Scholars treat the married, horse-riding Tamil Ayyaṉār-Śāstā and the celibate Keralan Ayyappa as distinct cult-figures later conflated under shared names

title: Shankara Disappears at Kedarnath
description: After his works and tour, Shankara dies at age 32, traditionally disappearing at Kedarnath in the Himalayas

title: Sundarar and the slave-deed legend
description: At his wedding Śiva, disguised as an old Brahmin, produces a deed proving Sundarar's family were his hereditary bond-slaves; Sundarar accepts the call, abandons the wedding and begins his hymns chiding Śiva

title: Śītalā among the disease-mothers with Jvarāsura
description: Śītalā heads the vasanta/pox disease-mother set, attended by Jvarāsura the Fever-Demon and grouped as 'seven sisters', structurally twinning the southern Māriyammaṉ

title: The 18th-century Gaekwad-era temple
description: The present Becharājī temple is traditionally said to have been built or rebuilt in the 18th century under Gaekwad (Maratha) patronage, consolidating the older folk seat

title: The bed of iron spikes becomes flowers
description: Sent a bed of iron spikes to kill her, Mira lies down and it becomes a bed of flowers

title: The curtain/jhanki darshan and no-bells seva custom
description: Distinctive worship arises: intermittent curtain (jhanki) darshan, no bells or conch, and the Mangala/feet darshan opened only once a year on Akshaya Tritiya

title: The merger at Udero Lal
description: Jhulelal directs a shrine to be built and vanishes/merges into the river, founding the joint mandir-dargah tirtha of Udero Lal

title: The Śūnya-Purāṇa and Buddhist-survival debate
description: Rāmāi Paṇḍit's Śūnya-Purāṇa frames Dharma as Śūnya/Niraṅjan, fueling the modern scholarly thesis (Śāstrī, Dasgupta) that the god is a vestige of Pāla-era Buddhism — a still-disputed claim

title: The Saundatti-Yellamma hill cult and jātre
description: The Saundatti hill shrine becomes the great pan-Deccan Yellammā center with its annual full-moon jātre and bathing tank

title: The Tiruvaḷḷuvar-sister legend and riddle-poet fame
description: Folk legend makes Avvaiyār the sister of Tiruvaḷḷuvar (author of the Tirukkuṟaḷ) among seven siblings turned sages; her popular fame also rests on floating riddle-and-retort verse, both legendary rather than historical

title: Tirumaṅgai Ālvār sings Tiru Siṅgavēḷ Kuṇḍram
description: The Ālvār's maṅgalāśāsanam canonizes Ahobilam as the sole Narasiṃha Divya Desam

title: Tirumala/Tirupati Teppotsavam
description: The five-day float festival of Venkaṭeśwara (Malayappa Swāmi) with consorts on the Svāmi Puṣkariṇi at Tirumala, a Vaikhānasa-Āgama float-utsava distinct from the nine-day Brahmotsavam
source: TTD (Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams); Vaikhānasa Āgama; Wikipedia (Tirumala Venkateswara Temple)

title: Tiruppāṇ Āḻvār carried into the sanctum and merges
description: The musician-saint is carried into the sanctum by Lokasāraṅga Muni at the Lord's command, sings the Amalanādipirān, and merges into Raṅganātha

title: Tukārām and the Tukārām Gāthā
description: Tukārām (c.1598/1608–1649/1650 CE) of Dehu, the poetic summit of Vārkarī devotion, composes the thousands of raw Marathi abhaṅgas of the Tukārām Gāthā

title: Tēvāram hymnal glorification
description: The 7th–8th-c. Nāyanmār (Sambandar, Appar, Sundarar) sing Aruṇācala in the Tamil Tēvāram, fixing it as a Pāḍal Petṟa Sthalam

title: Tyāgarāja and the kṛti as nāma-saṅkīrtana
description: Carnatic Trinity composer (1767–1847), 700+ Telugu kṛtis, Pañcaratna kṛtis, frames music as singing the Name; signature 'Tyāgarāja'

title: Vallabha Founds Pushtimarg
description: Vallabhacharya (1479-1531) revives Shuddhadvaita and founds Pushtimarg, Krishna-worship as the child Shrinathji of Govardhana, seated at Nathdwara

title: Variant: martyr's death against the Ghaznavids
description: In alternative recensions Gugga dies fighting the Turkic/Ghaznavid invaders and is deified as a battle-martyr rather than vanishing into the earth

title: Vādirāja Tīrtha reforms the paryāya to a two-year cycle
description: The 16th-c. Sōde pontiff Vādirāja regularises the Aṣṭa Maṭha worship-rotation into a two-year paryāya, completing one full eight-maṭha round every 16 years

title: Veṅkaṭamakhin establishes the 72-melakarta system
description: The Caturdaṇḍī-prakāśikā derives exactly 72 exhaustive parent scales with the kaṭapayādi mnemonic, founding modern Carnatic music

title: Veneration as Sant Janābāī, foremost early woman Vārkarī poet
description: Janābāī is venerated as Sant Janābāī at Pandharpur and Gangākheḍ and fixed in the roster of Marathi and pan-Indian women saints alongside Mīrābāī, Āṇḍāḷ and Karaikkāl Ammaiyār

title: Vijayanagara–Nāyaka building of the Śrīmuṣṇam Bhū-Varāha temple
description: The monumental temple with its carved ratha-maṇḍapa and Nityapuṣkariṇī tank is founded and endowed under Vijayanagara authority and the Tanjore/Senji Nāyakas in the 16th c
source: Wikipedia Bhuvarahaswamy Temple Srimushnam; South Indian Inscriptions; ASI

title: Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Mission
description: Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, fusing renunciation with social service under the maxim of serving the living being as God

title: Weaving of the Bṛndāvanī Vastra
description: Around 1554 Śaṅkaradeva has a ~40-yard tapestry woven depicting Kṛṣṇa's Vṛndāvana līlā, a rare material relic of the movement

title: Śaṅkara's bhāṣya on the Praśna
description: Ādi Śaṅkara composes a commentary on the Praśna, framing it as the prose complement to the verse Muṇḍaka among his ten canonical Upaniṣad bhāṣyas

title: Allama Prabhu's awakening at the cave temple
description: After his dancer wife Kamalate's death plunges him into grief and wandering, the siddha Animishayya gives Allama a linga and instruction in a cave temple, igniting his enlightenment and his signature 'Guheshvara.'

title: Aśokan and later inscriptions on the Girnar boulder
description: A boulder at the hill's foot carries Aśoka's Major Rock Edicts (c. 257 BCE) plus Rudradāman and Skandagupta inscriptions on the Sudarśana lake dam

title: Aruṇagirinātar's Tiruppugaḻ
description: The 15th-c. Tiruvaṇṇāmalai-born saint Aruṇagirinātar, redeemed by the hill's grace, composes the Tiruppugaḻ devotional hymns

title: Attributed works Sūr Sārāvalī and Sāhitya Laharī
description: Two further works attributed to Sūr — the Sūr Sārāvalī (essence-garland) and the riddle-verse Sāhitya Laharī — of debated authenticity
source: Sūr Sārāvalī; Sāhitya Laharī; Wikipedia Surdas; Encyclopædia of Indian Literature

title: Aurobindo withdraws to Pondicherry and founds his Ashram
description: Aurobindo withdraws from the freedom struggle to Pondicherry in 1910, develops Integral Yoga aiming at the descent of the Supermind, and co-founds the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in 1926 with the Mother

title: Bābā Kīnārām founds the Aghorī order
description: The Vārāṇasī ascetic Bābā Kīnārām founds the named Aghorī order (the sole surviving Kāpālika-descended line) with its seat at Krīṃ-Kuṇḍ, dying in the latter 18th c

title: Beheading of Bhairavnāth
description: At the Holy Cave the Goddess takes her Mahākālī/Caṇḍī form and beheads Bhairavnāth at the threshold

title: Beholding the cosmic dance at Tiruvālaṅkāṭu
description: Directed to Tiruvālaṅkāṭu, the skeletal Ammaiyār dances at Śiva's feet beating cymbals, eternally watching His cremation-ground tāṇḍava

title: Bhātkhaṇḍe fixes the 10-thāṭ classification
description: V. N. Bhātkhaṇḍe organizes Hindustani rāgas under ten parent thāṭs, a practical counterpart to the South's 72 melakartas
source: Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati of Bhātkhaṇḍe (early 20th c.)

title: Caitanya Mahāprabhu's Years at Purī
description: Caitanya (1486–1534 CE) spent his last ~18 years at Purī absorbed in Jagannātha worship, making it a supreme Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tīrtha

title: Chaitanya's initiation and ecstatic turn at Gaya
description: Travelling to Gaya c.1508-09 for his father's shraddha, the scholar Nimai is initiated by the ascetic Ishvara Puri into the Gopala mantra and overtaken by ecstatic Krishna-bhava

title: Composition and transmission of her abhaṅgas
description: Her Marathi abhaṅgas, cries to Viṭṭhal as sole protector, are preserved in the Vārkarī Sakal Sant Gāthā corpus
source: Kānhopātrā's abhaṅgas in the Sakal Sant Gāthā

title: Composition of the Bonbibi Jahuranama
description: The dobhasi-Bengali puthi codifying Bonbibi's narrative is composed/printed in the 19th century, ascribed to Munshi Mohammad Khater (and earlier Bayanuddin)

title: Composition of the Dāsbodh
description: Dictated the Dāsbodh (20 daśakas × 10 samāsas) as a guru-disciple dialogue on practical Vedānta, dharma and statecraft, traditionally at Śivthar Ghaḷ

title: Concealment and Maratha restoration of the image
description: The image is concealed during medieval invasions and worship restored under Maratha (Kolhapur Chhatrapati) patronage

title: Creation of the bhāruḍ folk-dramas
description: Eknāth originates the bhāruḍ — allegorical, comic Marathi folk-songs/street-dramas using everyday characters to teach spirituality, democratizing scripture for the unlettered, alongside abhaṅgas and gauḷaṇī

title: Critical edition of the vākhs (Grierson & Barnett)
description: After ~400 years of oral transmission the vākhs are collected and edited as Lallā-vākyāni by Grierson and Barnett (1920), establishing the standard scholarly text

title: Crystallization of the pālkhī Wārī processions
description: In the 18th c. Haibatrāo organizes the pālkhī foot-processions carrying the sants' pādukās (Jñāneśvar from Āḷandī, Tukārām from Dehu) into the modern Pandharpur Wārī drawing up to a million pilgrims

title: Deification as Jāharvīr nāg-devtā
description: Through his death Gugga becomes the manifest hero and serpent-lord who protects devotees from snakebite, venerated at the Gogāmeḍī shrine across Hindu, Muslim and Sikh communities
source: Gogāmeḍī sthala tradition; Gugga Naumī observance

title: Ādi Śaṅkara Consecrates the Śrī-Cakra before Kāmākṣī
description: Ādi Śaṅkara pacifies the fierce Kāmākṣī by consecrating a Śrī-Cakra before her in the cavity under the central shrine, seating her in yogic calm and founding a living Śrī-Vidyā seat

title: Ādi Śaṅkara Installs Chaṇḍī Devī Image
description: Ādi Śaṅkarācārya is said to install the main image of Chaṇḍī Devī on Nīl Parvat in the 8th century

title: Enshrinement of Bībī/Tuḷukka Nācciyār
description: The Sultan's daughter follows the recovered icon to Melkote out of devotion, dies of separation, and is enshrined at the deity's feet

title: Founding of the Ahobila Maṭha (c. 1398 CE)
description: Narasiṃha grants the Mālōla icon to the first Jīyar, founding the itinerant Śrīvaiṣṇava Ahobila Maṭha

title: Founding of the Kabir Panth
description: After Kabir's death the Sant-mat sect crystallizes in the 17th-18th c. revering him as Satguru and divine incarnation, splitting into the Kabir Chaura and Dharmadasi/Chhattisgarh branches
source: Anurag Sagar; Sukh Nidhan (late Panthi texts)

title: Gopīcand's renunciation
description: King Gopīcand is persuaded by his mother Maināvatī to renounce and is initiated by Jālandhara/Hāḍipā; the Bhartṛhari–Gopīcand ballads become the chief Nāth epics

title: Heliodorus Pillar Erected
description: The Greek devotee Heliodorus erects a Garuḍa-stambha to Vāsudeva at Besnagar c. 113 BCE, the earliest dated physical witness to Garuḍa-Vaiṣṇava cult

title: Historical elaboration of the temple complex
description: From the Sātavāhana–Ikṣvāku era cult near Nāgārjunakoṇḍa, the standing complex (prākāra wall, gopuras, galleries) is built up under the Reḍḍi, Kākatīya, and Vijayanagara dynasties
source: Epigraphy and temple history; Vīraśaiva maṭha tradition

title: Hymns enshrined in the Bhaktamāl and Gurū Granth Sāhib
description: Ravidās features in Nābhādās's Bhaktamāl (c. 1600) and ~40 of his hymns are compiled into the Gurū Granth Sāhib by Gurū Arjan Dev in 1604
source: Bhaktamāl; Gurū Granth Sāhib; Wikipedia Ravidas, Bhaktamal

title: Installation at Nathdwārā under Rāṇā Rāj Siṃh
description: Mahārāṇā Rāj Siṃh I of Mewār grants asylum; the havelī is built at renamed Nāthdvāra and the icon installed in 1672 CE (V.S. 1728)

title: Institution of Cheti Chand
description: Jhulelal's appearance is commemorated as Cheti Chand, the Sindhi New Year and his birthday, with the bahirano procession and river-immersion

title: Jogti/jogappa and contested devadasi dedication
description: Dedicated jogti/jogappa orders and the legally banned but persistent devadasi dedication develop around Saundatti-Yellammā
source: Jogti/jogappa and devadasi ethnography; Karnataka Devadasis Act 1982

title: Kali-yuga dynastic chronicle (Maurya–Gupta)
description: Future-tense king-lists of Bārhadratha, Pradyota, Śiśunāga, Nanda, Maurya, Śuṅga, Kāṇva, Andhra/Sātavāhana and Gupta dynasties — datable historical memory recast as prophecy

title: Karuvūrār and the Bṛhadīśvara consecration
description: The Siddhar-poet Karuvūr-tēvar is associated with the Chola Tanjore Bṛhadīśvara temple, his Tiruvicaippā hymns entering Tirumuṟai Book 9

title: Koch rebuilding of 1565 CE
description: The destroyed temple is rebuilt by Koch king Naranārāyaṇa and Chilarāi in 1565 CE in the nilachala-dome form

title: Lakhindar dies of snakebite
description: Manasā sends the serpent Kālnāgini through the pinhole and Lakhindar is fatally bitten on his wedding night

title: Lalla
description: Eighth-century author of the Śiṣyadhīvṛddhida-tantra, a major post-Brahmagupta siddhānta on planetary theory and eclipse correction

title: Later life, children, and death
description: She bears children (traditionally a son Viṭhobā), keeps composing, and dies c. 1700, reputedly foretelling her own death in verse

title: Madhva proclaims himself the third Vayu-avatara
description: Madhva proclaims himself the third incarnation of Vayu after Hanuman and Bhima, sent to restore right doctrine, and brands Advaita 'crypto-Buddhism.'

title: Medieval temple-building and Pañcārāma grouping
description: The five shrines are built/expanded under Eastern Cālukya, Cōḻa and Kākatīya patronage (9th–13th c. CE) and later bundled as a single fivefold set; Śrīnātha glorifies Drākṣārāma in 15th-c. Telugu

title: Millennium celebration and UNESCO living-temple status
description: Continuous worship for ~1000 years culminates in the 2010 millennium festivities; UNESCO inscribes it as a Great Living Chola Temple
actors: Tamil Nadu state; temple community; UNESCO

title: Mirabai merges into the Krishna image at Dwarka
description: In old age Mira travels to Dwarka and, when Mewar emissaries come to summon her home, embraces the Ranchhor-ray image and merges bodily into the Krishna-murti, leaving only her garment

title: Modern reclamation as Mahar/Dalit icon
description: Chokhamela becomes a central symbol of Mahar self-respect in 19th-20th-c. Maharashtra, standing at the hinge between bhakti-era devotion and Ambedkar-era Dalit assertion
actors: Mahar community; B. R. Ambedkar movement

title: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar's Sanskrit kṛtis
description: Trinity composer (1775–1835), grand slow Sanskrit kṛtis, Navagraha and Kamalāmbā Navāvaraṇa cycles, nottu-svara; signature 'Guruguha'

title: Muṉīśvaraṉ in the Malaysia/Singapore diaspora
description: Muṉīśvaraṉ temples become major Tamil community shrines in Malaysia and Singapore, the god travelling as protector of estate and urban communities

title: Mylapore Kapālīśwarar Theppam
description: The Chennai Kapālīśwarar (Śiva) temple's float festival, with processional deities floated over three nights on the Mylapore tank in the month of Thai — a metropolitan Śaiva instance of the genre
source: Wikipedia (Kapaleeshwarar Temple); Chennai temple festival calendar

title: Nandanar Enters the Chidambaram Sanctum
description: The untouchable Pulaiyar labourer-saint Nandanar enters the Chidambaram sanctum, becoming an emblem of bhakti dissolving caste barriers

title: Nimbarka Pioneers Joint Radha-Krishna Worship
description: Nimbarka, head of the Kumara Sampradaya and an amsha of the Sudarshana cakra, settles at Vrindavana and pioneers the joint worship of Radha-Krishna under the Dvaitadvaita school

title: Nivṛttināth's samādhi at Tryambakeśvar
description: After Jñāneśvar's samādhi the eldest brother goes to Tryambakeśvar near Nashik and takes samādhi c. 1297; his shrine there is a Vārkarī pilgrimage site

title: Northern journey to the Punjab
description: Nāmdev travels north and spends years in the Punjab (village Ghuman), bridging Marathi Viṭṭhal-bhakti into the north-Indian Sant-mat world

title: Patronage of the hijra community and the nirvāṇa rite
description: Bahucharā becomes chief patron of the hijra community; the ritual emasculation (nirvāṇa) is performed under her invocation and hijras make pilgrimage to Becharājī as her devotees
source: Hijra devotional tradition; Serena Nanda, Neither Man nor Woman

title: Perpetual sandalwood coating ritual
description: The fierce ugra-Narasiṃha icon is kept permanently encased in cooling sandalwood paste, appearing as a liṅga-like mound year-round

title: Pochamma the smallpox-and-fertility mother
description: The beloved Telugu village mother who sends and cures pox and guards children, sister to Māriyammaṉ and Śītalā

title: Redaction of the Mahabharata
description: The Mahabharata is redacted c. 400 BCE-400 CE (traditionally composed by Vyasa at the Dvapara/Kali cusp recording events of ~3102 BCE)

title: Redaction of the Ramayana
description: Valmiki Ramayana core composed c. 500 BCE-200 CE (scholarly); tradition places events in Treta Yuga

title: Rāmānuja makes Śrīraṅgam the Śrī Vaiṣṇava capital
description: Rāmānuja reorganizes the temple's worship and administration, establishing it as the headquarters of Viśiṣṭādvaita Śrī Vaiṣṇavism

title: Seasonal winter shift of worship to Pāṇḍukeśwar/Joshimath
description: Each winter, when the snow-locked shrine closes, the festival image descends to Yogadhyān Badrī at Pāṇḍukeśwar (and the Joshimath maṭha) so worship is never dark

title: Seasonal worship and winter idol-shift
description: The snow-locked high shrine opens Akṣaya-tṛtīyā to Kārttika; in winter the utsava-mūrti shifts to Omkareśvara Temple at Ukhimaṭh
source: Wikipedia, Panch Kedar; Chota Char Dham

title: Sectarian commentaries and daily recitation
description: Later Vaiṣṇava ācāryas (Parāśara Bhaṭṭa, Madhva tradition) gloss the names; the hymn becomes the most-recited Vaiṣṇava/Smārta daily stotra

title: Sembiyaṉ Mahādevī's bronze & temple patronage
description: The 10th-c. Cōḻa queen donates temples and bronze icons across the Kāveri delta, a key dated horizon in the bronze sequence
source: Dehejia, Chola: Sacred Bronzes; Cōḻa inscriptions

title: Smallpox eradication and the cult's survival
description: After the WHO declared smallpox eradicated in 1980 the Śītalā cult broadened to cover chickenpox, measles, heat-fevers and child-protection rather than dying out

title: Sundarar blinded and his sight restored
description: Married to Paravai and Caṅkili, Sundarar breaks his oath and is struck blind, gradually regaining sight through penitent hymns; Śiva acts as go-between to reconcile him with Paravai

title: The 2013 Kedarnath Flash Floods
description: Catastrophic June 2013 flash floods devastate the Kedarnath valley while the temple itself survives

title: The Belaguri debate and conversion of Madhavadeva
description: Once a Śākta sacrificer, Madhavadeva is converted to single-refuge bhakti by Śaṅkaradeva at the famous Belaguri debate (maṇi-kāñcana saṃyoga), adding Guru as a cāri-vastu principle

title: The Cāṅgadeva (wall-riding) episode and Pāsaṣṭī
description: The proud yogī Cāṅgadeva arrives on a tiger; the siblings ride a moving mud wall to meet him, and Jñāneśvar answers his blank letter with the 65-verse Cāṅgadeva Pāsaṣṭī, humbling him into discipleship

title: The living Amarnāth Yātrā
description: One of India's largest pilgrimages, via Pahalgām and Baltāl routes, culminating on Śrāvaṇa Pūrṇimā with the chaḍī mubarak procession
source: Living Amarnāth Yātrā tradition; Nīlamata Purāṇa & Rājataraṅgiṇī (early footprint)

title: The Paryāya Mahotsava handover
description: Every changeover year on Makara Saṅkrānti the incoming maṭha svāmī receives the akṣaya pātra and ritual charge of the kṣetra in Udupi's greatest festival

title: The rājagopuram as the Tamil Nadu state emblem
description: Srivilliputhur's eleven-tier rājagopuram, raised under medieval Pāṇḍya/Nāyaka patronage, becomes the emblem on the Government of Tamil Nadu state symbol
source: Temple tradition; Government of Tamil Nadu

title: The Srikurmam Kurma-kshetra cult
description: At Srikurmam in Andhra Pradesh the tortoise form is the presiding deity; theologised as the Kurma-kshetra and tied by tradition to Ramanuja's Vaishnava reform

title: Tukaram's manuscripts float back from the Indrayani
description: The Shudra grocer-sant Tukaram of Dehu, emotional apex of the Varkari tradition, sees his abhanga manuscripts drowned in the Indrayani river float back intact, and is traditionally taken bodily to Vaikuntha at his death

title: Ujjaini Mahakali temple founded (Bonalu charter)
description: In 1813 a Hyderabad battalion at Ujjain vowed to install Mahakali's idol if she lifted a plague back home; on deliverance they founded the Ujjaini Mahakali temple, origin of the Bonalu cycle

title: Vāgbhaṭa's synthesis of the two schools
description: Vāgbhaṭa harmonizes the Caraka and Suśruta traditions into the Aṣṭāṅga Saṅgraha and Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya, completing the Bṛhat-trayī

title: Vishnupad Temple Rebuilt by Ahalyābāī Holkar
description: The Maratha queen Ahalyābāī Holkar of Indore rebuilds the octagonal Vishnupad temple enclosing Viṣṇu's footprint in its present form in 1787 CE

title: Worship as Kūttāṇṭavar and the Kūvākam festival
description: Aravān is enshrined in Tamil Nadu as Kūttāṇṭavar (a severed-head icon); the eighteen-day Kūvākam (Koovagam) festival re-enacts the marriage, sacrifice, and widowhood, and is the great gathering of the Aravāṇi/Thirunaṅgai community
source: Kūttāṇṭavar temple tradition (Kūvākam, Villupuram, Tamil Nadu)

title: 2013 flood survival
description: The temple survives the catastrophic June 2013 Kedarnath flash floods that devastated the valley, a boulder credited with diverting the water
source: Wikipedia, Chota Char Dham / Kedarnath Temple

title: Abhinavagupta canonizes śānta as the ninth rasa
description: Abhinavagupta's Abhinavabhāratī expounds rasa as disinterested aesthetic bliss and champions śānta-rasa to complete the nava-rasa

title: Śaṅkaradeva's death at Bheladuar
description: Śaṅkaradeva dies (traditionally 1568) at Bheladuar in Cooch Behar under Koch king Naranārāyaṇa's patronage

title: Śaṅkara's bhāṣya on the Muṇḍaka
description: Ādi Śaṅkara (c. 8th c. CE) composes a commentary treating the Atharvan trio together, making the parā/aparā distinction central to Advaita epistemology

title: Allama Prabhu merges with the linga at Kadalivana
description: Allama Prabhu is said to have become one with the linga at Kadalivana near Srisailam

title: Ascribed authorship of the Nandikeśvara Kāśikā and Abhinaya-darpaṇa
description: Nandikeśvara is the named speaker of the Nandikeśvara Kāśikā (Māheśvara Sūtras) and traditional author of the Abhinaya-darpaṇa, the post-classical dance-gesture grammar

title: Baladeva Vidyabhushana Wins the Galta Debate
description: Baladeva Vidyabhushana composes the Govinda-bhashya and Prameya-ratnavali (18th c.) to win the Gaudiyas a recognized seat at the Galta (Jaipur) debate, bridging them to Madhva

title: Basava founds the Liṅgāyat tradition
description: Basava (c. 1105–1167), treasurer under Kalachuri king Bijjala II, organizes the Liṅgāyat/Vīraśaiva bhakti movement rejecting caste, ritual sacrifice and priestly mediation

title: Behulā's raft-journey with the corpse
description: Refusing to abandon him, Behulā floats down-river on a raft with Lakhindar's decaying body to reach the gods

title: Bhāskara II and the Siddhānta Śiromaṇi (1150 CE)
description: Summit of classical astronomy (Līlāvatī, Bījagaṇita, etc.); anticipates differential calculus with instantaneous planetary velocity and the cakravāla solution of Pell's equation

title: Buddha's Enlightenment at Bodh Gayā
description: Gautama Buddha attains enlightenment under the Bodhi tree beside the Phalgu at Bodh Gayā, the Buddhist pole of the Gayā district

title: Cekkilar Versifies the Periya Puranam
description: Cekkilar (c. 1135 CE) versifies the hagiographies of the 63 Nayanars in the Periya Puranam, added as Book 12 to complete the Tirumurai canon

title: Chaitanya launches sankirtana at Navadvipa
description: Chaitanya launches nightly congregational sankirtana of the Hare Krishna maha-mantra with Nityananda and Advaita Acharya at Shrivasa's courtyard, inaugurating mass Gaudiya devotion

title: Chandanotsavam — annual Nijarūpa Darśanam
description: On Akṣaya Tṛtīyā the paste is removed and the true carved Varāha-Narasiṃha form is revealed for about twelve hours before being re-coated in four annual installments

title: Charter of śālagrāma–tulasī worship and Tulsī-Vivāha
description: The episode grounds the joint śālagrāma–tulasī pūjā, the Tulsī-Vivāha festival on Prabodhinī Ekādaśī, and the conch's place in Vaiṣṇava worship
source: Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; festival tradition

title: Composition of Manāche Ślok and Mārutī stotras
description: Wrote the 205-verse Manāche Ślok (Manobodh) counselling the mind, and the Bhīm-rūpī Mārutī Stotra and other Hanumān hymns

title: Composition of Marathi abhaṅgas forming the Vārkarī canon
description: Nāmdev's Marathi abhaṅgas, with the Jñāneśvarī and Tukārām Gāthā, become the core scriptural canon of the Vārkarī tradition

title: Composition of the four Tirumuṟai Book 11 works
description: She composes the Aṟputat Tiruvantāti (100 vv), Tiru Iraṭṭai Maṇimālai (20 vv), and two Mūtta Tiruppatikams (~22-23 vv), ~143 verses in Tirumuṟai Book 11
source: Tirumuṟai Book 11 (Aṟputat Tiruvantāti, Tiru Iraṭṭai Maṇimālai, Mūtta Tiruppatikam I & II)

title: Ādi Śaṅkara Founds the Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha
description: By the Kāñcī matha's tradition, Ādi Śaṅkara founds the Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha at Kāñcī and attains his final siddhi there

title: Dispersal of the Seven Houses across Rajasthan
description: The same Aurangzeb-era flight scatters the other Puṣṭimārga deities — Dvārkādhīśa to Kankroli, Mathureśa to Kota, etc. — across Rajasthan

title: Ekvīrā as Maharashtrian kuladevī
description: At Karla and Māhūr Reṇukā is worshipped as Ekvīrā/Reṇukā-Mātā, kuladevī of the CKP, Agri-Koli and Mahar communities
source: Karla Ekvīrā sthala tradition; Maharashtrian Śakti-pīṭha tradition

title: Flying severed head and redemptive boon
description: Bhairavnāth's severed head flies ~3 km up the mountain to the Bhairavnāth shrine; repenting, he is forgiven and granted that no yātrā is complete without visiting his shrine
source: Vaiṣṇo Devī sthala legend; regional variant

title: Formation of the Siddha-vaidya medical system
description: The Siddhars develop Siddha medicine—mineral/metal-based therapy, varma vital-points and nāḍi pulse diagnosis—as a distinct Tamil medical science

title: Founding of the Yatirāja Maṭha
description: Rāmānuja, titled Yatirāja, establishes the Yatirāja Maṭha at Melkote as a seat of his order and paramparā transmission

title: Gahininath transmits the Nāth current to the Vārkarīs
description: Maharashtrian Nāth Gahininath initiates Nivṛttināth, channeling the Nāth lineage into Jñāneśvar's Vārkarī movement

title: Hiḍimbā Devī cult at Manali
description: Hiḍimbā is later worshipped as a Kullu-valley goddess with the 1553 CE Dhungri cedar-wood temple, recast from rākṣasī to tutelary mountain deity and royal ancestress

title: Independent knowledge-cult of Hayagrīva
description: Hayagrīva worshipped as patron of learning in Śrī-Vaiṣṇava and Tantric traditions, with shrines at Tirumala and Chettipunyam and Vedānta Deśika's Hayagrīva Stotra
source: Hayagrīva Upaniṣad; Śrī-Vaiṣṇava temple tradition; Vedānta Deśika's Hayagrīva Stotra

title: Institution of Chaliho Sahib
description: The forty-day Chaliho penance is kept in gratitude, re-enacting the founding forty-day Indus prayer

title: Jayarashi composes the Tattvopaplavasimha
description: Jayarashi Bhatta writes a radically skeptical Lokayata-linked work undermining the validity of every pramana (c. 8th c. CE)

title: Joint enshrinement of the kāval cluster at the village edge
description: Karuppasāmi, Maturai-Vīraṉ, Muṉīśvaraṉ and Sudalaimāḍaṉ are grouped as a hot male guardian-ring around a presiding ammaṉ such as Māriyammaṉ, served by non-Brahman pūcāri with blood-sacrifice and possession-dance

title: Kapila's āśrama and the Makar Saṅkrānti melā at Sāgara-dvīpa
description: The Kapil Muni temple marks the hermitage; the annual Makar Saṅkrānti Gaṅgāsāgar Melā draws millions, encoded in the proverb 'Sab tīrtha bār bār, Gaṅgāsāgar ek bār'
source: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa / Kapila tradition; sthala-purāṇa; folk proverb

title: Later invocation as brahmavādinī exemplars
description: Gārgī and Maitreyī become the canonical names cited for women's access to Vedic learning and brahmavidyā, commented on by Ādi Śaṅkara and invoked in modern debates and institutions
source: Ādi Śaṅkara, Bṛhadāraṇyaka-bhāṣya; Wikipedia (Gargi Vachaknavi, Maitreyi)

title: Maurya Empire & Ashoka
description: First pan-Indian empire c. 322-185 BCE; Ashoka patronizes Buddhism and issues rock/pillar edicts

title: Mirabai and Jiva Gosvami at Vrindavana
description: Told that the ascetic Jiva Gosvami would not meet a woman, Mira retorts that Krishna is the only true male in Vrindavana and all else are gopis, whereupon the abashed scholar comes out to meet her

title: Naraka-caturdaśī / Dīpāvalī aetiology
description: The slaying of Naraka becomes the charter-myth for Naraka-caturdaśī before Dīpāvalī, observed with the pre-dawn oil bath and lamps across India

title: Near-simultaneous end of the prodigy generation
description: All four siblings plus Cāṅgadeva take samādhi or depart within roughly a year (1296–1297), closing the founding Vārkarī household

title: Nāyaka rebuilding of the temple-city
description: After Sultanate-era damage, the Madurai-Nāyaka rulers (esp. Tirumalai Nāyaka) rebuild the complex with its gopurams and thousand-pillar hall

title: Onam — Mahābali's Annual Return
description: Kerala folk-tradition holds that the golden-age king Māveli (Mahābali) returns to visit his people once a year, celebrated as the Onam harvest festival

title: Pan-Deccan equation Reṇukā = Yellammā = Māri
description: A single Deccan mother-goddess identified across regions as Reṇukā, Yellammā, Ekvīrā, Māriyammaṉ, Padmākṣī and Aai

title: Poleramma and Maisamma the boundary guardians
description: Boundary mothers stationed at the village limit, gate or irrigation-tank who turn back epidemic and demon and receive buffalo-bali

title: Prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā and netra-unmīlana animate the cast icon
description: The finished bronze is consecrated by life-installation and the eye-opening rite, at which the image first 'sees' and becomes the living deity fit for pūjā

title: Priyādās commentary elaborates his life
description: Priyādās's 1712 commentary on the Bhaktamāl elaborates the miracle-tales and full hagiographic life of Ravidās

title: Ramaṇa Mahaṛṣi's tapas at Aruṇācala
description: From 1896 the sage Ramana Maharshi makes Aruṇācala his lifelong seat of tapas, teaching the hill as Śiva and the Heart/Self and composing the Five Hymns to Aruṇācala
source: Ramana Maharshi corpus (Akṣaramaṇamālai / Five Hymns to Aruṇācala)

title: Ramana Maharshi's death-experience and Self-realization
description: At sixteen in 1896 Ramana undergoes a spontaneous death-experience resolving into permanent Self-realization, then settles for life at Tiruvannamalai teaching atma-vichara, 'Who am I?'

title: Ramanuja Learns the Charama Sloka at Tirukkoshtiyur
description: At Tirukkoshtiyur, Ramanuja learns the secret charama sloka from his teacher

title: Redaction of the Valmiki Ramayana
description: The Ramayana's core text is composed c. 500 BCE-200 CE (traditionally narrating Treta Yuga events far earlier)

title: Rise of the Haridasa movement
description: The Kannada bhakti-musical Haridasa wing of Madhva's school carries Dvaita to the common people through devaranamas and dasa-sahitya, with Purandaradasa hailed grandfather of Carnatic music

title: Rāmānuja's body enshrined as a tomb-shrine
description: Rāmānuja's preserved body is enshrined within the temple in the fifth prākāra, a rare relic-shrine in Hinduism

title: Sañjīvana (living) samādhi at Āḷandī
description: At about 21 Jñāneśvar voluntarily seals himself in conscious meditation at Āḷandī in 1296; the tradition holds him still present beneath the shrine

title: Samādhi at Paithan (1599) and Eknāth Ṣaṣṭhī
description: Eknāth takes samādhi at Paithan on the Godāvarī in 1599, commemorated by the Eknāth Ṣaṣṭhī and an Eknāth Mahārāj pālkhī within Vārkarī palanquin culture

title: Shankaradeva founds Ekasarana Dharma
description: The Assamese polymath Shankaradeva founds Ekasarana Dharma, a single-refuge monotheistic Krishna-devotion, and creates the Kirtana-ghosha, the borgeet song-genre, ankiya nat plays, and the sattra and namghar institutional network

title: Sītā Eliya / Seetha Amman temple identification
description: The modern Sri Lankan Rāmāyaṇa trail identifies the Aśoka-vāṭikā with Sītā Eliya near Hakgala, site of the living Seetha Amman kovil and the Sītā Oya stream

title: Sundarar composes the Tiruttoṇḍa Tohai
description: Sundarar composes the Tiruttoṇḍa Tohai naming the foremost Śiva-devotees, the seed-list from which the canonical 63 Nāyaṉārs were fixed

title: Tagore's Songs of Kabir
description: Rabindranath Tagore publishes Songs of Kabir in 1915, making Kabir a global figure of universalist mysticism

title: The annual Girnar (Lili) Parikramā
description: Pilgrims and sādhus circumambulate the massif over ~36 km from Kārttika Ekādaśī to Pūrṇimā, with the Bhavnāth Mahāśivarātri fair gathering renunciants

title: The garland-link tradition with Śrīraṅgam
description: Garlands made at Āṇḍāḷ's natal shrine are sent to be offered to Raṅganātha at Śrīraṅgam, with mutual festival exchange (Āḍi Pūram, mārgaḻi Tiruppāvai)

title: The Pañcasakhā and Odia Bhakti
description: The five Odia poet-devotees (Balarāma, Jagannātha, Yaśovanta, Ananta, Acyutānanda Dāsa) centered Utkala Vaiṣṇavism on Jagannātha; Jagannātha Dāsa's Odia Bhāgavata became household scripture

title: The Sabarimala sacred-geography identification
description: The Ayyappan pilgrimage shrine of Sabarimala in Kerala takes its name from Śabarī's hill, a traditional devotional overlay linking the tribal ascetic's tapas to the living pilgrimage cult
source: Bhakti and regional folk tradition; Kerala sacred geography

title: Tulsīdās's vision of Rāma at Rāmghāṭ
description: Hanumān leads Tulsīdās to a darśana of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as young hunters at Citrakūṭa's Rāmghāṭ, the origin of his famous couplet

title: Tulsidas Begins the Ramcaritmanas at Ayodhya (1574)
description: Gosvami Tulsidas begins composing the Ramcaritmanas at Ayodhya in 1574 CE, recasting Valmiki's Sanskrit epic into Avadhi for the people

title: Vijayanagara-era construction of the Ahobilam temples
description: Vijayanagara kings and the Maṭha build and endow the standing Upper and Lower Ahobilam shrines (15th–16th c. CE)

title: Viśvanātha Temple Rebuilt by Ahilyābāī Holkar
description: After repeated medieval demolitions the Kāśī Viśvanātha (Gyanvapi) temple is rebuilt by Ahilyābāī Holkar in 1780

title: Āḻvār consecration of Tiruvēṅkaṭam as Divya Deśam
description: The Āḻvārs (Nammāḻvār, Tirumaṅgai) hymn Tirumala as Tiruvēṅkaṭam in the Divya Prabandham, making it one of the most-sung 108 Divya Deśams and a horizon of prapatti

title: Worship as Khāṭū Śyām Jī / Śyām Bābā
description: The self-manifested head is enshrined at Khāṭū, Rajasthan; worshipped as Khāṭū Śyām Jī, Śyām Bābā, Hāre kā Sahārā, with the annual Phālguna fair

title: Śyāma Śāstri, the Devī-upāsaka composer
description: Eldest of the Trinity (1762–1827), archaka of Baṅgāru Kāmākṣī, Navaratnamālikā and rhythmically intricate svarajatis; signature 'Śyāmakṛṣṇa'

title: Akka Mahadevi renounces clothing for Shiva
description: After the Jain king Kaushika breaks his pact never to violate her devotion, Akka Mahadevi leaves him, renounces all possessions and clothing covering herself only with her hair, and walks to Kalyana

title: Ankalamman carries Brahmā's skull
description: The Tamil grief-and-cremation mother who carries Brahmā's severed skull / relieves Śiva of the Brahmahatyā sin, a local Kālī of the cremation-ground

title: Behulā's dance and the revival bargain
description: Behulā dances before Śiva and the devas; Manasā agrees to revive Lakhindar and the six sons in exchange for Chand's worship

title: Canonization among the 63 Nāyaṉārs
description: Named in Cuntarar's Tiruttoṇḍa Tohai as among the earliest devotees and versified by Cēkkiḻār in the Periya Purāṇam, ranked senior to the Nālvar

title: Chaitanya takes sannyasa at Katwa
description: In 1510 Chaitanya takes sannyasa at Katwa from Keshava Bharati, receiving the name Krishna Chaitanya

title: Compilation of the Navnāth Bhaktisār
description: The 18th-c. Marathi hagiographic cycle narrating the nine Nāths' miracles and initiations becomes a household devotional grantha

title: Composition of nirguṇa hymns enshrined in the Guru Granth Sāhib
description: About 61 Hindi/Marwari nirguṇa hymns attributed to Nāmdev enter the Sikh Guru Granth Sāhib, making him a poet straddling both saguṇa and nirguṇa bhakti
actors: Nāmdev; Sikh tradition (compilers of the Ādi Granth)
source: Hindi/Marwari hymns in the Guru Granth Sāhib; Wikipedia Namdev

title: Discovery of the Varadvinayak Idol from the Lake (1690)
description: The Varada-Vinayaka murti is reportedly found immersed in an adjoining lake at Mahad in 1690 CE, leading to the temple's construction in 1725

title: Eastern Gaṅga Temple Construction
description: The surviving 12th-c. Kaliṅga-style temple was built under Eastern Gaṅga kings Anantavarman Coḍagaṅga and Anaṅgabhīma III (c. 1135–1230 CE) over an older, likely Sabara-origin cult

title: Establishment of the Āḷandī pālkhī and the four-saint succession
description: Jñāneśvar heads the Jñāneśvar→Nāmdev→Eknāth→Tukārām lineage; his pādukā are carried annually from Āḷandī to Pandharpur, the procession reshaped in the 1820s by Haibatravbābā Ārphaḷkar

title: Establishment of the Anubhava Maṇṭapa
description: Basava establishes the Anubhava Maṇṭapa at Basavakalyāṇ, the 'first religious parliament,' where śaraṇas of all backgrounds debate and produce the vachana corpus

title: Founding of the Maurya Empire
description: The Maurya Empire (c. 322-185 BCE), first pan-Indian empire, is founded by Chandragupta; Ashoka patronizes Buddhism and issues rock and pillar edicts

title: Institution of the Vairamudi diamond-crown festival
description: Melkote's signature brahmotsava crowns the processional Celuvarāya with the secret diamond Vairamudi crown kept under treasury seal

title: Madhavadeva composes the Nāma-ghoṣā
description: Madhavadeva composes the Nāma-ghoṣā ('book of the Name'/Hajāri-ghoṣā), consolidating the faith after the founder's death and producing a peak of Assamese literature

title: Madhava-Vidyaranya compiles the Sarva-darshana-sangraha
description: Madhava-Vidyaranya surveys sixteen darshanas (14th c.), opening with Carvaka as the lowest and ascending to Advaita, providing the standard Carvaka portrait

title: Mādhava of Saṅgamagrāma and the Kerala school
description: Founder of the Kerala school, credited with infinite-series expansions for π, sine and cosine anticipating European calculus by ~250 years

title: Nambiyandar Nambi Recovers the Tevaram Hymns
description: The scattered Tevaram hymns, legendarily found walled-up at Chidambaram, are rediscovered and organized into Tirumurai Books 1-7 by Nambiyandar Nambi under Chola king Rajaraja I

title: Pañcavaṭī / Nāsik as living tīrtha
description: Sītā Guphā, Kālārām Mandir, Tapovan, Rāmkuṇḍ and the Godāvarī ghāṭs constitute the worshipped site
actors: Pilgrims; Peśvā-era builders; B. R. Ambedkar (1930 satyāgraha)

title: Place in the Vārkarī succession
description: Eknāth is the consolidator third link in Jñāneśvar→Nāmdev→Eknāth→Tukārām, recovering the textual heritage and bridging the gap to Tukārām's age

title: Priyadas's narrative elaboration of Mira's life
description: Priyadas's 1712 commentary on the Bhaktamal provides the first full narrative of Mira — the poison, snake-basket, persecuting Rana and miracles — building the familiar dramatic life out of Nabhadas's bare notice

title: Ravidāssia movement and 2009 Vienna attack
description: The Camār-based Ravidāssia movement venerates Ravidās as founder-Guru; the 2009 murder of Sant Rāmānand in a Vienna dera attack pushes it toward separate identity

title: Śārṅgadeva compiles the Saṅgīta-ratnākara
description: At the Yādava court of Devagiri, Śārṅgadeva synthesizes the music-and-dance science bridging the Nāṭya Śāstra and the modern rāga–tāla systems

title: Rāmānuja's ordering of the shrine worship
description: Rāmānuja organises Tirumala worship, fixes the Vaiṣṇava emblems and establishes the Pāñcarātra liturgy, settling the deity's identity as Veṅkaṭeśvara-Viṣṇu

title: Rukmiṇī-kalyāṇam recitation and festival tradition
description: The marriage narrative is read as an auspicious maṅgala text and ritually enacted as a kalyāṇotsavam across South India, held to confer marital harmony
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.52-54 (liturgical use); Potana Telugu Bhāgavatamu

title: Sanskritization of the folk goddess
description: Temple back-stories reframe Māri as Pārvatī/Durgā/Ādi Parāśakti and replace blood-sacrifice with Agamic vegetarian worship, contested between reform temples and village shrines

title: Seat at Sajjangad and mahāsamādhi
description: Made Sajjangad fort near Sātārā the order's mother-maṭh with a Rāma temple, and died there in 1681

title: Sivananda founds the Divine Life Society
description: The physician-turned-monk Sivananda founds the Divine Life Society in 1936 at Rishikesh, propagating a synthetic practical yoga and seeding global teachers

title: Sundarar's bodily ascent to Kailāsa
description: Śiva sends a white elephant to carry Sundarar bodily to Kailāsa, with his friend Cēramāṉ Perumāḷ following on horseback

title: Syncretic identification as Zinda Pir / Khwaja Khizr
description: At the Indus river-shrines Jhulelal is identified with the immortal water-saint Zinda Pir / Khwaja Khizr, venerated by Hindus and Muslims alike
source: Udero Lal sthala-tradition; floating-shrine (Zindapir) cult; Khidr lore

title: The 1311 Sultanate raid and the icon's exile
description: Malik Kāfūr's army sacks the south; Nam Perumāḷ is hidden and carried into decades of exile, later restored under Vijayanagara
source: Koil Oḻugu; folk Tulukka Nācciyār variant

title: The Avvaiyar Riddle at Pazhamudircholai
description: Murugan disguised as a boy poses the roasted-fruit riddle to the aged poet Avvaiyar, humbling her bookish learning before divine grace

title: The Nandi maṇḍapa of temple tradition
description: The couchant white bull faces the liṅga in a dedicated pavilion (Nandi-maṇḍapa); monumental examples at Lepākṣi, Tanjore, Mysuru, Hampi, and Kāśī

title: The Siṃhastha Kumbh at Nāsik–Tryambak
description: The Godāvarī source-region hosts the Siṃhastha (Jupiter-in-Leo) Kumbh every ~12 years, with bathing split between Rāmkuṇḍ (Nāsik) and Kuśāvarta (Tryambak)

title: The three pinḍīs of the Holy Cave
description: The Goddess is enshrined aniconically as three natural rock pinḍīs — Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī, Mahāsarasvatī — the Tridevī fused in the cave
source: Śākta tradition of the three pinḍīs; Devī Māhātmya

title: Tirumangai Alvar sings Tiru Naimisaranyam (Divya Desam)
description: The Alvar poet-saint composes the mangalasasana enshrining Naimisharanya as a Divya Desam with Devaraja Perumal and Harilakshmi Thayar

title: Varadarāja's Six Words to Rāmānuja
description: Through Tirukkacci Nambi, the deity Varadarāja answers young Rāmānuja's doubts with six sentences that become foundational axioms of Viśiṣṭādvaita Śrī Vaiṣṇavism

title: 2010 proclamation of Ravidāssia religion and Amritbāṇī
description: In 2010 at Seer Govardhanpur the Ravidāssia community proclaims a distinct religion with its own scripture, the Amritbani Guru Ravidass Ji (~240 hymns)

title: Abhayadatta compiles the lives of the 84 Mahāsiddhas
description: 12th-c. Abhayadatta Śrī's Caturaśīti-siddha-pravṛtti fixes the canonical roster of the 84 perfected tantric adepts, transmitted to Tibet as the Grub-thob brgyad-cu

title: Akka Mahadevi tested at the Anubhava Mantapa
description: Akka Mahadevi's nakedness scandalizes the orthodox assembly; Allama Prabhu interrogates her and she wins the debate, establishing herself as a fully realized Sharane

title: Annamācārya's Telugu saṅkīrtana corpus
description: The 15th-century padakavi Annamayya composes thousands of saṅkīrtana on Veṅkaṭeśvara, centring the deity in Telugu devotional song; copper-plate songs survive in the temple

title: Chaitanya rediscovers the holy sites of Braj
description: Making Jagannatha Puri his base, Chaitanya tours South India and then Vrindavana/Braj, rediscovering the lost holy sites of Krishna's lila

title: Chand's left-handed worship establishes Manasā's cult
description: Chand finally offers the pūjā-flower with his left hand while looking away, grudgingly establishing Manasā's worship among humans

title: Composition of the Major Puranas
description: The major Puranas are composed c. 300-1000 CE, encoding the yuga/manvantara/kalpa cosmology, avatar theology and the Kali-Yuga decline narrative
source: Vishnu, Bhagavata, Shiva, Markandeya, Devi-Bhagavata Puranas

title: Deification as Subhadrā of the Jagannātha Purī triad
description: Subhadrā is worshipped as a goddess flanked by Jagannātha (Kṛṣṇa) and Balabhadra (Balarāma) at Purī, riding the chariot Darpadalana in the Rath Yātrā

title: Ādi Śaṅkara Re-consecrates Bharat Mandir
description: Ādi Śaṅkarācārya re-consecrates the Bharat Mandir of Rishikesh (dedicated to Hṛṣīkeśa Nārāyaṇa) c. 789 CE on Basant Panchami

title: Diaspora spread and firewalking abroad
description: Māri carried by indentured and merchant Tamils becomes a principal diaspora goddess across Singapore, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, South Africa, Mauritius, Réunion and the Caribbean, exporting the tīmiti firewalk

title: Ellamma and Mutyalamma head a kin-group of mothers
description: Ellamma the all-mother and Mutyālamma the pearl/pox-mother lead a large kin-group of Telugu/Kannada village mothers, one Mother in many aspects

title: Establishment of Barpetā Sattra
description: Madhavadeva establishes and develops the great Barpetā Sattra, a principal seat of the Nika tradition and of post-founder organization

title: Godāvarī-māhātmya and the Siṃhastha Kumbh
description: Nāsik–Tryambak hosts the Jupiter-in-Leo Kumbh Mela at Rāmkuṇḍ and Kuśāvarta on the Dakṣiṇa Gaṅgā
source: Brahma Purāṇa Gautamī-māhātmya; Godāvarī-māhātmya; pilgrimage tradition

title: Gupta Empire & Aryabhata
description: Golden Age c. 320-550 CE; Kalidasa's literature, and Aryabhata's Aryabhatiya (499 CE) fixes the 3102 BCE Kali epoch

title: Hagiography in Mahīpati's Bhaktalīlāmṛta
description: The 18th-c. hagiographer Mahīpati recorded Rāmdās's life and miracles in the Bhaktalīlāmṛta, a principal devotional source

title: Hoysaḷa–Vijayanagara–Woḍeyar building and endowment
description: Successive dynasties endow the temples, raise the gopuras and Rāya-gopura and tank, fixing the site's historical clock (12th–19th c. CE)

title: Jhulelal as portable patron of the Sindhi diaspora
description: After the 1947 Partition displaced Sindhi Hindus from Sindh, Jhulelal became the central portable identity-marker of the scattered community
source: Daryapanthi tradition; scholarly accounts of the Sindhi diaspora

title: Matsyendranāth founds the Nāth lineage
description: Matsyendranāth (9th–10th c.) becomes the foundational human guru of the Nāth Siddha-yogī order and the Kaula yoga stream

title: Medieval consolidation of the eight as one network
description: Sri Vaishnava commentators and Pancharatra doctrine crystallise the eight into a single fixed numbered set mirroring the twelve Jyotirlingas
source: Divya Suri Carita; Pancharatra Agama; medieval Vaishnava commentary

title: Māṇikkavācakar's initiation and the horse legend
description: Sent to buy cavalry horses, Māṇikkavācakar meets Śiva disguised as a guru, is initiated and spends the treasury gold building a temple; Śiva sends jackals turned to horses and floods the Vaigai to vindicate him

title: Nakkirar Composes the Tirumurukarruppatai
description: The Sangam poet Nakkirar composes the Tirumurukarruppatai, the founding charter enumerating Murugan's six abodes, c. 2nd-4th c. CE

title: Nīlakaṇṭha Somayājī and the Tantrasaṅgraha (1501)
description: Kerala-school systematiser who proposed a geo-heliocentric model with five planets orbiting the Sun, predating Tycho Brahe's scheme

title: Pañcavaṭī as living Rāma-tīrtha and Kumbh city
description: Nāsik/Pañcavaṭī becomes a tīrtha-cluster (Sītā Gufā, Tapovan, Kapāleśvara, Rāmkuṇḍ, Kālārām) and one of four Siṃhastha Kumbh cities
source: Gautamī-māhātmya (Brahma Purāṇa); Nāsik sthala-mahātmya; pilgrimage and historical record

title: Pan-Indian veneration and the two-Nāmdevs question
description: Venerated as Sant Nāmdev in Maharashtra and Bhagat Nāmdev in Sikh/Punjabi tradition, his cross-regional dual corpus later spawns the disputed two-Nāmdevs hypothesis

title: Swaminarayan codifies the Swaminarayan Sampradaya
description: The Gujarati ascetic Swaminarayan forms the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, preaching strict ethics and Krishna-Narayana devotion and codifying conduct in the Shikshapatri and teachings in the Vachanamrut

title: Vaiṣṇo Devī as major modern Śākta pilgrimage
description: The Trikūṭa cave-shrine above Katra becomes one of the most-visited goddess shrines in India, drawing millions yearly under the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board
source: Living Vaiṣṇo Devī Yātrā tradition; Wikipedia

title: Śaṅkara's Two Bhāṣyas
description: Ādi Śaṅkara composes two distinct commentaries on the Kena — a pada-bhāṣya (word-gloss) and a vākya-bhāṣya (sentence commentary)

title: Akka Mahadevi merges into Chennamallikarjuna at Srisailam
description: Akka Mahadevi journeys to the Kadalivana forest at Srisailam seeking final union with Chennamallikarjuna, where she is said to have merged into the divine

title: Arunagirinatar Sings the Thiruppugazh
description: The 15th-century saint Arunagirinatar composes the Thiruppugazh and companion hymns, the great medieval bhakti layer over the Arupadai network

title: Building of the Konārk Sun Temple
description: King Narasiṃhadeva I of the Eastern Gaṅga dynasty builds the colossal Konārk Sun Temple as Sūrya's stone chariot with seven horses and twenty-four wheels around 1250 CE

title: Chaitanya composes the Shikshashtakam and deputes the Six Goswamis
description: Chaitanya leaves the eight-verse Shikshashtakam summarizing his mission and deputes the Six Goswamis of Vrindavana to recover Braj and codify Gaudiya teaching in Sanskrit

title: Gorakhnāth organizes the Nāth order and haṭha-yoga
description: Gorakhnāth, disciple of Matsyendranāth, organizes the Nāth Sampradāya and haṭha-yoga and founds the Kānphaṭa yogī order and the Gorakhpur seat

title: Gupta Empire Golden Age
description: The Gupta Empire (c. 320-550 CE) sees classical Sanskrit literature, Aryabhata fixing the 3102 BCE Kali epoch astronomically (Aryabhatiya, 499 CE), and the crystallization of classical Hinduism

title: Jai Singh II's Jantar Mantar observatories
description: Rajput ruler who built five masonry observatories (c. 1724–1738) with giant fixed instruments and compiled the Zīj-i Muhammad Shāhī, fusing Sanskrit, Islamic and European astronomy
source: histories of Indian astronomy; Zīj-i Muhammad Shāhī

title: Kausalyā-suprabhātam veneration
description: The Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam opens by invoking Kausalyā, making her name the liturgical first word of dawn in Viṣṇu temples
source: Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam; cf. Vālmīki Bāla Kāṇḍa

title: Māṇikkavācakar merges into Naṭarāja at Chidambaram
description: After defeating a Buddhist delegation at Chidambaram and restoring a mute princess's speech, Māṇikkavācakar sings the Accō Patikam and merges into the form of Naṭarāja, attaining liberation

title: Modern Dalit assertion and Jayantī devotion
description: Ravidās becomes a principal saint-icon of Dalit self-respect; Guru Ravidāss Jayantī (Māgh Pūrṇimā) is celebrated across Punjab and the diaspora
