source: Omvedt Seeking Begumpura; Grokipedia Guru Ravidass Jayanti [scholarly/folk]

title: Selective Sanskritization into Durgā/Kālī/Pārvatī
description: Village mothers are progressively identified with Purāṇic Devī forms and their buffalo-bali read as Mahiṣāsura-mardana, contested by reform that replaces blood-sacrifice with vegetarian worship
actors: Village mothers; Durgā/Kālī/Pārvatī; reform temple managements

title: Shastriji Maharaj founds BAPS
description: Shastriji Maharaj founds BAPS on the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, consecrating murtis at Bochasan on 5 June 1907

title: Tamil Bhakti — Alvars & Nayanars
description: 5th-9th c. CE earliest organized Bhakti movement: 12 Alvars (Vaishnava) and 63 Nayanars (Shaiva) sing Tamil hymns

title: The historical Somnath temple (recorded-history clock)
description: The Somnath shrine is repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt, sacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025-26 CE and last reconsecrated in 1951

title: The Saṃhati schisms into four branches
description: After the founders' era the Ekaśaraṇa movement fractures into four Saṃhatis (Brahma, Puruṣa, Nika, Kala) led by distinct successors differing on cāri-vastu emphasis and Brahminism

title: Vijayanagara woven Kiṣkindhā geography
description: The Vijayanagara empire (1336–1565 CE) read its capital as Rāma's Kiṣkindhā, building the Virūpākṣa and Hazāra Rāma (Rāmacandra) temples and fixing the Hampi-Anegundi identification of the vānara kingdom
source: Vijayanagara-era Rāma tradition; Hazāra Rāma temple reliefs; epigraphy [scholarly]

title: Adi Shankara Founds Advaita
description: Shankara (c. 700-750 CE scholarly) systematizes Advaita Vedanta and founds the four mathas; traditional date 509-477 BCE

title: Agastya Founds Tamil Grammar (the Agattiyam)
description: Tamil tradition makes Agastya author of the lost Agattiyam, earliest Tamil grammar, and head of the First Tamil Sangam at Madurai teaching Tolkappiyar

title: Anthologization of vachanas under Vijayanagara
description: In the 15th-16th c. the scattered vachanas are collected and the Shunyasampadane and other compilations produced, fixing the canon and the dramatized memory of the Anubhava Mantapa

title: Canonization of the Tirumuṟai
description: The rediscovered Tēvāram palm-leaves are organized into Books 1–7 by Nambiyāṇḍār Nambi under Chola Rājarāja I, completed by Cēkkiḻār's Periya Purāṇam (c. 1135) as Book 12

title: Death of Chaitanya at Puri
description: Chaitanya dies at Puri in 1534, traditions holding he merged into the Jagannatha/Tota-Gopinatha deity or drowned in the sea in ecstasy

title: Gangamma and Reṇukā-Yellammā as elaborated instances
description: Two village goddesses outgrew the local frame into pan-regional cults with their own pilgrimage centres at Tirupati and Saundatti
actors: Gangamma of Tirupati; Reṇukā–Yellammā of Saundatti
source: Regional cult studies; Deccan folk tradition

title: Rise of the Tamil Bhakti Movement
description: The 12 Alvars and 63 Nayanars (5th-9th c. CE) sing Tamil hymns to Vishnu and Shiva, forming the earliest organized Bhakti movement that later spreads north

title: Two clocks synchronised at the Kali-yuga epoch
description: The siddhānta astronomers' adoption of the 3102 BCE Kali-yuga epoch and the 4,320,000-year Mahāyuga welds the historical astronomical clock to the cyclic cosmological clock

title: Yijing reports the grammarian Bhartṛhari
description: the 7th-c. Chinese pilgrim's notice anchors the Vākyapadīya author, whose identity with the Śatakatraya poet remains unresolved [scholarly] [disputed]

title: Yogananda founds the Self-Realization Fellowship
description: Yogananda comes to the U.S. in 1920 and founds the Self-Realization Fellowship to bring Kriya Yoga to the West, later authoring the influential Autobiography of a Yogi (1946)

title: Adi Shankara Founds the Four Mathas
description: Adi Shankara (c. 700-750 CE) establishes Advaita Vedanta, founds the four mathas, and writes the Brahmasutra-bhashya (traditional Kanchi dating of 509-477 BCE disputed)

title: Idol-Shifting to Bet Dvaraka (1551)
description: When raiders threatened Dvaraka, the deity is said to have been moved to Bet Dvaraka for safety, anchoring Bet's claim as Krishna's home

title: Prabhupada founds ISKCON
description: Arriving in New York in 1965, Prabhupada founds ISKCON in July 1966, spreading Hare Krishna sankirtana worldwide and translating the Bhagavad Gita As It Is and the Srimad Bhagavatam
source: Bhagavad Gita As It Is; Srimad Bhagavatam

title: Ramanuja and Madhva — Vedanta Acharyas
description: Ramanuja (~11th-12th c.) founds Vishishtadvaita; Madhva (1238-1317) founds Dvaita and the Udupi Krishna matha

title: Mahmud of Ghazni Sacks Somnath
description: The Somnath temple is sacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025–26 CE, beginning its history as the most-destroyed-and-rebuilt temple, last rebuilt in 1951

title: Marine Excavations at Dvaraka (1983-1990)
description: The NIO Marine Archaeology Unit under S. R. Rao excavates submerged structures, a jetty and stone anchors off Dvaraka and Bet Dvaraka, dating a port to c. 1500 BCE
source: S. R. Rao, The Lost City of Dvaraka (1999); NIO surveys

title: North Indian Bhakti & Sant Movement
description: 14th-17th c. vernacular devotion: Kabir, Mirabai, Chaitanya, Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas), Surdas, Tukaram

title: Shalivahana's victory inaugurates the Shaka era
description: An alternate Gudi Padwa charter marks Shalivahana's victory and the start of the Shalivahana Shaka era

title: Aurangzeb Demolishes and Ahilyabai Rebuilds Kashi Vishwanath
description: Aurangzeb demolishes the Kashi Vishwanath temple in 1669 CE, and Ahilyabai Holkar rebuilds the present temple in 1780

title: Founding of the Khalsa
description: On Vaisakhi in 1699 Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa, an event mapped onto the Mesha Sankranti harvest/new-year date

title: Madhva Founds Dvaita Vedanta
description: Madhva (1238-1317 CE) founds Dvaita Vedanta and the Udupi Krishna matha, holding an irreducible difference between jiva and Brahman

title: Tulsidas composes the Hanuman Chalisa
description: Goswami Tulsidas composes the 40-verse Awadhi Hanuman Chalisa and the Ramcharitmanas (1574), crystallizing North Indian Hanuman bhakti

title: Vijayanagara & Maratha Hindu Sovereignty
description: Vijayanagara (1336-1646) last great southern Hindu empire; Shivaji (1630-1680) frames Hindavi Swarajya

title: Brahmo Samaj Founded
description: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founds the Brahmo Samaj on 20 Aug 1828, Calcutta — monotheist, anti-sati, anti-caste reform

title: Kabir's Nirguna Bhakti
description: Kabir (c. 1440-1518 CE), weaver-poet of the nirguna Sant tradition, composes dohas critiquing both Hindu ritualism and Islamic legalism, later claimed by Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs

title: Sumitra Defeated by Mahapadma Nanda
description: Sumitra, traditionally the last Ikshvaku king of Ayodhya, is defeated by Mahapadma Nanda of Magadha and flees to Rohtas, ending the dynasty

title: Vasishtha's fire-pit and the Agnikula origin
description: At Mt. Abu, Vasishtha's fire-pit (agni-kunda) gives rise to the Agnikula Rajput-origin legend

title: Arya Samaj Founded
description: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founds the Arya Samaj in 1875 with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas'

title: Birth of Santoshi Ma
description: Santoshi Ma, a goddess of recent popular origin said to be a daughter of Ganesha, emerges through 1960s vrat literature and is propelled to fame by the 1975 film Jai Santoshi Maa

title: Guru Nanak Founds Sikhism
description: Guru Nanak (1469-1539 CE) founds Sikhism within the Sant milieu, teaching nirguna devotion

title: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Gaudiya Vaishnavism
description: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534 CE) leads ecstatic Krishna sankirtana in Bengal, founding the inspiration for Gaudiya Vaishnavism (Achintya Bheda Abheda)

title: Manjunatha Linga Installed at Dharmasthala
description: A Shiva linga from Kadri is later installed and named Manjunatha (attributed to Vadiraja Tirtha's 16th-c. influence), fusing folk daiva worship, Jain stewardship and Shaiva temple

title: Vivekananda & Ramakrishna Mission
description: Vivekananda gives the 1893 Chicago Parliament address and founds the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897

title: Composition of the Adhyatma Ramayana
description: The Advaita-Vedanta Adhyatma Ramayana, recasting Rama as supreme Brahman, is composed (c. 13th-15th c. CE) and embedded in the Brahmanda Purana

title: Dayananda founds the Arya Samaj condemning murti-puja
description: Dayananda Sarasvati founds the Arya Samaj in 1875, condemning image-worship as un-Vedic and calling Hindus back to nirguna theism

title: Modern Global Hindu Movements
description: 20th c. global gurus and movements: Yogananda, ISKCON (Prabhupada, 1966), TM, and yoga's worldwide export

title: Shankara founds Advaita and the Dashanami orders
description: Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) composes the Brahma Sutra Bhashya, organizes renunciate monks into the ten Dashanami orders, and founds four cardinal mathas
source: Brahma Sutra Bhashya; Advaita matha tradition

title: Sri Yukteswar's Ascending-Yuga Variant
description: Sri Yukteswar (The Holy Science, 1894) claims Kali ended ~1700 CE and we are now in ascending Dvapara Yuga

title: Vijayanagara Empire
description: The Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1646), the last great Hindu empire of the south, sustains temple Hinduism through the Mughal era

title: Caitanya Mahāprabhu Rediscovers the Lost Tīrthas of Braj
description: Visiting Braj c. 1515, Caitanya Mahāprabhu locates lost sites like Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Imlītalā by trance and deputes the Six Goswamis to recover the tīrthas and write the theology of bhakti

title: Lakulisha founds the Pashupata sampradaya
description: The last of the 28 Yogeshvara avatars, Lakulisha, descends as the historical founder of the Pashupata sampradaya

title: Rūpa Goswami Recovers the Govinda-deva Deity
description: Rūpa Goswami recovers the Rādhā-Govinda-deva deity at Gomā-ṭīlā c. 1525; the great red-sandstone temple is built in 1590 under Mān Singh of Amber with Akbar's patronage

title: Shivaji and the Maratha Resurgence
description: Shivaji (1630-1680) frames Hindu sovereignty as Hindavi Swarajya, leading the Maratha resurgence

title: Founding of the Brahmo Samaj
description: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founds the Brahmo Samaj on 20 Aug 1828 in Calcutta, a monotheist, anti-idolatry, anti-sati, anti-caste reform movement
actors: Raja Ram Mohan Roy; Dwarkanath Tagore

title: Rādhā-Ramaṇa Self-Manifests for Gopāla Bhaṭṭa
description: The Rādhā-Ramaṇa deity self-manifests from a śālagrāma-śilā for Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Goswami in 1542

title: Founding of the Arya Samaj
description: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founds the Arya Samaj in 1875 in Bombay with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas,' rejecting Puranic ritual and idolatry, and publishes Satyarth Prakash

title: Svāmī Haridāsa Manifests Banke Bihārī
description: The singer-saint Svāmī Haridāsa manifests the combined Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa deity Banke Bihārī at Nidhivana and founds the Haridāsī Sampradāya of devotional music

title: Adi Shankara Consecrates Mukambika at Kollur
description: Adi Shankara is said to have consecrated the Goddess Mukambika at Kollur, strongly associating the svayambhu shrine with him

title: Vallabhācārya Rediscovers Śrī Nāthajī on Govardhana
description: Vallabhācārya, founder of the Puṣṭimārga, rediscovers the self-manifest Śrī Nāthajī (the Govardhana-dhāraṇa form) on Govardhana hill, later moved to Nathdwara

title: Vivekananda's Chicago Address and Ramakrishna Mission
description: Swami Vivekananda delivers his 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions address in Chicago and founds the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, carrying Vedanta to the West

title: Sri Yukteswar's Ascending-Yuga Reframing
description: Sri Yukteswar in The Holy Science (1894) holds Kali Yuga ended ~1700 CE and we are now in an ascending Dvapara Yuga on a 24,000-year precessional cycle, reframing the entire 'we are in Kali' premise

title: Founding of ISKCON
description: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada founds ISKCON in 1966, spreading Gaudiya Vaishnavism worldwide

title: Rise of Hindu Nationalism
description: Hindu nationalism crystallizes through Savarkar's Hindutva (1923), the RSS (1925) and the VHP (1964), shaping diaspora temple-building and live heritage debates

title: Composition of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas
description: Tulsidas begins the Awadhi Ramcharitmanas on Ramanavami 1574 CE in Ayodhya, the dominant North-Indian bhakti retelling and basis of Ramlila

title: Ramanuja composes the Sri Bhashya
description: Ramanuja (1017-1137 CE) establishes Vishishtadvaita, reading souls and matter as the real body of Brahman

title: Ramanuja's Saptavidha-anupapatti against Advaita maya
description: Ramanuja launches the seven great untenables against the Advaita avidya/maya in his Sri Bhashya, the most famous demolition of the doctrine

title: Shankara founds the four cardinal mathas
description: Adi Shankara organizes renunciates into the Dashanami orders and founds four mathas at Shringeri, Puri, Dvaraka, and Jyotir/Badri, each headed by a Shankaracharya

title: Woodroffe publishes The Serpent Power
description: Sir John Woodroffe (Arthur Avalon) translates the Shat-chakra-nirupana in 1919, fixing the now-dominant seven-chakra image

title: Ramcharitmanas Inscribed on UNESCO Memory of the World
description: The Ramcharitmanas is inscribed on UNESCO's MOWCAP Regional Register on 7-8 May 2024 in Ulaanbaatar, alongside the Panchatantra and Sahridayaloka-Locana

title: Basava founds the Virashaiva/Lingayat tradition
description: Basava (12th c.) founds the Virashaiva/Lingayat movement rejecting temple icons in favor of the personal ishta-linga

title: Composition of Kamban's Iramavataram
description: Kamban composes the Tamil Iramavataram (Kambaramayanam) under Chola patronage c. 12th c. CE, recasting Rama as full incarnate Vishnu and ending at his coronation

title: Madhva founds Dvaita Tattvavada
description: Madhva (1238-1317 CE) systematizes Dvaita with the five eternal differences, teaching eternal soul-God distinction

title: Self-sacrifice of the Elder Brothers (Annanmar Katai)
description: The twin Tamil warrior-brothers Ponnar and Cankar of Ponnivala, serving Shiva/Vishnu, willingly sacrifice themselves to the gods, their sister Tankal performing their funeral rites; they become guardian deities

title: Martyrdom and deification of Madurai Veeran
description: The low-caste warrior-hero Madurai Veeran is executed and dismembered over a forbidden love, then deified as a Tamil guardian deity worshipped with his consorts

title: Death and deification of Pabuji
description: The Rajput hero-chieftain Pabuji Rathod, a camel-rescuer regarded as an incarnation of Lakshmana, dies in battle and is deified as a grama-devata and camel-protector god

title: Saga of Devnarayan
description: Devnarayan, deified hero-king of the Gujar community held to be an incarnation of Vishnu, avenges the Bagaravat brothers and is worshipped via the giant phad scroll

title: Romance of Dhola and Maru
description: Dhola (prince Sal Kunvar) and Marvani, betrothed as children and separated, are reunited across desert and rival queens in the Rajasthani romance-epic
source: Dhola Maru ra Duha (Rajasthani ballad cycle)

title: The 52 battles of Alha and Udal
description: The brother-heroes Alha and Udal, Banaphar commanders of King Paramardideva of Mahoba, fight their 52 battles culminating in resistance to Prithviraj Chauhan (assoc. 1182 CE); Alha is held never to have died

title: Lakulisa founds the Pasupata order
description: Lakulisa (c. 2nd c. CE) founds the ash-smeared Lakulisa-Pasupata ascetic order, among the earliest organised Saiva sects

title: The Battle of Palnadu
description: The fratricidal Battle of Palnadu (c. 1178-1182 CE) pits two factions of Palnadu chiefs; statesman-warrior Brahma Nayudu preaches an anti-caste order and the boy-hero Balachandrudu dies heroically, the fallen worshipped as the Palnati Virulu
source: Palnati Virula Katha; Srinatha's Palnati Vira Caritra

title: Miracles of Male Madeshvara
description: The miracle-working Virashaiva siddha Madeshvara of the Male Madeshvara hills, worshipped as a form of Shiva, is celebrated in the Kannada oral epic

title: Behula recovers Lakhindar's life (Manasa-mangal)
description: The merchant Chand Sadagar refuses serpent-goddess Manasa's worship, so she kills his son Lakhindar by snakebite on his wedding night, until the widowed bride Behula floats the corpse to the gods, wins his life back, and forces Chand to worship Manasa

title: Vasugupta receives the Siva-Sutras
description: Vasugupta (9th c.) receives and composes the Siva-Sutras and Spanda-Karika, founding the textual basis of non-dual Kashmir Saivism

title: Chandi establishes her worship (Chandi-mangal)
description: The fierce Durga-form Chandi establishes her worship among hunters and merchants through the Kalaketu hunter and Dhanapati/Srimanta merchant cycles

title: Composition of the Krittivasi Ramayan
description: Krittibas Ojha composes the Bengali Srirama Panchali (15th c. CE), the most beloved Bengali retelling and charter-text of Bengali Durga Puja

title: Maṇḍana Misra converted to Advaita by Sankara
description: The Mimamsaka Maṇḍana Misra is, by tradition, converted to Advaita Vedanta by Sankara, a hinge moment between Mimamsa and Vedanta

title: Vallabha founds Shuddhadvaita and Pushti-marga
description: Vallabha (1479-1531 CE) teaches pure non-dualism with the world as real emanation of Krishna and the path of grace

title: Bonbibi protects the Sundarbans against Dakshin Ray
description: The forest-goddess Bonbibi protects honey-gatherers and woodcutters of the Sundarbans against the tiger-demon Dakshin Ray, her cult shared by Hindus and Muslims

title: Sankara composes the Brahma-sutra-bhasya
description: Adi Sankara (c. 8th c.) composes his Brahma-sutra-bhasya, the oldest surviving complete commentary, founding the Advaita reading of Vedanta

title: Ramanuja writes the Sri Bhasya
description: Ramanuja (11th-12th c.) composes the Sri Bhasya on the Brahma Sutras, founding Visistadvaita and defending Pancaratra as Veda-concordant

title: Madhva writes the Dvaita commentary
description: Madhva (13th c.) composes his Brahma-sutra-bhasya and Aṇu-bhasya, founding the Dvaita dualist school of Vedanta

title: Gaṅgesa founds Navya-Nyaya
description: Gaṅgesa Upadhyaya (c. 1325, Mithila) composes the Tattva-cintamaṇi, founding the Navya-Nyaya 'New Logic' school

title: Praśastapada re-founds Vaiseṣika
description: Praśastapada (c. 4th-6th c. CE) composes the Padartha-dharma-saṃgraha, re-founding classical Vaiseṣika and introducing a creator-Isvara into the atomist system

title: Chaitanya founds Achintya-bhedabheda
description: Chaitanya (1486-1534 CE), systematized by the Gosvamis of Vrindavana, teaches inconceivable difference-and-non-difference, the basis of Gaudiya Vaishnavism

title: Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Math
description: Vivekananda, disciple of Ramakrishna, founds the Ramakrishna Math, a modern global lineage

title: Composition of Vimalasuri's Paumacariya
description: Vimalasuri composes the Paumacariya (c. 3rd-5th c. CE), the earliest extant Jain Ramayana, rationalizing the epic and reframing Rama within Jain shalakapurusha cosmology

title: Gaudapada composes the Mandukya Karika
description: Gaudapada (Shankara's parama-guru) develops ajata-vada in the earliest systematic Advaita text, holding nothing is ever truly born

title: Vikramaditya's victory founds the Vikrama era
description: The legendary Vikramaditya of Ujjain, after victory over the Shakas, founds the Vikrama Samvat era (epoch 57/58 BCE)

title: Discovery of the Paippalada Manuscripts in Odisha (1957)
description: Durgamohan Bhattacharyya discovers a well-preserved set of Paippalada palm-leaf manuscripts in Odisha in 1957, becoming the basis of the modern critical edition of the lost recension

title: Mahavira takes his first disciple Indrabhuti Gautama
description: Jains honor the Ashadha full moon as the day Mahavira took his first disciple, Indrabhuti Gautama

title: Sayana Composes the Rigveda Bhashya at Vijayanagara
description: Sayanacharya, minister-scholar at the Vijayanagara court under Bukka I and Harihara II, composes the authoritative classical commentary on the entire Rigveda with his brother Madhava

title: Adi Shankara Founds Advaita Vedanta
description: Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) systematizes non-dualist Advaita Vedanta in his bhashyas on the prasthana-trayi, teaching that Brahman alone is real and Atman=Brahman

title: Ramanuja Founds Vishishtadvaita
description: Ramanuja (c. 11th-12th c. CE) establishes qualified non-dualism, teaching Brahman (Vishnu/Narayana) qualified by real souls and matter, with bhakti and prapatti central, in his Sri Bhashya

title: Madhvacharya Founds Dvaita Vedanta
description: Madhvacharya (c. 13th c. CE) establishes dualist Tattvavada with five eternal distinctions, holding God, souls, and matter as distinct realities and liberation by grace and bhakti

title: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Founds Achintya Bheda Abheda
description: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (c. 15th-16th c. CE) founds the Gaudiya Vaishnava school of inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference of soul and God

title: Founding of Shree Siddhivinayaka, Prabhadevi
description: Contractor Lakṣmaṇ Viṭhu Pāṭīl builds the Siddhivināyaka (Gaṇeśa) temple at Prabhādevī, Mumbai, funded by the devout childless Deubāī Pāṭīl who wished other barren women might obtain children by the deity; later grown into one of India's most-visited and wealthiest temples
actors: Lakṣmaṇ Viṭhu Pāṭīl; Deubāī Pāṭīl; Gaṇeśa

title: Samādhi of Shirdi Sāī Bābā and rise of the Shirdi kṣetra
description: On 15 October 1918 the composite supra-sectarian saint Sāī Bābā of Shirdi attains samādhi; his body is interred in the Buṭī Wāḍā (built as a Kṛṣṇa temple), which becomes the Samādhi Mandir, while his Dwārakāmāī mosque, ever-burning dhuni and ūdī anchor a modern all-India Sāī pilgrimage network
actors: Sāī Bābā of Shirdi; Gopālrāo Buṭī; Govind Dabholkar ('Hemādpant')
source: Śrī Sāī Satcharita; Wikipedia, Sai Baba of Shirdi

title: Tilak popularizes public Ganesh Chaturthi
description: Lokmanya Tilak popularizes the modern mass sarvajanik Ganesh Chaturthi in Maharashtra in 1893, a datable historical layer atop the Puranic myth

title: Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath
description: The same Ashadha full moon marks the Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath, observed as Guru Purnima across Indic traditions

title: Birth-story of Bhautya Manu
description: When the sacrificial fire in sage Bhuti's ashram goes out, his disciple Shanti propitiates Agni, who rekindles the fire and grants the boon that the childless Bhuti will have a son — the future 14th Manu, Indra-Savarni/Bhautya

title: Descent of Vishnu as Dharmasetu (11th Manvantara)
description: In the 11th (Dharma-Savarni) manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Dharmasetu, born of Vaidhrita and Aryaka, to sustain cosmic order, the Manu himself being a prior manifestation of this avatar

title: Descent of Vishnu as Rishabha (9th Manvantara)
description: In the 9th (Daksha-Savarni) manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Rishabha, born of Ayushman and Ambudhara, to uphold dharma and support Indra Adbhuta and Manu Daksha-Savarni

title: Descent of Vishnu as Svadhaman (12th Manvantara)
description: In the 12th (Rudra-Savarni) manvantara the Vishnu amsha Svadhaman/Sudhaman is born of Sunrita, wife of Satyasaha, to uphold dharma and Manu Rudra-Savarni's rule

title: Descent of Vishnu as Vishvaksena (10th Manvantara)
description: In the 10th (Brahma-Savarni) manvantara Vishnu manifests as Vishvaksena, born from the womb of Vishuchi in the house of the brahmana Vishvasrishta, to assist Manu Brahma-Savarni and his friend Indra Shambhu in upholding dharma

title: Kali Yuga reaches its nadir
description: Dharma stands on one leg as mleccha and thieving kings dominate, prompting Vishnu's final descent

title: Ruci Refuses Marriage and Is Rebuked by the Pitris
description: The ascetic Ruci refuses to wed, holding household life breeds only suffering, until his ancestral Pitris appear, teach the value of the five great sacrifices and householder duty, and Ruci composes the Pitri-stotra

title: Suratha's worship of the Goddess and rebirth as Savarni
description: King Suratha, having lost his kingdom, worships Mahamaya/Durga and by her boon is destined to be reborn as Savarni, the eighth Manu

title: Bali ascends to the throne of Indra
description: As recompense for his truthfulness, the daitya king Bali becomes Indra in the Savarni manvantara, fulfilling Vishnu's Vamana-boon

title: Birth of Kalki in Shambhala
description: Vishnu is born as Kalki, son of the brahmin Vishnuyasha and Sumati, in the village of Shambhala

title: Brahma Commands Ruci to Marry
description: After Ruci performs tapas for a hundred divine years, Brahma appears and commands him to marry and beget a son destined to be a Manu

title: Close of the 14th Manvantara and end of the Kalpa
description: When Bhautya's 71 mahayugas complete, the last Manu-period and the entire Day of Brahma end, dissolving into the Night of Brahma

title: Reign of Bhautya Manu (14th Manvantara)
description: Indra-Savarni (Bhautya) presides as the fourteenth and final Manu of the current Kalpa, with Suci as Indra, seven named sages, and the avatar Brhadbhanu sustaining the age
source: Vishnu Purana III.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.33-35; Matsya Purana 9

title: Avatar Sarvabhauma enthrones Bali
description: Vishnu incarnates as Sarvabhauma, son of Devaguhya and Sarasvati, wrests Svarga from the reigning Indra and bestows it on Bali

title: Descent of Brhadbhanu (avatar of the Bhautya age)
description: Vishnu's sustaining avatar Brhadbhanu is born of Satrayana and Vitana as Hari's manifestation for the final Manvantara, though no deeds are narrated

title: Malini Given to Ruci in Marriage
description: The apsaras Pramlocha presents her daughter Malini as Ruci's bride, fulfilling Brahma's command

title: Tutelage under Parashurama and Shiva's gifts
description: The chiranjivi Parashurama teaches and arms Kalki, who receives the white horse Devadatta, the sage-parrot Shuka, and a blazing sword from Shiva

title: Bali Ascends as Indra of the Savarni Age
description: In the 8th (Savarni) manvantara the chiranjivi Bali ascends to the throne of Indra, king of the devas, fulfilling Vishnu's earlier boon

title: Birth of Manu Raucya
description: From Malini's womb is born a son of great heroism and intellect who becomes the Manu Raucya (Deva-Savarni), presiding over the 13th manvantara

title: Campaign against the adharmic and mleccha kings
description: Mounted on Devadatta with his sword, Kalki sweeps the earth slaying thieves and barbarian warlords who abandoned dharma

title: Close of the 14th Manvantara / end of the Kalpa
description: When Bhautya's 71 Mahayugas complete, the last Manu-period and the entire Day of Brahma end, closing the present Kalpa

title: Advent of Kalki
description: When adharma reaches its limit, Vishnu incarnates as Kalki in the village of Shambhala, son of the brahmana Vishnuyasha, mounting the white horse Devadatta and bearing a blazing sword from Shiva
source: Kalki Purana; Bhagavata Purana 12.2.18-19; Vishnu Purana 4.24

title: Descent of Vishnu as Sarvabhauma
description: In the 8th manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Sarvabhauma, son of Devaguhya and Sarasvati, who wrests Svarga and the office of Indra from the reigning Indra Purandara and bestows it on Bali

title: Descent of Vishnu as Yogeshvara (13th Manvantara)
description: In the 13th (Deva-Savarni/Raucya) manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Yogeshvara, born of Devahotra and Brihati, who by his mystic yoga power frees the worlds from misery

title: Night of Brahma (naimittika pralaya)
description: After the Kalpa ends the three worlds (Bhur, Bhuvar, Svar) are burned and flooded, and creation rests for one Night of Brahma before the next Kalpa dawns

title: Slaying of the demon Kali
description: Kalki and his allies wage cosmic war against Kali personified and his progeny, finally vanquishing the age-demon

title: Kalki's cleansing of the wicked
description: Kalki slaughters the mleccha and dasyu kings and robbers by the millions, exterminating the wicked who have lost all spiritual sense

title: Pramiti / Kalki prophecy in the Mahabharata
description: Markandeya foretells the brahmin destroyer Pramiti (Kalki Vishnuyasha) who slaughters the mleccha kings and re-establishes the Krita age

title: Future Collapse of the Badrinath Route and Shift to Bhavishya Badri
description: When adharma overwhelms the world, the Nara and Narayana mountains will collapse and seal the route to Badrinath, whereupon Badrinath will manifest at Bhavishya Badri, marked by the withering arm of the Joshimath Narasimha idol

title: Marriage to Padma/Padmavati and Rama
description: Kalki weds Padma (Padmavati) of Simhala, an incarnation of Lakshmi, and the princess Rama of the Brihadratha line, fathering the first kings of the new age

title: Return of Satya Yuga and the cosmic reset
description: With the destroyers gone the survivors' minds become spontaneously pure, becoming the seed-population of the next Satya Yuga, which dawns when Moon, Sun, and Jupiter together enter the asterism Pushya

title: The future Manus (Sāvarṇi and after)
description: The Madhya-bhāga details the future manvantaras — the Sāvarṇi group of Manus with their Indras, ṛṣis and devas in the second half of the present kalpa

title: Re-emergence of Devapi and Maru
description: Two immortals, Devapi of the lunar line and Maru of the solar line, who survived all four yugas in meditation at Kalapa, re-emerge to re-found the kshatriya dynasties and teach proper dharma

title: Turning of Kali Yuga into the next Satya Yuga
description: With the wicked destroyed and Kali subdued, the righteous are purified, dharma is restored on all four legs, and a new Satya Yuga dawns marked by the Sun, Moon and Jupiter conjoining in Pushya
source: Vishnu Purana 4.24; Bhagavata Purana 12.2.23-24; Kalki Purana

title: Future collapse of route and shift to Bhaviṣya Badrī
description: At the close of the age the Nara and Nārāyaṇa peaks collapse and seal the route, after which Badrinath manifests permanently at Bhaviṣya Badrī, signalled by the withering arm of the Joshimath Narsingh idol

title: Future manvantaras and the Sāvarṇi Manus
description: Account of the fourteen Manus including the future Sāvarṇi group with their Indras, ṛṣis and devas, manvantaras 8–14 of the present kalpa

title: Kalki's return and continuation of the wheel
description: His mission complete, Kalki ascends to his abode while the new royal line he founded carries the cycle into the next Mahayuga

title: Bali becomes Indra of the Savarni Manvantara
description: Bali, demoted by Vamana in the present age, is foretold to become the Indra of the future 8th (Savarni) manvantara, the classic demotion-to-promotion arc

title: Parashurama to be Kalki's preceptor
description: Parashurama is prophesied to reappear at Kali's end as the preceptor of the Kalki avatara, closing the cosmic loop into the next Satya Yuga

title: The pralaya and final dissolution
description: The Vishnu Purana describes the naimittika, prakritika, and atyantika dissolutions, with yoga as the road to moksha at the kalpa- and Brahma-life boundaries

title: Kalki closes the Kali age
description: The Kalki avatara destroys the mleccha kings and restores the Krita-yuga, ending the age

title: Kalki prophecy
description: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa and Kalki Purāṇa prophesy the future Kalki avatāra of Viṣṇu who will end Kali Yuga

title: Preceptor of Kalki
description: As a cirañjīvi surviving into Kali Yuga, Paraśurāma initiates and arms Kalki, the tenth avatāra, closing the Daśāvatāra loop

title: Prakritika Pralaya — the Great Dissolution
description: At the end of Brahma's 100-year life the cosmos collapses in reverse order of emanation, each element reabsorbed into its subtler source until only Prakriti and Brahman remain

title: Death of Brahma and birth of a new Brahma
description: After 311.04 trillion years Brahma is reabsorbed; the cosmos rests in Maha-Vishnu, and after an equal span a new Brahma is born to begin the next Mahakalpa

title: Bali becomes Indra in the future Savarni manvantara
description: The demon-king Bali, demoted by Vamana in the present age, is foretold to become Indra in the 8th (Savarni) manvantara — the demotion-to-promotion arc

title: Kalki ends Kali Yuga and restores Satya
description: At Kali's close the Kalki avatara destroys adharma and ushers in a new Satya Yuga, restarting the Mahayuga cycle
source: Bhagavata Purana 12.2, Kalki Purana, Vishnu Purana 4.24

title: Kalki avatara descends
description: At Kali's end the Lord descends as Kalki, son of Viṣṇuyasas in Sambhala, to destroy the wicked and inaugurate a new Satya Yuga

title: Eleven Rudras emerge from Saṅkarṣaṇa's brows at pralaya
description: At cosmic dissolution, eleven three-eyed trident-bearing Rudras emerge from between Ananta-Saṅkarṣaṇa's wrath-knit eyebrows to annihilate the entire creation

title: Kalki ends Kali Yuga
description: At the close of Kali Yuga, Vishnu will be born as Kalki, son of Vishnuyashas in Shambhala, riding the white horse Devadatta, destroying the wicked, defeating the demon Kali, and inaugurating the next Satya Yuga
source: Bhagavata Purana 1.3.25, 12.2; Kalki Purana; Vishnu Purana 4.24

title: Naimittika Pralaya — the Night of Brahma
description: At each kalpa's end seven suns and the Samvartaka fire scorch the three worlds, floods drown them into one ocean, and the universe is withdrawn into Narayana sleeping on Shesha until the next dawn

title: Maha-pralaya at the end of Brahma's life
description: When Brahma's 100 years complete, twelve suns and the Samvartaka fire scorch the worlds, a deluge floods the cosmos, and all tattvas including Brahma reabsorb in reverse order into unmanifest Prakriti

title: Prakritika Pralaya — reverse-order elemental collapse
description: At the end of Brahma's life each element loses its quality and merges into its cause back to Prakriti, dissolving everything manifest including Brahma into Purusha/Brahman

title: Birth of a new Brahma after Maha-pralaya
description: After a span equal to Brahma's life, a new Brahma is generated from Maha-Vishnu's navel-lotus and the entire Mahakalpa cycle begins anew, time being beginningless and endless

title: Kalpa-ending night of Brahma after the 14th manvantara
description: At the close of the 14th (Indra-savarni/Bhautya) manvantara comes the Kalpa-ending night of Brahma (naimittika pralaya)

title: "As in dance, so in painting"
description: the Citrasūtra's governing dictum yathā nṛtte tathā citre makes the painted body a frozen moment of dance, fixing gesture, proportion, and rasa as the shared grammar of the visual and performing arts

title: "Hence I depart not" — the refusal of heaven
description: when Dharma and Indra arrive with the celestial car, Vipaścit declines to ascend while thousands cry to him for relief, holding compassion for the distressed above the joys of Svarga

title: "I am lord only of the rest"
description: Yama confesses he governs all mankind by Brahmā's appointment save the Vaiṣṇavas, over whom Hari alone rules — prabhur aham anya-nṛṇāṃ na vaiṣṇavānām

title: "If you are cut, do you not bleed?"
description: the thoṭṭam's charter verse: Brahmin and Pulaya bleed the same red blood, so caste has no ground in the body

title: "The air that clings to thy body"
description: the tortured souls beg the king to stay, revealing that the cool wind was his own presence, whose radiated merit dispels their burning and pain

title: "The whole earth is one family"
description: the Hitopadeśa's friendship-book preserves the famed verse vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam, holding that to the noble-hearted no one is stranger

title: "We drink the same water"
description: the argument extends to shared sun, water and toddy, dissolving the fictions of tīṇḍal and high/low caste

title: A brahmin refuses Indra's throne
description: Indra descends to Kālikā-grāma to check a mortal whose recitation of Gītā chapter 18 rivals his merit, and the reciter spurns Indra's seat to choose Viṣṇu-sāyujya

title: A charter for shared karmic fruit
description: Somaka's insistence on shouldering a sin committed for his sake stages the epic's loophole of loyalty, prefiguring Yudhiṣṭhira's own refusal to enter heaven alone
source: Mahābhārata, Vana Parva CXXVIII; Svargārohaṇa Parva

title: A lifetime of sons and grandsons
description: over many years Suśīlā bears the king many sons who grow, marry, and give her grandsons — an entire ripening life of saṃsāric love lived inside the illusion

title: Abhijit slips from the sky
description: the 28th nakṣatra Abhijit falls from heaven while contesting seniority with Rohiṇī, the mythic charter behind the star and its victorious midday muhūrta

title: Agastya brings Tamil and founds the Siddhar lineage
description: The sage Agastya, crossing south of the Vindhyas, is held in Tamil tradition to be the ādi-guru of the Siddhars and patron of Siddha medicine

title: Agni reveals the Agni Purāṇa to Vasiṣṭha
description: The fire-god Agni reveals the encyclopedic Agni Purāṇa, the essence of all sciences, to the sage Vasiṣṭha, who transmits it down the chain to Vyāsa and the Sūta

title: Ajamila's Fall through the Dasi
description: The virtuous brahmana Ajamila of Kanyakubja is overpowered by lust at the sight of a drunken dasi, casts off his wedded wife, and descends into a life of theft and deceit

title: Akūpāra the tortoise remembers
description: the oldest being on earth weeps and knows Indradyumna, for the lake he dwells in was scooped out by the hooves of the countless cattle the king gave away in charity

title: Alakṣmī expelled by the Kārtika lamps
description: Jyeṣṭhā-Alakṣmī, risen from the churning before Lakṣmī and assigned to dwell in filth and strife, is driven out by the swept house and rows of lamps of the Kārtika/Dīpāvalī vow that invite Śrī in

title: Alarka's 66,000-year youthful reign
description: Alarka, son of Pratardana and (in the Mārkaṇḍeya splice) of Madālasā, rules the earth 66,000 years while remaining young, then renounces after Dattātreya's instruction

title: Anaraṇya renounces his throne for Śivaloka
description: grieving the loss of his favourite daughter, King Anaraṇya of the Indra-Sāvarṇi line abandons the kingdom for forest penance and attains Śivaloka, leaving his son Kīrtimān to rule

title: Annam Brahma — food revealed as Brahman
description: Varuṇa sends his son Bhṛgu into austerity, who first realizes that food (anna) itself is Brahman before ascending through breath, mind and bliss

title: Annapūrṇā feeds Śiva at Kāśī
description: in the poem's Deva-frame the Great Goddess as Annadā fills the begging Śiva's bowl, the anna-theology that the giver of food sustains even the Absolute

title: Annapūrṇā feeds Śiva in Kāśī
description: Pārvatī as the goddess who is full of food gives alms to Śiva himself, who begs at her ladle; no one in her city goes hungry, and Śaṅkara enshrines her in the Annapūrṇā-stotra

title: Āpaduddhāraka — the rescuer from calamity
description: invoked through the Vaṭuka-Bhairava Stotra and kavaca, the boy-Bhairava lifts devotees out of disease, enemies, debt, fear, and untimely death

title: Apotheosis of the impaled god
description: his wrongful, violent death on the stake generates godhood, making Kāttavarāyaṉ a kāval teyvam whose stake becomes his throne and emblem — the South Indian death-and-deification engine

title: Aśokasundarī born of the Kalpavṛkṣa
description: lonely Pārvatī voices her wish before the wish-fulfilling tree, which produces a maiden of surpassing beauty named for ending the goddess's grief (śoka), reckoned a Śaiva daughter beside Gaṇeśa and Skanda

title: Atri rescued from the burning pit
description: cast into a fiery chasm (ṛbīsa) by his enemies, Atri Saptavadhri is cooled and freed unharmed by the Aśvins with a coolness-giving draught

title: Atri restores the darkened Sun
description: the Āsura Svarbhānu strikes Sūrya with darkness and the ṛṣi Atri alone finds and re-fixes the sun in the sky by the fourth brahman-formula — the Vedic prototype of the Rāhu eclipse-myth

title: Aṭṭa-vīraṭṭāṉam — the eight feat-shrines
description: a closed Tamil set of eight Śiva temples, each fixing one of his fierce cosmos-ordering deeds to a named delta town, the presiding liṅga called Vīraṭṭāṉeśvarar

title: Bala consents to be the gods' sacrificial victim
description: The devas ask the truth-bound asura to serve as the pashu of their yajna, and Bala freely offers his own body to his enemies' rite
source: Garuda Purana, Purva-khanda gem chapters; Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha

title: Bala's ascendancy over the gods
description: In the primordial deva–asura war the asura Bala (Vala) grows invincible and the devas, unable to slay him in battle, resort to stratagem

title: Bala's blood and eyes fall on Lanka
description: The asura's blood falls into the Ravanaganga river of Simhala and his eyes on the same island, chartering Ceylon's ruby-gravels and blue-sapphire beds
source: Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha, ruby and sapphire sections

title: Bala's dismembered body becomes the gem-seeds
description: Slain as a sanctified victim, Bala's members turn into the seeds of the gems: blood→ruby, teeth→pearl, bile→emerald, eyes→sapphire, bones→diamond
source: Garuda Purana, Purva-khanda chs. ~68–70; Agni Purana 246

title: Bāṇāī the Dhangar shepherdess
description: Khaṇḍobā wins his second wife, the Dhangar shepherdess Bāṇāī, in pastoral guise, writing the pastoral layer into the high god's own biography

title: Between ghost and god
description: a fierce spirit or fallen pastoral hero, bound to a devotee and propitiated by possession and blood-sacrifice, is progressively deified into a temple-god and equated with Bhairava

title: Bhadrā bound into the karaṇa cycle
description: the fierce daughter of Sūrya and Chāyā, sister of Śani, is assigned by Brahmā a fixed seat as the Viṣṭi karaṇa so her destructive hours can be known and avoided

title: Bhadrāyu revived with holy ash
description: the poisoned, forest-abandoned infant of queen Sumati dies and is resuscitated by the yogin Ṛṣabha with Śiva's bhasma, named Bhadrāyu, and taught the Śiva-kavaca

title: Bhakti above the sacrificial fire
description: the Bhāgavata makes the yajña-patnī episode its charter that loving surrender outranks Vedic ritualism, with disqualified women reaching the Lord where learned twice-born ritualists fail

title: Bhṛgu curses Viṣṇu to mortal births
description: After Viṣṇu beheads Śukra's mother sheltering the war-broken asuras, Bhṛgu curses him to be born again and again among mortals — the Matsya's charter for the human avatāras

title: Bhṛgu revives Kāvyamātā
description: Bhṛgu sprinkles water from his kamaṇḍalu and restores his beheaded wife to life, though the curse on Viṣṇu still stands

title: Bhṛgu's curse dooms Viṣṇu to mortal births
description: finding his wife slain, Bhṛgu curses Viṣṇu to be born again and again among men and to live long separated from his consort — the charter of the avatāras

title: Bhṛgu's word makes Vītahavya a Brāhmaṇa
description: the defeated king takes refuge with Bhṛgu, who tells the pursuing Pratardana "there are only Brāhmaṇas here" — and the true word of the ṛṣi transmutes the Kṣatriya into a Brāhmaṇa on the instant

title: Bhṛṅgī cursed to be fleshless
description: the Śiva-only gaṇa defends his lord as cheated, and the furious Goddess curses him to skin and bone, the etiology of his skeletal three-legged form

title: Bhujyu saved from the shipwreck
description: the Aśvins pluck Bhujyu, son of Tugra, from the midst of the ocean and bear him home over three days in self-propelling winged ships

title: Bhuśuṇḍa the immortal crow recounts the kalpas
description: Vasiṣṭha visits the crow-sage nested on the kalpa-taru on Meru, who remembers repeated ocean-churnings and pralayas and survives cosmic dissolution by prāṇa-contemplation

title: Bhuśuṇḍa the immortal crow survives the pralayas
description: The ancient crow on Meru's kalpa-tree tells Vasiṣṭha how he has watched dissolutions and world-ages repeat, abiding in prāṇa-contemplation while creation burns

title: Biroba born of Māyavā
description: the Dhangar shepherd-god is miraculously born of, or given by, the goddess Māyavā (Māyakkā) and fostered in a shepherd household, emerging to herd sheep and found his cult

title: Birth of Bhadrakālī from Śiva's third eye
description: Alerted by Nārada to Dārika's outrages, Śiva opens his third eye and from its fire Bhadrakālī is born fully armed as his daughter, with the vetāla given as her mount

title: Birth of Sārasvata
description: Dadhīca's seed, spilled at the sight of the apsaras Alambuṣā, falls into the Sarasvatī, who preserves it and bears the sage Sārasvata

title: Birth of the water-child Lauhitya
description: Amoghā bears Brahmā's seed, conveyed through Śāntanu, and gives birth to a son in the form of water — the Brahmaputra

title: Bobbariya, the Muslim mariner made daiva
description: a Byāri merchant-sailor who dies at sea is deified as a Tuḷu sea-spirit guarding trade and fishermen, his shrine marked by the mast-like bobbariyana kambo

title: Both cousins liberated
description: Khāṇḍikya entrusts his son with the throne and by steady meditation on Viṣṇu attains release, and Keśidhvaja is freed likewise, closing the Viṣṇu Purāṇa on its mokṣa coda

title: Brahmā enthrones Ripuñjaya as Divodāsa
description: In an age of anarchy Brahmā persuades the ascetic Ripuñjaya to rule the earth from Kāśī on condition that all gods withdraw to heaven

title: Brahmā's desire for Amoghā
description: Brahmā, smitten by Amoghā, wife of the sage Śāntanu, is rebuked and departs in shame, his seed fallen at the hermitage

title: Brahmā's ten aśvamedhas at Kāśī
description: Testing Divodāsa, Brahmā demands ten simultaneous horse-sacrifices, which the king executes flawlessly — the etiology of Daśāśvamedha Ghāṭ; Sūrya likewise stays as the twelve Ādityas of Kāśī

title: Brahmā's yajña at Puṣkara and Sāvitrī's curse
description: Brahmā sacrifices at Puṣkara with substitute bride Gāyatrī when Sāvitrī delays, and her curse limits his worship to this one tīrtha

title: Brahmā, Śatarūpā, and the fifth head
description: the Purāṇic reflex: Brahmā grows extra heads to keep gazing at his own created daughter Śatarūpā/Sandhyā, and Kāla Bhairava shears off the fifth head, incurring the brahmahatyā skull-penance

title: Bṛhaspati impersonates Śukra and deludes the asuras
description: While Śukra endures his vow for Śiva's mantras and weds Jayantī, Bṛhaspati teaches in his form and turns the asuras from their true guru

title: Bṛhaspati impersonates the asura-guru
description: during Śukra's hidden decade the deva-guru takes Śukra's very form, preaches a heterodox dharma to disunite the Daityas, and gets the returning true Śukra rejected as the fraud

title: Brihaspati's curse blinds Dirghatamas in the womb
description: The embryo in Mamata's womb blocks Brihaspati's intruding seed, and the enraged god-priest curses him to be born into 'long darkness', giving the blind seer his name

title: Caṇḍikeśvara, guardian of the nirmālya
description: as Śiva's appointed officer (adhikārin), Caṇḍeśa becomes the standing Āgamic recipient of all offerings already given to Śiva (nirmālya), from whom alone devotees may receive them

title: Candrāṅgada drowned and rescued by nāgas
description: Sīmantinī's husband Candrāṅgada of Niṣadha sinks in a Yamunā whirlpool, is carried to Pātāla by nāga-maidens, honoured by Takṣaka for his Śiva-devotion, and returns alive to reunite with her — the Somavāra-vrata's proof

title: Candrāvatī desecrates the prasād
description: royal women scorn the Svasthānī offerings, casting the sacred flowers into the river, and lose husbands, sons, and kingdom until they re-perform the vow and are wholly restored

title: Chastity restores Pippalāda's youth
description: pleased by her proven fidelity, Dharma reveals himself and grants boons: the aged Pippalāda is made young and vigorous, Padmā eternally youthful, with ten virtuous sons and boundless wealth

title: Ciṟuttoṇḍar's extreme naivedya
description: The Nāyanār cooks and offers his own son as food to a Bhairava-guest, the limit-case of food-devotion, before the child is restored

title: Consecration of Sthāṇu-tīrtha
description: the ground where Śiva stood by the sage as the immovable Sthāṇu becomes Sthāneśvara (Thanesar) at Kurukṣetra, a tīrtha granting Śiva-sāyujya

title: Cūḍālā appears as the sage Kumbha
description: Disguised as a young brahmin sage claiming to be Nārada's pot-born son, Cūḍālā becomes her husband's guru and exposes his false renunciation through the cintāmaṇi and Vindhya-elephant parables

title: Cūḍālā liberates King Śikhidhvaja as the sage Kumbha
description: The realized queen Cūḍālā, disguised as the brahmin youth Kumbha, teaches and tests her renunciate husband until both rule as jīvanmuktas

title: Cūḍālā's awakening in the palace
description: Queen Cūḍālā of Mālava attains Self-knowledge through self-inquiry (ātma-vicāra) while living as a reigning queen, without external renunciation

title: Curds bought with a gold ring
description: thirsty on the march, the two disguised Lords drink the milkmaid Māṇikā's curds and, having no coin, pay her with a gold ring, bidding her collect the debt from the king coming behind

title: Cyavana initiates the gleaner
description: Dharmāraṇya seeks out Cyavana of Bhṛgu's line for formal saṃskāra into the Uñcha vow, then takes up Yama and Niyama and withdraws into another forest to live it

title: Dadhīca's curse foretelling the Dakṣa-yajña
description: victorious, Dadhīca curses the gods for siding with the king and prophesies that Rudra will scatter and burn them all, Viṣṇu included, at the future sacrifice of Dakṣa

title: Dakṣa's sacrifice and Satī's fire (Svasthānī telling)
description: Satī, humiliated at her father Dakṣa's Śiva-excluding sacrifice, immolates herself, and Śiva's hosts wreck the rite

title: Damanaka sunders lion and bull
description: the jackal Damanaka poisons the friendship of lion-king Piṅgalaka and the bull Sañjīvaka with insinuation until the lion kills his friend, the exemplum of Suhṛdbheda

title: Dambhodbhava's daily boast
description: the universal emperor Dambhodbhava asks each morning whether anyone on earth is his equal in battle, until brāhmaṇas name the ascetics Nara and Nārāyaṇa as his superiors

title: Dārika's boon from Brahmā
description: The asura Dārika wins invincibility against every male being — god, asura, or human — leaving only a woman able to kill him, and tyrannizes the worlds

title: Dārika-vadham — the beheading of Dārika
description: After a long war in which the vetāla drinks the demon blood before it seeds new demons, Bhadrakālī severs Dārika's head and holds it aloft, the defining Kerala Bhagavati icon

title: Death teaches Naciketas the yogic Song
description: the Agni Purāṇa's Yama-Gītā, framed on the Kaṭha archetype, has Yama expound jñāna, yoga, and the chariot-of-the-body path to release

title: Deva Śarmā's tapas at Devprayag
description: the sage's austerities and divine vision at the confluence give Devprayag its name [regional]

title: Devaśarman and the goatherd Mitravat
description: a brahmin seeking supreme knowledge learns from a forest goatherd that steady duty ripens into wisdom, the lesson of Gītā chapter 2

title: Devaśayanī and Prabodhinī — Viṣṇu's four-month cosmic sleep
description: Viṣṇu lies down on Śeṣa at Āṣāḍha śukla Ekādaśī and wakes at Kārttika śukla Ekādaśī, the two tithis bounding Cāturmāsya and the Tulasī-vivāha
source: Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa; pan-purāṇic calendar lore

title: Dhaneśvara saved by the company of Kārttika-vratins
description: a lifelong cheat dying among Kārttika observers on the Narmadā is spared Yama's hells by their contagious merit

title: Dharma disguised tests Padmā's chastity
description: the god Dharma takes the guise of a lustful king and, meeting Padmā at the celestial river, urges her to cast off the ruthless old brahmin, but she refuses utterly

title: Dharmāraṇya converted to the gleaner's life
description: his doubt dispelled, the brāhmaṇa declares he has learnt the value of the Uñcha vow and resolves to abandon acquisition for the humblest, harm-minimal livelihood

title: Dharmāraṇya seeks the Nāga Padmanābha
description: a righteous but doubt-gnawed brāhmaṇa, unsure which dharma most surely wins liberation, journeys to the serpent-city in the Naimiṣa forest on the Gomatī to question the virtuous Nāga

title: Dhuloba, the dust-lord of the flock
description: the fierce Bhairava-type Dhangar god of the Vīr–Phalṭaṇ tract is born, marries and founds his cult in his own sung ovī

title: Dīrghajihvī the soma-licker trapped
description: Indra, unable to catch the demoness who licks up the gods' soma with her long tongue, fashions the youth Sumitra Kutsa to seduce and destroy her

title: Dundubhinirhrāda hunts the brahmins of Kāśī
description: the Daitya uncle of Prahlāda, avenging Hiraṇyākṣa, resolves to starve the gods by devouring their sacrificing brahmins and comes to Kāśī, ambushing them in the shapes of forest-dweller, water-beast, invisible form, and tiger, leaving not even a bone

title: Durgama steals the Vedas
description: the asura Durgama, son of Ruru of Hiraṇyākṣa's line, wins the four Vedas as a boon from Brahmā, extinguishing all yajña so that the rains fail and a hundred-year drought grips the earth

title: Even Mārkaṇḍeya is not old enough
description: the deathless sage who survives the deluge confesses he does not know Indradyumna and sends him to an elder still, the owl Prāvārakarṇa

title: Faith held before vindication
description: Nandabhadra refutes the materialist on scripture and reason, defends the devas and Liṅga-worship, then walks to the Bahūdaka tīrtha at Mahīsāgara-Saṅgama to end his life

title: Gaṇeśa settles in Kāśī as Ḍhuṇḍhirāja
description: Disguised as an aged brāhmaṇa astrologer, Gaṇeśa wins the city's trust, foretells the counselor to come on the eighteenth day, and remains as Ḍhuṇḍhi-Vināyaka, chief guardian Gaṇeśa of Kāśī

title: Garuḍa humbled and restored at Garuḍa-tīrtha
description: Garuḍa imprisons the Śiva-protected serpent Maṇināga, is crushed under Viṣṇu's little finger, and rises stronger after bathing in the Gautamī

title: Garuḍa reconciled and the wedding of Sumukha and Guṇakeśī
description: the humbled Garuḍa makes peace with Sumukha, who weds Guṇakeśī, laying to rest the bird-and-serpent enmity in this instance

title: Garuda seizes the bile of Bala, seeding the emeralds
description: Bala's bile, taken by the serpent-king Vasuki, is snatched by Garuda and dropped in a remote mountain land, whence the emerald mines
source: Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha, emerald section; Garuda Purana emerald chapter

title: Garuḍa's one-month death-term revealed
description: Nārada discloses that Garuḍa devoured Sumukha's father Cikura and has fixed a term one month hence to eat Sumukha too, dismaying the grandfather Āryaka

title: Gaurī wins half of Śiva's body by the Kedāra vrata
description: Pārvatī keeps the 21-day Kedāra Gaurī vow and is granted the left half of Śiva, the vrata-charter for Ardhanārīśvara

title: Gautama's curse of Devī-aversion
description: outraged at the framing, Gautama curses his benefactees to become averse to Gāyatrī and Mūla-Prakṛti Śrī Devī, to Veda, sandhyā and yajña, and to turn instead to Kāpālikas, Bauddha śāstras and pāṣaṇḍa heresy

title: Gāyatrī's inexhaustible vessel
description: in a twelve-year famine the Sage Gautama worships Gāyatrī Devī, who grants him a brim-full vessel that yields whatever he wishes, so no starving brāhmaṇa is turned away

title: Ghoṣā cured and wed
description: the seer Ghoṣā Kākṣīvatī, disfigured by skin disease and unmarried into old age, wins from the Aśvins both a cure and a husband in her own hymns

title: Gobhila's curse of idiocy
description: insulted when Devadatta of Kosala rebukes his Sāma-singing at a Putreṣṭi on the Tamasā, the sage Gobhila curses the brahmin's son-to-be to be born dull, illiterate, and dumb

title: Godhā the lizard saved by a bath's transferred merit
description: Rukmāṅgada's horse crushes a she-lizard (once a sorceress-wife of Śākala, punished in the hell Tāmrabhrāṣṭra); over Mohinī's objection the king gifts her his Vijayā-rite merit from the Gaṅgā–Sarayū confluence and she ascends to Viṣṇu's realm

title: Goma married to the seventy-year-old brahmin
description: the young brahmin girl Goma is given by fate and Śiva's will to Śiva Śarma, a brahmin of seventy, dramatising a wife's dharma under the harshest marital fortune

title: Goma takes the Svasthānī vow
description: in her misery Goma undertakes the month-of-Māgh vow of the goddess Svasthānī, and by its power her fortunes turn and her son thrives

title: Gopāla agrees to walk south
description: pleaded to testify in a hostile assembly, Kṛṣṇa's Deity consents to follow the youth on one condition — that he never look back while the ankle-bells sound behind him

title: Guliga, the insatiable one born of ash and stone
description: a devouring goblin-daiva born from a stone Pārvatī finds in ash is handed to Viṣṇu, who curbs his world-swallowing hunger and fixes him as Kṣetra-pāla, guardian of the precinct

title: Gulikan sprung from Śiva's toe
description: when Śiva strikes down Yama to save Mārkaṇḍeya, he brings forth the death-being Gulikan from his left great toe and deputizes him over death, making him North Malabar's Yama-aspect and, once propitiated, a guardian against untimely death

title: Guṇanidhi's unwitting Śivarātri vrata
description: Starving on Śivarātri night, Guṇanidhi enters a Śiva shrine to steal the food-offerings and, feeding his torn garment as a wick to the dying lamp before the liṅga, unknowingly completes the fast-vigil-lamp vrata before being killed as a thief

title: Gurudruh's unwitting Śivarātri vigil
description: a sinful hunter, having caught nothing all day (an accidental fast), spends the night in a bilva tree above a hidden liṅga, unknowingly showering it with bilva leaves and water in each of the four watches

title: Guruvayurappan comes to taste the payasam
description: legend holds the Lord of Guruvayur visits Ambalappuzha daily to taste its pal-payasam, binding the two Kerala Krishna-kshetras

title: Harmukh–Gaṅgabal ash-immersion
description: Kashmiri Pandits carry the ashes of their dead to the alpine lake Gaṅgabal below Śiva's peak Harmukh, the valley's northern Gaṅgā, in the Harmukh-Gaṅga death-rite yātrā

title: Hayagrīva reveals the Rahasya-nāma-sāhasra to Agastya
description: having withheld the secret litany, the horse-headed Viṣṇu-form yields to Agastya's pressing and transmits the Lalitā Sahasranāma, chartering the Śrī-Vidyā guru-transmission

title: Hayagrīva transmits the Lalitā Triśatī
description: in the same frame Hayagrīva also gives Agastya the 300-name hymn, its names arranged twenty to each syllable of the Pañcadaśī mantra

title: Hemalekhā teaches that pleasure lies in the mind
description: the dispassionate wife awakens her besotted husband by showing that joy and sorrow reside not in objects but in the mind's own imagining, turning him to inquiry into the witnessing Self

title: Hiraṇyahasta given to Vadhrimatī
description: to Vadhrimatī, whose husband was impotent, the Aśvins grant a son, Golden-hand (Hiraṇyahasta), restoring the line

title: Iḍā, Manu's flood-daughter
description: in the oldest stratum Manu's post-deluge offering yields the woman Iḍā, the offering-goddess and progenitrix of Manu's race, with no sex-change — the Vedic root of the later Sudyumna myth

title: Indra cleansed at the Aruṇā tīrtha
description: pursued by the guilt of the treacherous slaying, Indra bathes at the Aruṇā-saṃgama on the Sarasvatī and is freed of the sin-stain

title: Indra defeats the tyrant Mayadenawa (Galungan origin legend)
description: the god strikes forth the Tirta Empul spring to revive his poisoned troops and slays the worship-banning tyrant whose blood curses the Petanu river, commemorated every 210 days at Galungan [regional] [folk]

title: Indra distributes the Brahmahatyā
description: after slaying the brāhmaṇa Vṛtra/Viśvarūpa, Indra hides in a lotus-fibre and is purified by dividing the great sin into four — earth, water, trees, and women — each taking a share for a boon, then by the Aśvamedha

title: Indra grants Sumukha long life
description: carried to heaven before Indra and Viṣṇu, Sumukha is granted length of days rather than the amṛta, escaping Garuḍa's appointed term

title: Indra plants Jayantī at Śukra's side
description: fearing the completed tapas, Indra sends his daughter Jayantī to serve the penancing sage, who rewards her with a ten-year union behind a veil of māyā

title: Indra refuses Brāhmaṇahood
description: Indra appears again and again to tell Mātaṅga that Brāhmaṇahood, the highest station, cannot be won in one life by the Caṇḍāla-born; varṇa rises only gradually across many births

title: Indra throws the Yatis to the salāvṛkas
description: one of the canonical sins of Indra: he gives the ascetic Yatis to hyenas to be devoured, a transgression the tradition itself flags

title: Indra's apsara counter-insurgency
description: the recurring dispatch of Menakā, Rambhā and Pramlocā to break world-threatening tapas, yielding Śakuntalā and a stone-cursed Rambhā

title: Indra's crosswise birth dialogue
description: the unborn Indra refuses the 'ancient proven path' of birth and emerges crosswise through his mother's side, with Vamadeva's famine-verse attached

title: Indra's six decoy Vitaṅkas
description: Indra makes six identical replicas to trick Muchukunda, but by Śiva's grace the king picks the true image and Indra yields all seven emerald Somāskanda icons

title: Indradyumna falls from heaven for want of a rememberer
description: the celestials cast the royal sage back to earth because his store of merit lapses once no living being recalls his deeds, and bid him find one witness who knows him

title: Indrani's quarrel over Vrishakapi
description: Indrani rages at Indra's pet bull-ape Vrishakapi in a ribald three-way dialogue closing with the refrain 'Indra is supreme over all'

title: Installation of Bālāditya
description: the boy discharges his karma through solar penance and voluntary death; Nandabhadra cremates him at Barkarikā Tīrtha and founds the Bālāditya Sun-shrine on his instruction

title: Īśvarī Pāṭunī ferries the goddess
description: Annadā in disguise as a radiant woman asks the low-caste boatman Īśvarī Pāṭunī to row her across the Bhāgīrathī at night, then reveals her four-armed form and offers a boon

title: Jalandhara, Vṛndā and the birth of Tulsī
description: Viṣṇu deceives the chaste Vṛndā to break the asura Jalandhara's invincibility, and she is reborn as the tulsī plant, charter of Tulsī Vivāha

title: Jaya-Vijaya's three-birth curse drives the avatāras
description: the cursed doorkeepers choose three births as Viṣṇu's enemies, necessitating Varāha, Narasiṃha, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa

title: Jyotibā born of the Trimūrti
description: Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva combine their aṃśas to bring forth the radiant warrior-god Jyotibā (Kedāreśvara), taking birth to the sage Paugaṇḍa to answer the harassed ṛṣis of Karavīra

title: Jyotibā takes Wadi Ratnagiri
description: with the demons dead, Jyotibā liberates Karavīra and establishes his permanent guardian-seat on the Wadi Ratnagiri hill above Kolhapur as the male counterpart of the enthroned Goddess

title: Kāla comes for the rājarṣi Śveta
description: At the end of his allotted span, Death-as-Time arrives to seize the royal sage Śveta while he is absorbed in worship of the Śiva-liṅga

title: Kālī saves Sundara at the śmaśāna
description: caught as a thief and condemned to death, Sundara hymns Kālī at the execution-ground; the goddess manifests, stays the executioners, and reveals him as the prince of Kāñcī, winning his proper marriage to Vidyā

title: Kāmodā's tears of joy become Gaṅgā lotuses
description: Each spring at her seat ten yojanas above Gaṅgādvāra, the meditating Kāmodā laughs with delight and her tears fall into the Gaṅgā as fragrant yellow lotuses, with which devotees worship Śiva for their desires

title: Kandalī the ogress regains human form by a righteous deed
description: Cursed by Durvāsas into rākṣasī shape, Kandalī helps Kāṣṭhīlā's wandering husband slay the demon Gobhila with a śakti weapon, wins back her benign form, and weds him alongside Ratnāvalī of Vārāṇasī

title: Kandiyūr — the severing of Brahmā's fifth head
description: the shrine of Brahmaśiraḥ-Kaṇḍeśvarar where Bhairava shears off Brahmā's insolent fifth head; a local variant has Viṣṇu, not Kāśī, free Śiva of the brahmahatyā

title: Karabhājana's yuga-avatāra doctrine
description: the Lord descends white in Satya (worshipped by meditation), red in Tretā (by sacrifice), dark in Dvāpara (by royal/tantric worship), and in Kali by saṅkīrtana

title: Karkaṭī becomes the needle-demoness Viśūcikā
description: The Himālayan rākṣasī wins from Brahmā the form of a piercing needle-sickness, repents of formless misery, regains her body Self-knowing, and tests a king and minister with riddles on the Ātman

title: Karkaṭī the rākṣasī becomes the needle Viśūcikā and repents
description: The demoness wins a boon to become a piercing sickness, wearies of formless hunger, regains her body Self-knowing, and tests a king and minister with riddles on the Ātman
actors: a mountain king and his minister

title: Karma, the three guṇas and transmigration
description: action as mental, verbal and bodily yields specific animal and hellish rebirths, with sattva leading upward to godhood, rajas to human states and tamas downward

title: Kārtika-vrata charter (Dāmodara-māsa)
description: the month sacred to Viṣṇu is glorified through the vows of dawn bath, lamp-offering, and Tulasī worship, illustrated by a fixed cluster of devotee tales recited each Kārtika
source: Skanda P., Vaiṣṇava-khaṇḍa, Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya; Padma P., Uttara-khaṇḍa

title: Kārttikeya founds the Kumārikā-kṣetra & plants Stambheśvara
description: the boy-general Skanda, victor over Tāraka, consecrates the Mahī-mouth as his kṣetra and installs the pillar-liṅga Stambheśvara at the sea's edge, giving Khambhāt (Stambhatīrtha) its name

title: Kaśmīrā is Pārvatī
description: the governing maxim of the valley's sacred geography, that the land itself is the Goddess and its king a portion of Śiva, making every spring and hill a limb of the divine landscape

title: Kataragama, the multi-faith abode of Skanda
description: the deep-south Murugan shrine worshipped at once by Hindus, Buddhists, Muslims and Vedda, centred on the god's marriage to the Vedda maiden Vaḷḷi

title: Kathivanūr Vīran deified with Chemmarathi
description: the archer-hero Mandappan Chekavar, disowned and settled at Kathivanūr in Coorg, is ambushed and killed in the Kodagu war, whereupon his wife Chemmarathi enters his pyre and the two are deified together as a hero-theyyam

title: Kauṇḍinya tears the ananta-thread
description: the sage scorns his wife Suśīlā's 14-knot cord, burns it, falls to ruin, and after a riddle-quest past mango tree, cow, bull, ponds, donkey and elephant is restored by fourteen years of the vrata

title: Kāvyamātā shelters the routed asuras
description: with Śukra hidden, the beaten Daityas flee to Bhṛgu's wife Kāvyamātā, who grants them refuge and moves to burn and stupefy Indra by yogic power

title: Keśidhvaja's yoga discourse
description: the jñāna-master teaches that avidyā is false self-identification, defines yoga and its stages, and prescribes contemplation (dhāraṇā) on the embodied form of Viṣṇu withdrawn toward the formless Brahman

title: Khāṇḍikya asks for yoga, not a throne
description: the deposed karma-master requests as his fee the knowledge that severs rebirth, and Keśidhvaja rejoices that by refusing the kingdom his cousin has truly conquered

title: Khāṇḍikya spares his conqueror
description: with the defenceless Keśidhvaja in his power and ministers urging the kill, Khāṇḍikya lays down his bow, reasoning that slaying wins only this world while teaching the expiation wins the world beyond

title: King Mahīratha gives his merit to hell
description: the Vaiśākha-vrata king makes over his accumulated merit to hell's sufferers, releasing them, and ascends to Viṣṇu's world

title: King Narasiṃha and the half-verse in the rock
description: a Gauḍa king finds half a verse of Gītā chapter 15 in a fissure; its mere reading sends a karma-bound horse to heaven and wins salvation for the king, his son, and ministers

title: King Padma's death
description: Padma dies; Līlā preserves his flower-heaped body and invokes her first boon to keep his spirit near, and Sarasvatī reveals the soul is present but dwelling in a world of its own making

title: King Tāladhvaja marries Suśīlā
description: the palmyra-bannered king finds the solitary woman by the lake, is smitten, and takes her as his queen, beginning a full married household

title: King Vipaścit finds himself in hell
description: the just monarch, who sacrificed, ruled fairly and honoured guests, gods and ancestors, walks bewildered into Naraka and protests his innocence

title: Kolhāsura and the naming of Kolhāpura
description: the demon Kolhāsura who gives Kolhapur its name is slain in the Karavīra war, credited to Mahālakṣmī in her charter and to Jyotibā as her guardian-general in his

title: Koneśvaram, the southern Kailāsa
description: the Trincomalee Śiva temple styled Dakṣiṇa-Kailāsa, tied by legend to Rāvaṇa's Śiva-worship and sung in the Tamil Tēvāram as one of the Pāḍal Petṟa Sthalams

title: Kordabbu, the Koraga wonder-worker deified
description: a hero of the marginalised Koraga community, able to make a dry stick sprout green and raise water, is worshipped as the daiva Koragajja, giver of lost things and vows

title: Krishna reveals himself and commutes the debt
description: the sage discloses he is Krishna and converts the unpayable rice into an eternal duty to serve pal-payasam to every devotee until repaid

title: Kṣupa's vajra nullified
description: the enraged king hurls Indra's thunderbolt at Dadhīca, but Śiva's boon renders it harmless against the sage's body — the kṣatra's ultimate weapon defeated by brahma

title: Kubera named and enthroned by Śiva
description: Reborn (in the Meghavāhana kalpa) and doing tapas at Kāśī, the future wealth-lord's left eye bursts as he stares at Umā; Śiva names him Kubera and grants wealth-lordship, yakṣa-kingship, Alakā, and his own friendship

title: Kukura slain in buffalo-form
description: the Goddess battles the daitya Kukura, who takes mahiṣa shape, and beheads him on the Bālā-ghāṭ, re-enacting the Mahiṣāsura-mardinī act on Deccan soil

title: Kuṇḍadhara grants dharma, not wealth
description: the cloud-spirit Kuṇḍadhara, pleased with a poor Brahmin who begged for riches, gives him instead attachment to righteousness, which carries him past rebirth

title: Kuṇi-Garga's will-born daughter
description: the ṛṣi Kuṇi surnamed Garga creates a fair-browed daughter by a fiat of will, then ascends to heaven, leaving her to a lifetime of severe penance unmarried

title: Kuñjala the pious parrot instructs Cyavana
description: the learned parrot teaches dharma and the inner-tīrtha doctrine to his four sons, the sage Cyavana, and Divyadevī

title: Kurukkai — the burning of Kāma
description: the shrine where Śiva's third eye reduced the love-god Kāma to ash, later restored bodiless as Anaṅga at Rati's plea

title: Kutsa Aurava, Indra's doppelgänger
description: the ṛṣi Kutsa so exactly resembles Indra that, carried to heaven bound by a single shared lock of hair, even Indrāṇī cannot tell god from man

title: Kuṭṭichāttan slain and multiplied
description: the wild boy-imp born of Śiva and Pārvatī and fostered at the Kāḷakāṭṭ Illam slaughters the household's cow, is cut down by the Nampūtiri, and multiplies from his own blood into hundreds of Chāttans who torment the illam until propitiated and enshrined

title: Lakṣmī commands Cārumatī in a dream
description: Mahālakṣmī visits the virtuous Cārumatī of Kuṇḍina and institutes the Varalakṣmī vratam of Śrāvaṇa's Friday, showering the town's women with fortune at each pradakṣiṇā

title: Līlā's two boons against widowhood
description: dreading her husband's death, Queen Līlā propitiates the goddess Sarasvatī and wins that Padma's soul stay in the palace when he dies and that the goddess come whenever called

title: Madālasā dies of grief
description: hearing the false report and seeing her husband's ornament, the faithful queen at once yields up her life, a death only nāga power can undo

title: Madana Vinoda sails and leaves the guardian bird
description: the reformed merchant's son departs on a trading voyage, entrusting his wife to the parrot, while in the two-bird recension a blunt myna is nearly killed for rebuking her

title: Mahānandā's rudrākṣa vow
description: the pious courtesan of Nandigrāma, sworn on oath to a Vaiśya devotee, follows him into the fire when his jewelled liṅga burns, and Śiva halts her and lifts her whole household to his realm

title: Mahiṣāsura's gender-clause boon
description: invincibility against gods and men forces the devas' pooled tejas to condense into the Goddess who alone can slay him

title: Mala-māsa adopted as Puruṣottama-māsa
description: the reviled personified leap month weeps before Viṣṇu, who leads it to Goloka where Kṛṣṇa bestows his own name Puruṣottama and supremacy among months [late text]
source: Puruṣottama-māsa-māhātmya, transmitted under the Padma Purāṇa

title: Māṇabasā Gurubāra (Gurubāra Oṣā) vrata
description: every Thursday of Mārgaśira Odia women seat the māṇa of new paddy as Lakṣmī, draw jhoṭi-chitā, and recite the Lakṣmī Purāṇa, annually re-performing the goddess's verdict
source: Lakṣmī Purāṇa as vrata liturgy; Odia household practice

title: Mānasa-Pūjā Vindicated
description: the charter-parable that worship built wholly in the mind outweighs the grandest temple of dressed stone, pairing Pūcalār with Vāyilār of Mylapore as the canon's exemplars of interior devotion

title: Manifestation of Vaṭuka Bhairava
description: Śiva brings forth a radiant, fierce boy from his own being as a protective son-form (putra-rūpa), not womb-born, charged with guarding sages and devotees

title: Maṇikuṇḍala's dharma-wager vindicated
description: Mutilated and blinded after wagers on dharma vs adharma, the vaiśya Maṇikuṇḍala is healed by the viśalyakaraṇī herb on the Gautamī's bank, becomes king, and pardons his betrayer

title: Manu Nīti Cholan's chariot-justice
description: the Chola king of Tiruvārūr drives his own war-chariot over his son to avenge a calf the prince's wheel had killed, and Śiva restores both to life

title: March on the hermitage of the twin sages
description: Dambhodbhava leads his six-limbed army to Gandhamādana and, spurning the ascetics' hospitality and repeated refusals, demands battle of the emaciated Nara and Nārāyaṇa

title: Marriage bought with half a lifetime of penance
description: the old maid offers half her ascetic merit as bride-price, and Śṛṅgavat of Gālava's line weds her on the condition of a single night together

title: Mātali's quest for a Nāga son-in-law
description: Indra's charioteer Mātali, finding no groom worthy of his daughter Guṇakeśī in the upper worlds, resolves to search the netherworld of Pātāla

title: Mātaṅga's consolation boon and death
description: after collapsing from a century on one toe, Mātaṅga is caught by Indra, granted shape-shifting and worship by women in place of the caste he sought, and dies without ever becoming a Brāhmaṇa

title: Mātaṅga's vow to win Brāhmaṇahood
description: shaken by the truth of his mixed birth, Mātaṅga undertakes penances of terrifying severity to propitiate Indra and force his way into the Brāhmaṇa varṇa

title: Māyāmoha frames the tale
description: Viṣṇu's emitted deluder strips the Daityas of the Vedas on the Narmadā, creating the pāṣaṇḍa class whose mere conversation dooms Śatadhanu

title: Maynāmatī's ordeal-proof
description: to prove that yogic deathlessness is real, Maynāmatī passes unharmed through fire and water, demonstrating the kāya-siddhi her son may attain

title: Mhaskoba the buffalo-lord
description: the Deccan Mhasobā of Vīr is raised into a temple-god and identified with Kāḷ-Bhairava, the fierce skull-bearing form of Śiva

title: Mohinī destroys Bhasmāsura through dance
description: Viṣṇu's enchantress-form lures the demon into placing his boon-hand on his own head, the namesake charter-myth of Mohiniyāṭṭam

title: Muchilōṭṭu Bhagavathi immolates and is enshrined
description: a learned Brahmin virgin of Perinchellūr, excommunicated on a malicious slur after out-debating the scholars, immolates herself at Karivellūr and is enshrined by a Vāṇiyan oil-presser as the benign bride-goddess Muchilōṭṭu Bhagavathi

title: Muchukunda wins the Somāskanda
description: the Chola king Muchukunda, having aided Indra in a deva–asura war, claims as reward the Tyāgarāja/Somāskanda image worshipped on Viṣṇu's chest

title: Mudgala and Mudgalani's chariot race
description: Mudgala wins a thousand cattle in a race with a cart yoked to a bull and a wooden club, his wife Mudgalani driving as charioteer

title: Namuci as prototype loophole-boon
description: Namuci's "neither wet nor dry, neither day nor night" is the earliest fully-articulated boon-loophole, the template for Hiraṇyakaśipu, Mahiṣa, and Tāraka

title: Namuci steals Indra's strength with the surā
description: the Dānava Namuci carries off Indra's vigour and the essence of food and drink together with the Soma and Surā, leaving the king of the gods powerless

title: Namuci's sunbeam refuge and sworn friendship
description: in the epic Namuci hides in a ray of the sun and binds Indra by a pact of friendship on the wet/dry, day/night terms

title: Nandā identified as Pārvatī, daughter of the hills
description: Uttarakhand tradition localizes the Purāṇic Pārvatī cycle, worshipping the goddess as the region's married-out daughter (dhiyāṇī) sent yearly toward Kailāsa
source: Śiva Purāṇa frame; Kumaoni/Garhwali jāgar ballads [regional]

title: Nandabhadra merges into Rudra
description: his faith vindicated by the theodicy of karma, the merchant becomes a lifelong worshipper of Śiva and Sūrya and at the end attains mokṣa, merging into Rudra's body

title: Nandabhadra tested at the confluence
description: the flawless merchant, stripped of son and wife and baited to abandon dharma, holds fast and is answered by a karma-theodicy at the Mahīsāgara-saṃgama — a Book-of-Job analogue

title: Nandabhadra the honest merchant
description: a vaiśya of flawless piety trades without deceit and worships Śiva's Liṅga daily, keeping only what suffices

title: Nandikeśvara delivers the Kāśī-fruit on the Narmadā
description: Gaṅgā appears to Suvāda as a maiden at Viṃśatigrāma and sends him to cast the bones at Nandikeśvara on Vaiśākha-saptamī; his mother rises in divine form and ascends to Śiva's world

title: Nara's sermon and Dambhodbhava's reform
description: granting the fallen king safety, Nara commands him to honor brāhmaṇas, conquer his senses, and never insult anyone again, and the chastened emperor rules righteously ever after

title: Nara-Nārāyaṇa manifests Urvaśī
