description: in Drumila's avatāra recital, the sage Nārāyaṇa at Badarī foils Indra's temptation by producing a nymph lovelier than the apsarases sent against him

title: Nārada asks to see Mahāmāyā
description: the deathless sage begs Bhagavān Viṣṇu (Hari) to reveal the Goddess's power of illusion directly, not in words, and Viṣṇu sets out to teach him by experience

title: Nārada baits the demons toward Pārvatī
description: at Śiva's direction Nārada extols the Goddess's beauty to Vidala and Utpala until, inflamed with lust, they resolve to abduct her from Kailāsa

title: Nārada denies the old maid heaven
description: Nārada rules that the aged virgin ascetic cannot reach the blessed regions unpurified by the rite of marriage, however great her tapas

title: Nārada proposes the dice-game
description: on Kailāsa the sage interrupts Śiva and Pārvatī's embraces and sets them at akṣa-krīḍā, seeding the quarrel

title: Nārada rises as the woman Suśīlā
description: plunging into the water the sage forgets he is Nārada entirely and emerges on the bank as a beautiful young woman with no memory of his prior self — māyā as amnesia, not disguise

title: Nārada voices the 84 bhakti aphorisms
description: tradition ascribes the Nārada Bhakti Sūtra, defining bhakti as parama-prema, to the timeless wandering devarṣi

title: Nārada's love for Sukumārī and the concealment
description: smitten with Sṛñjaya's daughter Sukumārī and wed to her, Nārada hides his desire from Parvata, breaking their vow of full disclosure

title: Nārada's tour of the seven Pātālas
description: Nārada guides Mātali down through the subterranean worlds, cataloguing the Vaḍavāmukha fire, the asura strongholds, Hiraṇyapura, Rasātala with Surabhi, and the serpent-cities

title: Naravāhanadatta consecrated Vidyādhara emperor (Mahābhiṣeka)
description: the mortal-born son of Udayana of Vatsa wins the vidyās and brides mortal and celestial and is crowned cakravartin of the Vidyādharas, fulfilling Śiva's decree that frames the whole story-ocean

title: Navarāj born, the old husband gone
description: Goma bears a son, Navarāj, but poverty drives the aged Śiva Śarma to leave and never return, leaving her a destitute single mother

title: Navarāj crowned by the elephant's garland
description: grown by the vow's grace, Navarāj wins an heirless kingdom when the late king's state elephant garlands him, and the beggar-widow's son becomes king

title: Nīli deified as Icakki Ammaṉ
description: the blood-taking pēy is placated and enshrined as the far-southern yakṣi-goddess Icakkiyammaṉ, her sung katai the charter of her bow-song cult

title: Origin of blinking — Nimi in every eyelid
description: the gods set Nimi in the eyes of all creatures as the moving vāyu, so that eyelids open and close on his account; the twinkling (nimeṣa) is named for him

title: Origin of painting: Nārāyaṇa and Urvaśī
description: to humble the proud apsarases, the sage Nārāyaṇa paints a surpassingly beautiful woman on his thigh with mango juice, and from the image springs Urvaśī — the first act of citra

title: Pacification of Bhadrakālī's fury
description: Still blazing after the kill, the goddess is calmed — by darśana of her father Śiva, by the gods' masked kōlam dances (padayani's charter), or by an infant placed in her path — variants that found Kerala's ritual arts

title: Padma reborn as King Vidūratha
description: at death Padma's own vāsanā spins a further nested world in which he lives as the young King Vidūratha beside a second Queen Līlā, a world set inside the space of Padma's death-chamber

title: Padmā's curse fixes dharma's yuga-decline
description: enraged, Padmā curses the disguised seducer to lose a leg each age — four legs in Kṛta, one in Kali, restored in the next Kṛta — then, learning she has cursed Dharma himself, refines but keeps the curse

title: Panjurli raised on Kailāsa and exiled to guard the fields
description: an orphaned wild-boar piglet is reared by Pārvatī in Śiva's household, ravages the divine garden, and is cast to Earth by Śiva as a guardian-daiva of crops and justice

title: Pariyalūr — the wrecking of Dakṣa's sacrifice
description: the feat-shrine of the Dakṣa-yajña destruction, where Vīrabhadra sprung from Śiva's wrath beheads the Prajāpati Dakṣa

title: Pārvatī becomes the Śabarī huntress
description: the Goddess takes the guise of a dark tribal huntress with bow and quiver to seduce her ascetic husband back

title: Pārvatī curses Puṣpadanta and Mālyavān to mortal births
description: furious at the leak of her 'unheard' tale, Pārvatī curses the eavesdropper and his intercessor, to be freed only when the Great Tale passes through the piśāca Kāṇabhūti and is published to the world

title: Pārvatī receives Upamanyu as a son
description: The Goddess takes the milk-fed boy-devotee into Śiva's own household and gaṇa-circle

title: Pārvatī's curse on the plantain-grove boar
description: variant paddana in which Śiva creates the boar-being and Pārvatī curses it for destroying her kadaḷi (plantain) grove, softening the curse into a commission to be born on Earth as a redeeming spirit

title: Pārvatī's marriage-prophecy
description: the goddess blesses Aśokasundarī to wed the Indra-like Lunar king Nahuṣa who will rule the three worlds, a prophecy that marks both bride and groom for the demon Huṇḍa's schemes

title: Pārvatī's play-ball slays Vidala and Utpala
description: understanding Śiva's signal, the Goddess strikes both disguised demons at once with her kanduka and they drop dead like ripe palmyra fruit, the ball becoming the Kandukeśvara liṅga at Kāśī

title: Pārvatī's tapas, Madana-dahana, and the god-marriage
description: the goddess reborn as Himavān's daughter wins the mourning Śiva by austerity; Kāma is burned to ash and the ideal marriage is sealed

title: Pippalāda seizes Padmā by threat of ash
description: the aged sage Pippalāda, inflamed after meeting a lustful Gandharva, demands King Anaraṇya's daughter Padmā and threatens to burn all to ashes; on his preceptor's counsel the king surrenders her in marriage

title: Pitṛvartti reborn as King Brahmadatta of Kāmpilya
description: the most pious of the seven returns as the yogin-king Brahmadatta, son of Aṇuha and Kṛtvī (Śuka's daughter), who understands the speech of all creatures

title: Pottan Theyyam rebukes Śaṅkara
description: Śiva appears as the Pulaya "Pottan" and blocks Śaṅkarācārya's path, defeating him with the anti-caste argument that the same blood flows from high-born and low-born alike, and is ordained to be worshipped in that casteless form

title: Prabhāvadatta wins the Nāgara-mantra
description: harried by the serpent-folk of Pātāla, the brahmin Prabhāvadatta does penance to Śiva and is granted the Nāgara-mantra that subdues the Nāgas, securing Camatkārapura for the brahmins

title: Prajāpati becomes Mṛgaśiras
description: pierced, the Creator is fixed in the heavens as Mṛga, the deer's-head constellation (Orion), while the hunter Mṛgavyādha (Sirius), the doe Rohiṇī, and the three-barbed arrow (Orion's Belt) complete the sky-picture

title: Pratardana the born-avenger
description: Bharadvāja's putrakāmeṣṭi yields Pratardana, who matures supernaturally fast, leads Kāśī's army back, and exterminates Vītahavya's hundred sons to the last man

title: Prince Hemacūḍa marries the sage-reared Hemalekhā
description: separated on a hunt and sheltering in Vyāghrapada's hermitage, the Daśārṇa prince Hemacūḍa weds Hemalekhā, foundling daughter of the apsaras Vidyullekhā and already established in Self-knowledge

title: Queen Līlā's journey through nested worlds
description: Guided by Sarasvatī, Queen Līlā discovers her whole royal universe exists inside a village brahmin's hut-space, world nested within world with time running at different rates

title: Raden Kusuma given to the Bromo crater (Tengger founding legend)
description: Roro Anteng and Joko Seger's prayed-for twenty-five children are granted on condition the youngest returns to the volcano, redeemed yearly at Yadnya Kasada [oral tradition] [regional]

title: Rādhāṣṭamī
description: Rādhā's appearance day on Bhādrapada śukla aṣṭamī, a fortnight after Janmāṣṭamī, celebrated grandest at Barsānā with the once-yearly caraṇa-darśana of her feet at Vṛndāvana temples

title: Raktabhoja the blood-devourer
description: Jyotibā destroys Raktabhoja, a Deccan reflex of the Devī Māhātmya's Raktabīja whose blood-drops spawn clones, freeing the Karavīra country

title: Rantideva's supreme annadāna
description: After 48 days of famine the king gives his last food and water to a Brāhmaṇa, an outcaste, and a dog-keeper with his dogs — the gods in disguise — seeking only to relieve all beings' suffering

title: Rāvaḷnāth and Betāḷ guard the village
description: the fierce Bhairava-type tutelaries — Rāvaḷnāth the horseman-protector and Betāḷ the naked lord of ghost-hosts offered new sandals worn out by night-walking — patrol the Goan grāma bounds

title: Ṛbhu and Nidāgha become the stock non-dual guru–disciple pair
description: The pair migrate from the Viṣṇu Purāṇa parable into later Advaita literature — the Śaiva Ribhu-Gītā of the Śivarahasya Purāṇa and the Tejobindu, Varāha, and Annapūrṇā Upaniṣads

title: Rebha drawn from the waters
description: the Aśvins lift the wounded, bound Rebha, hidden in water for ten nights and nine days, and revive him like soma pressed from the vat

title: Rebirth as Dama, lamp-king of Kaliṅga
description: By the Śivarātri merit Guṇanidhi is reborn as Dama, son of Arindama and king of Kaliṅga, who has lamps kept burning in every Śiva shrine of his realm

title: Reborn as cakravāka birds on the Mānasa lake
description: as ruddy geese renamed Sumanas, Vasu, Citradarśin and the rest, they recite aloud the verse of their past births, watching King Aṇuha disport in worldly splendour

title: Reborn as deer on Kālañjara
description: the memory-keeping souls take deer bodies, remain indifferent to the herd, and fast to death at the Prapatana cliff

title: Reborn as hunters of Daśārṇa
description: the seven return as fowlers on Mount Kālañjara, and sickened by the killing life yet remembering all, they cast off their bodies by yoga

title: Recognition and release
description: Brahmadatta and his companions Subālaka and Puṇḍarīka recognise one another through the verse, complete the yoga begun in the hunter-birth, and the memory-bearing souls attain liberation

title: Reconciliation and Śiva's coronation
description: awakened from his delusion by Nārada, Śiva pardons Pārvatī and is re-enthroned at Gandhamādana by Aṅgiras and the sages

title: Renunciation and the vow of truth
description: broken by ridicule, Utathya withdraws to the Ganges bank, builds a hermitage, and takes a strict vow of truth (satya-vrata) — earning the name Satyavrata

title: Rescue of Madālasā in Purandarapura
description: in the subterranean city the prince finds Madālasā, gandharva-king Viśvāvasu's daughter, held captive, and her companion Kuṇḍalā reports Surabhi's prophecy that her rescuer shall wed her

title: Restored by the witness of the land
description: the moment the eldest creature affirms his deeds endure, a celestial car descends and Indradyumna is carried back to the heavenly worlds

title: Restored to Nārada in a moment
description: the second bath dissolves the spell: the woman, marriage, sons, and grief all vanish, Nārada stands as himself again, and Viṣṇu smiles on the bank where only a moment has passed

title: Return to earth on the horse Kuvalaya
description: reunited with his resurrected wife, Kuvalayāśva takes Madālasā up from the nāga-world and rides in splendour back to his own city, closing the netherworld arc

title: Revatī and Kakudmī's return across the ages
description: waiting through one Gandharva song in Brahmaloka, twenty-seven catur-yugas pass on earth, and Brahmā directs the out-of-time princess Revatī to wed Balarāma

title: Revelation and the liberated reign
description: Cūḍālā reveals herself; Śikhidhvaja salutes her as his guru, and the two return to rule Mālava as jīvanmukta king and queen for ten thousand years before final liberation

title: Ṛṣabha and the gaunt sage Tanu
description: the emaciated ascetic Tanu teaches the royal sage Ṛṣabha that hope (āśā) is thinner than his own wasted frame and the hardest thing to slay

title: Rukmāṅgada tested by Mohinī
description: the Vidiśā king's realm-wide Ekādaśī enforcement empties Yama's hells; Brahmā's mind-born temptress Mohinī demands he break the fast or behead his son Dharmāṅgada, and Viṣṇu intervenes at the sword-fall

title: Śākambharī feeds the world
description: the Goddess brings forth vegetables, greens, roots and fruit from her own body to feed a famished world until the rains return, earning the name Śākambharī, the Herb-Bearer

title: Śaktideva finds the Golden City of Kanakapurī
description: to win a princess who will wed only one who has seen the golden Vidyādhara city, Śaktideva survives being swallowed by a giant fish, reaches Kanakapurī, weds four cursed princesses, and is renamed Śaktivega

title: Śambara conjures Dāma-Vyāla-Kaṭa and Bhīma-Bhāsa-Dṛḍha
description: Three conjured demons are invincible while ego-less and fall once self-identity breeds death-fear; their knowing successors fight untouched — egohood itself is the vulnerability

title: Sandhyāvalī frees Kāṣṭhīlā the wood-worm with Māgha merit
description: The queen rescues a talking worm (once a brāhmaṇa's wife who refused her husband her wealth) from a crow and deeds her one-fourth of her Māgha-observance merit, sending her by aerial chariot to Viṣṇu's region

title: Śaṅkara receives the Ānanda-laharī on Kailāsa
description: Ascending Mount Kailāsa, Ādi Śaṅkara obtains the first 41 verses (Ānanda-laharī) from Śiva himself, the half held to be revealed rather than authored

title: Ashtavakra Curses His Father from the Womb
description: From the womb the unborn Ashtavakra corrects his father Kahoda's faulty Vedic recitation, and the wounded father curses him to be born bent in eight places

title: Ashvapati's eighteen-year penance and the goddess's boon
description: The childless king Ashvapati of Madra propitiates the goddess Savitri with eighteen years of austerity, and she grants him a single radiant daughter named Savitri

title: Avadhūta-Gītā taught by Dattātreya
description: Dattātreya, the avadhūta-avatāra, declares the ~289-verse, 8-chapter Song of the Free Soul to a disciple as eternal brahma-vidyā with no fixed yuga-date
actors: Dattātreya (speaker); a disciple (traditionally Kārtika / Svāmī Kārttikeya

title: Aśvapati's penance and the boon of Sāvitrī
description: The childless king Aśvapati's eighteen-year austerity wins from goddess Sāvitrī a radiant daughter named Sāvitrī

title: Bhrgu Tests the Trimurti and Kicks Vishnu
description: Sage Bhrgu, sent to test which of the Trimurti is supreme, kicks Vishnu on the chest; Vishnu humbly massages the offending foot, crushing Bhrgu's eye of ego

title: Ṛbhu instructs Nidāgha on non-duality
description: The sage Ṛbhu delivers a vast ~2,200-verse, 44-chapter Advaita discourse to his disciple Nidāgha, teaching that Śiva, Brahman, and the Self are one and the world is unreal

title: Birth and swelling of the cosmic being
description: A formless being is born (from Shiva's sweat in the Andhaka battle, or unbidden) and swells until it threatens to blot out the worlds

title: Birth from the cremation ground
description: Sudalaimāḍaṉ is born as a son of Śiva and Pārvatī from or into the burning-ground, taking the cuṭalai as his domain
source: Sudalaimāḍaṉ kodai oral tradition; Tamil villuppāṭṭu ballad

title: Birth of Bharadvaja from Brihaspati and Mamata
description: Bharadvaja is born of Brihaspati's union with Mamata (wife of Utathya); rejected by the womb-child Dirghatamas, the seed grows into a separate boy named via the folk-etymology 'bhara dva-jam'

title: Birth of Bhaṇḍāsura from the ash of Kāmadeva
description: Citrakarman molds the ash of Śiva-burnt Kāmadeva into a figure that Śiva's glance brings to life; the gaṇas cry 'bhaṇḍa!' and name him Bhaṇḍāsura

title: Birth of Durvāsā as the Śiva-portion at Atri's hermitage
description: Durvāsā, the irascible Rudra-natured sage, is born as the aṃśa (portion) of Śiva to the Saptarṣi Atri and the chaste Anasūyā, alongside his brothers Soma/Candra (Brahmā-portion) and Dattātreya (Viṣṇu-portion)

title: Bāṇāsura's boon of invincibility
description: The demon Bāṇāsura obtains a boon that he can be slain only by a virgin maiden (kanyā), forcing the gods to need an unwed Goddess

title: Childless Cāraṇ couple and the penance
description: The scorned childless Cāraṇ Mamaḍiyā and Devaḷ do severe penance and are granted that goddesses will be born as their daughters

title: Citrasutra revealed (Markandeya to king Vajra)
description: The sage Markandeya instructs king Vajra in the art of painting, the dialogue that forms the Citrasutra of the Vishnudharmottara Purana, the foundational treatise on citra-kala

title: Cākṣuṣī-mantra transmission through Viśvāvasu
description: The Cākṣuṣī-mantra of supernatural sight, devised by Manu, passes down the gandharva line Soma → Viśvāvasu → Chitraratha, who finally gifts it to Arjuna

title: Composition of the body from the five elements
description: The Garbha Upaniṣad teaches that the human body is built of earth, water, fire, air and space, with a fivefold function in each element

title: Daksha gives his 27 nakshatra-daughters to Candra
description: Daksha Prajapati marries all twenty-seven of his nakshatra-daughters to the Moon-god Candra on the condition he treat them equally, personifying the lunar mansions

title: Daksha's curse on Candra
description: Daksha curses the Moon-god Soma to waste away for neglecting his other 26 wives in favor of Rohini

title: Devī manifests and Himavat questions her
description: After the cosmos longs for the Goddess and Himavat propitiates her, the Devī appears in dazzling form and Himavat asks her to reveal her true nature and the means of liberation

title: Dānava birth of Maya
description: Maya is born a Dānava, son of Danu and Kaśyapa, brother of Namuci, in the asura genealogy

title: Dream-revelation to Budha-Kauśika
description: Śiva appears to the sage Budha-Kauśika in a dream and dictates the Rāma-rakṣā Stotra, which the sage records on waking

title: Durga formed from the gods' pooled tejas
description: The combined radiance of the gods coalesces into the supreme Goddess Durga/Candika to confront the asura host

title: Durvasa's curse strips the devas of fortune
description: Durvasa gifts Indra a divine garland; Indra carelessly lets Airavata trample it, and the insulted sage curses the devas to lose all sri, weakening them

title: Durvāsas gifts a garland to Indra
description: The sage Durvāsas offers Indra a never-fading celestial garland, which Indra, seated on Airāvata, carelessly places on the elephant's head

title: Emanation and stationing of the Aṣṭa-Bhairava as directional kṣetrapālas
description: From the supreme Kāla-Bhairava emanate eight kṣetrapāla-Bhairavas — Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodha, Unmatta, Kapāla, Bhīṣaṇa, Saṃhāra — each stationed to guard one of the eight directions, each pairing one-to-one with a Mātṛkā Śakti in the Śrī Chakra and presiding over eight further sub-Bhairavas to yield the sixty-four Bhairavas; they anchor the guardian-circuits of Kāśī and Ujjain
source: Skanda Purāṇa (Kāśī Khaṇḍa); Rudrayāmala Tantra; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Enumeration of the pañca-sarovara (five sacred lakes)
description: Tradition fixes a closed roster of five supreme lakes — Mānasa, Puṣkara, Bindu, Pampā, Nārāyaṇa — binding far-flung sites into one sacred circuit

title: Establishment of the Ashta Svayam-vyakta class
description: Padma and Garuda Puranas fix the closed set of eight self-disclosed Vishnu icons as the apex tier of the Pancharatra five-fold arca-grading
actors: Vishnu; Pancharatra Agama tradition; Padma & Garuda Purana redactors
source: Padma Purana (Patala Khanda); Garuda Purana; Pancharatra Agama; Divya Suri Carita

title: Gautama as Saptarṣi and Gautama-gotra founder
description: Gautama is reckoned a Saptarṣi of the present Vaivasvata Manvantara and eponymous ancestor of the Gautama (Gotama) gotra, a Vedic seer whose ṛṣi-status frames the whole episode
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa Saptarṣi lists; Ṛgveda Gotama hymns

title: Gayāsura's Penance
description: The colossal asura Gaya performs terrible austerities until his body becomes so pure that the mere sight or touch of him sends beings straight to Vaikuṇṭha

title: Generation of Murugan from Shiva's Six Sparks
description: To produce a deva commander able to slay Surapadma, Murugan is generated from Shiva's six fiery sparks, nursed by the Krittikas and fused into the six-faced Shanmukha

title: Ghoṣā healed by the Aśvins
description: The skin-afflicted, long-unmarried seer Ghoṣā praises the physician-twins the Aśvins, who restore her health and youth so she can wed

title: Ghṛtācī bears the ten sons of Raudrāśva
description: The Paurava king Raudrāśva/Rudrāśva unites with the apsarā Ghṛtācī and begets ten sons (the -eyu brothers) from whom the Paurava–Bhārata dynastic stem descends through Matināra toward Saṃvaraṇa, Kuru, and ultimately the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.20

title: Hayagrīva narrates the Lalitā lore to Agastya
description: In the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa's Lalitopākhyāna, the horse-headed Viṣṇu-form Hayagrīva narrates the Lalitā Sahasranāma and Triśatī to the ṛṣi Agastya, the charter-myth of Śrīvidyā transmission

title: Hālāsya founding & the 64 Tiruviḷaiyāḍal
description: Śiva-Sundareśvara consecrates Madurā with falling nectar and founds the lotus-plan city in the Kaḍamba forest, the setting of his sixty-four sacred sports

title: Huhū Cursed to Become the Crocodile (Gajendra-mokṣa)
description: The gandharva Huhū pulls sage Devala's leg while sporting in water and is cursed to become the crocodile that seizes the elephant Gajendra, released only when Viṣṇu liberates Gajendra

title: Indra slays Viśvarūpa Triśiras
description: Fearing the three-headed Viśvarūpa's divided loyalty, Indra beheads him, committing brahmahatyā; from the severed heads spring birds

title: Indra slays Vritra
description: Fortified by soma, Indra hurls the vajra forged by Tvashtr and smashes the serpent Vritra, releasing the captive cosmic waters and ordering the cosmos

title: Indra Slays Vritra (Vritrahatya)
description: Indra wields the vajra to slay the serpent-dragon Vritra who had dammed the cosmic waters, releasing the seven rivers — the central Vedic act of cosmic order over chaos

title: Indra Slays Vṛtra and Flees
description: After killing the brāhmaṇa-born Vṛtra, Indra is overtaken by brahmahatyā and hides in a lotus-stalk, leaving heaven kingless

title: Indra teaches Dadhyañc the Madhu-vidyā
description: Indra imparts the esoteric honey-doctrine (Madhu-vidyā) to Dadhyañc, binding it with a curse that his head will be struck off if he teaches it to anyone

title: Śaṅkukarṇa the merchant-serpent yields his hoard
description: a miser reborn a serpent guarding his buried treasure is restored to human form and sent to Viṣṇu-loka when his sons recite Gītā chapter 7 over the gold

title: Śāntā-Durgā stills the Hari-Hara war
description: when Viṣṇu and Śiva battle to the ruin of the worlds, Brahmā appeals to the Great Goddess, who descends between them and pacifies the fight, earning the name Durgā-of-peace

title: Sārasvata re-teaches the Vedas to sixty thousand ṛṣis
description: the returning sages, having forgotten scripture, accept the boy-brahmarṣi as preceptor and relearn the lost Vedas from his unbroken memory

title: Sarasvatī opens the door of knowledge
description: pleased by the accidental seed-syllable, the Goddess makes the fool a seer and poet in an instant, equal to the Muni Vālmīki

title: Sarasvatī's gift of all sound to the nāgas
description: moved by the couple's ruin, the nāga king Aśvatara propitiates Sarasvatī, who grants him and his brother Kambala mastery of every musical note, scale, and poetic art

title: Śatadhanu's lapse at the Bhāgīrathī
description: after the Kārttika full-moon fast, the king courteously converses with a pāṣaṇḍa (his arms-preceptor's friend) while Śaibyā turns away and gazes at the sun

title: Śatākṣī weeps the rains
description: invoked by the starving Brāhmaṇas, the Great Goddess manifests covered with a hundred eyes and, weeping torrents from them, ends the drought — whence her name Śatākṣī, the Hundred-Eyed

title: Sāterī the anthill-mother
description: the aniconic earth-goddess is worshipped in her living termite-mound (roeṇ), the oldest stratum of Goan religion, widely identified with Śāntā-Durgā/Śānterī

title: Satī's Eye Falls at Tārāpīṭha
description: in the Birbhum reckoning the eye / third eye (nayana-tārā) of Satī falls at Tārāpīṭha as Viṣṇu dismembers her corpse, sanctifying the death-ground pīṭha

title: Satyavrata's Lokāyata bait
description: the envious atheist neighbour Satyavrata exploits the grief, arguing that Liṅga-worship caused the losses and that virtue is a fraud to be traded for hedonism

title: Sauminī's fall from brahmin girl to outcaste
description: a widowed brahmin girl, fallen through lust to a Śūdra husband and cāṇḍāla status, eats meat, drinks wine, and drunkenly kills a calf, and is reborn by Yama as a blind, leprous Cāṇḍāla daughter

title: Seven sons from the dead king
description: obeying the boon, the chaste Bhadrā conceives by her dead husband and bears seven children — three Śalvas and four Madras, eponyms of those peoples

title: Shiva appears as Rudra to Nārada at Rudraprayag
description: the music-proud sage's penance at the Mandākinī confluence draws Shiva's Rudra form, who graces him in music; a tāṇḍava variant also circulates [folk]

title: Sight restored to the blind
description: the Aśvins give back sight to Ṛjrāśva (blinded by his father) and Kaṇva, and make the blind-and-lame Parāvṛj see and walk

title: Śikhidhvaja dismisses his enlightened wife
description: Asked about her new radiance, Cūḍālā says she has found the Self; the king laughs her off as a prattling child, refusing to believe a wife could be enlightened

title: Sīmantinī takes the Somavāra-vrata
description: warned by astrologers she will be widowed young, princess Sīmantinī is taught the Monday fast of Śiva-and-Gaurī by Maitreyī, wife of Yājñavalkya, and keeps it faithfully

title: Śiva bursts from the liṅga as the tiger-lord
description: on Śivarātri, as a meditating devotee is attacked by the tiger-shaped Daitya, Śiva springs from the worshipped liṅga, pins Dundubhinirhrāda under his armpit and kills him with a fist-blow, then vows to lift the torments of all who see him in that form

title: Śiva descends as the Pulaya
description: to humble Brahmin pride, Śiva takes the body of a drunken untouchable corpse-bearer (with Pārvatī and Gaṇapati as his family) and walks a forest path

title: Śiva exiled from Kāśī to Mount Mandara
description: Bound by Divodāsa's compact, Śiva must forsake his never-forsaken city Avimukta and pine for it on Mandara with the newly-wed Pārvatī

title: Śiva flees Kailāsa as a deer into the Śleṣmāntaka forest
description: Wearied of duty, Śiva abandons Kailāsa and roams the Bāgmatī valley as an antelope, refusing to return

title: Jaimini's four Mahabharata questions referred to the four birds
description: The Mimamsa master Jaimini brings four unresolved Mahabharata puzzles to Markandeya, who deflects him to four wise birds whose answers open the Purana

title: Kacha and Devayānī's mutual curses
description: Kacha steals the revival-mantra from Śukra; refusing to wed Devayānī, the two exchange curses sealing her future marriage to a kṣatriya

title: Kadrū–Vinatā wager and the slave-bet
description: Kaśyapa's co-wives Kadrū and Vinatā bet on the horse Uccaiḥśravas; Kadrū wins by cheating and enslaves Vinatā

title: Kama burnt to ash by Shiva's third eye
description: Sent to break Shiva's meditation and kindle desire for Parvati, Kama looses an arrow and Shiva opens his third eye to reduce him to ash, whence the name Ananga

title: Kāmākṣī's Penance and Marriage to Śiva (Ekāmra Legend)
description: At Kāñcī, Kāmākṣī fashions a sand Śiva-liṅga under a mango tree and shields it with her body as the Vegavati floods to test her; Śiva, won, takes her as bride

title: Kojagari Lakshmi Puja — 'Ko jagarti?'
description: Lakshmi roams the Sharad full-moon night asking 'who is awake?' and blesses the wakeful with wealth, kept as the Kojagara/Kaumudi vrata of nightlong vigil
actors: Lakshmi; devotees keeping vigil (jagarana); regional: Kartikeya/Kumara (Odisha)
source: Skanda Purana; Brahmavaivarta Purana (Kojagara/Kaumudi vrata); regional Bengal/Mithila/Odisha tradition

title: Kūrma bears Mount Mandara at the Samudra-manthana
description: Vishnu becomes the tortoise and dives beneath the sinking Mount Mandara to serve as the churning-pivot for the ocean of milk, the cosmogonic deed Śrīkūrmam localizes
source: Kūrma Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8; Mahābhārata Ādi-parva; Śrīkūrma-māhātmya

title: Kārttikeya departs to Śrīśaila after the Gaṇeśa marriage-contest
description: The boy Skanda, slighted when Gaṇeśa wins the marriage-precedence contest, leaves Kailāsa in pique and settles as an ascetic on the southern hill

title: Kāverī born as Brahmā's daughter / Lopāmudrā, raised by Kavera
description: The river-goddess Kāverī (Kāveramma), daughter of Brahmā and identified with Lopāmudrā, is fostered by the sage-king Kavera at Brahmagiri

title: Lalitā Tripura-Sundarī arises and slays Bhaṇḍāsura
description: Bhaṇḍāsura, formed from the ashes of Kāmadeva, conquers the worlds; the gods' fire-offering produces Lalitā Tripura-Sundarī from the Cidagni-kuṇḍa, who weds Kāmeśvara, founds Śrī-Nagara, and annihilates Bhaṇḍa and his city Śūnyaka

title: Liṅgodbhava — Śiva's infinite pillar of fire
description: Disputing Brahmā and Viṣṇu are confronted by Śiva manifesting as a boundless column of fire whose ends neither can find

title: Mahakala Bursts Forth to Slay Dushana
description: When the demon Dushana torments Avanti, the devotee-king Candrasena (or boy Shrikara) cries out, and Shiva bursts from the earth as Mahakala, incinerates the demon, and stays forever as the jyotirlinga

title: Mahakali slays Madhu-Kaitabha
description: As the tamasika aspect, the Goddess slays the demons Madhu and Kaitabha in the first carita of the Devi Mahatmya

title: Mātṛkās Emanate to Fight Śumbha-Niśumbha
description: As Durgā battles the asura generals, the Sapta-Mātṛkās burst forth as śaktis from the bodies of the gods and join the Goddess to annihilate the demon host, re-merging into her at the end

title: Mudgala Purana Eight Incarnations of Ganesha
description: The Mudgala Purana narrates Ganesha's eight avataras (Vakratunda through Dhumravarna), each slaying a demon personifying an inner vice such as jealousy, pride, greed, anger, lust, and ego

title: Murugan slays Surapadma with the Vel
description: Parvati gives Murugan (Kartikeya/Skanda) the divine Vel lance, with which he slays the asura Surapadma/Soorapadman at Tiruchendur; commemorated by Thaipusam on the Pushya nakshatra of Tamil Thai, with penitential kavadi-bearing and vel-piercing

title: Ānanda Tāṇḍava in the Kanaka/Poṟ Sabhai (Chidambaram)
description: Śiva dances the Dance of Bliss in the golden hall at Thillai for the sages Patañjali and Vyāghrapāda, enacting the five cosmic acts (pañca-kṛtya)

title: Nandi's dual identity (bull vs. gaṇa-lord)
description: Tradition carries two figures under one name — Nandī the bull-mount and Nandikeśvara the anthropomorphic bull-faced gaṇa-chieftain — never fully merged
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Śaiva Āgamas; temple tradition

title: Nara–Nārāyaṇa take up eternal tapas at Badarikāśrama
description: Viṣṇu descends as the twin sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa, sons of Dharma, performing perpetual penance between the Nara and Nārāyaṇa peaks on the Alaknandā

title: Neminātha / Ariṣṭanemi renounces on his wedding day
description: The 22nd Tīrthaṅkara Neminātha (Ariṣṭanemi), a Yādava cousin of Vāsudeva Kṛṣṇa, renounces the world on his wedding day on hearing the cries of animals penned for the marriage feast, becoming the clearest narrative bridge between the Jain Tīrthaṅkara roster and the Hindu Kṛṣṇa cycle

title: Nārada asks Brahmā how to cross Kali
description: At the end of Dvāpara, the sage Nārada approaches the creator Brahmā and asks how one may be delivered from the evils of the Kali age

title: Nārada beholds the deformed rāgas and rāgiṇīs and undertakes tapas to master music
description: Vain of his musicianship, the celestial singer Nārada is led by Viṣṇu (var. Śiva) through the divine realm, where he sees maimed and crippled figures — the embodied rāgas and rāgiṇīs whose bodies he had broken by singing them out of tune and against rule. Shamed, he abandons his pride and undertakes severe tapas (var. learning from Tumburu) to master music properly and heal what he marred
source: Later Purāṇic / musicological and rāga-mālā lore; bhakti tradition (folk / devotional — not in the early epics)

title: Nārada frames the tale
description: Nārada narrates Gālava's story to dissuade Duryodhana from prideful obstinacy on the eve of the Kurukṣetra war

title: Origin of the Kīrtimukha — Śiva's wrath-being commanded to devour itself
description: When Jalandhara's envoy Rāhu demands Pārvatī, Śiva's wrath bursts forth as a ravening lion-faced being; with no other prey it is told to eat its own body, and the surviving jawless face is fixed forever above the temple door as Kīrtimukha, the 'Face of Glory'
source: Skanda Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā Yuddha-khaṇḍa); Coomaraswamy, 'The Face of Glory'

title: Parvati creates Ganesha from her body-dirt
description: Parvati forms a boy from the turmeric paste or scurf of her own body and breathes life into him as a guardian while she bathes

title: Pāṇḍava pursuit of Śiva for expiation
description: After Kurukṣetra, the Pāṇḍavas pursue Śiva to expiate kin- and Brahmin-slaying; Śiva evades them past Kāśī into the Garhwal Himalaya

title: Penance of Sutapas and Pṛśni
description: In the Svāyambhuva Manvantara the Prajāpati Sutapas and his wife Pṛśni perform tapas for twelve thousand celestial years until Viṣṇu appears and offers a boon

title: Piplada curses Shani
description: The Shiva-avatar Piplada, abandoned as a child, curses Saturn for the suffering his gaze causes, winning the boon that Shani would not afflict children under sixteen

title: Pulastya recites the tīrtha-catalogue to Bhīṣma
description: The sage Pulastya enumerates the holy fords of Bhāratavarṣa to a young Bhīṣma, the prototype anukramaṇī of tīrthas with their merits

title: Puṣpadanta granted the boon of invisibility
description: Śiva grants the gandharva Puṣpadanta the power of unseen movement wherever he wishes
source: Puṣpadanta frame-legend (Śiva-mahimnaḥ stotra tradition / Purāṇic legend)

title: Recitation of the Bilvashtaka at bilva-leaf offering
description: The eight-verse Bilvashtaka is recited as a samarpana-mantra while laying the trifoliate bilva leaf on the Shiva-linga in shiva-puja

title: Renewal of the cosmic administration at each manvantara turnover
description: At every manvantara turnover an entire cosmic administration is recreated: a new Manu, Indra, Devas, Saptarishis, sons of Manu, and a manvantara-avatara of Vishnu

title: Rukmangada's Ekadashi-vrata empties Yama's realm
description: King Rukmangada so successfully enforces the Ekadashi fast that the sinful stop dying and Yama's underworld empties, prompting Yama to complain to Brahma

title: Sage Kālava Cured by the Navagrahas and Brahmā's Curse
description: The leprous sage Kalava is cured by the nine planets at Suryanar Kovil; Brahma curses the planets with leprosy for altering fate, and they regain health by worshipping Shiva there

title: Sarasvatī disappears at Vinaśana
description: The Sarasvatī river sinks underground and is lost to view (adarśana) in the desert sands at Vinaśana, out of disdain for the Niṣāda/Ābhīra tribes, running hidden before re-emerging; bathing at the vanishing-ford removes sin

title: Satī's yoni falls on Nīlācala
description: In the Daksha-yajña dismemberment, Satī's yoni falls on Nīlācala hill, sanctifying the supreme yoni-pīṭha

title: Sādhyas seek the highest good
description: A class of demigods, the Sādhyas, approach seeking instruction in the supreme good (śreyas), the highest dharma, and the conduct of the wise

title: Śiva gambles away his regalia
description: throw by throw Pārvatī wins his crescent moon, the serpent-necklace Vāsuki, his nāga ear-rings, elephant-hide and loincloth, stripping the ascetic bare

title: Śiva grants the Sudarśana Cakra
description: the pleased Śiva manifests and bestows the discus 'shining with a mass of splendour,' with which Viṣṇu at once slays the daityas

title: Śiva hides one flower
description: to test Viṣṇu's devotion Śiva secretly withdraws a single lotus, leaving the offering one short at the final name

title: Śiva Kapālin and Kapālamocana
description: for severing Brahmā's fifth head Śiva incurs Brahmahatyā, and the skull clings to his hand as kāpālika penance until it drops at Kapālamocana in Kāśī — the mythic charter of the skull-bearing vow

title: Śiva narrates the Gītā-Māhātmya to Pārvatī
description: in a timeless Śaiva teaching-scene Śiva relays Viṣṇu's dialogue with Lakṣmī, telling one deliverance-parable for each of the Gītā's eighteen chapters

title: Śiva seen in all; Viṣṇu stupefied
description: Viṣṇu unleashes his māyā, multiplying into countless forms, but Dadhīca perceives Parama-Śiva pervading every form, the Devas flee, and Viṣṇu is left motionless — the Liṅga Purāṇa's Śaiva-supremacy proof

title: Śiva settles on Kailāsa for Kubera's sake
description: Honouring the friendship, Śiva proceeds with his gaṇas to Mount Kailāsa beside Kubera's Alakā and takes his seat there — the Purāṇic charter of Kailāsa as Śiva's abode

title: Śiva slays Kāla to save Śveta
description: When Death lays hands on the rapt worshipper in the liṅga's presence, Śiva manifests and strikes Kāla dead, vindicating the devotee's fearlessness as Kālakāla, the Death of death

title: Śiva smitten by the huntress
description: the god who fled a woman seizes the vanishing Śabarī's hand and is sent to seek her from her 'father' Himavān, the disguise naming its own truth

title: Śiva storms off to the forest
description: shamed and stripped, the god abandons Pārvatī and Kailāsa to sit alone in yoga in the Siddhavaṭa forest

title: Śiva tells Pārvatī the Great Tale on Kailāsa
description: Pārvatī demands a story never before heard, and behind barred doors Śiva narrates the tale of the seven Vidyādhara emperors, overheard by the invisible gaṇa Puṣpadanta

title: Śiva the tiger and 'trāhi mām gīrīśa'
description: Śiva takes tiger-form to frighten Pārvatī, who cries 'trāhi mām gīrīśa!' ('Lord of the mountains, save me!'), and from 'mām gīrīśa' the liṅga takes the name Mangeś

title: Śiva worships Maṅgala Caṇḍī before the Tripura war
description: the beneficent form of Caṇḍī grants Śiva victory over the three cities, after which her Tuesday and household worship spreads

title: Śiva worships Maṅgalā Caṇḍī before Tripura
description: the destroyer bows to the beneficent fortune-goddess for victory and conquers the three flying cities as Tripurāntaka, spreading her Tuesday cult through the worlds

title: Śiva's boon: Madālasā reborn from a nāga
description: hymning Śiva with their new song, the nāgas win the boon that Madālasā be reborn as Aśvatara's daughter through a śrāddha rite he performs and consumes

title: Śiva's gaṇas repel Yama's messengers for Guṇanidhi
description: Yama's noose-bearing messengers come for the slain sinner but Śiva's gaṇas read out his accidental Śivarātri merit and carry him to Śiva's realm

title: Śiva's return to Kāśī
description: Śiva re-enters Kāśī in triumphal procession with Pārvatī and the gaṇa-host, never to leave again — the charter of Avimukta and Viśveśvara's eternal residence

title: Śiva's wedding-priests settled at Hāṭakeśvara
description: Śiva creates a class of Brāhmaṇas to officiate at his marriage to Umā and settles them permanently in the kṣetra, the founding pedigree of the Nāgara Brāhmaṇas

title: Śivaśarman tests his five sons
description: the yogin-brahmin subjects his five sons to conjured ordeals, including dismembering their mother's illusory corpse, opening the Somaśarman–Suvrata piety cycle

title: Slaying of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa charters the Sandhi Pūjā
description: the 48-minute Aṣṭamī–Navamī juncture worships the Goddess as Cāmuṇḍā at the instant Kālī beheaded Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa in the Devī Māhātmya war

title: Slaying of Pātālaketu with Tvaṣṭṛ's weapon
description: Kuvalayāśva weds Madālasā, and when the Dānava host attacks their departure he looses the divine weapon of Tvaṣṭṛ, reducing Pātālaketu and his demons to heaps of bones

title: Slaying of Ratnāsura
description: Jyotibā kills the demon Ratnāsura on the hill thereafter named Ratnāgiri, where he settles as Vāḍī-Ratnāgirīcā Jyotibā

title: Soma abducts Tārā
description: The Moon-god Soma, infatuated, carries off Tārā the wife of his teacher Bṛhaspati and refuses to return her, triggering a cosmic crisis
source: Padma Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata

title: Somaprabhā's automata of Maya
description: the asura-engineer's daughter entertains her friend Kaliṅgasenā with Maya's mechanical dolls that fetch garlands, bring water, dance and guard — a locus classicus of Indian automata

title: Sukalā the pativratā defeats Indra and Kāma
description: while her merchant husband is away on pilgrimage, Indra and Kāma conspire to break Sukalā's fidelity and are routed by her pativrata power

title: Śukra curses the ungrateful Daityas
description: spurned in favour of the imposter, Śukra curses the asuras to defeat and lost power; they repent only when Bṛhaspati vanishes, the war already lost

title: Śukra revives Dadhīca; Śiva hardens his spine
description: struck near death, Dadhīca is restored by Śukra's Mṛta-sañjīvanī, then wins from Śiva a boon making his backbone many times harder than the vajra — the etiology of the bones that will one day slay Vṛtra

title: Śukra's husk-smoke tapas for the counter-lore
description: leaderless in the deva war, Śukra performs Śiva's head-down chaff-smoke penance for a thousand years and wins an invincible mantra, Prajāpati-hood and avadhyatva

title: Śukra's mind-made lifetimes
description: Young Śukra follows an apsarā in mind through heaven and a chain of imagined rebirths while his body withers, until Kāla shows Bhṛgu that mind alone transmigrates and the revived Śukra becomes the asuras' preceptor

title: Sukumārī's fidelity and the reconciliation
description: Sukumārī cleaves to her ape-faced husband unflinching, and Parvata, moved, releases Nārada from the curse while Nārada frees Parvata to ascend to heaven

title: Sulabhā defeats Janaka in debate
description: the woman renouncer Sulabhā enters King Janaka's court and refutes his claim that a woman cannot attain liberation, as narrated by Bhīṣma

title: Sumati's hell-birth for thwarting cattle
description: in his seventh former birth the wise dullard Sumati (Jaḍa), born a merchant, blocks thirsty cattle from water and is cast for a century into a hell of iron-beaked birds and rivers of blood

title: Sumukha chosen from Airāvata's line
description: Mātali selects the young Nāga Sumukha, son of Cikura and grandson of Āryaka, as Guṇakeśī's husband

title: Sundarar's descent from Kailāsa
description: the gana Ālāla Sundarar is sent to earthly birth for loving two of Pārvatī's attendants, framing the whole epic

title: Sūrapadma's boon of Śiva
description: the daitya Sūrapadma, son of Kaśyapa and Māyā, wins from Śiva sovereignty over the worlds and invulnerability to all but a son of Śiva

title: Sūrapadma's defiance and the burning of the city
description: the asura mocks Skanda as a child and refuses; Vīrabāhu routs the guards, lays waste the assembly-hall and gardens, and returns to report

title: Sūrasaṃhāram and the split into peacock and cock
description: Sūrapadma rises from the sea as a world-spanning mango tree; the Vēl splits it into Skanda's peacock-mount and cock-banner, the enemy converted to service

title: Suratha and Samadhi meet at Medhas's hermitage
description: A king who lost his kingdom and a betrayed merchant, both still attached to those who wronged them, meet at the forest hermitage of sage Medhas, framing the Devi Mahatmya

title: Sureśvara — Śiva tests Upamanyu as Indra
description: Śiva appears as Indra offering boons and reviling Śiva; Upamanyu refuses any gift but Śiva's and would rather die than hear the blasphemy
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Śatarudra-saṃhitā 32; Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva

title: Suryaa's wedding to Soma
description: Suryaa, daughter of Surya/Savitr, is wed to Soma with the Ashvins as wooers, the hymn becoming the charter of the Hindu vivaha rite

title: Suśarman the bullock freed by a parrot's chapter
description: a sinful brahmin reborn an oil-press ox is delivered when a courtesan gifts him merit earned by overhearing a caged parrot recite Gītā chapter 1

title: Svayaṃvara reunion and ascent beyond Indra
description: Śaibyā chooses her former lord at her svayaṃvara; he reigns, sacrifices, dies in battle, she mounts his pyre, and both rise beyond Indra's sphere

title: Śveta defies Death's universal boast
description: Kāla claims nothing in the three worlds escapes him, even the gods; the sage answers that one whose heart holds Maheśvara has nothing to dread, and continues his liṅga-pūjā

title: Śveta granted deathlessness
description: With Death destroyed, the sage is freed from mortality altogether — the Liṅga Purāṇa's proof that liṅga-worship confers mṛtyuṃjaya, distinct from the Mārkaṇḍeya telling

title: Śvetaketu binds the marriage-vow
description: outraged to see a Brahmana lead his mother away, Śvetaketu son of Uddālaka institutes the rule of wifely fidelity, the charter Pāṇḍu cites for controlled niyoga

title: Tālaketu's false death-report
description: the slain demon's brother Tālaketu, disguised as a Yamunā-bank ascetic, tricks the prince out of his neck-jewel and carries a lie to the capital that Kuvalayāśva has been speared and burned

title: Tāpoi and the Khudurukuṇī Oṣā
description: the tormented merchant's daughter is saved by goddess Maṅgaḷā, re-performed by unmarried girls each Bhādraba Sunday in coastal Odisha [folk] [oral tradition]

title: Tārā Suckles the Poison-Burnt Śiva
description: after Śiva swallows the halāhala at the Samudra Manthana and his throat burns, the goddess Tārā takes him as an infant to her breast and nurses away the venom's fire, the icon enshrined at Tārāpīṭha
source: Tārāpīṭha sthala tradition; cf. Samudra Manthana

title: Tarakasura's boon and the liṅga at his throat
description: The boon-protected asura Tārakāsura wears a Śivaliṅga that makes his body proof against death, slayable only by a son of Śiva
source: Skanda Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā, Kumāra-khaṇḍa); local Andhra sthala-purāṇa

title: Ten thousand brāhmaṇas fed through the famine
description: Gautama sustains ten thousand brāhmaṇas and munis for the whole twelve famine-years, his refuge-āśrama swelling to a hundred-yojana boundary and his fame reaching Indra's court

title: The 1,008-world empire from Vīramahendrapuram
description: Sūrapadma conquers the three worlds, rules 1,008 aṇḍas from the sea-fortress Māyaṉ built, and enslaves the devas

title: The 64 Yoginīs stay in Kāśī
description: Sent by Śiva to find a flaw in Divodāsa, the 64 Yoginīs find none, fall in love with the city, and settle there permanently

title: The ajapā-naṭanam
description: Tiruvārūr's Vīdhividaṅkar sways in the "dance without chanting," borne on the rhythm of breath alone as Somāskanda rocks on Viṣṇu's chest

title: The amma-theyyam raised at the kāvus
description: across 100+ Muchilōṭṭu kāvus of North Malabar the possessed dancer becomes the living Bhagavatī, the grand Perunkaḷiyāṭṭam held only at long intervals

title: The Aṅkāḷammaṉ and Kerala recensions
description: the Nīli myth is absorbed into the fierce goddess Aṅkāḷaparamēcuvari's cult, while the Malayalam Yakṣi-Nīli of Kalliyaṅkāḍu is subdued by the sorcerer Kaṭamaṟṟattu Kattanār

title: The anna-dāna charter of self-consumption
description: the recurring parable that a king who fed only himself must in death feed on himself, twinning the Rāmāyaṇa Śveta with the Mahābhārata's dāna-upākhyāna and the half-golden mongoose
source: Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa 77–78; Mahābhārata Vana & Āśvamedhika Parvas

title: The Anna-vows — never disparage food
description: The injunctions annam na nindyāt, na paricakṣīta, bahu kurvīta and to turn no guest from one's door establish food-reverence and hospitality as spiritual attainment

title: The armed ascetics of Badarī humble a conqueror
description: the recurring motif in which a proud challenger mistakes Nara-Nārāyaṇa for weaklings and is undone: Prahlāda in a thousand-year duel, Dambhodbhava by a fistful of grass-blades
source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9; Vāmana Purāṇa; Mahābhārata 5.94

title: The Āṣāḍhī–Kārttikī Wārī cycle
description: twice yearly, at the Ekādaśīs of Viṣṇu's cosmic sleep (Śayanī) and waking (Prabodhinī), the Jñāneśvar (Āḷandī) and Tukārām (Dehu) pālkhīs with hundreds of thousands of Vārkarīs converge on Pandharpur

title: The Aśvins and Sarasvatī restore Indra
description: the twin healers and the goddess supply the loophole-foam and cure Indra, drawing his stolen strength back out through the surā

title: The Bhārgava gotra seeded from a king
description: Vītahavya, now a Brahmarṣi, begets Gṛtsamada (seer of Ṛgveda Maṇḍala II), founding the line to Śunaka and Śaunaka and the Vītahavya/Gṛtsamada Bhārgava gaṇa of the pravara-lists

title: The birth of Skanda from six sparks
description: Śiva emits six fiery sparks, the Kṛttikās nurse them into the six-faced Ṣaṇmukha, armed with Pārvatī's Vēl as Devasenāpati

title: The bleeding stone in the well
description: three disabled brothers digging a well in drought-parched Kāṇipākam strike a hard object that wells up blood, and the blood-mingled spring-water instantly cures all three of blindness, deafness, and muteness/lameness

title: The boar's cry and the half-uttered bīja
description: a boar wounded by a fowler flees into Satyavrata's hermitage, and in pity the illiterate ascetic cries "Aiṃ! Aiṃ!" — the vāg-bīja of Sarasvatī voiced by pure accident, its meaning unknown to him

title: The bonfire of the hermitage and the king's awakening
description: Śikhidhvaja burns hut, staff, rosary and deer-skin; Kumbha teaches that the mind alone is the 'all' to be renounced, and the king awakens from samādhi a jīvanmukta

title: The boon of a gold-voiding son
description: pleased with Sṛñjaya, Nārada grants him a son whose every excretion turns to gold, to be named Suvarṇaṣṭhīvin, warning that the very gold will make the boy short-lived

title: The boy-guardian of the threshold
description: as kṣetrapāla and dvārapāla, Vaṭuka is propitiated first at temple boundaries before the fiercer Bhairavas and the main shrine

title: The brahma-vs-kṣatra debate
description: King Kṣupa and the sage Dadhīca, once friends, quarrel over whether the kṣatriya or the brāhmaṇa is supreme, until the sage strikes the king on the head with his fist

title: The Brahmakuṇḍa formed
description: the water-child is penned amid the four mountains Kailāsa, Gandhamādana, Jārudhi and Saṃvartaka, growing as the sacred red lake Brahmakuṇḍa

title: The Brihadaranyaka fuses rta, satya and dharma
description: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4.14 declares satya and dharma to be one and nothing higher than dharma, the pivotal late-Vedic teaching bridging the old cosmic order (rta) into the new ethical-legal order

title: The caṇḍāla frees the brahmarākṣasa Somaśarmā
description: An ekādaśī-keeping outcaste devotee of Viṣṇu keeps his pledge to return to be eaten, then gifts part of his vigil-merit to free the demon Somaśarmā from his rākṣasa state

title: The Cāndrāyaṇa lunar fast
description: the penitent's food waxes and wanes with the moon: mouthfuls decrease each day of the dark fortnight to a total fast on new-moon, then increase through the bright fortnight to the full-moon peak

title: The catalogue of sins and torments
description: at the king's asking the officer recites which crimes earn which hells — eye-torture for covetousness, the torn tongue for false teachers, the saw for sowers of discord — with the maxim that a trifling sin still pricks like a thorn

title: The chain of ignorant sages
description: Keśidhvaja's priests, then Kaśeru, then Śunaka each confess they do not know the expiation, leaving only his exiled enemy Khāṇḍikya able to purify the rite

title: The chain of the arts
description: Mārkaṇḍeya declares that image-making cannot be learned without painting, painting without dance, dance without instrumental music, and that without vocal song — binding all the arts into one dependent tree

title: The champion who dies by treachery becomes a god
description: the Northern Songs run the North-Malabar vīra-ārādhana engine: a martial hero martyred in valour or betrayal is venerated at shrines and embodied as theyyam, the deified-hero logic shared with Kathivanur Veeran
source: Vaṭakkan Pāṭṭukaḷ; Kurup, Cult of Teyyam

title: The Chandra river heads the Chandrabhāgā at the Moon Lake
description: Chandra Tāl sits at the source-basin of the Chandra ("moon") river, which joins the Bhāga to form the Chandrabhāgā, the Chenab of the Punjab five-rivers, giving the Moon Lake a place at the head of a great Indus tributary

title: The chase into Pātāla
description: Kuvalayāśva pursues the boar-shaped Dānava Pātālaketu across thousands of yojanas until it plunges into a chasm, and horse and rider fall in after it into the netherworld

title: The chaste lady raises her fallen husband to heaven
description: A śūdra wife nurses her courtesan-keeping, disease-stricken husband, follows him onto the pyre, and both ascend to heaven — Dharmāṅgada's exemplum for honouring Mohinī without jealousy

title: The Chiranjīvī Hanumān localised as Bālājī
description: the deathless Tretā-Yuga Rudrāvatāra, son of Vāyu, is worshipped as the Rajasthani folk healer Bālājī, doctrinally present in Kali Yuga by his own immortal nature

title: The city of jīvanmuktas
description: realization spreads from Hemacūḍa to King Muktacūḍa, prince Maṇicūḍa, ministers and citizens until the whole Daśārṇa city becomes a community of the liberated who still farm, rule, and worship

title: The color-omen spring of Tulmul
description: the hexagonal spring of Kṣīr Bhavānī changes color as an omen for Kashmir, milky-white to rose in peace but blackening before calamity, receiving milk and kheer offerings

title: The contest of Veda versus the lute
description: the Gandharvas woo Vāc by reciting the Veda while the gods invent the vīṇā and win her with song and dance

title: The cow offered to the ancestors — the saving reflex
description: before eating, the seven dedicate the flesh as a śrāddha to the pitṛs, and that single act of ancestor-piety earns them unbroken memory of former births through everything that follows

title: The cow returns as Queen Sannati
description: the soul of the slaughtered cow is reborn as Sannati, who weds Brahmadatta and bears his son Viṣvaksena, closing the karmic circle of the founding sin

title: The deer family's pleas and pledges
description: a pregnant doe, a second doe, and the stag each come to the water in successive watches, plead in human speech for reprieve, and vow to return to be killed

title: The deity who comes out to the excluded
description: across the Purī triad the same grace-pattern recurs: shut out as yavana, untouchable, or too poor, the devotee loves anyway and Jagannātha comes out to meet him, teaching that his grace is casteless, creedless, and cannot be timetabled

title: The devas restored and the deva-bride
description: the prison is opened, Jayanta and the gods freed, Indra restored, and Skanda weds Indra's foster-daughter Deivānai at Tirupparaṅkuṉṟam

title: The Devī re-charters a dynasty
description: the Śākta Devī-Bhāgavata rewrites the Haihaya eponym's origin as a mantra-driven divine descent, giving the marauding Haihaya house a Goddess-devotee founder

title: The Devī rests at Saptaśṛṅgī after slaying Mahiṣa
description: the eighteen-armed goddess of the seven-peaked hill at Vaṇī is read as the Devī-Māhātmya's Mahiṣa-slayer resting after battle, with Mārkaṇḍeya reciting her Māhātmya from the facing hill

title: The Diamond-Needle thesis posed
description: The Upaniṣad announces the vajra-sūcī teaching that destroys ignorance and poses its central question: what makes one a brāhmaṇa?

title: The diptych's opposed morals
description: set adjacent and unreconciled, the pair teaches both that varṇa is fixed by birth (Mātaṅga refused by Indra) and that it is moved by a sage's fiat (Vītahavya raised by Bhṛgu) — a Brāhmaṇa the gatekeeper either way

title: The disguised sage's chess wager
description: Krishna, arriving as a travelling sage, challenges the chess-loving Chempakasseri king and asks only for rice doubled square by square across the board

title: The dismembered goddess and the pīṭhas
description: grief-mad Śiva bears Satī's corpse across the worlds; her body is cut apart and its pieces fall as the Śakti pīṭhas, localised in the Kathmandu Valley

title: The doctrine of united brahma-kṣatra
description: the upākhyāna's charter: the Brahmaṇa's energy and the Kṣatriya's energy are twin pillars of sovereignty that conquer joined and fail divided

title: The dog of Vaidiśā garlanded
description: Śaibyā, reborn a jātismarā princess of Kāśī, refuses all suitors, recognizes her husband reborn as a dog at Vaidiśā, garlands him and names his fault; remembering, he dies in the desert

title: The doves feed the hunter at Kapota-tīrtha
description: A male and female pigeon cast themselves into the fire to feed a starving hunter-guest and both ascend to heaven, chartering the ford

title: The dudhe-bhāte boon
description: the humble ferryman asks not for wealth or heaven but only that his children live ever "in milk and rice," a line that passed into Bengali speech as the archetypal blessing

title: The eight forms of marriage
description: the code grades marriage from the meritorious Brāhma gift of a daughter down through Gāndharva to the Rākṣasa and Paiśāca abduction/rape, assigning each to its varṇas

title: The eighteen titles of law (vyavahāra)
description: Manu enumerates the eighteen grounds of litigation, from non-payment of debt through assault, theft and adultery, systematising civil and criminal procedure

title: The encounter on the narrow path
description: the Pulaya meets the ācārya on a way too narrow for two and refuses to step aside for the purity code, opening the dispute

title: The eponymous charter for Gāndhāra
description: the Uttara-kāṇḍa ties two real northwestern cities into the Ikṣvāku line by deriving their names from Bharata's sons, a foundation-legend claiming Gandhāra for the Solar dynasty

title: The equivocal-oath ordeal
description: a suspected wife passes a Yakṣa chastity-ordeal by having her lover embrace her disguised as a madman, then swearing truthfully that no man touched her but her husband and this lunatic

title: The errand to the lake
description: near a city Viṣṇu feigns thirst and sends Nārada down to fetch water from a tank, the threshold between the sage's true self and the coming dream

title: The ever-growing Ganesha
description: the Kāṇipākam svayambhū is held to be slowly enlarging as a living stone, the stock proof being a donated silver kavaca that no longer fits the grown image

title: The fall of Guṇanidhi
description: The brahmin Yajñadatta of Kāmpilya discovers via a gem-ring on a gambler's hand that his son Guṇanidhi has ruined himself at dice, and disowns him

title: The fall of the asura champions
description: over the six-day war Sūrapadma's son Bānukōpaṉ and his brothers Taraka and Siṃhamukha are cut down by Skanda's Vēl

title: The Father and the Daughter (RV 10.61)
description: the earliest, veiled attestation: the Father unites with the Daughter and spills his seed on the earth, and the gods fashion the brahman and form Vāstoṣpati to set the deed right

title: The fed brāhmaṇas turn envious
description: when good rains return and harvests abound, the sheltered brāhmaṇas grow jealous of the honour heaped on their host and resolve to abandon his āśrama

title: The five further births awakened
description: Śaibyā tracks Śatadhanu as jackal on mount Kolāhala, wolf, vulture, crow, and peacock, reminding him each time of the heretic-conversation until he abandons each body

title: The five gandharva maidens delivered
description: cursed into a piśāca-state, five gandharva maidens are restored when a passing vratin gifts them a share of his Māgha-snāna merit

title: The five great sins and their penances (prāyaścitta)
description: brahmin-murder, drinking liquor, stealing gold, violating the guru's bed and association with such sinners are graded as mahāpātaka, expiated by Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa fasts

title: The five mahāpātakas codified
description: Manu names the five mortal sins — brahmahatyā, surāpāna, gold-theft, violating the guru's bed, and association with those who do — each demanding caste-loss and the heaviest expiation

title: The foam of the waters at twilight
description: Indra beheads Namuci in the dawn-mist with the foam of the waters (apāṃ phena), the one instrument that is neither wet nor dry, no weapon, and struck at neither day nor night

title: The foot-dipping taboo of Chandra Tāl
description: because the moon-lake is held to be the threshold of Yudhiṣṭhira's heavenward departure, Spiti locals revere it as a doorway between earth and Svarga and traditionally refuse to dip their feet in its water

title: The forms foretold
description: in the Nārāyaṇī Stuti the Goddess prophesies she will become Śatākṣī, Śākambharī and Durgā in a future age of hundred-year drought — the older text's seed of the whole episode

title: The four friends of Mitralābha
description: the mouse Hiraṇyaka, crow Laghupatanaka, tortoise Mantharaka, and deer Citrāṅga cooperate to free one another, proving alliance among the weak defeats the strong

title: The four Kumāras seek liberation
description: The aged primordial sages Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, and Sanatkumāra wander seeking the truth of the Self

title: The four roots of dharma
description: Manu ranks the sources of law as Veda, Smṛti, the conduct of the good and the satisfaction of one's own conscience, the charter of Dharmaśāstra authority

title: The fourteen-birth ledger
description: the boy reveals he was, fourteen births earlier, Dharmajālika of Vidiśā, a hypocrite-preacher whose descent through hell, worm, crow and jackal explains suffering as karma across many lives

title: The gaṇa-disguised infiltration of Kailāsa
description: descending by Śāmbarī illusion in the guise of Śiva's attendants, the two Daityas approach the ball-playing Pārvatī, but Śiva reads the tremulousness of their eyes and warns her with a silent glance

title: The Gandharvas claim Vāc back
description: following after, the Gandharvas demand "the Soma is yours, let Vāc be ours," and the gods agree to a wooing-contest rather than let her be seized by force

title: The Gautamī serpent dialogue on karma
description: A bereaved mother Gautamī refuses to let a fowler kill the snake that killed her child; the serpent, Death, and Time each deflect blame until karma is named the true cause, teaching that vengeance is futile

title: The Gayasura legend
description: The daitya Gayasura's body grows so holy by devotion to Vishnu that touching it liberates anyone, threatening to empty hell; the gods perform a yajna on his recumbent body, Vishnu pins him with his foot, and dying he is granted the boon that his body become the eternal tirtha of Gaya where ancestral offerings free the dead
source: Garuda Purana; Vishnu Purana; Vayu Purana

title: The ghost Jaḍa released at Kāśī
description: a brahmin turned trader and murdered by robbers becomes a preta until his son's recitation of Gītā chapter 3 at Vārāṇasī lifts him and his ancestors to Vaikuṇṭha

title: The gleaner who reached the solar disc
description: Sūrya's own tale within the Nāga's account: a brāhmaṇa living by the Uñcha vow, subsisting on gleaned grain, fallen leaves, water, and air, won a station above the gods and to this day circles the Earth within the disc of the Sun

title: The Goddess behind the sword
description: the folk hero-song touches the Purāṇic frame where the champion's power flows from Lōkanārkāvu Bhagavatī, a Durgā/Bhadrakāḷī form, tying the Malabar kaḷari cult into the pan-Keralan Goddess complex
source: Vaṭakkan Pāṭṭukaḷ, Tacōḷi cycle; Lōkanārkāvu tradition

title: The Goddess hastens to Anubhūti (Tvaritā)
description: the Devī appears instantly at the widowed sage-wife Anubhūti's cry, slays the demon Kukura in his buffalo-form, and stays enthroned on the Bālā-ghāṭ hill as Tuḷjā Bhavānī

title: The Goddess stays on the Yamunācalā
description: at Anubhūti's prayer the Devī consents to remain permanently on the hill, the seat-fixing that turns a māhātmya rescue into a standing Śakti Pīṭha

title: The gods scatter the gem-seeds and the mines arise
description: Devas, nagas and celestial beings carry off the radiant seeds through the sky and drop them, and wherever a seed falls in ocean, river, mountain or forest a gem-mine (akara) is born
source: Garuda Purana, Purva-khanda gem chapters; Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha

title: The gods wipe their blood-guilt onto the Āptyas
description: because they knew of Viśvarūpa's killing, the guilt is drained onto Trita, Dvita, and Ekata with the rinse-water of every soma-rite ("For Trita thee!"), and they pass it on to the fee-less sacrificer

title: The grass-blade rout
description: Nara hurls a handful of iṣīkā grass-blades that fill the sky and pierce the eyes, ears, and noses of the emperor's host, and Dambhodbhava falls at the sage's feet begging protection

title: The Guptakṣetra and its phala-śruti
description: the Kaumārikā-khaṇḍa styles the Mahī-mouth a concealed 'hidden holy ground' and closes its 66 chapters with the fruit-of-hearing promised to whoever bathes there or hears its glory

title: The Haihaya war on Kāśī
description: Vītahavya and his hundred sons crush three generations of Kāśī kings — Haryaśva slain, Sudeva beaten, Divodāsa routed despite fortifying Vārāṇasī at Indra's command

title: The Hāṭakeśvara liṅga rises from Pātāla
description: a self-manifest Śiva-liṅga whose seat was in Nāgaloka surfaces at Vaḍnagar, named Hāṭakeśvara after the golden (hāṭaka) nether-world, and is received by the Nāgaras

title: The household stripped away
description: in old age Nandabhadra loses his son and then his chaste wife Kanakā, and the ever-composed merchant is at last driven to grief and doubt

title: The hunter outshines the brāhmaṇa Veda
description: An unlettered hunter's pure-faith worship of Śiva pleases the god more than the learned brāhmaṇa Veda's correct ritual

title: The illusion-test and recovery from the nāga's body
description: invited to Pātāla, Kuvalayāśva refuses Aśvatara's treasures, is warned "it is illusion, touch her not" as Madālasā is shown, faints, and learns she is truly restored from death

title: The illusory dying cow (māyā-dhenu)
description: the ingrate brāhmaṇas fashion an aged phantom cow by māyā and drive her into Gautama's homa-hall; when he shoos her she drops dead and they charge him with go-hatyā

title: The impossible doubled-grain debt
description: the doubling reaches 2^64 − 1 grains of rice, an unpayable mountain that no granary can meet, and the king despairs

title: The imprisonment of Jayanta and the devas
description: Indra is expelled from Amarāvatī and Jayanta and the gods are cast into the dungeon of Vīramahendrapuram and made menial servants

title: The Indo-Iranian dragon-slayer — Thraētaona / Thrita
description: the same figure survives in the Avesta: Āthwya's son Thraētaona (Fereydun) slays the three-headed dragon Aži Dahāka, and Thrita, the third Haoma-presser, becomes the first physician

title: The Indra temptation and staged infidelity
description: Cūḍālā conjures Indra inviting the king to heaven, then an illusion of Madanikā with a lover; Śikhidhvaja remains desireless and unangered, passing every test

title: The jīva returns and Padma revives
description: Vidūratha's soul travels back along the nesting into Padma's preserved corpse, which stirs to life, exposing the chain brahmin→Padma→Vidūratha→Padma as mere changes of mental scene

title: The justice-bell of Tiruvārūr
description: Manu Nīti Cholan hangs a bell at his palace gate for any wronged being to ring, and the bereaved mother-cow tolls it for judgment against the king's own heir

title: The Karṇikī widow's dying wish for Kāśī
description: a pious brahmin widow of Karṇikī on the Revā, unable to reach Kāśī in life, bids her elder son Suvāda immerse her bones in the Gaṅgā after death

title: The Keshin muni drinks the poison-cup with Rudra
description: the long-haired, wind-girdled ecstatic rides the winds and shares Rudra's poison-cup, the earliest proto-yogi image

title: The king gives his merit and empties the hell
description: Vipaścit asks Indra that all his lifelong good deeds be spent to deliver the sinners from torment; the damned are freed even as he at last mounts the chariot to heaven

title: The king's midnight flight and the queen's regency
description: Śikhidhvaja secretly abandons his throne for austerities on Mount Mandara; Cūḍālā, following by yogic flight, judges him unripe and rules the kingdom in his stead for eighteen years

title: The kingdom inside a dead brahmin's hut
description: Sarasvatī reveals that Padma is the projection of an unfulfilled kingship-wish of a dead village brahmin Vasiṣṭha, and that the whole realm exists within a corner of his death-hut, where decades pass in days

title: The kolam re-enacts the combat
description: annually in the theyyam season the possessed dancer fights Kathivanur Veeran's mock-battle, dies, and searches for his severed fingers before rising as the living god

title: The kṣaṇa-mukti exemplum
description: Khaṭvāṅga becomes the standing proof that the quantum of remaining time is irrelevant to salvation, dramatising the Gītā's teaching that whoever remembers the Lord at death attains Him

title: The Kumaras barred at Vaikuntha's gate
description: Visnu's doorkeepers Jaya and Vijaya block the four child-sage Kumaras from the seventh gate of Vaikuntha, the seed-offence of the avatara-cycle

title: The Kumbh of the South
description: the twelve-yearly Mahāmaham bath fires when Jupiter enters Siṃha and the Sun enters Kumbha on Māśi-Magha full moon, an amṛta-pot festival paralleling the northern Kumbh Mela

title: The ladder of ever-older witnesses
description: the owl Prāvārakarṇa passes the king to the crane Nāḍījaṅgha, who passes him to the tortoise Akūpāra, each too young to remember and naming an elder

title: The leprous boy as teacher
description: at Bahūdaka a seven-year-old wracked with leprosy consoles the despairing merchant, teaching mastery of attachment and the difference between bodily affliction and mental suffering

title: The lesson of Mahāmāyā
description: Viṣṇu declares that the whole lived lifetime was the Goddess's Mahāmāyā, the power Nārada asked to see — provable only by being suffered and woken from, showing even the gods are bound by illusion

title: The look-back roots the Witness-Gopāla
description: nearing Vidyānagara the brāhmaṇa turns to point out the Deity and looks back, whereupon Gopāla halts, becomes fixed at the spot, and speaks to confirm the marriage-vow before the assembly

title: The Lubdhaka saved from Yama
description: at the hunter's death Yama's noose-bearing messengers are barred and repelled by Śiva's gaṇas, who bear the Śivarātri-purified sinner to Śiva's world

title: The lullaby and the raising of Alarka
description: restored to earth, Madālasā sings non-dual Vedānta to her infants so Vikrānta, Subāhu and Śatrumardana renounce, while the fourth son Alarka is reared for kingship with a ring of secret counsel

title: The Madanikā marriage test
description: Claiming Durvāsas cursed him to become a woman each night, Kumbha becomes Madanikā and weds the king, who accepts with perfect equanimity — ascetic friends by day, spouses by night

title: The maker crippled by his patron — a charter of the artisan's grievance
description: the Kalkuḍa–Kallurṭi paddana enshrines the recurring protest of the wronged craftsman, telescoping the Kārkaḷa (1432) and Vēṇūr (1604) statue-events into one biography of genius punished for its excellence

title: The Man-Lion recension
description: the Nṛsiṃha Purāṇa retells Yama's order to shun Viṣṇu's and Narasiṃha's devotees, adding that souls in the narakas are eased of torment on hearing Hari's names

title: The marks the noose cannot bind
description: Yama lists for his servant the signs of the true devotee (even-minded, harmless, truthful, fixed on Kṛṣṇa) whom the pāśa must pass by

title: The marriage upheld and the shrine raised
description: the assembly, awed by the speaking Deity, enforces the promise; the marriage is performed and a temple built over the spot, the Deity taking the name Sākṣi-Gopāla, 'Gopāla the Witness'

title: The Mātaṅga slaying at Tuljapur
description: at the appeal of Brahmā and the gods the goddess destroys the demon Mātaṅga, a second demon-cycle attached to the Tuljapur seat

title: The metres fetch Soma from heaven
description: the metres led by Gāyatrī fly to the far heaven for the Soma, framing the Vāc-purchase in the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurvedic account

title: The mind-journey through cid-ākāśa
description: Līlā and Sarasvatī abandon their bodies in trance and travel through the space of pure consciousness to the brahmin's cottage, where Vasiṣṭha and Arundhatī lie dead with Līlā's whole empire dreaming inside the room

title: The mouse that lit the lamp
description: nibbling at a dying temple lamp's ghee in Kārttika, a mouse drags the wick and rekindles the flame, and is freed from its animal birth by the accidental dīpa-sevā

title: The Nāga absent on the Sun's car
description: reaching the city Dharmāraṇya finds Padmanābha away on his monthly turn dragging the one-wheeled chariot of Vivasvat; the Nāga's wife honours the guest and is persuaded to send for her husband

title: The Navarātra-vidhi ordained
description: Vyāsa codifies the twice-yearly nine-night vrata of Caitra and Āśvina with ghaṭa-sthāpana, homa, and kumārī-pūjā of the nine named virgins, open to rich and poor alike

title: The need for a war-god against Taraka
description: The boon-protected asura Taraka, killable only by a son of Shiva, oppresses the devas, prompting the gods to engineer Parvati's tapas and marriage to the ascetic Shiva

title: The nine rivers converge at the Mahāmaham
description: once in twelve years the nava-nadī (Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī and the rest) descend in person into the tank to shed the sins deposited in them by pilgrims

title: The Niṣāda hunter's Śivarātri (Garuḍa parallel)
description: a Niṣāda hunter (Sundarasenaka in printed editions), out with his dog and catching nothing, keeps the fast and vigil unknowingly beside a liṅga and escapes Yama's realm

title: The objection of youth answered
description: challenged as too young to teach elders, Sārasvata declares fitness is measured by understanding and conduct, not grey hairs, age, wealth, or lineage

title: The ocean-of-milk boon
description: Śiva reveals himself and grants the boy the Kṣīra-sāgara itself, eternal youth, undying devotion, and his abiding presence near the hermitage
source: Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva XIV; Śiva Purāṇa, Śatarudra-saṃhitā 32

title: The old brahmin's consolation
description: Viṣṇu appears as an aged brahmin beside the grieving woman, teaching that kinship itself is Māyā's knot, and bids her bathe again to make the funeral offering

title: The origin of the 'oldest animals' motif
description: the parable establishes the Sanskrit archetype of a quest passed up a chain of ever-older creatures to the eldest, the world-bearing tortoise Akūpāra

title: The outcaste woman's inadvertent worship wins Śivaloka
description: at a Śivarātri festival dropped bilva-leaves fall on the Mahābala liṅga and the blind Cāṇḍālī unknowingly keeps night-vigil, whereupon Mahābala instantly carries her to Śiva's abode

title: The owl–dove war ended at Yama-tīrtha
description: A terrible war between owl and dove hosts, propitiating Agni and Yama respectively, is ended only when all worship the Gautamī

title: The pañcagavya purification
description: the five cow-products — milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung, mixed with kuśa-water as brahma-kūrca — are drunk as an internal cleanser central to the sāntapana penance and re-admission after defilement

title: The Panchagni Vidya and the two after-death paths
description: The 'doctrine of the five fires' sets out the devayana (path of light, no return) and pitryana (path of smoke, returning via the moon) by which the soul travels at death sorted by knowledge and conduct

title: The Panjurli–Guliga double-nēma
description: the just, forgiving boar-daiva and the fierce blood-taking watcher are worshipped as one complementary pair, Panjurli passing judgement and Guliga enforcing it

title: The parrot's seventy-night vigil
description: a household parrot, entrusted with a merchant's lonely wife, holds her back from adultery by telling one cliff-hanger tale each night for seventy nights until her husband returns

title: The parrot's stratagem of indirection
description: the parrot grants the legitimacy of desire but breaks each tale off at its crisis, asking whether Prabhāvatī has the wit to escape as its heroine did, so that waiting for the ending saves the night

title: The pativratā who out-gives a pativratā
description: the Mārkaṇḍeya charter-myth resolves one faithful wife's world-freezing vow not by breaking her but through a second faithful wife, Anasūyā, whose compassion earns the Datta boon

title: The peacock bathed at the aśvamedha
description: at the avabhṛtha ablutions of the Kāśī king's horse-sacrifice Śaibyā bathes her peacock and reminds him of all his births; he resigns the body and is reborn a man of distinction

title: The peerless paṇḍit returns home
description: Satyavrata becomes a poet and scholar without rival, recites the Satyavrata mantram, and is welcomed back with honour by his estranged father Devadatta

title: The penance of Triśiras
description: a three-headed asura performs severe tapas to Śiva on the rock and wins his boon, giving the town the etymology Trisirapuram → Tiruchirāppaḷḷi (a Śaiva penitent, not the Rāmāyaṇa Triśiras)

title: The plural Avvaiyār tradition
description: The title Avvaiyār ('venerable matron') was borne by at least three or four distinct Tamil women poets across the Sangam, Chola, and later eras, later fused into one venerated poet-saint

title: The Prājāpatya krīcchra
description: the standard arduous penance: twelve days of graded fasting — three mornings-only, three evenings-only, three days of unsolicited food, three of total fast

title: The Puṇyaka rite taught by Umā
