description: the vow's mythic charter: Umā (Pārvatī) first laid down the Puṇyaka regulations to an assembly of celestial ladies, Arundhatī and the rest, in ages past

title: The reciprocal curses — Nārada's monkey face
description: the wronged Parvata curses Nārada's beautiful face to become an ape's, and Nārada counter-curses Parvata never to reach heaven

title: The recognition-verse — 'seven hunters among the Daśārṇas…'
description: the reborn birds/brahmins recite a mnemonic gāthā naming every rung of the ladder, and whoever hears it swoons under the flood of recollection — a stanza later quoted across vairāgya literature

title: The rival Janaka cousins
description: of the Videha line Keśidhvaja masters Self-knowledge (ātma-jñāna) and Khāṇḍikya the science of works (karma), and Keśidhvaja conquers his cousin and drives him into forest exile

title: The rival origins of the discus
description: competing traditions derive the Sudarśana instead from Viśvakarmā's forging of Sūrya's pared radiance, from Viṣṇu's seizure of it from Hayagrīva, or as his eternal attribute — sectarian claims held side by side

title: The river feeds her son fish
description: Sarasvatī stays Sārasvata from fleeing and sustains him on fish through the drought, so he alone keeps his Vedic study and offerings unbroken

title: The rudrākṣa-wearing monkey and cock reborn as princes
description: Mahānandā's pet monkey and rooster, adorned with rudrākṣa, are reborn as Prince Sudharmā and the minister's son Tāraka, retaining their craving for the bead — the rudrākṣa's potency even for animals

title: The Ṣaḍgarbha curse-chain
description: the recurring pattern of fallen divinities passing through successive asura births until a curse is spent and the soul is redeemed, cataloged across Bhāgavata, Harivaṃśa and Devī-Bhāgavata with variant demon fathers (Hiraṇyakaśipu vs Kālanemi)

title: The Sapta-Vitaṅka distribution
description: Muchukunda enshrines the seven Vitaṅka images across the Kāverī delta (Tiruvārūr, Tirunallāṟu, Nāgapaṭṭinam, Tirukkāraiyil, Tirukkuvaḷai, Tiruvaimūr, Vedāraṇyam), each with its own dance of the Tyāgarāja bronze

title: The Saptarṣi tell Himavān of Padmā
description: to overcome Himavān's fear of marrying young Pārvatī to the aged, fearsome ascetic Śiva, Vasiṣṭha and the seven sages narrate the exemplum of the faithful wife Padmā

title: The Satī–Rāma chronological knot and its cyclic resolution
description: Tradition harmonizes primordial Satī meeting Tretā-Yuga Rāma by holding that Rāma's līlā recurs in every cycle, as witnessed by the immortal Kākabhuśuṇḍi

title: The Sautrāmaṇī charter
description: the beheading and cure become the aetiology of the Sautrāmaṇī surā-offering to Indra Sutrāman with the Aśvins and Sarasvatī, the rare Vedic sanction of the intoxicant

title: The self-emptying dāna-king archetype
description: Rantideva stands with Śibi as the paired exemplar of the king who gives away everything and is tested by gods in disguise, a compassion-over-mokṣa ideal quoted across Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain gift-literature

title: The self-revelation of Poṭṭan Daivam
description: after out-reasoning the master of scripture, Śiva sheds the disguise; the ācārya bows and the untouchable's body becomes the throne of god

title: The serpent Arbuda saves Nandin
description: The nāga Arbuda raises his hood to bear Śiva's falling bull Nandin out of an earth-chasm, and the hill is named Arbuda-giri after him
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa (Arbuda-khaṇḍa); Arbuda sthala tradition

title: The seven students eat their teacher's cow
description: during a famine seven brahmin disciples of the sage Garga slaughter the milch-cow they were set to guard, incurring go-hatyā and betrayal of trust

title: The seventieth night and the parrot's plea
description: on the seventieth night Madana returns with the sin never consummated, Prabhāvatī confesses, and the parrot's last tale intercedes for her forgiveness

title: The severed head cries 'friend-betrayer'
description: Namuci's foam-severed head rolls after Indra reproaching him as mitra-ghna (friend-slayer) for breaking the sworn oath

title: The she-ass reveals Mātaṅga's birth
description: as Mātaṅga whips an ass-colt on the road to a sacrifice, the mother she-ass consoles her calf by disclosing that the driver is no Brāhmaṇa but Caṇḍāla-born, begotten on a Brāhmaṇa woman by a low-caste man

title: The showcase of bīja-mantra power
description: the DBP holds Satyavrata's transformation up as proof that the Goddess's seed-syllable works by its own sound-power even when uttered in ignorance, the Śākta twin of Ajāmila's saving Name

title: The signs of unexpiated sin
description: Manu teaches that sin not discharged surfaces in the next birth as disease or deformity: the brahmin-killer consumptive, the drinker black-toothed, the gold-thief with diseased nails — the explicit weld of prāyaścitta to karma

title: The Śiva-kavaca armours Bhadrāyu
description: wearing the unfailing armour-hymn and wielding a divine sword and conch, Bhadrāyu single-handedly routs the Magadha army, rescues Vajrabāhu, and weds Kīrtimālinī, daughter of Candrāṅgada and Sīmantinī

title: The sixfold chain of narrators
description: the epic wraps the tale in a deep transmission — Cyavana to Janaka to Nārada to Indra to the brāhmaṇas to Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira — staging uñchavṛtti as settled, handed-down doctrine

title: The sixth-night destiny-writing
description: Ṣaṣṭhī (with Vidhātā) visits the birth-chamber on the sixth night to write the infant's fate on its forehead, the rationale of the sūtikā-ṣaṣṭhī rite

title: The sky-born horse Kuvalaya
description: as the Dānava wrecks sage Gālava's sacrifice in beast-shapes, a tireless heaven-sent steed descends and King Śatrujit's son Ṛtadhvaja mounts it, taking the name Kuvalayāśva

title: The slaying of Durgama
description: Durgama attacks to reclaim the Vedas; the Goddess emits an army of Śaktis, fells him with her bow, and absorbs his tejas — and because she slew Durgama she is famed as Durgā

title: The slaying of Mātaṅga
description: appealed to by Brahmā and the devas, Tuljā Bhavānī destroys the demon Mātaṅga who oppressed gods and sages, a second demon-cycle fixed to the seat

title: The slaying of Mura and the origin of Ekādaśī
description: a śakti born of Viṣṇu's body slays the demon Mura and becomes the goddess of the Ekādaśī fast, founding the year-round vrata cycle

title: The Solah Somvār dice-game curse
description: Pārvatī beats Śiva at dice, curses the temple priest with leprosy for a partial lie, and apsaras teach him the sixteen-Monday vrata that cures him and chains onward through Pārvatī, Kārttikeya and a brahmin-turned-king

title: The somakrayaṇa and the beaten Soma-seller
description: the gods' recovery of the price becomes the ritual buying of King Soma with the tawny cow, followed by reclaiming goods and driving off the Soma-seller

title: The son who is the father
description: the boy-Bhairava, though called a son, is Śiva himself in juvenile shape — the guardian the god emanates when protection is needed, not a separate deity

title: The sparing at dawn and Śiva's grace
description: the whole deer family returns true to its word, each offering to die first; the hunter, purified by the unwitting vrata, spares them all and both hunter and deer receive Śiva's grace

title: The speaking goat halts its own sacrifice
description: a goat about to be immolated reveals it was a brahmin cursed by Caṇḍikā and recounts how Gītā chapter 9 once shielded King Candraśarman from the demons Pāpa and Nindā

title: The Sthāṇu-Māl-Ayaṉ liṅga
description: a single self-manifest liṅga worshipped at once as Śiva (Sthāṇu), Viṣṇu (Māl) and Brahmā (Ayaṉ), making Suchindram a rare joint Hari–Hara–Ayaṉ shrine

title: The stotra recited against Saturn's afflictions
description: the Daśaratha Śani-stotra becomes a pan-Indian remedial hymn chanted on Saturdays, on Śani Jayantī, and during sāḍe-sātī at shrines like Tirunallar and Śani Śiṅgṇāpur

title: The sudden cool wind in Naraka
description: after a hundred years of torment a fragrant cool breeze unaccountably eases every condemned soul, the unexplained prelude to a righteous king's arrival

title: The svayambhu ice-liṅga forms
description: A self-manifest column of ice venerated as Śiva's liṅga forms in the Amarnāth cave and waxes/wanes with the moon
source: Amareśvara sthala-māhātmya; living Amarnāth Yātrā tradition

title: The svayambhū liṅga of the Rock Fort
description: the maternal Lord is worshipped as a self-manifest liṅga on the living Archaean granite, with the consort Mattuvār Kuḻali (Sugandha Kuntaḷāmbikā) in her own shrine

title: The svayambhū Vināyaka refuses to be moved
description: the villagers cannot bale the well dry nor lift the self-manifest Gaṇeśa image, the spring endlessly refilling, so the god fixes himself in situ submerged in his own sanctum-water

title: The tapo-bhaṅga pattern (penance broken by an apsaras)
description: Māṇḍakarṇi joins the recurring type in which the gods send celestial nymphs to dissolve a threatening mortal austerity, kin to Viśvāmitra–Menakā and Ṛśyaśṛṅga

title: The teacher's fee refused
description: returning to discharge the debt of instruction, Keśidhvaja offers any prize, and Khāṇḍikya's counsellors demand the kingdom back, but he declines empire as transient

title: The ten sons of Indu become ten Brahmās
description: Ten brahmin brothers resolve in meditation "I am Brahmā" and each becomes a world-creating Brahmā, ten complete cosmoses arising from ten sustained convictions

title: The terrestrial Vaitaraṇī at Viraja-kṣetra (Jajpur)
description: The earthly Baitaraṇī/Vaitaraṇī river of Odisha, flowing past Jajpur (Viraja-kṣetra), is sanctified as a holy ford whose very name doubles the underworld death-river
source: Mahābhārata Tīrtha-yātrā Parva; Padma & Skanda Purāṇa māhātmyas; regional gazetteers

title: The thoṭṭam song draws the god into the dancer
description: across the 400-plus open-ended theyyam pantheon of North Malabar, the sung thoṭṭam narrates each deity's birth and deeds and, with the placing of the mudi headdress, marks the god entering the possessed Dalit performer who is then venerated as the living deity across caste lines

title: The thousand lotuses for the thousand names
description: Viṣṇu recites Śiva's thousand names and lays down one lotus from the Mānasa lake for each, a perfect thousand-and-thousand pūjā

title: The Three Dogs of Dharma
description: the Ayodhyā petitioner-dog is distinguished from Yudhiṣṭhira's faithful hound (Dharma/Yama in disguise) and from Yama's four-eyed hounds Śarvara and Śyāma, three separate dog-motifs kept apart

title: The tiger and the sacrificial cow
description: during Keśidhvaja's rite to conquer death a tiger kills the milch-cow whose milk the offering requires, defiling and halting the sacrifice

title: The tiger test of Bhadrāyu
description: Śiva and Pārvatī, disguised as a tiger, its Brahmin victim, and an aged suppliant, demand Bhadrāyu's queen and then his life; when he surrenders both they reveal themselves and grant Śiva-sāyujya to him, Kīrtimālinī, and their parents

title: The traveller and the tiger
description: an old tiger feigns piety and dangles a gold bracelet to lure a greedy traveller into quicksand, where he is devoured — greed blinds prudence

title: The trifling sin revealed
description: Yama's officer tells Vipaścit his chariot to heaven waits, and that he burns here only for one lapse: neglecting his wife Pīvarī's fertile season out of infatuation with Kaikeyī

title: The twelve devāsura saṅgrāmas enumerated
description: The Matsya Purāṇa counts the twelve primordial god-demon wars as a fixed roster, from Nārasiṃha to Kolāhala

title: The twelve-year drought scatters the ṛṣis
description: a dvādaśa-vārṣikī famine drives the starving sages from their hermitages and the Vedas are forgotten from human memory

title: The twelve-year skull vow (mahāvrata)
description: the brahmin-killer's expiation: twelve years in a forest hut on alms, bearing the slain man's skull as a banner and proclaiming the deed, or dying for a brāhmaṇa in battle

title: The two apsaras turned to badarī trees
description: celestial girls who broke Satyatapas' penance and were cursed to treehood are freed when the saint Bharata recalls Gītā chapter 4

title: The two daily twilights born
description: Sandhyā casts her body into Medhātithi's Jyotiṣṭoma fire; the Sun splits it into Prātaḥ-sandhyā (dawn, for the gods) and Sāyaṃ-sandhyā (dusk, for the ancestors), the origin of sandhyā-vandana

title: The two effulgences merge
description: the Nāga's most astonishing sight: a radiant Being of equal splendour approaches Sūrya and their two energies fuse so wholly that none can tell which was which

title: The two Līlās meet, one liberated
description: the first and second Līlās are revealed as one consciousness in two projected forms; knowing every world to be mind, Līlā lives on liberated beside the revived Padma, free of her original fear

title: The two Śaṅkhacūḍas kept apart
description: the corpus distinguishes the minor Vraja Yakṣa slain by Kṛṣṇa's fist from the cosmic daitya Śaṅkhacūḍa of the Tulasī cycle, sharing only the name 'conch-crest'

title: The two-serpent icon of Kavlem
description: Śāntā-Durgā is enshrined holding a nāga in each hand, the two serpents read as Viṣṇu and Śiva whom she grasps and holds apart as mediatrix

title: The unteachable Utathya
description: born as Utathya, the cursed brahmin cannot learn a word in twelve years, fails even the daily sandhyā rites, and becomes the laughing-stock of his village

title: The Vedas restored
description: with Durgama dead the Goddess recovers the four Vedas and returns them to Brahmā and the Brāhmaṇas, re-establishing yajña, rain and dharma

title: The voice from the corpse
description: as Bhadrā laments over his body an incorporeal voice — the dead king's own generative will — grants her a boon, bidding her lie beside the corpse on the eighth or fourteenth lunar night

title: The Void corrected, Hemacūḍa awakens
description: reaching a blank thought-free absorption he mistakes for the goal, Hemacūḍa is corrected by Hemalekhā — the knower of the void remains — and realizes the Self as ever-present awareness, becoming a jīvanmukta while still a prince

title: The vow of Nārada and Parvata
description: the sky-roaming Devarṣi Nārada and his nephew Parvata wander bound by a compact of total disclosure, concealing no thought from each other, and lodge with King Sṛñjaya

title: The Vṛddhakanyā-tīrtha benediction
description: regaining youth for the wedding night, the maiden at dawn grants that one night at her ford equals fifty-eight years' brahmacarya, then casts off her body and ascends to heaven

title: The Vṛndāvana promise before Gopāla
description: an old brāhmaṇa, moved by a poor youth's faithful pilgrimage-service, vows to give his daughter in marriage, swearing the pledge before the Gopāla Deity as witness

title: The war and the burning-ground
description: a battle between Tāladhvaja and a rival king slays all of Suśīlā's sons and grandsons, and she breaks down wailing over their pyres at the cremation ground

title: The war and Vidūratha's fall
description: a rival monarch invades Vidūratha's kingdom; watched unseen from the sky by Sarasvatī and the first Līlā, Vidūratha is mortally wounded and dies

title: The war of swans and peacocks
description: swan-king Hiraṇyagarbha of Karpūra-dvīpa and peacock-king Citravarṇa go to war, the vulture Dūradarśī counselling the six-fold policy of statecraft

title: The water-fairy guardian of Chandra Tāl
description: Spitian folklore sets a supernatural lake-guardian (a jal-parī or protective spirit) over the moon-lake, said to appear to and mislead travellers — a spirit-lore layer parallel to the Mahābhārata charter

title: The wet/dry, day/night compact
description: to recover his strength Indra swears a pact with Namuci to slay him "neither by day nor by night, neither with the wet nor with the dry"

title: The winning of Sūryā
description: in the charioteers' race the Aśvins win Sūryā, Daughter of the Sun, who mounts their car as bride — the Indic Sun-maiden myth behind the wedding hymn

title: The wonder of Sūrya
description: from his turns bearing the Sun's car Padmanābha recounts that all creatures flow from Sūrya, that ascetics and gods dwell in his rays, and that the Supreme Soul gazes on the worlds from within the solar disc

title: The wooden brothers ride to war
description: Jagannātha on a black horse and Balabhadra on a white ride out of the Purī sanctum as two soldiers ahead of the Gajapati army, the dark and fair images made mounted flesh

title: The wooden Lord's hand reaches out
description: before the temple's eyes the carved Jagannātha image stretches out its arm and takes the untouchable Dāsiā's coconut directly, refusing what the high-caste bearer would have offered

title: Thee Chāmuṇḍi, the goddess who sits in fire
description: the fierce Chāmuṇḍi fire-goddess of the North-Malabar kāvus is worshipped through the theyyam's ember-ordeal, her thoṭṭam and rite placing her among the amma-theyyams of the Kerala Bhadrakālī sphere

title: Tirukkaḍavūr — the conquest of Death
description: the Amṛtaghaṭeśvarar shrine where Śiva as Kālāntaka bursts from the liṅga to kick down Yama and grant the boy Mārkaṇḍeya deathless youth; seat of the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya

title: Tirukkōvilūr — the slaying of Andhaka
description: the feat-shrine on the Teṉ Peṇṇai where Śiva impales the blind demon Andhaka on his trident while the Mātṛkās drink his cloning blood

title: Tiruvatikai — the burning of Tripura
description: the shrine localising Śiva as Tripurāntaka, who incinerated the three flying asura cities with a single arrow; also where Appar reconverted to Śaivism

title: Tiruvirkuḍi — the slaying of Jalandhara
description: the shrine marking Śiva's decapitation of the asura Jalandhara with the razor-edge of his cakra after Vṛndā's vow is broken

title: Tripurā as the self-aware Absolute (Cit-Śakti)
description: Dattātreya expounds the Goddess Tripurā, who transcends the three states, bodies, worlds, and guṇas, as self-luminous consciousness whose self-knowing throb (vimarśa) projects and reabsorbs the cosmos

title: Tripurantaka burns the three flying cities (Kartik Purnima charter)
description: Shiva as Tripurantaka destroys the three flying cities (Tripura) of the asuras with a single arrow of the Pinaka bow, commemorated on Kartik Shukla Purnima as Tripurari/Tripuri Purnima

title: Trita slays the three-headed Triśiras
description: urged and aided by Indra, Trita Āptya smites Viśvarūpa Triśiras, the three-headed son of Tvaṣṭṛ, strikes off his heads, and drives out the penned cows

title: Tvaritā comes in haste
description: at the cry of the sage-widow Anubhūti, the Goddess descends *instantly* (tvarita) on the Yamunācalā hill, the etymology that names Tuḷjā and her town Tuljapur

title: Two brahmarṣis reduced to squabbling birds
description: the Śākta reading of the Āḍi-Baka war: if masters of tapas can be dragged into a ten-thousand-year animal war by ego, the guṇas of Prakṛti bind every embodied being

title: Two Khaṭvāṅgas disambiguated
description: the Ikṣvāku king who wins liberation in an hour is distinct from the khaṭvāṅga skull-staff, the bed-post club wielded by Śiva-Bhairava, Kālī and Kāpālika ascetics as conquerors of death

title: Two māyā-cow legends of Gautama
description: the same phantom-cow framing drives two incompatible endings: the Brahma Purāṇa's Godāvarī descent from Śiva's locks (no curse) versus the Devī-Bhāgavata's curse of Devī-aversion (no river)
source: Devī-Bhāgavata XII.8–9; cf. Brahma Purāṇa, Gautamī-māhātmya

title: Tyranny of Maṇi and Malla
description: The daitya brothers Maṇi and Malla ravage the sages of the Deccan forest, who appeal to Śiva for deliverance

title: Umā's annual homecoming (Āgomoni)
description: each autumn Umā/Gaurī returns from Kailāsa to her natal home of Himālaya and Menakā with Gaṇeśa, Kārtikeya, Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī for the pūjā days, departing at visarjan

title: Upamanyu denied milk — the childhood vow
description: Given flour paste in water instead of milk, the boy Upamanyu learns from his mother that milk flows only from Śiva's grace and resolves to win Śiva by austerity

title: Upamanyu's Pañcākṣara tapas
description: The boy withdraws to the Himālaya and performs ferocious penance with ceaseless japa of the five-syllable mantra Namaḥ Śivāya

title: Uṣas carries bad dreams to Trita
description: worshippers pray Dawn to bear away their nightmares and evil to Trita Āptya, the scapegoat-god who wears the bad dreams like ornaments on his limbs

title: Uttaṅka's daughter freed by Ṛṣi Pañcamī
description: a widowed daughter's worm-afflicted body is traced to a former birth's breach of rajasvalā rules and released by the Saptarṣi-honoring vrata

title: Vāc fashioned into a woman to buy Soma
description: lacking the Soma the Gandharvas guard, the gods shape Speech (Vāc) into a woman and send her as the buying-price, and she returns to them bringing the Soma

title: Vāc won back by the dance
description: the Taittirīya recension has the gods give Vāc to the Gandharvas and recover her by dance and song, so women are fond of the dancer and singer

title: Vāg-devatās compose the thousand names
description: at Lalitā's own command the eight goddesses of speech headed by Vaśinī compose and sing her secret thousand names before her throne in Śrīpura

title: Vaiṣṇavī's birth and vow
description: The Goddess takes form as the maiden Vaiṣṇavī, an aṃśa of the Tridevī, and vows lifelong virginity and tapas until merging with Viṣṇu at the age's end
source: Vaiṣṇo Devī sthala/folk legend; regional Trikūṭa-māhātmya

title: Vaḻuvūr — the flaying of Gajāsura
description: the feat-shrine of Gajasaṃhāra-mūrti, Śiva impaling and flaying the elephant-demon to wear its hide as Kṛttivāsas; home of the famed Cōḻa bronze

title: Vandana raised from the pit
description: the Aśvins draw the aged Vandana out of a pit into the light and restore his youth, like buried gold dug up and made to shine

title: Vanmīkanāthar, the anthill-liṅga
description: the beginningless swayambhū liṅga of Tiruvārūr manifests within an anthill (puṟṟu), named Puṟṟiḍaṅkoṇḍār by Appar

title: Variant: Viṣṇu rigs the rematch
description: in a parallel telling Śiva meets Viṣṇu, wins everything back, and Viṣṇu reveals his spirit had entered the dice — the game an illusion, the quarrel mere moha

title: Varuṇa demoted from Vedic sovereign to devotee
description: the archaic Ṛgvedic lord of ṛta and cosmic order appears in Purāṇic form as mere water-guardian bowing to Krishna, dramatizing the relativizing of the Vedic pantheon beneath the Supreme

title: Varuṇa's noose and the debt of énas
description: the earliest Hindu conception of sin: transgression (énas) against cosmic order (ṛta) is a debt (ṛṇa) owed to Varuṇa, who binds the guilty with his pāśa, and the penitent begs release incurred knowingly or unknowingly

title: Vasu proclaims the Gaṅgā-māhātmya to the restored Mohinī
description: After Brahmā restores Mohinī's body, the brāhmaṇa Vasu declares the Gaṅgā supreme among tīrthas — a mouthful of her water equal to a horse-sacrifice, sins fleeing the bather like a serpent's shed slough

title: Vasu wins eternal residence in Vṛndāvana
description: Mohinī's priest-guide reports to Brahmā, gains the boon of dwelling in Vṛndāvana, performs austerities over five thousand years until the Lord grants him Vraja forever, and hears from Nārada the deeds Kṛṣṇa will work on earth

title: Vaṭuka distinguished from Kāla-Bhairava
description: the youthful guardian-boy carries no brahmahatyā narrative, standing apart from the skull-bearing adult Kāla-Bhairava born of severing Brahmā's fifth head
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa, Kāśī Khaṇḍa

title: Vidala and Utpala's boon of immunity from man
description: the two Daitya brothers, granted by Brahmā that no man may slay them, defeat the gods, who petition Brahmā and are told the Goddess alone will kill them

title: Vikuṇḍala's merit-transfer debate with the Devadūta
description: two accidental Māgha baths in the Yamunā outweigh a wastrel's life, and Vikuṇḍala assigns their fruit to free his brother Śrīkuṇḍala from hell

title: Vīrabāhu's embassy to the asura court
description: Skanda sends Vīrabāhu, chief of the Nava-Vīrar, into Vīramahendrapuram with an ultimatum to free the devas — the Tamil parallel to Hanumān's Laṅkā-dūta

title: Vīravara's loyal sacrifice
description: the retainer Vīravara offers his consenting son Śaktidhara to goddess Caṇḍikā to save King Śūdraka's life, and the moved goddess restores the whole slain family

title: Vishnu appears to Nārada at Vishnuprayag
description: the sage's austerities at the Dhauligaṅgā–Alaknandā confluence are rewarded with Vishnu's darśana, naming the highest prayāga

title: Vishnu Gifts Ambarisha the Sudarshana
description: Pleased by the king-devotee Ambarisha's flawless total sensory devotion, Vishnu personally awards him the Sudarshana-cakra as a perpetual guardian

title: Vishnu instructs Garuda on death and the afterlife
description: Garuda asks Vishnu about the fate of the dead; Vishnu describes the thumb-sized soul's departure, seizure by Yamaduutas, and the year-long road to Yama-loka — the framing teaching of the Preta-khanda

title: Vishṇumūrti Theyyam avenges Palanthāyi Kaṇṇan
description: the Narasiṁha-theyyam wraps the Man-Lion's slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu around the local martyr Palanthāyi Kaṇṇan, a low-caste Viṣṇu-devotee murdered by the Kuruvāṭṭ landlord, whose house institutes the fire-theyyam to appease Viṣṇu's wrath

title: Viṣṇu accepts the curse for the worlds
description: rather than resisting, Viṣṇu willingly takes the curse upon himself, converting punishment into the theological mechanism of his descents

title: Viṣṇu beheads Kāvyamātā with the Sudarśana
description: to save the paralyzed Indra, Viṣṇu looses the discus and severs the head of Bhṛgu's wife, though she is a woman and a brāhmaṇa's spouse

title: Viṣṇu cursed to become the śālagrāma stone (Tulasī–Jālandhara legend)
description: Viṣṇu deceives the chaste Vṛndā to break asura Jālandhara's invincibility; she curses Viṣṇu to dwell as a black stone and becomes the Tulasī plant

title: Viṣṇu humbles Garuḍa's pride
description: when Garuḍa protests and boasts of bearing the worlds on one feather, Viṣṇu lays a single arm on him and crushes him to the ground, shattering his arrogance

title: Viṣṇu narrates the fate of the dead to Garuḍa
description: the trans-temporal frame-dialogue in which the trembling eagle asks how souls escape Yama's torments and receives the Preta-khaṇḍa's doctrine, chartered by this tale

title: Viṣṇu offers his own eye
description: reflecting that his eye is itself a lotus, Viṣṇu plucks it out and offers it as the thousandth flower, the charter of his 'lotus-eyed' epithets (Kamala-nayana, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, Rājīva-locana)

title: Viṣṇu's deception and Divodāsa's mokṣa
description: Viṣṇu, arriving in heterodox mendicant guise with Lakṣmī and Garuḍa, reveals the king's sole flaw — excluding Śiva — whereupon Divodāsa installs the Divodāseśvara liṅga and attains liberation

title: Viṣṇu's discus defeated
description: Kṣupa wins Viṣṇu's aid; Viṣṇu, disguised as a brāhmaṇa, deploys the Sudarśana-cakra and his astras, but all are turned back by Dadhīca's Śiva-empowered blades of kuśa-grass

title: Viṣṇu's tapas at Kailāsa
description: pressed by invincible daityas, Viṣṇu digs a fire-pit on Kailāsa and undertakes penance to propitiate Śiva for a weapon

title: Viśpalā's iron leg
description: after she loses her leg in the night-battle of Khela, the Aśvins fit the warrior-woman Viśpalā with an iron leg so she can run again at dawn

title: Viśvāmitra's penance broken by Menakā; birth of Śakuntalā
description: Indra sends Menakā to break Viśvāmitra's tapas; their daughter Śakuntalā is abandoned, sheltered by śakunta birds, and raised by Kaṇva

title: Vṛddhagautama and his aged bride renewed
description: The noseless son of Gautama, made handsome and learned by an old woman's banked boons, bathes with her in the Gautamī and she rises young

title: Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira with the Sixteen Kings
description: After Abhimanyu's death, Vyasa recites the deaths of sixteen mighty kings to console the grieving Yudhishthira and teach that grief is vain

title: Vyāsa dictates the Mahābhārata to Gaṇeśa as scribe
description: Vyāsa dictates the epic and Gaṇeśa agrees to write it on condition he never pause; Vyāsa composes knotty kūṭa-ślokas to buy time, and when Gaṇeśa's stylus breaks he snaps off his own tusk to continue, explaining his one-tusked iconography

title: Vāyu Purāṇa — four-pāda structure and Brahmāṇḍa twinning
description: One of the oldest Mahāpurāṇas, narrated by Vāyu, organised in Prakriyā/Anuṣaṅga/Upodghāta/Upasaṃhāra pādas and anciently one corpus with the Brahmāṇḍa

title: Vyuṣitāśva dies of excess
description: the righteous Puru king, conqueror of all directions by the Aśvamedha, is undone by conjugal excess and dies childless of phthisis, leaving his queen Bhadrā a sonless widow

title: Why women love song and dance
description: Vāc turns from the reciters to the singers, and thus "women are given to vanity" and favour the man who dances and sings

title: Yadugiri as a Kṛta-Yuga abode of Nārāyaṇa
description: The kṣetra-māhātmya charters Yādavādri/Yadugiri as an ancient self-chosen seat of Nārāyaṇa worshipped across all four Yugas

title: Agastya weds Kāverī and holds her in his kamaṇḍalu
description: Agastya marries Kāverī and carries her, transformed into water, within his water-pot across the parched Deccan

title: Airāvata tramples the garland and Durvāsas curses the devas
description: Irritated by the bees, Airāvata flings the garland down and tramples it; the enraged Durvāsas curses Indra and the devas to lose their śrī, becoming subject to decay and defeat

title: Ajamila Cries 'Narayana' at Death
description: Dying at eighty-eight with his mind on his youngest son Narayana, the terrified Ajamila cries out the name, pronouncing the very name of the Supreme Lord

title: Alekhya enumerated among the 64 kalas
description: Painting (alekhya) is fixed as the 5th of Vatsyayana's sixty-four arts, establishing the classical text-anchor for the whole devotional-painting family

title: Ambarisha's Ekadashi Vow and the Paarana Dilemma
description: Ambarisha completes a year-long Ekadashi-Dvadashi vow but, with Durvasa lingering past the Dvadashi window, resolves the dharma-conflict by drinking only water

title: Amrita-varsha — the moon drips nectar onto the kheer
description: On this one night the full moon's rays carry amrita; rice-kheer left under the moonbeams becomes cooling, medicinal prasada, linked to the moon's churning-born soma
actors: Candra/Soma (the moon); devotees; substrate: gods of the Samudra Manthana
source: Folk amrita-moon / kheer tradition; Samudra Manthana and Chandra/Soma Puranic substrate; Ayurvedic ritu logic

title: Amrta Drop Falls at Ujjain on the Kshipra
description: In the samudra-manthana etiology, a drop of amrta from the kumbha fell at Ujjain, sanctifying the Kshipra river and grounding the Simhastha Kumbh bathing

title: Anatomical census of the body
description: The text enumerates the body's parts — 360 bones, joints, sinews, hairs, fluid-measures, the three doṣas, seven dhātus, six tastes and the vital airs
source: Garbha Upaniṣad 1; cf. Caraka- and Suśruta-Saṃhitā

title: Annakūṭa / Govardhana Pūjā instituted
description: Cowherds' offering to Govardhana becomes the Annakūṭa festival, the chief annual utsava re-enacted before Śrīnāthajī

title: Apālā's Soma offering and triple purification by Indra
description: Apālā presses Soma with her teeth for Indra, who draws her through the chariot/cart/yoke holes to purify her skin and grants fertility boons to her father's head, his field, and her body

title: Aśvins give Dadhyañc a horse's head and learn the honey-doctrine
description: The Aśvins remove Dadhyañc's head for safekeeping, fix a horse's head on him through which he teaches them the Madhu-vidyā, then restore his own head after Indra strikes off the horse-head

title: Bharata-Bharadvaja (Vitatha) dynastic transfer
description: The childless emperor Bharata is given Bharadvaja (called Vitatha) by the gods to continue the Lunar/Bharata line

title: Bhaṇḍāsura's penance and boon
description: Tutored by the asura-guru Śukra, Bhaṇḍa wins from Śiva the boon that half of any foe's strength passes to him, making him near-invincible

title: Birajā Devī and the navel Śakti Pīṭha
description: Jajpur is the Śakti Pīṭha where Satī's navel fell, presided over by Birajā/Girijā Devī with Bhairava Jagannātha/Varāha, binding goddess-pīṭha to the pitṛ-river

title: Birth of Durgā from combined tejas
description: The gods, ousted by Mahiṣāsura, emit their radiant tejas which coalesces into the eighteen-armed warrior Goddess Durgā, each god arming her with his weapon

title: Birth of Gaṇeśa from Lalitā's glance (Śākta version)
description: When Viśukra plants the Vighna-yantra to paralyse Lalitā's army, the goddess glances at Kāmeśvara and Mahā-Gaṇapati is born, shattering the obstruction

title: Birth of the female Tīrthaṅkara Mallinātha (Mallī)
description: Per the Śvetāmbara account, the 19th Tīrthaṅkara Mallinātha is born female (Mallī) owing to a karmic residue of deceit in a past life and attains liberation as a woman; the Digambara tradition denies this, holding the figure male because (on its premises) a woman cannot attain mokṣa

title: Birth of the goddess-daughters and Merakhiyā
description: Several divine daughters including Janbāī (future Khodiyār) and a son Merakhiyā are born and recognized as Cāraṇ āīs

title: Birth of Urvashī from Nara-Nārāyaṇa's thigh
description: Urvashī is born from the thigh of the sage Nara-Nārāyaṇa at Badarī, created to humble the apsarās Indra had sent to disturb his penance

title: Brahmā and the origin-of-painting floor-drawing legend
description: Brahmā bids a grieving father draw his dead son's likeness on the ground so He can restore his life, mythologized as the origin of painting and floor-art

title: Brahmā appears as the swan (haṃsa)
description: The creator Brahmā takes the form of a haṃsa (swan/goose) to answer the Sādhyas, embodying the paramahaṃsa ideal of the discriminating sage

title: Brahmā reveals the Name of Nārāyaṇa as the secret of all Vedas
description: Brahmā answers that the deliverance from Kali is the secret hidden in all the Vedas: uttering the name of the original Person, Nārāyaṇa

title: Brahmā's Aśvamedha at Satyavrata-kṣetra
description: Brahmā performs the great aśvamedha at Kāñcī; when the river Vegavati rises to wash it away, Viṣṇu lies across the flood to stop it and rises as Varadarāja from the yajña-fire to dwell forever

title: Bull-form dive at Guptakāśī
description: Śiva takes the bull (vṛṣabha) form at Guptakāśī; Bhīma seizes him, and the bull-Śiva dives into the earth refusing capture

title: Candra favours Rohini and neglects the others
description: Candra becomes enamoured of Rohini and lingers with her, neglecting his other twenty-six wives, who appeal to their father Daksha

title: Chain of divine worshippers of the mūla-mūrti
description: The Celuvanārāyaṇa image is said to have been worshipped successively by Brahmā, Sanatkumāra, Rāma (Tretā) and Kṛṣṇa (Dvāpara) before being lost

title: Collapse of Cosmic Order by Gayāsura's Holiness
description: Because everyone who sees Gayāsura attains liberation regardless of karma, Yama's hells empty and the order of reward-and-punishment collapses, prompting the devas under Brahmā to act

title: Cosmic egg and Adi-Sāṅkhya cosmogony
description: From the unmanifest Pradhāna arise mahat, ahaṃkāra, the tanmātras and elements, condensing into the golden brahmāṇḍa within which Brahmā fashions the worlds

title: Curse-origin of the four learned birds
description: Four brahmana sons (grandsons of Vipulasva) are cursed by their father to be reborn as birds yet retain Vedic knowledge, becoming enlightened expounders in the Vindhyas

title: Dakṣa's Curse on Chandra (the Moon)
description: Chandra marries Daksha's daughters but dotes only on Rohini; the slighted wives complain and Daksha curses the Moon to wane, until Chandra worships Shiva at Thingalur and regains his light

title: Dattātreya's eternal tapas on the Girnar summit
description: The deathless avadhūta Dattātreya performs and abides in eternal tapas on the highest peak, leaving his worshipped footprints (Datta Pādukā)

title: Declaration of ātman–Brahman identity (Chapter 1)
description: The opening chapter pours out the conviction of all-pervading non-duality, framing grace itself as impelling the realization that ātman is Brahman

title: Devas and Asuras contend over the Udgītha
description: Gods and demons contend; the gods meditate on each sense-faculty as Udgītha but each is pierced with evil until the vital breath (mukhya prāṇa) shatters the demons like a clod on rock

title: Dev Deepawali — the gods descend to bathe at Kashi
description: On Kartik Purnima the gods are said to descend to the Ganga ghats of Varanasi, celebrated as the gods' own Diwali with myriad lamps

title: Durvāsā's garland and the curse of lost śrī (Samudra-manthana frame)
description: Durvāsā gifts Indra a śrī-bearing garland which Airāvata tramples; the slighted sage curses the Devas to lose all fortune and vigor, driving the weakened gods to undertake the churning of the ocean for amṛta
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9 (Santānaka garland variant); absent in Mahābhārata Ādi Parva Amṛta-manthana

title: Duṣyanta weds Śakuntalā by gāndharva rite
description: King Duṣyanta meets Śakuntalā at Kaṇva's hermitage and marries her by gāndharva rite on the condition their son be heir

title: Fire-birth of Mīnākṣī
description: A three-breasted girl, Pārvatī incarnate, rises from the sacrificial fire-pit of childless Pāṇḍya Malayadhvaja and queen Kāñcanamālai

title: Ganesha Slays Sindhurasura at Morgaon
description: Riding his peacock vahana as Mayureshvara, Ganesha slays the asura Sindhura whose head falls at Morgaon (peacock-village), the chief Ashtavinayaka shrine

title: Goddess Ekādaśī born as śakti to destroy Mura
description: In the Padma Purāṇa Ekādaśī-māhātmya tradition, the demon Mura arises from Viṣṇu's body during his cosmic sleep; the personified goddess Ekādaśī is born as the śakti who destroys Mura while protecting the sleeping god — the etiological basis of the Ekādaśī fast. A distinct, non-Kṛṣṇa Mura harmonized with the Bhāgavata figure by the shared name

title: Hara-Sapa-Vimochana Frees Shiva of the Brahma-Slaying Curse
description: At Tirukkandiyur, Vishnu as Hara-Sapa-Vimochana Perumal frees Shiva from the curse of Brahma-slaying (brahma-hatya)

title: Identity of Śiva, Self, and Brahman declared
description: Ṛbhu collapses the Śaiva Śiva, Vedāntic Brahman, and innermost Ātman into one undivided awareness, dissolving sectarian Śaivism into pure non-dual jñāna

title: Idumban and the origin of the kavadi
description: Sage Agastya sends his disciple Idumban to carry the hills Sivagiri and Saktigiri south on a shoulder-pole; at Palani the boy-Murugan (Dandayudhapani) sits immovable on one hill and slays then revives Idumban, the shoulder-pole becoming the prototype kavadi and Idumban the guardian saluted first

title: Śilāda's penance for a deathless son
description: Childless sage Śilāda performs tapas to Śiva for an un-womb-born, immortal son

title: Indra breaks open the Vala cave
description: Aided by Sarama, the Angirasas and Brihaspati, Indra splits the Vala enclosure where the Panis hid the cosmic cows, driving out the cows, dawn and waters

title: Indra Splits Open Vala to Free the Cattle and Dawns
description: Indra breaks open the Vala cave to release the imprisoned cattle and dawns, a recurring Vedic myth of liberating light and order

title: Invention and bearing of the Mahatī vīṇā
description: Nārada becomes patron of saṅgīta and the seven svaras as wielder of the great vīṇā Mahatī, earning the epithet Mahatī-vīṇā-dhara

title: Śiva and Pārvatī follow their son and manifest as Mallikārjuna
description: Grieving the absent Kumāra, Śiva and Pārvatī follow him to Śrīśaila and abide there as the self-manifest liṅga named Mallikā (Pārvatī/jasmine) + Arjuna (Śiva)
source: Skanda Purāṇa (Śrīśaila-khaṇḍa); Śiva Purāṇa; Dvādaśa Jyotirliṅga Stotra

title: Śiva descends as Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava
description: Śiva manifests as a fierce mounted solar-warrior form (Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava) and rides to Jejuri/Mailāra to confront the demons

title: Śiva manifests as the youthful south-facing Guru
description: Śiva appears beneath a banyan as a radiant sixteen-year-old yogin facing south, the young teacher among aged pupils

title: Śiva states the guṇa-classification of Purāṇas to Pārvatī
description: Śiva teaches Pārvatī the sāttvic/rājasic/tāmasic grouping of the eighteen Purāṇas, each tied to a deity and destination

title: Śiva teaches the guṇa-classification to Pārvatī
description: Śiva instructs Pārvatī, grouping the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas into sāttvic, rājasic and tāmasic classes by presiding deity and destination

title: Jaya and Vijaya's three demonic births across the yugas
description: The cursed pair are born as Hiraṇyākṣa/Hiraṇyakaśipu (Satya), Rāvaṇa/Kumbhakarṇa (Tretā), and Śiśupāla/Dantavakra (Dvāpara), each slain by Viṣṇu's avatāras

title: Kadrū's curse on the nāgas (ratified by Brahmā)
description: Kadrū curses her serpent-sons to burn in Janamejaya's sacrifice; Brahmā ratifies it as a cull of the over-numerous nāgas

title: Kahoda Drowned by Bandin
description: Ashtavakra's father Kahoda is defeated in debate by Bandin at King Janaka's sacrifice and drowned per the contest's rule

title: Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa and Arjuna-Nara identity affirmed
description: The Mahābhārata identifies Kṛṣṇa as Nārāyaṇa and Arjuna as Nara reborn, anchoring epic theology to the Badarikāśrama hermitage

title: Kīrtimukha conflated with Rāhu the eclipse-demon
description: In variant tellings the self-consuming, jawless devouring-face is identified with or doubled by Rāhu the eclipse-graha who swallows sun and moon

title: Kubera's former-life merit as Gunanidhi
description: In a folk variant, the thief Gunanidhi, robbing a Shiva temple, inadvertently keeps a lamp burning before the linga, earning merit that reincarnates him as the wealth-god and friend of Shiva

title: Lakshmi Departs Vaikuntha for Earth
description: Offended that her abode was kicked by Bhrgu, Lakshmi leaves Vaikuntha for earth, triggering Vishnu's descent after her as Shrinivasa

title: Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean and asuras rout the devas
description: Stripped of fortune, the three worlds wither, Lakshmi re-enters the Kshira-Sagara, and Bali's asuras rout the weakened devas, who flee Svarga

title: Mahalakshmi slays Mahishasura
description: As the rajasika aspect, the Goddess slays the buffalo-demon Mahishasura in the middle carita

title: Maṅkaṇaka's sap-blood and Śiva's humbling at Saptasārasvata
description: The sage Maṅkaṇaka cuts his hand and vegetable sap (not blood) flows out; he dances in cosmic exultation until Śiva, cutting his own thumb to make ash flow forth, humbles him, after which the sage settles at Saptasārasvata where the Sarasvatī flows as seven streams (Suprabhā, Kāñcanākṣī, Viśālā, Mānasahradā, Sarasvatī/Oghavatī, Sureṇu, Vimalodakā)

title: Mohini tests Rukmangada and Vishnu bears the family to Vaikuntha
description: Brahma fashions the enchantress Mohini to break Rukmangada's vow; she forces him to choose between his fast and beheading his son Dharmangada, but as the sword falls Vishnu intervenes, reveals the test, and bears the family to Vaikuntha

title: Mārkaṇḍeya's First Narmadā Parikramā
description: Sage Markandeya, held to be the first parikramavasi, circumambulates the Narmada and each of her tributaries, founding the most extensive form of the river-circuit vow

title: Naming of Ekāmra Kṣetra (the one-mango field)
description: The temple-city is sacralized as the field of the single primordial mango tree under which Śiva dwelt with Pārvatī, around the Bindusāgara

title: Nandin snatches back the manuscript
description: Śiva's attendant Nandin tears away the leaf Śaṅkara had copied, leaving him only the first portion, which prompts Śaṅkara to compose the remaining 59 verses

title: Narada consoles King Srinjaya (Shodasarajakiya recap)
description: Narada and Parvata console King Srinjaya over his son Svarnasthivin's death by reciting the same roll of sixteen great kings who all died

title: Nara-Nārāyaṇa Teach at Badarī
description: The twin sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa impart ekāntika devotion to the sage Nārada at their hermitage at Badarī

title: Nightly flower-gathering from the royal garden
description: Moving invisibly, Puṣpadanta plucks choice flowers each night from a royal (often King Citraratha's) garden to offer Śiva

title: Nightly theft of flowers for Śiva
description: Invisible, Puṣpadanta gathers choice flowers from a royal garden each night to offer to Śiva

title: Nārada listed among Viṣṇu's avatāras
description: The Bhāgavata's descent-list names Nārada as the avatāra who propounds the Pāñcarātra/Sātvata-tantra path of devotion

title: Nārāyaṇa-sarovar — Viṣṇu's self-manifestation at the sea's edge
description: Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa manifests at the Kutch lake, sanctifying it as a Vaiṣṇava tīrtha and member of the five lakes

title: Parvati Gives Murugan the Vel
description: Parvati/Shakti gives Murugan her crystallised power as the lance Vel, the Shakti-vel that becomes the network's central object of worship

title: Pārvatī asks the secret of immortality
description: Pārvatī asks Śiva why he is deathless and she is reborn, prompting him to reveal the Amar Kathā
source: Amareśvara māhātmya; Kashmiri Śaiva oral tradition

title: Rati's penance wins Kama's rebirth
description: Rati performs penance and the gods intercede; Shiva grants that Kama will be reborn, visible to Rati alone or bodily in the next age

title: Rāma defers union to end of Kali Yuga
description: Rāma, met during exile and bound to Sītā, tells Vaiṣṇavī to do tapas in the Trikūṭa hills and await union with him as Kalki at the close of Kali Yuga

title: Sandhyā Tāṇḍava in the Rajata/Veḷḷi Sabhai (Madurai)
description: As Sundareśvara, consort of Mīnākṣī, Śiva dances the twilight dance with the right foot raised (mirror of Chidambaram) at the Pāṇḍya king's request

title: Sarasvati curses Ganga to flow on earth
description: In the Shakta account, after a jealous quarrel among Vishnu's three consorts, Sarasvati curses Ganga to flow on earth as a river

title: Savitri chooses Satyavan and Narada's death-prophecy
description: Savitri chooses the forest-prince Satyavan, son of the blind dethroned king Dyumatsena; the sage Narada declares Satyavan destined to die in exactly one year, but Savitri refuses to recant

title: Self-manifestation of Ranganatha at Srirangam
description: Vishnu's reclining Ranganatha murti is disclosed (given to Ikshvaku) on the Kaveri island, uncarved by mortal hand, as Bhuloka Vaikuntha

title: Shiva beheads the boy guardian
description: The boy posted at the door bars Shiva from entering Parvati's chamber, fights the ganas, and is decapitated by Shiva's trident

title: Six candidate definitions of brāhmaṇa enumerated
description: Five-to-six possible definitions of brāhmaṇa-hood (jīva, body, birth, knowledge, karma, dharma) are set up as positions to be refuted

title: Six-fold birth of Skanda (Shanmukha)
description: Shiva's too-potent seed, relayed through Agni, Ganga and a reed-thicket, becomes six infants nursed by the six Krittikas and fused by Parvati into the six-faced Kartikeya

title: Skanda shatters the liṅga into five fragments
description: Kumāra/Skanda slays Tārakāsura, and the self-rejoining Śivaliṅga is held apart by the gods and splinters into five pieces that fly to the five Andhra sites
source: Pañcārāma sthala-purāṇa (regional); cf. Skanda & Śiva Purāṇas

title: Soma's penance and the tempering of the curse at Prabhasa
description: Soma worships a Shiva-linga at the Sarasvati-sea confluence; Shiva halves the curse into the waxing/waning lunar cycle, restoring the moon's radiance and naming the place Prabhasa and the linga Somanatha

title: Sāvitrī chooses Satyavān despite Nārada's death-prophecy
description: Sāvitrī chooses the forest-prince Satyavān; Nārada foretells he will die in one year, but she refuses to recant

title: The aṅga-rakṣā limb-armouring
description: The hymn sets Rāma and his Rāmāyaṇa epithets upon each limb of the reciter's body in sequence, enclosing it in a protective kavaca

title: The boar and the swan fail to find the ends
description: Viṣṇu as the boar Varāha digs downward and Brahmā as a swan flies upward, but neither reaches an end of the fiery pillar, revealing Śiva as the unbounded source

title: The boon of a son equal to Viṣṇu, granted as three births
description: Unable to wish for anything higher than a son like Viṣṇu, the couple receive the only possible fulfilment: the Lord himself will be born to them as their son three times

title: The cast-out / ash-born child
description: Variant: the boy is rejected, cursed or cast into the cremation fire by his divine parents and survives to rule the burning-ground, explaining his fierceness

title: The Devī's self-disclosure as Brahman
description: The Goddess declares she alone existed before creation as the one non-dual Brahman/Cit-śakti, from whom māyā and the manifest world arose

title: The divine medical relay (Brahmā to Indra)
description: Āyurveda passes from Brahmā to Dakṣa Prajāpati, to the Aśvins, to Indra, from whom it reaches the human sage-world
source: Caraka Saṃhitā Sū. 1; Suśruta Saṃhitā Sū. 1

title: The Goddess manifests as Kanyākumārī and performs tapas
description: Ādi Parāśakti / Pārvatī abides as the virgin Kanyākumārī at the southern cape and undertakes severe penance to win Śiva of Suchīndram as husband

title: The gods pin the being face-down
description: The assembled devas overthrow the giant and hold it permanently face-down (adhomukha), head to the northeast, each god gripping a limb

title: The gods seize the deer and the antler breaks into the Paśupati liṅga
description: In the struggle to fetch Śiva back, his horn/antler breaks; the fragment becomes the worshipped liṅga and he consents to dwell as Paśupati

title: The guru's question 'Who are you?' (Narmada cave frame)
description: In the hagiographic frame, Govinda Bhagavatpada asks the young Shankara 'ko'si tvam' and the six verses are his answer, negating every false identity down to Shiva-Consciousness
source: Shankara-vijaya hagiographies (Madhava-Vidyaranya Shankara-dig-vijaya); traditional frame of the Nirvana Shatkam

title: The hill turns blue (Nīlācala)
description: The mountain turns blue where the yoni struck it, giving Nīlācala/Nīlaśaila its name

title: The slaying of Mahiṣāsura
description: Durga beheads the shape-shifting buffalo-demon Mahiṣa, the central victory the hymn exults in

title: The soul's crossing of the Vaitarani river
description: The preta crosses the dreadful river of blood and pus only by merit and a cow gifted (vaitarani-dana) by the family, which becomes its boat

title: The Tārakāmaya War
description: The heavens split into war over Tārā, with devas demanding her return against Soma, Śukra, and Śiva, until Brahmā intervenes and forces Tārā's return

title: Threefold birth of the self
description: Aitareya teaches the self's three births — conception, gestation, and rebirth in one's offspring — with the ātman entering the body through the crown

title: Threefold reading of the bilva leaf
description: The opening verse glosses the leaf's three leaflets as the three gunas, Shiva's three eyes, and the three-pointed trishula (with a parallel trimurti reading)

title: Tvaṣṭṛ creates Vṛtra in revenge
description: Enraged at his son's murder, Tvaṣṭṛ bars Indra from the soma sacrifice and performs a fire-rite to generate the avenger Vṛtra, but a mispronunciation dooms Vṛtra to die by Indra's hand
source: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.4.12; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9

title: Vasiṣṭha's hermitage and the Gaumukh spring
description: Vasiṣṭha settles his āśrama on Arbuda; the Gaumukh spring issues from a stone cow's-mouth and is linked to his wish-cow Nandinī/Kāmadhenu
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Arbuda-khaṇḍa; Gaumukh sthala tradition; cf. Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa

title: Vishnu's footprint enshrined at Vishnupada Temple
description: The Vishnupada Temple at Gaya enshrines the basalt footprint of Vishnu, the foot that subdued Gayasura, marking the principal site of Gaya pinda-dana

title: Viṣṇu's decree to reside as śālagrāma in the Gaṇḍakī beside Tulasī
description: Accepting the curse, Viṣṇu ordains he will forever manifest as the self-born śālagrāma-śilā in the Kālī-Gandakī, worshipped only with Tulasī

title: Vrika Questions Narada
description: The asura Vrika, son of Shakuni, meets the wandering Narada and asks which of the three chief gods is most quickly pleased

title: Yama's whisper to his noose-bearer
description: watching his own dūta set out pāśa in hand, the death-god leans to his ear and orders him to keep clear of the worshippers of Madhusūdana

title: Yayāti rescues Devayānī and weds her
description: Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into a well; King Yayāti pulls her out, weds her, with Śarmiṣṭhā given as her serving-maid

title: Aṅgāraka (Mars) Healed of Leprosy
description: Mars, afflicted with leprosy, worships Vaidyanatha-Shiva at Vaitheeswaran Koil and is healed, fixing the temple as the Mars node and divine-physician shrine

title: Ambikā sanctifies the Vastrāpatha-kṣetra
description: The Goddess as Ambikā/Ambā becomes the presiding kṣetra-devī of the hill, paired with Dattātreya in the Purāṇic charter of Vastrāpatha

title: Ashtavakra Defeats Bandin in Debate
description: The boy Ashtavakra out-argues the unbeaten Bandin in a counting debate, completing the verse on thirteen; Bandin reveals he is Varuna's son and the drowned brahmanas rise alive

title: Betrothal to Śiva of Suchīndram
description: Pleased by her tapas, Śiva of Suchīndram agrees to wed Kanyākumārī and a pre-dawn wedding muhūrta is fixed

title: Bhārgava line founded (Śukra, Cyavana, Paraśurāma)
description: Bhṛgu's descendants — Śukra the asura-guru, Cyavana, and through Ṛcīka–Jamadagni the avatāra Paraśurāma — form the Bhārgava clan

title: Birth of Budha (Mercury)
description: Tārā returns pregnant and, pressed by Brahmā, confesses Soma is the father; the radiant child is named Budha, the planet Mercury

title: Birth of Nandi from the sacrificial ground
description: Nandi arises in Śilāda's yajña-field as a portion (aṃśa) of Śiva himself

title: Brahma and the origin of painting
description: Grieving a brahmana's dead son, Brahma bids the father draw the boy on the ground and breathes life into the image, the legendary first painting

title: Brahma's boon — the Vastu-purusha
description: The pinned being begs not to be forgotten; Brahma makes him lord of every building-site, to be honored in construction on pain of vastu-dosha

title: Brahmā's false witness and curse
description: Brahmā falsely claims to have reached the summit, using the ketakī flower and a cow as witnesses, and is cursed to receive no worship while the ketakī is barred from Śiva's pūjā

title: Candravatī discovers the self-manifest liṅga (variant)
description: A princess Candravatī sees a kapila cow emptying its milk over an anthill, digs, and finds the svayambhu liṅga, worshipping it under jasmine creepers

title: Conception from blood and seed; sex-determination
description: Conception arises from the union of mother's blood and father's seed; predominance of one yields son or daughter, equality an intersex child, division twins

title: Cow-and-milk rediscovery of the buried four-faced horn (variant)
description: A cow spontaneously sprinkles milk over a spot; digging reveals the radiant chaturmukha liṅga of the lost horn

title: Dakṣa-yajña, Satī's self-immolation, and Vīrabhadra's destruction of the rite
description: Dakṣa Prajāpati holds a great sacrifice without inviting Śiva; Satī self-immolates and Śiva's emanation Vīrabhadra destroys the sacrifice — the archetypal sacrifice gone wrong

title: Dakṣiṇāmūrti teaches in silence
description: Śiva as the south-facing supreme guru expounds jñāna and yoga wordlessly through cinmudrā to the four aged Kumāras

title: Daksha curses Candra with wasting disease
description: Daksha curses Candra with kshaya-roga (wasting disease) so his brilliance dwindles away, in response to the wives' complaint

title: Dattātreya's eternal tapas on the summit (Datta-tīrtha)
description: The avadhūta Dattātreya performs and still performs deathless tapas on Girnar's highest peak, sanctifying it as Vastrāpatha

title: Defeat of Śumbha and Niśumbha
description: The hymn extends praise to the Goddess's destruction of the asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha and their armies

title: Disclosure of the sixteen-word mahāmantra
description: Brahmā discloses the sixteen-word, thirty-two-syllable Hare Rāma / Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra as the audible form of the Name and the supreme Kali-crossing formula

title: Drying and Disappearance of the Sarasvatī
description: The once-mighty Sarasvati dries and goes underground (the vinashana), re-emerging unseen at sacred confluences such as the Triveni Sangam

title: Durvasa Hurls the Kritya Fire-Demon
description: Enraged that the king 'ate' before serving him, Durvasa tears a lock from his hair and creates a blazing female fire-demon, the Kritya, to attack Ambarisha

title: Duṣyanta denies Śakuntalā; the celestial voice names Bharata
description: Duṣyanta publicly disowns Śakuntalā and son until a sky-voice affirms the child, who is named Bharata and crowned heir

title: Emanation of the Daśa Mahāvidyā from Satī
description: The ten Mahāvidyā goddesses emanate from Satī (or Pārvatī) when she blocks Śiva's exit in a quarrel, surrounding him with ten terrifying forms

title: Enrolment in Śiva's bhūta-gaṇa
description: Sudalaimāḍaṉ is folded into Śiva's host of fierce cremation-ground attendant spirits as a localized Tamil bhūta-guardian

title: First birth as Pṛśnigarbha
description: In the first age the Lord is born to Sutapas and Pṛśni and becomes renowned by the name Pṛśnigarbha, 'he of Pṛśni's womb'

title: Founding of Pushkara as Brahma's tirtha
description: Brahma's sacrifice founds Pushkara (Ajmer) as his chief shrine, with the Savitri/Gayatri episode explaining Brahma's near-absence of temples

title: Gaṇḍakī enumerated as a tīrtha in the Tīrtha-yātrā Parva
description: Sages Pulastya/Dhaumya list the Gaṇḍakī and its śālagrāma-tīrtha among the great sin-cleansing fords during the Pāṇḍavas' pilgrimage

title: Gaṇeśa-as-crow tips the kamaṇḍalu — Talakāverī descent
description: During a famine Gaṇeśa in crow-form tips Agastya's pot, releasing Kāverī to well up at Talakāverī and flow east

title: Gajendra-Moksha at Tirukkavithalam
description: Vishnu as Gajendra Varadan saves the elephant-king Gajendra from the crocodile, the Gajendra-moksha legend localized at Tirukkavithalam

title: Ganesha restored with an elephant head
description: To console the grieving Parvati, Shiva fixes an elephant's head onto the boy's body, reviving him as Gajanana and granting him first worship among gods

title: Garuḍa fetches the amṛta; serpents get forked tongues
description: Garuḍa frees Vinatā by fetching the gods' nectar as nāga-ransom; Indra reclaims it and the snakes split their tongues licking the kuśa-grass

title: Ghṛtācī as consort of Viśvakarmā
description: In the Vāmana Purāṇa tradition Ghṛtācī is named the wife of the architect-god Viśvakarmā, mother of his daughters (including Saṃjñā/Saraṇyū) and artisan progeny, linking her by adjacency to the Saṃvaraṇa–Sūrya material

title: Indra slays Namuci by a foam-trick
description: Indra kills the demon Namuci, who could be slain by neither wet nor dry nor day nor night, using a trick of foam

title: Indra slays the Vṛtras with Dadhyañc's bones
description: Dadhyañc's horse-head is recovered from the lake Śaryaṇāvat near Kurukṣetra, and Indra, using the bones of that head, slays ninety-nine Vṛtras — the Vedic germ of the spine-vajra story

title: Ishvara Gita spoken by Shiva
description: After Vishnu and Shiva embrace, Shiva expounds Atman, Brahman, Prakriti, Maya, yoga and moksha through a Shaiva non-dualist lens — a Bhagavad Gita with Shiva as spokesman

title: Śiva Lifts Kāśī on His Trident at Pralaya
description: At each universal dissolution Śiva lifts Kashi up on his trident to keep it safe, setting it back when creation resumes, so the city alone survives every pralaya

title: Judgment of the soul by Yama and Citragupta
description: At Yama's city the scribe Citragupta reads the ledger of deeds and Yama assigns heaven, a hell, or rebirth

title: Kakudmi and Revati visit Brahmaloka
description: King Kakudmi (Raivata), finding no suitor worthy of his daughter Revati, travels with her to Brahma's realm to ask Brahma directly for a husband, arriving while Brahma is absorbed in a Gandharva performance

title: Kalpa, manvantara and yuga arithmetic
description: Exposition of the fourteen Manus, the mahāyuga/manvantara/kalpa numbers and the four yugas — a base witness for the timeline's chronology

title: Kāmadeva regains his form in Kāmarūpa
description: The love-god Kāma, burnt by Śiva, regains his form and desire in this land, glossing the name Kāma-rūpa

title: Kshipra Breaks Mahadev into 84 Pieces
description: In one legend the river Shipra breaks Mahadev into 84 pieces to slay the demon Dushana, each piece becoming one of the Chaurasi Mahadev shrines

title: Madalasa's Atma-jnana lullaby and her sons' renunciation
description: Queen Madalasa, a jivanmukta, sings non-dual Vedanta to each infant son, and her first three sons renounce the world straightaway

title: Mahasarasvati slays Shumbha-Nishumbha
description: As the sattvika aspect, the Goddess slays Shumbha and Nishumbha and emanates Kali/Chandika in the third carita

title: Marriage of Savitri and Satyavan in the forest
description: Ashvapati gives Savitri to Satyavan in the hermitage; she dons bark-cloth and serves her blind father-in-law Dyumatsena as a devoted ascetic-wife

title: Meenakshi Tirukalyanam — the celestial wedding at Madurai
description: Born from the Pandya king's yajna with a third breast that vanishes on meeting Shiva, the fish-eyed goddess Meenakshi conquers the directions, is crowned Pandya sovereign, and weds Shiva as Sundareswarar; enacted as the Chithirai Tirukalyanam, one of Shiva's 64 tiruvilaiyadal

title: Mīnākṣī's conquests and meeting with Śiva
description: Crowned as warrior-queen Taḍātakai, she conquers the directions and besieges Kailāsa, where her third breast vanishes on meeting Śiva, revealing him as her destined consort

title: Mohinī beguiles Śiva, begetting Ayyappa
description: Mohinī later beguiles Śiva, their union begetting Ayyappa (Hari-Hara-putra), and also deludes the demon Bhasmāsura

title: Murugan Slays Surapadman and Weds Deivanai
description: At the Arupadai Veedu abodes Murugan slays the demon Surapadman (who falls at Tiruchendur) and marries Deivanai at Thiruparankundram

title: Namuci-slaying as a source of Indra's brahmahatyā stain
description: The treacherous twilight beheading of Namuci, an oath-breaking, is counted (with the Vṛtra- and Triśiras-slayings) among the deeds that incur Indra's brahmahatyā / sin-stain; some retellings add Namuci's severed head rolling after Indra reproaching him for breaking the truce

title: Negation of ritual, caste, and observance (Chapters 2, 7)
description: The avadhūta is declared beyond varṇāśrama, prescribed conduct, purity-rules, praise and blame — his ruleless wandering body itself the teaching

title: Nāga-jewel rescue from Pātāla
description: When Merakhiyā is snake-bitten/dying, Janbāī plunges into the netherworld waters to fetch the life-restoring nāga-maṇi

title: Nārada's Journey to Śvetadvīpa
description: Nārada journeys north past Mount Meru to the White Island to behold the universal form of the Lord and the perfected single-minded white devotees

title: Nārada's previous life as the maidservant's son
description: In a former kalpa Nārada was a poor maidservant's boy purified by serving travelling bhakti-yogins, granted a fleeting vision of the Lord, who at death merged into Nārāyaṇa and was reborn the immortal sage

title: Nārāyaṇa creates Urvaśī from his thigh
description: When Indra sends apsarases to break the sages' tapas, Nārāyaṇa generates the beautiful Urvaśī from his thigh, shaming the nymphs and proving his serenity

title: Prajapati-to-Vishnu attribution shift
description: Across the Brahmana-to-Purana transition the creator-tortoise is re-identified as a form of Vishnu/Narayana, paralleling Matsya and Varaha

title: Prāṇa overcomes the demons (Pavamāna prayer)
description: The vital breath (prāṇa) overcomes the demons' evil, the context of the 'asato mā sadgamaya' prayer leading from untruth to truth, darkness to light, death to immortality

title: Pratardana dialogue with Indra
description: Indra teaches Pratardana that he is prāṇa, the conscious self, life and immortality, declaring life-breath and cognition inseparable

title: Pārvatī Creates Gaṇeśa at Gaurī Kuṇḍa
description: At Gaurī Kuṇḍa below Dolma La, Pārvatī fashions a son from the paste of her body to guard her bath; Śiva strikes off his head and replaces it, the boy becoming Gaṇeśa

title: Pārvatī slays the demons Kṛti and Vāsa
description: Pārvatī (Gaurī) slays the asuras Kṛti and Vāsa in the field, the episode etymologizing the Kṛttivāsa epithet of the liṅga

title: Ūrdhva Tāṇḍava and the Kālī dance-contest (Tiruvalangadu)
description: In the banyan cremation-forest Śiva defeats the goddess Kālī in a dance-duel by raising one leg vertically, a posture she would not copy out of modesty, pacifying her
source: Tiruvalangadu sthala-purāṇa; Tēvāram; Kāraikkāl Ammaiyār's Aṟputat Tiruvantāti; Periya Purāṇa

title: Refutation of jīva and body
description: The brāhmaṇa is shown to be neither the soul (common to all beings) nor the body (made of the same five elements, no colour-rule of caste)

title: Roll-call of the sixteen chakravartins
description: Marutta, Suhotra, Brihadratha/Paurava, Shibi, Rama Dasarathi, Bhagiratha, Dilipa, Mandhatr, Yayati, Ambarisha, Shashabindu, Gaya, Rantideva, Bharata, Prithu, and Sagara are each praised as supreme sacrificer-conqueror-givers and shown to have died

title: Romaśā's bridal dialogue with King Svanaya/Bhāvayavya
description: Queen Romaśā answers her royal husband's touch in a frank conjugal verse appended to Kakṣīvat's gift-praise hymn

title: Rudra Creates and Rolls Up the Worlds
description: The one Rudra, allowing no second, holds all worlds with his ruling powers, creates beings, and at the end of time rolls them up (samcukoca) into himself

title: Sarayū saṅgama tīrthas with Gomatī and Gaṅgā
description: The Sarayū's confluences with the Gomatī and (via the Ghāghrā) the Gaṅgā are revered bathing-tīrthas, read as a reunion of sister-rivers
source: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 23–24; Skanda Purāṇa Ayodhyā-māhātmya; sthala-tradition

title: Sati immolates herself at the Daksha-yajna
description: Sati, married to Shiva against her father Daksha's contempt and humiliated at his sacrifice, immolates herself in yogic fire

title: Satī's Navel Falls at Kāñcī
description: In the Satī dismemberment myth the goddess's navel falls at Kāñcī, anchoring Kāmākṣī as a Śakti Pīṭha and the 'navel of the goddess'

title: Satī's self-immolation and the Dakṣa-yajña
description: Dakṣa stages an insulting sacrifice; Satī immolates herself, rupturing Dakṣa and Śiva, after which Pārvatī later performs austerity to win Śiva

title: Satyavān dies and Sāvitrī follows Yama
description: On the foretold day Satyavān dies; Yama comes in person to take his soul and Sāvitrī follows Death southward

title: Seer of Rigveda Mandala VI
description: Bharadvaja is the apical rishi to whom the sixth family-book of the Rigveda (75 hymns, chiefly to Agni and Indra) is ascribed

title: Self-manifestation of Bhu-Varaha at Srimushnam
description: The Sveta-Varaha (white-boar) murti lifting Bhu-devi arises on its own at the white-boar tank, the chief southern Varaha-kshetra

title: Sivah saktya yuktah — the opening declaration
description: Verse 1 declares that only when joined with Shakti is Shiva able to act, the charter statement of Shakta theology

title: Slaughter of the Exposed Kalakeyas
description: With the ocean drained, the gods slaughter the exposed Kalakeya asuras, already weakened by the wrath of the brahmins

title: Slaying of Mahiṣāsura
description: After a shape-shifting duel the Goddess pins the buffalo-demon Mahiṣāsura and beheads him as the true demon emerges from the buffalo's mouth, earning the name Mahiṣāsura-mardinī

title: Slaying of Malla and Maṇi
description: The god slays Malla (hence Mallāri); the dying Maṇi gifts his white horse and wins the boon of joined worship and animal offerings
source: Mallāri Māhātmya; Jejuri/Kannada Mailāra folk variants

title: Slaying of Surapadma at Tiruchendur
description: After a six-day fast Murugan fells the asura Surapadma in the seaside battle at Tiruchendur, the climactic victory of the Skanda war-cycle

title: Taraka-vadha by Skanda
description: Anointed Devasenapati, Skanda leads the devas and slays Tarakasura (and in expanded cycles Surapadma, Simhamukha and Pralamba), restoring cosmic order

title: Teaching by silence (mauna-vyākhyāna)
description: Dakṣiṇāmūrti raises the cin-mudrā and the disciples' doubts dissolve through wordless transmission of para-brahman

title: Teaching of ajāta-vāda (no world, no bondage, no liberation)
description: Through sustained refrain Ṛbhu affirms that body, mind, guru, disciple, bondage, path, and liberation do not exist as separate realities — only the one Self is

title: Teaching of māyā and the unfolding world
description: The Goddess expounds māyā as her own power by which the one appears as many, blending Sāṃkhya prakṛti-categories with Vedāntic non-duality

title: The ahaituki bhakti prayer
description: The poet prays for nothing but motiveless devotion birth after birth, disclaiming wealth, followers, beauty, and fame
source: Mukunda-mala Stotra (na dhanam na janam verse)

title: The avatāra-and-dharma doctrine
description: Gaṇeśa reveals himself as the unborn Lord who takes form age after age to protect dharma, adapting Bhagavad Gītā 4 into a Gāṇapatya frame

title: The eight-case Rāma-nāma benediction
description: The famed verse declines the name 'Rāma' through all eight Sanskrit grammatical cases, beginning 'Rāmo rāja-maṇiḥ sadā vijayate.'

title: The gods install their fragments at the five ārāmas
description: Indra, Soma/Candra, Viṣṇu and Kumāra each install a liṅga-fragment, giving the sites their names (Amarārāma, Somārāma, Kumārārāma, etc.)

title: The hump surfaces at Kedarnath
description: Re-emerging piecemeal across Garhwal, the bull's hump rises at Kedarnath as a conical svayambhu rock; the Pāṇḍavas raise the temple and are absolved

title: The ladder of negation across six verses
description: The hymn negates inner organ and senses, vital airs and sheaths, passions and purusharthas, merit/sin and ritual, death/caste/kin, then declares the formless all-pervading Self
actors: the meditating Self / aspirant; Adi Shankara as author

title: The Mahābhārata Vaitaraṇī ford
description: The Vaitaraṇī is named as a Kaliṅga river-ford in the Tīrtha-yātrā Parva (Pulastya's roster and Lomaśa's walked route), bathing there yielding cleansing and cow-gift merit

title: The phala-shruti and forgiveness prayer
description: The closing verses declare the fruit of bilva-offering and end on a ksama-prarthana, the single offered leaf standing in for ritual faults

title: The race around the parents
description: In a race against Kārtikeya for a divine fruit, Gaṇeśa circumambulates his parents declaring them his whole world and wins, sending the slighted Kārtikeya south

title: The road as shedding of attachments
description: Śiva leaves Nandi at Pahalgām, the moon at Chandanwāḍī, the serpents at Śeṣanāg, Gaṇeśa and the five elements at Mahāgaṇeś/Pañchtaraṇī, so none can overhear

title: The Sarasvati resurfaces at Prabhasa
description: The vanished Sarasvati river flows unseen and re-emerges at Prabhasa to pour into the ocean, forming the Triveni river-sea confluence
source: Mahabharata Vana Parva 80-82; Skanda Purana Prabhasa-khanda

title: The Sarasvatī merges into the sea at Nārāyaṇa-sarovar
description: The lost Sarasvatī river is held to complete its course and join the Arabian Sea at the Kutch coast, an oceanic confluence-sanctity

title: The Spider and the Elephant at Thiruvanaikaval
description: Two cursed Shiva-ganas reborn as a spider and an elephant worship the jambu-linga; their rivalry kills both, and Shiva frees them from the curse, the spider reborn as the Chola king Koccengat

title: The swan teaches forbearance and patient silence
description: The swan-Brahmā teaches that the highest good is self-conquest: repay abuse not with retaliation but with patient silence and equanimity, conquering both the abuser and oneself

title: The Vedavyāsa office and the 28th Vyāsa
description: A Veda-Vyāsa is appointed each Dvāpara to re-arrange the Veda; Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana is the 28th of the cycle, with Aśvatthāmā named as the coming 29th

title: The Vritra-gita: Vritra accepts his destiny
description: The defeated asura-king Vritra, taught by Shukracharya, expounds calm renunciation and devotion to Vishnu

title: Trampling of Śiva's consecrated offering
description: Not seeing them, Puṣpadanta treads on bilva leaves/flowers (or nirmālya) already consecrated to Śiva, and the sacrilege instantly strips him of his invisibility

title: Trampling of Śiva's sacred offering
description: Unaware, Puṣpadanta treads on bilva leaves/flowers already consecrated to Śiva and instantly loses his invisibility

title: Tumburu–Nārada musical rivalry
description: Nārada and the gandharva Tumburu are paired as rival celestial virtuosi, with Tumburu's superior vīṇā-craft repeatedly humbling Nārada's pride before Viṣṇu, Śiva and Indra

title: Tyranny from Śūnyaka and desolation of the worlds
description: Bhaṇḍāsura rules from the City of the Void with brothers Viṣukra and Viṣaṅga, draining the cosmos of love and fertility; Nārada counsels the devas to invoke Parāśakti

title: Uddālaka teaches Śvetaketu 'Tat tvam asi'
description: To humble his conceited son Śvetaketu, Uddālaka Āruṇi teaches the Sad-vidyā through nine parables, each closing with 'Tat tvam asi' — that thou art

title: Śukra curses Yayāti with premature old age
description: Discovering the broken oath, Śukra curses Yayāti to instant decrepitude, granting the loophole that he may trade his age for another's youth

title: Varāha lifts Bhū-devī and slays Hiraṇyākṣa at Śrīmuṣṇam
description: The Boar avatāra rescues the Earth-goddess from the pralaya-waters and kills the demon Hiraṇyākṣa, then remains present at Śrīmuṣṇam as Bhū-Varāha
source: Varāha Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa Śrīmuṣṇa-māhātmya

title: Vasiṣṭha's agni-kuṇḍa fire-sacrifice
description: Robbed of his wish-cow or beset by asuras, Vasiṣṭha kindles a great fire-pit atop Arbuda and performs a homa to bring forth defenders of dharma
source: Pṛthvīrāj Rāso; Agnikula bardic tradition [late text][disputed]

title: Vāg-Devatās recite the Lalitā-Sahasranāma
description: The Vāg-Devatās recite the thousand-name hymn to Lalitā to Hayagrīva, encoding the Śrī-Cakra and Śrī-Vidyā mantra doctrine

title: Vishnu counsels the churning truce
description: The devas approach Vishnu at the Kshira-Sagara, who counsels a temporary truce with the asuras to churn the ocean for amrita, promising the devas will ultimately keep it

title: Vishnudutas Rescue Ajamila from the Yamadutas
description: Hearing the holy name, four Vishnudutas descend and forcibly stop the three Yamadutas from binding and removing Ajamila's soul, then debate the jurisdiction of Yama

title: Vishnu's Three Strides (Trivikrama)
description: Vishnu measures out the three worlds — earth, mid-air, and heaven — in three strides, establishing the cosmos as living-space for gods and men and setting his 'highest step' as the abode of bliss

title: Vishnu Worships Ganesha to Subdue Madhu and Kaitabha at Siddhatek
description: At creation's edge Vishnu cannot subdue the asuras Madhu and Kaitabha until he worships Ganesha at Siddhatek and obtains siddhi, then prevails

title: Visnu accepts the curse and offers two roads
description: Visnu bows to the Kumaras, accepts the irrevocable curse, and offers his servants seven devotee-births or three enemy-births back to him

title: Viṣṇu Leaves His Footprint at Har-ki-Pauri
description: Viṣṇu appears at Har-ki-Pauri in the Vedic age and leaves his footprints in the stone of the ghāṭ, kept perpetually touched by the Gaṅgā

title: Vrika's Flesh-Offering Penance at Kedara
description: At Kedaranatha Vrika feeds the sacrificial fire with pieces of his own flesh for seven days until Shiva emerges from the fire to stay his self-beheading

title: Yajña on Gayāsura's Body
description: Asked for a boon, Gayāsura offers his own body as the altar; he lies head-to-north and Brahmā and the devas perform the great sacrifice upon him, making his body the holiest ground

title: Ajamila's Repentance and Liberation at Haridvara
description: Restored and transformed by faith, Ajamila renounces his home, performs bhakti-yoga at Haridvara, and at his second death is borne by the Vishnudutas to Vaikuntha

title: Ajāta-vāda: no creation, no bondage, no seeker
description: Core teaching that nothing was ever created or bound, there is no aspirant and no path, and liberation is only the falling-away of an illusion

title: Ashtavakra Made Straight in the River
description: The restored Kahoda bids Ashtavakra bathe in the river Samanga, and his eight bends are made straight

title: Aṣṭāvakra debates the celestial woman on women's independence
description: The sage Aṣṭāvakra, sent to test marriage, debates a celestial woman (Diśā) on whether a woman is independent or always under guardianship, expounding strī-dharma

title: Bharata becomes Cakravartin and eponym of Bhāratavarṣa
description: Bharata grows into a universal sovereign whose name is given to the dynasty and to the subcontinent Bhāratavarṣa

title: Bilva-offering on Mahashivaratri and Pradosha
description: The hymn accompanies bilva-arpana held especially efficacious on Mahashivaratri and at each fortnightly Pradosha dusk

title: Birth of Kauśikī and Kālikā
description: From Pārvatī's bodily sheath emerges the radiant Ambikā/Kauśikī to fight Śumbha-Niśumbha, while her darkened remainder becomes Kālikā

title: Birth of the Agnikula Rajput clans
description: Armed heroes spring from the fire-pit as ancestors of the Agnivaṃśa Rajputs — Pratīhāra, Cāhamāna (Chauhan), Caulukya (Solanki) and Paramāra; variants give a single Paramāra hero
source: Pṛthvīrāj Rāso; bardic genealogies; Paramāra inscriptional variant [late text][disputed]

title: Body-distribution: head at Paśupatinātha
description: Trans-Himalayan tradition holds the bull's head/face surfaced at Paśupatinātha in Nepal while the hump remains at Kedarnath, linking the two kṣetras
