source: Folk/regional tradition; cf. Skanda Purāṇa Kedāra-khaṇḍa Pañcha Kedār variant

title: Boy-Sage Śveta Saved from Yama
description: The boy-sage Sveta, fated to die at sixteen, is saved from Yama by Shiva at Thiruvenkadu, where Shiva subdues death itself

title: Brahma's revelation of elapsed time
description: Brahma laughs and explains that twenty-seven chaturyugas (roughly 116 million human years) have passed on Earth during their brief wait, so the proposed bridegrooms and their dynasties are long dead — an early literary depiction of time dilation

title: Bull/buffalo-form Śiva flees the Pāṇḍavas and dives at Guptakāśī
description: Pursued by the Pāṇḍavas seeking absolution, the bull-form Śiva dives into the earth at Guptakāśī to re-emerge across the Himalaya

title: Capture and punishment
description: Made visible, Puṣpadanta is seized by the garden guards and imprisoned, bereft of his power

title: Caraka lineage descends to Bharadvāja and Ātreya
description: Indra transmits medicine to Bharadvāja (seeking relief of human suffering), then to Ātreya Punarvasu and Agniveśa, founding the internal-medicine school

title: Chandra's Curse Tempered at Somnath
description: The Moon-god Chandra, cursed by Daksha to wane for neglecting his wives, worships Shiva at Prabhas Patan, and Shiva tempers the curse into periodic waxing and waning, founding the Somnath jyotirlinga

title: Child Murugan Teaches Om to Shiva at Swamimalai
description: At Swamimalai the child Murugan teaches the meaning of the Pranava (Om) to his father Shiva, becoming Swaminatha

title: Dadhīci drinks the gods' weapons
description: Tired of guarding the divine weapons deposited with him, Dadhīci dissolves them in water and drinks them, absorbing their power into his bones so his skeleton alone can yield the supreme weapon

title: Dadhichi sacrifices his bones for the vajra
description: When a Vritra can only be killed by a sage's bones, the ascetic Dadhichi yields his body, and Vishvakarma forges the Vajrayudha from his spine for Indra

title: Declaration of rule-free chanting and phala-śruti
description: Brahmā declares the mantra destroys Kali's covering, may be chanted without restriction of time or purity, and grants purification and liberation to the chanter

title: Durvāsā's curse of forgetting on Śakuntalā
description: Daydreaming of her husband Duṣyanta, Śakuntalā fails to honor the visiting Durvāsā, who curses that the one she thinks of will forget her; softened, the curse lifts when the king sees his signet ring — driving the second half of Kālidāsa's drama
source: Kālidāsa, Abhijñānaśākuntalam Act 4 (Kālidāsa's invention, absent in Mahābhārata)

title: Fall of Satī's body-part establishes the Bhramarāmbā Śakti Pīṭha
description: During Śiva's grief-wandering with Satī's corpse, a fragment (right anklet per Pīṭhanirṇaya; neck/upper lip per folk variant) falls at Śrīśaila, fixing the Goddess Bhramarāmbā and Bhairava Sundarānanda
source: Aṣṭādaśa Pīṭha Stotram; Tantra Cūḍāmaṇi/Pīṭhanirṇaya; Skanda Purāṇa (Śrīśaila-khaṇḍa)

title: Four-armed birth and self-revelation to Devakī
description: Viṣṇu is born to Devakī in full four-armed majesty in the Mathurā prison and, before shrinking to infant form, reveals that this is his third birth from her and Vasudeva

title: Ghora Āṅgirasa instructs Kṛṣṇa Devakīputra
description: The sage Ghora Āṅgirasa instructs Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī — one of the earliest textual mentions of Kṛṣṇa — figuring life as a soma-sacrifice

title: Hariṇī's curse (apsarā backstory)
description: In a former life Indumatī was the apsarā Hariṇī, sent by Indra to break Tṛṇabindu's tapas; the sage cursed her to mortal birth, releasable when a celestial object touched her

title: Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada, and Narasimha (Vishnu P.)
description: The asura king Hiranyakashipu persecutes his Vishnu-devoted son Prahlada, prompting Vishnu to erupt as the man-lion Narasimha and slay the boon-protected tyrant

title: Import of the Maga (Śākadvīpīya) priests
description: Sāmba brings sun-worshipping Maga priests from Śākadvīpa to serve the Sun-image, the Purāṇic memory of the Indo-Iranian solar cult entering India

title: Indra eclipses Varuṇa as king of the gods
description: Across the later Vedic layers the warrior storm-god Indra rises and displaces Varuṇa as effective king of the gods, his slaying of Vṛtra overtaking Varuṇa's law-sovereignty

title: Indra's sabotage of the hundredth Aśvamedha
description: Because a hundred horse sacrifices entitle the performer to Indra's throne, Indra habitually sabotages the hundredth Aśvamedha to protect his sovereignty

title: Instruction of King Alarka by Dattatreya
description: Alarka, his kingdom threatened to provoke his awakening, follows his mother's ring-counsel to the avadhuta Dattatreya and receives the realization of the Self, finally renouncing

title: Śiva narrates the Amar Kathā in the empty cave
description: Stripped of every witness, Śiva spreads a deer-skin / ring of fire and tells Pārvatī the secret of amaratva

title: Jaya and Vijaya choose three demonic births
description: Unable to bear long separation, the two choose to be born three times as Visnu's enemies, each life ended by his hand, to return home swiftly

title: Kallazhagar's late arrival and Vaigai crossing
description: Kallazhagar (Vishnu, the bride Meenakshi's brother) sets out from Alagar Koil to give away the bride but arrives late, finds the wedding done, and turns back at the river Vaigai; his entry into the river is the Vaishnava climax of the Madurai Chithirai festival, a rare Shaiva-Vaishnava civic confluence
source: Madurai Chithirai festival tradition; Wikipedia (Chithirai Thiruvizha)

title: Koṭeśvar and the crore of liṅgas (Rāvaṇa's ātma-liṅga)
description: Rāvaṇa receives a powerful liṅga from Śiva and, through trickery, leaves a crore of replica liṅgas at Koṭeśvar beside Nārāyaṇa-sarovar

title: Kumāra consecrates Kumārārāma at Samalkota
description: Skanda himself installs and worships his fragment as Kumāra Bhīmeśvara, the site most directly tied to the shattering-myth

title: Lakṣmī becomes the badarī tree to shelter Viṣṇu
description: As Viṣṇu does open-air austerities in Himalayan cold, Lakṣmī transforms into a jujube-berry (badarī) tree to shade him, naming the place Badari-kā-āśrama

title: Mahiṣāsura-vadha (Śākta variant)
description: The gods pool their tejas into the lion-riding Durgā/Caṇḍikā, who is armed by each deity and slays the buffalo-demon Mahiṣa

title: Maya the asura-architect and the burning of Tripura
description: The asura craftsman Maya builds the three flying cities and a life-restoring nectar step-well; Vishnu drains the well to stop the demons' resurrection and Shiva destroys Tripura with a single fiery arrow

title: Meditation on Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as lions
description: Closing verses contemplate Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa striding forth like two bow-bearing lions, with the 'āpadām apahartāram' benediction

title: Menakā breaks Viśvāmitra's penance
description: Indra sends Menakā against the rishi Viśvāmitra; aided by Vāyu and Kāmadeva she seduces him, and from their union is born Śakuntalā
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa

title: Month-by-month development of the fetus
description: The conceptus passes from kalala (drop) through bubble and lump to a fetus whose head, limbs, spine, face and sense-organs form across eight months

title: Mārkaṇḍeya's vision of the pralaya
description: The deathless sage Mārkaṇḍeya survives the dissolution, beholds the infant Viṣṇu on a banyan leaf upon the cosmic waters, is swallowed, and sees the universe inside the Lord's body

title: Muktī/Tāmira Tāṇḍava in the copper hall (Tirunelveli)
description: Śiva as Nellaiappar dances the liberation-dance in the copper-roofed sabhā of the Kāntimati–Nellaiappar temple, famed for its musical stone pillars

title: Naṭarāja's Ānanda Tāṇḍava
description: Śiva as Lord of Dance performs the cosmic dance of bliss at Cidambaram, enacting the five acts (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, grace) and crushing the dwarf Apasmāra
source: Cidambaram Naṭarāja tradition, Tirumantiram, Śaiva Siddhānta

title: Naṭarāja's Ānanda Tāṇḍava — the cosmic dance of bliss
description: Śiva as Lord of Dance performs the dance of bliss at Cidambaram, enacting the five cosmic acts (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, grace) and crushing the dwarf of ignorance Apasmāra
source: Cidambaram Naṭarāja tradition; Śaiva Siddhānta; Tirumular's Tirumantiram

title: Naciketas's three boons and Yama's teaching
description: The boy Naciketas, sent to Yama's realm, wins three boons and Yama reluctantly teaches him the immortal Self that is never born and never dies

title: Nandi granted deathlessness and union with Śiva
description: Śiva bathes Nandi in the Gaṅgā, grants a third eye and bull-crest, and declares him ageless and never to be parted from himself; weds him to Suyaśā/Marudvatī

title: Naraka and the Kāmarūpa dynasty
description: King Naraka of Prāgjyotiṣa-Kāmarūpa worships then transgresses the Goddess, who withdraws favour, fixing the royal line to her shrine

title: Nemīnātha's renunciation, omniscience and nirvāṇa on Ujjayanta
description: The 22nd Jain Tīrthaṅkara Nemīnātha (Ariṣṭanemi), Kṛṣṇa's cousin, renounces on his wedding day and attains dīkṣā, kevala-jñāna and nirvāṇa on Girnar

title: Nidāgha's awakening
description: The disciple Nidāgha recognizes his own identity with the formless Self as the illusion of separateness falls away

title: Nārada's cock-crow thwarts the wedding
description: To preserve the celibate Śakti needed to kill Bāṇāsura, Nārada takes a cock's form and crows; Śiva, thinking dawn had passed, turns back and the marriage hour lapses

title: Original shrine decays and icon buried
description: Prahlāda's original temple decays across the Yugas and the self-manifest icon lies buried in an anthill until refound

title: Origin of bhaṇḍāra (turmeric) worship
description: In victory the god and army are showered in turmeric, founding the defining bhaṇḍāra offering and the cry 'Yelkoṭ! Jai Mālhār!'

title: Pairing with the second Māḍaṉ
description: Variant: Sudalaimāḍaṉ is paired with a second Māḍaṉ (e.g. Vellai-māḍaṉ) as brothers or two faces of the guardian

title: Pattachitra and the Jagannatha cult of Puri
description: Odisha cloth-scroll painters depict the Jagannatha-Balabhadra-Subhadra triad and supply the Anasara-patti substitute icons worshipped while the wooden murtis are repainted

title: Pūru gives his youth; sons cursed and the dynasty splits
description: The four elder sons refuse and are cursed; youngest Pūru gives his youth and is crowned heir, forking the Lunar line into Yādava and Paurava branches

title: Puṣpadanta caught and bereft of his power
description: Made suddenly visible, Puṣpadanta is exposed and seized by the king's guards, robbed of the gift that defined him

title: Purāṇic pitṛ/śrāddha-māhātmya of the river
description: Purāṇic māhātmyas rank the Vaitaraṇī a first-tier ancestor-rite river where bathing, tarpaṇa and piṇḍa-offering discharge the debt to the dead

title: Refutation of birth via the roll-call of low-born sages
description: Birth cannot define brāhmaṇa-hood: revered ṛṣis (Ṛṣyaśṛnga, Vyāsa, Vālmīki, Vasiṣṭha, Agastya, Gautama, Kauśika, Jāmbuka) had irregular or non-brahmin origins yet are supreme brāhmaṇas
actors: Upaniṣadic teacher; the cited sages Ṛṣyaśṛnga

title: Rehearsal of Hanuman's Ramayana feats
description: The hymn's caupais retell Hanuman's Treta-yuga deeds (Sita's message, burning of Lanka, carrying the Sanjivani mountain) as eternally present devotional content
source: Hanuman Chalisa cpr. 11-18; Valmiki Ramayana Sundara-kanda/Yuddha-kanda

title: Sapindikarana (preta becomes pitr)
description: The recurring decisive death-rite in which, on the 12th day, the single preta-pinda is merged into the three ancestral pindas, converting the hungry ghost into a settled ancestor and bumping the great-great-grandfather into the remote ancestors

title: Sarasvatī saves Vasiṣṭha and is cursed at Vasiṣṭhāpavāha
description: Commanded by Viśvāmitra to sweep Vasiṣṭha to him for slaughter, the Sarasvatī instead carries Vasiṣṭha away to safety; Viśvāmitra curses her to flow with blood until rākṣasas drink there and are freed and the sages restore her purity (the Aruṇā confluence). The ford Viśāla/Vasiṣṭha-tīrtha commemorates her loyalty

title: Savitri's Triratra vow and Satyavan's death
description: Savitri undertakes a three-night standing fast, accompanies Satyavan into the forest on the fatal day, and he is stricken and dies with his head in her lap as Yama comes in person to take his soul

title: Self-manifestation of Venkateshwara on Tirumala
description: Srinivasa-Venkateshwara stands self-manifest on the Seven Hills as the Kali-yuga refuge where Vishnu stays bodily present through the dark age

title: Shani's glance burns off Ganesha's head
description: In a variant, Shani's destructive glance burns off the infant Ganesha's head and Vishnu brings a young elephant's head to replace it

title: Shanti Parva recapitulation by Bhishma
description: Bhishma re-states the Sixteen-Kings consolation within the Raja-/Moksha-dharma instruction, the verses recurring on the deaths of the great emperors

title: Shibi gives his eyes to a blind beggar (Sibi Jataka)
description: In the Buddhist Sibi Jataka, Sakka disguised as a blind brahmana begs an eye and Shibi gives both, then has them restored by an Act of Truth

title: Shiva Grants the Death-Touch Boon
description: Shiva, bound by his word, grants Vrika the boon that whomever he touches on the head with his hand will die

title: Shiva manifests as the fire-column at Arunachala
description: At Arunachala/Tiruvannamalai Shiva manifests as the infinite column of fire (teja-linga), the etiology of the Karttikai-Dipam festival

title: Shiva Teaches Akhilāṇḍeśvarī Shiva-jñāna
description: Shiva imparts Shiva-jnana to the fierce goddess Akhilandeshvari at Thiruvanaikaval, where she stands facing east as disciple and the linga faces west as guru

title: Skanda slays Surapadman (Tamil recension)
description: In the Tamil Kandapuranam, Skanda destroys the demon Surapadman across six war-camps and marries Valli

title: Sūrya reveals the Sūrya Siddhānta to Maya
description: At a yuga-junction the Sun sends an emissary to teach Maya the astronomy of planetary motions, sphericity and the Mahāyuga

title: Surapadma Split into Peacock and Cock
description: The dying Surapadma turns into a mango tree which the Vel splits in two; one half becomes Murugan's peacock vahana and the other the cock of his banner, redeeming the asura into service

title: Sāvitrī wins five boons and Satyavān's life from Yama
description: By her dharma-wisdom Sāvitrī extracts five boons, trapping Yama with the boon of sons by Satyavān, forcing him to restore Satyavān to life

title: Teaching of Nārada at Badarī (Naranārāyaṇīya frame)
description: The twin sages impart the ekāntika dharma to Nārada at Badarī, the inner narrative frame of the Nārāyaṇīya that transmits to Bhīṣma and Yudhiṣṭhira

title: Teaching on control of speech and truthfulness
description: The swan exalts restraint of speech (vāk-saṃyama), measured gentle true words or silence, and truthfulness (satya) paired with non-injury and self-restraint as the path to the supreme good

title: The Bindusāgara gathers a drop of every tīrtha
description: The temple-tank is said to collect a drop of every sacred tīrtha of India, so a bath there equals all pilgrimages

title: The body becomes the cosmogram grid
description: The prone body is mapped onto the squared site as the vastu-purusha-mandala (64- and 81-pada grids) with the 45 devatas and the central Brahmasthana

title: The Datta-pādukā footprint shrine
description: The summit enshrines Dattātreya's footprints as his abiding bodily presence, the focal darśana of the climb

title: The death-bed prayer for remembrance of Hari
description: The hymn begs that the Name remain on the lips at the hour of death when the throat is choked

title: The deformed rāgas humble Nārada
description: Vain of his music, Nārada is shown the rāgas and rāgiṇīs personified as maimed beings he mangled by singing out of tune, and undertakes tapas to master music properly
source: later Purāṇic / musicological lore; rāga-mālā tradition

title: The fire-pillar cools into Aruṇācala hill
description: At the gods' plea the unbearable fiery column cools and condenses into the Aruṇācala mountain, with a worshippable liṅga (Aṇṇāmalaiyār) installed at its base

title: The foot-dust cosmogony
description: Verse 2 holds that Brahma creates, Vishnu sustains, and Rudra destroys the worlds from the dust of the Goddess's feet

title: The Hamsa-gita: Brahma as swan instructs the Sadhyas
description: Brahma in the form of a swan answers the Sadhyas on the highest good, teaching forbearance and self-mastery

title: The limp and the name Khoḍiyār
description: Hurrying back before the pyre, Janbāī injures her foot and walks with a limp (khoḍa), revives Merakhiyā, and is named Khoḍiyār
source: Cāraṇ folk tradition; variant of the agreed funeral signal

title: The Mahāyāga and the rise of Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī
description: From the fire-pit (cit-kuṇḍa) of the devas' great sacrifice arises Lalitā Tripurasundarī, four-armed with noose, goad, sugarcane bow and five flower-arrows

title: The moon's curse on Gaṇeśa Caturthī
description: Mocked by Candra after his belly bursts from modakas, Gaṇeśa decrees that whoever views the moon on his festival day will be falsely accused

title: The Sarasvatī-sacrifice dispute and Bhṛgu's commission
description: Sages disputing Trimūrti supremacy depute Bhṛgu to test Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva for worthiness of the chief offerings

title: The Sudarshana Destroys the Kritya and Pursues Durvasa
description: The Sudarshana-cakra instantly incinerates the Kritya, then turns on its sender Durvasa, chasing him across the three worlds as Brahma and Shiva confess they cannot save him

title: The Virāṭ (cosmic) theophany
description: At Himavat's request the Goddess grants divine sight and reveals her all-pervading universal form containing all worlds and beings — the Śākta counterpart to Bhagavad Gītā ch. 11

title: The waxing-and-waning compromise
description: Unable to revoke his word, Daksha modulates the curse so the Moon wanes for half the month and waxes back for the other half, originating the dark and bright fortnights

title: Three lifetimes of Veda study
description: Indra grants Bharadvaja three full lifetimes of study, then shows his learning is a handful of dust against the mountains of the Veda, teaching him the Savitra Agni rite as essence

title: Tirukkalyāṇam — the celestial marriage
description: The wedding of Mīnākṣī and Sundareśvara at Madurai, with Viṣṇu giving away the bride as her brother, celebrated as the Chithirai Tiruviḻā

title: Treading down Apasmāra (ignorance)
description: The icon's pendant foot rests on the dwarf-demon Apasmāra/Muyalaka, knowledge treading down nescience

title: Tuṅgā and Bhadrā spring from the Varāha's tusks
description: The two streams Tuṅgā and Bhadrā issue from the tusks of Viṣṇu's Varāha avatāra on Varāha-parvata and unite as the Tuṅgabhadrā

title: Tulasī deceived; the śālagrāma curse
description: To enable Śaṅkhacūḍa's slaying, Viṣṇu deceives the chaste Tulasī by taking her husband's form; the enraged Tulasī curses Viṣṇu into the śālagrāma stone and is herself transformed into the tulasī plant and the Gaṇḍakī river

title: Vibhīṣaṇa sets the vimāna on the Kāverī island
description: Carrying the vimāna under the rule that it roots wherever grounded, Vibhīṣaṇa halts at Tiruvaraṅgam and Raṅganātha refuses to rise

title: Vishnu incarnates as Kurma to bear Mount Mandara
description: Mount Mandara is uprooted as churning-rod and Vasuki wound as the rope; when the mountain sinks Vishnu incarnates as the tortoise Kurma and supports it on his shell

title: Vishvakarma trims the Sun
description: To relieve Sanjna who could not bear Surya's blaze, Vishvakarma shaves off an eighth of the Sun's radiance, the shavings forged into Vishnu's chakra, Shiva's trident, and other divine weapons

title: Viṣṇu Pins Gayāsura with the Dharmaśilā
description: When Gayāsura's body keeps quaking, Viṣṇu places a great stone slab on him and presses it with his foot, leaving the Viṣṇupada footprint

title: Viśvavārā tends the dawn fire-sacrifice
description: The Atri-clan seer Viśvavārā herself kindles and offers at the Agni fire-altar at dawn, praying for household concord and prosperity

title: Vyasa Gita taught by Vyasa
description: Vyasa teaches knowledge of Shiva through combined devotion and prescribed works, the duties of the ashramas, and the path to liberation

title: Yama visits his sister Yamuna (Bhai Dooj charter)
description: Yama, lord of death, visits his sister Yamuna who tilaks and feasts him; moved, he decrees that brothers so honored by sisters on Kartik Shukla Dvitiya escape Naraka

title: Yājñavalkya cursed and the Yajurveda split
description: Cursed by his teacher Vaiśampāyana, Yājñavalkya vomits the old Kṛṣṇa Yajus (taken up as partridges), then the Sun-god as a horse teaches him the fresh Śukla Yajurveda — the origin myth of the White/Black split

title: Yājñavalkya–Maitreyī dialogue
description: About to renounce, Yājñavalkya teaches his wife Maitreyī that immortality comes not from wealth but from knowing the Ātman, for whose sake all is dear

title: Yuga-dharma and the decline of the ages
description: Detailed account of how dharma contracts from Satya to Kali, with the lengths and degeneration of varṇa, lifespan and virtue across the four yugas

title: Achaleśvar — Śiva's earth-steadying toe-print
description: Śiva is worshipped at Achaleśvar as a natural toe-print holding up the earth — the deity Achala, 'the immovable,' fixing the hill and world in place

title: Aditi's Payo-vrata and the second birth as Vāmana
description: The same souls reborn as Kaśyapa and Aditi; Aditi's milk-vow penance earns Viṣṇu's descent as the dwarf Vāmana/Upendra, the couple's second birth

title: Agastya Digests the Asura Vatapi
description: Agastya eats the goat-disguised cannibal asura Vatapi served by Ilvala and says 'Vatapi jiryatam,' digesting and dissolving the demon before he can be summoned back

title: Ambikā as kṣetra-devī of Vastrāpatha
description: The Goddess Ambā/Ambikā presides over the hill as kuladevī, paired with Dattātreya as the two powers sanctifying the field

title: Andhaka-vadha — impalement of the blind demon
description: Andhaka, monstrous son of Hiranyaksha, lusts after Parvati and is impaled on Shiva's trident until his pride burns away, then converted into a devotee and gana-chief

title: Appointment as gaṇa-chief and gatekeeper of Kailāsa
description: Śiva makes Nandi commander of his gaṇa-host (Nandikeśvara/Nandīśvara) and dvārapāla controlling access to the god
source: Liṅga Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa

title: Ashtavakra's Marriage Test for Suprabha
description: To wed Suprabha, the grown Ashtavakra passes the northern temptation set by the rishi Vadanya, refusing a queen's seduction

title: Bharata, the deer, and Jada-Bharata
description: King Bharata renounces his kingdom but becomes attached to a fawn, is reborn a deer and then as the idiot-seeming sage Jada-Bharata, who instructs the king of Sauvira in non-dualist wisdom

title: Bhṛgu–Varuṇa inquiry into Brahman
description: Varuṇa guides his son Bhṛgu through successive realizations deriving Brahman as food ascending to bliss in the Taittirīya teaching

title: Bilva-mahatmya in the Skanda Purana
description: The Skanda Purana carries extensive bilva-mahatmya praising the tree and the merit of leaf-offering to Shiva, a reservoir the hymn echoes

title: Birth of Hariharaputra (Śāstā / Ayyappa)
description: In regional Śaiva tradition the Śiva–Mohinī union produces Hariharaputra, Śāstā/Ayyappan of Śabarimala, son of Hari and Hara (implicit/appended, not in the Bhāgavata text proper)
source: South Indian / Śaiva Ayyappa tradition (cf. Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.12)

title: Body-distribution: head at Paśupatinātha, hump at Kedarnath
description: The re-emerging bull-form Śiva leaves his head/face at Paśupatinātha in Nepal and his hump at Kedarnath, joining the two as one dismembered bull across the range
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Kedāra-khaṇḍa; Nepāla-māhātmya; folk tradition

title: Boon of Gayā the Eternal Pitṛ-Tīrtha
description: Viṣṇu and the gods grant that the demon's name mark the spot forever and that any ancestral rite performed there liberate the dead, turning the demon's self-sacrifice into sacred geography

title: Brahmā and Śiva fail the test
description: Bhṛgu provokes Brahmā (anger) and Śiva (trident raised, restrained by Pārvatī), disqualifying both as rajas/tamas-stained

title: Candra's penance to Shiva at Prabhasa
description: Candra worships Shiva at Somnath/Prabhasa to be cured, and Shiva wears the saved crescent as Candrashekhara

title: Citra/Tripura Tāṇḍava in the picture hall (Kutralam)
description: At Courtallam Śiva as Kuṟṟālanāthar dances the picture-dance worshipped through a mural rather than a metal icon; Agastya is said to have founded the Śaiva shrine

title: Codification by the divine architects
description: Vishvakarma (architect of devas) and Maya (architect of asuras) are made the mythic authors of the vastu/shilpa craft and its two textual streams
source: Mahabharata Sabha Parva; Mayamata; Shilpa Shastras

title: Composition of the Śiva Mahimna Stotra as atonement
description: Realizing the offense was against Śiva, Puṣpadanta composes the Śiva-mahimnaḥ stotra praising the god's immeasurable greatness to win back grace; the hymn pleases Śiva and his powers are restored
source: Śiva-mahimnaḥ stotra (Puṣpadanta frame; signature/colophon verses naming the author)

title: Conception of Skanda/Kārtikeya
description: Śiva's too-fiery seed is carried by Agni and Gaṅgā and deposited in the Saravaṇa reeds, conceived to produce a son able to slay Tārakāsura

title: Dadhīci gives his bones for the vajra
description: When Viṣṇu reveals that only a weapon forged from Dadhīci's thunder-laden bones can slay Vṛtra, the sage consents to give his life and quits his body in samādhi so his spine can be taken

title: Dakṣa's yajña at Drākṣārāma and Manikyāmbā Śakti Pīṭha
description: Drākṣārāma is identified as Dakṣa's garden / yajña-site, and consort Manikyāmbā is counted as the pīṭha where Sati's left cheek fell
source: Bhīmeśvara Purāṇamu (Śrīnātha); Aṣṭādaśa Śakti Pīṭha Stotra

title: Dakshas curse causes the moon's waning
description: Candra favors Rohini and neglects his other 26 nakshatra-wives; Daksha curses him to waste away, and Shiva redeems him to wax and wane eternally

title: Dhūmralocana burnt to ash
description: The Goddess reduces Śumbha's general Dhūmralocana to ashes with a single huṃkāra and her lion mauls his army

title: Dismemberment of the asura Bala into the nine gems
description: The great asura Bala (Vala) is sacrificed by the gods and his scattered body-parts become the nine precious gems (blood→ruby, teeth→pearl, etc.), the origin myth of the navaratna
source: Garuda Purana (gem section); Agni Purana; Buddha-bhatta's Ratna-pariksha

title: Ensoulment of the fetus
description: In the seventh month the fetus is endowed with the jīva (individual soul) and becomes animate

title: Establishment of Muktinath as a jwālā-mukhī mokṣa-kṣetra shared with Buddhism
description: The Mukti-kṣetra with its 108 dhārās and natural rock-flame becomes a liberation-granting shrine revered jointly as the Buddhist Chumig Gyatsa
source: Vaiṣṇava sthala-māhātmya; Varāha Purāṇa tradition; temple/Tibetan tradition

title: Establishment of the seat and disappearance
description: Khodiyār establishes her sthāna and finally withdraws/merges into the divine, leaving the Galdharā springs and river-shrines as tīrthas

title: Exposition of the three yogas (jñāna, karma, bhakti)
description: The Goddess lays out the converging paths of knowledge, desireless action, and devotion, distinguishing supreme (parā) from preparatory (gauṇī) bhakti

title: Forbearance declared the higher strength
description: The swan answers that endurance is not weakness: the forbearing man who is unmoved by praise or blame is the stronger, having conquered his own mind, the harder enemy

title: Founding of the Pañcha Kedār circuit
description: Kedarnath becomes head of the five Garhwal body-part shrines (hump→Kedarnath … hair→Kalpeśvara), the only Pañcha Kedār shrine that is also a Jyotirliṅga
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Kedāra-khaṇḍa; Wikipedia, Panch Kedar

title: Ganesha Grants Boons to Sage Gritsamada at Mahad
description: Sage Gritsamada worships Ganesha at Mahad after a curse and is granted boons, enshrining the deity as Varada-Vinayaka, the boon-giver

title: Gautama brings the Godavari (Gautamī Gaṅgā) to the Deccan
description: After a contrived cow-killing sin engineered by jealous ṛṣis, the sage Gautama brings the Gaṅgā down to the Deccan as the Godavari to expiate it

title: Gayāsura and the Gayā-māhātmya
description: The pious asura Gayāsura is pinned to the earth so his sanctified ground becomes the supreme pitṛ-tīrtha where a single piṇḍa-offering liberates one's forebears

title: Hālāhala / Nīlakaṇṭha
description: During the ocean-churning Śiva drinks the all-destroying Hālāhala poison to save creation; Pārvatī holds his throat, lodging it there and turning his throat blue
source: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.7, Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Śiva Purāṇa

title: Indra slays Vṛtra mounted on Airāvata
description: Airāvata is the mount on which Indra slays the dragon Vṛtra, cementing the elephant's rain-and-war role

title: Inversion of the Trimūrti hierarchy
description: Within the discourse Gaṇeśa is declared the source from whom Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva derive their powers, and is identified with OṂ and the bindu as the first principle of reality

title: Invocation of the rescued devotees
description: The hymn invokes past acts of grace across the yugas as warrant for refuge: Gajendra freed, Draupadi clothed, Prahlada saved, Ahalya lifted

title: Jānaśruti seeks the sage Raikva
description: The proud king Jānaśruti, hearing flamingoes praise the cart-man sage Raikva, seeks him out and is taught the saṃvarga-vidyā of air and breath as the absorbers

title: Kacha infiltrates Śukra to steal the Sañjīvanī
description: The devas send Bṛhaspati's son Kacha to become Śukra's disciple and secretly learn the life-restoring mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā that the asuras alone possess
source: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Matsya Purāṇa; Agni Purāṇa

title: Kallaḻagar Vaigai river-crossing
description: Viṣṇu as Kallaḻagar rides late to give away his sister, finds the wedding done, and steps into the Vaigai river instead of entering the city

title: Kardama's tapas and the naming of Bindu-sarovara
description: Viṣṇu's tears (bindu) of compassion fall at the Sarasvatī-bank lake where the Prajāpati Kardama performs austerity, naming Bindu-sarovara

title: Katyayani born to slay Mahishasura
description: The Goddess is born in sage Katyayana's hermitage specifically as the fierce warrior-form Katyayani to slay Mahishasura
source: Devi Mahatmya; Devi Kavaca; Bhagavata Purana 10

title: Kundalini ascent and the Sri Cakra
description: Verses 8–11 locate the Goddess as Kundalini ascending the cakras to union with Shiva and describe the Sri Cakra of intersecting Shiva and Shakti triangles

title: Lingodbhava — Shiva's infinite pillar of fire at Arunachala
description: When Brahma and Vishnu dispute supremacy, Shiva appears as an endless column of fire whose top and base neither can find; Arunachala hill is that fiery linga, re-enacted annually by the Maha/Bharani Deepam ghee-beacon atop Tiruvannamalai during Karthigai Deepam on the Krittika asterism
source: Lingodbhava / Arunachala sthala purana; Wikipedia (Karthikai Deepam)

title: Lopāmudrā urges Agastya to householder dharma
description: In a dialogue-hymn Lopāmudrā presses the long-austere Agastya to balance tapas with procreation

title: Mahishasura conquers heaven
description: After a hundred-year war the buffalo-demon Mahishasura defeats Indra, usurps the three worlds, and expels the gods from svarga

title: Marriage of Lalitā to Kāmeśvara and enthronement in Śrīpura
description: Śiva as Kāmeśvara weds Lalitā; the pair are enthroned on the Pañca-brahmāsana in the jeweled city Śrīpura, cosmographic form of the Śrīcakra

title: Marriage to Mhāḷsā
description: Khaṇḍobā weds Mhāḷsā, a Brahmin merchant's daughter identified with Pārvatī, representing the settled agrarian-Brahmin pole of the cult

title: Murugan's Marriage to Deivanai at Tirupparankundram
description: After his victory Murugan weds Deivanai, Indra's foster-daughter, at Tirupparankundram, taking the dharmic deva-bride

title: Named among the seven rishis in the Brihadaranyaka
description: The vamsha-style enumeration of Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 2.2.4 names Bharadvaja among the seven rishis, paired with his father Brihaspati

title: Nārada attains Viṣṇu's vision at the Nārada-kuṇḍa
description: Sage Nārada attains the vision of Viṣṇu at Badarī; the Nārada-kuṇḍa pool in the Alaknandā is named for him and yields the self-manifest mūrti

title: Pabuji ki phad sung before the painted shrine
description: The Bhopa bard unrolls the Pabuji phad scroll as a portable shrine and sings the epic of the Rathod folk-deity Pabuji, held an amsa of Lakshmana
source: Wikipedia, Phad painting; J. D. Smith, The Epic of Pabuji

title: Pampā the river-goddess weds Śiva as Virūpākṣa
description: Pampā/Pampāvatī, daughter of Brahmā, wins Śiva as Virūpākṣa through tapas on Hemakūṭa, naming Pampā-kṣetra (Hampi)

title: Piṅgalā retold among the Avadhūta's 24 gurus
description: In the Bhāgavata's Uddhava-Gītā the young avadhūta tells King Yadu that Piṅgalā the courtesan of Videha was one of his twenty-four gurus, quoting the hope-maxim almost verbatim
actors: the avadhūta brāhmaṇa; King Yadu; Piṅgalā (cited); (frame: Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava)

title: Prajāpati's da-da-da teaching
description: Prajāpati's single syllable 'da' is heard by gods, humans and demons as the threefold instruction to control oneself, give, and be compassionate

title: Pride after Kāma's failure against Śiva
description: Nārada grows proud of conquering desire where the burned Kāmadeva failed against Śiva, prompting Viṣṇu to humble him

title: Pārvatī's penance and Ardhanārīśvara merger
description: Pārvatī covers Śiva's eyes plunging the cosmos into darkness, does penance at Tiruvaṇṇāmalai (slaying the demon Mahiṣa), and is re-merged into Śiva's left half as Ardhanārīśvara; she becomes the goddess Apītakucāmbāḷ/Uṇṇāmulai

title: Raṅganātha reclines facing south toward Laṅkā
description: To console Vibhīṣaṇa, Raṅganātha stays but reclines facing south so his blessing perpetually reaches Laṅkā

title: Rambhā cursed to stone by Viśvāmitra
description: Sent against Viśvāmitra, Rambhā fails and is cursed to become stone for ten thousand years

title: Refuge-invocation of Hanumān
description: The hymn closes by taking refuge in Hanumān, swift as thought and chief of the monkey host, as Rāma's messenger and guardian

title: Refutation of knowledge, karma and dharma
description: Scholarship, ritual action and piety are each rejected as the definition of brāhmaṇa because they are shared with other varṇas or are external

title: Sati's body becomes the Shakti Pithas
description: In the variant where Shiva carries Sati's corpse and Vishnu's discus dismembers it, her scattered body-parts fall to earth and become the Shakti Pithas

title: Satī's Heart and Navel Fall at Māyāpurī
description: When Viṣṇu dismembers Satī's corpse to end Śiva's grief-dance, her heart and navel fall at Māyāpurī (Haridwar), anchoring it among the Śakti Pīṭhas
source: Wikipedia, Maya Devi Temple; Shakti Pitha tradition

title: Savitri's dialectical duel and five boons from Yama
description: Following Yama southward and reciting dharma aphorisms, Savitri wins boons restoring Dyumatsena's sight and kingdom, a hundred sons for Ashvapati, and a hundred sons by Satyavan, trapping Yama into restoring Satyavan's life

title: Self-formation of the shaligrama at Salagrama/Muktinath
description: On the Kali-Gandaki in Mustang the aniconic self-formed shaligrama stones are worshipped as Vishnu without consecration, the purest self-manifest form

title: Shiva and Parvati Follow Skanda to Srisailam
description: After Kartikeya leaves in pique over Ganesha's marriage, Shiva and Parvati follow him to the hill and reside there as Mallikarjuna, establishing the Mallikarjuna jyotirlinga

title: Shiva drinks the Halahala poison and becomes Nilakantha
description: The world-poison Halahala/Kalakuta surfaces first, threatening creation; Shiva drinks it and Parvati stays it in his throat, which turns blue, giving him the name Nilakantha
source: Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Vishnu Purana; Shiva Purana

title: Shiva Flees to Vaikuntha
description: Vrika turns to test the boon on Shiva's own head, and the terrified god flees across the universe to Vishnu's Vaikuntha

title: Slaying of Andhakasura by Bhairava
description: The blind demon Andhaka is defeated, the slaying associated with Bhairava, culminating in Andhaka's redemption as a gana

title: Slaying of Śumbha, Niśumbha, and Raktabīja
description: The Goddess emanates the fair Kauśikī, leaving dark Kālikā behind, and destroys Śumbha and Niśumbha with their generals Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa (→Cāmuṇḍā) and Raktabīja, whose blood-drops Kālī drinks

title: Soma cured of Dakṣa's wasting-curse at Soma-tīrtha
description: Soma (the Moon), afflicted with the kṣaya (consumption) curse of Dakṣa for neglecting his other daughter-wives, bathes in the Sarasvatī at Soma-tīrtha and is released, his waxing and waning fixed thereafter; the ford thereby gains power to cure illness, with special merit on Somavatī Amāvasyā
source: Mahābhārata, Vana-parva (Tīrtha-yātrā); Śalya-parva; Soma–Dakṣa curse cycle

title: Suśruta lineage descends through Divodāsa Dhanvantari
description: Dhanvantari incarnate as Divodāsa, king of Kāśī, teaches the surgical science to Suśruta and fellow pupils

title: Sāvitrī wins Satyavān back from Yama
description: Sāvitrī follows Yama as he carries off her husband Satyavān's soul and wins him back by her wit and virtue, in an expanded Sāvitrī–Yama discourse on dharma and the soul

title: The avadhūta-lakṣaṇa and the four syllables (Chapter 8)
description: The marks of the true avadhūta are given and the word a-va-dhū-ta is read as a map of liberation; this chapter is often judged a later addition

title: The Bull of Dharma loses a leg each yuga
description: Dharma personified as a bull loses one leg each yuga, virtue diminishing from four quarters to one across Satya, Treta, Dvapara, and Kali, restored to four at the next Satya

title: The dance-contest against Kālī
description: Śiva wins a dance-duel against Kālī by raising his leg in the ūrdhva-tāṇḍava pose, which Kālī, bound by modesty, cannot match and concedes

title: The Goddess slays the bee-demon Aruṇāsura as a swarm of bees
description: To destroy a demon immune to weapons, the Goddess emits black bees from her body that kill him, earning the name Bhramarāmbā, she-who-fought-as-bees
source: Devī-māhātmya / Śākta lore; Śrīśaila sthala tradition

title: The mythic Vaitaraṇī crossing and vaitaraṇī-dāna
description: The preta crosses the foul underworld Vaitaraṇī by holding the tail of a cow gifted at death (vaitaraṇī-dāna); the earthly river inherits this saving logic
actors: the preta (soul); Yama; the family; the Vaitaraṇī cow

title: The pair of pigeons overhear and become deathless
description: A pair of doves (kapota) unnoticed overhear the entire Amar Kathā and become immortal, said to still inhabit the cave
source: Amar Kathā tradition; living pilgrim lore

title: The swayambhū Kṛttivāsa liṅga and Harihara compact
description: The self-manifest Śiva-liṅga is declared Tribhuvaneśvara, lord of all three worlds and both sects, so Hari shares Hara's seat

title: The three-wives quarrel and Vishnu's redistribution of consorts
description: Jealous Sarasvati curses Lakshmi to become the Tulasi plant and a river; Ganga curses Sarasvati to become a river bearing people's sins; Vishnu ends the strife by keeping Lakshmi, sending Ganga to Shiva and Sarasvati to Brahma

title: Umā–Maheśvara dialogue on women's duties
description: Śiva, questioned by Umā (Pārvatī), expounds the ideal conduct of a wife: devotion, sweet speech, and treating the husband as god

title: Upamanyu's childhood vow for Śiva's grace
description: The boy Upamanyu, craving milk, is told it is Śiva's gift alone and resolves to win it by austerity to Śiva

title: Vishnu Declares Himself Subject to His Devotees
description: Fleeing to Vaikuntha, Durvasa is told by Vishnu that He cannot recall the discus or act against His devotee, uttering 'aham bhakta-paradhino,' and is sent to beg Ambarisha's pardon

title: Vow of perpetual virginity
description: Left unwed at the missed muhūrta, the Goddess resolves to remain forever Kumārī, retaining the undiminished celibate power that enables her victory

title: Yama Confesses Vishnu's Supremacy
description: When the baffled Yamadutas report their defeat, Yamaraja reveals there is a Supreme Lord above him, names the twelve mahajanas, and commands his servants never to approach devotees of the Name

title: Yayāti's renunciation after a thousand years of indulgence
description: After a millennium of pleasure Yayāti realizes desire only grows, returns Pūru's youth, and retires to the forest attaining heaven

title: Yogis See the Self-Power of the Deva
description: Practitioners of dhyana-yoga, through meditation, perceive the hidden self-power (devatma-shakti) of God veiled by its own qualities, identifying the personal Lord as the first cause

title: Agastya Destroys Ilvala
description: Enraged that his brother is digested, Ilvala is reduced to ashes by the fire from Agastya's glance, and the sage departs with the riches he sought

title: Agni Purified by Worshipping Shiva at Kanjanur
description: The fire-god Agni worships Shiva at Kanjanur to be purified, giving the temple its name Agnishvarar

title: Ambarisha's Prayer Spares Durvasa
description: After a year of pursuit Durvasa falls at the king's feet; Ambarisha prays the Sudarshana-stuti, the discus relents, and the king feeds Durvasa before breaking his own fast

title: Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest; the Śrīvatsa mark
description: Bhṛgu kicks the sleeping Viṣṇu's chest; Viṣṇu calmly massages the sage's foot, the print remaining as the Śrīvatsa, winning the verdict of supremacy

title: Bhrāmarī Devī slays Aruṇāsura
description: When the demon Aruṇa, immune to harm from any two-footed creature, threatens the gods, the Goddess takes the form of Bhrāmarī and swarms of six-legged bees and wasps tear his army apart

title: Bilva-mahatmya in the Padma Purana
description: The Padma Purana preserves bilva-mahatmya glorifying the leaf-offering and the tree's link to the goddess Lakshmi

title: Birth of Durga from combined tejas
description: The enraged gods emit tejas that coalesces into the eighteen-armed Goddess Durga/Chandika, each body-part formed from a specific god's light

title: Birth of Kapila and the Kapilopadeśa at Bindu-sarovar
description: Kapila, Viṣṇu incarnate, is born to Kardama and Devahūti and expounds the Sāṅkhya tattva-system to his mother, liberating her

title: Bāṇāsura-vadha
description: Because she remains a virgin, the boon's loophole holds and Kanyākumārī battles and slays the demon Bāṇāsura at Land's End, freeing the devas

title: Candra abducts Tara and the Tarakamaya war
description: Candra abducts Tara, wife of Brihaspati, triggering the Tarakamaya war until Brahma intervenes; from the union Budha is born, founding the Lunar line

title: Chandra cursed by Ganesha
description: Chandra mocks Ganesha's broken-tusk form and is cursed so that whoever sees the Moon on Ganesha Chaturthi is falsely accused

title: Daksha's sacrifice destroyed; Shiva weds Uma
description: The Vamana Purana narrates Sati's self-immolation at Daksha's sacrifice, Shiva's wrecking of the yajna, and his later marriage to Parvati/Uma

title: Daksha-yajna wrecked by Virabhadra
description: Daksha's sacrifice slights Shiva and is wrecked by Virabhadra and Bhadrakali — Bhaga's eye and Pushan's teeth are struck — until Shiva is honored and order restored

title: Devnarayan ki phad
description: The longest phad scroll narrates the epic of the Gurjar deity Devnarayan, regarded an avatara of Vishnu, recited before the cloth-shrine

title: Devāpi enters yogic suspension at Kalāpa-grāma
description: Rather than dying, Devāpi enters deep yogic samādhi at the hidden village Kalāpa and survives in concealment through the entirety of Kali Yuga
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.24; Bhāgavata Purāṇa XII.2.37-38

title: Division of the Veda by the 28 Vyasas
description: The Veda is recurringly redacted by a Vyasa in each Dvapara, situating Krishna-Dvaipayana as the 28th, one per mahayuga across the manvantara

title: Fixing of the Vishnu-kshetra at Naimisharanya
description: Hari's Manomaya Cakra strikes earth at the Gomati forest, opening the Cakra-tirtha and fixing the self-manifest abode amid the Purana frame-story sattra

title: Ganesha Recovers the Chintamani Jewel at Theur
description: After the greedy prince Guna steals sage Kapila's wish-fulfilling Chintamani jewel, Ganesha slays Guna and recovers it, becoming Chintamani Vinayaka

title: Ganesha Slays Sindhu at Morgaon
description: Ganesha as the peacock-rider Mayureshwar slays the demon Sindhu, founding the adi node of the Ashtavinayaka at Morgaon

title: Guru Śikhar — Dattātreya's summit
description: The highest Aravalli peak is crowned by a shrine to Dattātreya (and Anasūyā), echoing the Datta summit-cult of nearby Girnar

title: Head-to-foot praise (anga-varnana)
description: Verses 42–100 describe the Goddess limb by limb from crown to lotus-feet, closing with self-surrender offering her own radiance back to her

title: Identification with Kauśikī
description: The Vindhya-dwelling goddess is equated with Kauśikī/Ambikā, who emerged from Pārvatī's sheath to fight Śumbha-Niśumbha

title: Indra incurs Brahmahatya and hides
description: Because the Puranic Vritra/Vishvarupa is a brahmana, killing him incurs Brahmahatya; crushed by the sin, Indra shrinks into a lotus stalk and vanishes, leaving Svarga kingless

title: Śiva slays Tripura and Andhaka
description: The Śiva Purāṇa records Śiva's slaying of the Tripura demons and of Andhaka

title: Śiva's Ānanda-tāṇḍava as Naṭarāja at Cidambaram
description: Śiva dances the bliss-dance enacting the five cosmic acts of creation, preservation, destruction, concealment and grace
source: Nāṭya Śāstra ch. 4; Śaiva Āgamas; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Śiva Whispers the Tāraka-Mantra at Death
description: At the moment of death within Kashi, Śiva whispers the ferry-mantra into the dying's ear, cutting the knot of karma and granting immediate liberation regardless of prior deeds

title: Jihve kirtaya — command to the faculties
description: The poet commands his own tongue, mind, hands, ears, and eyes to worship Keshava, turning the body into an instrument of kirtana

title: Kacha killed thrice and revived; the belly reversal
description: The asuras murder Kacha three times, finally feeding his ashes to Śukra in wine; Śukra teaches the Sañjīvanī from inside his own belly, Kacha bursts out killing the guru and then revives him

title: Kadrū's curse fulfilled
description: The burning fulfills Kadrū's ancient curse that her serpent-sons perish in Janamejaya's fire, tying the rite to the Garuḍa/churning backstory

title: Karthigai Deepam — the summit beacon
description: At the Kārttikai full moon a colossal ghee lamp (Mahā-Dīpa) is kindled atop Aruṇācala, re-enacting the original pillar of fire as Śiva again shows his endless fiery form

title: King Bhaṅgāśvana becomes a woman
description: A king transformed into a woman bears children as both sexes and, asked to choose, keeps the female form, declaring a mother's love and a woman's pleasure greater

title: Kālī slays Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa
description: Kālī springs from Caṇḍikā's brow and beheads the generals Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, earning the name Cāmuṇḍā

title: Krittika nurses suckle Kartikeya/Skanda
description: The six Pleiad-nurses of the Krittika nakshatra suckle the war-god Karttikeya/Skanda, the origin of his name

title: Manifestation as the dual Tiruvappana and Vellatam theyyam
description: Muthappan is venerated as a Viṣṇu-Śiva (Harihara) fusion performed as two paired theyyam figures — the Vaiṣṇava fisher Tiruvappana and the Śaiva hunter Vellatam
source: Theyyam / Kaliyāṭṭam tradition; North Malabar folk Śaiva-Vaiṣṇava tradition

title: Murugan's Marriage to Valli at Tiruttani
description: At Tiruttani Murugan woos and weds Valli, the hunter-girl of the kurinci hills, the indigenous Tamil love-marriage counterpart to Deivanai

title: Mustering of the Goddess's army of śaktis
description: Lalitā fields Vārāhī/Daṇḍanāthā as commander, Śyāmalā/Mantriṇī (Mātaṅgī) as prime minister, child-goddess Bālā, the Nityās, yoginīs and śaktis born of her own body

title: Nandi as bearer of whispered prayers
description: Devotees whisper petitions into Nandi's ear at the temple for conveyance to Śiva — the living custom before the liṅga's darśana

title: Nara–Nārāyaṇa in the Bhāgavata avatāra rosters
description: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa lists Nara-Nārāyaṇa among Viṣṇu's līlā-avatāras as the tapas-and-dharma exemplifying descent, outside the fixed canonical Daśāvatāra

title: Oppiliappan Served Food Without Salt
description: The founding legend of Tiruvinnagar where Vishnu as Oppiliappan vows to accept food served without salt, marking the marriage to Bhumi Devi

title: Origin of the four Shaktis from Shiva
description: Four Goddess-energies (Shaktis) arise from Shiva, a Shakta theophany folded into the Shaiva cosmology

title: Parvati's rebirth and tapas
description: Sati is reborn as Parvati, daughter of Himavan, and wins the ascetic Shiva through severe penance

title: Pāṇḍava Mahāprasthāna terminus
description: After absolution the Pāṇḍavas begin their Mahāprasthāna, the northward renunciatory ascent into the Himālaya read as passing through the high Kedār country
source: Mahābhārata, Mahāprasthānika Parva tradition; Skanda Purāṇa, Kedāra-khaṇḍa

title: Phala-śruti coda — reciting the ford-list itself confers merit
description: The parva closes its enumeration with the promise that even hearing or reciting the catalogue of fords frees one from sin, making the list itself a tīrtha

title: Purāṇic geography — seven dvīpas and Meru
description: Systematic geography of Jambūdvīpa, the concentric continents and oceans, Mount Meru as world-axis, the varṣas of Bhārata and the motion of the heavenly bodies

title: Pushkara and Brihaspati charter (River Pushkaram)
description: The deva Pushkara, granted by Shiva (var. Brahma) the power to sanctify waters, agrees with Brihaspati (Jupiter) that he will enter a river to charge it with full tirtha-power for twelve days whenever Jupiter transits into that river's corresponding zodiacal sign — establishing the 12-yearly Pushkaram bathing-fair cycle across twelve sacred rivers (notably Godavari in Simha and Krishna in Kanya), with Adi and Antya Pushkaram book-ending each transit

title: Recognition as Ādi-Śakti / kuladevī
description: Khodiyār is read as a manifestation of Ādi-Śakti/Durgā and becomes kuladevī of many Gujarati communities with major pilgrimage temples and the crocodile vāhana
source: Gujarati kuladevī tradition; Cāraṇ āī theology

title: Redaction of the Caraka Saṃhitā
description: Agniveśa's tantra is redacted by Caraka and completed by Dṛḍhabala into the foundational text of internal medicine and the tridoṣa doctrine

title: Restoration of grace and powers
description: Pleased by the hymn, Śiva restores Puṣpadanta's invisibility and grace, establishing the stotra as a model expiatory prayer

title: Śrīparvata named as a tīrtha in the Mahābhārata pilgrimage catalogue
description: The Tīrtha-yātrā-parvan lists Śrīparvata among the southern Śaiva fords of Bhārata, an early pre-temple witness to the hill's sanctity

title: Sanskritizing graft of the Hariharaputra genealogy
description: The older Dravidian guardian Ayyaṉār-Śāstā is given the son-of-Śiva-and-Mohinī (Hariharaputra/Bhūtanātha) parentage, folding the village god into the Purāṇic Śāstā genealogy
source: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa Śāstā stratum; harmonized tradition

title: Saptarshi of the Vaivasvata Manvantara and gotra-father
description: Bharadvaja is counted among the seven sages of the current Manvantara and is the eponymous founder of the Bharadvaja gotra (Angirasa-Barhaspatya-Bharadvaja pravara)

title: Satī's Self-Immolation at Māyāpurī
description: In a local telling Satī performs her yogic self-immolation at Māyāpurī, sitting in dhyāna and consuming her body by inner fire (linked to Daksha's spoiled sacrifice at Kankhal)

title: Satyakāma Jābāla's truthful lineage
description: The boy Satyakāma honestly reports his unknown parentage; teacher Gautama accepts him as a true brāhmaṇa, and the elements and birds teach him the quarters of Brahman

title: Satyavan revived and every boon fulfilled
description: Yama looses the noose granting Satyavan four hundred years; Satyavan revives, Dyumatsena's sight and throne are restored as the usurper dies, and both Savitri and Ashvapati gain a hundred sons

title: Self-manifest śālagrāma Badrī-Nārāyaṇa mūrti enshrined
description: A black śālagrāma image of Viṣṇu in meditation arises self-manifest (svayam-vyakta) and is worshipped as Badrī Viśāl, flanked by Nara–Nārāyaṇa, Kubera, Nārada and Uddhava
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Badarī-māhātmya; Garuḍa Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa

title: Shiva Slays Dushana as Mahakala at Ujjain
description: Shiva emerges as Mahakala to slay the demon Dushana who tormented the devout brahmin Vridhi and the pious king, founding the Mahakaleshwar jyotirlinga at Ujjain

title: Siddhidatri grants Shiva his powers
description: The Navadurga form Siddhidatri is said to have given Shiva his occult powers, making him Ardhanarishvara

title: Six-fold birth of Kārtikeya
description: The seed becomes six infants in the reeds suckled by the six Kṛttikās; Pārvatī's embrace fuses them into the six-faced, twelve-armed Ṣaṇmukha
source: Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Skanda Purāṇa, Śiva Purāṇa

title: Soma worships at Somārāma for curse-relief
description: Candra/Soma, afflicted by Dakṣa's wasting-curse, worships the moon-coloured liṅga at Gunupūdi-Bhimavaram to regain his light

title: Tat tvam asi — Uddālaka teaches Śvetaketu
description: Uddālaka Āruṇi instructs his son Śvetaketu nine times that 'That thou art,' teaching the identity of the self with universal Being

title: Teaching of aṣṭāṅga-yoga and kuṇḍalinī
description: The Goddess teaches the eight limbs of yoga together with nāḍī/cakra physiology and the rousing of kuṇḍalinī, the text's Tantric layer

title: The Ashtavakra Gita Spoken to Janaka
description: Ashtavakra instructs King Janaka in radical Advaita non-dualism, with Janaka voicing his own awakening mid-dialogue

title: The co-wife quarrel of Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī
description: Viṣṇu's three consorts quarrel and curse one another, explaining why Gaṅgā descends to earth and Sarasvatī becomes a river

title: The golden-lotus tank & Sangam judgment-pool
description: Śiva blooms a golden lotus in the Poṟṟāmarai Kuḷam, tradition holding it the pool that judged Sangam verses by floating or sinking

title: Theology of the pre-paid crossing (name-as-soteriology)
description: Bathing and offering at the hell-named earthly river is held to pre-cross the death-river, so the dead need never face the infernal Vaitaraṇī — the distinctive inversion of Jajpur
actors: pilgrims; the ancestors; the two Vaitaraṇīs (earthly and infernal)
source: Padma/Skanda māhātmyas; Garuḍa Purāṇa; tīrtha etymology

title: The Pārvatī–Śiva framing dialogue (appended)
description: An appended frame has Pārvatī ask Śiva the easy recitation, and Śiva answer that the single name 'Rāma' equals the whole thousand
source: Appended liturgical frame-verses of the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma

title: The siddhānta: the brāhmaṇa is the knower of Brahman
description: The text concludes that the brāhmaṇa is one who has directly realized the non-dual Ātman/Brahman as sat-cit-ānanda, free of egoism and the afflictions, ending as an Advaitic meditation-instruction

title: The soul recollects past lives in the womb
description: The ensouled fetus remembers its previous births and karma, recognizes its bondage to saṃsāra, and suffers in the womb

title: The Spider, Serpent and Elephant at Srikalahasti
description: A spider, a serpent and an elephant each worship the Vayu-linga in their own way until their daily worship clashes; all three attain moksha and their names fuse into Sri-Kala-Hasti

title: Third birth as Kṛṣṇa and the instruction to Gokula
description: The same souls now Vasudeva and Devakī receive the Lord a third time as Kṛṣṇa, who then bids them treat him as an ordinary child and carry him to Gokula

title: Two-clocks placement of ritual body-art
description: Body-adornment is fixed scripturally in the timeless 64-kalā curriculum (Kṛṣṇa's 64-day mastery) and historically as a living folk art of the kali-historical period

title: Upamanyu wins the ocean of milk from Śiva
description: By terrible penance Upamanyu compels Śiva (who first tests him as Indra) to grant an ocean of milk and unwavering devotion

title: Vishnu Tricks Vrika into Self-Destruction
description: Vishnu, as a brahmana boy, plants doubt in Vrika and dares him to test the boon on himself, so Vrika lays his hand on his own head and his skull shatters

title: Viṣṇumāyā and the monkey-face curse
description: Given a monkey's face at a svayaṃvara instead of Viṣṇu's beauty, the humiliated Nārada curses Viṣṇu to suffer separation from a wife and depend on monkeys, fulfilled in the Rāma avatāra
source: Bhāgavata-tradition retellings; Devī Bhāgavata; folk Rāmāyaṇa frames

title: Viśvakarman forges the vajra from Dadhīci's spine
description: The divine architect Viśvakarman fashions the adamantine thunderbolt (vajra) and other weapons from Dadhīci's bones, hammering the vajra specifically from his backbone

title: Vāk Āmbhṛṇī proclaims herself the all-pervading power
description: In the Devī Sūkta the seer Vāk (Speech), as both ṛṣikā and deity, declares herself the sustaining power over all gods and worlds — a Śākta foundation-text

title: Winning of Bāṇāī the Dhangar wife
description: Khaṇḍobā in pastoral guise herds sheep to win Bāṇāī, a Dhangar shepherd woman; the two-wife structure unites agrarian and pastoral communities
source: Marathi folk tradition; ovī oral epics [folk/regional]

title: Yama's Boon to His Sister Yamuna at Yamunotri
description: Yama grants his sister Yamuna the boon that bathing in or touching her water grants a painless death, the significance of the Yamunotri shrine

title: Yayāti falls from heaven and is saved by his grandsons
description: Cast out of svarga for pride, Yayāti is restored by the merit of his daughter Mādhavī's four royal-sage sons

title: Yājñavalkya defeats the sages at Janaka's court
description: At King Janaka's great sacrifice Yājñavalkya claims the prize cattle and defeats challenger after challenger (Aśvala, Ārtabhāga, Bhujyu, Uṣasta, Kahola, Gārgī, Uddālaka) on Brahman and the Self

title: Abhijit descends and contests Rohini for seniority
description: In the Mahabharata, the star Abhijit slips down from the sky contesting with Rohini for seniority, narrated to Skanda/Indra as why an extra (28th) nakshatra was needed; it becomes the nakshatra of victory

title: Ambarisha Attains the Lord's Abode
description: Having demonstrated bhagavata-dharma perfectly, Ambarisha in old age divides his kingdom among his sons, retires to the forest, and attains the abode of Vishnu

title: Attukal Amma identified with Kannagi
description: The Attukal Bhagavathy charter identifies the goddess with Kannagi of the Silappatikaram, who burned Madurai in vengeance, grounding the women-only Attukal Pongala offering

title: Bṛhaddevatā enumerates the women seers
description: Śaunaka's Bṛhaddevatā fixes the canonical roll of Ṛgvedic brahmavādinīs (Ghoṣā, Viśvavārā, Apālā, Romaśā, Lopāmudrā, et al.)

title: Bharadvaja receives Ayurveda from Indra
description: Deputed by the sages, Bharadvaja approaches Indra and brings the science of life (Ayurveda) back to the rishis, founding the medical lineage through Atreya and Agnivesha

title: Bhasmasura Destroyed by Mohini's Dance
description: In the folk version, the ash-demon Bhasmasura wins the incinerate-by-touch boon, turns on Shiva, and Vishnu as Mohini dances him into laying his hand on his own head, reducing him to ashes

title: Bṛhaspati proclaims ahiṃsā the highest dharma
description: Bṛhaspati delivers the celebrated declaration that non-violence is the highest dharma, self-control, gift, and austerity, counselling universal compassion

title: Bhrigu kicks Vishnu's chest (the Bhrigu-test)
description: The Prajapati Bhrigu kicks Vishnu's chest to decide the supreme god, earning the foot-mark Shrivatsa

title: Bindu-sarovar established as the mātṛ-tīrtha (Mātṛ-gayā)
description: Siddhpur's lake becomes the foremost site of the mother's death-rite, counterpart to Gayā's pitṛ-rite, read back from Kapila liberating Devahūti

title: Birth and beheading of Gaṇeśa (Śani-gaze version)
description: Pārvatī obtains a son by the Puṇyaka-vrata; Śani's inauspicious gaze severs the infant's head, and Viṣṇu fetches a young elephant's head (Airāvata's calf) to restore him

title: Burning of Kama (Kama-dahana)
description: Kamadeva, sent to rekindle desire in the ascetic Shiva, is burned to ash by Shiva's third eye and later restored bodiless as Ananga

title: Chaṇḍī Slays Śumbha and Niśumbha
description: The goddess Chaṇḍī/Chaṇḍikā slays the asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha and their generals Chaṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the deed enshrined at Chaṇḍī Devī on Nīl Parvat

title: Compilation of the Suśruta Saṃhitā
description: Suśruta's teaching is preserved as the foundational surgical text, describing instruments, incisions, cataract couching, rhinoplasty, and cadaver anatomy

title: Creation of Lopamudra
description: Fearing his ancestors hang in limbo for want of offspring, Agastya assembles the most beautiful limbs of all creatures and infuses the child into the queen of Vidarbha, born as Lopamudra

title: Cross-tradition identity as Mailāra/Mallanna/Khaṇḍerāo
description: The deity is recognized across the Deccan as a single god under regional names (Mailāralinga, Mallanna, Khaṇḍerāo), with Kannada Mailāra as the older stratum
source: Kannada Mailāra and Telugu Mallanna traditions [folk/regional]; modern scholarship

title: Devāpi and Maru re-establish the kṣatriya dynasties at Kali's close
description: At the end of Kali Yuga, the immortal Devāpi (lunar line) with Maru/Moru (solar Ikṣvāku line) re-emerge from Kalāpa to re-found the kṣatriya dynasties and restore dharma at the dawn of the next Kṛta/Satya Yuga
source: Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.24; Bhāgavata Purāṇa XII.2.37-38, IX.12

title: Devī slays Mahiṣāsura and Śumbha–Niśumbha
description: The Devī Māhātmya narrates the Goddess Durgā slaying the buffalo-demon Mahiṣāsura and the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha

title: Durga assembled from the devas' tejas
description: The supreme warrior Durga is assembled from the combined radiant energy of all the devas to slay Mahishasura

title: Gajendra seized by the crocodile
description: Gajendra, an elephant-king (cursed former king Indradyumna), is seized by the leg by a crocodile (the cursed gandharva Hūhū) while gathering lotuses on Mount Trikūṭa

title: Ganesha wins the race around the parents
description: Set a race to circle the world for a divine fruit, Ganesha circumambulates his parents declaring they are his whole world, winning over Kartikeya

title: Hayagrīva named in the Nārāyaṇīya avatāra roster
description: The Śānti Parva's early avatāra list names Hayaśiras/Hayagrīva as the horse-headed recoverer of the Vedas alongside Haṃsa, Varāha, Narasiṃha, Vāmana

title: Indra slays Triśiras and Vṛtra (Śākta reframing)
description: Indra slays the three-headed Triśiras (Viśvarūpa) and the dragon Vṛtra, then purifies the resulting brahmahatyā guilt through Goddess-worship

title: Indra slays Vṛtra with the Dadhīci-vajra
description: Armed with the vajra forged from Dadhīci's spine, Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra, releasing the cosmic waters and restoring world order; in the Bhāgavata Vṛtra dies a willing devotee and attains liberation

title: King Suratha and merchant Samadhi worship the Devi
description: The dethroned king Suratha and the merchant Samadhi worship the Goddess under the sage Medhas; Suratha is destined to be reborn as the future 8th Savarni Manu

title: Kṛṣṇā issues from the cow-mouth at Mahābaleśvar — Pañcagaṅgā
description: The Kṛṣṇā rises from a stone cow-mouth at Mahābaleśvar as one of five rivers (Pañcagaṅgā) born from the same source

title: Kālī springs from Durgā's brow and slays Raktabīja
description: In the battle with Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa, and Raktabīja, Kālī springs from Durgā's forehead and drinks Raktabīja's cloning blood to win

title: Lakṣmī's pique and departure; Tirumala/Kolhapur sequels
description: Affronted her seat was struck, Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha, settling at Kolhapur while Viṣṇu descends as Śrīnivāsa to Tirumala — the separated-couple frame

title: Lakshmi re-emerges and weds Vishnu
description: The goddess of fortune rises radiant from the ocean and of her own choice garlands and weds Vishnu, restoring sri to the cosmos

title: Madhubani Rama-Sita wedding painting
description: Mithila women paint the Rama-Sita wedding in the kohbar nuptial chamber, Mithila being Sita's homeland, alongside Krishna, Durga and Shiva-Parvati

title: March on Śūnyaka in the Śrīcakra chariots
description: Lalitā rides the nine-tiered Cakra-rāja-ratha, with Mantriṇī on Geya-cakra and Vārāhī on Kiri-cakra, advancing on Bhaṇḍāsura's city

title: Markandeya witnesses the pralaya
description: The deathless Markandeya survives a dissolution, floating on the cosmic waters and seeing the infant Vishnu on the banyan leaf

title: Mārkaṇḍeya's Penance Tested by Kāmadeva
description: Fearing the sage's austerity, Indra sends Kāmadeva, spring and apsarases to break his penance, but Mārkaṇḍeya remains unmoved

title: Muchukunda's service to the devas and boon of sleep
description: The Ikshvaku prince Muchukunda, son of Mandhatri, led the devas' armies in a deva-asura war and on release asked Indra only for undisturbed sleep, with the boon that any waker be burnt by his glance

title: Nahusha usurps Svarga and is cursed
description: During Indra's absence the mortal king Nahusha is crowned regent, lusts after Shachi, and kicks sage Agastya, who curses him to fall as a serpent; Indra is then restored

title: Nandi's curse of Rāvaṇa
description: Barred at Kailāsa and mocked for his face, Nandi curses Rāvaṇa that monkeys will destroy his race and city; Rāvaṇa then tries to lift Kailāsa and is pinned by Śiva's toe

title: Parvati's Penance and Birth of Girijatmaj at Lenyadri
description: Parvati (Girija) performs penance at Lenyadri desiring a son, and Ganesha is born/installed there as Girijatmaja, her own son

title: Prescription of worship and enumeration of pīṭhas
description: The Goddess prescribes external and internal worship (image, mantra, Śrī-cakra, mānasa-pūjā, Navarātri) and enumerates her sacred pīṭhas/kṣetras as the geography of her presence

title: Rāma worships at Kṣīrārāma
description: Rāma is said to have worshipped the milk-white liṅga at Palakollu, giving the deity the name Rāmaliṅgeśvara

title: Rāvaṇānugraha iconographic tradition
description: The legend becomes a canonical sculptural form (Ellora, Elephanta) of Śiva and Pārvatī above the straining demon below
source: Śaiva Āgama/Śilpa iconography; Ellora and Elephanta reliefs [scholarly]

title: Sanatkumāra teaches Nārada the Infinite
description: Sanatkumāra instructs Nārada on bhūman, the Infinite, surpassing all lesser knowledge in the Chāndogya

title: Sanjna flees Surya leaving Chhaya
description: Unable to endure Surya's heat, Sanjna leaves her shadow-double Chhaya in her place and flees as a mare to perform tapas

title: Sarasvati carries the Vadava fire to the ocean
description: Sarasvati is dispatched to bear the world-destroying submarine Vadava-agni into the ocean where it can burn harmlessly, splitting into channels and descending as a river to do it

title: Satī's Earring Falls at Maṇikarṇikā / Viśālākṣī
description: A part of Satī (variously an earring or her eyes) falls at Kashi, establishing the Viśālākṣī Śakti-pīṭha and fusing the cremation-ground with goddess-ground

title: Satī's yoni falls at Kāmākhyā
description: The originating myth of the Kāmākhyā pīṭha: the spot in Kāmrūp, Assam where Satī's yoni fell, becoming the foremost yoginī-pīṭha and a natural yoni-stone cult-image

title: Self-manifestation at Totadri/Vanamamalai
description: Vishnu reclines as Deivanayaga Perumal with Varamangai Nachiyar at the Nanguneri hill-shrine, counted among the eight self-disclosed seats
actors: Vishnu as Deivanayaga Perumal; Varamangai Nachiyar

title: Shiva Splits into Omkara and Amaleshwara at Omkareshwar
description: When the Vindhya mountain worships Shiva and the Devas battle the Danavas, Shiva splits into Omkareshwar and Mamleshwar to save the devotees, founding the Omkareshwar jyotirlinga on the Om-shaped Mandhata island

title: Siddhars enter jiva-samadhi
description: Perfected Siddhars are said not to die but to enter conscious living entombment (jiva-samadhi) at shrines such as Palani, Marutamalai and Madurai, remaining present across the Kali age

title: Skanda made general and slays Tārakāsura
description: Anointed Devasenāpati and armed with the Vel, the boy Skanda leads the devas and kills the otherwise-invincible Tārakāsura, fulfilling his birth-purpose
source: Skanda Purāṇa, Matsya Purāṇa, Mahābhārata Vana Parva

title: Slaying of Raktabīja
description: Kālī drinks every drop of the demon Raktabīja's blood mid-air, preventing the clones his blood spawns, so the bloodless original collapses dead

title: Solar and lunar dynasty genealogies
description: Sūrya- and Candra-vaṃśa king-lists (vaṃśa/vaṃśānucarita lakṣaṇas) from the Manus through the heroes of the present age

title: The conch passes to Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa; etiology of the worship-conch
description: The demon's substance becomes the sacred śaṅkha of Viṣṇu-worship and his conch-jewel folds into Kṛṣṇa's regalia, closing the Sudāmā arc

title: The Fruit-of-Wisdom Race and Murugan's Renunciation at Palani
description: In Narada's fruit contest Ganesha wins by circling his parents while Murugan races the world; the slighted Murugan storms off to Palani as the renunciate Dandayudhapani

title: The Goddess remains as guardian-maiden of the cape
description: Her task complete, Kanyākumārī stays at the subcontinent's tip as the eternal virgin facing the sea, absorbed in perpetual tapas

title: The gods arm Durga weapon by weapon
description: Each god gives Durga a replica of his own weapon or emblem, and Himavan gives her the lion as mount

title: The gods dig Nakki Lake
description: Folk etymology holds the heart-shaped Nakki Lake was scooped out by gods with their fingernails (nakh) in one night to confront the demon Bāskali

title: The Kālī dance-contest and ūrdhva-tāṇḍava
description: Śiva subdues the fierce goddess Kālī by performing the raised-leg ūrdhva-tāṇḍava she cannot modestly copy, winning the contest at Tillai/Cidambaram

title: The sacred fires teach Upakosala
description: The neglected pupil Upakosala is taught by the three sacred fires that prāṇa, joy and space are Brahman, and shown the path of the gods (devayāna)

title: The silver-hall (Sandhyā) dance
description: Śiva dances the evening Sandhyā Tāṇḍava in Madurai's Veḷḷi/Rajata Sabhai with his right foot raised, mirror of Chidambaram's left

title: The Vindhyavāsinī promise in the Nārāyaṇī-stuti
description: In Devī Māhātmya ch. 11 the Devī names Vindhyavāsinī among her promised future manifestations alongside Raktadantikā, Śākambharī, Bhīmā, Bhrāmarī

title: The womb-vow of liberation
description: In anguish the soul vows that, if delivered from the womb, it will resort to Sāṃkhya-Yoga / Nārāyaṇa-Maheśvara to attain liberation
actors: the soul in the womb; Nārāyaṇa/Maheśvara invoked

title: Tilottamā destroys Sunda and Upasunda
description: Fashioned by Viśvakarmā from the finest particle of every beautiful thing, Tilottamā is created to destroy the invincible asura brothers Sunda and Upasunda, who fight each other to death over her

title: Tripura-dahana, slaying of Jalandhara, and burning of Kama
description: Shiva burns the three flying cities of Tripura, slays Jalandhara, and reduces Kama to ash with his third eye

title: Tripurāntaka — destruction of the three cities
description: Śiva incinerates the three flying fortresses of Tāraka's sons (Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa) with a single arrow when the cities align, the whole cosmos serving as his weapon
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā, Liṅga Purāṇa, Matsya Purāṇa, Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva

title: Śukra bans wine for brahmins
description: Disgusted at being tricked through liquor, Śukra decrees that no brahmin shall henceforth drink intoxicants, an etiological first prohibition

title: Vidagdha Śākalya's head shatters
description: In the final debate Yājñavalkya turns examiner; unable to name Yājñavalkya's ultimate support, Vidagdha Śākalya's head shatters and robbers carry off his bones

title: Vishnu Gains Siddhi at Siddhatek
description: Vishnu worships Ganesha at Siddhatek to gain the siddhi (perfection) needed to defeat the demons Madhu and Kaitabha

title: Vishnu's maya-moha deludes the asuras
description: Vishnu emanates a deceiver (read as a proto-Buddha figure) to seduce the asuras from the Veda so the gods can defeat them

title: Vishvamitra Composes the Gayatri Mantra
description: The seer Vishvamitra composes the Gayatri/Savitri verse to Savitr in the gayatri metre, which becomes the most revered Vedic mantra and is personified as the goddess Gayatri

title: Annapūrṇā Feeds the Begging Śiva
description: In the Kashi myth Śiva himself begs alms from the bowl of the goddess Annapūrṇā, the deity of renunciation accepting food from the deity of abundance

title: Bhṛgu's authorship — Bhṛgu Saṃhitā and Manu Smṛti
description: Bhṛgu is the reputed compiler of the astrological Bhṛgu Saṃhitā and the reciter of Manu's dharma in the Manu Smṛti

title: Birth of the Ashvins from Surya and Sanjna
description: The twin horse-headed Ashvin physicians are conceived when Surya, as a stallion, reunites with Sanjna as a mare

title: Bālā slays the sons of Bhaṇḍāsura
description: The nine-year-old Bālā Tripurasundarī insists on fighting and singlehandedly destroys Bhaṇḍāsura's thirty sons

title: Cāmpāṣaṣṭhī festival commemoration
description: The six-day Cāmpāṣaṣṭhī festival at Jejuri annually commemorates the slaying of the demons with turmeric-showering

title: Dakṣa's curse of perpetual wandering
description: After Nārada persuades Dakṣa's sons to renounce procreation, the furious Dakṣa curses him to ceaseless roving, an etiology for the wandering-sage archetype

title: Death of Niśumbha and Śumbha
description: The Goddess reabsorbs all the Mātṛkās into herself and slays the asura brothers Niśumbha and Śumbha in single combat, restoring heaven to the gods

title: Durga slays Mahishasura's generals
description: Durga annihilates Mahishasura's army and slays his generals Chikshura, Chamara, Udagra, Mahahanu and others

title: Durga slays the asura Durgama
description: In the Shatakshi/Shakambhari episode, the Goddess slays the asura Durgama, an etymon of her name Durga

title: Forgetting at birth by the Vaiṣṇava wind
description: At birth the newborn is struck by the vaiṣṇava-vāyu (cosmic illusory wind) and forgets its past lives and its resolve, re-entering worldly life in ignorance

title: Gajendra-mokṣa — Viṣṇu rescues the elephant-king
description: After a thousand-year struggle Gajendra cries to Viṣṇu, who flies in on Garuḍa, beheads the crocodile with the Sudarśana-cakra, and grants Gajendra sārūpya-mukti

title: Ganesha curses the moon
description: After Candra mocks his burst belly, the furious Ganesha decrees that whoever looks at the moon on his festival day will be falsely accused

title: Ganesha Defeats Vighnasura at Ozar
description: Ganesha defeats the demon Vighnasura (created by Indra to wreck King Abhinandana's sacrifice), sparing him on condition he trouble no worshippers, becoming Vighneshvara

title: Ganesha Slays Vighnasura at Ozar
description: Ganesha as Vigneshwar slays the demon Vighnasura, founding the gold-domed Ashtavinayaka shrine at Ozar

title: Hayagrīva in the Bhāgavata 24-avatāra list
description: Hayagrīva is added with Haṃsa to extend the Bhāgavata līlā-avatāra enumeration to twenty-four; not part of the fixed Daśāvatāra

title: Idumban Carries the Twin Hills (Origin of Kavadi)
description: Murugan's disciple Idumban carries twin hills on a kavadi yoke at Palani, the origin of the kavadi-bearing pilgrimage tradition

title: Jāmbavān recognises Rāma reborn (Rāmāyaṇa bridge)
description: Jāmbavān realises his opponent is the Supreme Lord he once served as Rāma and submits, giving the gem and his daughter

title: Kanyākumārī fixed as a Śakti Pīṭha
description: In the 51 Śakti Pīṭha scheme, Satī's back/spine fell at the cape, enshrining Śakti Śarvāṇī with Bhairava Nimiṣa, layering the Pīṭha stratum onto the virgin-warrior myth
actors: Satī; Śiva; Śakti Śarvāṇī; Bhairava Nimiṣa

title: Kṛṣṇa re-transmits the Haṃsa teaching to Uddhava
description: At the Dvāpara–Kali cusp, Kṛṣṇa recounts the ancient swan-dialogue to Uddhava as primordial wisdom, giving the Uddhava Gītā its alternate name Haṃsa Gītā

title: Kṛṣṇa's boon — worship as Śyām in Kali Yuga
description: Kṛṣṇa blesses Barbarīka to be worshipped under Kṛṣṇa's own name Śyām in Kali Yuga, the charter of the later cult

title: Kālī halted upon the supine Śiva
description: Kālī's battle-rampage is halted only when Śiva lies in her path; she steps on him and bites her tongue in abashment, expressing Śakti as dynamic and Śiva as the still ground

title: Kāmadahana — burning of Kāma
description: Śiva opens his third eye and burns the love-god Kāmadeva to ash for disturbing his meditation; later restored bodiless (Ananga) at Rati's plea
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā, Matsya Purāṇa, Kumārasaṃbhava

title: Marriage of Agastya and Lopamudra
description: Grown Lopamudra consents to wed the poverty-sworn ascetic Agastya, sheds her royal silks for bark, and follows him into the forest

title: Marriage of Shiva and Parvati
description: After Parvati's penance, the divine wedding of Shiva and Parvati follows, prerequisite to the births of their sons

title: Maya's cross-yuga persistence
description: Never slain by an avatāra, Maya recurs as the asura world's permanent engineer across Satya, Treta and Dvāpara — effectively chiranjivi-like

title: Mārkaṇḍeya's Boon to Behold Māyā
description: After ages of austerity, Mārkaṇḍeya asks Nārāyaṇa not for a gift but to behold the Lord's illusory potency that creates and dissolves the universe

title: Murugan slays Sūrapadman
