description: In the Tamil cycle Murugan hurls the Vel and splits the demon Sūrapadman in two, whose halves become his peacock mount and rooster banner

title: Mutual curses of Kacha and Devayānī
description: Kacha refuses to marry Devayānī, declaring her his sister; she curses that the stolen vidyā will fail in his hands and he counter-curses that no sage's son will marry her, driving her to wed King Yayāti

title: Nachiketā visits Yama's realm and returns
description: The boy Nāciketa visits the realm of Yama and returns with knowledge of the afterlife and of right gifting, a Mahābhārata recension of the Kaṭha Upaniṣad tale

title: Nandikeśvara as lord and transmitter of music and dance
description: Nandi keeps time for Śiva's Tāṇḍava and is venerated as master of saṅgīta and nṛtya, presiding over the heavenly arts

title: Parable of the yakṣa and Umā Haimavatī
description: The gods Agni, Vāyu, and Indra boast of victory until a mysterious yakṣa (Brahman), revealed by the goddess Umā Haimavatī, humbles them, showing their power is borrowed

title: Paraśurāma breaks Gaṇeśa's tusk (Ekadanta)
description: Barred at Śiva's gate by Gaṇeśa, Paraśurāma hurls Śiva's own axe; Gaṇeśa refuses to nullify his father's weapon and loses his left tusk, becoming Ekadanta

title: Pravāhaṇa Jaivali teaches the Five Fires
description: The Pāñcāla king Pravāhaṇa Jaivali poses five unanswerable questions to Śvetaketu and Uddālaka, then teaches the pañcāgni-vidyā and the two paths (devayāna/pitṛyāna) of rebirth

title: Pārvatī transmits the Lāsya to women
description: Pārvatī teaches the tender feminine Lāsya to women (Uṣā, thence the women of Dvārakā), founding the feminine solo-dance lineage

title: Ramopakhyana retold in the Pandava forest
description: The Mahabharata's Rama-narrative compresses the Dandaka exile and abduction, told to Yudhishthira within the Pandava exile-forest, linking the two great vanavasas

title: Reṇukā beheading etiology of the Māri head
description: Paraśurāma beheads and restores Reṇukā with a head-and-body swap, the Treta-yuga myth used to explain the fierce severed-head Māri/Yellammā icon of the kali-historical cult
source: Mahābhārata/Purāṇa Reṇukā tale; South Indian folk variants

title: Satī's self-immolation at Dakṣa's yajña creates the pīṭhas
description: Satī, born as Dakṣa's daughter, immolates herself at his sacrifice; in the Śākta telling her scattered body creates the Śakti Pīṭhas

title: Shukra obtains the Mritasanjivani vidya from Shiva
description: Through severe tapas Shukra obtains from Shiva the Mritasanjivani, the science of reviving the dead, with which he keeps resurrecting slain asuras against the devas

title: Srikalahasti Kalamkari temple narratives
description: Kalamkari pen-artists draw freehand Ramayana, Mahabharata and Krishna-lila friezes in vegetable dyes as temple cloth-hangings

title: Surya's seven-horsed chariot turns northward (Ratha Saptami)
description: On Magha Shukla Saptami the Sun-god's seven-horsed chariot turns decisively northward, marking Surya's birthday and awakening, observed with arka-leaf bathing

title: Sāvitrī's curse turns the gods into the Pañcagaṅgā rivers
description: Angered Sāvitrī curses the gods so that Viṣṇu, Śiva and Brahmā become the Kṛṣṇā, Kōynā and Veṇī streams

title: The Ānanda Tāṇḍava at Chidambaram
description: For the sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada, and after defeating the goddess Kali in a dance-contest, Shiva performs the Dance of Bliss in the golden hall, enacting the five cosmic acts of creation, preservation, destruction, concealment and grace

title: The Skandapurāṇa Vindhyavāsinī war-cycle
description: In the early Skandapurāṇa the goddess takes the Vindhya as her seat, gathers fierce attendants, and wages war on the buffalo/Śumbha-class demons—an oldest full Goddess-war account feeding the Devī Māhātmya

title: Tripurāntaka — destruction of the three flying cities
description: Śiva mounts a cosmic chariot built from all the gods and looses a single arrow that incinerates the three indestructible flying cities (Tripura) of the asura brothers at the one aligned instant
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Liṅga Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva

title: Vishnu svayam-vyakta seat at Pushkara
description: The Pushkara lake-tirtha, foremost where all gods reside, is counted a Vishnu self-manifest seat (Varaha/Veni-Madhava) despite its Brahma dominance

title: Viṣṇu's war on the rākṣasas; slaying of Mālī and flight to Pātāla
description: Grown arrogant from Brahmā's boons, the three brothers harry the devas; Viṣṇu wars on them, kills Mālī with his discus, and Mālyavān and Sumālī flee to Pātāla, abandoning Laṅkā to Kubera

title: Birth of Dridhasyu
description: Agastya and Lopamudra beget the son Dridhasyu (Idhmavaha), who chants the Vedas from the womb, releasing the ancestors from limbo

title: Birth of Ganesha and the elephant head
description: Parvati fashions Ganesha from her body to guard her door; Shiva beheads him in fury and replaces his head with an elephant's, making him lord of the ganas and remover of obstacles

title: Cheriyal scrolls of the caste-Puranas
description: Nakashi painters create vertical narrative scrolls of the Markandeya-purana and epic episodes for bard-communities who sing them village to village

title: Cyavana shares the fate of the netted fish
description: The sage Cyavana, caught in a fisherman's net, insists on sharing the fate and value of the fish, teaching the worth of all life and the dharma of the Niṣādas

title: Divakara Muni and the Mischievous Boy at Ananta-kadu
description: A divine boy defiles the sage Divakara Muni's shalagrama and vanishes into Ananta-kadu forest, where an ilappa tree falls and transforms into the colossal reclining Vishnu of Padmanabhasvami

title: Durga beheads the shape-shifting Mahishasura
description: Mahishasura morphs through buffalo, lion, man, and elephant forms; Durga pins the buffalo, pierces its neck, and beheads the demon as he emerges from its mouth, becoming Mahishasuramardini

title: Durga slays Mahishasura (Madhyama-carita)
description: The gods' combined splendor coalesces into Durga, who rides her lion and destroys the buffalo-demon Mahishasura — the Mahishasuramardini episode

title: Gautama Brings Down the Godāvarī
description: Sage Gautama, atoning for the accidental death of a cow, uses a tuft of Ganga's hair (or Shiva's gift) to bring down the Godavari at Tryambakeshvar

title: Kaikasī sent to seduce Viśravas
description: Sumālī sends his daughter Kaikasī to win the sage Viśravas to breed a champion who could overthrow Kubera, producing Rāvaṇa and his siblings

title: Kali springs from Chandi's brow to slay Raktabija
description: Kali springs from the wrathful Chandi's furrowed brow and drinks the blood of Raktabija

title: Kamakhya's annual menstruation (Ambubachi Mela)
description: The Kamakhya Shakti Peetha (where Sati's yoni fell) closes for three days marking the goddess's annual menstruation, then reopens, the rite sacralizing menstruation as cosmic fertility

title: Kanyā-tīrtha in the Mahābhārata pilgrimage-tour
description: The Mahābhārata's tīrtha-yātrā names a Kanyā/Kumārī tīrtha at the far southern shore among the holy bathing-places, attesting the virgin-goddess cape's antiquity

title: Ketu Granted Planetary Status at Keezhaperumpallam
description: The headless serpent-body Ketu worships Shiva at Keezhaperumpallam and is blessed with planetary status, fixing the spot as the Ketu parihara

title: Kālāntaka — Mārkaṇḍeya saved from Yama
description: Śiva bursts from the liṅga as Ender-of-Death to strike down Yama and grant the boy-devotee Mārkaṇḍeya deathless eternal youth at sixteen
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Skanda Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa

title: Left as protector of Parikshit at the Great Departure
description: As the Pandavas renounce the world and install Parikshit, Yuyutsu the senior Kuru survivor is left as steward-protector of the young king's realm, bridging Dvapara's end into the Kali age

title: Manifestation of Mahā-Gaṇapati against the obstacle-yantra
description: To counter Viṣukra's paralyzing Jaya-vighna yantra, the Goddess manifests Mahā-Gaṇapati, who shatters the obstacle and clears the army's path

title: Marriages of Kārtikeya to Devasenā and Vaḷḷi
description: Skanda weds the army-bride Devasenā given by Indra and the hill-tribe love-bride Vaḷḷi, wooed in disguise with Gaṇeśa's help

title: Murugan Imprisons Brahma and Teaches Om to Shiva at Swamimalai
description: Having imprisoned Brahma for failing to explain Pranava (Om), Murugan expounds Om to Shiva himself, becoming the guru of his own father as Swaminatha

title: Nala loses his kingdom to Kali's possession
description: Possessed by the demon Kali, Nala gambles away his kingdom to his brother Pushkara and is exiled with Damayanti

title: Narration framed by Śiva to Pārvatī
description: The whole discourse is transmitted as Śiva narrating the secret Rāma-story to Pārvatī, who reports Rāma's words to Lakṣmaṇa

title: Parable of the dog transformed into ever-fiercer beasts
description: A ṛṣi's pet dog is successively transformed into fiercer beasts for protection until it turns on its master and is reduced again to a dog, a parable against raising the base to high station

title: Pradyumna as the third Pāñcarātra vyūha
description: In Pāñcarātra theology Pradyumna is the third of the four eternal vyūhas (Vāsudeva-Saṅkarṣaṇa-Pradyumna-Aniruddha), correlated with manas and the creative principle
source: Nārāyaṇīya (Mahābhārata Śānti Parva); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.5.29-30; Pāñcarātra Āgamas

title: Pramlocā and the 907-year tapas of Kandu
description: Sent to break rishi Kandu's world-scorching penance, Pramlocā lives with him 907 years; when banished, her foetus exudes as sweat onto the trees, becoming Māriṣā, later mother of Dakṣa

title: Raibhya Ṛṣi's Penance and Naming of Rishikesh
description: The sage Raibhya performs severe tapasya on the Gaṅgā bank; pleased, Nārāyaṇa appears on a mango branch and boons to remain there as Hṛṣīkeśa Nārāyaṇa, giving the place its name Rishikesh

title: Recovery of self-manifest Badarinarayana at Badari
description: The self-formed shaligrama Badarinarayana murti, tapas-seat of Nara-Narayana, is disclosed/recovered from the Narada-kunda in the Alaknanda
actors: Vishnu as Badarinarayana; Nara-Narayana; (Shankaracharya in legend)

title: Sanatkumāra teaches Nārada the Bhūman
description: The sorrowing Nārada, knowing only texts, asks Sanatkumāra to lead him across; Sanatkumāra ascends a ladder of faculties to the infinite Bhūman, the bliss that is the Self

title: Shiva Destroys Tripurasura as Bhima at Bhimashankar
description: Shiva manifests as Bhima to destroy the demon Tripurasura tormenting the devotee-king Kamarupeshwar, and the sweat of the fierce battle becomes the Bhima river, founding the Bhimashankar jyotirlinga

title: Shiva Worships Ganesha Before Destroying Tripurasura at Ranjangaon
description: Shiva worships Ganesha at Ranjangaon before marching to destroy the three flying cities of Tripurasura, inverting the usual order with the great god propitiating his own son

title: Shiva Worships Ganesha Before Fighting Tripurasura
description: At Ranjangaon Shiva worships the powerful Mahaganapati form of Ganesha before going to battle the demon Tripurasura

title: Six disciples question Pippalāda
description: Six seekers question the sage Pippalāda on creation, prāṇa, sleep, the syllable Oṃ, and the person of sixteen parts

title: Tarakasura's boon of restricted death
description: The asura Tarakasura wins from Brahma that he can be slain only by a true son of Shiva, counting on the widowed ascetic Shiva never fathering one

title: The Devī Gītā delivered to Himavat
description: The Goddess Bhuvaneśvarī instructs Himavat and the gods, revealing her Virāṭ universal form and expounding nondual Brahman, māyā, yoga, and her worship — the Śākta analogue of the Bhagavad Gītā

title: The Kacha-Devayani episode
description: Brihaspati's son Kacha infiltrates as Shukra's disciple to learn the vidya; killed repeatedly and finally fed to Shukra in wine, he learns the mantra from inside Shukra's belly, bursts forth and revives Shukra, then mutual curses follow including Devayani's curse to marry a non-brahmin

title: The knower-of-the-body and the internal fires
description: The text closes by turning from the body's anatomy to the kṣetrajña (knower within) and the internal fires that sustain life, framing embryology as self-knowledge

title: The Pralaya Deluge Engulfs the World
description: The cosmic dissolution suddenly floods all worlds as the seven oceans merge, leaving Mārkaṇḍeya the sole survivor tossed on endless waters

title: Tāpī created from Sūrya's own heat
description: Sūrya fashions his daughter Tāpī from his excessive heat to provide a cooling presence; she becomes the westward river

title: Vishnu becomes Mohini and serves nectar to the devas
description: The asuras seize the amrita, but Vishnu assumes the enchantress Mohini, bewitches them into surrendering the pot, and serves the nectar only to the devas

title: Viṣṇu deludes the Tripura asuras
description: Before the Tripura war Viṣṇu, as a heretic teacher or Buddha-like preacher, seduces the Tripura asuras away from dharma to make them vulnerable to Śiva's arrow

title: Vrishabha slays the netherworld demons
description: Shiva assumes a bull-form to descend into Patala and slay the degenerate sons who terrorized the netherworld

title: Yama, First Mortal to Die, Becomes Lord of the Dead
description: Yama, the first mortal to die, becomes the path-finder of the dead and benevolent lord of the ancestral realm (Pitrloka), gathering the dead to a heavenly pasture

title: Yoga Upaniṣads bridge classical Upaniṣads to Haṭha/Tantra
description: Their chakra, nāḍī, kuṇḍalinī, bandha, mudrā and nāda system, rooted in Kaṭha/Śvetāśvatara/Maitrī and the Yoga darśana, becomes the direct scriptural ancestor of the Haṭha manuals and Tantric subtle-body theory
source: Kaṭha, Śvetāśvatara, Maitrī Ups.; Yoga-sūtra; Haṭha-yoga-pradīpikā; Gheraṇḍa-saṃhitā; Śiva-saṃhitā

title: Ahimsa Paramo Dharmah spoken to Ruru
description: A serpent-brahmin teaches the sage Ruru that non-violence is the highest dharma, the maxim recurring across the Mahabharata

title: Avatara of Vakratunda slaying Matsarasura
description: Ganesha descends as Vakratunda to slay Matsarasura, the demon personifying envy, an allegory of conquering jealousy

title: Beheading of Svarbhanu and origin of Rahu and Ketu
description: The asura Svarbhanu disguises as a deva to drink the nectar; Surya and Chandra expose him and Mohini severs his head with the Sudarshana Chakra, but the nectar-touched head and body become the immortal eclipse-causers Rahu and Ketu

title: Bhadrakali born from Shiva's wrath at the Daksha-yajna
description: The variant Kali form Bhadrakali is born from Shiva's wrath at Daksha's sacrifice

title: Birth of Kartikeya and slaying of Tarakasura
description: Shiva's fiery seed, passed through Agni and Ganga to the Krittikas, is born as the six-faced Kartikeya/Skanda, who as war-general slays the invincible demon Tarakasura

title: Birth of Skanda and slaying of Taraka (Vamana telling)
description: Shiva's seed borne by Agni, Ganga and the Krittikas generates six-faced Skanda, consecrated commander of the gods, who slays the boon-protected Taraka

title: Curse and Disappearance of the Sarasvatī River
description: The Sarasvati is cursed to sink into the desert and goes underground, reappearing only at named tirthas such as Prabhasa and Kurukshetra

title: Devi slays Shumbha, Nishumbha and Raktabija (Uttama-carita)
description: The Goddess campaigns against Shumbha and Nishumbha and their generals Dhumralochana and Chanda-Munda, and Kali drinks the blood of Raktabija, capped by the Devi's declaration of supremacy

title: Durga slays Mahishasura (Navaratri/Dussehra)
description: Durga, forged from the combined tejas of the devas, battles the buffalo-demon Mahishasura over nine nights and beheads him, commemorated by Navaratri and Vijayadashami

title: Fall of Viṣukra and Viṣaṅga and the demon army
description: Vārāhī and the Nityās overcome Bhaṇḍāsura's brothers and forces, defeating their illusion-engines and revived-asura weapons with superior Daśāvatāra-astras

title: Indra and Virocana learn the Self from Prajāpati
description: Gods and demons send Indra and Virocana to Prajāpati, who tests them over a 101-year discipleship through four answers; Virocana settles for the bodily self while Indra persists to the true bodiless Self

title: Indra assumes many forms through his mayas
description: In the Rigveda, Indra wields maya as wonder-working power, assuming many forms, the earliest Vedic sense of maya as creative potency

title: Krishna revives Parikshit; the line preserved
description: Krishna revives the dead-born child Parikshit, who succeeds to Hastinapura and continues the Kuru dynasty into the Kali Yuga; Ashvatthaman is cursed to deathless wandering
source: Mahabharata, Sauptika & Ashvamedhika Parvas; Bhagavata Purana 1.8-1.12

title: Krishna's dehotsarga (departure from the world)
description: Krishna casts off his body at the Prabhasa Triveni (Dehotsarga), returning to his transcendent abode and ending the Dvapara Yuga at the Dvapara-Kali hinge

title: Kundalini revealed by Shiva to the Goddess
description: The subtle-body anatomy of nadis, chakras, and the coiled serpent-power is revealed by Shiva to the Goddess as the body's eternal map

title: Kāśyapa-gotra as universal fallback
description: In gotra-tradition anyone without a known gotra is assigned the Kāśyapa gotra, since Kaśyapa is the father of all beings

title: Manasā Tends Śiva After the Hālāhala
description: The serpent-goddess Manasā, destroyer of poison, is assimilated to Śaiva myth as the one who tended Śiva after he drank the Hālāhala poison

title: Mataris­van brings fire to humans
description: When fire was hidden from humans, Matarisvan stole/fetched Agni from heaven and gave him to the Bhrigus, who established sacrificial fire among the clans of men

title: Music section and Pāśupata-Śaiva lore
description: Early Purāṇic treatise on music (svaras, grāmas, mūrcchanās, tāla) plus the Lakulīśa/Māheśvara yogeśvaras, the Śiva incarnations founding the Pāśupata school

title: Nachiketa's Three Boons from Yama
description: Given to Death by his father's angry word, the boy Nachiketa waits three nights at Yama's house and receives three boons, including Yama's teaching of the secret of the Atman beyond death

title: Nalinika seduces Isisinga (Buddhist Jataka parallel)
description: In the Nalinika Jataka the horned ascetic Isisinga, born of a doe, is seduced and his ascetic power broken by the king's daughter Nalinika disguised as a young ascetic, sent by Sakka

title: Nārada as bhakti author and Purāṇa namesake
description: Tradition ascribes to Nārada the Nārada Bhakti Sūtra defining devotion as supreme love of God, and casts the Nārada Purāṇa as his Vaiṣṇava discourse

title: Nārada initiates Dhruva and counsels Vyāsa
description: As guru-bhakta he initiates Dhruva into Viṣṇu-worship and counsels Vyāsa to compose the Bhāgavata, embodying the nāma-saṅkīrtana ideal

title: Parvati scorches Kubera's eye
description: In a folk Shaiva variant, Kubera gazes enviously at Parvati and her glance scorches one of his eyes yellow, making him Ekakshipingala, the one tawny-eyed

title: Pichwai hangings behind Shrinathji at Nathdwara
description: Large cloth pichwai are hung behind the child-Krishna Shrinathji icon, their subjects fixed by the Vallabha Pushtimarga festival-calendar

title: Reunion of Nala and Damayanti
description: Transformed by the naga Karkotaka into the dwarf Bahuka, Nala exchanges dice-lore for horse-lore with Rituparna, expels Kali, and reunites with Damayanti, winning back his kingdom

title: Rāvaṇānugraha-mūrti iconographic tradition
description: The episode becomes a canonical Śaiva sculptural form — Śiva and Pārvatī atop Kailāsa with Rāvaṇa straining beneath — famously at Ellora and Elephanta
source: Śaiva Āgama/Śilpa iconography; Ellora & Elephanta reliefs

title: Sage Gautama Brings Down the Godavari at Trimbakeshwar
description: Falsely accused of killing a maya-cow, sage Gautama brings the Ganga down as the Godavari to purify the sin, and Shiva remains as the three-faced Trimbakeshwar jyotirlinga

title: Sage Shvetashvatara Teaches the Upanishad
description: The eponymous sage Shvetashvatara, by the power of his austerity and God's grace, sees and declares the supreme purifying knowledge to the assembly of renunciate seers, transmitting it as a guarded teaching

title: Shiva burns Kama and is won by Parvati's tapas
description: The devas send Kama to fire desire at the meditating Shiva; Shiva burns him to ash with his third eye, but Parvati's long tapas eventually wins him

title: Shumbha and Nishumbha usurp heaven
description: The asura brothers Shumbha and Nishumbha seize the cosmos and strip the gods of their shares of sacrifice

title: The Child Vishnu on the Banyan Leaf
description: Amid the flood Mārkaṇḍeya sees a luminous infant (Bāla-Mukunda) resting on a banyan leaf, sucking his toe

title: The Yama-Yami Dialogue
description: The twins Yama and Yami hold their famous incest dialogue, with Yama refusing his sister's advances

title: Tāpatī weds Saṃvaraṇa and bears Kuru
description: The river-goddess Tāpatī marries king Saṃvaraṇa, united by Vasiṣṭha, and bears Kuru, eponym of the Kuru dynasty

title: Uddalaka teaches Shvetaketu 'Tat Tvam Asi'
description: The teacher Uddalaka instructs his son Shvetaketu nine times that 'That Thou Art,' delivering the great Samavedic mahavakya

title: Śukra's penance to Śiva and rebirth as semen
description: Śukra performs extreme tapas to Śiva at Kāśī; pleased, Śiva swallows him and expels him as semen (śukra), fixing his name and granting him the Mṛtasañjīvanī mantra

title: Variant disputes over the boundary member
description: Recensions differ over Naimisha vs Salagrama as the northern pole and over substituting Pushkara, while the Garuda-Padma roster keeps both/all
source: Garuda Purana; Padma Purana; Vaishnava mahatmya recensions

title: Varuna teaches Bhrigu to know Brahman (Bhrigu Valli)
description: Sage Varuna gives his son Bhrigu the definition of Brahman, and through tapas Bhrigu realizes Brahman successively as anna, prana, manas, vijnana, and finally ananda

title: Vishvamitra reveals the Gayatri Mantra
description: The seer Vishvamitra perceives and reveals the Gayatri Mantra addressed to Savitr, the most revered Vedic mantra

title: Vyāsa as chiranjīvi and Kuru counsellor
description: A deathless chiranjīvi, Vyāsa advises the Kurus, grants Sañjaya divine sight and Gāndhārī her hundred sons, and raises the war-dead from the Gaṅgā for one night

title: Yatinatha tests the Bhil devotees
description: As an ascetic guest Shiva tests the hospitality of the tribal Ahuka and Ahuka, rewarding their sacrifice of self for a guest

title: Agastya Brings the Kāverī to the South
description: Sage Agastya brings the Kaveri south by releasing her from his kamandalu, often via Ganesha-as-crow tipping the pot, sourcing the river at Talakaveri

title: Agni hides in the waters and plants
description: Weary of his consuming role, Agni hides in the waters and plants; the gods search and he is betrayed by aquatic creatures and revealed, whereupon he curses those who disclosed him

title: Alambusa seduces Isisinga (Buddhist Jataka parallel)
description: In the Alambusa Jataka Sakka sends the nymph Alambusa to seduce Isisinga; he falls but then recovers his ascetic resolve

title: Ashvins Rescue Bhujyu and Rejuvenate Cyavana
description: The twin physician-horsemen Ashvins rescue the shipwrecked Bhujyu and restore the aged sage Cyavana, performing their characteristic healing and rescue miracles

title: Avadhuta humbles Indra
description: The naked wandering renunciate form of Shiva humbles Indra, who blocked his path, by paralyzing the king of gods to teach ego-dissolution

title: Avatara of Ekadanta slaying Madasura
description: Ganesha descends as Ekadanta to slay Madasura, demon of arrogance/conceit

title: Bhīmā springs from Śiva's sweat after the Tripura slaying
description: The Bhīmā river rises at Bhīmāśaṅkar from Śiva's sweat after he destroys the demon Tripura/Bhīma

title: Birth of Hariharaputra (Ayyappa) to Slay Mahishi
description: Because the demoness Mahishi can be killed only by a child of both Hari and Hara, Vishnu takes the Mohini form, unites with Shiva, and Hariharaputra (Ayyappa) is born

title: Birth of Kaushiki from Parvati's sheath
description: From Parvati's bodily sheath emerges the radiant Ambika/Kaushiki, while Parvati's remainder darkens into Kalika (Kalaratri)

title: Chamunda slays Chanda and Munda
description: Kali earns the name Chamunda by slaying the asura generals Chanda and Munda

title: Charter of Tulsi-Vivaha and the city Jalandhar
description: The myth grounds the Tulsi-Vivaha festival, daily Tulsi/shalagrama worship, and the naming of Jalandhar as a Shakti Pitha
source: Padma Purana; festival and sthala-purana tradition

title: Dawn of the New Satya Yuga
description: With the wicked gone, survivors' minds turn crystal-pure; Satya returns when Moon, Sun and Jupiter enter Pushya together

title: Gajāsura-saṃhāra
description: Śiva slays the elephant-demon Gajāsura, son of Mahiṣāsura, and wears his flayed hide, becoming Kṛttivāsas, the hide-clad one
source: Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Kūrma Purāṇa

title: Mārkaṇḍeya Inhaled into the Cosmic Body
description: The child inhales Mārkaṇḍeya, who sees the entire universe within, then is exhaled back onto the cosmic ocean

title: Origin of Ganesha (Vamana telling)
description: The elephant-headed son of Parvati is given an origin-account and made lord of obstacles and chief of the ganas

title: Origin of Jagannatha at Puri
description: King Indradyumna founds the worship of Jagannatha at Puri from the daru-brahman (log-deity), whose images are left unfinished

title: Pampā weds Śiva as Virūpākṣa (Pampā-kṣetra naming)
description: The river-goddess Pampā/Pampāvatī performs tapas on Hemakūṭa hill and wins Śiva as Virūpākṣa; from her the place is named Pampā-kṣetra, whence 'Hampi' — the Śaiva-Śākta layer beneath the Rāmāyaṇa geography

title: Shiva's seed carried to the Sharavana reeds
description: Shiva's fiery seed, too potent for any womb, is carried by Agni then Ganga, who deposits it in a thicket of Shara reeds

title: Slaying of Bhaṇḍāsura and burning of Śūnyaka
description: Lalitā looses the Mahā-Kāmeśvarāstra, reducing Bhaṇḍāsura and his City of the Void to ash

title: The cat Lomaśa and mouse Palita's expedient alliance
description: A wise mouse and a cat caught in a hunter's snare form a temporary alliance against common enemies; the mouse frees the cat at the last instant, teaching expedient alliance with an enemy under necessity

title: Tripura-dahana (burning of the three cities)
description: Three asura brothers win three indestructible flying cities; mounting a cosmic chariot built of the gods, Shiva incinerates all three Tripura with a single arrow

title: Union of Shiva and Mohini producing Ayyappa
description: In a sequel Shiva asks to see Mohini and, enchanted, their union produces Ayyappa/Hariharaputra (Shasta)

title: Yājñavalkya–Gārgī debate at Janaka's court
description: At King Janaka's court the philosopher Gārgī Vācaknavī challenges Yājñavalkya in debate over the ground of all being

title: Ajamila saved by uttering 'Narayana'
description: The fallen brahmana Ajamila is saved at death by calling his son's name 'Narayana,' the locus classicus for the power of the divine name

title: Andhaka-vadha
description: Andhaka, born of Shiva's sweat, lusts after Parvati; Shiva impales him on the trident while the Matrikas drink his cloning blood, and the chastened Andhaka becomes the gana Bhringi
source: Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita, Yuddha-khanda); cf. Kurma/Linga Purana

title: Andhakāsura-vadha
description: Śiva impales the blind demon Andhaka, who lusted after his unknowing mother Pārvatī; the Mātṛkās drink his cloning blood and he is redeemed as the gaṇa-chief Bhṛṅgi
source: Matsya Purāṇa, Kūrma Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Padma Purāṇa, Śiva Purāṇa

title: Atri Rescues Surya
description: The sage Atri rescues the sun Surya in the legend associated with the Atri lineage of Rigvedic seers

title: Avatara of Mahodara slaying Mohasura
description: Ganesha descends as Mahodara to slay Mohasura, demon of delusion/confusion

title: Bhrigu's curse making Agni all-devouring
description: Sage Bhrigu curses Agni to become eater of everything pure and impure; distressed, Agni withdraws until the gods coax him back with the boon that fire purifies whatever it touches

title: Birth of Kartikeya from the reeds
description: In the reed-bed the seed becomes six infants suckled by the six Krittikas; when Parvati embraces all six they fuse into the six-faced Shanmukha (Kartikeya)
source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva; Skanda Purana; Shiva Purana

title: Burning of Kāma by Śiva
description: At the Aṅga site Viśvāmitra recounts how Śiva reduced Kāma to ash, making him Ananga, the bodiless

title: Devapi and Maru Restore Dharma
description: Two immortals, Devapi (lunar line) and Maru (solar line), re-emerge from Kalapa to re-found the kshatriya dynasties

title: Devi's vow to marry only her conqueror
description: When Shumbha's envoy demands she marry him, the Goddess refuses, vowing to wed only one who defeats her in battle, inviting the war

title: Indra slays Diti's womb-son, creating the Maruts
description: To forestall an Indra-killer, Indra slays Diti's gestating son in the womb, and the fragments become the Maruts, the storm-gods and Indra's allies

title: Śiva disrupts Dakṣa's sacrifice (Bhaviṣya Parva)
description: In the heterogeneous Bhaviṣya Parva, sectarian myth recounts Śiva's disruption of Dakṣa's sacrifice and Hari's combat with him — a Vaiṣṇava retelling among the alternate cosmogonies and hymns

title: Kālāntaka — Śiva conquers Death for Mārkaṇḍeya
description: When Yama comes to claim the Śiva-devotee boy Mārkaṇḍeya at his fated death at sixteen, Śiva bursts from the liṅga as Kālāntaka, strikes down Yama, and grants the boy deathless eternal youth
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Ṛgveda 7.59.12

title: Lalita emerges from yajna fire to slay Bhandasura
description: Lalita Tripurasundari emerges from the fire of a yajna and slays the demon Bhandasura, who was born of Kama's ashes, commanding the Sri Chakra battle-array

title: Manikantha Slays Mahishi and Founds Sabarimala
description: The divine infant Manikantha, raised by King Rajashekhara of Pandalam, fetches tiger's milk, defeats Mahishi, reveals his divinity, and asks a shrine be built where his arrow lands at Sabarimala

title: Narasiṃha as fourth Daśāvatāra
description: Narasiṃha takes his place as the fourth of the ten classical avatāras within the Satya-yuga descent group, linking forward to Vāmana via Prahlāda's grandson Bali

title: Puranas Recited to the Sages at Naimisaranyam
description: At Tiru Naimisaranyam, the forest where Suta recites the Puranas to the assembled sages

title: Revival of Kāmadeva and restoration of the worlds
description: From the victorious fire (or at Rati's plea) Kāmadeva is restored to bodily form and reunited with Rati; desire and fertility return, the devas regain their stations, and Lalitā returns to Śrīpura as Rājarājeśvarī

title: Shani's gaze severs Ganesha's head
description: In a folk variant, the reluctant Shani is pressed to look at baby Ganesha and his destroying glance severs the child's head, leading to the elephant-head substitution

title: Shared Hindu–Buddhist Siddha membership
description: Matsyendra/Lūipa, Gorakṣa, Jālandhara, Kāṇha/Kṛṣṇacārya, Caurangī and Saraha recur in both Nāth and Vajrayāna lists, marking a single trans-sectarian Siddha milieu and the fountainhead of haṭha-yoga, alchemy and Sahaja Tantra

title: Shiva Frees Supriya and Slays Daruka at Nageshwar
description: Shiva frees his devotee Supriya and fellow prisoners held by the demon Daruka in their undersea city, destroying the demon and remaining as Nagesha, lord of serpents, in Darukavana

title: Shiva Rescues Supriya and Slays Daruka at Nageshvara
description: Shiva manifests as the Nageshvara jyotirlinga near Dvaraka in connection with rescuing his devotee Supriya and the legend of the demon Daruka

title: Shiva slays Andhaka and Andhaka becomes Bhringin
description: Shiva in Bhairava form impales the demon Andhaka on the trident; from his blood emerge the Ashta-Bhairavas and the planet Mangala, and the purified Andhaka becomes the gana Bhringin

title: Shiva Slays Yama to Save Markandeya (Kalantaka)
description: When Yama casts his noose at the boy Markandeya clinging to a Shivalinga, Shiva bursts forth as Kalantaka and slays the god of death, then grants Markandeya eternal youth

title: Sureshvara tests Upamanyu
description: Shiva appears as Indra to test the boy-sage Upamanyu's devotion, then reveals himself and grants boons

title: The fowler converted by the self-immolating pigeon
description: A bird-catcher caught in a storm is shown selfless hospitality by a captured pigeon and its mate, who immolate themselves for their guest; moved, the fowler renounces violence and takes to asceticism

title: The nectar-strengthened devas win the Amrita-manthana war
description: Strengthened by the nectar, the devas with Vishnu defeat the asuras, Indra is restored to Svarga, and Lakshmi's fortune returns

title: Tāmraparṇī drips from Agastya's pot on Pothigai
description: The pearl-bearing Tāmraparṇī is said to issue from Agastya's water-pot on the Pothigai (Malaya) hill

title: Vishnu's Self-Revelation to Mārkaṇḍeya
description: The boy reveals himself as Nārāyaṇa, source and end of all worlds, who reabsorbs and re-emits creation, telling the sage he alone may witness it

title: Avatara of Gajavaktra slaying Lobhasura
description: Ganesha descends as Gajanana/Gajavaktra to slay Lobhasura, demon of greed

title: Battle of the Ten Kings (Dasarajna)
description: With the seer Vasishtha as his priest, King Sudas defeats a confederation of ten kings in the Dasarajna war on the Parushni river

title: Birth of Kārttikeya to slay Tāraka
description: Viśvāmitra narrates the cosmic birth of Skanda from Agni and the Kṛttikās to kill the asura Tāraka, alongside the births of Gaṅgā and Umā

title: Birth of the Three-Breasted Minakshi
description: Born of a yajna to the childless Pandya king Malayadhvaja, the girl Minakshi has three breasts, with a prophecy that the third will vanish when she meets her destined husband

title: Devi burns Dhumralochana to ash
description: The Goddess reduces the general Dhumralochana to ashes with a single humkara, and her lion mauls his army

title: Hanuman shields devotees from Shani
description: In folk tradition Hanuman frees or defeats Shani, who then grants that devotees of Hanuman are spared his worst affliction

title: Jalandhara-vadha and the Vrinda deception
description: Vishnu disguised as Jalandhara tricks the chaste Vrinda into breaking her vow, destroying the asura's invincibility; Shiva slays Jalandhara, and Vrinda immolates herself to be reborn as Tulasi

title: Jālandhara-vadha & the Vṛndā deception
description: Viṣṇu tricks the chaste Vṛndā into breaking her vow so Śiva can slay her invincible ocean-born husband Jālandhara with a toe-spun discus; Vṛndā curses Viṣṇu and immolates herself
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā Yuddha-khaṇḍa, Padma Purāṇa

title: Kripa counted among the eight Chiranjivis and future Saptarshi
description: Kripa is named in the chiranjivi-smarana verse as a deathless one and is held to become a Saptarshi of the future Savarni Manvantara

title: Revelation of the Lalitā Sahasranāma and Śrī Vidyā charter
description: The eight Vāg-devīs reveal the thousand names encoding the myth; the Lalitopākhyāna and Tripurā-rahasya become the foundation legend and inner allegory of the Śrī Vidyā Śrīkula cult

title: Shatakshi/Shakambhari slays Durgama
description: When the asura Durgama seizes the Vedas and causes a hundred-year drought, the Goddess manifests as the hundred-eyed Shatakshi and herb-bearing Shakambhari, nourishes the world, and destroys Durgama

title: Shiva reclaims Kashi from King Divodasa
description: Through the 64 Yoginis and Ganesha, Shiva reclaims the city of Varanasi from King Divodasa, establishing Kashi as the supreme moksha-kshetra

title: Shiva Restores Yama to Life
description: The gods plead and Shiva revives the slain Yama so the cosmic order of death can continue, earning Shiva the epithet Mrityunjaya

title: Shiva's Closing Boons to Mārkaṇḍeya
description: After the vision vanishes, Shiva and Pārvatī appear and grant Mārkaṇḍeya undying fame, freedom from age and death, and mastery of the Purāṇas

title: Skanda made general of the gods
description: Even as a boy Skanda is anointed Devasenapati, commander of the celestial army, by Indra and armed by Shiva with the Vel

title: Spilled amrita founds the Kumbh Mela sites
description: In popular tradition drops of amrita fall at Prayag, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik during the contest over the pot, the origin legend of the Kumbh Mela

title: Svaha unites with Agni (Karttikeya conception)
description: Svaha, in love with Agni, takes the forms of six of the seven saptarshi wives to unite with him, a strand woven into the birth of the war-god Karttikeya

title: The Rāmopākhyāna retelling
description: Mārkaṇḍeya narrates the compressed Daṇḍaka sequence to Yudhiṣṭhira in the Pāṇḍavas' Dvāpara exile-forest

title: Uma-Haimavati reveals Brahman to the gods
description: Uma-Haimavati appears to the gods in the Kena Upanishad to reveal Brahman, the earliest named appearance of the Goddess as teacher

title: Viṣṇu slays Hayagrīva and seizes the Sudarśana disc
description: In a Rāmāyaṇa-variant origin, Viṣṇu seizes the Sudarśana discus after slaying the dānava Hayagrīva atop Mt. Cakravāna

title: Vṛtrasura battles Indra
description: The demon-devotee Vṛtra battles Indra; the Narayana-kavaca mantra-armor figures in the episode

title: Vyāsa instructs his son Śuka, who attains liberation
description: The renunciate Śuka, having mastered the Vedas, questions Vyāsa on the highest good; Vyāsa teaches the path to Brahman and Śuka attains liberation, merging into the elements

title: Annapurna feeds Shiva proving food is real
description: Parvati as Annapurna, goddess of nourishment, feeds Shiva at Kashi to prove that food is real after he declared the world illusory

title: Avatara of Lambodara slaying Krodhasura
description: Ganesha descends as Lambodara to slay Krodhasura, demon of anger/wrath

title: Bhairava's Kāpālika penance and the skull's fall at Kāśī
description: Bhairava wanders as a naked mendicant begging with the skull-bowl until the brahmahatyā sin is expiated and the skull finally drops at Kapāla-mocana in Kāśī, making Vārāṇasī the supreme place of liberation
source: Śiva Purāṇa Śatarudra-saṃhitā; Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa

title: Citraketu cursed by Parvati to become Vṛtra
description: King Citraketu is cursed by Parvati to be born as the demon Vṛtra, linking the two skandha-6 episodes

title: Descent of the Narmada (Reva)
description: The river Narmada (Reva) originates from Shiva's tapas on Mt. Maikala, gaining such power that the mere sight of her equals bathing in the Ganga

title: Śiva gifts the Sudarśana Cakra to Viṣṇu
description: In the Śaiva variant, Viṣṇu worships Śiva with a thousand lotuses, offers his own eye for the flower Śiva hid, and Śiva gifts him the discus — hence 'Sudarśana.'

title: Kali springs from the brow and is named Chamunda
description: Facing Chanda and Munda, Kali leaps from the Goddess's brow, devours the asura army, beheads the two generals, and is named Chamunda

title: Markandeya's vision of pralaya
description: The deathless sage survives the cosmic dissolution and beholds Vishnu as a divine infant on a banyan leaf, entering the child to see the universe within

title: Marriage of Minakshi and Sundareshvara
description: The warrior-queen Minakshi storms Kailasa; facing Shiva her third breast vanishes, recognizing her lord, and Shiva comes to Madurai as Sundareshvara to wed her

title: Shiva and Vishnu jointly slay Jalodbhava
description: The water-born demon Jalodbhava is destroyed by Shiva and Vishnu together; in the episode Shiva gifts the Sudarshana-cakra to Vishnu and sacred rivers are materialized

title: Shiva Revives Ghushma's Son at Grishneshwar
description: The devotee Ghushma keeps faith after her co-wife murders her son and throws him in the tank where she immerses her daily lingas, and Shiva revives the boy and manifests as Grishneshwar, the last jyotirlinga

title: Skanda slays Tarakasura
description: Skanda leads the devas and slays Taraka with the Vel, fulfilling his birth-purpose and ending the asura's terror of the three worlds

title: Slaying of Shankhachuda
description: Shankhachuda, protected by his wife Tulasi's chastity, loses his power when Vishnu in disguise breaks her vow, and is then slain by Shiva's trident

title: Sulabhā enters King Janaka's mind and out-argues him
description: The female ascetic Sulabhā, doubting Janaka's claimed liberation-while-ruling, enters his mind by yogic power and out-argues him in a famous debate on whether one truly free can remain a king

title: Surya's Marriage (Wedding Hymn)
description: The wedding of Surya (the sun-maiden) is narrated in the archetypal Vedic marriage hymn, the model for human wedding rites

title: Ajamila Saved by the Name
description: The fallen brahmana Ajamila is saved at death by calling his son 'Narayana,' demonstrating the glory of the divine Name in the Vishnuduta-Yamaduta debate

title: Avatara of Vikata slaying Kamasura
description: Ganesha descends as the peacock-mounted Vikata to slay Kamasura, demon of lust/desire

title: Durgā Slays Mahiṣāsura
description: The buffalo-demon Mahiṣa, unkillable by god or man, conquers heaven until the gods pool their tejas into Durgā, who beheads him mid-shapeshift with her triśūla, earning the name Mahiṣāsuramardinī

title: Gajāsura-saṃhāra — slaying the elephant-demon
description: Śiva impales the elephant-demon Gajāsura on his trident, dances upon him, and flays his hide to wear as a garment, becoming Kṛttivāsas, the hide-clad one
source: Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Kūrma Purāṇa

title: Markandeya and Kalantaka (conquest of death)
description: The boy-sage Markandeya, fated to die at sixteen, embraces the linga; when Yama's noose snares it, Shiva bursts forth as Kalantaka, strikes down Yama, and grants Markandeya deathless youth

title: Murugan splits Surapadman
description: In the Tamil cycle Murugan hurls the Vel and splits Surapadman in two; the halves become his peacock vahana and rooster banner

title: Shiva's 64 Sacred Games (Tiruvilaiyadal) at Madurai
description: Shiva performs sixty-four lilas across Madurai (carrying sand for pittu, the poetry contest with Nakkirar), making the whole city the kshetra of his sacred sports

title: Soma cursed by Daksha and restored at Prabhasa
description: The Moon-god Soma, cursed by his father-in-law Daksha to wane, regains his light by worshiping Shiva at Prabhasa, the etiology of the Somnath ('Lord of Soma') jyotirlinga

title: The Dharma-vyādha (righteous butcher) teaches the proud Brahmin
description: The righteous butcher of Mithilā teaches a proud Brahmin that dharma lies in doing one's own duty without attachment, even in a low trade

title: The eclipse vendetta of Rahu and Ketu
description: In revenge for exposing him, Rahu and Ketu periodically swallow Surya and Chandra, who pass through the severed throat and reappear, causing eclipses

title: The Seven Mothers emerge
description: The shaktis of the major gods burst forth as the Saptamatrika, each a feminine mirror of her god with his vahana and weapons

title: Yaksheshvara humbles the proud devas
description: After the devas grow proud of defeating the asuras, the mysterious Yaksha-form of Shiva humbles them by setting a blade of grass none can burn or cut

title: Ajamila Saved by the Name (Yamaduta encounter)
description: The Yamadutas are driven off by Vishnu's Vishnudutas when the dying sinner Ajamila cries 'Narayana,' establishing that devotion overrides Yama's jurisdiction

title: Andhakāsura-vadha — slaying the blind demon
description: Śiva impales the lustful demon Andhaka on his trident and holds him aloft until his pride burns away, while the Mātṛkās drink his cloning blood; the chastened Andhaka becomes the gaṇa-leader Bhṛṅgi
source: Matsya Purāṇa; Kūrma Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa

title: Avatara of Vighnaraja slaying Mamasura
description: Ganesha descends as Vighnaraja, mounted on the serpent Shesha, to slay Mamasura/Mamatasura, demon of attachment/possessiveness

title: Birth of Skanda to slay Taraka
description: Agni and the Krittikas rear the war-god Skanda, born to slay Taraka, who becomes commander of the gods' army

title: Hanuman identified as a Rudra-amsha
description: The Shatarudra-samhita enumerates Shiva's manifestations and identifies Hanuman as a partial incarnation (amsha) of Rudra

title: Kali drinks Raktabija's blood
description: As Chandika strikes the cloning demon Raktabija, Kali drinks every falling drop and devours the spawned clones before they touch ground, killing him bloodless

title: King Sukeshi and the flying city
description: The Shiva-devoted rakshasa king Sukeshi is granted invincibility and a flying city, and teaches dharma so that the demons become virtuous

title: Kālī Slays Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa (Cāmuṇḍā)
description: The generals Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa of Śumbha-Niśumbha are slain by Kālī, who springs from Durgā's brow and is renamed Cāmuṇḍā

title: Mankanaka's dance and Shiva's humbling
description: Vegetable sap flows from the sage's wound and he dances the world into dancing, until Shiva humbles his pride by showing ash from his own thumb

title: Marriage of Kartikeya to Devasena
description: Kartikeya weds Devasena, given to him by Indra as his army-bride at Tiruparankunram after the demon-war

title: Mothers emanated to fight Raktabija
description: The Sapta/Ashta Matrikas, shaktis of the male gods, are emanated to fight the demon Raktabija

title: Shiva and Parvati Follow Kartikeya to Srisailam
description: After the fruit-quarrel with Ganesha, Kartikeya sulks off to Srisailam, and his parents follow to settle on the hill as Mallikarjuna and Bhramaramba

title: Tulādhāra teaches the penance-proud Jājali
description: A heavenly voice declares the merchant Tulādhāra greater in righteousness than the austerity-proud Jājali; Tulādhāra teaches that true dharma is universal harmlessness and honest livelihood, not ritual

title: Viśvāmitra reveals the Gāyatrī mantra
description: As Ṛgvedic seer of Maṇḍala 3, Viśvāmitra is the draṣṭṛ of RV 3.62.10, the Sāvitrī/Gāyatrī, the most sacred Vedic verse

title: Avatara of Dhumravarna slaying Abhimanasura
description: Ganesha descends as the blue-horse-mounted Dhumravarna to slay Abhimanasura/Ahankarasura, demon of pride/egotism

title: Bhramaramba Slays the Bee-Demon Arunasura
description: The Goddess takes the form Bhramari and emits swarms of six-legged bees to destroy the demon Arunasura, who held a boon against death by any two- or four-legged being

title: Death of Nishumbha
description: Chandika duels and fells Nishumbha, decapitating the being that tries to emerge from his body

title: Gajendra-moksa
description: The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile, is liberated when he surrenders to Viṣṇu, a touchstone of saranagati

title: Indra splits Diti's foetus into the Maruts
description: Indra, to abort the asura who would kill him, splits the sleeping Diti's foetus into the forty-nine Maruts

title: Jālandhara-vadha and the Vṛndā deception
description: To defeat the invincible ocean-born Jālandhara, Viṣṇu impersonates him and breaks the chastity of his wife Vṛndā; Śiva then slays Jālandhara with a discus, and the betrayed Vṛndā curses Viṣṇu and immolates herself, reborn as Tulasī
source: Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā Yuddha-khaṇḍa; Padma Purāṇa

title: Kalantaka conquers Death for Markandeya
description: Shiva conquers Death by kicking down Yama to save the boy-devotee Markandeya, the root of the Mrityunjaya conqueror-of-death form

title: Murugan woos and weds Valli
description: Murugan woos Valli, daughter of a Tamil hunter chieftain, in disguise (aided by Ganesha as an elephant) and weds her as his love-bride

title: Raktabīja Slain, Blood Drunk by Kālī
description: The asura general Raktabīja, whose every spilled blood-drop spawns a clone, is ended when Kālī drinks his blood mid-air and the Mātṛkās devour the duplicates

title: The worm reborn upward to godhood
description: A worm taught by a sage to meditate on the supreme is reborn upward through the orders of being to godhood, a parable of devotion and the soul's ascent

title: Viśvāmitra parts the rivers for Sudās
description: As purohita of King Sudās, Viśvāmitra persuades the rivers to lower their waters so the Bharata army can cross

title: Citraketu Cursed to be Born Vritra
description: The grieving king Citraketu becomes a vidyadhara, mocks Shiva-Parvati, and is cursed by Parvati to be born as the demon Vritra

title: Devi reabsorbs all goddesses into herself
description: When Shumbha taunts that she fights with others' help, the Devi declares she alone exists and reabsorbs the Matrikas and Kali into her single self

title: Goddess Slays Niśumbha and Śumbha
description: The asura brothers Śumbha and Niśumbha, who seized the three worlds, are slain in sequence by the Goddess (Kauśikī/Ambikā), who reabsorbs Kālī for the final duel, ending the war

title: Markandeya survives the cosmic deluge
description: The deathless sage adrift on the dissolution-ocean enters and exits the mouth of the child Vishnu on the banyan leaf, beholding cyclic time

title: Parvati manifests as Annapurna at Kashi
description: When Shiva declares the world maya, Parvati withdraws and food vanishes from the cosmos; she manifests as Annapurna at Kashi, feeding even Shiva, establishing the Goddess as sustaining material reality

title: Skanda teaches Pranava to Shiva at Swamimalai
description: The child Skanda imprisons Brahma for failing to explain Om, briefly takes over creation, and expounds the syllable to Shiva himself, becoming Swaminatha

title: Tripurantaka destroys the three cities
description: Shiva, with a single arrow from his bow Pinaka, destroys the three flying cities (Tripura) of the asuras
source: Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita; Mahabharata Karna Parva

title: Two clocks for the sectarian Upaniṣads
description: Academically a late CE layer post-dating Pāñcarātra/Pāśupata/Śrīvidyā; traditionally eternal apauruṣeya Śruti fixed at the ~3102 BCE Kali junction
source: Muktikā Upaniṣad; Adyar editions; scholarly dating

title: Death of Shumbha
description: The Goddess pierces Shumbha through the heart with her trident; with the demon-kings gone the gods regain heaven and sing the Narayani Stuti

title: Diti's Vow and the Birth of the Maruts
description: Diti performs penance to bear an Indra-killer, but Indra enters her womb and cuts the embryo into the forty-nine Maruts

title: Gajasuravadha — Shiva slays the elephant-demon
description: Shiva slays and dances within the flayed hide of the elephant-demon Gajasura, taking the elephant-skin-clad terror form

title: Kartikeya departs south after the race
description: Losing the fruit-race to Ganesha, the proud Kartikeya abandons Kailasa and settles in the Tamil south as Murugan

title: Andhakasura-vadha — Shiva impales Andhaka
description: Shiva impales the blind asura Andhaka on his trident, drinking each drop of his blood to prevent new demons, finally converting him into the gana Bhringi

title: Ascent of Kundalini and union of Shakti with Shiva
description: The roused Kundalini-Shakti uncoils, rises through sushumna piercing each chakra, and reunites with Shiva at the crown, producing the nectar of liberation

title: Birth of Skanda and slaying of Taraka
description: Skanda is born from Agni and the Krittikas, becomes generalissimo of the divine host, and slays the demon Taraka

title: Brahma Distills the Natya Shastra from the Four Vedas
description: Brahma creates the dramatic/aesthetic science (Gandharvaveda/Natya Shastra) as a 'fifth Veda' by drawing recitation from Rig, song from Sama, gesture from Yajur, and rasa from Atharva

title: Devi foretells future incarnations
description: In the Narayani Stuti the Devi promises to descend again, listing future forms including Shakambhari, who feeds the world in a drought, and Bhramari, who slays Aruna

title: Dharmavyadha teaches Kaushika (Vyadha-gita)
description: The righteous fowler Dharmavyadha instructs the brahmin Kaushika that ahimsa is the highest dharma, a renunciant ideal

title: Forging of Indra's Vajra from Dadhīci's bones
description: The sage Dadhīci gives up his body so the gods can forge the Vajra thunderbolt from his spine/bones — the one weapon able to slay the asura Vṛtra

title: Mahakaleshvara linga emerges (slaying of Dushana)
description: Shiva bursts forth at Ujjain to destroy the demon Dushana threatening a devotee-boy, remaining as the south-facing svayambhu Mahakaleshvara jyotirlinga

title: Vaishnavi Beheads Bhairavnath at Trikuta
description: The divine girl Vaishnavi, pursued by the lustful tantric Bhairavnath at Shridhar's feast, flees to the Trikuta cave and beheads him at the cave-mouth

title: Devi grants Suratha and Samadhi their boons
description: After three years of worship the Goddess grants Suratha rebirth as the future Manu Savarni and Samadhi spiritual liberation, closing the frame

title: Jalandharavadha — Shiva slays Jalandhara
description: Shiva slays the asura Jalandhara, born of his own brow-fire, by cutting him with a chakra drawn from his toe
source: Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Yuddha Khanda

title: Naciketa's journey to Yama-loka
description: The boy Naciketa, sent to the abode of death by his angry father Uddalaka, traverses Yama's world, sees the rewards of dharma and punishments of sin, and returns to describe it

title: The Boon to Bhairavnath
description: Dying repentant, Bhairavnath is forgiven and granted that no Vaishno Devi pilgrimage is complete until the devotee also visits his shrine above the cave

title: Transmission of Ayurveda from Brahma to Sages
description: The science of medicine descends through a divine chain — Brahma to Daksha Prajapati to the Ashvins to Indra to Dhanvantari/Bharadvaja and finally to human sages — founding Ayurveda

title: Bhikshatana seduces the Daruka-vana sages' wives
description: As a naked beautiful mendicant wandering in penance for severing Brahma's head, Shiva seduces the wives of the Daruka forest sages

title: Śiva burns the three cities of Tripurāsura with the Pināka
description: Śiva uses his bow Pināka (and in some tellings the Vijaya bow made by Viśvakarmā) to destroy the three flying cities of Tripurāsura, earning the epithet Pinākī

title: Kanya Kumari's Sabotaged Wedding to Shiva
description: To keep the Goddess virgin so she can kill Banasura, the gods sabotage her dawn wedding to Shiva (Narada crows like a cock), so she remains kumari forever

title: Matrikas born from Vaishnavi's distracted mind
description: In the Varaha Purana's unusual account, the eight Mother-Goddesses arise from the goddess Vaishnavi losing concentration during austerity, with Yamuna as seventh and Yogeshvari as eighth

title: Nahusha's Fall
description: Becoming interim Indra, Nahusha grows arrogant, kicks Agastya while demanding the saptarshis carry his palanquin, and is cursed to fall as a python, later liberated by Yudhishthira

title: Shiva Reveals Rama's Secret to Parvati
description: As the Adhyatma's outer frame, Shiva — supreme jnanin and devotee — discloses the esoteric inner (Brahman) meaning of Rama's life to Parvati in an Uma-Maheshvara dialogue

title: Durga slays Mahishasura (Varaha telling)
description: The Varaha Purana carries the Goddess's destruction of the buffalo-demon Mahishasura and allied demons

title: Kapila Reborn as Avatara of Vishnu (Samkhya Founder)
description: The mythic sage Kapila, said to be an avatara of Vishnu, founds the Samkhya enumeration of Purusha and Prakriti, establishing the dualist darshana

title: Kumari Slays Banasura
description: The Goddess incarnates as the virgin Kumari and slays the demon Banasura, who held a boon that only a virgin girl could kill him, with her cakra

title: Sudarśana cuts Satī's corpse into 51 pieces
description: Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra cuts the corpse of Satī into pieces that fall to earth as the 51 Śākta pīṭhas

title: Durgā receives her lion mount from Himavān
description: The Himālaya (Himavān) gives Durgā her lion/tiger mount, which the warrior-goddess rides into battle against Mahiṣāsura

title: Priyavrata enlightened by Narada
description: The king Priyavrata gains past-life wisdom and heaven through bhakti after instruction by Narada

title: Pārvatī gives the Vel spear to Kārttikeya
description: Pārvatī gifts the divine spear Vel to Kārttikeya/Murugan, the emblem with which he slays Tāraka/Sūrapadma

title: Rudrākṣa born of Śiva's tears
description: The Rudrākṣa seeds are born of Śiva's tears of compassion (over Tripura / over the world), strung into mālās for japa

title: Yama Dvitiya / Bhai Duj Charter
description: Yama visits his sister Yamuna who honors him with a feast, and he grants that brothers who receive their sister's tilaka or bathe in the Yamuna escape untimely death

title: Ashvashira's liberation
description: The king Ashvashira learns Narayana's omnipresence and that detached performance of duty (nishkama-karma) leads to liberation

title: Devi Mutes and Slays Mukasura at Kollur
description: The Goddess robs a tapas-performing demon of speech, making him Muka; when the mute demon harasses sage Kola, she slays him and stays on as Mukambika at Kola's request

title: Pippalada Answers the Six Questions
description: The sage Pippalada is approached by six pupils who put six questions to him on creation, prana, Om, sleep, and the sixteen kalas of the Purusha, delivering the Prashna Upanishad's teaching

title: The pigeon's self-sacrifice for the hunter
description: A male pigeon immolates himself in his own fire to feast the hunter who had snared his mate, the supreme tale of guest-hospitality

title: Vṛndā curses Viṣṇu to become the Śālagrāma stone
description: After Viṣṇu breaks Vṛndā's chastity by impersonating her asura husband Jālandhara so Śiva can slay him, the heartbroken Vṛndā curses Viṣṇu to become stone (the Śālagrāma) and immolates herself, rising as the Tulsī plant

title: Establishment of the manvantara administration
description: At each manvantara turnover Brahma renews the cosmic administration — a new Manu, Indra, Devas, Saptarishis, Manu's sons, and a manvantara-avatara of Vishnu

title: Gautama kills the crane-king Rajadharman
description: The ungrateful brahmin kills and eats his benefactor the crane-king and is destroyed, a fable on ingratitude

title: Markandeya's pralaya vision of Bala-Mukunda
description: Granted to behold Vishnu's maya, the deathless Markandeya survives the cosmic deluge, sees the infant Vishnu on a banyan leaf, is inhaled into him to witness the whole universe, and exhaled back

title: Sarasvati River Dries Up at Vinashana
description: The mighty Vedic river Sarasvati dries up and sinks underground at Vinashana, surviving as the hidden third stream at Prayag

title: Tulasī becomes the Gaṇḍakī river and Tulsī plant
description: In the Śaṅkhacūḍa variant, Tulasī does penance to win Viṣṇu and is married to the asura Śaṅkhacūḍa; after Śiva slays him, Viṣṇu decrees her body becomes the Gaṇḍakī river and her hair the Tulsī plant
source: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Tulasi in Hinduism (Wikipedia)

title: Uddalaka Aruni Teaches Shvetaketu 'Tat Tvam Asi'
description: The sage Uddalaka Aruni instructs his son Shvetaketu with the great mahavakya 'tat tvam asi' (That thou art), a foundational teaching of Vedanta delivered in the Chandogya

title: Mārkaṇḍeya sees the infant Viṣṇu on the Akṣaya-vaṭa
description: During the cosmic dissolution, Mārkaṇḍeya sees the infant Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu floating on the leaf of the imperishable banyan (Akṣaya-vaṭa) on the pralaya-waters

title: Naciketas Questions Yama on Death and the Self
description: The boy Naciketas confronts Yama, god of death, and through a dialogue receives the teaching on the immortal Self and the 'razor's edge' path, recorded in the Katha Upanishad

title: Bhrigu Progressively Realizes Brahman
description: Taught by his father Varuna, the sage Bhrigu ascends through anna, prana, manas, vijnana to ananda, progressively realizing Brahman in the Bhrigu-valli of the Taittiriya Upanishad

title: Descent of the Godavari (Gautami Ganga)
description: To expiate the accidental killing of a phantom cow, the sage Gautama propitiates Shiva, who releases a strand of Ganga into the Deccan as the Godavari

title: Gajendra-mokṣa — Viṣṇu liberates the elephant-king
description: The elephant-king Gajendra, seized in a lake by the crocodile Hūhū and struggling for a thousand years, surrenders utterly with a raised lotus; Viṣṇu flies in on Garuḍa, slays the crocodile with the Sudarśana cakra, and liberates him

title: The Matsya flood — saving of Vaivasvata Manu
description: Vishnu as the fish Matsya warns Vaivasvata of a coming deluge; the Manu's boat carries the seven sages, the seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya
source: Matsya Purana, Bhagavata Purana 8.24, Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1

title: Surya reveals the Surya Siddhanta to Maya
description: The Sun-god Surya reveals the Surya Siddhanta, the cornerstone of Hindu mathematical astronomy, to the asura Maya, framing the science of time as divinely given

title: Naraka(sura) of Kamarupa
description: The Kalika Purana records the legend of the demon-king Naraka of Pragjyotisha/Kamarupa, from whom the historical Assamese dynasties claimed descent

title: Sati Takes Sita's Form to Test Rama
description: In the Manas frame, Parvati (as Sati) doubts Rama's divinity and assumes Sita's form to test him, prompting Shiva to instruct her in true devotion

title: Śukra wins the Mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā
description: Bhṛgu's son Śukra, guru of the asuras, obtains from Śiva the Mṛtasañjīvanī science to revive the slain

title: Cyavana rejuvenated by the Aśvins
description: The aged sage Cyavana, married to princess Sukanyā, is rejuvenated by the Aśvins (the origin of Cyavanaprāśa), and in return secures them a soma-share

title: Kakabhushundi Recounts Rama's Glory to Garuda
description: The immortal crow-sage Kakabhushundi expounds Rama's glory to Garuda, who had been confused by Rama's human-seeming bondage in the war

title: Atyantika Pralaya — moksha of the individual soul
description: The individual soul's permanent merger with Brahman through liberating knowledge; ego is destroyed and samsara ends forever for that being

title: Markandeya survives the cosmic flood
description: The deathless sage Markandeya survives the cosmic dissolution-flood and sees the whole cosmos in the infant resting on a banyan leaf

title: Bhikṣāṭana and the Dāruka-vana (pine-forest) myth
description: Śiva wanders the Dāruka pine-forest as the naked, beautiful, ash-smeared mendicant Bhikṣāṭana to humble a colony of arrogant Mīmāṃsaka/atheist ṛṣis who hold that ritual karma alone governs the cosmos; he seduces their wives while Viṣṇu-as-Mohinī deludes the sages, and when the enraged ṛṣis hurl conjured weapons (tiger, serpent, the Apasmāra dwarf, fire, ḍamaru, deer, axe) he subdues each and takes it as a permanent attribute, finally dancing the tāṇḍava on the dwarf — the etiological charter for his entire core iconography
actors: the Dāruka-vana Mīmāṃsaka/heretical ṛṣis and their wives
source: Liṅga Purāṇa; Kūrma Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Sūta Saṃhitā; Tamil Śaiva sthala-purāṇa

title: Indra slays Vritra after drinking soma
description: Empowered by drinking vast quantities of the immortality-giving soma, Indra slays the demon Vritra

title: Kaṅkālamūrti — bearing the skeleton-staff of Viṣvaksena
description: In the continuous penitential form linked to the Bhairava/brahmahatyā wandering, Śiva roams as a begging ascetic bearing on his trident the kaṅkāla (skeleton/bone-staff) of Viṣvaksena, Viṣṇu's gatekeeper-commander whom he slew when barred entry; the bone-staff becomes the defining emblem of the form as he expiates the killing
source: Kāraṇāgama; Śaiva Āgama / śilpa tradition; sthala-purāṇa

title: Chandra weds the 27 nakshatra daughters of Daksha
description: Chandra marries the twenty-seven daughters of Daksha Prajapati who personify the lunar mansions, visiting one wife per night — the calendrical core of the myth

title: Daksha curses Chandra with wasting disease
description: Enraged by Chandra's neglect of all wives but Rohini, Daksha curses him with kshaya-roga (consumption), causing the Moon to dwindle — the etiology of the lunar phases

title: Kapila transmits Sankhya through the lineage
description: Kapila teaches Sankhya at the dawn of the present cosmic order, transmitting it through Asuri and Pancasikha to a disciple-lineage later versified by Isvarakṛṣṇa

title: Markandeya Beholds the Pralaya
description: The deathless sage Markandeya beholds the cosmic dissolution and the child on the banyan-leaf, and resists Kamadeva

title: Narayana reveals Pancaratra over five nights
description: The Lord Narayana reveals the Pancaratra doctrine over five nights to five sages, the originating revelation of the Vaiṣṇava Agama stream

title: Shiva grants Chandra periodic waxing and waning (Somanatha origin)
description: The dying Chandra worships Shiva at Prabhasa; Shiva places the crescent on his head and grants that he will wane and wax forever rather than die — founding the Somanatha jyotirlinga

title: Chandra abducts Tara
description: After arrogance bred by his Rajasuya sacrifice, Chandra abducts Tara, wife of Brihaspati, and refuses every plea to return her

title: Śeṣa abandons Kadrū's curse-plot
description: Revolted by his kinsmen's deceit in clinging to Uccaiḥśravas's tail to cheat Vinatā, the eldest nāga Śeṣa abandons the serpent-society to undertake penance

title: The Tarakamaya War
description: The dispute over Tara escalates into a cosmic war pitting Brihaspati, Indra and Rudra against Chandra, Shukra and the asuras, threatening universal destruction until Brahma mediates

title: Birth of Budha to Tara and Chandra
description: Tara returns pregnant; pressed before the assembly she declares Chandra the father, and the radiant son Budha (Mercury) is born

title: Śeṣa's great austerity
description: Śeṣa performs terrible tapas, subsisting on air, at Gandhamādana, Badarī, Gokarṇa, Puṣkara and the Himavat foothills

title: Siva reveals the Agamas as dialogue
description: The Agama revelation is framed as a dialogue of Siva (or Viṣṇu/Devi) with consort or disciple, the originating frame of Tantric/Agamic scripture for Kali Yuga

title: Brahmā's boon charging Śeṣa to uphold the earth
description: Pleased by his tapas, Brahmā grants Śeṣa his boon and charges him to steady the unstable, quaking earth

title: Śeṣa passes through the earth to become its axis
description: At Brahmā's word Śeṣa passes through a crevice clear through the globe and emerges below, bearing the earth steadily on his hood as its foundation

title: Sati surrounds Shiva as the Ten Mahavidyas
description: Forbidden by Shiva to attend Daksha's sacrifice, Sati assumes a terrifying form and multiplies into ten goddesses occupying the ten directions; whichever way Shiva turns a fierce form blocks him until he recognizes her supremacy — the origin of the Dasha Mahavidya

title: Sundareśvara's sixty-four Tiruviḷaiyāḍal at Madurai
description: Śiva-Sundareśvara performs sixty-four 'holy sports' (tiruviḷaiyāḍal) across Madurai — carrying earth for the pittu cake, the Nakkīrar poetry-contest, selling bangles, animating a stone elephant to eat sugarcane, turning jackals to horses — making the whole city the kṣetra of his play
actors: Śiva (Sundareśvara); Nakkīrar; the old woman Vandhi; the Pāṇḍya king

title: Chinnamasta severs her own head
description: Bathing with her hungry attendants, the Goddess severs her own head to feed them with three jets of her own blood — the origin myth of the self-decapitated Mahavidya Chinnamasta

title: The 64 Līlās of Śiva — Tiruviḷaiyāḍal of Sundareśvara at Madurai
description: The Tamil Śaiva cycle of sixty-four sacred sports in which Śiva as Sundareśvara, consort of Mīnākṣī, repeatedly intervenes in the Pāṇḍya capital Madurai — carrying sand for a cake of piṭṭu, the Tamil poetry-contest with Nakkīrar, selling bangles, the stone elephant eating sugarcane, opening/convening the Tamil Sangam, turning jackals into horses — foundational to Mīnākṣī-Sundareśvara temple theology and the Madurai sthala-purāṇa
source: Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam (Paranjothi Munivar; Perumpaṟṟappuliyūr Nampi); Hālāsya Māhātmya / Skanda Purāṇa; Tamil Śaiva tradition

title: Mahālakṣmī settles at Karavīra and slays Kolhāsura
description: Śrī-Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha after estrangement from Viṣṇu (in the southern recension triggered by Bhṛgu's kick) and takes permanent earthly residence at Karavīra/Kolhapur, where she also slays the demon-king Kolhāsura who, dying, begs the city bear his name and the Goddess remain

title: Origin of Dhumavati from Sati
description: Hungry and refused food at the yajna, Sati swallows Shiva himself and is cursed by him into widow's form (or emerges from the smoke of her self-immolation) — the origin of Dhumavati the widow-goddess

title: End of Dvapara and onset of Kali Yuga
description: Krishna's departure (traditionally 3102 BCE) ends Dvapara Yuga and marks the dawn of Kali Yuga

title: Lalita slays Bhandasura
description: The warrior form of Tripurasundari (Lalita) slays the demon Bhandasura, as told in the Lalitopakhyana

title: Bagalamukhi halts a world-destroying demon
description: The crane-headed goddess Bagalamukhi arises to halt a world-destroying storm/demon (Madanasura) by seizing his tongue and paralyzing him — the power of stambhana

title: Indra and the Ants (procession of past Indras)
description: Indra's pride is humbled when a procession of ants is revealed to be a line of former Indras, asserting a beginningless succession of Brahmas and Indras across cycling universes

title: The Maruts aid Indra in slaying Vṛtra
description: As Indra's war-band the Maruts lend their roar and force while he slays Vṛtra and releases the waters

title: Agastya mediates the Indra-Marut dispute
description: In the Ṛgvedic quarrel between Indra and the Maruts over the offering-share, the sage Agastya mediates and reconciles them

title: Diti's vow for a son to kill Indra
description: Grieving for her slain asura sons, Diti begs Kaśyapa for a son who will kill Indra, and is granted the powerful embryo on condition of a strict purity-vow

title: Indra splits Diti's embryo into the 49 Maruts
description: Seizing on Diti's ritual lapse, Indra enters her womb and cuts the embryo with his vajra into seven and then seven-times-seven (49) crying fragments, telling them 'mā ruda' (do not weep), thus naming the Maruts

title: Markandeya witnesses the cosmic deluge
description: The long-lived sage Markandeya floats on the cosmic ocean between cosmic days and glimpses the infant Vishnu/Krishna who contains all worlds, witnessing repeated dissolution and re-creation

title: Diti's boon makes the 49 fragments into gods
description: Waking and forgiving Indra, Diti asks that her 49 fragment-children be made devas ranged through the heavens, so the asura-born become gods

title: Holika burns and Prahlada is spared (Holika Dahan)
description: Hiranyakashipu sends his fire-immune sister Holika to burn the Vishnu-devotee Prahlada on her lap; she burns instead and Prahlada survives, enacted by the Holi bonfire

title: Shiva instructs Parvati in the Guru Gita
description: The Guru Gita is framed as Shiva instructing Parvati on the guru's nature, embedded in the Skanda Purana

title: Citraketu cursed by Pārvatī to become Vṛtra
description: The Vidyādhara king Citraketu, a former earthly king elevated to lordship, is cursed by Pārvatī to become the asura Vṛtra

title: Dasaratha Exiles His Children (Dasaratha Jataka)
description: In the Pali Dasaratha Jataka, King Dasaratha of Benares sends Rama-pandita, Lakkhana, and Sita into the forest for twelve years to avert a succession war — with no Ravana, abduction, or battle

title: Indra slays Vritra with Dadhichi's bones
description: Indra slays the great drought-demon Vritra, who held back the cosmic waters, using the vajra fashioned from sage Dadhichi's bones — the foundational deva-asura combat

title: Durga slays Mahishasura
description: The buffalo-demon Mahishasura, granted invincibility against all males, is slain by the goddess Durga as Mahishasuramardini

title: Rama-pandita's Equanimity at His Father's Death
description: On hearing (initially false) news of his father's death, Rama-pandita remains composed and teaches that all that is born must die — the Jataka's sermon on impermanence and equanimity

title: Bhṛṅgi cursed to skin-and-bone
description: The gaṇa-sage Bhṛṅgi, devotee of Śiva alone, is cursed to skin-and-bone and given a third leg for refusing to honour Pārvatī in his circumambulation — origin of the Ardhanārīśvara lesson

title: Kartikeya slays Tarakasura
description: The asura Tarakasura, slayable only by Shiva's son, is killed by Kartikeya/Skanda

title: Rama-pandita Returns, Rules, and Weds His Sister-Queen
description: After the exile term and the widow-queen's death, Rama-pandita returns to rule and takes his sister Sita as consecrated chief queen — the Buddhist sibling-couple inversion

title: Buddha Reveals the Bodhisatta Identifications
description: In the closing samodhana the Buddha reveals Rama-pandita was the Bodhisatta, Lakkhana was Sariputta, and the other characters his past-life associates

title: Shiva destroys Tripura
description: Shiva destroys the three flying cities (Tripura) of the asuras Tarakaksha, Vidyunmali and Kamalaksha with a single arrow

title: The Vālakhilyas' penance births Garuḍa
description: Mocked by Indra at Kaśyapa's sacrifice, the thumb-sized Vālakhilya sages perform penance to create a rival Indra, the boon ripening as the mighty Garuḍa

title: The Siddha instructs the Brahmana of the Kashyapa line
description: In the Anugita's opening embedded story, a wandering perfected being teaches a troubled Brahmana about transmigration and release, likening the soul entering a body to molten iron poured into a mould

title: The Brahmana teaches his wife (the Brahmana-gita)
description: A sage's wife finds her husband in meditative seclusion and questions him on the attainable worlds, sacrifice, and liberation, eliciting the inner-fire allegory of the agnihotra within the body

title: The guru instructs the disciple on Samkhya tattvas
description: In the closing Anugita dialogue an enlightened teacher answers a disciple's questions on the highest truth, expounding the three gunas and the Samkhya enumeration of tattvas up to liberation

title: Markandeya's witness of the pralaya flood
description: Granted vision of the dissolution, the sage Markandeya sees the cosmic flood and the infant Krishna floating on a banyan leaf, the narrative anchor for what persists through pralaya

title: The dialogue of the adhvaryu priest and the ascetic
description: An officiating adhvaryu priest and an ascetic debate whether internal concentration outranks outer sacrificial slaughter, touching on ahimsa and the ethics of ritual killing

title: Harikeśa banished and adopted by Śiva as guardian of Kāśī
description: The yakṣa Harikeśa, banished for worshipping Śiva against his father's Kubera-devotion, is adopted by Śiva as an attendant and set as guardian of Kāśī

title: Shiva burns Kama to ash (Kamadahana)
description: Shiva burns Kama, the love-god, to ash with his third eye, commemorated in the South as Kama Dahanam, devotion triumphing over desire

title: Lingodbhava - appearance of the infinite jyotirlinga
description: Shiva appears as an infinite pillar of light (jyotirlinga) whose top and bottom Brahma and Vishnu cannot find, basis of Maha Shivaratri and the 12 Jyotirlingas

title: Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu (Narasimha Jayanti)
description: Narasimha, the man-lion 4th avatar, appears to slay Hiranyakashipu and save Prahlada, commemorated on Vaishakha Shukla Chaturdashi

title: Birth of Ganesha and his beheading and restoration
description: Parvati forms Ganesha from her body's paste; Shiva beheads the boy guarding her door and restores him with an elephant's head; commemorated at Ganesh Chaturthi

title: Kartikeya slays Surapadma (Skanda Shashthi)
description: Kartikeya/Murugan slays the asura Surapadma, commemorated by the Skanda Shashthi festival especially in Tamil Nadu

title: Goddess Sankranti slays Sankarasura
description: The goddess Sankranti slays the demon Sankarasura in a Puranic legend tied to Makar Sankranti

title: Indrani ties a raksha thread on Indra
description: Indrani ties a sacred thread on Indra before his war with the asuras to ensure victory, an early raksha charter

title: Savitri compels Yama to restore Satyavan (Vat Savitri)
description: Savitri compels Yama to restore the life of her husband Satyavan, the upakhyana enacted by married women at Vat Savitri

title: Ekadashi born to slay the demon Mura
description: The Padma Purana personifies Ekadashi as a power born to slay the demon Mura, charter of the Ekadashi vrata
